The CNN-LSTM model exhibits outstanding performance in the seven-category audio classification task. The model converges after 100 epochs, achieving a final overall accuracy of 93.8% for the validation set and 92.6% for the test set. This system is significant for the energy-efficient and intelligent development of tunnels, as it effectively harvests renewable energy sources and enhances safety monitoring.
Keywords: Acoustic energy-driven sound monitoring sensor | Halbach array | Hybrid energy harvesting | Wind energy-driven electromagnetic generator

Title: An efficient hyperspectral classification model for foodborne pathogens based on fractional-order differentiation lightweight deep learning and membership broad learning
Abstract: Foodborne pathogens are major causative agents of food safety issues. Although traditional detection methods provide high accuracy, they often suffer from long detection cycles and complex operational procedures. As a non-destructive technique, hyperspectral imaging integrates spectral and spatial information and has shown great potential for bacterial detection. However, its practical application is still challenged by spectral noise, high-dimensional redundancy, and sensitivity to outliers. To address these challenges, this study constructs a foodborne pathogen hyperspectral dataset consisting of three representative bacteria—Candida albicans, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus—collected over three consecutive days. Furthermore, an efficient bacterial classification model, termed Efficient Deep Learning and Membership-based Broad Learning System (EDL-MBLS), is proposed. The model combines a lightweight deep network with an improved membership-based broad learning mechanism to enhance feature extraction and classification robustness. Specifically, the deep network employs multi-scale depthwise separable convolution and a channel attention mechanism to extract multi-level spectral–spatial features, while the membership broad learning module quantifies sample reliability, suppresses outlier interference, and optimizes weight distribution. Experimental results demonstrate clear performance improvements of the proposed method. On nine cross-day datasets, EDL-MBLS achieves an overall classification accuracy of 87.78%, consistently outperforming all comparison models. On single-day datasets, the proposed model attains accuracies of 96.67%, 98.33%, and 100% on Day 1, Day 2, and Day 3, respectively, all of which are higher than those of existing methods. Moreover, EDL-MBLS maintains a significantly lower parameter count and computational cost while achieving high classification accuracy, demonstrating its efficiency and suitability for practical applications. These results confirm the effectiveness, stability, and generalization capability of the proposed model, providing a reliable and non-destructive solution for rapid foodborne pathogen detection in food safety scenarios.
Keywords: Bacterial classification | Efficient deep learning | Hyperspectral data of bacteria | Membership broad learning system | Non-destructive detection

Title: AI-enhanced non-invasive diagnosis of chronic kidney disease using LIBS of fingernail biomarkers
Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a systemic condition that leads to progressive renal failure and metabolic imbalances that may be detected in the keratinized bio-tissues of the body such as fingernails. Nevertheless, still its early detection is difficult due to the invasive nature of current clinical screening approaches. This research paper provides a precise, non-invasive, and AI-enhanced diagnostic model of CKD screening through the combination of Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) and the cutting-edge ensemble machine learning to determine the elemental patterns of fingernail biomarkers. In this study, 55 participants with chronic kidney disease and 45 healthy controls were taken as the subjects and their emission spectra were measured with a nanosecond LIBS spectrometer using a laser of a fundamental wavelength @ 1064 nm. To handle the high-dimensional spectral data, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used as a feature extraction approach, forming the basis for novel machine-learning models. A sophisticated ensemble learning algorithm specifically Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) was applied to examine the biochemical change between CKD and control samples and the predictive quality was tested by a relative comparison with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm. Using 10-fold cross-validation, the XGBoost model outperformed SVM, attaining 97% accuracy, 98% sensitivity, 96% precision and specificity, and a 97% F1-Score. Moreover, external validation on a separate dataset showed that the model is robust and generalizable with 95% accuracy, 97% sensitivity, and an F1-score of 95%. The results conclude that fingernail-based LIBS integrated with ensemble machine learning is a potential and non-invasive instrument for CKD classification.
Keywords: Chronic kidney disease | Ensemble learning | LIBS | Machine learning | SVM | XGBoost

Title: Deep-learning-based acoustic state sensing of microbubble emission boiling by image recognition using the spectrogram and the cepstrogram
Abstract: Understanding the boiling state inside cooling tubes that utilize boiling heat transfer is important for the early detection of accidents and other anomalies. Acoustic-signal-based methods for detecting boiling states are effective because of their noncontact and real-time monitoring capabilities. In deep-learning-based models for boiling-state detection and prediction, acoustic signals are commonly converted into time–frequency representations such as spectrograms and processed as images by convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and similar architectures. Here, we applied deep learning to acoustic signals from subcooled boiling experiments, using both conventional spectrograms and cepstrograms (similar time–quefrency representations that can also be treated as images) as input features to evaluate their effectiveness in boiling-state identification. We focused on the transition from low- to high-heat-flux conditions, encompassing the regime up to microbubble emission boiling. Comparisons were conducted under a subcooling degree of 50 K using three deep CNN (DCNN) learning models: AlexNet, VGG-16, and ResNet-50. The results demonstrated that, across all of the DCNN models, both classification accuracy and the coefficient of determination ( R <sup>2</sup>) in regression tasks were superior when cepstrograms rather than spectrograms were used as inputs. Among the evaluated architectures, the combination of ResNet-50 with cepstrogram inputs achieved the highest performance: an F1-score of 0.9971 for the classification task and an R <sup>2</sup> of 0.9967 for the regression task. These findings indicate that the proposed approach is effective for accurately identifying and predicting boiling states under subcooled boiling conditions and holds strong potential for application as an anomaly detection method in boiling heat transfer equipment.
Keywords: Acoustic state sensing | Cepstrogram | Deep learning | Spectrogram | Subcooled boiling

Title: AI meets Piaget and Vygotsky: A theory-driven approach to fraction learning in Greek lower secondary mathematics
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into education, its pedagogical application must be guided by established learning theories to ensure relevance and developmental appropriateness. This study investigates the innovative integration of AI-based tools into mathematics instruction, focusing on fractions in a Greek lower secondary school. Drawing on Piaget’s constructivist theory, Vygotsky’s sociocultural theory, and information processing theory, it examines whether AI-supported environments can enhance conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and engagement. A quantitative quasi-experimental design was implemented over six weeks with 63 seventh-grade students divided into an experimental group (n = 31) and a control group (n = 32). The experimental group received AI-enhanced instruction using DreamBox Learning, Fractions Lab, ChatGPT, and Mathia (Carnegie Learning), while the control group followed the standard curriculum. Instruments included a mathematics conceptual understanding test, a procedural fluency test, and a student engagement questionnaire measuring behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement. Statistical tests confirmed significant differences between groups, with the experimental group showing higher performance and engagement. The study’s innovation lies in combining adaptive, interactive, and dialogic AI tools within a theory-driven framework. Implications include guiding educators in selecting AI tools that align with cognitive and socio-constructivist principles, fostering both academic achievement and student engagement. Beyond empirical gains, this study contributes a theory-aligned integration model that operationalizes Piagetian constructivism, Vygotskian scaffolding, and information-processing principles within AI-enhanced fraction instruction, offering a transferable blueprint for research and practice.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | fractions | learning theories | mathematics education | secondary education

Title: Streamlined Traffic Flow Uncertainty Quantification Based on Interval Type-II Fuzzy Inference System with Gradient Descent Optimization
Abstract: Uncertainty quantification is essential for building reliable traffic management and control applications, with current methods broadly classified into distribution-based methods that rely on probability distribution function and nondistribution-based methods that depend on other theoretical instruments. Among nondistribution-based methods, interval Type-II fuzzy inference system-based methods are promising in modeling uncertainty in traffic condition data. However, these methods generally lack a mechanism for parameter adaptation to accommodate evolving traffic patterns. Therefore, in this paper, an interval Type-II fuzzy inference system-based traffic flow uncertainty quantification method is introduced that can dynamically adjust model parameters via the gradient descent algorithm. First, an interval Type-II fuzzy inference system is proposed to model traffic flow uncertainty structure. Subsequently, built upon this structure, an uncertainty quantification method is developed that can produce prediction intervals using streaming traffic flow data. In the empirical study, real-world highway traffic flow data are used to validate the proposed method. Experimental results reveal that the proposed method maintains workable uncertainty prediction performance with respect to different time of day and traffic flow levels. In addition, the proposed method demonstrates a better performance compared with its Type-I counterpart. Discussions are provided on uncertainty quantification, its characteristics, and applications in transportation systems.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | Intelligent transportation system | Interval Type-II fuzzy inference system | Traffic uncertainty quantification

Title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence generated immersive virtual reality Simulation on skill mastery
Abstract: Background: Nursing education faces challenges in providing nursing students with sufficient clinical site opportunities due to healthcare staffing shortages and faculty resource constraints. The decline in clinical opportunities has a negative impact on nursing students' growth in critical thinking, clinical decision making, and nursing skill proficiency levels. Artificial intelligence (AI)- generated Immersive Virtual Reality (IVR) simulation provides a potential solution to improve these clinical education outcomes. Purpose: AI-generated IVR simulations for nursing students included two clinical skill scenarios: medication administration and intravenous (IV) insertion performed at three checkpoints. Forty-two undergraduate nursing students completed prebriefing activities, physical skill performance, and two IVR simulation sessions over several months. Method: Participant performance was evaluated at three checkpoints: physical simulation performance (checkpoint 1), the first AI-generated IVR simulation attempt (checkpoint 2), and the second AI-generated IVR simulation attempt (checkpoint 3) using the Creighton Competency Evaluation Instrument (C-CEI) and AI-generated data analytics. Student satisfaction was assessed using the Simulation Effectiveness Tool-Modified (SET-M). Results: Student performance scores increased across the three checkpoints for both medication administration and intravenous (IV) insertion skills. Improvements were observed in areas related to critical thinking, clinical decision-making, and nursing skill proficiency based on C-CEI evaluations and AI-generated performance analytics. Students also reported high satisfaction with the AI-generated IVR simulation experience as measured by the Simulation Effectiveness Tool-Modified (SET-M). Conclusion: Participation in AI-generated IVR simulation was associated with higher nursing student scores in critical thinking, clinical decision-making, and nursing skill proficiency. Students also reported high satisfaction with the AI-generated IVR simulation experience. These findings support the use of AI-generated IVR simulation as an additional strategy for expanding clinical learning opportunities within nursing education and preparing nursing students for professional clinical practice.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | Clinical decision making | Critical thinking | Immersive virtual reality | Nursing education | Nursing skill proficiency | Simulation satisfaction

Title: A knowledge-driven adaptive meta-heuristic for wafer probing scheduling problem with resource-dependent and batch-processing machines
Abstract: Within the context of industrial AI and smart manufacturing, intelligent scheduling methods have become essential for semiconductor production to enhance productivity and operational efficiency. As the final step in the front-end process, wafer probing requires efficient scheduling plans to maximize throughput. Due to the specific configuration constraints and batch-processing machinery in wafer probing facilities, the wafer probing scheduling problem (WPSP) becomes highly complex. Meta-heuristics are efficient stochastic methods for global optimization in large-scale problems. However, existing approaches often incorporate limited domain knowledge, hindering their performance in large-scale problems with complex constraints. First of all, the WPSP is investigated with both resource-dependent and batch-processing machines in this paper, and a novel mixed-integer linear programming model is proposed to represent the problem mathematically. Then, an improved knowledge-driven adaptive genetic algorithm (KAGA) is proposed to address WPSP instances. The KAGA employs a specialized two-stage encoding scheme to accommodate multiple operation types, and integrates a novel knowledge-driven active decoding mechanism designed to minimize the idle time of machines. To balance the load among machines, an adaptive weight machine allocation strategy is incorporated into the initial population. Also, three local search operators are introduced to enhance scheduling quality. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed KAGA efficiently solves large-scale WPSP instances with complex constraints. Comparative experiments with state-of-the-art algorithms demonstrate in makespan, the KAGA achieves 23 best solutions in 30 instances of small, medium and large scale. This research offers a practical solution for the WPSP in semiconductor fabrication.
Keywords: Adaptive | Meta-heuristic | Production scheduling | Semiconductor manufacturing | Wafer probing

Title: Depth map filtering method for shape-from-focus recovery based on hybrid network model
Abstract: Shape-from-focus (SFF) is an economically efficient 3D shape recovery technology. As a core module of 3D digital microscopes, its primary goal is to acquire high-quality depth maps. However, the performance of such technology is highly dependent on the richness of image textures, which inevitably introduces noise into the generated depth maps and seriously impairs their quality. This has become a critical technical challenge in the field. To address this problem, this paper proposes a depth map filtering framework based on a hybrid network model. First, a depth reconstruction method combining the full width at half maximum (FWHM) and Gaussian fitting is designed to generate the initial depth map. Second, a hybrid network model for focus signal classification is constructed, which extracts the differential features of different signals to identify focus signals with noise patterns and generate a flag matrix. Finally, the initial depth map is filtered based on this flag matrix to obtain a high-quality depth map. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively distinguish the patterns of focus signals, filter out depth map noise caused by signal distortion, and simultaneously preserve the integrity of structural details in the depth map, exhibiting excellent filtering performance. In addition, the method proposed in this paper can serve as a general SFF framework, which is applicable to 3D shape measurement or high-end instrument design in different fields.
Keywords: Deep learning | Depth estimation | Depth map enhancement | Microscopic objects | Shape from focus

Title: LFMCA-Net: A lightweight retinal vessel segmentation method based on adaptive edge perception and multi-stage feature fusion
Abstract: Segmenting retinal vessels is essential for the auxiliary diagnosis of fundus-related disorders. To address limitations in existing methods such as high model complexity, insufficient contextual information fusion, and weak edge perception, we propose a lightweight retinal vessel segmentation network named LFMCA-Net. The network aims to accurately extract fine-grained vascular structures through the integration of several efficient modules. First, we introduce a Lightweight Detail Enhancement Block (LDEB) to replace U-Net’s basic skip connections, enhancing edge and detail representation via separable convolution and attention mechanisms. Second, a Cross Feature Refinement Fusion Module (CFRFM) is designed to promote effective multi-level information interaction through cross-scale fusion and local feature enhancement. Third, we propose an Adaptive Feature Fusing Block (AFFB) that performs dynamic weighting to integrate cross-scale outputs, enabling the model to adapt to both coarse and fine vessel structures. Additionally, an adaptive weighted combination loss function (ATCE-Dice Loss) is presented to strengthen supervision during training by dynamically balancing multiple loss terms via learnable parameters, which enhances the detection of vessel edges and small branches. Experimental results on public datasets including DRIVE, STARE, and CHASEDB1 demonstrate that LFMCA-Net achieves competitive segmentation performance with reduced computational complexity, indicating its potential for clinical and mobile applications.
Keywords: Adaptive feature fusion | Detail enhancement | Edge perception | Multi-stage feature extraction | Retinal vessel segmentation

Title: Predicting thermal diffusivity of materials using laser induced thermal images with machine learning
Abstract: Accurate, non-contact measurements of thermal diffusivity continue to be challenging. Conventional methods often require intrusive setups, careful sample preparation, or expensive instrumentation. In this study, an innovative method is proposed to determine thermal diffusivity. A laser is employed to non-intrusively heat a material surface, and then an infrared camera captures the resultant temperature distribution, which is processed by machine learning (ML) to predict thermal diffusivity. Since ML requires a large dataset, therefore, in order to test this hypothesis COMSOL Multiphysics software was utilized to generate the dataset using a validated model. The ML hybrid algorithms are based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) combined with four other regressors. Additionally, parametric studies on reflectivity and convection coefficient are conducted, and the approach is also compared to a nondimensional analysis method to predict thermal diffusivity. The results showed that for the main analysis, all hybrid models can predict the thermal diffusivity except for eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) model. The combination of CNN with Random Forest (RF) and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) showed the best performance. The CNN algorithm showed strong performance in predicting thermal diffusivity for the reflectivity and convection coefficient studies. Moreover, the results of the direct method showed higher prediction accuracy compared to the nondimensional analysis. The study demonstrates a fully non-intrusive approach to predict thermal diffusivity from temperature distributions. The procedure suggests a potential device concept that captures post-heating thermograms, applies a trained ML model to the images, and outputs thermal diffusivity, thereby simplifying existing experimental setups.
Keywords: Convolutional neural networks | Dimensionless analysis | Infrared thermography | Laser heating | Machine learning | Thermal diffusivity | Thermal properties

Title: Dual-task network with attention-guided U-net and gradient-based adaptive weighting optimization for fetal ultrasound plane classification and biometric measurement (DTNAU-Net)
Abstract: Automated fetal biometric analysis is essential for early diagnosis of growth-related abnormalities. This study presents the Dual-Task Network with Attention-Guided U-Net (DTNAU-Net), a novel deep learning architecture integrating Residual Blocks, Dual Attention Mechanisms, Multi-Scale Feature Extraction, and Gradient-Based Adaptive Weighting Optimization for simultaneous fetal ultrasound segmentation and classification of fetal ultrasound planes. Ablation studies demonstrated that each component significantly contributed to the model, and ultimately achieved Dice Index of 91.12% and classification accuracy of 94.85%. Comparative analysis against existing state-of-the-art deep learning models on the HC18 and Zenodo datasets confirmed DTNAU-Net’s superiority, with statistically significant improvements in segmentation accuracy (Dice Index of 91.12% ± 0.20) and classification performance (F1 Score of 94.30% ± 0.12). Additionally, dual-task can reduce inference time by 0.12 sec/24 frames when used classification task to remove undesired frames vs applying segmentation-task on all the frames, making real-time ultrasound analysis more feasible. Statistical validation using Paired t-test, Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test, and Friedman Test reinforced these findings. Furthermore, Explainable AI techniques using Shapley Additive Explanations and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations confirmed DTNAU-Net’s interpretability by highlighting its focus on critical anatomical structures. These results demonstrate the model’s potential for robust, efficient, and clinically reliable fetal biometric assessment, aiding in the early diagnosis of conditions like intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) and macrosomia.
Keywords: Attention mechanism | Biometric measurement | Dual-task learning | Fetal ultrasound imaging | Multi-objective optimization | Segmentation and classification

Title: A multi-source precipitation blending method combining hydrological model-guided precipitation adjustment and double transfer learning-based data merging
Abstract: Precipitation blending has been established as an effective approach for enhancing quantitative precipitation estimation accuracy. However, conventional precipitation blending methods exhibit two inherent limitations: (1) poor applicability in regions with sparse rain gauge networks; and (2) degraded estimation performance due to insufficient accuracy of input data sources. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multi-source precipitation blending (MSPB) method to integrate three datasets—ground, gridded precipitation, and auxiliary meteorological datasets—characterized by high spatiotemporal resolution and real-time capability. The methodology involves: (1) preprocessing all datasets into standardized input–output structures; (2) implementing an HBV-guided precipitation adjustment (HBV_PA) model to enhance data quality; (3) developing a double transfer learning (DTL) model using the corrected datasets to generate the blended precipitation product; and (4) conducting comprehensive performance evaluation against comparative objects, with demonstration through a case study in the source area of the Yellow River (YRSA). The evaluation metrics include probability of detection (POD), false alarm ratio (FAR), and critical success index (CSI) for event detection, as well as the Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE), Kling-Gupta efficiency (KGE), and root mean square error (RMSE) for quantitative assessment. Results demonstrate that HBV_PA-adjusted precipitation products significantly outperform the three original sources (IMERG-Late, GSMaP-Gauge, and ERA5-Land) across most statistical metrics in both temporal and spatial dimensions. Following the application of DTL to fuse HBV_PA-adjusted multi-source precipitation inputs, the MSPB method exhibits enhanced rainy-event detection performance (POD = 0.87 ± 0.01, FAR = 0.23 ± 0.01, CSI = 0.69 ± 0.01) alongside optimal precipitation quantification capabilities (NSE = 0.46 ± 0.02, KGE = 0.62 ± 0.01, RMSE = 2.28 ± 0.04), and outperforms other multi-source precipitation products and benchmark methods. Benchmark experiments conducted in the Tangnaihai–Lanzhou reach (TLR) further confirm that the proposed DTL model outperforms all benchmark methods by effectively leveraging extra-basin information, offering a superior solution for reliable estimation in data-sparse basins. Contribution analysis further reveals distinctive functional roles of input data sources in merging performance, confirming the substantial contribution of multi-source precipitation data and auxiliary meteorological information to precipitation estimation accuracy. This study establishes the MSPB method as a scalable solution for developing high-precision precipitation products. By integrating physically meaningful adjustments with a powerful transfer learning capability, the framework achieves robust predictive performance while effectively overcoming the critical challenge of in-situ data scarcity in sparsely gauged basins.
Keywords: Double transfer learning (DTL) | HBV-guided precipitation adjustment (HBV_PA) | Precipitation blending | The source area of the Yellow River (YRSA)

Title: A novel multi-scale Bayesian-KAN model for PV defect detection
Abstract: The use of AI techniques to detect defects in photovoltaic electroluminescence (EL) images is becoming increasingly important. However, most existing AI-based models fail to fully capture the diversity of defect types present in EL images, resulting in suboptimal detection performance for small defects such as linear cracks, star cracks, and so on. In this work, a novel defect segmentation framework is proposed, which integrates Bayesian Neural Networks (BNN) and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KAN) into an enhanced U-shaped architecture. The proposed model is an encoder-decoder architecture. First, a multi-scale Bayesian module (MSBM) is designed to allow the encoder to learn weight distributions instead of deterministic convolution kernels, thereby enhancing robustness and predictive reliability. Second, a KAN-based Feature Mining (KFM) module is introduced to learn complex nonlinear mappings in place of conventional linear combinations, providing more effective representations of diverse defect patterns. Furthermore, a specialized decoder is incorporated to efficiently fuse multi-scale features, balancing accuracy and inference speed for practical deployment. Extensive experiments on two public PV defect datasets show that the proposed method outperforms baselines in five metrics, achieving a 5.1% and 7.1% improvement in the IOU metric on two datasets. Overall, the proposed method combines deep uncertainty modeling with photovoltaic defect detection, which is crucial for reliable large-scale solar deployment. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/limiaoair/PVdefect.
Keywords: Bayesian network | Defect detection | Electroluminescence | Kolmogorov-Arnold network | Photovoltaic

Title: A deep learning feature mapping algorithm for emotion detection via facial and audio signals
Abstract: Automatic emotion recognition plays a critical role in areas such as mental-health monitoring, human–robot interaction, and personalised learning systems, yet current multimodal approaches often struggle with high intra-class variability and the limited discriminative power of raw audio–visual features. Existing methods typically rely on direct classification of audio or facial data, which does not explicitly enforce a structured joint embedding in which emotional categories become separable. This paper addresses this limitation by proposing a supervised contrastive feature-mapping algorithm that transforms temporal audio and video features into a representation that minimises intra-class distances while maximising inter-class distances. In contrast to prior work, which usually focuses on handcrafted feature engineering or end-to-end classifiers, our approach explicitly learns a discriminative metric space that enhances the geometry of the feature distribution. The method is evaluated on the RAVDESS and CREMA-D benchmark datasets. Experimental results show that the proposed mapping yields consistent accuracy improvements over strong machine-learning baselines, with gains of up to approximately 6%, achieving 96.07% accuracy on RAVDESS and competitive performance on CREMA-D, while outperforming or matching recent state-of-the-art multimodal emotion-recognition pipelines. Statistical tests (Kruskal–Wallis and paired t-tests) confirm that the learned representation significantly increases class separability (p<10<sup>−5</sup>). While the method assumes the availability of paired audio–visual inputs without requiring explicit temporal alignment, the learned feature space is compact, discriminative, and well suited to downstream tasks such as affect-aware dialogue systems, rehabilitation monitoring, and adaptive educational interfaces. These results demonstrate that contrastive feature mapping provides a robust and generalisable framework for multimodal emotion analysis.
Keywords: Affective computing | Deep learning | Emotion detection | Signal processing

Title: SurgiFormer: A multi-scale vision transformer for precise surgical instrument segmentation
Abstract: Robot-assisted and autonomous robotic surgeries critically rely on accurate and real-time segmentation of surgical instruments. Precise and efficient segmentation in complex, dynamic surgical environments remains challenging. Therefore, the need for models that offer both high precision and computational efficiency remains critical for Surgical Instrument Segmentation (SIS). To address these challenges, this study introduces SurgiFormer, a compute-efficient vision transformer-based segmentation network designed for real-time applications with a focus on precise edge segmentation. By utilizing a pre-trained Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVTv2) backbone with a reduced number of encoder and decoder stages, SurgiFormer achieves a compute-efficient architecture suitable for real-time processing on standard GPU hardware. The model incorporates novel components, such as the Multi-Scale Attention Convolution Unit (MSACU) and the Scale-Aware Feature Transformer (SAFT) with Hybrid Contextual Hierarchical Attention (HyCoHA), enabling it to capture both global dependencies and local spatial information, including fine details at the instrument edges, across multiple scales. Additionally, Hybrid Boundary Aware Loss (HBAL) and mosaic augmentation enhance the model’s performance in segmenting instruments from the background. Evaluated on three surgical instrument datasets, SurgiFormer demonstrates superior performance over current state-of-the-art methods, showcasing its effectiveness in advancing surgical instrument segmentation.
Keywords: Deep learning | Surgical instrument segmentation Robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery | Vision transformer

Title: MFformer: Time series forecasting via Fourier transform and meta-learning routing
Abstract: Long-term time series forecasting remains challenging when data are noisy and temporal patterns evolve over time. We propose MFformer, an adaptive multi-scale forecasting model. MFformer integrates a Fourier transform module, a meta-learning routing module, and an adaptive multi-scale modeling module. The Fourier module extracts frequency-domain information to capture periodic patterns. The routing module assigns weights to candidate scales and selects the Top-K scales for weighted aggregation. We evaluate MFformer on seven benchmark datasets: ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, Weather, Traffic, and ILI. All datasets are split chronologically into training, validation, and test sets. We adopt a ratio of 6:2:2 for the ETT datasets and 7:1:2 for the remaining datasets. Experimental results show that MFformer achieves competitive performance across most forecasting horizons. The performance gains are more pronounced on strongly periodic datasets such as ETTh2 and ETTm2.
Keywords: Deep learning | Fourier transform | Meta-learning routing | Multi-scale modeling | Time series prediction

Title: Linear-complexity global context modeling and cross-scale feature alignment for automated pseudomyxoma peritonei segmentation
Abstract: Precise segmentation of diffusely disseminated lesions in Pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) from computed tomography (CT) images presents a formidable clinical challenge. This challenge stems from the disease’s characteristically widespread and heterogeneous dissemination, and is further compounded by frequently ambiguous lesion boundaries. Conventional deep learning models encounter inherent limitations when addressing this task. On one hand, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), while proficient at local feature extraction, are constrained by limited receptive fields, which impedes effective modeling of long-range spatial dependencies crucial for capturing the full extent of PMP’s global dissemination. On the other hand, although standard Transformer architectures can capture global context via self-attention, their quadratic computational complexity becomes prohibitive for high-resolution medical imaging, while potentially compromising the fine-grained textural details essential for precise boundary delineation. To resolve this inherent trade-off among global context modeling, local detail fidelity, and computational efficiency, we propose a novel hybrid encoder–decoder framework. The encoder synergistically integrates convolutional modules with an efficient additive attention mechanism, enabling simultaneous capture of high-fidelity local details and long-range global dependencies with linear complexity. Its hierarchical decoder further leverages a dual cross-attention fusion strategy to align multi-scale features, thereby enhancing the delineation of ambiguous lesion boundaries. Evaluated on a real-world clinical PMP CT cohort (55 patients; 13,864 slices) under patient-level five-fold cross-validation, the proposed method achieves leading performance with mDice = 95.55  ±  0.67% and mIoU = 91.73  ±  1.15%, together with markedly improved boundary fidelity (HD95 = 6.22  ±  1.57, ASSD = 1.86  ±  0.46), significantly outperforming competing segmentation architectures. These results demonstrate the considerable promise of the proposed methodology as a clinical instrument to refine PMP assessment and support therapeutic decision-making.
Keywords: Additive attention | Deep learning | Medical image segmentation | Multi-scale feature fusion | Pseudomyxoma peritonei

Title: AMFU-Net: A multi-scale attention network for lesion segmentation in fused breast ultrasound imaging
Abstract: Breast lesions represent a serious threat to women's health, highlighting the need for accurate and efficient diagnostic imaging techniques. Since no single imaging modality can fully characterize breast tissue, ultrasound computed tomography (USCT) combines reflection and transmission imaging to provide complementary structural and acoustic information. This paper proposes a novel fusion strategy based on the HIS discrete wavelet transform, optimized via the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, to integrate reflection and transmission images into a fused breast ultrasound imaging containing both modalities’ salient features. To further improve lesion segmentation performance, we introduce AMFU-Net—an Attention-guided Multi-scale Feature Extraction and Fusion Network. AMFU-Net incorporates a Multi-scale Feature Extraction and Fusion (MFEF) module at the bottleneck layer and a Dual-branch Attention Gate (DAG) in the encoder–decoder skip connections, enabling adaptive weighting and enhanced cross-scale contextual feature integration. Experimental evaluations were performed on a clinical breast USCT dataset consisting of 215 annotated slices from 210 patients, which was partitioned into training, validation, and test sets in an 8:1:1 ratio. AMFU-Net achieved a Dice coefficient of 91.42%, outperforming the classical U-Net by 2.36%. This work provides a comprehensive solution that synergistically combines multimodal image fusion and advanced deep segmentation, offering significant potential for accurate breast lesion diagnosis and clinical decision support.
Keywords: AMFU-net | Breast ultrasound tomosynthesis | Deep learning | Image fusion | Semantic segmentation

Title: ShuffleNet-AGWO-ALM: Smart insoles-based body weight estimation via ShuffleNet with AGWO and ALM strategies
Abstract: Background and Objective: Body weight (BW) is a key health indicator associated with obesity, cachexia, and musculoskeletal rehabilitation. Traditional weighing scales lack portability and real-time capability. This study proposes a deep learning (DL) method for predicting BW using plantar pressure data from smart insoles, enabling real-time monitoring to support personalized rehabilitation and long-term health management. Methods: A pair of wireless insoles, each side with a 13-channel capacitive pressure sensor array, was employed to collect plantar pressure data. The ShuffleNet-based model was trained to estimate BW. To improve BW estimation accuracy, the Adaptive Gray Wolf Optimization (AGWO) was employed for parameter initialization. Besides, the Augmented Lagrange Multiplier (ALM) method was utilized to impose prior knowledge constraints. The ShuffleNet-ALM-AGWO model was subjected to training and evaluation using standard regression metrics, including root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE). Results: The proposed model achieves a MAE of 0.84 kg and a RMSE of 1.09, with a coefficient of determination (R<sup>2</sup>) exceeding 0.99, demonstrating strong explanatory capability. The performance of ShuffleNet-AGWO-ALM exceeds that of other lightweight models such as MobileNet and EfficientNet, and reduces estimation error by 80% in comparison with the latest related studies. Moreover, the ShuffleNet-AGWO-ALM model performs consistently across various standing postures, demonstrating robustness and cross-posture generalization. Conclusions: This study proposes a methodology for the objective measurement of body weight, utilizing smart insoles in conjunction with a DL framework. This methodology for real-time, convenient, and mobile BW estimation has the potential to facilitate intelligent weight management and rehabilitation.
Keywords: Body weight | Deep learning | Lagrange multiplier | Smart insoles | Weight estimation

Title: CatSeg: A holistic cataract surgical scene segmentation model
Abstract: Cataract surgery is the primary treatment for cataracts and requires precise surgical skills that are critical for successful outcomes. To enhance the training of new surgeons, automated analysis of surgical videos can provide valuable feedback, particularly in identifying instruments and anatomical structures. However, current segmentation methods often fail to accurately identify these components with consistent performance, which limits their effectiveness as training tools. To address this, we propose CatSeg, an advanced surgical scene segmentation model designed to improve the accuracy of both instrument and anatomical segmentation during cataract surgery. CatSeg employs a pyramidal convolution backbone and a Multi-Scale Instrument Feature Attention (MSIFA) module, enhancing edge feature preservation for better instrument identification. Evaluated on the Cataract-1k and CaDIS benchmarks, CatSeg achieved an improved mean IoU of +8.13% (0.8107 → 0.8920) and +1.35% (0.8670 → 0.8805), respectively. With an efficient operation speed of 6.35 to 7.66 frames per second, CatSeg is well-suited for surgical video analysis, paving the way for enhanced training and analysis in the development of new surgeons. Source code is available at: https://github.com/Muraam-Abdel-Ghani/CatSeg/.
Keywords: Anterior segment structures | Cataract surgical segmentation | Deep learning | Holistic scene segmentation | Intraocular lens | Multi-scale attention | Pyramidal convolution

Title: SAVI-cracker: A hybrid deep learning model for enhanced lung disease classification
Abstract: This paper reports SAVI-Cracker (Semi-supervised Adaptive Vision Integration Cracker), a hybrid deep learning knowledge of version that combines better architectures, and the Nutcracker function extraction set of rules to enhance diagnostic accuracy of diseases, including most cancers, COVID-19, allergies, emphysema, tuberculosis (TB) and normal lung conditions by way of combining SaganNet, ZonNet, VISAM and SleekNet with semi supervised getting to know. That version transfers the Adam optimizer to ensure green schooling and faster convergence simultaneously and the Nutcracker set of rules isolates key functions, reducing information dimensionality and enhancing computation speeds. The outcome of the experiment shows that SAVI-Cracker has a diagnostic accuracy of 98.37, which is better than the precision of traditional model, bear in mind, and F1 rating. The semi-supervised approach allows the model to make correct extrapolation of the restrained categorized knowledge, making it a powerful instrument of detecting lung disorder at its early and precise stages. The results suggest that the SAVI-Cracker model reveals much potential of scientific implementation providing healthcare workers with a sophisticated tool of increasing the effects of diagnostics.
Keywords: Adam Optimizer | Cancer | Nut-Cracker | Sleeknet

Title: HiDC-QRS: A Hierarchical Dilated Convolutional Network for efficient QRS detection in 1-second single-lead ECG
Abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) plays a crucial role in detecting cardiovascular diseases, yet precise QRS complex delineation in ultrashort (e.g., 1-second) recordings remains an open challenge. Existing methods, which typically focus on R-peak detection or fixed-length segmentation, fail to achieve accurate boundary localization and require longer durations. To address these issues, we propose HiDC-QRS, a Hierarchical Dilated Convolutional Network featuring a principled re-design of feature hierarchy and learning dynamics. The innovations are twofold: (1) a hierarchical dilated convolution scheme tailored for one-dimensional ECG to natively capture multi-scale temporal features, with each encoder layer characterizing distinct ECG components, thereby forming a physiologically interpretable feature hierarchy; and (2) a novel weighted output aggregation mechanism that explicitly balances the contributions of multi-scale feature representations and establishes direct gradient feedback paths during training, enabling joint optimization of all network layers for detecting a wide spectrum of waveform characteristics. In this work, we introduce a high-quality clinical dataset to evaluate HiDC-QRS and address the scarcity of ultrashort ECG resources. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, with a sensitivity of 0.970 and a positive predictive value of 0.995. Additionally, the proposed model demonstrates robust zero-shot learning across four public datasets, indicating its adaptability and potential for clinical application. We make our dataset and code publicly available on https://github.com/neu2270Ma/HiDC-QRS/releases.
Keywords: 1-second single-lead ECG | Deep learning for biomedical signals | Electrocardiography (ECG) | QRS complex detection

Title: Tape-assisted nanoplasmonic biosensors for facile protein-on-chip visualization and multiplexed point-of-care diagnostics
Abstract: Visual point-of-care testing (POCT) technologies convert biomolecular events into naked-eye readable signals. These systems offer rapid assay times, user-friendly operation, and eliminate the need for specialized instruments, making them particularly valuable for clinical diagnosis, public health emergency response, and post-operative monitoring. Here, we report a tape-assisted plasmon-enabled (TAPE) sensor, which enables direct naked-eye visualization of protein-on-chip via a simple “physical” pasting step. Minimal thickness variations were transduced into visible signals through the plasmonic coupling effect. TAPE sensors enable highly sensitive, label-free protein quantification over a seven-order-of-magnitude dynamic range, as demonstrated by the accurate detection of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). The Limit of Confirmation (LoC) for detection of HBsAg is 2.80 ng mL<sup>−1</sup>. This diagnostic capability extends to practical POCT applications, enabling the successful quantification of HBsAg in unprocessed whole blood (10 μL) within 30 min. Rigorous clinical validation, utilizing over 500 human serum samples, confirmed the reliability and robustness of this platform. Beyond single-analyte detection, the TAPE sensor exhibits remarkable versatility by enabling simultaneous high-throughput detection of six viral biomarkers (antigens and antibodies). Coupled with smartphone imaging and machine learning, this system offers a user-friendly diagnostic strategy. These features establish the TAPE sensor as a promising platform for advanced POCT diagnostics.
Keywords: Machine learning | Multiplexed detection | Naked-eye visualization | Plasmonic biosensors | Point-of-care testing (POCT)

Title: PE-YOLO: An efficient segmentation algorithm for surgical instruments in percutaneous spinal endoscopic surgery
Abstract: The application of deep learning technology in the medical field continues to gain momentum, especially in the precise segmentation of surgical instruments. However, current algorithms primarily focus on common surgical instruments, and there is still a lack of effective solutions for the challenge of determining the contours of instruments in percutaneous spinal endoscopic surgery. To address this issue, this article constructed a dataset that includes surgical instruments for seven different surgical postures. A highly efficient segmentation algorithm called PE-YOLO is proposed to address the uncertainty of instrument edges caused by partial occlusion in the internal environment during percutaneous endoscopic spinal surgery. This algorithm optimizes the issue of shallow information loss due to the relatively large proportion of surgical instrument pixels by introducing the CDBB feature extraction module. At the same time, it employs a cross-layer feature fusion path to enhance the preservation of edge information. Experimental results demonstrate that the PE-YOLO algorithm achieves a 4.1% improvement over existing algorithms in both mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 evaluation metrics, with only a 1ms increase in algorithm inference time, providing a new and effective method for the precise segmentation of surgical instruments in percutaneous spinal endoscopic surgery.
Keywords: Deep learning | Percutaneous spinal endoscopic surgery | Surgical instruments segmentation | YOLO

Title: An audit of machine learning experiments on software defect prediction
Abstract: Background: Machine learning algorithms are increasingly being proposed to solve the problem of predicting defect-prone software components. In this literature, computational experiments are the primary means of evaluating and comparing learners and the credibility of findings depends critically on their experimental design and reporting. Objective: This paper audits recent software defect prediction (SDP) experiments by assessing their experimental design, analysis and reporting practices against widely accepted norms from statistics, machine learning and empirical software engineering. Our aim is to characterise the current state of practice and evaluate the reproducibility of published findings. Method: We undertook an audit of relevant studies published from the SCOPUS database (2019-2023) focusing on their experimental design and analysis choices e.g., the outcome variables such as F-measure and the type of out of sample (OOS) validation regime, e.g., cross-validation, plus the statistical analysis and inference mechanisms. In all, we evaluated nine different study issues. This was complemented by an assessment of reproducibility using the instrument proposed by González-Barahona and Robles. Results: Our search located approximately 1,585 experiments in SDP (2019-2023), a substantial body of work. From this, we randomly sampled 101 () papers, 61 journal and 40 conference papers. Almost 50% are behind ‘paywalls’. We found considerable divergence in research practice. The number of datasets used ranged 1-365, the number of learners or learner variants evaluated from 1-34 and the number of performance metrics from 1 to 9. Approximately 45% of papers made use of formal statistical inference. We detected a total of 427 issues distributed across 101 papers (median=4) with only one paper being entirely issue-free. In terms of reproducibility, experiments ranged from near perfect to lacking almost all required information. We also found two examples of tortured phrases and potential “paper mill” activity. Conclusions: Approaches to designing and reporting computational experiments varied greatly, but almost half the studies provided insufficient information such that reproduction would be challenging. Overall, our audit suggests that as a research community, we have considerable scope for improvement. Fortunately, many improvements should be neither difficult nor costly to achieve.
Keywords: Audit | Machine learning | Research review | Software defect

Title: Significance of Technical Indicators in the Era of Machine Learning
Abstract: This paper examines the significance of technical indicators in the context of machine learning. We commence by constructing a machine learning–based cross-sectional asset pricing model that incorporates 124 previously identified asset pricing characteristics and fourteen macroeconomic factors. Subsequently, we assess widely regarded technical indicators in their ability to influence machine learning–based model accuracy. Our findings indicate that Bollinger Bands, moving averages, momentum reversal, MIN–MAX retracement, trender, and the parabolic time/price system have a significant influence on the predictability of machine learning–based models. Interestingly, we find that a well-curated machine learning model with technical indicators is comparable in performance to models with much larger asset pricing characteristics. We also document a time-varying phenomenon in the predictability of asset pricing models. Finally, long–short portfolio analysis suggests that active investment using technical indicators and machine learning can yield positive alpha.
Keywords: asset pricing | explainable AI | machine learning | SHAP | technical indicators

Title: Interpretable machine learning framework for predicting cement adhesive bond strength in NSM FRP systems using differential evolution and SHAP analysis
Abstract: This study presents a robust and interpretable machine learning framework for predicting the average bond strength (τ<inf>avg</inf>) of cement-based adhesives in Near-Surface Mounted (NSM) FRP systems. Four state-of-the-art ensemble algorithms were evaluated on a dataset of 150 experimental tests using a rigorous nested cross-validation protocol and Differential Evolution for hyperparameter optimization. A key aspect of the framework is the explicit engineering of interaction terms to model physical synergies. The optimized LightGBM model emerged as the superior predictor, achieving a mean R² of 0.42 on unseen test data while fitting the training data with an R² of 0.79. This contrast reflects the high heterogeneity of the aggregated dataset. A SHAP analysis revealed that engineered interaction terms were the most influential predictors across all models, with the interplay between groove depth and surface treatment (d<inf>g</inf> · Treatment) consistently highly ranked. For the best-performing LightGBM model specifically, the synergy between surface treatment and FRP tensile strength (f<inf>frp</inf>) proved most dominant. These findings highlight that the predictive power of primary variables is significantly enhanced when their complex interdependencies are explicitly modeled. This work provides a transparent, methodologically rigorous framework that serves as both a predictive tool and an instrument for scientific insight into NSM FRP bond mechanics.
Keywords: Bond strength | Cement adhesives | Differential evolution | Machine learning | NSM FRP | SHAP analysis

Title: Machine learning combined with sensory evaluation and multi-sensor technology to evaluate the overall quality of commercial soybean paste in China
Abstract: Soybean paste has been a prominent condiment in East Asia for millennia. Nonetheless, the current methodologies for comprehensively assessing the quality of commercially available soybean paste through sensory evaluation or traditional instruments present significant challenges. In this study, contemporary detection techniques and machine learning methodologies were employed to quantitatively characterize and evaluate the overall quality of soybean paste. Sensory evaluations were conducted on 33 varieties of commercial soybean paste using three types of sensors: a colorimeter, an electronic nose (E-nose), and an electronic tongue (E-tongue) for detection purposes. Subsequently, machine learning models, including Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest (RF), extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Bayesian Ridge Regression (BRR), Ridge Regression (RR), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) were developed based on the sensory evaluation data to characterize and assess the overall quality of the soybean paste. The findings from both sensory evaluations and sensor detection indicated notable differences between the various soybean pastes. Soybean pastes can be distinguished using three sensors. The quantitative characterization model informed by the sensor data revealed that the SVR model exhibited the highest R² value of 0.9998 for the training set and 0.997 for the test set, which was close to the ideal value of 1. Additionally, the root mean square error (RMSE) for the test set was the lowest at 0.5359. These results suggest that SVR demonstrates superior performance in cross-validation and testing, aligning closely with human sensory perceptions, thereby establishing it as the most effective predictive model. This study underscores the potential of integrating sensor data with modern machine learning techniques to supplement traditional sensory evaluations for comprehensive characterization and assessment of soybean paste quality. The outcomes of this study offer significant insights and guidance for the advancement of the soybean paste industry and the enhancement of soybean paste quality.
Keywords: Aroma | Color | Machine learning | Sensor Detection | Sensory evaluation | Soybean paste | Taste

Title: Spectral-spatial co-learning with adaptive multi-scale calibration for industrial coating defect detection
Abstract: Surface defect detection plays a critical role in modern manufacturing quality control systems. However, existing deep learning methods face significant challenges in industrial coating inspection: texture-type defects manifest as subtle anomalies that are difficult to distinguish from complex reflective backgrounds, while the multi-scale variations of defects require adaptive feature fusion strategies beyond fixed-weight approaches. Moreover, the lack of publicly available coating-specific datasets has hindered the development of tailored detection algorithms for coating processes. To address these limitations, we propose FreqDETR, a novel framework that systematically integrates frequency-domain enhancement mechanisms with adaptive multi-scale calibration, and contribute a specialized benchmark for coating defect detection. Specifically, this work makes three main contributions: (1) We design the Spectral-Spatial Feature Enhancement Stage (SSFES) that embeds three synergistic frequency-domain modules into the backbone network, capturing textural anomalies and geometric discontinuities through spectral analysis. (2) We construct ICD-4, the first publicly available industrial coating defect dataset, containing 3,099 annotated instances across four representative defect types collected from real-world coating production lines, filling a critical gap in coating quality inspection research. (3) We propose the Adaptive Multi-scale Feature Calibration (AMFC) module that dynamically adjusts the contribution of each scale through cross-scale attention interaction and adaptive weight prediction. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance: FreqDETR achieves 94.1% AP<inf>50</inf> on ICD-4, 77.3% AP<inf>50</inf> on NEU-DET, 97.9% AP<inf>50</inf> on PCB, and 63.1% AP<inf>50</inf> on CSDD, outperforming existing methods while maintaining real-time inference capability. This work demonstrates that frequency-spatial co-learning provides more discriminative feature representations for industrial defect detection.
Keywords: Deep learning | Frequency-domain enhancement | Multi-scale feature calibration | Surface defect detection

Title: In-orbit GRB Identification Using an LLM-based Model for the CXPD CubeSat
Abstract: To validate key technologies for wide field-of-view (FOV) X-ray polarization measurements, the Cosmic X-ray Polarization Detector CubeSat series has been developed as a prototype platform for the Low-Energy X-ray Polarization Detector onboard the POLAR-2 mission. The wide-FOV design significantly increases the complexity of the background environment, posing notable challenges for real-time gamma-ray burst (GRB) identification. In this work, we propose an in-orbit GRB identification method based on machine learning, using simulated spectral data as input. A training dataset was constructed using a Geant4-based simulator, incorporating in-orbit background and GRB events modeled within the 2–10 keV energy range. To meet the computational constraints of onboard processing, we employ a multimodal large language model, which is fine-tuned using low-rank adaptation based on miniCPM-V2.6 and quantized to 4-bit precision. The model achieves perfect classification accuracy on validation data and demonstrates strong regression performance in estimating GRB spectral indices, with a root mean square error of 0.118. Furthermore, we validate the feasibility of onboard deployment through a simulated satellite data processing pipeline, highlighting the potential of our approach to enable future real-time GRB detection and spectral analysis in orbit.
Keywords: (stars:) gamma-ray burst: general | methods: data analysis | space vehicles: instruments

Title: Symptom-based machine learning framework for screening hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism
Abstract: Screening for adult thyroid disorders remains challenging as conventional symptom-based screening methods lack sufficient diagnostic accuracy. Furthermore, most existing machine learning (ML) approaches rely heavily on invasive laboratory inputs, which makes them impractical for routine use. This study addresses these gaps by proposing a non-invasive symptom-based ML framework that delivers an interpretable risk calculator for accurate screening of thyroid disorders in settings where regular systematic TSH-based screening is not implemented. The framework integrates population-specific reference intervals to carefully label each instance with the appropriate thyroid class. A multidimensional set of input features, including demographics, family history, symptoms, aggregated symptom scores, and predicted thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels, was utilized to train and test a sequence of binary classifiers to identify patients with hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism in both subclinical and overt conditions. Among the implemented models, the XGBoost classifier demonstrated superior, consistent performance compared with the others. The Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) enhances model interpretability by revealing distinct feature patterns across classification tasks. Aggregated symptom scores stood as the most influential features across all models. The developed risk calculator not only outperformed conventional symptom-based screening methods but also revealed important clinical insights, highlighting the value of considering the aggregated impact of symptoms alongside predicted TSH levels to detect hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism. The presented methodological framework can be replicated across different populations in the Middle East or worldwide with appropriate local calibration, which will be the next step of our work. This will assist in using this tool as a screening aid until regular TSH screening is implemented for adult populations. Ultimately, the proposed symptom-based screening tool offers a time-efficient complement to laboratory testing that can support thyroid-disorder screening and management.
Keywords: Hyperthyroidism | Hypothyroidism | Non-Invasive | Symptom scores | Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone

Title: Deep ensemble learning for automated acoustic identification of bats: A case study on the SCAR dataset
Abstract: Bats serve as important bioindicators of ecosystem health, but their nocturnal and active flight behavior makes traditional monitoring challenging. Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) provides a scalable and non-invasive alternative, while species-level classification remains difficult due to call variability and limited reference datasets. Here, we developed the Sino-Chiroptera Acoustic Resource (SCAR), a large-scale echolocation call dataset covering 43 species of Chinese bats. Time–frequency features were extracted using the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), and multiple deep learning backbones were evaluated within a unified training pipeline. We further introduced IRPNet, a lightweight Inverted Residual Pyramid Network, and integrated it with ResNet18 and MobileNetV2 using probability-level soft voting (I ⊕ R ⊕ M). On the SCAR test set, the ensemble achieved 94.26% accuracy and an F1 score of 94.27%, outperforming individual models and improving robustness for acoustically similar and low-sample species. While the proposed framework shows strong performance, remaining challenges include species imbalance and geographic bias. We encourage further contributions to expand the dataset, which will enhance its generalizability across more species, regions, and diverse recording conditions. Overall, SCAR and the proposed modeling framework provide a practical resource for automated bat acoustic classification and biodiversity monitoring.
Keywords: Bat classification | Bioacoustics | Deep learning | Model ensemble | SCAR dataset

Title: PfAgo-guided SERS signal conversion for amplification-free and semi-quantitative detection of Salmonella typhimurium in food and physiological samples
Abstract: Rapid detection of foodborne pathogens is critical for food safety. Conventional qPCR offers high sensitivity but relies on nucleic acid amplification, increasing operational complexity and false-positive risks. Here, we developed a biosensor platform named PAF-SERS (PfAgo-mediated Amplification-Free Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Biosensor) for detecting Salmonella typhimurium (S. typhimurium) without pre-amplification. In this platform, PfAgo specifically cleaves target DNA guided by a single-stranded DNA guide, generating a linker sequence that enables quantitative detection through SERS signal conversion. The assay completes within 55 min, with a detection limit as low as 10 CFU/mL and a linear range of 10^1 to 10^7 CFU/mL, exhibiting high specificity and reproducibility. We further applied a support vector machine (SVM) algorithm to accurately classify low-concentration samples. The method was successfully validated in milk, eggs, chicken, and feces and blood from infected mice, demonstrating its potential for rapid, on-site detection without bulky instruments.
Keywords: Amplification-free detection | Foodborne pathogens | PfAgo | Salmonella typhimurium | SERS

Title: AI-optimized pulsed electric field for low-carbon urban water disinfection
Abstract: Urban water systems are critical hubs for the flow of carbon and materials in urban metabolism. Traditional disinfection methods, such as chlorination, face a dual challenge. On one hand, they rely on energy-intensive chemical production and transportation, resulting in significant indirect carbon emissions. On the other hand, they release disinfection by products that harm ecosystems and public health, which directly contradicts the “One Health” framework. To address these issues, we have developed a new disinfection platform centered around an AI-optimized pulsed electric field system. Using wide-bandgap semiconductor technology, the platform achieves high-frequency nanosecond pulse generation with up to 97% energy efficiency. Building on this, we conducted a systematic study on the inactivation mechanisms of resilient Bacillus and developed a key quantitative model. This model served as the foundation for building a dynamic AI adaptive control system that responds in real time to changes in water quality. Compared with fixed-parameter operation, the AI-guided mode maintained a high sterilization rate (72.3–81.8% inactivation) while reducing energy consumption by 15–25% and cutting performance variation by 47% in simulation tests. As a chemical-free process, this method eliminates the carbon footprint associated with traditional disinfectants and prevents the release of toxic byproducts. By combining precise physical disinfection with adaptive information technology, this study presents a sustainable, low-carbon solution for urban water management. Thus, the work may represent a step toward optimizing the flow of carbon and materials in cities.
Keywords: AI-Optimization | Bacillus spore inactivation | Carbon-neutral disinfection | Eco-informatics | One health | Pulsed electric field (PEF) | Silicon carbide devices | Urban metabolism

Title: TCN-MUSIC: Hybrid MUSIC-based deep network using temporal convolutions for DoA estimation
Abstract: Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation is a critical task in signal processing. Traditional model-based (MB) methods, such as MUSIC, often suffer from performance degradation under challenging conditions like low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), correlated signal environments, and array imperfections. To address these limitations, recent advancements have focused on hybrid model-based/data-driven (MB/DD) approaches that integrate deep learning with classical DoA estimation techniques. In this paper, we propose TCN-MUSIC, a novel hybrid method that combines Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) with the MUSIC algorithm. TCN-MUSIC leverages TCNs for feature extraction, enabling robust DoA estimation and source number classification. We demonstrate through extensive simulations that TCN-MUSIC outperforms classic MUSIC and state-of-the-art hybrid methods in terms of performance and computational efficiency, particularly in scenarios involving closely spaced sources, array imperfections, correlated signals, and one-bit quantization.
Keywords: DoA estimation | Hybrid model-based deep learning | MUSIC algorithm | Temporal convolutional networks (TCNs)

Title: DB-MLCNet: A dual-branch network for microbubble localization and counting in PFO assessment
Abstract: The quantitative evaluation of right-to-left shunt (RLS) in patent foramen ovale (PFO), a key pathological mechanism in cryptogenic stroke and paradoxical embolism, depends on microbubble detection via contrast-enhanced transthoracic echocardiography (cTTE) and contrast-enhanced transcranial Doppler (c-TCD). Traditional methods rely on manual expertise or optical instruments, which are prone to interference from microbubbles’ optical properties and suffer from low efficiency. Current technologies struggle to achieve both high-precision localization and counting of microbubbles, particularly lacking the capability for quantitative analysis of their dynamic spatiotemporal characteristics in ultrasound imaging. This study proposes a dual-branch deep learning network, DB-MLCNet, which establishes a microbubble distribution model by parallel learning of local details and global spatial dependencies in cTTE images. The model achieves precise localization and automated counting of microbubbles, and quantitatively assesses the severity of RLS based on microbubble counts. The experimental results demonstrate that DB-MLCNet achieves high-precision performance in microbubble detection, with both MAE and MSE evaluation metrics exhibiting superior performance. In the classification task for RLS shunt severity, the model's performance is comparable to that of mid-career physicians. The model demonstrates a high concordance (Accuracy: 82.76%) with the ground truth labels provided by senior experts. This level of performance suggests that the automated system can effectively support clinical decision-making by providing consistent, objective grading, thereby potentially reducing inter-observer variability.
Keywords: cTTE | Microbubble | PFO | RLS

Title: Respiratory rate estimation from breath sounds based on deep learning
Abstract: Objective: Respiratory rate (RR) is a fundamental vital sign for evaluating pulmonary and cardiovascular function, with demonstrated value in predicting short-term mortality and early clinical deterioration. As one of the most sensitive physiological indicators, RR often reflects physical and psychological imbalances prior to alterations in other vital signs. This study aims to develop a robust deep learning (DL)-based framework for RR estimation from respiratory sounds. Methods: A dedicated database for RR estimation was created, encompassing a wide range of simulated and real-world acoustic environments. Two data augmentation techniques, commonly used in audio processing but novel for this biomedical task, were applied to expand the size of RR breathing sound signals. The framework leverages pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for feature extraction from spectrograms, which are then used to estimate RR. The proposed method was evaluated against several state-of-the-art approaches, encompassing envelope-based methods, respiratory spectral activation models and neural network architectures such as CNNs and recurrent neural networks (RNNs). Results: In noisy acoustic conditions, ResNet50 outperformed all other approaches, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.63 breaths per minute (bpm) even at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of –20 dB. It was followed by the LSTM-based method (2.35 bpm) and the CNN-based method (3.12 bpm). Conclusion: Our findings reveal the limitations of existing approaches under severe acoustic degradation and underscore the robustness of ResNet50, which maintains low errors across RR ranges, noise levels, and all evaluated acoustic environments.
Keywords: Auscultation | Breaths per minute (bpm) | Data augmentation | Deep learning | ResNet50 | Respiratory rate

Title: Integration of item response theory and machine learning for automated prediction in occupational health and safety
Abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) of the upper limbs remain a significant concern in occupational health, and their assessment is generally based on subjective reports, limiting the consistency, scalability, and accuracy of ergonomic screening. This study proposes a methodological approach integrating Item Response Theory (IRT) and Machine Learning (ML) to enable automated classification of upper-limb musculoskeletal discomfort levels among workers. The sample consisted of 300 individuals assessed using a reliable and validated psychometric instrument (McDonald’s omega = 0.94; all items showed factor loadings and commonalities greater than 0.50). The IRT parameters enabled the construction of a hierarchical musculoskeletal discomfort scale comprising six levels, anchored in cumulative response probabilities and ranging from minimal to maximal discomfort. Six ML algorithms were trained to estimate individual discomfort levels based on IRT scale levels and WMSD symptoms. The Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieved the best performance, with an F1-score above 96% and low variability confirmed through 5,000 bootstrap resamples (standard deviation < 4%). Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis identified symptoms in the forearm and hand regions as key predictors of the outcome. The results demonstrate the feasibility of IRT–ML integration for automated ergonomic risk screening, reducing subjectivity and enabling robust, scalable, individualized analysis through combined psychometric and predictive power. This psychometric-computational approach functions as a data-driven surrogate expert system, embedding expert knowledge within a validated measurement model and operationalizing it through machine learning for scalable, individualized risk screening in Industry 4.0 environments.
Keywords: Applied psychometrics | Artificial intelligence | Automated classification | Ergonomics | WMSD

Title: Permutation-learning state-space model for distributed acoustic sensing recognition
Abstract: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) technology represents an innovative fiber-optic-based sensing methodology that enables real-time measurement and monitoring of acoustic signals through the detection of minute perturbations along optical fibers. This sensing approach offers compelling advantages, including extensive measurement ranges, exceptional spatial resolution, and an expansive dynamic measurement spectrum. The integration of machine learning (ML) paradigms presents transformative potential for DAS technology, particularly in improving measurement accuracy and reliability through advanced data processing preprocessing techniques, and advanced acoustic event classification and recognition. By leveraging ML algorithms, DAS systems can transition from traditional data processing methodologies to more automated and intelligent analytical frameworks. The computational intelligence afforded by ML-enhanced DAS technologies facilitates improved measurement consistency and reliability across diverse critical infrastructure sectors. Particularly noteworthy are the technology's applications in transportation infrastructure, energy management systems, and natural disaster monitoring frameworks, where accurate measurement and reliable interpretation of acoustic signals are essential. This research critically examines the comparative performance characteristics of classical machine learning methodologies and state-of-the-art deep learning models in the context of DAS data recognition and interpretation, offering comprehensive insights into the evolving landscape of intelligent sensing technologies.
Keywords: Acoustic event classification | Deep learning | Distributed acoustic sensing | Machine learning

Title: A Set of Data-Driven Models to Predict VS30 from the Horizontal-to-Vertical Spectral Ratio of Microtremors
Abstract: We investigate the use of microtremor horizontal-to-vertical spectral ratio (mHVSR) measurements to predict the time-averaged shear-wave velocity in the upper 30 m (V<inf>S30</inf> ) using data-driven machine learning models. We develop a global dataset comprising 2861 three-component ambient noise recordings made at 536 sites. We consider two different types of predictive models: low-dimensional models, which use mHVSR features such as the fundamental site frequency (f<inf>0,HVSR</inf> ) and amplitude (A<inf>0,HVSR</inf> ), and high-dimensional models, which use the entire lognormal median mHVSR curve to predict V<inf>S30</inf> . In addition, we integrate two topographic features: binned elevation, as a proxy for geologic composition, and topographic position index, as a proxy for topography features. The low-dimensional models are shown to reasonably approximate V<inf>S30</inf> when using mHVSR and the topographic features (coefficient of determination, R<sup>2</sup>, up to 0.69 on the testing set). The high-dimensional models outperform the low-dimensional models (R<sup>2</sup> of 0.82 on the testing set) regardless of whether the lognormal median mHVSR curve is supplemented by the topographic features. In addition, we show that our top-performing model outperforms a recently developed model to predict V<inf>S30</inf> from remote sensing data at sites from our testing set. Finally, we apply our models to predict V<inf>S30</inf> from mHVSR computed at 1855 permanent broadband sta-tions. We compare our data-driven V<inf>S30</inf> predictions at a subset of 156 stations with measured V<inf>S30</inf> values and find a reduction in the recommended model’s predictive power (R<sup>2</sup> of 0.18). The reduction in performance at permanent broadband stations is shown to be related in part to differences in instrument type and data distribution between the temporary and permanent broadband datasets. Therefore, the proposed models are expected to perform best when mHVSR is measured using temporary deployments of broadband sensors. All the data-driven models developed in this study have been made publicly available.

Title: Machine learning-based classification of active galaxies and estimation of supermassive black hole masses
Abstract: Distinguishing active galaxies from star-forming galaxies is essential for understanding galaxy evolution. Diagnostic methods like the BPT (Baldwin, Phillips, and Terlevich) diagram use optical emission-line ratios to separate galaxies. However, with growing availability of large surveys and high-resolution instruments, manually identifying galaxy types has become increasingly challenging. In this study, we investigate machine learning to classify active and star-forming galaxies using properties such as stellar mass, stellar velocity dispersion, colour, redshift, and [O III] luminosity.
