This survey offers a structured taxonomy of 2D image-to-audio generation models and outlines future research pathways for advancing spectrogram-guided synthesis using GANs and related deep learning frameworks.
Keywords: 2D image processing | Deep generative models | Diffusion models | Encoder-decoder architecture | Generative adversarial networks (GANs) | Image-to-audio synthesis | Multimodal learning | Spectrogram-based audio generation

Title: Machine Learning Advancements for Lung Cancer Detection: An In-Depth Review and Future Prospects
Abstract: Lung cancer is a major cause of cancer-related mortality globally, underscoring the necessity for efficient diagnostic instruments. The review paper summarizes the role of ML and DL in detection, staging, and prognostication of lung cancer. We evaluate the relative efficacy of several models, such as CNNs, SVMs, and ensemble approaches, by analyzing publically accessible imaging and molecular information. We emphasize difficulties including class imbalance, model interpretability, and generalizability across clinical environments. We also talk about new trends that could improve clinical translation, like vision transformers, explainable AI, and federated learning. This interdisciplinary approach highlights the revolutionary potential of AI-driven techniques in lung cancer therapy and delineates critical future research directions to enhance clinical integration.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | CNN | Explainable AI | Lung Cancer | Medical Image Processing

Title: A Comprehensive Framework for Deepfake Detection: Fusing Visual and Audio Modalities with Advanced Deep Learning Models
Abstract: The emergence of deepfake technology presents considerable challenges to multimedia authentication. This study introduces an innovative detection framework that analyses both visual and audio data. The methodology combines Convolutional Neural Networks in conjunction with Generative Adversarial Networks. Performance remains robust against sophisticated manipulation techniques. Strategic frame extraction reduces computational demands without sacrificing accuracy. Validation in the Deepfake Detection Challenge Dataset achieved 93.9% accuracy. The dual-modality approach addresses falsified content that undermines digital trust.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) | Deepfake Detection | Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) | Multi-modal Analysis | Video Frame Extraction

Title: Digital Competencies of Teaching Staff in Technical and Technological Education in Ecuador
Abstract: Digital competencies enable teachers to use digital technologies in their educational practice in a critical, creative, ethical, and effective way. These competencies include aspects like planning with technologies, creating digital content, evaluating in virtual environments, data protection, and promoting digital skills in students. This research aims to diagnose the level of teachers’ digital competencies based on the sixth area of the European Framework for the Digital Competence of Educators, specifically referencing the promotion of digital competencies in students. For this purpose, a self-assessment instrument was adapted with the help of artificial intelligence and applied as a case study to full-time teachers at the ITCA Higher Technological Institute. Factorial analyses showed high internal consistency and appropriate sample adequacy. The results indicate high levels of performance in basic skills, such as searching, evaluating, and organizing digital information, while showing lower performance in dimensions such as content creation, responsible use of technology, and problem-solving. This highlights a training gap in the development of digital competencies. Differences in standardized means were observed by self-perception level and gender gaps in various competencies. This research provides relevant empirical evidence on the viability of using the adapted framework to diagnose and evaluate digital competencies in technical and technological education teachers in the country. This can guide the improvement of educational processes and the establishment of institutional policies that promote contextualized adaptations.
Keywords: Digital skills | Educational planning | Educational policy | Educational reform | Information literacy

Title: HNCOP: Designing a Robust Medicinal Plant Identification Using Hybrid Neural Classification and Optimization Principle
Abstract: The identification of medicinal plants is essential in traditional medicine, pharmaceutical research and ecology conservation. However, the identification of medicinal plant species is a complicated task because of similarity of visual appearance of the species, differences within the species, and interference with real life conditions in the form of noisy backgrounds, uneven lighting, etc. To address these challenges, this paper presents HNCOP- a Hybrid Neural Classification and Optimization Principal framework that can aid with the robust medicinal plant recognition. The model uses a combination of deep convolutional neural networks with handcrafted features such as texture, shape and color allowing comprehensive visual comprehension. These characteristics are combined with the help of the attention-enabled layer that highlights significant characteristics selectively. Besides, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is used to optimize model parameters and ensemble weights. The HNCOP has shown superiority over the classical classifier and separate deep models to benchmark data sets with an impressive accuracy of 99.7% and high precision, recall and ROC-AUC scores. The ablation analysis and the cross-validation indicate the stability of the model and the good-quality generalization on different types of plants. HNCOP has the potential to be useful in mobile devices and digital herbal databases with its effective inference velocity and scalable design, which provides a powerful instrument to identify plant species with unparalleled accuracy to botanists, researchers, and conservationists.
Keywords: computer vision | convolutional neural networks | deep learning | ensemble learning | feature fusion | hybrid neural networks | Medicinal plant identification | particle swarm optimization

Title: AI-Enhanced Stock Screening System for Multi-Bagger Identification Using Financial and Market Indicators
Abstract: The paper will outline a new AI-enhanced stock screening tool to find possible multi-bagger stocks using the combination of financial and market-indicator-driven approach. The offered system utilizes an integrated machine-learning pipeline that combines a set of standard measures, including revenue growth, profitability ratios, cash-flow stability, and debt efficiency, and technical features, such as trend strength, volatility changes, and momentum signals. A feature-engineering layer is added that converts the raw financial statements and market data into predictive variables that are best suited to detect long-term values. The model also has an adaptive weighting mechanism that dynamically changes the weighting of indicators depending on the changing market conditions. The system predicts better and reduces false positives by training gradient-boosting algorithms and ensemble learning on multi-bagger forecasting. Multi-sector historical back-testing shows that the discovery of stocks at their early-stage is significantly enhanced using the machine learning approach as compared to the conventional screening heuristics. The findings confirm the fact that AI-based hybrid analysis has a significant positive impact on the reliability, speed, and accuracy of stocks with high long-term compounding potential.
Keywords: Feature Engineering | Financial Indicators | Machine Learning | Stock Selection

Title: A Framework to Investigate the Effects of Observation Error on Neural Network Predictions of Fish Age
Abstract: Technological innovations for predicting fish age represent a paradigm shift from conventional age estimation methods used in fisheries science. Recently developed secondary methods rely on models trained on conventional age estimates, derived from subjective interpretation of growth patterns and a biological property of the fish to predict age. Hence, quantifying the error that propagates from these models and the conventional age estimates on which they are trained is critical to fully account for uncertainty in predicted ages used in fisheries stock assessments. We review the development of three secondary age prediction methods: image analysis, epigenetics and Fourier transform near-infrared spectroscopy (FT-NIRS); the use of artificial intelligence (AI) within each method; and present an approach to examine the effects of ageing error on AI age prediction models. As a case study, we conducted an empirical study, coupled with simulation, to quantify the effects of ageing error on the performance of a multimodal convolutional neural network (MMCNN) model used to predict eastern Bering Sea walleye pollock (Gadus chalcogrammus) ages from otoliths analysed using FT-NIRS. Results indicated repeatability of predicted ages was high between instrument operators, while adding ageing error resulted in a slight decrease in model performance from R<sup>2</sup> = 0.92 and CV = 7.6% to R<sup>2</sup> = 0.87 and CV = 10.2% on test datasets. Our results also suggest the MMCNN model is robust to noise in calibration age data and model performance may be better than performance metrics indicate when the model is evaluated against data with increased error.
Keywords: convolutional neural network | deep machine learning | fish age | model-predicted age | near-infrared spectroscopy

Title: AI-Enhanced Cybersecurity Risk Assessment for Smart Grid Infrastructures Using NIST Framework
Abstract: The digitalization of power systems has introduced cyber-physical vulnerabilities in smart grid infrastructures that traditional, rule-based detection mechanisms are insufficient to address. This paper presents an AI-enhanced cybersecurity risk assessment framework that integrates the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF 2.0), NIST SP 800-30, and MITRE ATT&CK for ICS with machine learning-based threat detection. Three classifiers - Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost - were trained and evaluated on the Blockchain-Enabled 6 G Microgrid Dataset, a multi-layer dataset comprising physical, communication, and blockchain operational features with a severe class imbalance ratio of 29.5: 1. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROCAUC, with recall and F1-score prioritized given the asymmetric cost of false negatives in cybersecurity contexts. XGBoost achieved the highest performance (accuracy: 0.993, F1-score: 0.885, ROC-AUC: 0.974), outperforming Logistic Regression and Random Forest through its sequential boosting architecture and scale_pos_weight parameter, which up-weighted the minority attack class during training. A key contribution is the systematic mapping of XGBoost probabilistic output scores to NIST SP 800-30 likelihood tiers, enabling continuous quantitative risk scoring via R=L × I and supporting automated protective responses in real time. A case study of the 2015-2016 Ukrainian power grid attacks further contextualizes the framework's applicability to real-world critical infrastructure scenarios.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Machine Learning | NIST CSF 2.0 | NIST SP 800-30 | Risk Assessment | Risk Modelling | Smart Grid

Title: Hybrid Power Reduction Techniques for Lowpower Arithmetic Units in Portable Biomedical Instrumentation
Abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid low-power design for Binary Coded Decimal (BCD) adders, which consists of a combination of three techniques: power gating, clock gating and multi-Vdd architectures. BCD adders are known to finance, commerce, and embedded systems; in this metric is a critical requirement for efficiency in power utilization. The method reduces the static and dynamic power at a fine level. Power gating helps to cut off the leakage current by isolation idle blocks with a sleep transistor. Clock gating, which accesses clock pulses in inactivated units, reduces dynamic consumption. Multi-VDD allows the sub-blocks to be with different supply voltages according to their performance requirements to further increase the efficiency without sacrificing any function. Collectively, these techniques guard against the powerful and effective control of power across the adder. Simulations indicate that the total power and energy-delay-product is reduced to a much lower level with the hybrid design compared to the conventional BCD adders without optimizations. It would save up to 70% power in appropriate configurations and therefore be used in low-power VLSI applications and Bio-medical instruments.
Keywords: Bi-LSTM | deep learning | EEG emotion recognition | emotion classification

Title: Predicting Geriatric Rehabilitation Stays of ≤4 Weeks After Hip Fracture Surgery: Machine Learning Approach Using Physical Activity and Patient Data
Abstract: Background: In 2022, over 18,000 patients aged ≥70 years were hospitalized in the Netherlands for a hip fracture, with 50% requiring geriatric rehabilitation after surgery. Increasing geriatric rehabilitation patient numbers, staff shortages, and rising pressure on health care budgets make adequate care challenging. To make geriatric rehabilitation more future-proof, a stronger focus on home-based rehabilitation is needed. Early identification of patients likely to be discharged soon enables timely discharge planning and coordination of support at home. Early geriatric rehabilitation discharge planning may help organize home-based rehabilitation more effectively by arranging home care services in advance. This can facilitate smoother transitions toward home and prevent discharge delays, which is important to ensure optimal bed occupancy. Objective: This study aims to develop machine learning (ML) models to predict a geriatric rehabilitation stay of 4 weeks or less in a skilled nursing home for older patients after hip fracture surgery, using continuously monitored physical activity data from the first week of geriatric rehabilitation and patient characteristics. Methods: This prospective cohort study (January 2019-August 2024) included 100 patients. Patient characteristics and physical activity data from the MOX1 accelerometer (Maastricht Instruments BV) were collected during the first rehabilitation week. Principal component analysis was used to reduce the physical activity features. ML models were developed using Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and refined if necessary. The performance of the single best-performing configuration per remaining ML model type was evaluated, and the most important features for predicting the length of geriatric rehabilitation stay were identified. Results: Of the 3 ML models evaluated (support vector machine [SVM], ensemble of decision trees, and neural network), the SVM achieved the highest performance, with 19 out of 20 correct predictions (accuracy=0.95, 95% CI 0.85-1.00; precision=0.91, 95% CI 0.71-1.00; recall=1.00, 95% CI 1.00-1.00; F<inf>1</inf>-score=0.95238, 95% CI 0.83-1.00; area under the curve [AUC]=0.97, 95% CI 0.83-1.00). The most important features for predicting the length of geriatric rehabilitation stay across the best-performing ML models included the continuously monitored physical activity data, time in the emergency room, functional ambulation category (FAC) at hospital discharge, age, Katz Index of Independence in Activities of Daily Living–6 (Katz-ADL6) at hospital discharge, Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), availability of nonprofessional help, surgery type, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), gender, and hemoglobin level at hospital admission. Conclusions: This study developed several ML models to predict a geriatric rehabilitation stay of ≤4 weeks in a skilled nursing home for older patients after hip fracture surgery. Among these models, the SVM proved to be highly accurate in its predictions with an accuracy of 0.95 (95% CI 0.85-1.00), precision of 0.91 (95% CI 0.71-1.00), recall of 1.00 (95% CI 1.00-1.00), F<inf>1</inf>-score of 0.95 (95% CI 0.83-1.00), and AUC of 0.97 (95% CI 0.88-1.00).
Keywords: accelerometer | continuous physical activity monitoring | geriatric rehabilitation | hip fracture | length of stay | machine learning | prediction

Title: Satellite-based precipitation retrieval using cross-temporal attention and multiscale spatial representation
Abstract: Geostationary meteorological satellites provide valuable observations for hourly precipitation monitoring. However, single-time snapshot observations struggle to capture the dynamic evolution of cloud systems. Furthermore, the scale mismatch between point-based rain gauges and grid-based satellite pixels, combined with complex terrain, limits the spatial generalization of current retrieval models. To address these challenges, we propose DTPNet, a deep learning framework designed for station-level hourly precipitation retrieval. Instead of relying on a single snapshot, the model utilizes consecutive multi-channel observations from geostationary satellites (e.g., FY-4A/AGRI) to explicitly track cloud movement and development over time. A cross-temporal attention mechanism is introduced to extract these dynamic cloud evolution patterns, alongside multiscale spatial representations to bridge the spatial gap between satellite pixels and ground stations. To ensure robust performance across diverse landscapes, the model dynamically adapts to local terrain elevation and spatiotemporal context. It simultaneously detects precipitation occurrence and classifies precipitation intensity. Evaluated against nationwide hourly rain gauge data in China for 2021, DTPNet significantly outperforms operational products like GPM IMERG and FY-4 QPE. Specifically, the Critical Success Index (CSI) for precipitation detection improves by approximately 53% and 108% compared to these products, respectively, and the Macro-F1 score for intensity classification reaches 0.4370. These results demonstrate the method’s superior accuracy and robust generalization for satellite-based precipitation monitoring.
Keywords: Deep learning | Dual-temporal feature modeling | Multi-scale spatial features | Precipitation occurrence and intensity classification | Satellite precipitation | Terrain-aware modeling

Title: TM-MOE: A Degradation-Aware Transformer-Mamba MoE for Hyperspectral and Multispectral Image Fusion
Abstract: With the increasing necessity for hyperspectral images (HSIs) with fine spatial-spectral details, the hyperspectral (HS) and multispectral (MS) image fusion scheme becomes a consequential mechanism to attain such images due to physical and expense constraints for the standard imaging instruments. With the rapid advancement of deep learning (DL) in the field of image processing, the ability to model long-range dependencies in both HS and MS images has become crucial for achieving superior performance in HS-MS image fusion. Transformer-based models address this challenge effectively through attention mechanisms, whereas state-space models offer a more efficient alternative in terms of both computation and memory usage. Therefore, we devise a degradation-aware transformer-Mamba MoE (TM-MOE) for HS-MS image fusion, which leverages the benefits of the cross-attention mechanism and Mamba to enhance the fusion consequences. The core part of the devised framework is the suggested degradation-aware cross transformer-Mamba (DACTM) model, which leverages the capacity of Mamba in processing long-range relationships with improved training efficiency and the performance of the transformer's feature fusion for the observed pair. Moreover, the suggested Mamba module utilizes a 3-D scan to explore the correlation between pixels in an HSI, and it incorporates a mixture-of-experts (MoE) network to enrich model capability while maintaining effortless active parameter use. While the fusion process is accomplished on various scales, the novel feature accumulation and reconstruction block (FARB) devised reconstructs the final output from the fused features at different scales, gradually. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed TM-MOE. The code of this study will be available on https://github.com/Abdolraheemkhader/TM-MOE.
Keywords: Attention mechanism | hyperspectral image (HSI) | image super-resolution | multiscale fusion | spatial-spectral feature scanning

Title: Infrared and Visible Ship Image Fusion Based on Adaptive Cross-Modal Feature Interaction and Multiscale Frequency-Domain Transformation
Abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion serves as a pivotal technique for all-weather ship surveillance in maritime security applications, which can compensate for the inherent deficiencies of single-modal imaging under low-illumination and complex sea-state conditions. Nevertheless, existing fusion algorithms confront three core bottlenecks in coastal ship scenarios: first, insufficient robust feature representation capability against complex sea-sky backgrounds and multiscale ship targets; second, inefficient cross-modal feature interaction between infrared and visible modalities; third, weak scene adaptability arising from static weight allocation in multiscale frequency-domain fusion. To address these issues, this article proposes an infrared and visible ship image fusion algorithm (AMTFuse) based on adaptive cross-modal feature interaction and multiscale frequency-domain transformation, and constructs the IVSHIP dataset dedicated to ship image fusion. AMTFuse adopts an end-to-end framework and consists of three core modules: first, a contrastive learning-based feature enhancement network (CLFE) is developed, which mitigates small-target feature missing and insufficient modal discriminability in complex maritime scenarios via multiscale feature distillation paths, cross-modal contrastive learning, and enhanced spatial attention (ESA); second, an adaptive cross-modal feature interaction module (ACMF) is devised, which breaks through the limitations of static interaction and poor scene adaptability in existing cross-modal Transformers by virtue of modal-aware gating, multilevel feature alignment, and dynamic attention updating; finally, a multiscale dynamic frequency-domain fusion module (MSDF) is established, which implements multiscale frequency-domain decomposition and content-aware dynamic weight fusion at the deep feature level, remedying the defects of spatial-frequency decoupling and static weighting in conventional frequency-domain methods. Experimental results on the self-built IVSHIP dataset as well as public MSRS and TNO datasets demonstrate that AMTFuse significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art fusion algorithms in both quantitative metrics and visual effects. Furthermore, this article validates that the proposed algorithm can be applied to boost the performance of high-level computer vision tasks (i.e., object detection).
Keywords: Cross-modal fusion | image fusion | infrared image | visible light image

Title: M3DFuseNet: Multi-Sequence 3D Fusion Network via Global-Local Integration for Preoperative Microvascular Invasion Prediction in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
Abstract: Preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is of critical clinical importance for guiding surgical planning and postoperative adjuvant therapy. Although several deep learning-based fusion methods have been proposed for this task, most fail to fully exploit the complementary information across multi-sequence MRI, resulting in limited predictive performance. To address this limitation, we developed a multi-sequence 3D fusion network (M3DFuseNet) for MVI prediction. The model employs a 3D ResNet-34 backbone to extract multi-scale features from different MRI sequences, which are then processed by a global aware module (GAM) and a local aware module (LAM). The GAM incorporates positional encoding and attention mechanism to effectively capture cross-sequence interactions, while the LAM uses a bottom-up aggregation pathway with adaptive weighting to progressively fuse multi-scale features. The fused features are finally passed to a classifier for MVI prediction. M3DFuseNet was evaluated on a multi-center dataset collected from the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University and the Eastern Hepatobiliary Surgery Hospital. The experimental results showed that the model achieved an accuracy of 0.894 ± 0.016 and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ACC) of 0.917 ± 0.033 on the internal validation set, while the performance on the external test set reached an accuracy of 0.814 and an AUC of 0.829. These findings indicate that M3DFuseNet holds substantial potential for supporting preoperative clinical decision-making in HCC patients.
Keywords: A | deep learning | global aware module (GAM) | hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) | local aware module (LAM) | microvascular invasion (MVI) | multi-sequence fusion | R318 | TP391

Title: Comparing AI-enhanced instructional designs for EFL postgraduate proficiency: a multisite randomized controlled trial with exploratory ICC outcomes
Abstract: No randomized evidence directly compares immersive simulation, intelligent pairing, and adaptive learning instructional designs within the same postgraduate EFL study using a standardized proficiency endpoint. This multisite randomized controlled trial compared three AI-enhanced instructional designs—structured task bundles delivered via AI mediation and evaluated as instructional designs rather than technology platforms—specifically Immersive Simulation Technology (IST), Intelligent Pairing Systems (IPS), and Adaptive Learning Platform (ALP)—with an active control in required postgraduate TESOL coursework at four East Asian university sites (N = 245) over 12 wk. The preregistered confirmatory outcome was official ETS-administered TOEFL iBT total score; Intercultural Communicative Competence Performance-Oriented (ICC-PO) performance was analyzed as a secondary exploratory outcome. Within the preregistered confirmatory proficiency family, all three Holm–Bonferroni-corrected contrasts were supported: IST outperformed Control and ALP, and ALP outperformed Control on TOEFL iBT total score; IPS proficiency contrasts were exploratory. IST produced the largest adjusted gain (Δ = 36.99 TOEFL points, 95% CI [35.58, 38.44]; Hedges’ g = 3.02, 95% CI [2.65, 3.39]; d_resid = 5.67), interpreted as a near-transfer, high-dose, context-specific upper-bound estimate rather than a population-average expectation. Exploratory ICC-PO patterns broadly paralleled the proficiency results but are interpreted cautiously as context-bound performance differences under a partially aligned instrument, with cross-group measurement comparability not established. The study contributes head-to-head randomized evidence for instructional-design selection—not technology novelty—and supports a sequenced pedagogical logic in which ALP, IPS, and IST serve distinct roles in postgraduate EFL instruction.
Keywords: computer-assisted language learning | EFL proficiency | instructional design comparison | mixed-effects modeling | Randomized controlled trial

Title: MFN-Net: multi-scale adaptive fusion and flexible label assignment for small object detection in remote sensing images
Abstract: Object detection in remote sensing images is important yet challenging due to the small size of objects and interference from complex backgrounds. To address these challenges, we propose a novel detection framework named MFN-Net. First, a Multi-scale Feature Enhanced Adaptive Fusion architecture (MFEAF) is introduced, which effectively captures fine-grained features of objects by incorporating multi-scale downsampling and an adaptive weight fusion mechanism, thereby enhancing the representational capability of small object features. Second, we design a Similarity Distance-based Flexible Label Assignment (SFLA) strategy specifically tailored for small objects. This strategy employs aspect ratio filtering and a dynamic matching mechanism to assign sufficient high-quality positive samples to small objects, thereby improving detection performance. Through experiments on the SODA-A and AI-TOD datasets, the proposed method shows advantages in small object detection. The average precision (AP) is improved by 1.9% and 1.1%, respectively, compared to current state-of-the-art methods. Especially in the detection of very small and small objects, the method achieves a more significant performance improvement, demonstrating its superiority in small object detection tasks.
Keywords: feature pyramid network | label assignment | Remote-sensing images | small object detection

Title: Early risk stratification for carbapenem resistance among Pseudomonas aeruginosa infected patients using a clinico-laboratory machine-learning model based on routine complete blood count parameters
Abstract: Introduction: To address the delayed identification of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA), we developed an interpretable machine-learning (ML) model for early risk stratification. Utilizing routine complete blood count (CBC) and demographic data, this tool targets the critical 48-72 hour interval before final antimicrobial susceptibility results. Methods: Data from 1,666 patients with P. aeruginosa infection (223 CRPA) at a primary center were retrospectively analyzed, alongside an independent external validation cohort (n=471). Following the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression on 32 variables, eight ML algorithms were trained. Model interpretability and clinical utility were evaluated using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and decision curve analysis (DCA). Eight ML algorithms were trained using 5-fold cross-validation and Bayesian hyperparameter optimization. To ensure reproducibility and handle class imbalance, fixed random seeds were set, and a sensitivity analysis using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was conducted. Model calibration was assessed using the Brier score. Results: LASSO identified seven predictors: sex, age, mean corpuscular volume (MCV), hemoglobin (HGB), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI), and intensive care unit (ICU) admission status. Among the evaluated algorithms, the random forest (RF) model achieved the best discrimination. The training area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.993; it achieved an average 5-fold cross-validation AUC of 0.929 ± 0.005. In the internal test set, it achieved an AUC of 0.837 (95% CI: 0.779-0.893), specificity of 0.972, and sensitivity of 0.507, with excellent calibration (Brier score = 0.084). The model retained strong performance externally (AUC: 0.898, specificity: 0.985, sensitivity: 0.600, Brier score: 0.073). SHAP analysis indicated that HGB was the most influential feature, inversely associated with CRPA risk. Decision curve analysis supported the clinical utility across threshold probabilities ranging from 15% to 65%. Discussion: This clinlabomics-based RF model provides a rapid, low-cost adjunct for early CRPA stratification. Given its exceptionally high specificity (>0.97) and modest sensitivity, it functions exclusively as a reliable clinical "rule-in" tool. Positive predictions can confidently guide early targeted therapy and strict infection control. However, negative predictions cannot safely rule out CRPA, emphasizing its role alongside standard empirical practices rather than as a standalone screening instrument.
Keywords: carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa | clinico-laboratory omic | complete blood count | machine learning | predictive model | risk stratification

Title: Metaheuristic-driven optimization of ensemble deep learning model for image manipulation classification
Abstract: Detecting image manipulations, particularly in double Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG)-compressed images, remains a critical challenge in digital forensics due to the repetitive compression chain introduced by social media platforms. These processes obscure manipulation traces, complicating detection tasks. This study addresses these challenges by proposing a metaheuristic-optimized ensemble deep learning (DL) model that combines Squeeze-and-Excitation Residual Network (SE-ResNet50; fine-grained spatial detail extraction), Squeeze-and-Excitation Dense Convolutional Network (SE-DenseNet121; efficient feature reuse), Squeeze-and-Excitation Inception architecture (SE-InceptionV3; multi-scale feature extraction), and Vision Transformer (ViT-Base/32; long-range dependency and global relationship analysis). Ensemble weights were optimized using five metaheuristic techniques: Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Bayesian Optimization (BO), Differential Evolution (DE), and Genetic Algorithm (GA), with GA achieving the best optimization results. Experiments on three benchmark datasets—Break Our Steganographic System Base (BOSSBase), 10-class Mini-ImageNet (ImageNet-Mini10K), Uncompressed Colour Image Database (UCID)—across multiple JPEG quality factors (75, 85, 95) showed that the proposed ensemble model significantly outperformed individual DL models and traditional equal-weighted ensembles in terms of accuracy and F1-scores, while exhibiting strong cross-dataset generalization under domain shifts. The results highlight the effectiveness of metaheuristic-optimized ensemble learning for robust and scalable manipulation classification, making the proposed framework particularly suitable for offline forensic analysis scenarios involving realistic JPEG compression chains.
Keywords: Deep learning | Ensemble learning | Image compression | Image manipulation classification | Meta-heuristic optimization

Title: A CNN-RNN Dual-Stage Assamese Speech Synthesis and Recognition Framework Using Common Voice Corpus
Abstract: Speech processing for low-resource languages remains a important challenge in the field of artificial intelligence due to limited datasets, linguistic diversity and model generalization limitations. This study includes Text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-text (STT) transformation in unified process. With a short-time objective intelligibility (STOI) score of 0.82, the TTS component uses a hybrid CNN-RNN model for feature extraction and temporal modelling with waveform reconstruction using the Griffin-Lim algorithm. A CNN-RNN architecture optimized with CTCs loss is incorporated into the STT module which results in a word error rate (WER) of 0.20. The proposed system shows the high transcription accuracy while attaining good alignment between source and synthesised speech. This study offers a method to enhance speech technologies for underrepresented languages that can be easily replicated and scaled. The results shows that CNN-RNN architectures have considerable potential for efficient, end-to-end speech synthesis and recognition which will paved the way towards universally accessible digital communication and multilingual systems for AI.
Keywords: Assamese Speech Processing | Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) | Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) | Griffin-Lim Vocoder | Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) | Short-Time Objective Intelligibility (STOI) | Speech-to-Text (STT) | Text-to-Speech (TTS) | Word Error Rate (WER)

Title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Vocal Emotion Classification using Speech Signals
Abstract: Vocal emotion classification plays an important role in human-computer interaction, affective computing, and speech-based intelligent systems. Speech signals convey rich emotional information through variations in tone, pitch, and temporal patterns, making emotion recognition a challenging task. This paper presents a hybrid deep learning framework for vocal emotion classification using speech signals. The study evaluates traditional machine-learning models, deep learning architectures, and hybrid convolutional-recurrent networks to analyze their effectiveness in recognizing emotional states from audio data. Machine-learning models serve as baseline classifiers using handcrafted acoustic features, while deep learning models learn temporal and spectral representations directly from speech signals. To further enhance performance, hybrid CNN-recurrent models are employed to capture both local spectral characteristics and long-term temporal dependencies. Experimental results demonstrate that deep learning approaches outperform classical methods, with hybrid models achieving the highest classification accuracy. The findings highlight the suitability of hybrid deep learning architectures for robust vocal emotion classification.
Keywords: Audio signal processing | Deep learning | Hybrid CNN-RNN | Speech emotion recognition | Vocal emotion classification

Title: Pose-Guided Multi-Scale Vision Transformer for Robust and Accurate Person Re-Identification in Visual Surveillance
Abstract: Person Re-Identification (Re-ID) is the task of matching images of the same individual captured across multiple non-overlapping surveillance cameras. It plays a crucial role in intelligent video surveillance, public safety, and criminal investigation by enabling automated tracking of individuals across different locations. However, challenges such as pose variation, occlusion, illumination changes, and inconsistent image resolution make accurate re-identification difficult. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and attention-based models have achieved moderate success but often fall short in capturing long-range dependencies and semantic understanding. To address these limitations, this research proposes a Pose-Guided Multi-Scale ViT-ReID model with Part Tokens and an Attribute Head, which integrates a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone for global spatial reasoning, pose-aware token weighting to emphasize visible body parts, and multi-scale patch embedding for resolution robustness. An attribute prediction head is further employed to incorporate semantic-level identity cues. The model is trained and evaluated on the DukeMTMC-reID dataset, comprising 36,411 images across 1,812 identities from 8 cameras. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves 99.00% Rank-1 accuracy, 99.50% Rank-5 accuracy, 99.80% Rank-10 accuracy, and a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 85.12%, outperforming existing approaches. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of combining spatial, pose, and semantic cues in enhancing person re-identification performance under real-world surveillance conditions.
Keywords: Attribute Prediction | Deep Learning | Multi-Scale Patch Embedding | Occlusion | Person Re-Identification | Pose-Aware Token Weighting | Vision Transformer (ViT)

Title: MHDMC-Net: Multi-Head Dynamic Multi-Scale Convolutional Network with Adaptive Gated Mechanism for Crop Disease and Pest Detection
Abstract: Accurate and timely detection of crop diseases and pests is crucial for ensuring global food security and reducing agricultural losses. However, current deep learning approaches for crop disease detection face three critical limitations: (1) insufficient extraction of multi-scale discriminative features for disease symptoms of varying sizes, (2) ineffective feature fusion mechanisms that fail to capture complementary information across different receptive fields, and (3) limited attention to subtle pathological regions in complex agricultural environments. To address these challenges, we propose MHDMC-Net, a novel framework integrating three key innovations matching these limitations: (1) a Multi-Head Dynamic Multi-scale Convolutional (MHDMC) module that employs parallel multi-scale depth-wise convolutions with dynamic weight generation for adaptive feature extraction, (2) an Adaptive Multi-scale Gated Linear Unit (AM-GLU) that leverages gating mechanisms to selectively fuse multi-scale features, and (3) a Lightweight Attention mechanism that efficiently highlights disease-relevant regions with minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on a large-scale agricultural dataset containing 22 disease and pest categories demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, validating the effectiveness of our integrated framework.
Keywords: Crop disease detection | deep learning | dynamic convolution | gated linear unit | lightweight attention | multi-scale feature extraction | precision agriculture

Title: Real-Time Emergency Detection via Multimodal Fusion of Acoustic and Emotional Features
Abstract: This paper presents a new real-time emergency detection system that recognises emergency signals from noise using speech enhancement, automatic speech recognition (ASR) representations, and emotion modelling. The emergency detection system relied on time domain speech enhancement methods to improve the intelligibility of the audio signal for ASR. The intermediate representations produced by the ASR models (Wav2Vec2 and Whisper) take advantage of the richness of speech to encode connectivity and meaning. Emotion detection is performed using transformer-based models to predict urgency and emotion. Experimental results show improvements in performance over baseline systems developed using traditional methods that processed the raw audio with or without processing the text in noise. Additionally, the use of multimodal features allows this system to detect emergencies at low signal-to-noise ratios. We also explore keyword-based least impactful emergency detection as a quick response capability that can be used alongside the machine learning model. The designed pipelines can also produce low-latency and near-realtime systems that will favourably support emergency responses on mobile and edge devices. Future work includes expanding the system to detect more types of emergencies and potentially support multilingual speech recognition.
Keywords: automatic speech recognition | convtasnet | demucs | dnn | hubert | lightgbm | multimodal fusion | rnn | wav2vec2

Title: Machine Learning Enhancements for Cherenkov Telescope Data Analysis
Abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) will provide incredible opportunities for the future of ground-based very-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy. Its Science Alert Generation (SAG) system, part of the Array Control and Acquisition (ACADA) system, will handle real-time reconstruction, data quality monitoring, and scientific analysis to issue candidate science alerts. Real-time technical and observational variability, along with performance demands, can affect automated pipeline sensitivity. We developed two Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) prototypes to perform analyzes when requirements for standard techniques are not satisfied. The first is an autoencoder that removes background noise from counts maps without needing target positions, background templates, or Instrument Response Functions (IRFs). The second is a 2D regressor that localizes candidate sources in the field of view, also independent of background templates and IRFs. Verification against the gammapy analysis as implemented in ACADA/SAG v1.0.0 shows comparable results, with the added advantage of reduced dependency on prior knowledge. The CNN regressor achieved a 68% containment radius of approximately 0.07∘. Meanwhile, the autoencoder significantly improved localization accuracy by removing background noise and demonstrated promising potential for data quality applications.

Title: Scalable Multi-Agent DRL for Joint Offloading and Resource Allocation in MEC Networks
Abstract: A fundamental challenge in Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) systems is minimizing the long-term weighted cost of delay and energy through joint task offloading and resource allocation in dynamic, large-scale, multi-agent environments. While existing multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) methods, such as multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG), are promising, they often face limitations in global coordination efficiency and training stability. To address these challenges, we propose an advanced MADRL framework. The framework introduces a structured attention mechanism designed to explicitly model resource contention, enabling the critic to dynamically weigh the most critical inter-agent dependencies. Furthermore, a hybrid critic architecture synergistically combines this structured attention pathway with a holistic MLP pathway. This dual-pathway approach captures fine-grained coordination patterns with high precision while maintaining robust global value estimation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves faster convergence and superior performance in minimizing the total system cost compared to conventional MADRL baselines.
Keywords: attention mechanism | MADDPG | MADRL | MEC | task offloading

Title: Microstructural Evolution and In-Situ Deflection Behavior in Curing Cold Recycled Asphalt Mixtures Assessed by X-Ray Microtomography
Abstract: This study evaluates the microstructural characteristics and mechanical behavior of cold recycled asphalt mixtures (CRAM) stabilized with asphalt emulsion throughout their curing period. A multi-scale experimental framework was employed, combining high-resolution X-ray micro-computed tomography with in-situ falling weight deflectometer (FWD) testing. Field-extracted specimens from four full-depth reclaimed pavement sections were scanned at multiple depths and curing ages to quantify air void (AV) morphology, distribution, and connectivity using deep learning-based digital image processing. Complementary FWD testing, conducted over a 263-day period, enabled the backcalculation of elastic moduli to monitor the progressive stiffness gain of the CRAM layers under field conditions. Results revealed significant heterogeneity in AV distribution, particularly in interface and base zones, which exhibited higher void counts and volumes compared with other layers. Deflection and modulus trends followed a three-phase trajectory: initial low stiffness, intermediate stabilization, and advanced structural gain, with moduli increasing from 300–700 MPa to over 3,000 MPa. The integration of microstructural and mechanical data revealed a strong correlation between AV network refinement and structural performance over time. These findings underscore the importance of curing protocols, compaction quality, and layer interaction in recycled pavement systems. The study demonstrates the value of combining advanced imaging with field testing to support performance-based design, quality control, and long-term durability of cold-recycled asphalt technologies.
Keywords: air voids | asphalt emulsion | cold recycling | deflection | X-ray microtomography

Title: A Spatiotemporal CNN-LSTM Framework for Forecasting Crop Disease Progression
Abstract: The majority of deep learning methods used in plant pathology are based on the classification of the static images and do not consider the way diseases change with time. This limitation impairs premature diagnosis and accurate severity determination, in particular in the field, dynamic farm conditions. To overcome this, we suggest a spatiotemporal deep learning model that brings together a convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for image extraction with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network on temporal sequence modeling. This hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture studies the consecutive images in order to capture the progression of disease symptoms. Real time crop data are available only in small datasets, and time-varying datasets do not involve real-time. With scarcity, we present a synthetic sequence generation approach that simulates the disease development out of still pictures with alpha blending. The individual frames are run in a pre-trained inceptionV3 model to generate strong feature vectors, which the LSTM then use to learn the temporal patterns. The proposed approach is demonstrated to work with the publicly available rice leaf disease dataset constantly achieves higher performance than a state-of-the-art static CNN baseline in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score. By incorporating temporal information, this framework offers a more credible and informative instrument of predictive disease surveillance in precision agriculture.
Keywords: CNN | Computer Vision | Deep Learning | LSTM | Plant Disease Detection | Precision Agriculture | Spatiotemporal Analysis

Title: Enhancing ASR Performance in Noisy Environments Via Bridging Approach
Abstract: In this research work, we propose a method for noise-robust automatic speech recognition systems in the presence of non-stationary noise, specifically background speaker noise. This proposed technique will be extremely useful for any ASR system/application that needs to be accessed in an outdoor environment. Technically, we focus on the integration of speech enhancement (SE) and automatic speech recognition (ASR) to improve the performance of a pre-trained ASR model in noisy conditions. We employ a technique called observation addition (OA) where the original noisy signal is added to the SE version of itself using a weighting approach and then subsequently passed through the ASR model. We tested this approach using the Google FLEURS dataset. In this dataset, each speech sample is evaluated at five different SNR levels. Using an attention-based deep learning network, we estimate the SNR from the noisy samples. The SNR is then mapped to the best OA coefficient, which is then used for assigning weights to noisy and enhanced signal. Our proposed approach improves ASR performance across all SNR levels. At lower SNRs, it gives a 3.1% absolute gain at 3 dB when using a fixed OA coefficient for all utterances from a general domain.
Keywords: attention | Automatic speech recognition | deep learning | observation addition | speech enhancement

Title: A time–frequency heterogeneous dual-domain joint sampling–reconstruction and uncertainty quantification network for structural monitoring data reconstruction
Abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) systems generate massive volumes of data during long-term operation, imposing substantial challenges on storage and transmission. Compressed sensing, which leverages sparse sampling combined with deep-learning-based reconstruction, has emerged as an effective means to alleviate these bottlenecks. However, existing methods often suffer degraded reconstruction fidelity at high compression ratios or when limited to a single domain (time or frequency), and they typically lack sampling strategies tailored to inherent signal characteristics as well as principled quantification of reconstruction uncertainty—limitations that undermine their reliability in practical engineering applications. To address these shortcomings, this study proposes a time–frequency heterogeneous, dual-domain joint sampling–reconstruction and uncertainty-quantification network specifically designed for SHM data. The model performs joint sampling and reconstruction in separate time-domain and frequency-domain branches and fuses their complementary outputs through a designed multi-scale weighted fusion module to produce the final reconstruction. Uncertainty quantification of the reconstructed signals is obtained naturally via repeated Monte Carlo forward passes. The proposed method is validated on laboratory pedestrian-bridge tests and on an in-service steel truss bridge. Results show that, across a range of compression ratios, the method achieves excellent reconstruction performance in both time and frequency domains, with modal parameters of the reconstructed signals essentially matching those of the originals. Compared with conventional random undersampling and single-domain reconstruction, the network-learned dual-domain undersampling strategy yields higher reconstruction accuracy, reduced variability, and improved robustness. Furthermore, a parallel dual-channel sampling scheme designed for sensor-level deployment enables in situ compressed acquisition and high-fidelity downstream reconstruction in real SHM environments.
Keywords: compressed sensing | joint sampling-reconstruction | Structural health monitoring | time-frequency dual domain | uncertainty quantification

Title: A RICE GROWTH STAGE IDENTIFICATION MODEL BASED ON AN OPTIMIZED YOLOV12n ARCHITECTURE
Abstract: Accurately identifying rice growth stages in cold regions is challenging due to subtle morphological differences between key stages (e.g., tillering, jointing-booting) and complex field conditions, often leading to inefficient water use. This paper proposes an improved YOLOv12n-based method for rice growth stage recognition. First, a Deformable Large Kernel Attention (D-LKA) mechanism is introduced to enhance the model's ability to capture multi-scale morphological features of rice plants through large receptive field convolution and adaptive sampling grids. Second, a weighted Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) and a Dynamic Upsampling module (DySample) are employed to construct an efficient multi-scale feature interaction pathway, improving the model's perception of details in key plant parts. Finally, the Normalized Wasserstein Distance (NWD) is adopted to optimize the small-target detection strategy, effectively mitigating the under-detection of small-scale features. A cold-region rice growth stage image dataset was constructed for training and evaluation. Results show that the proposed YOLOv12n-DBD model achieves a precision of 93.4%, a recall of 89.7%, a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 94.4%, and an inference speed of 121.9 FPS. The mAP@0.5 represents an improvement of 4.9 percentage points over the baseline model, outperforming current mainstream detection models while maintaining real-time performance. A mobile recognition system was also developed to provide a convenient solution. The proposed YOLOv12n-DBD model effectively balances recognition accuracy and computational efficiency in the complex environments of cold-region rice fields, offering reliable technical support for growth-stage-specific field management.
Keywords: Cold region agriculture | Deep learning | Developmental stages | Object detection | YOLOv12n

Title: Dense Net-EMPA: A Hybrid Deep Learning and Metaheuristic Framework for Wireless Image Transmission in Multi-User NOMA-Aided Massive MIMO Channels
Abstract: The rapid expansion of 5G and upcoming 6G networks requires wireless image transmission schemes that deliver ultra-reliable, low-latency, and energy-efficient performance over highly dynamic multiuser channels. This paper presents a deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN) DenseNet- with Enhanced Marine Predator Algorithm (EMPA) and a hybrid deep learning and metaheuristic framework for wireless image transmission in non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-aided massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The proposed model combines a dense convolutional network (DenseNet) encoder-decoder with an enhanced marine predator algorithm (EMPA) optimizer to jointly tune channel coding power allocation, and resource scheduling under multi-user interference. DenseNet model dense feature propagation efficiently extracts multi-scale image representations, whereas EMPA adaptively minimizes transmission error and latency by optimizing NOMA power coefficients and MIMO beamforming weights. The benchmark proposed model DenseNet-EMPA against recent hybrid learning optimization paradigms, including a comparison of exit models such as deep reinforcement learning with self-optimized particle swarm joint source-channel coding (DRL-SOPSOJSCC), enhanced golden optimization algorithm integrated with deep reinforcement learning (EGOA-DRL), and improved golden jackal optimization with Bi-LSTM capsule network (IGJO-BiLSTM-CapsNet). Simulation results under realistic 5G/6G-orientated parameters show that DenseNet-EMPA achieves up to 18 - 24% lower bit error rate, 15% higher spectral efficiency, and 20% reduced latency compared to state-of-the-art approaches, while maintaining robust performance across varying SNR, user density, and mobility profiles. The performance results demonstrate that combining deep convolutional encoders with bioinspired metaheuristics provides a powerful design paradigm for next-generation wireless adaptive image transmissions.
Keywords: 5G/6G Networks | Deep Convolutional Neural Networks | Enhanced Marine Predator Algorithm | Low-latency Communication | Multi-user | Non-orthogonal Multiple Access Channels | Spectral Efficiency | Wireless Image Transmission

Title: Early Stage Parkinsonian Disorder Detection Using Machine Learning Classifiers and Neuro Motor Feature Analysis
Abstract: Parkinson disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease whose diagnosis is not an easy task because of subjective clinical examination and late onset of motor symptoms. Immediate and correct diagnosis is imperative in the prompt intervention and better patient outcomes. This paper introduces a machine learning-based system of earlystage Parkinsonian disorder detection with neuro-motor voice features. There was a publicly available biomedical voice dataset (22 acoustic features, 195 samples) in which each sample was classified as either Parkinson disease or healthy control. Some of the supervised machine learning classifier such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, Extra Trees and XGBoost were tested. In order to further improve classification performance and minimize falsenegative predictions, a hybrid stacking ensemble model was set forward that uses XGBoost and Extra Trees as base learners and Logistic Regression as a meta-learner. Adequate preprocessing methods like stratified data splitting and feature standardization were used. The results of the experiment show that the proposed hybrid stacking model is better than single classifiers; with an accuracy of 98.31 percent and is able to remove false negative cases of the Parkinson disease. The results suggest the usefulness of ensemble learning in addressing the issue of class imbalance and enhancing diagnostic accuracy, which means voice-based machine learning models might be proposed as a useful decision-supporting instrument to detect Parkinson disease at an early stage. Further research will be conducted on subject-independent validation and multimodal neuro-motor data integration to improve on its generalizability.
Keywords: early-stage detection | ensemble learning | hybrid stacking | machine learning | neuro-motor features | Parkinson's disease | voice signal analysis

Title: Enhancing Pre-Eclampsia Screening Through Machine Learning and Multi-Source Data Integration
Abstract: Pre-eclampsia remains one of the most severe pregnancy complications, tormenting the maternal and neonatal outcomes all over the world. In order to mitigate this risk, clinicians need risk-stratification instruments that are not only rapid but also evidence-based. This paper presents a predictive framework in modules that would combine clinical, biochemical, and biosensor data into a single and clear risk estimate. It consists of five modules which are inter-relational as follows: (1) acquisition and harmonization of multi-source data, (2) preprocessing and feature construction, (3) supervised machine-learning modelling, (4) clinical risk stratification and decision support, and (5) independent validation and performance monitoring. The Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting (XG Boost) models are crossvalidated and hyper-optimized to ensure strong discrimination and calibration. Individual risk type categories are thus created and incorporated to the clinician dashboards effortlessly and the patients are given brief educational information. The proven system helps to detect high-risk pregnancies at early stages and implement timely interventions, including low-dose aspirin and enhanced monitoring. Demonstrating that machine learning can be directly introduced into obstetric practice, the framework shows that a data-driven approach can offer a practical mechanism to improve maternal safety and the initial diagnosis of pre-eclampsia through the synthesis of clinical records, laboratory data, and biosensor inputs.
Keywords: early detection | ensemble models | gradient boosting | machine learning | obstetric analytics | Pre-eclampsia prediction | risk stratification

Title: Postpartum Depression Detection Using Ensemble Learning
Abstract: Postpartum Depression (PPD) is an important issue in mental health among new mothers in the world at a rate of {1 0 - 2 0} percent. Timely intervention in PPD is the best option to live with good health outcomes as mother and child. The paper introduces an all-inclusive machine learning strategy to detect PPD based on 5,000 simulated maternal health records. In this paper, we apply and compare five single machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, random forest, support vector machine (SVM), Naive Bayes, and XGBoost and three ensemble learning strategies: Hard Voting, Soft Voting, and Stacking. The samples were trained considering {1 4} characteristics such as demographic data, pregnancy complications, delivery type, sleep patterns, and psychological symptoms. Outcomes show that the use of ensemble techniques and specifically Stacking has a better performance with a high accuracy of over 92%. XGBoost and random forest also performed well with minimum accuracy of 91% on an individual basis. The researchers find such major predictive characteristics as frequent sadness, loss of interest, sudden crying, and sleep deprivation. This study can help in the creation of automated PPD screening instruments that will help healthcare professionals to early detect and intervene with at-risk mothers.
Keywords: Ensemble Learning | Healthcare Analytics | Machine Learning | Mental Health Detection | Postpartum Depression | Predictive Modeling

Title: Prosody Disruptor for Voice Protection Against Unauthorized Speech Synthesis
Abstract: Recent advances in neural speech synthesis enable highly realistic speech generation, raising concerns about unauthorized voice impersonation. To prevent this, proactive voice protection introduces imperceptible perturbations into speech signals that hinder synthesis models from learning a target speaker's identity. However, many existing approaches rely on complex optimization procedures and multiple auxiliary models, resulting in high computational cost. This paper proposes a lightweight prosody-driven voice protection method that disrupts prosodic cues used for speaker adaptation during neural speech synthesis training. The method simply perturbs pitch confidence and energy contours of the original waveform using a fixed pitch tracking model, enabling efficient and lightweight protection. Since prosodic features play a role in representing speaker identity, corrupting these cues reduces speaker similarity in synthesized speech while preserving perceptual quality. Experiments across multiple neural speech synthesis architectures demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves comparable protection performance while enabling a fourfold reduction in processing time.
Keywords: Adversarial machine learning | biometric authentication | deep learning | generative AI | information security | machine learning | speech processing | speech spoofing | speech synthesis | voice biometrics

Title: Stock Market Prediction in the Telecom Sector Using LSTM, BiLSTM, and RNN with Sentiment Analysis
Abstract: In this paper, we describe a deep learning framework for forecasting listed stock prices in India's telecommunication sector that combines market data, technical indicators, domain-conditioned event pulses, and news sentiment, all fed into recurrent models. This involved modeling ten years of daily data for three Indian firms-Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea, and Tata Communications - using LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory), BiLSTM (Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory), and RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) architectures that were trained on leak-safe, lagged sequences to predict the next-day log-return sequences. Among the three architectures modeled, BiLSTM achieved the best overall performance (average R2≈ 0.988, MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error) ≈ 1.7%), demonstrating the ability to capture temporal dependencies from both the past and the future. In conclusion, the simulation results demonstrate the significant contribution of fusing sentiment and technical-event features in forecasting short-term price movements of dynamically operated, policy-sensitive industries, such as telecommunications, and provide a reproducible hybrid benchmark for forecasting their associated financial instruments.
Keywords: BiLSTM | Deep learning | LSTM | RNN | Sentiment analysis | Stock market forecasting | Technical indicators | Telecom sector | Time-series modeling

Title: MixSense: AI Optimisation for Contiguous Music Segmentation at Scale
Abstract: MixSense is an AI optimisation framework for segmenting DJ-mixed music streams. It operates using self-similarity manifolds and dynamic programming. The approach employs evolutionary search for finding the parameters and global optimisation for boundary detection with possibly zero prior track counts. The system achieves solid performance in segmenting journeys into sub-trips with a mean absolute error of less than 18 seconds in track estimation when evaluated on a 640 -hour annotated corpus. It outperforms local novelty detection methods and is scalable for real-world music streaming applications.
Keywords: audio processing | DJ mixing | dynamic programming | evolutionary algorithms | Music segmentation | self-similarity matrices

Title: A Multi-stage Deep Learning and Clustering Framework for Early Parkinson’s Disease Risk Identification from Voice Biomarkers
Abstract: Early and accurate identification of Parkinson’s Disease (PD) risk seems to be an unmet challenge, particularly for diagnosing persons with sub clinical symptoms or those in early stages. Most of the existing frameworks for PD diagnosis rely on binary classification or predicting the severity of the disease by using Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) score, omitting nuanced risk gradation and failing to discover PD-like healthy subgroups essential for preventive medicine. The present work proposes a multi-stage framework, combining autoencoder-based latent feature extraction, 2-tier GMM-based hierarchical clustering and adaptive model fusion to differentiate between PD, healthy, and PD-like healthy groups using voice biomarkers based on Parkinson’s Disease Similarity Index (PDSI). The proposed framework is validated using 5-fold stratified cross validation on a clinically annotated dataset of 756 voice samples, significantly skewed towards PD-positive cases. Paired t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank statistical analysis are carried out against standard Random Forest and SVM baselines to investigate their selection correctly and reliably. The proposed model achieves a cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.957, PR-AUC of 0.986 and F1-score of 0.945 with statistically significant improvements over ensemble and margin-based classifiers (). The hierarchical approach uniquely enables detection of “PD-like healthy” individuals, thus supporting graded risk scores that can drive personalized early intervention strategies. The findings highlight PDSI as a valuable, scalable and clinically pertinent instrument for early diagnosis of PD and risk assessment and hence it creates new avenues for population wide preventative screening and incorporation into telemedicine systems.
Keywords: Deep learning | Machine learning | Parkinson’s disease | Risk stratification | Voice analysis

Title: GenAITD Score: A Quantitative Framework for Measuring Enterprise Technical Debt and Generative AI Readiness
Abstract: The rapid adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen-AI) in enterprise environments has outpaced the readiness of existing technical and governance infrastructures, exposing latent forms of technical debt across data pipelines, legacy workflows, and machine learning operations (MLOps) practices. While organizations are under increasing pressure to operationalize Gen-AI capabilities, existing maturity models lack the granularity required to identify the specific architectural and operational constraints that hinder reliable deployment. This paper introduces the Gen-AI Technical Debt (GenAITD) Score, a quantitative framework designed to measure enterprise readiness and Gen-AI-specific technical debt. The framework constructs a composite index on a normalized 0-500 scale and evaluates enterprise readiness across five weighted dimensions: Data Debt & Governance, Process & Automation, AI Platform Architecture, Organizational Readiness, and Risk & Compliance. A total of 45 objectively defined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are aggregated to produce both a numerical score and a corresponding letter-grade classification (A+ to D), enabling a standardized, audit-able mechanism for stakeholders to benchmark maturity.
Keywords: AI Governance | AI Readiness | Enterprise AI | Generative AI | MLOps | Model Lifecycle Management | Risk Management | Technical Debt

Title: Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting Organizational Behaviour: Role of Trust in Management and Colleagues in SMEs
Abstract: Organizational Citizenship Behaviour (OCB) is a critical contributor to organizational effectiveness, particularly in small and medium enterprises (SMEs) where discretionary employee efforts significantly influence outcomes. While existing research has largely relied on explanatory models to study antecedents of OCB, limited attention has been given to its predictive assessment using data-driven approaches. Addressing this gap, the present study applies explainable machine learning techniques to predict OCB by examining the role of trust in management and trust in colleagues. Primary data were collected from employees working in SMEs ({N}={3 9 7}). The measurement instruments demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha >0.98) and satisfactory construct validity. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) results indicated an excellent model fit (RMSEA {0. 0 3)} and revealed a strong positive association between trust in management and trust in colleagues. Building on this validated structure, explainable machine learning models-including logistic regression, decision tree, and random forest-were employed to predict organizational citizenship behaviour. The results indicate that trust in management and trust in colleagues consistently emerge as significant predictors of OCB across models. Tree-based models demonstrate comparatively better predictive performance while maintaining interpretability through feature-importance analysis. The findings highlight the centrality of trust dynamics in shaping citizenship behaviour and demonstrate the practical value of explainable machine learning as a decision-support approach for organizational behaviour research in SMEs.
Keywords: explainable machine learning | human resource analytics | Organizational citizenship behaviour | SMEs | trust in colleagues | trust in management

Title: A Curvature-Aware Enhancement and Geometrically Constrained Growing Method for Narrow River Extraction From TG2-InIRA Imagery
Abstract: Extracting narrow rivers from Tiangong-2 interferometric imaging radar altimeter (InIRA) imagery remains challenging due to nonstationary speckle noise, weak radiometric contrast, and complex river geometries under near-nadir imaging conditions. This study presents a task-oriented processing framework for fine-scale river delineation from InIRA data without relying on external auxiliary information. The proposed framework integrates anisotropic structure-adaptive despeckling to preserve linear features, multiscale feature enhancement to strengthen responses of narrow and sinuous channels, and a geometrically constrained priority-queue-based growing strategy to recover long-range river connectivity. A region-constrained Markov random field optimization is subsequently applied to enforce spatial consistency and refine river boundaries. Experimental evaluations conducted over six geographically diverse test sites demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves consistently improved performance compared with representative traditional filtering methods and deep-learning-based benchmarks. Specifically, the proposed method effectively mitigates the oversegmentation and topological fragmentation observed in the compared approaches. The proposed approach attains an average F1-score exceeding 89% and a Matthews correlation coefficient above 0.84, while maintaining lower breakage rates and fragmentation ratios in complex river networks. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a robust, computationally efficient, and training-data-independent solution for narrow river extraction from near-nadir interferometric radar altimeter observations.
Keywords: Curvature-based enhancement | interferometric radar altimeter (InIRA) | multiscale analysis | narrow river extraction | Tiangong-2 (TG-2)

Title: Leveraging Sample Difficulty in Computer Audition Analysis
Abstract: Despite the abundance and variety of computer audition (CA) tasks, only a few studies have investigated the delicate interplay between task data and deep learning model training. From a data perspective, the current literature lacks explanations of how CA-specific dataset characteristics influence model training, and why some samples are harder to learn than others. To bridge this gap, we leverage model-based estimations of sample difficulty as a tool to identify hard and easy samples from a dataset, allowing us to dive into aspects of difficulty in three common but dissimilar CA tasks: acoustic scene classification, speech command recognition and music genre recognition. Our results indicate that the difficulty of training data can provide a good estimation of test performance on a class-level. We further identify distributional differences between easy and hard samples, the latter of which mostly correspond to wrongly labelled or non-speech samples and show an undesirable model focus in the case of the speech commands dataset. Finally, we analyse how the exclusion of the easiest and hardest samples within datasets impacts model training.
Keywords: Computer audition | deep learning | explainability | sample difficulty

Title: MusicMorph: An Interactive System for Creating Immersive Music Video Experiences with AI-Driven Dance Generation
Abstract: We present MusicMorph, an interactive system for the user-centric creation and experience of immersive music videos featuring dancing avatars. Given a user-provided music track, our system automatically generates a corresponding dance skeleton and a virtual scene by analyzing the audio features of the track. Users can then select a preferred avatar, which is subsequently rigged with the generated skeleton and rendered within the generated immersive scene. The resulting music video can be experienced in Virtual Reality (VR), offering users an unconstrained, free-viewpoint perspective of the performance. In addition, users can directly manipulate the dance motion by dragging the avatar's joints to refine poses, or modify the animation by inputting specific action commands. This system enables users to upload their own music, watch the real-time generated music video, and perform edits in VR, offering a handson experience of creating an immersive music video from scratch.
Keywords: Dance Generation | Motion Editing | Motion Generation | Music Video Generation | Music Visualization

Title: Promises/Manual Labor Paradox: The Accountability Style of On-Site Validation in Microbiology Laboratory Automation
Abstract: This study investigates the role of validation reports in legitimizing laboratory automation through artificial intelligence and robotic systems in clinical microbiology. Based on a qualitative analysis of thirty reports authored by expert microbiologists between 2016 and 2023 across eight countries—Australia, Belgium, China, Spain, France, Italy, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom—we examine how technological promises are made accountable. Building on Science and Technology Studies (STS) and the sociology of expectations, we approach these reports not as mere sources of “objective” information, but as instruments of accountability that link future-oriented promises with conventional laboratory practices—particularly manual labor. We argue that they embody a distinct accountability style, diverging from an ethics-driven approach often found in influential STS contributions. Automation promises—largely framed through managerial values—actualize their contractual character when articulated through metrics designed to assess satisfactory performance. Yet numerical results alone are insufficient to legitimize devices that mostly match the performance of manual labor. A paradox emerges: while manual labor serves as the gold standard against which automation is assessed, for automation to be validated, manual labor must be discursively problematized as an “entrenched habit”—a hindrance to addressing contemporary healthcare challenges. We argue this constitutes an essential feature of the validation accountability style.
Keywords: accountability | credibility | legitimation | manual labor | robots and artificial intelligence | technoscientific promises

Title: Machine Learning-Based Multimode Ultrasonic Guided Wave Feature Extraction and Defect Identification Method for Tri-Post Insulators
Abstract: Gas insulated metal-enclosed transmission lines (GILs) have become the optimal solution for long-distance, high-capacity power transmission. However, the tri-post insulator may develop micro-cracks, gaps, and defects that degrade mechanical and insulation performance in GIL, posing risks of discharge breakdown and fracture. Special ultrasonic modes show great potential for identifying in complex structures, requiring deeper exploration of propagation mechanisms. Based on this, this article establishes wave equations and analyzes multimodal dispersion behaviors of ultrasonic guided waves in tri-post insulators. Sensors set at 9°, 25°, and 90° detect the leg defects, gas gaps, and belly holes using combined longitudinal/shear and bulk waves excited at 800 kHz and 2 MHz, with L(0,1) mode and critical angle analysis, supporting development of instrument incident parameters and detection modules. Simulations show critical wave transmission causes echo attenuation and significant reflections, forming defect waves with characteristic peaks in 0.1 mm. Waveform changes correlate with defect size, and energy decreases linearly with position. To address curvature-induced wave effects and signal distortion, a VMD-BAS-LSSVM machine learning method is proposed to recognize various micro-defects. The proposed method achieves 7.71% improvement in accuracy compared with conventional approaches, with classification errors below 5%, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness for high-precision detection of micro-defects in GIL insulators.
Keywords: Critical wave equation | defect feature extraction | gas insulated metal-enclosed transmission line (GIL) | machine learning recognition | multimode ultrasonic wave detection | tri-post insulator
