Title: The Impact of Financial Intelligence on Firm Performance: A Technology Acceptance Theory Perspective
Abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly disrupted the traditional finance domain. The application of AI in finance is referred to as financial intelligence. However, the theoretical understanding of why and how firms adopt financial intelligence remains underdeveloped. To address these research gaps, this study examines the key factors influencing the intention to adopt financial intelligence systems in the finance domain and investigates perceived firm performance associated with their adoption. We have developed a theoretical framework based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and formulated research hypotheses. To test these hypotheses, we used a structured, pre-tested instrument and collected 463 valid responses from finance professionals regarding their perceptions of financial intelligence systems adoption. We analysed the data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Our findings indicate that effort expectancy, performance expectancy, attitude, perceived trust, organisational competency, and organisational innovativeness are significant predictors of the intention to adopt financial intelligence systems. In contrast, neither social influence nor perceived risk was found to be statistically significant. Notably, performance expectancy has a strong impact on the development of a positive attitude toward financial intelligence systems. We also discovered a partially significant mediating effect of attitude on the relationship between effort expectancy and performance expectancy concerning the intention to adopt financial intelligence systems. The adoption of financial intelligence systems has a positive impact on firm performance. These insights will help firms identify the key factors that influence the adoption of financial intelligence systems and develop effective strategies for their implementation. Additionally, they will encourage future research into governance mechanisms that facilitate the responsible integration of these systems. This study serves as a valuable guide to the effective adoption of financial intelligence systems and represents the first comprehensive research on this topic among Indian firms, utilising the adapted UTAUT model, an extension of the TAM.
Keywords: Adoption | Artificial Intelligence | Finance | Financial Intelligence | Fintech | Firm Performance

Title: A Reliable Bayesian Deep Learning Framework With Rectified Flow for Fault Diagnosis Under Limited Data
Abstract: Despite advancements in intelligent fault diagnosis, the lack of sufficient training data remains a critical barrier in real-world industrial scenarios. To tackle this issue, numerous deep generative models have been proposed. However, existing methods often exhibit suboptimal generation quality, slow speed, and resource inefficiency when generating multi-class samples. Moreover, although the generated data can enhance the robustness of diagnostic models, it cannot ensure well-calibrated confidence estimates, and the reliability of predictions remains a persistent concern. To address these challenges in a unified manner, we propose a Bayesian Deep Learning Framework with a Rectified Flow-based Model (BDRF). Rectified Flow is introduced as the backbone for high-quality and efficient data augmentation by transforming Gaussian noise into industrial data distributions via optimized ordinary differential equations. We further incorporate classifier-free guidance algorithm to enable conditional multi-class generation within a single model. To bridge the gap between data-driven generation and domain-specific knowledge, large language models and text embeddings are leveraged to extract semantic information from fault descriptions as conditions, enhancing generation realism and interpretability. Finally, to remedy the issue of misaligned confidence, BDRF employs a Bayesian diagnostic classifier using the last-layer Laplace Approximation. Comprehensive experiments conducted on a benchmark simulation dataset and a real-world industrial dataset demonstrate that BDRF integrates data augmentation and calibrated confidence, effectively advancing the automation of fault diagnosis processes by improving both prediction performance and reliability under limited data. Note to Practitioners - In industries where automation is increasingly crucial, intelligent fault diagnosis methods are vital to maintaining the efficiency, productivity, and reliability of operations. However, these methods often struggle due to limited data, leading to inaccurate predictions and uncalibrated confidence in diagnostic results. This research proposes a unified framework, BDRF, that tackles these two critical issues simultaneously. BDRF introduces a Rectified Flow-based generation module and leverages large language models to incorporate domain-specific knowledge from fault descriptions, improving both the quality and efficiency of data generation for training diagnostic models. Additionally, a Bayesian diagnostic classifier is employed to enhance the reliability of predictions, thereby mitigating the risk of overconfidence or underconfidence in fault detection. Based on our experiments, BDRF demonstrates strong applicability in sectors with limited industrial fault data, such as condition monitoring for complex machinery including chemical processes and multi-phase flow systems. Furthermore, BDRF's ability to generate high-quality data and enhance classification reliability in resource-constrained environments makes it an effective instrument for improving automation in other domains like maintenance, healthcare, and finance.
Keywords: Bayesian deep learning | confidence calibration | Fault diagnosis | generative models | limited data

Title: Comparative Evaluation of Hybrid Deep Learning Models for mmWave Radar-Based Multihand Gesture Recognition
Abstract: According to data from the World Federation of the Hearing Impaired and the World Health Organization, in the world, there are about 72 million people who suffer from hearing impairment, and the total population of hearing-impaired people is 360 million, out of which 32 million are children. This group of individuals uses hand gestures as the main form of communication. The objective of hand gesture recognition is the acquisition of the hand-gesture data using a series of sensors. Many vision-based methods have been developed for HGR with an impressive level of accuracy; however, its performance is often impaired by the variation in lighting, occlusion and privacy issues. These shortcomings correspond to huge practical impediments for real-time applications. The millimetre-wave (mmWave) radar sensing dataset, which was deployed in this work using the AWR1642BOOST platform from Texas Instruments, is a potential alternative, given its tolerance to lighting conditions, its ability to see through some materials and its privacy-enhancing properties. The aim of this work is to realise high-performance classification of multihand gestures using mmWave radar point cloud data. This paper presents the comparative analysis of hybrid deep learning models for mmWave radar-based multihand gesture recognition based on a publicly available dataset. In this study, we trained, tested and validated a 1D-CNN with a gated MLP, a pure 1D-CNN and a CNN extractor with bidirectional LSTM. The CNN–LSTM model has the least number of parameters, 1,020,941, while achieving the best overall performance. It achieved a training accuracy of 99.73%, a validation accuracy of 97.02% and a test accuracy of 97.73%. The corresponding values of precision, recall and F1-score were 0.9759, 0.9791 and 0.9773, respectively. Cross-validation results also indicate its robustness, such that the mean accuracy is 93.9 and the standard deviation is 0.0146.
Keywords: 1D-CNN | 1D-CNN–GatedMLP | AWR1642BOOST | CNN–LSTM | human–computer interaction | multihand gesture | radar-based gesture

Title: Introducing Nylon Face Mask Attacks: A Dataset for Evaluating Generalised Face Presentation Attack Detection
Abstract: Face recognition systems are increasingly deployed across a wide range of applications, including smartphone authentication, access control, and border security. However, these systems remain vulnerable to presentation attacks (PAs), which can significantly compromise their reliability. In this work, we introduce a new dataset focused on a novel and realistic presentation attack instrument called Nylon Face Masks (NFMs), designed to simulate advanced 3D spoofing scenarios. NFMs are particularly concerning due to their elastic structure and photorealistic appearance, which enable them to closely mimic the victim's facial geometry when worn by an attacker. To reflect real-world smartphone-based usage conditions, we collected the dataset using an iPhone 11 Pro, capturing 3,760 bona fide samples from 100 subjects and 51,281 NFM attack samples across four distinct presentation scenarios involving both humans and mannequins. We benchmark the dataset using five state-of-theart PAD methods to evaluate their robustness under unseen attack conditions. The results demonstrate significant performance variability across methods, highlighting the challenges posed by NFMs and underscoring the importance of developing PAD techniques that generalise effectively to emerging spoofing threats.
Keywords: Biometric | Deep learning | Face Recognition | Presentation Attacks

Title: Portable NIR spectroscopy and machine learning for quantifying formaldehyde adulteration in buffalo milk
Abstract: This study uses portable spectroscopy, spectral preprocessing, principal component analysis (PCA), and machine learning (ML) to detect and quantify formaldehyde adulteration in buffalo milk. A calibration dataset was created by spiking milk samples with varying concentrations of formaldehyde (0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0, and 50.0%) to simulate varying levels of adulteration. Spectral data were acquired in the near-infrared (NIR) range (900–1700 nm) using a portable spectrophotometer. Model performance was assessed using two concentration ranges: a low-level adulteration subset (0–10%) to mimic realistic adulteration scenarios, and the entire dataset (0–50%) to evaluate performance across a broader range. The regression model had coefficient of determination (R<sup>2</sup>) values of 0.922–0.998, RMSE of 0.745 − 0.724, and RPD of 3.582–20.490 for 0–10% and 0–50% ranges, respectively, suggesting good to exceptional predictive performance. In classification, the 10-fold cross-validated Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) ranged from 0.845 ± 0.050 (0–10%) to 0.922 ± 0.019 (0–50%), indicating robust, stable performance. These findings suggest the use of portable NIR spectroscopy in conjunction with machine learning for quick, non-destructive identification of formaldehyde in milk.
Keywords: Adulteration | Formaldehyde | Formalin | Milk | Portable NIR spectrophotometer

Title: Machine Learning for Bearing Health Monitoring: A Controlled Experimental Benchmark Using Vibration-Based Statistical Features
Abstract: Reliable condition monitoring of rolling element bearings is essential for improving machinery availability and reducing unplanned downtime. Machine learning (ML) techniques have been widely applied for vibration-based bearing fault diagnosis; however, reported performance is often difficult to interpret due to variations in datasets, operating conditions, and validation protocols. This study presents a controlled experimental benchmark evaluating three classical ML algorithms—Support Vector Machine (SVM), k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN)—for vibration-based fault classification of cylindrical roller bearings. Experiments were conducted on SKF N204 bearings using a machinery fault simulator under three bearing conditions (healthy, outer race defect, and roller defect) at four rotational speeds (100–400 RPM). Artificial defects were introduced using electrical discharge machining (EDM), and vibration signals were acquired using a National Instruments data acquisition system. Root mean square (RMS), kurtosis, and crest factor were extracted as interpretable statistical features, resulting in a dataset of 119 feature samples. Model performance was evaluated using stratified train–validation–test splits, with k-fold cross-validation applied uniformly across all classifiers, including the ANN, to ensure fair comparison. Under the present laboratory conditions, the ANN exhibited the most consistent performance across validation and testing, while SVM and k-NN showed slightly lower validation accuracy but comparable testing behavior. The results demonstrate that high classification accuracy can be achieved using simple statistical features and classical ML models in a controlled setting. However, the findings should be interpreted as upper-bound diagnostic performance under laboratory conditions, rather than direct indicators of industrial-scale generalization. The study provides a transparent benchmarking reference and highlights the trade-off between interpretability, data efficiency, and classification performance in bearing health monitoring applications.
Keywords: Bearing fault diagnosis | Controlled experimental benchmarking | Cylindrical roller bearings | Machine learning | Statistical features | Vibration analysis

Title: Domain Generalised Adaptive Compressive Sensing with AMP and Attention Based Recovery
Abstract: Deep Learning based Compressive Sensing (DLCS) with block-based measurements brings a paradigm shift in the way images are acquired. It promises fast recovery from minimal measurements compared to traditional CS algorithms. However, key challenges, such as uniform measurement rate allocation across blocks, model learning for each rate, and models trained for each image family, limit its widespread adoption. In this work, we propose a novel Adaptive Rate Allocator integrated with a deep learning-based CS recovery network. Our Edge Aware Adaptive Rate Allocator assigns measurement rates based on block-level edge and texture information, considering multi-scale edge features. This efficient approach eliminates the need for expensive GPU computations during the sensing process. For recovery, we develop a Unified Matrix learned end-to-end, where the first n rows accommodate any measurement rate. The receiver employs an AMP-based recovery network that initially uses lightweight CNN denoisers for early iterations, followed by a CBAM ResNet attention module as a denoiser for later stages. Unlike complex transformer-based networks, this simple Deep unrolling on the effective AMP algorithm provides a simple yet effective solution for CS recovery problems. The network is trained on a multi-domain dataset. It employs a weighted combination of smooth L1 loss and SSIM function as a loss function to optimize PSNR and SSIM metrics. Extensive experimentation shows that the proposed method beats the performance of the other state-of-the-art techniques on standard datasets as well as generalizes well to completely new and unseen image classes, proving its practical viability.
Keywords: Approximate Message passing (AMP) | Block based Compressed sensing (BCS) | Convolution Block Attention Module (CBAM) | Deep Leaning based Compressed Sensing (DLCS) | Edge based rate allocation

Title: Cross-Domain Detection of AI-Generated Songs: Benchmarking Encoder Models on Bahasa Indonesia
Abstract: In recent years, advances in deep learning have significantly improved our ability to detect highly realistic AIgenerated song content. This progress has raised concerns about copyright protection, cultural authenticity, and the spread of misleading content. Despite growing global attention, there are still very few research studies related to this domain, especially in low-resource languages such as Bahasa Indonesia, due to the lack of appropriate datasets. To address this gap, we compiled and gathered a dataset of Indonesian songs collected from publicly available sources on social media, consisting of both real performances and AI-generated modifications, reflecting real situations in which AI-generated content is usually shared. We investigate our detection strategies by comparing several detection techniques using established audio encoders such as AST, Wave2Vec2, and WavLM. These models are then evaluated on unseen and different domain datasets. This is a crucial challenge given the rapid growth of AI music generation technologies. This experiment highlights both techniques and offers new insights into cross-generator detection, as well as dataset design and model robustness, which are important for protecting musical integrity in the era of generative AI.

Title: MicroPolluScan: A Deep Learning-Based Monitoring System for Classification of Microplastic Contamination in Fishponds
Abstract: Microplastics in aquatic life are hazardous to sea life, food safety, and aquaculture. In this paper, we describe MicroPolluScan, an AI-based deep learning system which uses automated microscopic image analysis to detect, classify, and quantify microplastic contamination in fishponds. To facilitate the development, we employed an Agile Scrum-CRISP-DM paradigm, that is an architectural process based on an iterative software design methodology, along with structured data science methodology. Microscopic pictures of beads, fragments, and fibers were taken from fishponds in Lucena City, augmented with Roboflow, and trained in YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 networks on Google Colab. Comparison results demonstrated that YOLOv8 provided the best performance (precision =0.82, recall =0.85, F1 =0.83, mAP=0.89) because of the anchor-free detection head and C2f supporting mechanism. A fine-tuned model was implemented in a Flask-based web system, for real-time detection and visualization dashboards for practitioners of aquaculture. Software quality of the software evaluated following ISO/IEC 25010 has a mean of 3.80 (Strongly Agree) followed by a Cronbach's α of 0.89 indicating instrument stability and system usability. Our results show that by combining computer vision and web technologies microplastic monitoring can be automated leading to rapid decision making. We envisage future research projects to provide more diversity on the dataset, incorporating IoT-based sensors, and applying explainable-AI models for improved transparency and ground application.
Keywords: Aquaculture | Deep Learning | Microplastic | YOLOv8

Title: Noise-Robust Automatic Speech Recognition for Indonesian Speech Using CNN and GoogLeNet
Abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems often experience significant performance degradation in noisy real-world environments, particularly for resource-constrained languages such as Indonesian where training data is still relatively scarce. This study aims to develop a noise-robust end-to-end ASR system by quantitatively comparing two different encoder architectures: a standard Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a complex multi-scale GoogLeNet-Attention architecture. Both models are trained end-to-end using Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss on the Indonesian Common Voice dataset, which is rigorously enriched with non-stationary environmental noise from the ESC-50 dataset at various Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs). Experimental results show that the standard CNN architecture significantly outperforms the GoogLeNet-Attention model, achieving a Word Error Rate (WER) of 45.45% compared to 51.21%. Furthermore, the CNN model proved to be significantly more computationally efficient, requiring approximately 35% less training time per epoch. These findings suggest that for low-resource tasks characterized by high acoustic variability, welltuned deep CNNs with increased capacity offer a superior balance between robustness and efficiency compared to complex multi-scale architectures.
Keywords: Automatic Speech Recognition | CNN | Deep Learning | GoogLeNet | Indonesian Language | Noise Robustness

Title: Age Estimation from Speech Using Whisper-based Speaker Representations
Abstract: Automatic age estimation from speech is a challenging paralinguistic task due to subtle age-related acoustic cues and variability in recording conditions across corpora. In this work, we investigate age estimation using speaker representations. Our approach employs an automatic speaker verification (ASV)adapted Whisper-small encoder as a fixed feature extractor and trains a regression head on top of the resulting embeddings. Experiments on multiple corpora demonstrate that ASV-oriented Whisper representations consistently achieve superior performance and outperform open-source self-supervised learning (SSL)-based baselines when evaluated across heterogeneous datasets recorded under diverse acoustic conditions, including TIMIT, AgeVoxCeleb, NIST SRE10, and RusIVR. We further validate the results using a balanced evaluation protocol on AgeVoxCeleb and RusIVR, where the proposed system achieves an MAE of 6.35 years and 81% accuracy within a 10 year tolerance, outperforming both open-source baselines and an anonymized commercial system. To analyze potential speaker-identity leakage, we introduce VoiceBiometricAge, a new dataset, and conduct both qualitative and quantitative representation analyses. The results indicate that the learned age projection substantially reduces speaker separability. Finally, duration-based experiments confirm that the proposed method remains effective for short utterances, achieving strong accuracy with only 5-7 seconds of speech.
Keywords: age estimation | cross-corpus generalization | speaker representations | speaker verification | speech paralinguistics | Whisper

Title: Poems as Musical Instruments: an AI Music Performance Interface Based on the Concepts of Chinese Qin Songs
Abstract: The author has designed a new interface of musical expression called Poem-Qin, which reveals the relationship between text and music, supporting self-accompanied singing and cross-media musical practices. Drawing inspiration from Chinese qin songs and movable-type printing, the author creatively integrates Chinese characters into the interface, controlling music with tone inflections and linguistic rhythms. Moreover, they have developed an AI model for text-to-melody composing to assist in creating new music content. User and audience testing has demonstrated that it offers a positive experience and effective creative results.

Title: BioPrint-LKM: An evidence-grounded large knowledge model for bioprinting knowledge retrieval and parameter initialization
Abstract: Bioprinting workflows often require repeated trial-and-error to achieve acceptable print quality, while relevant process knowledge and parameter ranges are dispersed across a rapidly growing literature. General-purpose language models can assist with scientific questions, but their output may be difficult to verify and can include unsupported claims. In this work, we present BioPrint-LKM, a bioprinting large knowledge model (LKM) implemented using a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline with citation grounding to provide traceable, evidence-based responses for bioprinting tasks. A curated knowledge base was constructed from 621 bioprinting papers, which were converted to text, segmented into passages, embedded into a vector index, and retrieved using exact nearest-neighbor similarity search. Retrieved passages were assembled into an augmented context and used to constrain generation under a domain prompt guideline that enforces source and page-level citation. The LKM was evaluated using 30 bioprinting-related questions and three large language model (LLM) backbones (GPT-4o, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, and Gemini-2.5-Flash). Across the tested 30-question benchmark, retrieval and citation grounding improved question-answer accuracy compared with LLM-only baselines by an average of 24.7, particularly for queries requiring paper specific details such as component concentrations, mixing ratios, and instrument settings. A retrieval hyperparameter sweep further showed that top- k and passage length affect both evidence coverage and noise, with an intermediate passage length providing the best overall performance. Beyond knowledge retrieval, the LKM was applied to bioprinting process setup by generating initial parameter sets that were used to warm-start multi-objective Bayesian optimization toward target filament width and height. Compared with manual initialization, BioPrint-LKM-assisted initialization reduced the number of calibration trials by an average of 36.0 and supported downstream printing demonstrations, including conductive cell-laden hydrogel lines and an anatomical ear model. These results suggest that BioPrint-LKM, a citation-grounded LKM, can serve as a practical lab-assistive tool to accelerate bioprinting setup and improve reproducibility.
Keywords: 3D bioprinting | Biofabrication | Citation grounding | Hydrogel | Large knowledge model | Machine learning | Process calibration | Retrieval-augmented generation

Title: Mapping latent environmental performance regimes: a spatial and explainable machine learning approach
Abstract: The purposes of the study were to offer a holistic approach to the assessment of global environmental sustainability, using spatial analysis, clustering, and explainable machine learning by employing data from 180 countries of the 2024 Environmental Performance Index. The methodological approach used is based on the integration of K-means clustering, regression analysis, and explainability using the SHAP model. Spatial analysis shows that regional gaps persist with Western Europe, North America, and parts of East Asia having good levels of performance, while Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia consistently rank the lowest. The K-Means clustering method identified five structurally different types of countries, offering differentiation beyond aggregate rankings. Finally, in the predictive phase, the best accuracy is found to be through the Stacking Regressor method (R<sup>2</sup>: 0.9997; MAE: 0.1235), followed by Gradient Boosting (R<sup>2</sup>: 0.9490) and XGBoost (R<sup>2</sup>: 0.9070). The results of the feature importance using the SHAP method have identified the top drivers to be Ecosystem Vitality (3.1394) and Environmental Health (3.0261); however, it is noticeable that Climate Change, Air Quality, Water Resources, and Sanitation/Drinking Water have also played a role. The results illustrate the value of the argument that different countries with similar overall scores may have significantly different environmental structures. The proposed framework offers a clear instrument for the development of sustainability-oriented policies.
Keywords: Ecosystem vitality | Environmental health | Machine learning | SHAP | Spatial analysis | Sustainability

Title: Bidirectional Process Prediction in the Laser-Induced-Graphene Production Using Blackbox Deep Learning
Abstract: Machine learning offers significant potential for automating manufacturing processes through prediction of parameters and properties. However, its adoption is limited by the needs for process-specific expertise, complex analytical models, and large, high-quality training datasets. This study introduces a streamlined, non-analytical blackbox deep-learning approach tailored to resource- and knowledge-limited settings. Applied to laser-induced graphene, an emerging technique for fabricating flexible electronics, this method uses a simple neural network for bidirectional predictions: forward estimation of graphene properties from laser parameters, and inverse prediction of laser settings from target properties. Using only a small dataset of 500 moderate-quality, high-variance samples, the model attained joint prediction accuracies of up to 95% on validation samples, and 96% in a functional flexible circuit. These results match or surpass more elaborate physics-informed or multi-component models in the literature, with minimal resources and no preprocessing. The method is widely applicable to various functional materials and fabrication techniques, minimizing dependence on prior knowledge, manual optimization, and specialized equipment. This demonstrates that high predictive performance can emerge from minimal overhead, making machine learning a practical, accessible instrument that democratizes intelligent manufacturing in graphene-based and related systems, enabling efficient and scalable real-world innovation.
Keywords: bidirectional prediction | blackbox modeling | deep learning | flexible electronics | laser-induced graphene | machine learning

Title: Addressing public speaking anxiety: a pedagogical action research approach
Abstract: Public Speaking Anxiety (PSA) is proven to have an adverse effect on the overall academic performance and future employability of young undergraduate population. With the increasing global interest towards PSA, there is a dearth of pedagogically anchored, culture-specific, and action-oriented research in the Pakistani context. The current study fills this gap by utilizing Pedagogical Action Research (PedAR), an active, cyclical model that integrates reflective teaching with curriculum development. A sample of 42 undergraduate students of Business and Professional Speech course at a private university in Karachi were recruited for this study. The research consisted of three action cycles with interventions that were customized to target the cognitive, behavioral and physiological outcomes of PSA. The ARTICULATE, CAPTIVATE, and CASCADE frameworks were employed and inspired by psychological theory, communication pedagogy, and digital technology (for instance, Yoodli AI). Quantitative data were collected using the Public Speaking Anxiety Scale (PSAS) and qualitative data were based on researcher’s observations, journals, and reflections of the students. Results demonstrated significant PSA decrease in all domains, and improvements in student performance. The research highlights the significance of the PedAR as a PSA-lowering instrument, and as a model of teacher-driven reform that is responsive, reflective, and culturally dynamic. By presenting the teacher as a researcher and the classroom as a site for transformation, this study validates PedAR’s promise as a tool for closing the gaps among theory, policy and practice, while fostering scalable, contextually grounded innovations in Pakistan’s educational context.
Keywords: cognitive restructuring | experiential learning | instructional frameworks | pedagogical action research (PedAR) | Public speaking anxiety

Title: Composite Algorithm for Autism Spectrum Disorder Early Identification
Abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that requires early diagnosis to facilitate timely intervention and care. Herein, we present an analysis of a publicly accessible dataset accessed through the ASD Tests app created by the Nelson Marlborough Institute of Technology. The dataset is comprised of self-reported answers of every age group adolescent and adults gathered using standardized screening instruments like Q-CHAT-10 and AQ10, however the experiments were performed on adolescent and adult's dataset. Preprocessing steps involved the removal of duplicates, missing value handling, and normalization of data to achieve the best model performance. A wide range of machine learning models was used, such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), AdaBoostM1, Logit Boost, and ensemble models like Voting, Stacking, and Boosting. The performance metrics used for evaluation were accuracy, precision, recall, F-measure, and ROC-AUC, supplemented with 5-fold cross-validation. SVM acquired high accuracy of 98%. This research provides robustness and cross validation model confirms the model stability, and highlights the potential for remote and accessible screening. This research open the pathway for early and scalable intervention.
Keywords: Autism spectrum Disorder | Ensemble Methods | ML | Weka

Title: Understanding the Phonetic Similarity in Imagined Speech Using Cross-Task Saliency Mapping
Abstract: Imagined speech electroencephalogram (EEG) provides a promising avenue for decoding internal language representations in brain-computer interfaces, yet the relationship between phonologically similar words and their corresponding EEG patterns during imagined articulation remains underexplored. To address this question, Multi-Scale EEGNet (MS-EEGNet), a modified version of the established EEGNet architecture with multi-scale frequency-aware capabilities, was developed. This framework was evaluated on two classification paradigms: binary classification grouping /iy/-phoneme-containing words and multi-class classification treating each word distinctly, while Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was employed to generate saliency maps for assessing activation overlap across tasks. Consistent performance exceeding 97% on all binary tasks and 96.43% on multi-class imagined speech decoding was demonstrated. Importantly, significant temporal overlap in saliency maps from different tasks was exhibited, as quantified through Jaccard similarity and validated statistically. This indicates the presence of task-invariant neural features linked to phonological structure. These findings suggest that imagined speech representations are organized along phonetic dimensions, offering new insights into neural language encoding and promising directions for efficient EEG-based speech decoding systems.
Keywords: Computational Neuroscience | Deep Learning | EEGNet | Explainable AI | Grad-CAM

Title: Multimodal electronic information fusion sensing method for complex scenarios
Abstract: AI-driven personalized college English learning platforms have made great progress thanks to deep learner modeling and adaptive content delivery. But a lot of current systems mainly depend on interaction logs and sound, so it’s hard to tell how well people speak when there’s background noise, different devices, and unclear words. To solve these problems, we redesign a closed-loop personalized learning platform and add a standard-webcam optical articulation stream. Platform integrates: (i) Learning behavior trajectory; (ii) Speech audio; (iii) Optical cue such as lip / jaw motion, face landmark, gaze / attention proxy into one end-to-end pipeline of multi-modal perception → representation learning → learner state inference → adaptive practice & feedback. For audiovisual speech representation, we use cross-modal temporal alignment and a reliability-weighted gating method, with modality weights adjusted based on online quality metrics (signal-to-noise ratio, distribution shift, local consistency) and further regularized through uncertainty-aware fusion. Besides vocabulary/reading personalization, the new platform offers pronunciation-focused formative feedback that aligns phoneme-level acoustic confidence with visual articulation consistency, and uses visual attention signals to improve intervention timing. Experiments on the platform learning datasets show good learner-state prediction performance (AUC of ROC curve up to 0.835). In pronunciation evaluation, adding optical cues improves the speaking score AUC from 0.781 (audio only) to 0.846 (full multimodal), reduces pronunciation error rate from 18.4% to 12.7%, and achieves a weekly retention improvement of 13.2%. A progressive personalization ablation increases 7-day retention from 52.3% to 66.2% and average weekly learning time from 72.5 to 90.2 minutes after adding user embeddings, item response features, spaced repetition, and reinforcement learning sequencing. These findings suggest that light weight webcams for optical sensing may improve the robustness and interpretability of speaking evaluations, as well as help with closed loop personalization at scale for college English learning.
Keywords: audiovisual fusion | multimodal learning analytics | Optical articulation modeling | personalized English learning | visual speech features | webcam-based feedback

Title: IoT-Driven Intelligent Water Fountain Controlled by MHRISCNN Algorithm for Music Therapy
Abstract: As per ancient age water fountains have been used for multipurpose entertainment events like laser shows at statue of unity Ahmadabad, Vradavan garden, Mysore and Akshardham etc. Design such fountains becomes the best opportunity for interdisciplinary learners. It's difficult to design the physical structure and control system of a fountain with water jet dancing effects with light which change the mood swing of a psychological patient. This paper gives ideas about indoor fountains in educational institutions and hospitals to target psychological patients to heal the mind and for students to concentrate on specific mind states for study. Proposed model work on IoT and modified machine learning algorithms. It captures emotions and facial expressions of patients(Fountain Viewer) and detects mood. Accordingly it will select musical instruments from the playlist as per mood. It converts the signals to create patterns which are input for solenoid valves and light systems. Solenoid activity and light systems will generate different water jet dancing patterns and light glowing patterns for different mood based scenarios. For the healing process, body and mind response with music therapy is a new area. The challenging issues here are which ragas to listen to, when to listen and how much time to listen. Feature extraction techniques from digital signal processing are adopted to address the particular raga with notes and swaras. Machine learning algorithms are used to classify the type of raga for a particular disease. Performance of classification of ragas is done using various classifier algorithms. MHRISCNN Algorithm (Mind Healing Raga Instrument Selection Convolution Neural Network) is being proposed which will select a particular Raga and instrument based on the person's mood at that time. This will help any person to reduce his or her stress who is near a fountain which in turn improves his health.
Keywords: IoT | Machine Learning | MHRISCNN | Music Therapy

Title: Leveraging Text and Image Information for Ovarian Tumors Segmentation in Ultrasound Images
Abstract: Accurate segmentation of ovarian tumors in ultrasound images is essential for early diagnosis and treatment planning. However, this task remains challenging due to the inherent limitations of ultrasound imaging, such as noise, shadowing, low contrast, and blurred tumor boundaries. Furthermore, the large variability in tumor shape, size, and position across patients further complicates traditional segmentation methods. Most existing deep learning approaches rely solely on visual features, overlooking the potential benefits of incorporating semantic information. In this study, we propose a novel multimodal segmentation framework that explicitly integrates both visual and textual information. Our architecture is based on a UNet-style backbone enhanced with a pretrained VGG16 encoder and a Spatial Pyramid Pooling Fast (SPPF) block for improved multi-scale feature learning. The key contribution lies in the integration of Image-Text Matching (ITM) modules into the segmentation pipeline, enabling deep cross-modal interaction between image features and semantic tumor descriptions. Additionally, we introduce a lightweight captioning module that automatically generates textual descriptions from ultrasound images, allowing the model to be trained even when manual annotations are unavailable. To further enhance performance, we employ a combination of loss functions including Tversky, Weighted Binary Cross Entropy (WBCE), and Structure Similarity (SSIM), aiming to balance precision, recall, and structural similarity. Experimental results on the OTU_2d dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving 90.16% Dice, 82.05% IoU, 90.23% Recall, 91.12% Precision.
Keywords: ovarian tumor | segmentation | ultrasound images

Title: InfernoFusion: An Edge-Optimized Audio-Visual Deep Learning Framework for Early Fire Smoke Detection
Abstract: The requirement for early, dependable fire detection is very high because it reduces damage and satisfies public safety requirements in large-scale complex environments. The paper presents an audio-visual early fire and smoke detection system based on deep learning for real-time deployment on edge devices. Besides, the system is not limited to vision alone, which can fail at low illumination or be compromised by occlusion due to visual ambiguity, but combines the visual features of fire and smoke with cracks and hissing as complementary acoustic cues to curb robustness. Convolutional neural networks are used to process visual data along with preprocessing and augmentation techniques aimed at enhancing generalization, while audio signals are analyzed using spectral features for the detection of fire-related acoustic patterns. A fusion multimodal strategy combines the predictions of both modalities, which can greatly reduce the number of false alarms and improve detection accuracy. It is also optimized to perform lightweight inference and assessed under different lighting conditions, thus sustaining performance across varied low-lux environments with particular reliance on audio cues in circumstances where visual clarity is compromised. The proposed framework is also scalable to multi-camera environments through parallel edge processing and could be eased into existing fire safety infrastructures involving means such as surveillance systems, alarms, and IoT-based alert mechanisms. The experimental results confirmed the proposed edge-optimized multimodal strategy would give a practical, accurate, and robust solution for early fire detection in real-world applications.
Keywords: Audio-Visual Fusion | Convolutional Neural Networks | Deep Learning | Early Fire Detection | Edge Devices | Real-Time Safety Systems | Smoke Detection | YOLOv8

Title: Enhanced Gender Recognition in Telugu Speech Using Augmented Transgender Audio
Abstract: This study presents a comprehensive approach to gender classification in Telugu audio using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and pitch features. This work fills a critical gap in inclusivity within speech-based systems by expanding the problem to include transgender voices, building on earlier research that mainly concentrated on binary (male/female) classification. The proposed system has two primary objectives: robust preprocessing and feature extraction, and multi-model classification for gender prediction. Each audio sample was processed to extract MFCCs and pitch from a carefully selected and balanced dataset of male, female, and transgender voices that was standardized to 16 kHz. Five popular machine learning models - Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and XGBoost - were trained and evaluated. Data augmentation techniques, including minor pitch shifting and noise addition, were applied to improve model generalization, only for limited transgender samples to reduce data imbalance. The results show that the integration of the MFCC and pitch features with augmentation significantly improved performance, achieving a total accuracy of over 97% in both both SVM and MLP models. This study underscores the effectiveness of feature fusion and data balancing in multi-class gender classification and promotes inclusivity in modern voice recognition systems.
Keywords: audio processing | MFCC | MLP | pitch | Random Forest | SVM | transgender voice recognition | XGBoost

Title: Robust and Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Early Detection of Chronic Kidney Disease with XGBoost
Abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a progressive and frequently asymptomatic condition that impacts millions globally, resulting in significant health issues if not identified promptly. Timely and precise prediction is essential for facilitating prompt clinical intervention and alleviating the burden of renal failure. This paper presents a robust and clinically interpretable machine learning system for chronic kidney disease prediction, incorporating advanced data preparation, ensemble learning, and explainable AI methodologies. Missing values in clinical data are managed with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to produce realistic synthetic samples while maintaining feature distributions. Class imbalance, prevalent in chronic kidney disease datasets, is addressed by the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), facilitating impartial model training. The ensemble classifier, XGBoost, is refined by hyperparameter tuning and assessed using stringent 5-fold cross-validation on a merged dataset of internal (UCI CKD) and external clinical records, attaining 100 percent accuracy internally and 99 percent accuracy overall. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is utilized for model interpretability, pinpointing significant predictors such as hemoglobin, serum creatinine, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), which correspond with clinically acknowledged risk factors. The findings indicate that the suggested paradigm offers both superior predictive accuracy and transparent, reliable insights for doctors. This methodology enhances cutting-edge CKD prediction by integrating high precision, generalizability, and interpretability, providing a pragmatic instrument for early illness identification and preventive healthcare administration.
Keywords: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) | Explain- able AI (SHAP) | Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) | SMOTE Balancing | XGBoost

Title: An Explainability-Aware Transformer Framework for Brain Tumor Segmentation and Classification Using MRI
Abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging is one of the most commonly used neuro-oncology imaging modalities, which is a non-invasive mode of imaging and helps in detecting brain abnormalities in an effective way. Earlier researchers have demonstrated that brain tumor segmentation and classification can be effectively performed using deep learning techniques. Existing studies are primarily aimed at increasing prediction accuracy and provide insignificant consideration to model interpretability, limiting their practical application in clinical practice. To address this limitation, this research presents a two-stage explainable deep learning model, which combines transformer-based segmentation with an ensemble classification model that is consistent in explanations. The first stage introduces Swin-DS-HAFUNetv2, an enhanced transformer-based segmentation architecture that integrates hierarchical Swin Transformer encoders, refined hierarchical attention fusion, a contextual bottleneck transformer, and multi-scale deep supervision to improve tumor localization in T1-weighted MRI, particularly under low-contrast and irregular morphological conditions. The second stage includes the ECWMEv2 ensemble classifier, which integrates a perturbation analysis based on Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) to systematically assess the consistency and clinical significance of visual explanations for candidate models. Only those architectures that exhibit stable and pathology-consistent explanations, such as ConvNeXt, Swin Transformer, and EVA02, are stored and merged by means of explanation-weighted soft voting with XGBoost-based meta-learning. Experimental evaluation on the BRISC2025 benchmark dataset indicates that Swin-DS-HAFUNetv2 has a mean Dice coefficient of 0.9782 and Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.8656, with ECWMEv2 having a classification accuracy of 0.9917 and a Macro-F1 score of 0.9867. The mean Grad-CAM IoU of 0.692 reflects uniform and anatomically significant consistency of attention to tumor regions. These results demonstrate that the integration of explanation stability as a fundamental design principle significantly improves model robustness and interpretability to provide a methodologically validated and benchmark-level framework for future studies of multimodal and clinically oriented brain tumor analysis systems.
Keywords: Brain tumor segmentation | classification | explainable artificial intelligence | Grad-CAM stability | medical image analysis | transformer networks

Title: Hybrid Machine Learning Approach for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction Using Enhanced SVM Model
Abstract: This paper has introduced a Hybrid Machine Learning architecture on which the Enhanced SVM model predicts cardiovascular diseases with high accuracy. The proposed system combines both hybrid feature selection and kernel optimization methods to obtain high diagnostic accuracy and strength. Based on the Cleveland Heart Disease data, the model has high performance in terms of accuracy of 96.4, precision of 96.0 and AUC of 97.8 when compared to traditional classifiers, which include: Logistic Regression, KNN, and Random Forest. The methodology focuses on preprocessing of data, balanced sampling and hybrid feature optimization to minimize noise and bias that improves stability of predictivity. The model is tested experimentally to be able to separate healthy and diseased patients with misclassification occurring at a minimum level. The suggested hybrid design is a scalable and valid diagnostic instrument that can be used in smart health systems. The study forms groundwork on future advances in predictive cardiology and data-driven healthcare intelligence based on AI.
Keywords: Cardiovascular Disease Prediction | Enhanced SVM | Feature Optimization | Healthcare Analytics | Hybrid Machine Learning

Title: DeepTrustChain: A Blockchain-Anchored Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for High-Integrity Fake News Detection
Abstract: The uncontrolled propagation of fake news on the digital frontiers continues to undermine the confidence of the populace, disorganizing supply chains and misled decision making on high stake regions. The existing fake news detectors are all largely text-based and are driven by machine learning or deep learning and do not pay much focus to integrity, provenance, and post-hoc verifiability of the model predictions. Moreover, the current procedures are usually trained and tested in controlled settings and do not facilitate adversarial manipulation of content and metadata, and are rarely provided to produce audit trails which cannot be modified by auditors of identified artifacts. It is in this respect that this paper introduces DeepTrustChain, a blockchain anchored hybrid deep learning framework in the detection of high-integrity fake news. The proposed system uses an encoder of text a transformer encoder with a Bidirectional recurrent module and an ensemble stacking layer to improve the robustness and generalization owing to the recent discoveries on stacking and ensemble methods of identifying fake news, and reliability-based methods of evaluation. At the same time, DeepTrustChain computes a trust score that represents a combination of model confidence and source level and propagation level features and anchors the prediction and proof on an authorized blockchain. Such a design provides verifiable, immutable records of the histories of the detection results and enables the decentralized checking of the news items by time. The conceptual evaluation of the framework in respect to multilingual and low resource states and can also leverage advancements in sequence modeling and representation learning in other applications such as music and affective computing. The key feature of DeepTrustChain is that it is an architecture that integrates integrity conscious hybrid deep learning with blockchain based anchoring, so that simultaneously achieves the high degree of detection accuracy, resistance to decision manipulation, and ultimate traceability of decision making regarding fake news.
Keywords: blockchain | Detection of fake news | ensemble learning | hybrid deep learning | integrity conscious classification | low resource languages | transformer networks

Title: Machine Learning-Driven Prediction and Detection of 5G-Induced Nonlinear Interference in Radio Altimeters
Abstract: Systems coexisting with mid-band 5G with aeronautical radio altimeters (RAs) have brought about a substantial safety issue by adjacent-band electromagnetic interference that has the potential to cause nonlinear distortion, compress gain on the IF, and cause errors in altitude measurements. These mechanisms are found to be described by conventional analytical and simulation-based studies, which do not have the ability to predict the severity of interference quantitatively, nor do they have the ability to detect the degradation of performance in real time. In this paper, a machine learning-based scheme will be suggested to detect and forecast the effect of 5 G on RAs due to interference. Classification and regression models were built using the features obtained by using the IF spectral responses and experimental injection measurements that were used to estimate the state of interference, height-error ratio, and the onset of nonlinear saturation. The offered classifier was found to be 98.4 percent accurate, and the regression model was able to predict height-error ratios with a ratio error rate of 0.37. The model found the critical interference threshold (e.g., -15 dBm at 4000 MHz) accurately, and the sensitivity of predicting the NCD conditions was 95.1 %. The outcomes prove that ML is an effective tool in improving the assessment of RA interference and assurance of safety.
Keywords: 5G interference | aviation safety | electromagnetic compatibility | gain compression | IF signal analysis | interference detection | interference prediction | machine learning | nonlinear distortion | Radio altimeter

Title: Detecting Sugarcane Leaf Diseases using InceptionV3 Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Sugarcane is an essential commercial crop whose productivity and quality are profoundly influenced by foliar diseases, including red rot, smut, and yellow leaf disease. Timely and precise identification of these diseases is essential to mitigate economic losses and promote sustainable farming practices. This research presents an automated method for detecting sugarcane leaf diseases using the InceptionV3 convolutional neural network (CNN). A total of 6,748 high-resolution leaf images including 11 categories of healthy and sick leaves were gathered, resized to 299 × 299 pixels, and normalized to optimize model performance. Transfer learning using the pre-trained InceptionV3 model was used for effective feature extraction and precise classification. The proposed technique attained an overall accuracy of 99.92%, with precision, recall, and F1-score at 99.55%, indicating robustness across disease groups. The model's resilience was also confirmed in actual field situations, encompassing occlusion, various soil backgrounds, and varied lighting and weather influences. Statistical significance tests showed that performance enhancements were not attributable to chance (p < 0.05). The findings demonstrate that the InceptionV3-based model is a dependable, scalable, and efficient instrument for automated sugarcane disease identification, facilitating prompt intervention and enhancing precision agriculture.
Keywords: Automated Disease Detection | Deep Learning | Image Classification | InceptionV3 | Leaf Disease Detection | Precision Agriculture | Sugarcane

Title: Speech Emotion Recognition Using Deep CNN-Bilstm with Attention Mechanism on EMO-DB Dataset
Abstract: This paper proposes a CNN-BiLSTM model with an attention mechanism for speech emotion recognition on the German EMO-DB corpus. The model classifies seven emotion categories and achieves a validation accuracy of 98.13%. Melspectrogram features are extracted using two convolutional blocks with 64 and 128 filters, followed by two bidirectional LSTM layers with 128 units to capture forward and backward temporal dependencies. An attention-based pooling strategy aggregates information across time instead of relying only on the final LSTM state, resulting in a 3.2% performance improvement over final-state pooling. To address the limited size of EMODB (535 utterances), eight-fold data augmentation is applied and validated through Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, a three-annotator perceptual study (κ=0.82,92 % agreement), and ablation experiments showing a 13 % improvement over non-augmented training. The model maintains over 84 % accuracy under white and babble noise at 10 dB SNR, achieves F1-scores above 0.97 for all emotion classes, and uses only 4.6 million parameters, making it computationally efficient compared to large transfer-learning models.
Keywords: affective computing | attention mechanism | CNNBiLSTM | deep learning | EMO-DB | mel spectrogram | Speech emotion recognition

Title: A Multimodal AI Framework for Tamil Speech Transcription, Translation, and Generative Visualization
Abstract: Multimodal artificial intelligence takes an integrated approach to language processing by combining various models. Tamil has over 75 million speakers worldwide but faces challenges in modern content processing because most conventional systems lack cultural understanding. This work presents a unified multimodal framework that converts Tamil audio into five synchronized outputs: Tamil transcription, English translation with cultural preservation, emotion classification, culturally relevant images, and creative text expansion. The framework includes five advanced models: Whisper Large V3 (transcription), Gemma 2 9B-IT (translation), DistilBERT (emotion analysis), FLUX.1-dev (image generation), and DeepSeek-R1 (text expansion). These operate in a parallel processing system where three independent branches work at the same time, cutting processing time by 40 percent. Experiments show 93.8 percent transcription accuracy, BLEU scores ranging from 0.68 to 0.78, 85.3 percent accuracy in emotion classification, image CLIP scores of 0.82, with a cultural relevance rating of 4.1 out of 5 from native speakers, and a text expansion ROUGE-L score of 0.76. Importantly, parallel processing keeps quality metrics the same as sequential execution without any decline. This work makes five specific contributions: (1) the first integrated Tamil-focused multimodal pipeline with cultural preservation, (2) practical application of cultural context through prompt engineering, (3) a parallel architecture that reduces latency by 40 percent, (4) emotioninformed image and text generation, and (5) a thorough evaluation that combines technical metrics with native speaker feedback. These findings show that multimodal systems can promote linguistic variety and digital accessibility for lowresource languages, laying the groundwork for culturally-aware content transformation in the Tamil ecosystem.
Keywords: Cultural Context Preservation | Emotion Analysis | Machine Translation | Multimodal AI | Parallel Processing | Tamil Speech Processing | Text-to-Image Generation

Title: LLM-Based Bitrate Selection Method for CMR-Supported Audio Codec
Abstract: Recent advances in AI-driven network algorithms have aimed to enhance user experience under diverse network conditions. However, designing and validating optimal AI models tailored to specific network environments and objectives remains a challenge for developers. To address this, frameworks such as netLLM [1], which integrates pretrained large language models (LLMs) with multimodal encoders, network heads, and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) [2], have been proposed and shown to improve performance through offline fine-tuning. In this paper, we extend the concept of netLLM to the bitrate optimization problem of audio codecs supporting Codec Mode Request (CMR). Unlike conventional offline training approaches, we propose an online learning-based bitrate selection method that dynamically adapts to fluctuating real-time communication environments. Our method leverages pretrained LLMs to adjust audio stream bitrates according to network conditions, achieving significant improvements in speech quality, as measured by the E-MODEL R-factor [4], compared to conventional AI models [7]. This study demonstrates an effective approach to audio streaming optimization through online fine-tuning, offering a novel pathway for improving speech quality under variable network conditions.
Keywords: AMR-WB | Audio Codec Mode Request | LLM | Real-time Transport Protocol | Reinforcement Learning | VoIP

Title: CRNN-Based Hierarchical Musician Identification in Classical Music
Abstract: This paper presents a machine-learning framework for identifying classical composers and performers based on stylistic characteristics embedded in audio recordings. Unlike conventional music recognition systems that rely on audio fingerprinting, the proposed approach focuses on expressive musical features such as articulation, phrasing, dynamics, and temporal shaping - properties that encapsulate interpreters' unique performance styles. The system integrates mel-spectrograms and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) with a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) architecture that captures both spatial and temporal attributes of musical expression. A hierarchical classification pipeline first determines the composer and subsequently refines the prediction to the performer within each composer group. The framework is supported by a user interface that accepts audio recordings and returns the model's predictions in real time. Our system integrates MFCC-based feature extraction with a hierarchical CRNN that performs both composer and performer classification. By modeling expressive cues and interpretive signatures, it achieves performer-level distinction, a capability largely absent in current music information retrieval (MIR) systems.
Keywords: Audio Feature Extraction | Classical Music | Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks | Music Information Retrieval

Title: An interpretable intelligent recognition method for voltage signals induced by wear debris in lubricating oil
Abstract: Monitoring and evaluating the in-service condition of equipment in real time is essential for maintaining the stable operation of large-scale complex electromechanical systems. Inductive oil debris sensors detect wear particles in lubricating oil via electromagnetic induction, providing a reliable basis for assessing the wear condition of critical mechanical components, and have been widely applied in the maintenance of large-scale mechanical equipment. However, the induced voltage signals generated by debris are usually weak and are difficult to identify accurately by manual feature extraction under the influence of various interferences, which limits the identification accuracy and generalization capability of inductive oil debris sensors. To address this issue, this paper proposes an intelligent recognition method for oil debris signals, referred to as PCatten. Firstly, the morphological stability of debris-induced signals under multiscale filtering is exploited to construct multiscale filtering features, which characterize the key geometric profiles and energy distribution of debris events and provide physically meaningful input representations for subsequent deep learning. Subsequently, a parallel convolution module is designed to perform branch-wise deep convolutional modeling of features at different scales, and an improved fusion attention module is introduced to adaptively recalibrate feature weights along the channel and temporal dimensions, thereby highlighting debrissensitive components and suppressing complex background interference. Finally, the reconstructed multiscale feature sequence is fed into a Vision Transformer, which captures long-range dependencies and cross-scale correlations through the self-attention mechanism, enabling accurate discrimination of debris-induced voltage signals under strong interference and low signal-to-noise ratios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves excellent performance on both three-coil sensor dataset and high-gradient static magnetic field sensor dataset, the interference elimination rate, debris identification rate, and debris identification accuracy are 99. 72%, 98. 94%, and 99. 44%, respectively, and the proposed method still exhibits superior debris-detection performance compared with traditional algorithms under low signal-to-noise ratios ranging from -5 to 0 dB.
Keywords: attention mechanism | debris detection | inductive debris sensor | neural network

Title: Real-time marker-less needle tracking for CT-guided interventions using multiple RGB cameras
Abstract: Purpose: In CT-guided interventions, instrument tracking reduces patient risk while improving the overall outcome. Though useful, marker-based tracking systems suffer from occlusion, are complex to set up, and fail when needles deflect. A marker-less tracking system could overcome these challenges, enabling streamlined integration. Methods: We developed and evaluated a proof-of-concept system combining standard RGB cameras with a U-Net-ConvNeXt architecture for needle detection and tracking. We compiled a fully annotated dataset of 35,000 frames, spanning multiple needle types and scenarios. We evaluated tracking accuracy against state-of-the-art marker-based systems, utilizing an IR-based and an image-based system on static positioning, dynamic movement, and needle-deflection scenarios. Moreover, our marker-less system was evaluated using both known and unknown needle types. Results: Our proof-of-concept system demonstrated a 3D tracking error of 2.70±1.07 mm at 25 FPS with 3 cameras, outperforming ArUco marker-based tracking (5.29±1.85 mm). Tracking accuracy remained consistent for unknown needle types not included in the training data, suggesting strong generalization. The system maintained a 99.4 % needle-tip detection rate across all frames with robust performance during needle deflection, while marker-based systems failed under identical conditions. With only 2 cameras, the tracking error of our system increased modestly (4.81±2.38 mm). Conclusion: Our proof-of-concept demonstrates the feasibility of marker-less needle tracking, suggesting potential for clinically relevant accuracy, reliability, and reduced complexity while exhibiting robustness to needle deflection and varying needle appearances. These preliminary results indicate promising directions for future clinical development.
Keywords: Biopsy needle | Deep learning | Marker-less video tracking | Surgical tool tracking

Title: Graph-Structured Deep Learning Framework for Multi-task Contention Identification with High-dimensional Metrics
Abstract: This study addresses the challenge of accurately identifying multi-task contention types in high-dimensional system environments and proposes a unified contention classification framework that integrates representation transformation, structural modeling, and a task decoupling mechanism. The method first constructs system state representations from high-dimensional metric sequences, applies nonlinear transformations to extract cross-dimensional dynamic features, and integrates multiple source information such as resource utilization, scheduling behavior, and task load variations within a shared representation space. It then introduces a graph-based modeling mechanism to capture latent dependencies among metrics, allowing the model to learn competitive propagation patterns and structural interference across resource links. On this basis, task-specific mapping structures are designed to model the differences among contention types and enhance the classifier's ability to distinguish multiple contention patterns. To achieve stable performance, the method employs an adaptive multi-task loss weighting strategy that balances shared feature learning with task-specific feature extraction and generates final contention predictions through a standardized inference process. Experiments conducted on a public system trace dataset demonstrate advantages in accuracy, recall, precision, and F1, and sensitivity analyses on batch size, training sample scale, and metric dimensionality further confirm the model's stability and applicability. The study shows that structured representations and multi-task classification based on high-dimensional metrics can significantly improve contention pattern recognition and offer a reliable technical approach for performance management in complex computing environments.
Keywords: High-dimensional index modeling | multi-task classification | resource contention identification | system performance analysis

Title: PRAD-Hybrid CNN (PRADHC): A Deep Learning Model for Assisted Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer on MRI
Abstract: Background: Prostate cancer is a prevalent malignancy in males, with prostate MRI imaging as the primary diagnostic method. However, this method is subjective and can miss early-stage cancers, necessitating more efficient diagnostic techniques. Method: In this study, we introduced the PRAD-Hybrid CNN (Prostate Adenocarcinoma Hybrid Convolutional Neural Network, PRADHC) model, a novel amalgamation of EfficientNet and Residual Blocks, which was developed and validated on 1,528 MRI images from 64 patients. By strategically increasing the number of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layers in the EfficientNet architecture, our model improved the diagnostic accuracy inherent to the original EfficientNet. Additionally, the integration of Residual Networks (ResNet) successfully mitigated the gradient vanishing issue often encountered during the training of deeper models, thereby significantly enhancing training accuracy. This innovative model, thus, offers clinicians an efficacious tool for assisted diagnosis. Result: The PRADHC model, upon validation, achieved an accuracy of 99.34% and an AUC of 99.34%, a 4% improvement over the conventional EfficientNet. The baseline elementary CNN model achieved 95.72% accuracy and 96.74% AUC, which are still lower than the PRADHC model. Discussion: The superior performance of PRADHC can be attributed to the synergistic integration of EfficientNet’s multi-scale feature extraction and residual learning, which facilitates deeper network optimization without degradation. Compared with single-architecture CNN models, the hybrid design enhances robustness to MRI appearance variability and improves discrimination between malignant and non-significant prostate tissue. Conclusion: This study introduces a novel deep learning model specifically designed for automated prostate cancer diagnosis. This model aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy, especially in the early stages of the disease. Such advancements have the potential to enhance the diagnostic proficiency of both radiologists and urologists, enabling more informed treatment planning. However, it is imperative to acknowledge that false-positive lesion detections remain a limitation of AI-assisted diagnostic tools. Nevertheless, this system can serve as a valuable supplementary instrument for radiologists in their diagnostic endeavors.
Keywords: Convolutional neural networks | Deep learning | Early-stage cancers | Magnetic resonance imaging | Precise assisted diagnosis | Prostate cancer

Title: The Kinematic Chain in Hindustani Classical Singing: An Exploratory Bioacoustic Pilot Study of Seated Posture and Vocal Quality
Abstract: Seated posture (Asana) is an important part of Hindustani classical vocal pedagogy, yet its biomechanical function remains under-researched. This exploratory pilot study applies “Kinematic Chain” theory—where proximal stability dictates distal mobility—to investigate the link between pelvic alignment and vocal acoustics. Ten students (n = 10), beginner-to-intermediate level, learning in a university music college were recorded performing Aalap (slow Swara improvisation) and Sapat (fast ascending-descending variation in a set tempo) tasks. To address the challenge of masking by drone accompaniment (Tanpura & Tabla), raw audio was processed using the ‘Demucs deep learning model’ to isolate the vocal stem prior to analysis of Spectral Centroid and Vocal Efficiency. Subsequently, the pYIN (Probabilistic YIN) algorithm was deployed for fundamental frequency (F<inf>0</inf>) estimation to objectively quantify performance efficiency through high-resolution pitch tracking. Descriptive analyses indicate that unstable postural bases are frequently associated with compensatory cervical protraction and reduced aerodynamic output. Intra-subject analysis revealed that correcting pelvic mechanics increased vocal efficiency by up to 38.5% (student 10) and Spectral Centroid by ∼171 Hz (student 7). Triangulation with participant feedback confirmed these findings: 70% of subjects identified mechanical anchoring (either via pelvic stabilization in Vajrasana or upper-body stabilization) as superior for breath control. These findings suggest that traditional stable postures, such as Vajrasana, function as a biomechanical optimization strategy to meet the specific acoustic and technical demands of Hindustani classical vocal performance.
Keywords: Hindustani music | Kinematic chain | Performance science | Source separation | Spectral centroid | Vocal biomechanics

Title: OFTNet: Omni-Feature and Texture-Aware Enhancement Learning Network for Continuous Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
Abstract: Continuous-scale super-resolution (CSSR) for remote sensing images (RSIs) offers critical flexibility for diverse Earth observation tasks, overcoming the fixed-scale limitations of conventional SR methods. However, current CSSR methods are primarily tailored for natural images, failing to address the unique characteristics of remote sensing scenes. Unlike object-centric natural images with clear foregrounds, RSIs feature arbitrary orientations, vast scale variations, and dense repetitive patterns. First, standard hierarchical extractors in existing methods exhibit limited receptive fields, struggling to capture the global context required for large-scale land covers while preserving the fine-grained details of small targets. Second, the inherent spectral bias in implicit neural representations (INRs) exacerbates the loss of high-frequency information, causing severe over-smoothing in regions with intricate textures. To address these challenges, we propose an omni-feature and texture-aware enhancement learning network (OFTNet), a novel network specifically designed for continuous-scale RSI super-resolution (SR). Our method introduces a powerful omni-feature enhancement and refinement pipeline, comprising three key modules: an omni-feature enhancement module (OFEM) that synergistically models global spatial dependencies, interchannel correlations, and multiscale local patterns; a texture-aware enhancement module (TAEM) that explicitly preserves high-frequency information and models nonlocal spatial correlations; and a learnable weighting aggregation module (LWAM) for intelligent, context-aware feature aggregation. Extensive experiments on commonly used benchmark remote sensing datasets demonstrate that OFTNet achieves state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of in-distribution scales, while also showing robust and highly competitive performance on out-of-distribution (OOD) scales.
Keywords: Continuous-scale super-resolution (CSSR) | feature aggregation | omni-feature enhancement | remote sensing image (RSI) | texture-aware learning

Title: A hybrid STL-LightGBM framework with probabilistic forecasting for Influenza A incidence in the post-pandemic Saudi Arabia
Abstract: Influenza A outbreaks in Saudi Arabia exhibit different seasonal patterns, influenced by significant changes, including a near-total halt during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2021) and a substantial rebound, as evidenced by national surveillance data, until the end of 2023. Traditional time-series models rely on stationarity and stable seasonal patterns; however, these assumptions are significantly undermined by regime shifts. This study introduces a forecasting method that uses light gradient boost machine (LightGBM) regression, along with Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS (STL), to better track influenza in changing contexts. The proposed method adapts to the evolving epidemiological dynamics shaped by policy and behavioral changes by decomposing the incidence series into long-term trends, stable annual seasonal components, and irregular residual fluctuations prior to nonlinear learning. Exploratory analysis supports strong winter seasonality, linear correlations with meteorological variables, and major structural disruptions linked to pandemic-related interventions. shows how standard SARIMAX and seasonal baseline models cannot be used across all epidemiological regimes. The hybrid model, when evaluated during the test window, shows strong out-of-sample performance, substantially outperforming the benchmark models (R2 = 0.831, MAE = 89.0). In-sample fitting throughout the study period indicates a high degree of representational capacity (R2 = 0.987). The framework is further extended to probabilistic forecasting via quantile regression, resulting in accurately calibrated 95% prediction intervals. The uncertainty in the predictions increases appropriately during periods of epidemiological disruption, highlighting the importance of uncertainty-aware prediction under structural change. The proposed STL-LightGBM architecture is a resilient and comprehensible instrument for monitoring influenza in post-pandemic contexts, facilitating early warning systems and expeditious public health decision-making in Saudi Arabia and analogous regions.
Keywords: epidemiological surveillance | Influenza A | LightGBM | non-stationary time series | probabilistic forecasting | STL decomposition | structural regime shifts

Title: Semiconductor Metrology and Inspection with Ultrafast Coherent Extreme Ultraviolet Light Source (Invited)
Abstract: Significance The rapid advancement of fields such as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing has intensified demand for advanced, high-performance integrated circuits (ICs). Lithography, as a core fabrication step in integrated circuit manufacturing, represents the most complex and critical process, directly determining chip performance. As lithographic processes evolve toward cutting-edge nodes, the scale of features to be patterned and defects to be detected continues to shrink. This miniaturization imposes stringent requirements on next-generation metrology tools. Measurement techniques based on short-wavelength, high-brightness, and coherent extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light sources have therefore emerged as a pivotal research direction. Progress From the perspective of lithography light source development, lithography systems have evolved from high-pressure mercury discharge lamps in the ultraviolet band to ArF excimer lasers in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) band, culminating in today’s state-of-the-art EUV lithography machines. The dramatic reduction in lithography wavelength—from 193 nm to 13.5 nm—necessitates entirely new optical components and materials compatible with EUV conditions, requiring renewed emphasis on optical component testing and material interaction studies at the operational wavelength (i.e., 13.5 nm). For instance, the shift from DUV transmissive photomasks to EUV reflective masks introduces phase-sensitive defects, creating new challenges for mask inspection.
