Similarly, EUV photoresist development must achieve reduced line edge roughness and controlled shot noise, imposing increasingly stringent demands at advanced process nodes. Furthermore, as process nodes and device dimensions continue to scale down, and integrated circuits adopt three-dimensional architectures, the need for three-dimensional (3D) metrology grows significantly. These trends introduce multiple technical challenges for measurement equipment related to feature miniaturization, structural complexity, and novel materials. Future progress will require extensive technological innovation to meet the specifications outlined in the International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors (ITRS) and those demanded by integrated device manufacturers (IDMs). Extreme ultraviolet spectroscopy, leveraging its short-wavelength radiation, offers unique advantages for metrology and defect inspection at advanced nodes. Its spectral range—spanning several to tens of nanometers—enables nanometer-scale spatial resolution. Additionally, the limited penetration depth of EUV radiation allows non-destructive imaging of internal structures within micron-thick samples, while element-specific absorption edges in this spectral region facilitate high-contrast imaging without labeling or staining. When combined with quantitative phase-sensitive detection methods, coherent EUV sources enable even nanoscale material differentiation, making the development of quantitative EUV-band metrology a critical research frontier. With semiconductor technology scaling to sub-nanometer dimensions and the adoption of three-dimensional stacked architectures, thermal management in integrated circuits has become a paramount concern. Understanding and engineering material properties at the nanoscale represent major scientific objectives with significant technological implications. For example, elucidating the dynamics of heat transfer and dissipation at the nanoscale can accelerate the design of next-generation chip architectures featuring lower power consumption, higher integration density, and increased operating frequencies. Indeed, a device’s thermal relaxation time influences its maximum sustainable frequency, while inadequate heat removal leading to excessive temperature rise may result in irreversible degradation or failure. Likewise, insights into nanoscale mechanical behavior can enhance the efficiency of micro-/nano-electromechanical systems (MEMS/NEMS) in harvesting energy from ambient vibrations. Transient gratings in the extreme ultraviolet regime have substantially enhanced Fourier-domain measurements of high-wavevector excitations, enabling contactless, all-optical characterization of nanoscale thermal and mechanical phenomena. Conclusions and Prospects This paper reviews the exploration and recent advances in semiconductor metrology and inspection technologies based on EUV light sources, primarily focusing on EUV coherent diffraction imaging (CDI) and EUV scattering measurements. Coherent diffraction imaging offers nanometer-scale resolution and enables non-destructive mapping of sample chemical composition. Meanwhile, EUV scattering extends the capabilities of conventional white-light optical critical dimension (OCD) metrology and defect inspection methods—widely employed in semiconductor manufacturing—into the shorter-wavelength EUV regime. Furthermore, this paper discusses the application of ultrafast EUV light sources in measuring elastic modulus and investigating thermal transport in nanoscale structures. Specifically, nanostructure thermal transport studies leveraging ultrafast EUV sources introduce a powerful new methodology. These advancements hold significant promise for next-generation semiconductor metrology and inspection technologies.
Keywords: advanced lithography | extreme ultraviolet | metrology and inspection | semiconductor

Title: DravHate-XAI: A Multimodal Transformer Approach for Hate Speech Detection
Abstract: Dealing with online hate speech is a nightmare, specifically in those linguistic communities which are very small and have not been taken into consideration by AI-developed differently. What we do is exactly the opposite; our work is directly filling the gap for the three major Dravidian languages - Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam. We have implemented a single structure that is capable of identifying hateful content not only in the written form but in speech as well. The first step is speech transcription using Wav2Vec2. We also provide a model for performance evaluation with a big emphasis on openness. Our measuring instrument involves a spectrum of methods starting from classic SVM classifiers and going up to various transformer (e.g. XLM-RoBERTa, IndicBERT, MuRIL, DistilBERT, ALBERT) methods. For each model, we have made use of our explainable AI tools, LIME and SHAP, to enhance the understandability of the predictions and to help explain the static conclusions produced by the system. The outcome is a system that is consistent in its operations for both written and spoken materials in all three languages. What is more, we provided the evidence that high accuracy and transparency are not mutually exclusive. We have shown that it is possible to develop ethical and trustworthy moderation tools for languages that have been traditionally overlooked by AI.
Keywords: Dravidian Languages | Explainable AI | Hate Speech Detection | LIME | Multimodal AI | SHAP | Transformer Models | Wav2Vec2

Title: Comparative Evaluation of Thai Speech-to-Text Models and Entity Extraction Methods for Beverage Ordering Systems
Abstract: Deploying robust voice-based ordering systems for tonal languages like Thai requires balancing transcription fidelity with real-time responsiveness. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of twelve end-to-end pipeline configurations, combining three Speech-to-Text (STT) architectures-OpenAI Whisper, FasterWhisper, and Biodatlab-Whisper-with four entity extraction strategies. We benchmark performance on a specialized beverage-ordering domain using an independent test set of 50 utterances (comprising both real-world recordings and AI-generated samples). Experimental results demonstrate that Faster-Whisper optimizes the latency-accuracy trade-off, achieving the lowest transcription latency via its optimized inference engine. Crucially, we address the issue of cascading errors by implementing a domain-adapted Custom NER model, fine-tuned on a synthetic corpus of 201,245 labeled samples. This proposed model significantly mitigates upstream transcription noise, achieving a peak entity-wise accuracy of 77.5%, drastically outperforming rule-based and general-purpose baselines. These findings offer actionable architectural guidelines for building scalable, real-time Thai voice interfaces.
Keywords: Beverage Ordering | Faster-Whisper | Named Entity Recognition | Speech-to-Text | Thai NLP | Whisper

Title: Optimizing Industrial Automation: A Multi-Algorithm Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Robotics Adoption Impact
Abstract: Implementation of industrial robotics is a decision-making process that is very critical to manufacturing organizations that should thoroughly evaluate various interdependent variables such as productivity, cost savings, workforce displacement and training needs. Hence a 14 different machine learning models on a variety of performance indices and the best model was LightGBM that demonstrated almost perfect training performance (R<sup>2</sup>=0.0001) and cross-validation (R<sup>2</sup>=-0.1797). The model includes in-depth feature analysis via correlation studies and feature rankings, which show that robots adopted, cost saving, and job displaced are the three factors that most significantly contribute to productivity savings. This approach will utilize a comparative analysis of algorithms based on classical regression methods to the latest ensemble techniques and neural networks through systematic comparison in terms of R<sup>2</sup> scores, RMSE, and MAE. The comparisons of the residual analysis and the prediction and the actual values indicate that the model is reliable enough to be deployed in the real world. The framework will offer manufacturing decision-makers an information-based planning instrument on strategic robotics investments decision-making based on technological progress and the workforce and financial optimization. The study adds significance in the domain as it has developed a repeatable methodology of multi-objective optimization of industrial automation
Keywords: cost-benefit optimization | ensemble methods | Industrial robotics | LightGBM | machine learning | predictive modeling | productivity forecasting

Title: Machine Learning Approaches for Consumer Behaviour Prediction in Marketing
Abstract: The current scenario in digital marketing requires the forecasting of consumer behaviour as a key component to help businesses maximize engagement and enhance the effectiveness of the campaigns. As more and more consumer data has become available through online sources, machine learning (ML) provides effective instruments to derive actionable insights. This paper seeks to compare the performance of five machine learning (ML) algorithms namely Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) in predicting consumer purchasing behavior. It is conducted with a sample of 400 consumer records and performed extensive preprocessing, as well as 10 -fold cross-validation in training and evaluation. Performance is analyzed using key metrics, accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. The findings indicated that the Random Forest model is the best model that had the highest accuracy (88.4%) and F1-score (88.4%) and that past purchases and income are the most significant predictors. The results prove the possibility of ensemble learning models to make a confident prediction of consumers and emphasize the importance of including ML in the contemporary marketing strategies. The study has some practical implications toward data-driven decision-making and opens up future avenues of implementation with larger datasets and more complicated forms of deep learning.
Keywords: Consumer Behaviour | Machine Learning | Marketing Analytics | Prediction Models

Title: Early Breast Cancer Detection Using an Advanced Deep Learning Neural Network Framework
Abstract: Breast cancer is the most prevalent malignancy afflicting American women; fortunately, mortality rates can be drastically reduced with early detection and prompt treatment. The high expense and radiation exposure of digital mammography with CE prevent its widespread usage, despite the fact that it outperforms ultrasound and conventional mammography in thick breast tissue in terms of accuracy. Early Breast Cancer Detection uses data pretreatment with Weiner Filtering and a region growth picture segmentation technique based on GSO. GSO ideally creates initial seed spots and threshold values. A hybrid strategy is used to increase feature extraction and forecast performance by combining traditional and deep learning methods. Introducing HitNet, a Hybrid Ternary RNN that uses ternary weights and activations, with a slope component in the activation functions to further improve accuracy and close the accuracy gap between full precision and quantised models. The suggested model is effective, as it obtains a precision of 94.06% when tested using a conventional RNN architecture. By merging state-of-the-art imaging analysis with hybrid neural network modelling, this method supplies a powerful instrument for early diagnosis of breast cancer, which has the ability to decrease breast cancer death rates and enhance diagnostic accuracy.
Keywords: Glowworm Swarm Optimisation (GSO) | low- and middle-income countries (LMIC) | Multi-Way Imaging (MWI) | Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)

Title: Unmasking Deepfakes: An AI Approach with Audio-Visual Analysis
Abstract: The rapid advancement of generative models has enabled the generation of unrealistically convincing manipulated audio-visual content, commonly referred to as DeepFakes. This type of content poses a serious threat to digital trust, security, biometric authentication systems, and the authenticity of digital media. In order to address these concerns, this work proposes a robust DeepFake detection system that jointly takes into consideration both input visual and audio signals. Different from methods that rely exclusively on either facial appearance or speech patterns, the system integrates deep spatial feature extraction using a ResNet architecture with temporal audio modeling through Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. This framework extracts from the visual modality facial texture inconsistencies, micro-expressions, and blending artifacts, while from the audio modality, it models speech features, pitch variations, and lip-audio synchronization patterns. In contrast, the presented approach integrates high-level abstractions from these two modalities to identify the very subtle incongruities that usually arise in manipulated content. Extensive experiments over benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework significantly outperforms unimodal techniques in terms of accuracy, compression resistance, and cross-dataset generalizability. Moreover, the model provides reliable performance under low-resolution and noisy conditions, which makes it suitable for practical applications with resource-limited deployments.
Keywords: Audio+video fusion | dataset wizardry | Deepfakes | feature hunting | forensics fun | lip-sync slip-ups | making it general for everyone | time-based modeling

Title: Interpretable Gender Classification from Malayalam Speech
Abstract: Speech serves as a primary medium of human communication and conveys important paralinguistic information such as speaker gender. This work investigates acoustic featurebased gender classification for Malayalam, a low resource Dravidian language that remains underexplored in speech processing research. A multi-speaker Malayalam speech corpus has been used in this study, from which a comprehensive feature set comprising of spectral, energy based and voice based characteristics of speech such as Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients, Jitter, Shimmer etc. have been extracted. Multiple machine learning classifiers are compared, among which Logistic Regression achieves the highest accuracy of 94.65% and a weighted F-measure of 94.6% on unseen speakers under speaker independent evaluation. Statistical significance tests, including McNemar, paired t-test, Wilcoxon, and Friedman tests, confirm meaningful performance differences across models. Robustness analysis under additive white noise demonstrates that Logistic Regression is the model most robust to noise with 90.84% accuracy at 20dB SNR, 84.90% at 15dB SNR and 82.88% at 10 dB SNR. Feature-level interpretability using SHAP on the best model further highlights the dominant role of MFCC-derived and spectral features.
Keywords: Acoustic feature analysis | Gender classification | Low resource languages | SHapley Additive exPlanations | Speech processing | Statistical testing of hypothesis

Title: Developing a Sinhala Speech Recognition System Using Whisper
Abstract: The demand for accurate and robust speech recognition in low-resource languages has increased significantly in recent years. Sinhala, despite being spoken by over 17 million people, remains underrepresented in Automatic Speech Recognition research due to the limited availability of annotated datasets and its linguistic complexity. This study presents the development of a Sinhala Automatic Speech Recognition system by fine-tuning OpenAI’s Whisper model on a curated and augmented Sinhala speech dataset. A combined dataset of 3078 clips (5.83 hours) was expanded to 12312 clips (23.32 hours) using multiple augmentation techniques. Fine-tuning was performed on individual datasets and their combinations, both with and without augmentation, to evaluate the impact of dataset diversity. Experimental results show that the zero-shot Whisper models performed very poorly on Sinhala. However, fine-tuning significantly improved performance. The Whisper medium model, trained on an augmented news-style custom dataset, achieved a Word Error Rate of 5%. These results confirm the importance of dataset quality, augmentation, and multi-source training for improving ASR in low-resource languages. Furthermore, a lightweight web interface was developed to enable real-time Sinhala speech-to-text transcription. This work demonstrates that fine-tuned multilingual ASR models can bridge the resource gap for Sinhala Language.
Keywords: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) | Data Augmentation | Low-Resource Languages | Speech-to-Text (STT) | Word Error Rate (WER)

Title: Genre Classification of Sinhala Songs Using Machine Learning Based on Audio Features
Abstract: Music genre classification plays a significant role in modern audio analysis and music retrieval systems, particularly in organizing and preserving culturally diverse musical traditions. Despite the growing use of automated genre classification techniques worldwide, Sinhala music remains largely underrepresented in computational music analysis, with limited publicly available datasets and genre-focused classification studies. In this context, this study presents a machine learning approach for classifying Sinhala songs into five genres: Pop, Rock, Hip Hop, Classical, and Folk. Due to the absence of public datasets and prior computational research on Sinhala music, a balanced dataset was curated and key audio features such as MFCCs, spectral descriptors, tempo, and rhythm were extracted. Four base models were evaluated: Support Vector Machine, k-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, and a Neural Network. The k-Nearest Neighbors model achieved an accuracy of 81.57%, followed by the Neural Network with an accuracy of 80.86% and Random Forest with an accuracy of 80.68%. A Soft Voting Ensemble combining the Neural Network and Random Forest achieved an accuracy of 81.93%, offering improved genre-wise balance. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of both individual and ensemble learning methods for Sinhala music classification and support applications in music retrieval and cultural preservation.
Keywords: audio feature extraction | genre classification | machine learning | Sinhala music | soft voting ensemble

Title: RoPEHAR: A Real-Time Rotary Position Encoding Informer for mmWave-Based Human Activity Recognition in Substations
Abstract: Safety monitoring of power operations in substations is crucial for accident prevention. However, traditional methods such as wearable devices and video surveillance suffer from limitations including high costs and reliance on lighting conditions. A solution that integrates millimeter-wave radar with deep learning ensures operational compliance by high precision gesture detection. This paper proposes RoPEHAR, a human activity recognition system based on millimeter-wave radar, which combines traditional transformer architecture with rotary positional encoding, specifically designed for human posture recognition in indoor industrial environments. To reduce interference from the coupling of human and instrument signals and noise in electrical scenarios, RoPEHAR introduces a hybrid filtering pipeline that combines hierarchical SNR denoising with enhanced DBSCAN clustering to accurately segment the point cloud data of limbs and instruments. The core innovation lies in the introduction of a spatiotemporal Informer, Roformer. It enhances the 3D-space vector information about data points through dynamic rotary positional encoding. This system effectively models limb motion trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that RoPEHAR achieves high-precision performance, reaching an accuracy of 95.8%, enabling real-time and reliable activity recognition for substation safety monitoring.
Keywords: deep learning | Electric power operation safety | human activity recognition | millimeter-wave radar | rotary positional encoding

Title: FEMBA on the Edge: Physiologically-Aware Pre-Training, Quantization, and Deployment of a Bidirectional Mamba EEG Foundation Model on an Ultra-Low Power Microcontroller
Abstract: Objective: To enable continuous, long-term neuro-monitoring on wearable devices by overcoming the computational bottlenecks of Transformer-based Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models and the quantization challenges inherent to State-Space Models (SSMs). Methods: We present FEMBA, a bidirectional Mamba architecture pre-trained on over 21,000 hours of EEG. We introduce a novel Physiologically-Aware pre-training objective, consisting of a reconstruction with low-pass filtering, to prioritize neural oscillations over high-frequency artifacts. To address the activation outliers common in SSMs, we employ Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) to compress the model to 2-bit weights. The framework is deployed on a parallel ultra-low-power RISC-V microcontroller (GAP9) using a custom double-buffered memory streaming scheme. Results: The proposed low-pass pre-training improves downstream AUROC on TUAB from 0.863 to 0.893 and AUPR from 0.862 to 0.898 compared to the best contrastive baseline. QAT successfully compresses weights with negligible performance loss, whereas standard post-training quantization degrades accuracy by approximately 30%. The embedded implementation achieves deterministic real-time inference (1.70 s per 5 s window) and reduces the memory footprint by 74% (to ≈2 MB), achieving competitive accuracy with up to 27× fewer FLOPs than Transformer benchmarks. Conclusion: FEMBA demonstrates that Mamba-based foundation models can be effectively quantized and deployed on extreme-edge hardware without sacrificing the representation quality required for robust clinical analysis. Significance: This work establishes the first full-stack framework for deploying large-scale EEG foundation models on ultra-low-power wearables, facilitating continuous, SSM based monitoring for epilepsy and sleep disorders.
Keywords: Edge AI | Electroencephalography | Foundation Models | Mamba | Quantization | RISC-V | Wearables

Title: The Spheres Dataset: Multitrack Orchestral Recordings for Music Source Separation and Information Retrieval
Abstract: This paper introduces The Spheres dataset, multitrack orchestral recordings designed to advance machine learning research in music source separation and related MIR tasks within the classical music domain. The dataset is composed of over one hour recordings of musical pieces performed by the Colibrì Ensemble at The Spheres recording studio, capturing two canonical works - Tchaikovsky's Romeo and Juliet and Mozart's Symphony No. 40 - along with chromatic scales and solo excerpts for each instrument. The recording setup employed 23 microphones, including close spot, main, and ambient microphones, enabling the creation of realistic stereo mixes with controlled bleeding and providing isolated stems for supervised training of source separation models. In addition, room impulse responses were estimated for each instrument position, offering valuable acoustic characterization of the recording space. We present the dataset structure, acoustic analysis, and different experiments for orchestral family separation and microphone debleeding. Results highlight both the potential and the challenges of source separation in complex orchestral scenarios, underscoring the dataset's value for benchmarking and for exploring new approaches to separation, localization, dereverberation, and immersive rendering of classical music.
Keywords: classical music | dataset | debleeding | immersive audio | machine learning | microphone bleeding | multitrack audio | Music source separation | orchestral recordings | room impulse responses (RIRs)

Title: A Novel Preprocessing Approach Applying Pairwise Differences of Opposite Samples for Improved Interpretability in Binary Medical Classification
Abstract: Interpretability is crucial for the clinical adoption of machine learning, as healthcare providers require transparent decision-making processes to trust predictive tools effectively. Traditional feature selection methods often struggle to capture subtle distinctions between patient subgroups, particularly in datasets with overlapping classes. To address this limitation, we propose the Pairwise Difference Filter (PDF) and its enhanced version, the directional Pairwise Difference Filter (dPDF). These preprocessing methods use margin-based instance selection to isolate 'hard examples' - patients from distinct clinical cohorts who share highly similar global phenotypic profiles. By anchoring feature extraction on these clinically ambiguous cases near the decision boundary, dPDF successfully identifies the subtle biomarkers responsible for true class separation. Evaluation across four medical datasets demonstrates that dPDF achieves competitive global performance (average accuracy: 74.63%, average rank: 2.00/6) among six established methods, while attaining leading accuracy (90.47%) on the primary MUSIC Med clinical dataset - outperforming techniques such as LASSO and Random Forest on complex clinical data. Furthermore, dPDF-generated feature rankings consistently align with clinical knowledge, isolating biologically plausible biomarkers rather than spurious variables associated with broad data divergence. This combination of competitive accuracy, intrinsic directional interpretability, and transparent methodology makes dPDF particularly valuable for real-world clinical implementation, effectively bridging the gap between model performance and practitioner trust.
Keywords: Binary classification | feature ranking | filter method | interpretability | medical applications | preprocessing

Title: MAFNet-DETR: Multi-Branch Adaptive Fusion Network for Small Object Detection in UAV Aerial Images
Abstract: Small object detection in high-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery presents formidable challenges, including severely constrained target scale and intricate background interference. To address these issues, this paper proposes MAFNet-DETR, a novel detection framework built upon RT-DETR-R18, designed to augment feature representation capability on densely populated small-object benchmarks such as VisDrone2019. MAFNet-DETR systematically advances detection performance through four core architectural innovations: the Three-branch Gated Enhancement Block (TGEB), which employs large-kernel convolutions to capture expansive global contextual information in conjunction with a gating mechanism for adaptive salient feature modulation, substantially elevating the model's perceptual sensitivity to sparse and inconspicuous signals; the Global-Local Spatial Attention (GLSA) module, which adopts a dual-branch parallel architecture to independently extract fine-grained local spatial details and long-range global dependencies, thereby achieving an effective equilibrium between local perceptual acuity and holistic contextual comprehension; the Adaptive Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (Adaptive-BiFPN), which incorporates a dual-weight fusion mechanism coupling spatially adaptive weights with globally learnable weights to realize fine-grained and computationally efficient multi-scale feature aggregation, significantly mitigating the degradation of small-object detail information during hierarchical feature propagation; and the Lightweight Progressive Upsampling Block (LPUB), which achieves high-fidelity feature map resolution restoration through the synergistic integration of depthwise separable convolutions, channel shuffling, and shift channel mixing operations. Extensive experimental evaluations conducted on three publicly available benchmark datasets - VisDrone2019, SIMD, and AI-TOD - demonstrate that, relative to the baseline RT-DETR-R18, the proposed method achieves improvements in mAP50 of 6.1%, 4.6%, and 4.8%, and in mAP 50-95 of 4.5%, 2.7%, and 3.3%, respectively, while concurrently reducing the parameter count by 12.46%, 8.7%, and 9.45%. The proposed model attains substantial gains in detection accuracy and exhibits strong applicability to small object detection under complex background conditions.
Keywords: feature fusion | RT-DETR | Small object detection | UAV aerial imagery

Title: Microphone Optimization and Development for AI-Based Detection of Flying Wildlife
Abstract: Acoustic monitoring is crucial for assessing the impact of renewable energy projects on biodiversity. However, commonly used Micro Electro Mechanical System (MEMS) microphones are susceptible to electromagnetic interference and ambient noise, which degrades the quality of recordings. This study compared the performance of a MEMS microphone with an electret microphone using bird songs from Monfragüe National Park and metrics such as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), total harmonic distortion (THD) and acoustic diversity index (ADI). The results revealed that the electret microphones outperformed MEMS in noise reduction, signal clarity and sensitivity, providing higher quality recordings that benefit artificial intelligence analysis for accurate species detection. This improvement is critical for more precise assessments of the environmental impact of renewable energy projects and for informed decision-making in the sustainable management of these infrastructures. These findings support the integration of electret-based systems into large-scale acoustic monitoring networks and the development of long-term biodiversity databases, strengthening the role of bioacoustics in conservation strategies aligned with renewable energy expansion.
Keywords: Audio monitoring techniques | Bioacoustics | Flying animal detection | Microphone comparative

Title: A Comparative Analysis of Music Genre Classification via Tree-based Ensemble Learning Algorithms
Abstract: Music Genre Classification (MGC) is a fundamental task in music information retrieval, aiming to automatically assign a genre label to an audio track based on its audio characteristics. This paper presents a comparative study on MGC using three Ensemble Learning Algorithms including Random Forests (RF), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) by employing various segmental information of music. Based on the simulation experiments, the effectiveness and efficiency of Ensemble Learning Algorithms in classifying music genres using extracted various duration audio features of GTZAN dataset has been investigated and summarized. Simulation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of RF (80.50% with 30 - sec MFCC, the highest among the three algorithms), the robustness of XGBoost (a 5.94% margin improvement higher than LightGBM from 3 - sec MFCC to 30 - sec MFCC), and the efficiency of LightGBM (73.11% with 3 - sec MFCC, higher than that of XGBoost) when deployed on the GTZAN dataset.
Keywords: LightGBM | Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) | Music Genre Classification | Random forest | XGBoost

Title: Adaptive Efficacy Assessment Method for Music Education via Multimodal Deep Learning Fusion
Abstract: Addressing the limitations inherent in traditional music education assessment - specifically strong subjectivity, delayed feedback, and the loss of technical details due to single-modality information - this paper proposes a novel Adaptive Efficacy Assessment Method (MAAF) based on multimodal deep learning fusion. The method constructs an audio-visual dual-stream neural network architecture: the auditory channel utilizes an improved ResNet to extract high-dimensional acoustic features from Mel-spectrograms; the visual channel integrates OpenPose hand keypoint detection with Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (ST-GCN) to capture fine-grained performance techniques, employing a confidence-based masking strategy to effectively suppress occlusion noise. Furthermore, to address the challenge of spatiotemporal asynchrony in heterogeneous data, we design a linear interpolation alignment strategy and an Adaptive Gated Attention Mechanism to realize dynamic weight allocation for audio-visual features. Empirical research based on the URMP dataset and a newly constructed Real-World Classroom Dataset (RWCD), validated by expert reliability tests, demonstrates that the proposed model achieves an assessment accuracy (PCC=0.898) that is significantly superior to mainstream SOTA architectures (e.g., Transformers). Furthermore, extensive experiments on heterogeneous instruments (e.g., Piano, Guitar) confirm the model's robustness and cross-domain generalization capabilities. The model effectively simulates the multi-sensory collaborative assessment logic of human experts.
Keywords: Adaptive Attention Mechanism | Deep Learning | Multimodal Fusion | Music Education Assessment | Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (ST-GCN)

Title: Application of Hierarchical Architecture Technology in Edge Devices
Abstract: With the deepening exploration of intelligent audio and the increasing demand for low latency, deploying deep learning models at the edge can not only effectively reduce latency, but also better protect user privacy. However, the high degree of hardware coupling of algorithms in traditional development models seriously restricts the portability and scalability of the system. With in-depth exploration of this issue, we propose a collaborative layered audio processing software architecture for multi-edge devices, which logically divides the various parts of the system into five relatively independent levels: hardware, drivers, data, algorithms, and applications. This eliminates the tight dependence of software and hardware and improves the flexibility and scalability of the system. At the same time, designing a heartbeat monitoring and asynchronous communication mechanism based on TCP/IP can achieve a stable and complete processing pipeline for VAD, streaming ASR, and punctuation recovery on a single edge node, which can also improve the reliability and synchronization efficiency of multi-device collaboration. In-depth experimental practice on Huawei Ascend Atlas 200I DK A2 has shown that it not only meets real-time performance requirements, but also has good system robustness and good scalability.
Keywords: edge audio processing | flow-based speech recognition | layered architecture | multiple device collaboration

Title: AI-Powered Voice Separation Algorithms: Testing Accuracy in Reconstructing Fundamental Frequency for Vocal Analysis
Abstract: Accurate analysis of the singing voice is often constrained by the need for clean, laboratory-quality recordings. Commercial recordings (CRs)—valuable for artistic and historical study—pose challenges due to complex accompaniment, recording artifacts, and undocumented post-production. This work evaluates whether voice-separation methods can support reliable extraction of fundamental frequency (f<inf>o</inf>) under such conditions.Synthesized vocals with ground-truth f<inf>o</inf> were mixed with instrumental introductions from seven CRs of Handel’s Ombra mai fu at five signal-to-noise ratios (SNR: −12, −6, 0, +6, +12 dB), yielding 105 samples. Two baselines (unfiltered; bandpass 2.2–6 kHz) and three separation methods (iZotope RX10, Music.ai, robust principal component analysis [RPCA]) were applied. f<inf>o</inf> contours were extracted in Praat and compared to ground truth using (i) success rate (valid f<inf>o</inf> detections), (ii) resolved rate (≤10 cents deviation), and (iii) receiver operating characteristic analysis.A clear hierarchy emerged: among the tested methods, Music.ai showed the most robust overall performance, typically exceeding 80% success at SNR ≥ 0 dB and degrading least at low SNR. iZotope RX10 performed similarly at positive SNRs but declined more with noise. Bandpass filtering performed comparably to the best separation techniques at higher SNR levels, whereas RPCA achieved lower accuracy overall. Accuracy decreased below 0 dB across methods and was strongly affected by accompaniment complexity and recording quality. Importantly, with per-segment accuracy near 80%, multiple independent segments are needed to reach high confidence, while correlated samples offer little gain.These results demonstrate that artificial intelligence-based separation methods can open new possibilities for analyzing singing voices in commercial and archival recordings, making large-scale studies of vocal style and technique more feasible than before. At the same time, careful validation across genres, recording conditions, and real performances remains essential to ensure that gains in f<inf>o</inf> tracking accuracy translate into reliable insights on spectral balance, timbre, and artistic expression. By clarifying both the promise and the boundaries of current approaches, this study provides a foundation for future research that seeks to bridge laboratory analysis and the complexity of real-world recordings.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | Commercial recordings | Fundamental frequency | Signal-to-noise ratio | Singing voice | Voice separation

Title: Improve OMI Observations on Ground-Level NO2 Using Multiple Observations, Simulations, and Machine Learning
Abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO<inf>2</inf> ) is a criteria air pollutant with adverse impacts on human health and the environment. An accurate ground-level NO<inf>2</inf> dataset with high spatial resolution is beneficial for NO<inf>2</inf> pollution management and public health studies. In this study, we leverage long-term ozone monitoring instrument (OMI) NO<inf>2</inf> observations by converting OMI NO<inf>2</inf> vertical column densities into ground-level NO<inf>2</inf> concentrations and improving its spatial resolution to 1×1 km by using the light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) learning model in three metro areas in USA: Metro New York, New York (NY), Baltimore, Maryland (MD), and Houston, Texas (TX). Our improved ground-level NO2 products achieved robust performance across all regions, with a correlation coefficient of 0.897 in NY, 0.876 in Baltimore, and 0.914 in Houston. The corresponding root-mean-squared error (RMSE) was 3.278 ppb in NY, 2.385 ppb in Baltimore, and 2.084 ppb in Houston, respectively. Furthermore, the products effectively captured the temporal variations in observed NO<inf>2</inf> concentrations across all cities. We also found that emissions, population density, boundary layer height (BLH), and winds are consistently important contributors to NO<inf>2</inf> concentrations across all three cities, while each city also has its own significant factors. This attribution analysis will be helpful to state and local air pollution agencies in their air pollution management efforts.
Keywords: Air pollution | atmospheric measurement | light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) | nitrogen dioxide (NO2 ) | ozone monitoring instrument (OMI) | Shapley additive explanation (SHAP)

Title: Real-Time Symbolic Music Accompaniment Generation for Edge Devices
Abstract: Music generation is a complex and challenging problem that has made significant progress through recent machine learning solutions. The challenge lies not only in rendering natural-sounding audio but also in capturing the underlying musical structure. This paper presents a real-time system that generates a musical accompaniment for an input lead melody in the MIDI format. In this paper, we introduce REMIBlock, a novel tokenization approach, and show that it is suited for accompaniment generation. Our method uses the GPT-2 architecture [11], optimized for efficient on-device performance, to generate accompaniments that are rhythmically and harmonically coherent with a musician’s performance. The model used in this papers reaches a perplexity of 7.69 on the test set, proving the model’s ability to understand musical language. Additionally, using two metrics—groove and scale consistency—proposed in [3], we show that the generated accompaniments closely match the ground truth, differing by at most 3.4%. This further highlights our model’s ability to capture the intricacies of musical language. The model weights and inference code is available at https://github.com/UncleBen420/JazzyGPT2.
Keywords: Edge AI | Generative AI | Symbolic music

Title: Maximizing Average Return from Stock Price Prediction using Machine Learning with Trading Indicators
Abstract: This study investigates the integration of financial metrics and trading indicators with regression-based machine learning methods for stock price prediction. Three models—multiple linear regression (MLR), ridge regression, and lasso regression—were applied to 38 securities in the SET50 index using historical data from February 29, 2016, to December 31, 2023. Data were standardized, and predictors with correlations ≥0.6 with stock prices were retained. MLR employed ordinary least squares, while ridge and lasso regression utilized generalized and k-fold cross-validation, respectively. Model performance was assessed using a Weighted Performance Score (WPS) with portions of MAE of 35%, MAPE of 25%, R2 of 25%, and MAPE of 15%. Results show that the MLR model achieved the highest Weighted Performance Score (0.2246), indicating superior predictive performance compared to the ridge (0.2236) and LASSO (0.2106) models while LASSO achieved the highest predictive consistency, ranking best for 18 stocks, compared to ridge for 13 and MLR for 7. However, Results from back testing showed predictive consistency for 18 stocks with LASSO, 13 stocks with ridge, and 8 stocks with multiple linear regression (MLR), which contrasts with forward testing outcomes where LASSO performed best for 25 stocks, ridge for 9 stocks, and MLR for 22 stocks. In addition, the profit percentage was evaluated using a Weighted Average Percentage Profit (WAPF). The models achieved WAPF of –3.34% (MLR), –4.34% (ridge), and –3.31% (LASSO) on SET50, substantially outperforming non-model trading (–14.81%). These findings highlight that model-assisted trading significantly maximized average return relative to the benchmark and reduced losses in downtrends, despite variations in individual model performance and consistency.
Keywords: back testing | lasso regression | machine learning | multiple linear regression | ridge regression | SET50 index | Stock price prediction

Title: Enhanced Deepfake Speech Classification With Ensemble Learning
Abstract: The advancement of speech synthesis technology has made detecting synthesized recordings a critical challenge in security and audio analysis. This study addresses the core challenge of cross-generator generalization under varying data availability by investigating the detection of synthesized speech using various machine learning architectures: Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks and Transformers. To evaluate model robustness, we introduce a tiered dataset framework comprising three variants, which simulate different levels of data scarcity and generator diversity. To improve robustness, Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) was applied as the primary ensemble aggregation method, allowing for uncertainty-aware integration of the individual model outputs. Our experimental results, evaluated using Equal Error Rate (EER) and ROC-AUC, demonstrate that the BMA ensemble significantly outperforms individual architectures, particularly in data-constrained and temporally varied scenarios. The models were intentionally trained on impoverished and imbalanced datasets to evaluate their resilience under adverse conditions, with the reduced variant being the most demanding due to its severe data constraints. In the challenging variant, the BMA approach achieved an EER of 1.02% and an AUC of 0.99, effectively mitigating the performance drop-off seen in standalone models, which reached EERs as high as 5.82%. Furthermore, on the complete dataset, the proposed system attained an exceptional EER of 0.22% and an accuracy of 99.82%. These findings offer valuable insights for researchers in cybersecurity and multimedia forensics, highlighting that model uncertainty-aware aggregation can compensate for limited training data and provide reliable detection of synthesized audio even across diverse temporal variations and augmentation-heavy environments.
Keywords: Bayesian model averaging | convolutional neural networks | speech processing | synthesized speech detection | transformers

Title: Real-Time Detection Method for Cracked Eggs Based on Improved YOLOv8 and Dual Verification with Triple Classification Granularity
Abstract: Addressing the urgent need for real-time detection of cracked eggs on production lines, this study proposes a high-precision real-time detection algorithm based on an improved YOLOv8 framework. This study innovatively introduced a dual-detection method, incorporating a "crack region" classification to assist in distinguishing between intact eggs and cracked eggs. This method identifies cracked eggs by recognizing either local or overall crack characteristics, effectively reducing both false negatives and false positives. At the architectural level, the model innovatively integrates Weighted Bidirectional Feature Pyramid (BiFPN) to optimize multi-scale feature fusion, Deformable Convolutional Network v2 (DCNv2) to enhance perception of irregular geometric deformations in cracks, Weighted Intersection over Union v2 (WIoUv2) loss function to improve detection accuracy for occluded samples, and adds a small object detection layer to strengthen recognition of minute defects. Experiments demonstrate that the improved model achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 92.9% on the test set, representing a 5.2% improvement over the original model and outperforming current mainstream detection models. In real-world production deployment testing, the system achieved a real-time detection speed of 45 FPS, with a false negative rate of only 0.46% and a false positive rate of 2.18% for intact eggs, while keeping the false positive rate for broken eggs below 2%. This performance far surpasses that of the original model and fully meets the requirements for industrial-grade real-time online quality inspection. This study provides an efficient solution for egg quality inspection with significant engineering application value.
Keywords: cracked eggs | deep learning | image processing | improved YOLOv8 | real-time detection

Title: A GAN-Augmented Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Framework for Explainable Crop Disease Detection
Abstract: The identification of crop diseases plays a crucial role in safeguarding agricultural productivity and ensuring global food security by enabling timely intervention and minimizing yield losses. Early diagnosis mitigates economic repercussions, optimizes pesticide application, and promotes sustainable agricultural practices. Automated detection systems enhance effective crop management and facilitate informed decision-making through increased accuracy and scalability. This research introduces a GAN-augmented multi-scale feature fusion network as an innovative methodology for crop disease detection and interpretability. To address class imbalance and improve generalization in real-world agricultural contexts, we employ generative adversarial networks (GANs) to enrich training datasets with diverse, high-quality synthetic crop images. The proposed framework utilizes a deep convolutional architecture with multi-scale feature fusion to extract hierarchical disease characteristics from leaf images, thereby enhancing recognition of subtle symptomatology across varying conditions. Our solution achieves cutting-edge detection accuracy (99.95% validation accuracy, AUC = 1.0), robust performance with limited data, and enhanced explainability through SHAP and LIME techniques. Comprehensive experiments conducted on publicly available crop disease datasets demonstrate superior performance compared to traditional methods including VGG16, ResNet50, and conventional augmentation approaches. This research advances precision agriculture and supports informed strategies for crop disease management by offering a scalable, interpretable deep learning instrument.
Keywords: Class Imbalance | Crop Disease Detection | Data Augmentation | Deep Learning | Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) | Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) | LIME | Multi-Scale Feature Fusion | Precision Agriculture | SHAP

Title: MSRA-Net: Multiscale Residual Attention Network for Land Use Land Cover Scene Classification From Remote Sensing Images
Abstract: Remote sensing image classification plays an important role in environmental monitoring, urban planning, and disaster management. Current deep-learning methods have major limitations, including single-scale feature extraction, suboptimal attention mechanisms, high computational complexity, and poor spectral-spatial integration, indicating the need for stronger classification frameworks. In this article, we propose a novel multiscale residual attention network (MSRA-Net), a multiscale residual attention network, composed of several multicomponent approaches to address these limitations. MSRA-Net incorporates adaptive inverted bottleneck blocks for efficient multiscale feature extraction, which are followed by lightweight dense blocks to promote feature reuse and gradient flow. After that, a comprehensive attention mechanism is adopted for optimal spectral-spatial integration, incorporating multiscale channel attention to dynamically weigh feature importance. We use an advanced cross-scale feature fusion module with attention-weighted aggregation to effectively represent features across different scales, along with an atrous spatial pyramid pooling based classification head that captures contextual information using dilated convolutions. Training is performed using a comprehensive data augmentation framework, AdamW optimization, and an early stopping strategy to ensure robust classification performance. The proposed model is evaluated on two publicly diverse datasets, such as MLRSNet and NWPU-RESISC45. On these datasets, the proposed model achieved superior performance with overall class accuracies of 93.71% and 97.95%, respectively, significantly outperforming conventional pretrained and contemporary state-of-the-art models.
Keywords: Aerial scene | cross-scale information | land use and land cover | remote sensing (RS) | residual attention

Title: Machine Learning Models for Predicting Diabetes Risk
Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is one of the most serious and emerging global public health issues requiring sophisticated instruments for early prediction to enable early interventions. This work introduces a machine learning framework for predicting diabetes risk with good accuracy. Methodologies include extensive preprocessing of data involving normalization and correction of class imbalance by using SMOTE followed by feature selection methodologies such as SHAP on the PIMA Indian Diabetes dataset. A suggested ensemble model incorporating multiple base learners was trained and tested. Experimental results confirm the better performance of the suggested ensemble model achieving an accuracy of 96.5%, AUC = 0.95, and F1-Score = 0.94 outperforming single classifiers such as Logistic Regression, SVM, and Random Forest. Deployment of explainable AI (XAI) methodologies provides enhanced model interpretability essential for clinical trust and acceptability. The research concludes that this machine learning framework provides a strong and consistent instrument for early stratification of diabetes risk with eventual development through addition of real-time wearable data and federated learning to enable personalization and preventability in healthcare.
Keywords: Diabetes Prediction | Ensemble Methods | Explainable AI | Machine Learning | Neural Networks | Risk Assessment | Supervised Learning

Title: DeepTexBoost OSCC: A Three-Stage Hybrid Classifier Combining GLCM, CNN, and XGBoost for Reliable Oral Cancer Detection
Abstract: Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC) is the most common oral cancer and continues to be a major health problem worldwide associated with late-stage diagnosis due to tissue complexity and diagnostic inconsistency among pathologists. To overcome these issues and enable early, trustworthy detection, in this work we propose DeepTexBoost OSCC, a unique three-level hybrid classification framework incorporating handcrafted texture descriptors, deep features and gradient-boosted learning. The presented methodology combines GLCM-based texture features to encompass crucial micro-patterns such as contrast, correlation, homogeneity, and energy, all of which are tightly associated with malignant changes in the epithelia layers. At the same time, a refined CNN is designed to learn high-level morphological representations directly from the histopathological images to fully capture OSCC-related structural variations. The GLCM and CNN features that are extracted are concatenated to construct a more descriptive feature vector that could represent both textured and spatial information. This fused representation is subjected to classification via XGBoost, a recently proposed scalable and robust optimized gradient boosting algorithm which has exhibited superior performance with heterogeneous feature spaces. The model is tested on a preprocessed OSCC histopathology dataset on 80-20 train-test split. DeepTexBoost OSCC attained a precision of 9 8 %, recall of 9 7 %-1 0 0 %, and F1-score of 0. 9 8 - 0. 9 9 in both Cancer and Normal classes under the overall accuracy of 99. The result of confusion matrix confirms the high ability of discrimination and the stability of the proposed framework, that is 79 out of 80 samples were successfully classified. he proposed hybrid structure significantly outperforms traditional CNN-only or texture-only approaches by integrating complementary feature and boosting-based classification. DeepTexBoost OSCC serves a strong, fast, and accurate computer-aided diagnostic instrument with great promise for clinical translation, enabling pathologists for rapid and objective screening of OSCC. In future work, the generalization will be evaluated as a multi-center retrospective study and a prospective study, and XAI-module which not only maintains the clinical image but also HINM will be developed.
Keywords: Federated Learning | Logistic Regression | Non-IID Data | Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning | Random Forest | Student Performance Prediction | Weighted Ensemble

Title: MOSAIC: A Unified Multilingual Deep Learning Framework for Detecting Manipulated Speech Audio Using Geometry-Aware Foundation Model Representations
Abstract: Audio deepfakes (AD) are increasingly used to spread misinformation, yet many detectors are evaluated in monolingual or narrowly multilingual settings and break under language mismatch. In this study, we take a step toward truly multilingual forensic audio deepfake detection (ADD). We conduct a systematic evaluation of pretrained speech encoders in multilingual settings. We observe that different pretrained encoders capture complementary spoofing cues arising from their distinct pretraining objectives. To leverage this complementarity, we propose MOSAIC, which fuses pretrained speech representations across multiple geometric spaces. MOSAIC performs gated additive fusion in hyperbolic, spherical, and Euclidean spaces, followed by self-attention for feature refinement. Experiments on large-scale multilingual benchmarks demonstrate strong crosslanguage generalization of the proposed framework. MOSAIC achieves SOTA performance, with MMS+PaSST attaining 0.02% EER on SpeechFake-MD and 0.07% on MLAAD. Through MOSAIC and complementary pretrained FMs, we attain top performance over individual FMs and standard fusion baselines. Such manipulated speech constitutes a form of audio misinformation that can mislead listeners across languages and platforms.
Keywords: Audio Misinformation | Deep Learning | Foundation Models | Multilingual Audio

Title: A Multi Module Deep Learning Framework for User Preferences and Behaviour in FM Radio
Abstract: The Speech Processing Project is a broad process of giving meaning to the audio with the help of state-of-the-art machine learning and deep learning. This project brings together a number of key modules in order to reach some very important goals, which include preparing audio, speech transcription, inappropriate content detection, identifying song preferences, and estimating the age of speakers. Taking advantage of state-of-the-art models like OpenAI's Whisper for converting speech to text, Facebook's Wav2Vec2 for classifying audio, and Cardiff NLP for detecting offensive material, the following project offers a powerful yet flexible means to analyze a wide variety of audio information. The preprocessing pipeline employs tools such as Librosa and Noisereduce for noise reduction, normalization, and dynamic range compression to make sure that high-quality audio goes into the models. Besides, in-house machine learning models with Scikit-learn-trained algorithms attained a mean squared error (MSE) of 0.35 for speaker age estimation and more than 95% accuracy for transcription analysis. The module for song preference analysis was seen to be able to classify songs by era with 90% confidence and map preferences to age groups successfully. Through automating music and conversation audio analysis, the project provides outputs as accurate transcripts, confidently detected inappropriate content, song tastes by time ranges and age groups, and results of age estimation. Provided through interactive visualizations and reports in details, the project outputs indicate that it can handle real-world tasks for audio analysis and promoting precision and scalability across applications.
Keywords: Audio Processing | Inappropriate Content Detection | Librosa | Offensive Content Detection | Scikit-learn | Song Preference Analysis | Speech-to-Text | Transcription Analysis | Wav2Vec2 | Whisper Model

Title: Predicting PHQ-9-Derived Depressive Symptom Screening Proxy Labels in NHANES
Abstract: Depression is a leading contributor to global disability, and population surveys such as the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) include validated symptom instruments (e.g., PHQ-9) for large-scale monitoring. This work presents a reproducible machine-learning baseline to predict a PHQ-9-derived screening proxy (PHQ-9 ≥q 10) using a compact set of demographic and socioeconomic NHANES covariates (with optional sleep information), intended for benchmarking and epidemiological analyses rather than clinical diagnosis. Using NHANES 2017-2018 (N=5,533; test N=1,107; prevalence=0.0488), we compare CatBoost, logistic regression, and random forest under deterministic stratified splits with strict leakage prevention. CatBoost achieves the best overall performance with ROC-AUC 0.7607 (unweighted bootstrap 95% CI [0.6951, 0.8233]), PR-AUC 0.1441, and balanced accuracy 0.7248 at a tuned threshold. We additionally report survey-weighted evaluation, subgroup and fairness auditing, decision curve analysis, robustness checks (sleep ablation and threshold sensitivity), and cross-cycle transfer across NHANES 2005-2018. Finally, calibration transport experiments show that Platt scaling improves expected calibration error for logistic regression under temporal shift without changing discrimination.
Keywords: calibration transport | fairness auditing | imbalanced classification | NHANES | PHQ-9 | reproducibility | temporal generalization

Title: A Framework for Stroke Prediction Using CDA-ResNet with Adaptive Feature Selection and Evaluation of Ensemble ML Methods
Abstract: This study provides a stroke prediction framework with CDA-ResNet with adaptive feature selection and a comparison of the performance of different ensemble machine learning (ML) approaches. The CDA-ResNet model is the second model that can improve the accuracy of the prediction process by using the dense convolutional blocks and attention to extract meaningful features out of the brain MRI images. Adaptive feature selection is the best approach to optimization of the model as it picks the most relevant features and minimizes overfitting and efficiency. Ensemble such as Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM are compared and evaluated on the framework to determine its performance. Based on the results obtained, the proposed CDA-ResNet model, with adaptive feature selection, has an accuracy of 94.5 % and F1-score of 0.93 and AUC of 0.97, which compares with the traditional models. The ensemble techniques also enhance the performance and XGBoost has the best precision and recall. This framework has a great potential of detecting early strokes which is a reliable instrument of clinical decision making and intervention planning.
Keywords: Adaptive Feature Selection | CDA-ResNet | Deep Learning | Ensemble Machine Learning | MRI Images | Stroke Prediction

Title: Machine Vision based Chili Species Recognition
Abstract: This study presents a comprehensive exploration of automated chili species classification using deep learning. We cover the full pipeline - data collection, preprocessing, model selection, and experimental analysis. A dataset of chili pepper images spanning multiple species was manually curated and augmented to increase diversity and size, then split 80/20 into training and test sets. Three state-of-the-art CNN backbones, InceptionV3, MobileNetV2, and Xception, were employed with transfer learning, initializing from large-scale image recognition weights. Each model was fine-tuned and optimized for accurate chili classification. Experiments yielded strong results, with the best configuration achieving 93% test accuracy. For each species, we report precision, recall, and F<inf>1</inf>-score, showing consistent performance across classes and validating both the model choices and the augmentation strategy. Beyond the technical results, the work has practical implications for agriculture, biodiversity research, and plant breeding programs. An automated chili species classification system can streamline field operations, enable precise species identification, and support monitoring of plant diversity and conservation efforts. Overall, our findings demonstrate that modern deep learning, coupled with careful dataset design, provides an effective and scalable approach to fine-grained plant identification. The approach is lightweight enough for deployment on modest hardware and can be extended to related crops with minimal additional labeling effort.
Keywords: agriculture | biodiversity | Capsicum | data augmentation | Deep learning | image classification | plant breeding | transfer learning

Title: An Improved Wireless Sensor Network for Secure and Real-Time Violin Performance Assessment in the Domain of 6G-IoT
Abstract: Currently, the music industry is the main focus of many researchers, scholars, and experts. However, there is limited research on real-time assessment and feedback mechanisms in the mentioned industry. Therefore, there is a pressing need for innovative solutions in the context of advancing musical education and performance that facilitate real-time assessment and feedback for musicians, particularly violinists. The conventional evaluation methods often lack the adaptability and immediacy required for effective skill enhancement. Keeping these in mind, this research paper proposes the Violin Real-Time Response to Data Collection Model (VRRTDCM) for real-time violin performance assessment within the framework of 6G Internet of Things (6G-IoT). In order to facilitate real-time performance for violinists, this research work presents a comprehensive system architecture that integrates a robust Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) by highlighting modular components for independent development and elevations. To capture critical performance metrics like bow speed, pressure, and angle, this research deploys low-power and lightweight sensors attached to the violin and its bow. The proposed framework uses WSNs and LSTM-CNN models to provide accurate evaluation while also ensuring secure, scalable, and reliable data transmission, making it an excellent choice for real-time performance assessment. Upon collecting data from the violin, the deployed sensors wirelessly transmit the same to a centralized Data Collection Hub utilizing secure communication protocols such as LoRa or Zigbee. By compiling the sensor data into a unified dataset that supports high temporal resolution for real-time analysis the centralized hub performs data aggregation and synchronization, which then passes to the Processing and Analysis Unit. This unit applies advanced algorithms, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), to evaluate performance metrics and provide immediate feedback by enabling musicians to make real-time adjustments. To ensure secure storage of all processed data, the data is handed over to the Data Storage and Feedback Unit by providing a sequential log of performance metrics while enabling a real-time feedback interface that visualizes key metrics. Experimental evaluations of the proposed VRRTDCM are compared with existing models, showing that our proposed model has highly superior performance by achieving an accuracy of 81.69% and an AUCROC of 0.89. from these results, it is clear that our suggested approach allows musicians to improve their techniques more efficiently by developing a deeper connection to their skill and elevating the quality of musical performance in educational settings.
Keywords: 6G-IoT | machine learning | real-time feedback | Violin performance assessment | wireless sensor network

Title: Beyond the Leaderboard: A Survey of the Science of Evaluation, Benchmarking, and Methodologies for Large Language Models
Abstract: The field of artificial intelligence is grappling with an evaluation crisis. Despite the proliferation of benchmarks and the relentless pursuit of state-of-the-art scores on public leaderboards, confidence in what these metrics truly measure is eroding. Large Language Models (LLMs) now consistently outperform humans on established benchmarks. However, their real-world utility is often undermined by brittleness, a lack of common sense, and a tendency to generate harmful or factually incorrect content. This paper argues that this disconnect stems from treating evaluation as a competitive afterthought rather than a rigorous metrological science. We contend that the current paradigm, characterized by static benchmarks and a narrow focus on accuracy, is fundamentally ill-equipped to assess the complex, multifaceted capabilities of modern LLMs. This survey aims to provide a comprehensive reference for the science of LLM evaluation by making four principal contributions. First, we offer a historical analysis of evaluation, tracing its evolution from traditional lexical-overlap metrics to the massive, holistic frameworks of today. Second, we introduce a systematic taxonomy of evaluation methodologies, classifying them into five key paradigms: static benchmarks, dynamic and adaptive evaluation, interactive and agentic evaluation, human-in-the-loop evaluation, and model-based evaluation (LLM-as-a-Judge). Third, we conduct a critical analysis of the pathologies plaguing the field, with a deep focus on the existential threat of data contamination, the perverse incentives of the leaderboard obsession, and the pervasive mismatch between benchmark performance and true capability. Finally, we propose a new conceptual framework, the Benchmark Lifecycle, to professionalize the design, validation, deployment, monitoring, and retirement of evaluation instruments. By framing evaluation as a scientific discipline, we aim to move beyond the leaderboard and build a more robust, reliable, and trustworthy foundation for measuring progress in artificial intelligence.
Keywords: AI safety | artificial intelligence | benchmarking | data contamination | emergent capabilities | evaluation | Large language models | metrology | natural language processing

Title: Temporal Data and Short-Time Averages Improve Multiphase Mass Flow Metering
Abstract: Reliable flow measurements are essential in many industries, but current instruments often fail to accurately estimate multiphase flows, which are frequently encountered in real-world operations. Combining machine learning (ML) algorithms with accurate single-phase flowmeters has therefore received extensive research attention in recent years. The Coriolis mass flowmeter is a widely used single-phase meter that provides direct mass flow measurements, which ML models can be trained to correct, thereby reducing measurement errors in multiphase conditions. This paper demonstrates that preserving temporal information significantly improves model performance in such scenarios. We compare a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a windowed MLP, a long short-term memory model, and a convolutional neural network (CNN) on three-phase air–water–oil flow data from 342 experiments. Whereas prior work typically compresses each experiment into a single averaged sample, we instead compute short-time averages from within each experiment and train models that preserve temporal information at several downsampling intervals. The CNN performed best at 0.25 Hz with approximately 95% of relative errors below 13%, a normalized root mean squared error of 0.03, and a mean absolute percentage error of approximately 4.3%, clearly outperforming the best single-averaged model and demonstrating that short-time averaging within individual experiments is preferable. While the CNN performed best, all three sequence models outperformed the non-temporal baseline MLP, clearly illustrating the benefits of temporal data and short-time averages. Results are consistent acrossmultiple data splits and random seeds, demonstrating robustness.
Keywords: Convolutional neural networks | Coriolis mass flowmeters | Mass flow estimation | Multiphase flow measurement | Multivariate time series

Title: Application of Computer Vision Technology in the Recognition of Guzheng Playing Posture
Abstract: This study addresses the performance teaching needs of traditional Chinese Guzheng and attempts to introduce computer vision and deep learning technologies into gesture recognition tasks. By constructing a dataset that includes various Guzheng playing actions, image sequences are collected during the performance process. Combined with convolutional neural networks for feature extraction, this approach achieves automatic recognition of multiple basic gestures. The model employs an optimized ResNet50 structure, maintaining high recognition accuracy under standardized image input and weighted classifiers. Experiments show that the system performs stably in recognizing typical actions and has a certain tolerance for complex action transitions and partial hand occlusions. When deployed in educational settings, the system can provide real-time feedback and visual presentations, assisting teachers in evaluating students’ gesture standards and enhancing interactive teaching effects. From the perspective of engineering implementation and practicality in education, this research provides methodological support for the integration of traditional arts and artificial intelligence, laying the groundwork for future intelligent musical instrument training systems. Overall results indicate that this technical approach holds practical significance and application potential in improving Guzheng performance quality and reducing teaching costs.
Keywords: computer vision technology | Guzheng playing | intelligent teaching system | posture recognition

Title: Flexible IMU Sensor Array For 3D Colonoscope Shape Reconstruction and AI-Based Loop Detection
Abstract: Looping during colonoscopy procedures is a major cause of patient discomfort and increases the risk of complications. With the rising incidence of colorectal cancer, there is an urgent need for safer and more efficient colonoscopy techniques. We developed a proof-of-concept platform for 3D visualization of the colonoscope combined with artificial intelligence (AI)-based loop detection. The system consists of an array of 15 inertial measurement units (IMUs) mounted on a flexible printed circuit board that can be retrofitted into the instrument channel of conventional colonoscopes. Using sensor fusion algorithms, the position and orientation of individual IMUs are estimated to reconstruct the 3D shape of the colonoscope in real time. The system successfully reconstructed the colonoscope shape in a silicone colon phantom, and the AI model achieved high loop-detection performance with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.95 on test data. These results demonstrate feasibility in an artificial environment, while further validation in clinical settings is required.
Keywords: ai | colonoscopy | imu | looping | sensor

Title: Data-Driven Energy Planning in Developing Countries: An Integrated LEAP-Machine Learning Approach
Abstract: Developing countries encounter substantial obstacles in regional energy planning stemming from scarce historical data and insufficient forecasting methodologies, thereby impeding the formulation of effective sustainable energy transition strategies. Conventional Long-range Energy Alternative Planning (LEAP) models frequently depend on static assumptions that diminish projection accuracy, especially under data-limited conditions. This study develops and applies an integrated hybrid algorithm–LEAP (HA–LEAP) framework to improve the precision of long-term regional energy planning and assess sustainable energy transition scenarios in Gorontalo Province, Indonesia. The research utilizes a quantitative case study methodology that integrates artificial intelligence with LEAP modeling, incorporating genetic algorithms and various optimization techniques. The HA–LEAP framework exhibits significant predictive performance enhancements compared to conventional LEAP approaches, achieving higher accuracy and diminished forecasting errors. Modeling results project a fundamental transformation in Gorontalo’s energy portfolio, with renewable energy penetration rising from 1.0% in 2015–41.8% by 2050, while petroleum dependency declines by 83% to 15.4%. Energy elasticity projections indicate successful decoupling between economic growth and energy consumption. This investigation presents the first comprehensive artificial intelligence-integrated energy planning methodology specifically designed for developing regions experiencing data constraints. The framework provides policymakers with superior analytical instruments for evidence-based sustainable energy transition planning, demonstrating the viability of ambitious renewable energy targets while preserving energy security objectives.
Keywords: developing countries | energy security | hybrid algorithms | Long-range Energy Planning | machine learning | renewable energy transition | scenario modeling

Title: Framework for Personalized Music and Lyrics Generation
Abstract: The Framework for Personalized Music and Lyrics Generation is designed to generate customized lyrics and corresponding melodies based on user input. The framework comprises two key components: lyrics generation and music melody generation. The lyrics generation module explores and compares two different approaches: topic modeling-based generation and retrieval-augmented generation. The effectiveness of these approaches is evaluated using various linguistic and structural metrics, including perplexity score, repetition score, coherence, and syllable variance. The music melody generation module takes the syllabified lyrics as input and generates suitable musical notes using different sequential models. The performance of these models is assessed based on statistical metrics to determine their effectiveness in producing musically coherent melodies. By integrating these components, the proposed framework aims to enhance personalized music composition by leveraging advanced techniques in natural language processing and deep learning.
Keywords: Lyric Data Processing | Lyrics Generation | Music Melody Generation | Retrieval-Augmented Generation | Sequential Models | Topic Modeling

Title: A Comprehensive Survey of Bird Sound Classification Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches
Abstract: Birds play an essential role in maintaining ecological balance, and the accurate identification of bird species is crucial for biodiversity monitoring. Traditional identification through physical characteristics and vocalizations is often hindered by the variability in appearance and complex acoustic patterns. These days advances in machine learning, particularly deep neural networks (DNNs), have significantly improved the performance of audio-based classification systems. This study presents an overview of various methods used for of bird sound classification techniques, emphasizing spectrogram-based analysis, feature extraction methods, such as MFCC, and the integration of deep learning models. This survey aims to support future research efforts in developing reliable and scalable bird sound identification systems.
Keywords: audio signal processing | bioacoustics | bird sound classification | bird species identification | deep learning | environmental monitoring | feature extraction | machine learning | MFCC | spectrogram

Title: A laser embedding frame work for cross-lingual hate speech detection
Abstract: Detection of hate speech in multilingual as well as code-switched settings continues to remain a major challenge for online content moderation. This paper presents a new method that employs Language-Agnostic SEntence Representations (LASER) embeddings with token-level language identification along with adapter layers for efficient hate speech identification in 13 languages. Our method provides three contributions: (1) token-level language identification to analyze code-switching behavior, (2) light-weight adapter layers for per-language few-shot learning with no loss of multilingual representation, as well as (3) an explanation module with clear decision-making. We experiment on a multilingual collection of 219,981 samples, which shows that our new model attains an F1-score of 0.7337 as well as AUC-ROC of 0.8802 with a 0.65 percentage point improvement over a baseline. Token-level analysis shows that 60.78% of text samples display code-switching behavior, indicating a need for fine-grain language identification. Our explanation study shows that LASER embeddings contribute 3.5 times more than language features towards final prediction. The generalizability of the model extends over a large range of languages that cover European, Asian, as well as low-resource languages, with good cross-lingual performance with hate detection rates between 20.10% as well as 48.71% across test languages.
Keywords: adapter layers | code-switching | deep learning | explainable AI | Hate speech detection | LASER embeddings | multilingual NLP

Title: Real-Time Human Tracking and Predictive Danger Zone Forecasting for Public Safety
Abstract: Community safety and security in high-density urban environments such as public transport terminals, commercial zones, schools, colleges, and places of public assembly need precautionary monitoring of pedestrian movement to mitigate accidents, risks, and hazards.
