Finally, a "dynamic human-machine collaborative creation mechanism"is proposed, which establishes a multi-node manual intervention interface to achieve real-time matching of machine and human creative intent. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm consumes only 28% of the time in the "detail optimization"phase, significantly lower than unimodal models (45%) and non-collaborative models (38%). However, its real-time performance in complex creative scenarios (such as multi-instrument arrangements) needs to be further improved.
Keywords: Affective Computing | Human-Computer Collaborative Creation | Modal Emotion Fusion | Music Generation Algorithm

Title: Estimating the Direction of Arrival Using Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: This work presents the performance of deep-learning-based Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation under challenging acoustical conditions. The problem is approached within a Sound Event Localization and Detection (SELD) scenario, restructured as a multi-class classification task and implemented using Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks (CRNNs). Two adapted network structures are introduced and analyzed: M-DOAnet, proposed exclusively for sound source localization, and M-SELDnet, which enables simultaneous sound event detection and localization. Experimental validation was performed using the STARSS23 dataset, comprising 13 sound classes and more than seven hours of audio data represented through spectrograms and acoustic intensity features derived from First-Order Ambisonics (FOA). The obtained results confirm the robustness of the proposed classification-based method. In particular, M-DOAnet provides competitive localization accuracy, achieving a DoA estimation error of 6.00° and perfect tracking performance (100% MOTA), while requiring significantly reduced computational resources, with a total training time of approximately 4.5 hours, compared to existing state-of-the-art approaches.
Keywords: acoustic signal processing | convolutional recurrent neural networks | Deep learning | deep neural networks | Direction of arrival estimation | sound event localization and detection | spatial audio analysis

Title: Visual Image Analysis for Predicting Hospital Food Leftovers Percentage Using Random Forest Regressor
Abstract: Monitoring hospital food consumption is an important component of nutritional care and food service management. Standard methods such as direct observation and weighed records remain the reference standard but they take a lot of work, subjective, and difficult to apply consistently in large scale monitoring. The proposed approach used a Random Forest Regressor trained on visual features that combine color, texture, and area information extracted from paired before and after meal images. The experiment was conducted using the LeFood-Set dataset, which contains 524 pairs of hospital meal images along with corresponding weight annotations. Two experimental scenarios are implemented: raw images and segmented images, where segmentation isolates the food region to enhance the relevance of extracted features. Experimental results show that the model trained on segmented images achieved better performance, with MAE = 11.35, MSE = 239.87, and R<sup>2</sup> = 0.834, outperforming the raw-image model (MAE = 17.43, MSE = 439.13, R<sup>2</sup> = 0.697). Feature importance analysis further shows that area and texture based features contribute most to prediction accuracy. This shows that segmentation not only improves precision but also increases model interpretability. These results confirm that integrating computer vision and machine learning provides a reliable framework for objective nutrition monitoring and future real-time food waste assessment in hospital settings.
Keywords: feature importance | image based dietary assessment | leftover estimation | random forest regressor | segmentation

Title: Multimodal MRI-Based Early Detection and Monitoring of Multiple Sclerosis Via an Efficientnet-Powered Deep Learning Framework
Abstract: Early identification and longitudinal disease surveillance Multimodal MRI offers an essential basis to identify and track Multiple Sclerosis (MS) disease pathology and progression, providing a subtle analysis. This paper presents an EfficientNet-based deep learning model that takes advantage of multimodal MRI levels to classify and track MS effectively and efficiently through clinically significant stages. The suggested system preprocesses and combines T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and FLAIR pixel intensity distribution and implements EfficientNet to extract features and classify them. The classification measures, plotted in terms of confusion matrix and ROC curve, exhibit moderate discriminatory capabilities in lower stage MS with AUCs of between 0.49 and 0.54 and per-class validation rates of about 34 % showing that it is not easy to discriminate minor variations in pathology. Although its results are modest, the stability of the framework is manifested by the strong performance of the model in different epochs and the low loss of validation. An efficacious EfficientNet implementation presents a good start to better multimodal diagnostic instruments to detect and monitor MS in its early stages.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Early Detection | EfficientNet | Multimodal MRI | Multiple Sclerosis

Title: Acoustic DOA Estimation in Underwater Environments by Integrating Spatial Domain Wiener Filtering and Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Objective Human activities in shallow-sea regions have increased with the progressive development and utilization of marine environments. However, interference from noise sources such as water currents, vessels, and marine organisms substantially reduces the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of received signals, leading to performance degradation in conventional Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation algorithms. These limitations affect accurate target localization and detection, which are essential for underwater acoustic applications. This paper proposes a method that combines Wiener filtering with deep learning, specifically an improved Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), to enhance the robustness and accuracy of DOA estimation in shallowsea environments by addressing challenges such as noise interference and grid mismatch. Methods The proposed algorithm integrates Wiener filtering and deep learning to optimize DOA estimation. First, Wiener filtering is applied to the covariance matrix of the received signals to reduce noise. Considering the complexity of underwater acoustic environments, this preprocessing step is essential for preserving spatial signal features and enhancing the effectiveness of network training. Second, an improved CNN architecture is designed to perform both classification and regression tasks, enabling accurate DOA angle estimation while correcting off-grid errors. A fractional label correction strategy is introduced to mitigate grid mismatch, allowing prediction errors to be compensated and the estimated angles to align more closely with true values. The network is trained using a large-scale dataset of simulated underwater acoustic signals, and its feasibility is verified through real-world sea trial data. Results and Discussions The proposed method is validated using both simulation data and sea trial data, demonstrating superior performance under low SNR conditions. Simulation results show that incorporating Wiener filtering improves overall network performance by 25.20% (Fig. 5). The proposed algorithm achieves lower estimation errors in low SNR environments (Fig. 6). Compared with the MUSIC and ESPRIT algorithms, the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) is reduced by 93.42% and 92.14%, respectively, at an SNR of —20 dB. Moreover, as the SNR increases, the algorithm exhibits a gradual reduction in estimation error (Fig. 6). In sea trial experiments, the algorithm accurately identifies target azimuths and achieves lower estimation errors compared to conventional methods (Fig. 9, Table 1). These results indicate that the proposed method meets the requirements for robustness and accuracy in practical underwater acoustic applications. Conclusions This paper proposes a method for direction estimation in shallow-water environments that integrates Wiener filtering with a deep learning-based CNN to address the performance degradation caused by low SNR conditions in conventional algorithms. The combination of noise reduction preprocessing with CNN model training enhances both network efficiency and estimation accuracy. Simulation and sea trial experiments yield the following results: (1) Overall network performance is improved by 25.20% through Wiener filtering optimization; (2) The improved binary cross-entropy loss function enables the network to perform both classification and regression tasks for DOA estimation; (3) The algorithm demonstrates higher robustness to noise interference and grid mismatch, particularly under low SNR and limited snapshot conditions, making it suitable for practical deployment. However, the network is trained using datasets with known source numbers. Future research will focus on network designs that accommodate more diverse source conditions, including blind source scenarios and adaptive noise reduction models.
Keywords: Deep learning | DOA estimation | Grid mismatch | Wiener filtering

Title: Modeling Frequency Correlation to Achieve Better Long-Term Series Forecasting
Abstract: Long-term time series prediction is of great value in finance, meteorology, and industry. The early mainstream frameworks are statistic-based models such as ARIMA and Moving Average. Such models were gradually replaced by deep learning models because they could not handle complex nonlinear relationships. Well-known deep models include RNN, LSTM, GRU, etc. However, these models exhibit limitations in capturing long-term temporal dependencies. The recent success of Transformer in natural language processing (NLP) has inspired their adaptation for time series forecasting. Their attention mechanism can model dependencies at arbitrary time steps, which is theoretically suitable for long-term prediction tasks. However, studies have shown that a simple MLP model can outperform Transformer-based approaches, which has led to renewed interest in MLP-based forecasting frameworks. A limitation of existing methods is that they mainly focus on time domain features and ignore frequency domain information. Although some studies have attempted to use frequency domain information, they examine single variables in isolation, and fail to capture frequency domain correlations across variables. To address these challenges, we propose a model based on cross-spectral entropy filtering and causal dilated pyramid convolution, called CSConv. Specifically, CSConv uses cross-spectral entropy for adaptive frequency-domain filtering, preserving multivariate joint spectral characteristics. In addition, CSConv includes a time-weighted causal dilated pyramid convolution, which captures multi-scale dependencies through dilation structures and temporal decay weights. The final prediction is achieved through an MLP-based architecture that decomposes trend, cyclical, and residual components. We validate the performance of CSConv on eight real-world datasets and compare the results with advanced baseline models. Experiments show that our model achieves competitive results on multiple evaluation metrics.
Keywords: Convolution | Fourier | Frequency Filtering | Time Series Forecasting

Title: DeepSalt: Bridging Laboratory and Satellite Spectra Through Domain Adaptation and Knowledge Distillation for Large-Scale Soil Salinity Estimation
Abstract: Soil salinization poses a significant threat to both ecosystems and agriculture because it limits plants' ability to absorb water and, in doing so, reduces crop productivity. This phenomenon alters the soil's spectral properties, creating a measurable relationship between salinity and light reflectance that enables remote monitoring. While laboratory spectroscopy provides precise measurements, its reliance on in-situ sampling limits scalability to regional or global levels. Conversely, hyperspectral satellite imagery enables wide-area observation but lacks the fine-grained interpretability of laboratory instruments. To bridge this gap, we introduce DeepSalt, a deep-learning-based spectral transfer framework that leverages knowledge distillation and a novel Spectral Adaptation Unit to transfer high-resolution spectral insights from laboratory-based spectroscopy to satellitebased hyperspectral sensing. Our approach eliminates the need for extensive ground sampling while enabling accurate, largescale salinity estimation, as demonstrated through comprehensive empirical benchmarks. DeepSalt achieves significant performance gains over methods without explicit domain adaptation, underscoring the impact of the proposed Spectral Adaptation Unit and the knowledge distillation strategy. The model also effectively generalized to unseen geographic regions, explaining a substantial portion of the salinity variance.
Keywords: Domain Adaptation | Hyperspectral Imagery | Knowledge Distillation | Soil Salinity Estimation | Transformer

Title: Interpretable Infrared Target Detection via Multi-Scale Robust Principle Component Analysis
Abstract: Infrared small target detection faces challenges of minimal target size, low signal-to-noise ratios, and complex backgrounds. Deep learning methods achieve impressive results, which lack theoretical interpretability. Although the Robust Principle Component Analysis (RPCA) theory has been integrated with deep learning to build up RPCANet, this network is limited by single-scale decomposition. To this end, we formulate infrared small target detection task as a Multi-scale RPCA Optimization (MRO) model, which can be unfolded as the MRO-Net. Considering that the MRO network does not explore cross-stage interaction and image-domain weighted fusion is overemphasized, we extend the standard MRO-Net as MRO-Net+ by inserting multi-scale decomposition block from each stage of MRO model into the encoder, bottle-neck layer, and decoder of high-throughput dynamic U-shape architecture. Experimental results have shown the proposed explicable MRO-Net+ has better performances than several state-of-the-art methods such as RPCANet, UIUNet, DNANet, AGPCNet, etc.
Keywords: Cross-stage interaction | Deep unfolding network | Infrared small target detection | Multi-scale decomposition

Title: MusicAIR: A Multimodal AI Music Generation Framework Powered by an Algorithm-Driven Core
Abstract: Recent advances in generative AI have made music generation a prominent research focus. However, many neural-based models rely on large datasets, raising concerns about copyright infringement and high-performance costs. In contrast, we propose MusicAIR, an innovative multimodal AI music generation framework powered by a novel algorithm-driven symbolic music core, effectively mitigating copyright infringement risks. The music core algorithms connect critical lyrical and rhythmic information to automatically derive musical features, creating a complete, coherent melodic score solely from the lyrics. The MusicAIR framework facilitates music generation from lyrics, text, and images. The generated score adheres to established principles of music theory, lyrical structure, and rhythmic conventions. We developed Generate AI Music (GenAIM<sup>1</sup><sup>1</sup>GenAIM: https://genaim.intellisky.ai/), a web tool using MusicAIR for lyric-to-song, text-to-music, and image-to-music generation. In our experiments, we evaluated AI-generated music scores produced by the system using both standard music metrics and innovative analysis that compares these compositions with original works. The system achieves an average key confidence of 85%, outperforming human composers at 79%, and aligns closely with established music theory standards, demonstrating its ability to generate diverse, human-like compositions. As a co-pilot tool, GenAIM can serve as a reliable music composition assistant and a possible educational composition tutor while simultaneously lowering the entry barrier for all aspiring musicians, which is innovative and significantly contributes to AI for music generation.
Keywords: AI music generation | image-to-music generation | lyric-rhythm alignment | lyric-to-music generation | melodic motion | melodic smoothness | natural language processing

Title: The Sub Band-based Randomizer (SBR): A Novel Approach to Balanced Randomization for Vast Configuration Spaces
Abstract: Deep Learning (DL) has emerged as a transformative force in domains such as Large Language Models, Computer Vision, etc. underpinned by the intricate functionality of DL operators. These operators execute mathematical transformations, facilitating the resolution of complex computational tasks. The efficacy of operator execution is paramount to the performance of DL models; however, variations in hardware can reveal latent implementation inefficiencies. A considerable proportion of defects in DL applications can be traced back to operators, posing challenges for developers who may lack insights into library intricacies. During training and inference, operators navigate vast configurations, complicating validation due to infinite sample space. Manual test development is challenging, and conventional randomization techniques face difficulties due to the curse of dimensionality, resulting in less optimal data distributions. This results in suboptimal test coverage and the risk of undetected anomalies. To address these challenges, we introduce the Sub Band-based Randomizer (SBR) tool, implemented in C++, designed to generate balanced operator shape configurations and tensor data. Central to SBR's effectiveness is its control distribution technique, which offers precise management over the distribution of generated data, making it versatile for multidomain use-cases. It ensures efficient resource utilization and optimized execution time, thereby enhancing test coverage and accelerating maturity of software stack. By offering a structured approach to randomization, the proposed solution effectively addresses inefficiencies in operator validation, establishing itself as an indispensable instrument for bolstering the reliability and robustness of AI applications across diverse fields. Furthermore, the utility extends beyond DL operators, offering potential applications in any domain where controlled randomization and efficient coverage of configuration spaces are paramount.
Keywords: Computer Vision | Deep Learning | Large Language Model | Operator Validation | Randomization Techniques | Sub-Band Randomizer | Tensor Shape Generation | Test Coverage

Title: Improving Piano Notation Transcription in Bisa Aku Bisa Children's Music Using Deep Learning
Abstract: This study provides a comparative analysis of manual and AI-Assisted transcription of the children's musical 'Bisa, Aku Bisa'. A basic understanding of manual music notation-especially when learned through instruments like the piano-can help young composers more quickly develop their skills in digital composition using tools such as MuseScore 4 and the music21 Python module. Learning how to arrange music also supports authentic self-expression, helping young composers convey emotions and develop healthy emotional regulation. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence have facilitated the automation of music notation transcription, with deep learning techniques. The research findings indicate that transcription using the music21 python module significantly reduce the time required compared to manual transcription and the use of MuseScore 4. These research results offer valuable insights into the pedagogical application of algorithmic music composition and transcription technologies in children's music education. Moreover, the process of creating children's musical scores by young composers inherently requires a combination of experiential understanding and instrument proficiency. Future research should focus on enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of automated music transcriptions systems, particularly in the context of educational applications and child-focused compositions.
Keywords: children's music | deep learning of music composition | piano notation transcription

Title: AI Based Advanced Green Supply Chain Through Sustainable Finance Strategies
Abstract: The evolution of the need to have sustainable industrial processes has led institutions to re-examine the traditional supply chain patterns that mostly overlook the environmental and financial harmony. The current paper outlines the AI-based model, which solves an appalling gap between sustainable finance initiatives and performance of green supply chains. Although there are greater levels of understanding on environmental, social and governance (ESG) measurements, numerous supply chains are unable to incorporate such aspects in their current operational and investment decisions that are real-Time. In order to address this issue, the paper presents a new kind of architecture, Intelligent GreenChain-Fin Framework (IGC-Fin), which allows making adaptive, carbon-innovative decisions in supply chain operations based on the use of artificial intelligence through the possible support of green financial instruments. The framework combines Deep Q-Learning used in the dynamic optimization of policy with the Green-Aware Digital Twin, which offers an in-Time, in-Time simulation, and a finance-Aware decision engine that uses ESG scores and carbon pricing models. Also, the model uses blockchain to facilitate transparent chain running of sustainability measures within the supply chain. With a single approach of operational intelligence and financial sustainability, IGC-Fin has a complete solution to enhance economic resilience and environmental performance. The suggested framework is an important game changer in the process of data-driven logistics and sustainable investment, which could create continuous value in the global supply networks. The suggested IGC-Fin Structure has an overall accuracy of 97.8%.
Keywords: AI | ESG | Green Supply Chain | GSCM | IGC-Fin

Title: SFA-DCSL: A Dynamically Hierarchical Enhancement PEFT Framework for Imbalanced Speech Emotion Recognition Research
Abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) has emerged as one of the core technologies in the field of human-computer interaction, and its significance continues to grow. As a key breakthrough in the field of SER, Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) enhances both computational efficiency and accuracy through innovative approaches such as directional parameter updates and modular designs. Experimental results on the Crowd-sourced Emotional Multimodal Actors (CREMA-D) dataset demonstrate that fine-tuning only 0.8% of the parameters can achieve an accuracy of 98.3%, which is comparable to that obtained through full-parameter fine-tuning. Although PEFT technology has shown strong performance across various dimensions, its effectiveness in speech and emotion recognition on the CREMA-D dataset is limited due to the uneven distribution of categories. To address this issue, this paper proposes an enhancement method based on the PEFT framework, integrating techniques like Hierarchical Feature Augmentation (SFA) and Dynamic Cost-Sensitive Learning (DCSL) to effectively tackle the data class imbalance problem. The experimental results reveal an 8.12% improvement in recognition accuracy under the unbalanced conditions of the CREMA-D dataset, significantly enhancing speech emotion recognition performance. This approach not only offers a novel technical pathway to address the class imbalance issue in emotion recognition but also holds considerable value for efficient fine-tuning strategies in lowresource settings. Furthermore, it can be generalized to other natural language processing tasks facing category imbalance, offering technical solutions for related research fields.
Keywords: Dynamic cost-sensitive learning | Full parameter fine-tuning | Hierarchical feature enhancement | Parameter efficient finetuning | Speech emotion recognition

Title: The Dual Role of Artificial Intelligence and LLM in Cybersecurity
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming the cybersecurity landscape, taking a dual role as both enablers of defense. This paper explores this duality by distinguishing between AI for Security, where intelligent models enhance threat analysis, intrusion detection, and automated mitigation, and Security for AI, which focuses on securing models themselves against adversarial manipulation, data leakage, and prompt-based exploitation. To empirically evaluate the capabilities of modern LLMs in cybersecurity, we conducted extensive experiments using the newly developed CyberMetric dataset, which assesses cybersecurity knowledge across multiple domains such as cryptography, network defense, and software vulnerabilities. Our evaluation of twenty state-of-the-art LLMs-including GPT-5 Chat, Grok 4 Fast, Qwen3 235B, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and DeepSeek V3.2-demonstrates that the 2025 generation of models achieves near-human performance, with GPT-5 Chat reaching 98.75% accuracy and several open-source models performing within a 2-3% margin. These results highlight the growing maturity of open LLM ecosystems for cybersecurity applications and confirm that modern LLMs are becoming reliable instruments for cyber defense, capable of supporting automated threat analysis, vulnerability assessment, and compliance verification, while also emphasizing the need to ensure their safety, transparency, and resilience against misuse.
Keywords: Adversarial Machine Learning | Artificial Intelligence | Cybersecurity | Deep Learning | Explainable AI | LLM | Threat Detection

Title: Perception-Guided EEG Analysis: A Deep Learning Approach Inspired by Level of Detail (LOD) Theory
Abstract: Objective: Analyzing the dynamic nature of human perceptual states from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals remains challenging for conventional deep learning methods. This study explores a novel approach, inspired by Level of Detail (LOD) theory, to address this by dynamically adjusting EEG data analysis to guide perceptual states. The core objective is to improve the identification accuracy of these states from EEG signals and to provide new avenues for personalized psychological therapy. Methods: The research employs portable EEG devices to collect data, combined with music rhythm signals for analysis. We introduce the LOD theory to dynamically adjust the processing levels of EEG signals, extracting core features related to perception. The software system is developed using the Unity engine, integrating audio materials and MIDI structures, and enabling the integration of EEG data with Unity. The deep learning model includes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for feature extraction and classification, and a Deep Q-Network (DQN) for reinforcement learning to optimize music rhythm adjustment strategies. Results: The CNN model achieved a 94.05% accuracy in the perceptual state classification task, demonstrating excellent classification performance. The DQN model successfully guided subjects' EEG signals to the target perceptual state with a 92.45% success rate on the validation set, requiring an average of 13.2 rhythm cycles to complete the state guidance. However, subjective feedback from users indicated that approximately 50 % of the researchers experienced psychological sensations corresponding to the target state during the rhythm adjustment process, suggesting room for improvement in the system's effectiveness. Discussion: The experimental results validate the potential of the LOD-based deep learning algorithm in EEG biofeedback and perceptual guidance. Despite the preliminary achievements, the study has limitations, such as the single source of the dataset, the subjectivity of labels, and the need for further optimization of the dynamic adjustment mechanism in the reinforcement learning reward function. Future research will expand to diverse subject groups, introduce more varied musical elements, and explore more advanced reward functions to enhance the model's generalization ability and personalized experience.
Keywords: deep learning | EEG analysis | Level of Detail (LOD) theory | mental state classification | perceptual guidance

Title: Bridging Speech and Text using Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Next-Gen Language Understanding
Abstract: Speech, body language, and design features are challenging due to lack of learning practices. Conventional multimodal systems process speech, text, and visual cues separately using rigid encoders, which limits contextual understanding and reduces performance in sentiment analysis, transcription, and emotion recognition (ER). Recent approaches use attention-based transformers to model cross-modal relationships, but they often struggle with long-range dependencies and high computational costs. This paper presents a hybrid transformer-based framework that fuses audio, text, icons, body language, and design features through adaptive cross-modal attention to enhance semantic understanding and reduce word error rate (WER). Audio is encoded using Wav2Vec 2.0, text is processed with a transformer, and visual cues such as lip movements and hand shapes are embedded for fusion. A joint loss models cross-modal relationships for stable training. An attention-aware mechanism selects key tokens, and a lightweight gated projection controls feature flow, lowering computation without reducing accuracy. Experiments on CMU-MOSEI, LibriSpeech, and MuST-C demonstrate gains in semantic accuracy (SA), F1-score, ER, and reductions in WER, achieving up to a 15% improvement in SA and a 3.5% drop in WER.
Keywords: balanced loss | dynamic attention | multimodal fusion | speech-text alignment | transformer model

Title: Weighted Ensemble Classification for Misinformation Detection using Optimized TF-IDF Features on a Large-Scale News Dataset
Abstract: The swift spread of fake news across digital platforms is really shaking up how people view information and trust in the media. This study rolls out a cutting-edge machine learning framework that works like a team to tell apart real news from fake. It combines the unique strengths of several models: Support Vector Machines (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Multinomial Naive Bayes (NB), and Gradient Boosting (GB). We've put together a thorough dataset of 44, 898 news articles 21, 417 of which are true and 23, 481 that are fake. To make sense of the text, we preprocess it by tokenizing, removing stopwords, lemmatizing, and using TF-IDF vectorization to pull out key features. We train our individual models on 80% of the data (that's 35, 918 samples), saving the other 20% (8, 980 samples) for testing. By using an ensemble approach, we blend the predictions from these models with optimized weights, which we fine-tune through a grid search to get the best accuracy. An impressive test accuracy of 99.82% is achieved. We dive into detailed evaluations, including classification reports and sample predictions, which show that our model holds up well across various types of news content. Our results highlight how effective ensemble learning can be for detecting fake news, providing a reliable and scalable solution for automated content verification - perfect for media monitoring and social media platforms. We also pinpoint some areas that could use improvement, like tackling the stylistic similarities between true and fake news, setting the stage for future research into better feature engineering and model designs.
Keywords: Ensemble Learning | Fake News Detection | Logistic Regression | Machine Learning | Naive Bayes | SVM

Title: Machine Learning-Driven Robotic Surgery: Advancing Precision, Efficiency, and Accessibility
Abstract: Robotics and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are increasingly being integrated across various sectors, including healthcare. In robotic surgery, however, achieving high precision remains a critical challenge, as even minor errors can have life-Threatening consequences. This study employs the YOLOv5 model developed by Ultralytics for surgical tool detection, addressing the fundamental need for accurate visual recognition. To enhance performance beyond detection, the SORT algorithm is integrated for real-Time tracking of surgical instruments, significantly improving accuracy, precision, and operational adaptability in diverse environments. The proposed system is evaluated using the Cholec80 dataset, with the model undergoing iterative fine-Tuning after every ten surgical procedures to optimize its weights and improve overall precision. Comparative analysis against existing approaches demonstrates that the YOLOv5-SORT integration achieves superior detection and tracking performance. The findings confirm that this approach enhances both the reliability and flexibility of AI-Assisted robotic surgery systems, paving the way for safer and more precise medical interventions.
Keywords: Accessibility | Cholec80 | Continuous learning | Deep learning | Deep SORT | Faster R-CNN | Machine learning | Robotic | SORT | surgery | Surgical tool | tracking | YOLO

Title: Research on State of Health Evaluation Mechanism of Electrochemical Energy Storage System Based on Time Series Modeling and Deep Learning
Abstract: The degradation of battery performance during long-term cyclic charging and discharging limits its large-scale application. Therefore, it is very important to accurately evaluate the state of health (SOH) of electrochemical energy storage system (ESS). In this paper, a SOH evaluation mechanism integrating time series modeling and deep learning is proposed. By constructing IWTFFM-MSAM mixed model and "absolute SOH+ relative SOH"dual matrix correction strategy, the accuracy and robustness of evaluation are significantly improved. IWTFFM (improved wavelet time-frequency fusion model) solves the problem of insufficient resolution of traditional time-frequency analysis methods, realizes efficient decoupling of multi-band degradation features, and improves the resolution of signals in both time and frequency dimensions. MSAM-Net (multi-scale attention mechanism network), by introducing multi-scale convolution structure and attention mechanism, dynamically identifies and weights the importance of different time scales and frequency scales, and enhances the ability to capture key degradation information of batteries in different aging stages. By quantifying the degradation differences between cells and fusing the matrices, the dual-matrix correction strategy can effectively solve the problem that the degradation paths of cells in the battery pack are inconsistent due to factors such as ladder mixing and manufacturing process differences, and improve the accuracy of cluster-level SOH evaluation. The experimental results show that the IWTFFM proposed in this paper is excellent in feature extraction, with the time-frequency resolution of 8ms/0.01Hz and the calculation time reduced to 0.49 seconds/cycle. MSAM-Net is superior to mainstream models such as LSTM and CNN+Attention in prediction accuracy, with RMSE of 1.72%, MAPE of 1.98% and R2 as high as 0.982. The dual matrix correction strategy significantly reduces RMSE and maximum deviation in cluster-level evaluation, and the missed detection rate of abnormal monomers is as low as 4.1%. The research in this paper provides an efficient and accurate new method for SOH evaluation of electrochemical energy storage system, which has important theoretical significance and application value.
Keywords: attention mechanism | bimatrix correction | deep learning | electrochemical energy storage system | evaluation mechanism | IWTFFM-MSAM mixed model | multiscale convolution structure | series modeling | state of health

Title: Renewable Energy Output Prediction using Machine Learning and Logistic Regression - A Framework
Abstract: This work attempts to explore the improved applicability of a logistic regression framework to predict the renewable energy output of a place based on natural and engineered weather condition data, such as temperature, wind speed, humidity, air pressure, solar radiation, and wind power index. After cleaning and processing the dataset, the machine learning model was trained to classify the energy output of that place into high or low energy categories with 92.88% accuracy. The Confusion Matrix approach was taken to test the other aspects of the model performance, such as Precision, Recall, and F1 Score, and all came out to be 0.93 on a scale of 0 - 1 (weighted mean). A feature engineering approach for creating a Wind Power Index helped improve the results, leading to the observation that the classifier is highly precise in identifying high-energy output locations (a precision score of 0.98) after proper training. Though the dataset lacks temporal features such as the time of the day/week/month/year, the energy will be high; future implementations can certainly include these features.
Keywords: Energy Prediction | Feature Engineering | Logistic Regression | Machine Learning | Renewable Energy | Weather Condition Data

Title: INVOX: A Robust System For Detecting Synthetic Voice Attacks
Abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI), especially in Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Voice Conversion (VC) technologies, has greatly enhanced the quality of voice-driven applications while also increasing vulnerability to synthetic voice attacks. This paper introduces Invox, an explainable deep learning framework aimed at ensuring reliable detection and characterization of AI-generated spoofed speech. The framework incorporates log-mel spectrogram preprocessing, a hybrid CNN - Transformer architecture for hierarchical feature representation, and an ensemble decision model that merges CNN-BiLSTM, SVM, and GBDT classifiers. Additionally, InVox presents a Voice Authenticity Score, detailed spoof-type categorization, and attention-driven visual interpretability to facilitate forensic analysis and promote transparent decision-making. By combining robust modeling with explainable outputs, InVox provides a practical and secure foundation for implementation in banking, customer service, and high-assurance voice authentication settings.
Keywords: CNN | Deepfake audio | Ensemble learning | Explainable AI | Synthetic speech detection | Transformer

Title: AI Generative Tools: Redefining Learning for Malaysian University Students
Abstract: In the contemporary digital era, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has exerted a substantial impact on higher education, particularly through generative AI tools that facilitate idea generation, summarization, and assignment enhancement. While these technologies offer notable academic advantages, concerns persist regarding their potential to diminish students' independent thinking, academic integrity, and intrinsic motivation. This study examines the influence of generative AI on university students across five domains: critical thinking, academic performance, fact-checking behavior, academic integrity, and study motivation. Data was collected from 124 students via Google Forms and analyzed using PSPP software, employing Spearman's rank correlation, one-sample t-tests, and chi-square tests. Findings reveal a positive but modest association between AI usage and improvements in academic performance, critical thinking, fact-checking, and motivation. Although more frequent users tend to exhibit permissive attitudes toward AI, its use does not demonstrate a strong relationship with academic misconduct. Overall, generative AI functions primarily as a supportive academic instrument rather than a transformative force within higher education.
Keywords: Academic integrity violation | Critical thinking skills | Generative AI tool | Study motivation

Title: Deep Ensemble Emotion Recognition from Speech Using YOLO Feature Extraction and RF+ADABoost Classification
Abstract: Emotion recognition through speech has proven to be an important aspect of developing human-computer interaction systems that will be empathetic. Conventional methods use manually designed feature and distinct modules to extract features and classify them which in many cases leads to less than optimal performance. The study presents a completely end-to-end deep learning system which learns discriminative audio representations using raw speech signals. A YOLO Ensemble is used as a feature extractor in the proposed system to extract salient patterns of time and spectral features within speech. These are then fed through a hybrid ensemble classifier with the combination of Random Forest (RF) and AdaBoost which is known as RFADABoost that improves the strength of classification with complementary decision boundaries and adaptive weighting. Unlike traditional CNN-LSTM models that need to process data in a specific order (like a sequence), this architecture doesn't rely on that. Instead, it uses ensemble learning, which is good at handling complex, high-dimensional data without needing to follow a strict sequence. When compared to the conventional classifiers Decision Tree and Naive Bayes, it can be seen that YOLO+RFADABoost performs much better, as it was able to reach 96% accuracy, which confirms that the algorithm is efficient in emotion recognition in speech.
Keywords: AdaBoost | CNN+LSTM | Decision Tree | NaiveBayes | RF | Speech recognition | YOLO

Title: DMSA-Unet: A Novel Architecture for Polyp Segmentation with Dynamic Multi-Scale Attention and CARAFE Upsampling
Abstract: Colorectal cancer, a leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally, often develops from adenomatous polyps. Precise polyp segmentation in colonoscopy is crucial for early intervention. However, the high variability in polyp size, shape, and texture, coupled with low contrast and blurred boundaries, poses significant challenges to existing segmentation models. This paper proposes DMSA-Unet, a novel end-to-end deep learning model, to address these issues. Built upon a ResUNet backbone, our model incorporates two key innovations: a Dynamic Multi-Scale Attention (DMSA) module and a Content-Aware Reassembly of Features (CARAFE) upsampling module. The DMSA module adaptively adjusts receptive fields and attention weights based on input context, enabling robust feature extraction across polyps of varying scales. The CARAFE module dynamically predicts upsampling kernels, enhancing the reconstruction of sharp and accurate segmentation boundaries. Comprehensive evaluations on the public Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB datasets demonstrate that DMSA-Unet achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of Dice coefficient and IoU, outperforming several existing methods. This study aims to provide a more accurate and reliable computer-aided diagnostic tool for clinicians.
Keywords: Attention Mechanism | CARAF | Colorectal Polyp | Medical Image Segmentation | U-Net

Title: Dynamic Multi-Scale Selective Graph Convolutional Network with Multi-Level Feature Refinement
Abstract: Skeleton-based action recognition technology holds significant application value in fields such as intelligent surveillance and human-computer interaction. However, existing methods still face severe challenges when processing visually similar yet semantically distinct ambiguous actions, primarily manifested as insufficient discriminative power of semantic features and inadequate use of multi-scale features. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Dynamic Multi-Scale Selective Graph Convolutional Network with Multi-Level Feature Refinement (DMS-GCN-HFR). The core innovations of this work are: (1) Selective Hierarchical Feature Refinement Mechanism, which selectively deploys the feature refinement module at the network's deeper layers (L6, L7), leveraging the rich semantic information inherent in deep features, and enhances feature discriminative power within higher-order semantic spaces while introducing feature optimization only at these deeper layers, significantly reducing computational overhead; (2) Dynamic Spatio-temporal Weight Fusion Strategy, which adapts the contribution weights of spatial and temporal branches based on action complexity, replacing traditional fixed-weight fusion; (3) Multi-granularity Contrastive Learning Framework, which combines scale-aware contrastive loss with differentiated prototype update strategies to achieve fine-grained discrimination of ambiguous actions. Experimental results on NTU60 and NTU120 datasets demonstrate a significant performance improvement on challenging similar actions, while maintaining excellent parameter efficiency with only marginal increases in computational complexity.
Keywords: Contrastive learning | Feature refinement | Graph convolutional networks | Skeleton-based action recognition

Title: Lightweight Multi-Step Refinement Network for 3D Registration Based on State Space Model
Abstract: 3D registration plays a crucial role in the manufacturing, precision measurement, and installation of large-scale astronomical instruments and similar equipment. Most existing learning-based PCR methods rely on Transformers, which suffer from quadratic computational complexity, limiting their usage in astronomical instruments with limited computational capabilities. To address this issue, a lightweight multi-step refinement 3D registration network (LMRN) based on state space models is proposed. First, a lightweight state space model is introduced, reducing the quadratic complexity of existing Transformer-based registration networks to linear complexity while achieving a balance between low floating-point operations and registration performance. Then, a multi-step refinement module is incorporated to overcome the registration failure issues faced by existing networks in low-overlap scenarios. Experimental results on the 3DMatch dataset demonstrate that the proposed registration network reduces computational requirements for both training and inference while minimizing performance degradation, achieving an effective balance between the two.
Keywords: 3D registration | deep learning | multi-step refinement | state space model | transformer

Title: Deep Learning Models for Speech Dereverberation: Dual-Label LSTMs Compared with Transformers
Abstract: In this paper, we present a reverberation removal approach for speaker verification, utilizing dual-label deep neural networks (DNNs). The networks perform feature mapping between the spectral features of reverberant and clean speech. Long short term memory recurrent neural networks (LSTMs) are trained to map corrupted Mel Filterbank (MFB) features to two sets of labels: i) the clean MFB features, and ii) one-hot vector representing speaker ID, estimated clean pitch tracks, or the fast Fourier transform (FFT) clean spectrogram. The performance of reverberation removal is evaluated by equal error rates (EERs) of speaker verification experiments. To contextualize our approach's performance, we also conducted preliminary comparison with SepFormer, a transformer model for speech reverberation removal, using the pre-trained model on WHAMR! dataset made available by its original authors.
Keywords: deep neural networks | dereverberation | long short term memory | speaker verification | transformers

Title: Web-Based Detection of Dyslexia Using Reading and Memory Features
Abstract: Dyslexia is a neurodevelopmental learning disorder common to the capacity to read, write, and spell, despite an average or above-average level of intelligence. Failure to identify early enough tends to cause academic and low confidence as well as social problems. Conventional diagnostic techniques used are based on manual assessment, which is subjective, time consuming and it requires qualified personnel. The proposed work suggests the CognitivePath AI web-based intelligent dyslexia detector that will operate under the power of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). The platform provides the multimodal data as interactive activities based on the handwriting strokes, reading tests, and memory-based games. Supervised learning models that are used to extract the features (handwriting patterns, reading fluency, pronunciation accuracy, and recall performance) into a combination include Random Forest, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks. The system is efficient at predicting the level of dyslexia risk, which is offered as a digital screening instrument to educators and parents. The goal of this approach is to transform the early detection of the dyslexia into the objectivity and scalability so that every educational institution, anywhere around the globe, could gain access to it.
Keywords: Behavioral Biomarkers | Dyslexia Detection | Education Technology | Gamified Assessments | Multimodal Fusion

Title: DeepThyroScan:EfficientNetB2 Architecture for Automated Thyroid Diagnosis
Abstract: There are thyroid diseases like hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism that can inflict serious dysfunctions on the human body in cognition skills, or the heart and the pregnancy. Early and proper diagnosis of these diseases ensures that there will be improved patient outcome, as well as effective treatment. Standard diagnoses include imaging and blood tests among others; both of them can be both expensive and time-consuming. In the work, the application of deep learning to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the diagnostic process was proposed through a modified EfficientNetB2 model used to classify thyroid disorders automatically. The model was divided into two categories, which were healthy (0) and thyroid illness (1), and was taught on a set of 7,288 images of thyroid. The pre-processing, picture resizing, standardizing, and enriching of the dataset were used to guarantee model robustness. The EfficientNet B2 model had an excellent performance of 90 percent with precision of 0.94, recall of 0.88, and F1-score of 0.91 in the detection of thyroid abnormalities in classes 1 (thyroid illness) and class 0 (healthy). The performance of the model was determined by employing a confusion matrix, loss curves and classification criteria and this made a well-balanced strategy to reduce false positives and false negatives. Through improved access to early detection methods, promotion of health, and facilitation of the development of innovative medical solutions that would be suitable to sustainability goals, this work advances healthcare. The outcomes indicate the possibility of the instrument to identify early thyroid diseases because EfficientNetB2 is an automated medical diagnostics system that is scalable and computationally efficient.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | automated healthcare | deep learning | early diagnosis | EfficientNetB2 | machine learning in healthcare | medical imaging | Thyroid disease classification

Title: Quantum Machine Learning for Disease Prediction: A Comparative and Multimodal Study on Early-Stage and Chronic Conditions
Abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is fast becoming a powerful instrument in medical diagnostics because it can process high-dimensional data and small samples efficiently. This paper is a detailed analysis of QML models used for disease prediction, with a relative comparison of Variational Quantum Classifiers (VQC), Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks (QCNN), and Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM) in clinical environments. We suggest a new multimodal quantumclassical hybrid approach that analyzes electronic health records (EHR), medical imaging, and biosignal data by means of dedicated QML pipelines with late fusion for ultimate decisionmaking. Recent IEEE literature is integrated in experimental performance glimpses to demonstrate the merits, difficulties, and viability of QML in real-world healthcare applications. The envisioned architecture provides the foundation for future applications of quantum-enhanced diagnostics with existing quantum simulators as well as emerging hardware.
Keywords: Disease Prediction | Healthcare AI | Medical Diagnosis | Multimodal Fusion | Quantum Machine Learning | Quantum Neural Networks | Quantum Support Vector Machine | Variational Quantum Classifier

Title: Intelligent Audio-to-Text Framework: Natural Language Processing Based AI-Powered Transcription and Subtitle Creation System
Abstract: In today's digital world, videos have become the main way we communicate, entertain, and educate. A slight distortion in media has created a barrier, especially in a country like India with so many languages. This project aims to create an AI-supported automated subtitle generation system that will make Kannada, Hindi, and English videos more accessible by accurately and synchronously turning spoken language into text. The system transcribes audio even in noisy environments and accommodates different accents and dialects using speech recognition algorithms and signal processing techniques. Efforts are underway to improve the raw transcriptions by adding proper punctuation, segmentation, and context through new NLP methods like Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), text normalization, and word segmentation. These transcriptions are then synced with the audio to generate both post-production and real-time subtitles. By speeding up the subtitle process, this framework enhances accessibility for the hard of hearing and broadens the audience to include people with different language preferences. This, in turn, helps broadcasters, publishers, and educators make content multilingual. It also allows for integration with public announcements, educational apps, and streaming platforms.
Keywords: automatic speech recognition (ASR) | Natural language processing (NLP) | real-time transcription with precise synchronization | text normalization | word segmentation

Title: Speech-Based Parkinson's Detection in Noisy Conditions using a Hybrid CNN-RNN Model
Abstract: The approach showcases a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network - Recurrent Neural Network (CNN-RNN) model aimed at determining Parkinson's disorder from speech signals in noisy environments. The model combines CNNs, which excel at feature extraction, with RNNs, which are fundamental for learning sequential patterns, allowing the model to strongly identify the vocal impairments of the disorder. The proposed system advances detection accuracy and trustworthiness in real-world conditions with ambient noise, thanks to the noise-resilient preprocessing and deep learning fusion. The proposed hybrid architecture considerably exceeds the performance with an accuracy of 91.4% of traditional single model approaches according to experimental outcomes, and therefore, provides a feasible means of diagnosing Parkinson's disorder at a very early stage in speech in a non-invasive way.
Keywords: Deep Learning Fusion | Medical Diagnosis | Parkinson's determination | Vocal Impairments

Title: Predicting Music Origin with Deep Learning
Abstract: This study explores the use of deep learning to predict the geographic origin of music based on audio features. Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) were extracted to capture acoustic information, while language was identified using OpenAI's Whisper model to provide additional contextual signals. A late fusion neural network architecture combining Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers for sequential MFCC input and dense layers for non-sequential language features were employed to support both classification and regression tasks. The classification model achieved an accuracy of 33.03% across 56 countries and territories, substantially outperforming the uniform random baseline (1.79%), the prior-weighted random baseline (3.59%), and andom Forest baseline (9.1%). The regression model produced a Mean Great-Circle Error (MGCE) of 2,754.83km. While regression offers more flexibility for geographic estimation, classification demonstrated a more promising performance with the current dataset. This work highlights the potential of multimodal learning in music-origin prediction.
Keywords: deep learning | geographic classification | LSTM | MFCC | MIR | Multimodal learning

Title: AI-Driven Predictive Analytics for Financial Risk Assessment and Smart Investment Decision-Making in Global Markets
Abstract: Climate risks, sustainability prerequisites and digital transformation have increased the volatility of international financial markets and hastened the adoption of artificial intelligence to conduct predictive analytics in financial risk analysis and investment choices. The literature indicates the application of the various methods: machine learning regression and decision tree models have been applied to capture behavioral finance patterns, deep learning can improve the accuracy of stock market forecasting by 10 to 15 % over classical econometric models, as well as natural language processing of financial disclosures improves the performance of ESG portfolios by about 12 % over traditional benchmarks. Moreover, AI-powered robo-advisors have also boosted the number of investors adopting sustainable investing by almost 20% and blockchain-based infrastructures have lowered the exposure to operational risks by an average of 30. Although these wins are successful, there still exist issues with prioritizing predictive accuracy and regulatory compliance and ethical issues. In this work, these methodologies are integrated and a hybrid predictive analytics approach is proposed, based on financial text mining, behavioral modeling and climate-risk remote sensing data. The framework will enhance greater precision in forecasts by at least 18% than traditional single-model forecasts and will match investment policy with indicators of sustainability. What will emerge is a stronger, flexible, and transparent decision-making instrument in global markets that will enable investors in reducing systemic risks and exploiting opportunities in a more uncertain world.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | behavioral finance | ESG | financial risk assessment | global markets | machine learning | Predictive analytics | sustainable investment

Title: AI-Enabled Orbital Trajectory Optimization for Low-Earth Satellites: A Hybrid Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: Hybrid deep learning architectures have become effective instruments for simulating nonlinear orbital dynamics in Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) systems. This paper suggests a hybrid framework that uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) to combine Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for accurate orbital trajectory optimization. The model uses Two-Line Element (TLE) data from the NORAD/CelesTrak General Perturbations (GP) catalogue and the Simplified General Perturbations 4 (SGP4) model to make normalised Cartesian position vectors. The CNN layers find spatial correlations in orbital sequences, and the LSTM layers find long-term temporal dependencies. Experimental evaluation shows that the suggested model has an overall prediction accuracy of 96.4%, with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.021 km and a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 0.94%. The model also makes calculations more efficient, with an energy-performance ratio 2.5 times higher than baseline methods and an average inference time of 8.6 milliseconds per prediction step. Combining physics-based orbital parameters with data-driven learning makes it possible to make reliable, understandable, and energy-efficient predictions about trajectories. The results show that the framework can be used for real-time satellite navigation, avoiding collisions, and smart mission planning in future autonomous LEO operations.
Keywords: CNN-LSTM Model | Energy-Efficient Satellite Navigation | Hybrid Deep Learning | Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) | NO-RAD/CelesTrak TLE Data | Orbital Trajectory Prediction | SGP4 Propagation

Title: Design and Performance Optimization of an Infrasonic Recording System for Elephant Call Detection
Abstract: Many animals, such as elephants, whales, crocodiles, big cats like tigers and lions, use infrasonic sound to communicate. This low-frequency channel is mostly invisible to human senses. Studying this range helps us understand animal behavior and tackles the increasing issue of human-wildlife conflict. However, current infrasonic recording systems tend to be costly and are not meant for ecological studies. This limits their use in conservation efforts. This paper introduces a new, low-cost infrasonic recording system that turns a geophone into a microphone. It includes special amplification, filtering circuits, and software modules for signal analysis. The system was tested with indoor trials using HG-24HS and HG-07 sensor setups. The HG-24HS geophone has shown the best results for sensitivity, signal-to-noise ratio, and classification accuracy. Signal processing has been enhanced with Kalman filtering, the Enhanced Empirical Denoising Method (EEDM), and machine learning algorithms. A Support Vector Machine classifier attained superior Accuracy and Precision in separating infrasonic calls from background noise. Field validation at Theppakadu Elephant Camp proved that the system could successfully record elephant infrasonic signals in controlled tests. Analyzing these recordings demonstrated clear communication patterns and reduced false detections. The results indicate that this system offers an affordable, portable, and scalable option for wildlife monitoring. Besides contributing to behavioral research, it has practical uses in early warning systems for reducing human-elephant conflicts and opens new paths for bioacoustics research in low-frequency communication.
Keywords: geophone sensor | human-elephant conflict | infrasonic signal | machine learning classification | signal processing | wildlife monitoring

Title: Developing A Multi-Disease Risk Prediction Model Using Machine Learning
Abstract: The ability to predict the risk of multiple diseases accurately is a crucial step toward improving early diagnosis and healthcare outcomes. With the potential to improve and automate the diagnostic procedure, machine learning methods have become more effective instruments for this aim in recent years. This study focuses on developing a machine learning model to predict the risk of different diseases by using Transfer Learning, where pre-trained models are used to enhance the prediction accuracy. A comparison was done of three models, namely, Transfer Learning (proposed model), VGG-16, and DenseNet-121, in the multi-disease risk prediction context. The proposed Transfer Learning model reached a maximum accuracy of 98.3%, which is higher than the VGG-16 at 94% and DenseNet-121 at 92% in key evaluation metrics, such as precision, recall, and F1-score. This demonstrated how Transfer Learning could produce more balanced and accurate predictions of a variety of diseases, including influenza, asthma, diabetes, heart attacks, and many others. The findings provide evidence that Transfer Learning can indeed be applied to real-world health care scenarios, and it thus offers a very promising tool in the early prediction of disease. Future work will include fine-tuning the model, dealing with class imbalances in health datasets, and ensemble learning to enhance the model even further. Ultimately, this may then allow for an efficient deployment of machine learning models in clinical settings to improve disease diagnosis and manage risks.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Disease Diagnosis | Healthcare Applications | Machine Learning | Model Optimization | Multi-Disease Risk Prediction | Transfer Learning

Title: Animal sound classification using Machine Learning
Abstract: This paper describes the development of a monitoring solution utilizing acoustics data for the automated recognition and classification of wild animals. We implemented machine learning (ML) algorithms for classification fed with features extracted from audio file streams. Mel-frequency cepstrum coefficients (MFCCs), Low-level, Psychoacoustic, and Auditory filterbank temporal envelope features were applied as four subset features. The data used in this study comes from different sources: the data science community Kaggle, Macauley Library, xeno-canto, and the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund. Together, these sources provided 2944 audio files on five taxa, including Birds (7.2% of files), cats (5.6% of files), domestic dogs (3.9% of files), Pan Troglodytes (chimpanzee) (66.4 % of files), Gorilla beringei (mountain gorilla) (1.6% of files), and wind (15.3 % of files) as background noise. Methodically, the results of Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Naive Bayes are presented. ML algorithms were compared, considering the use of the macro average (F1 score) as a performance metric instead of accuracy due to the imbalanced nature of the dataset. SVM performed best (93%), followed by Random Forest (92%). The MFCC feature set performed well against all other feature sets combined.
Keywords: Acoustic Monitoring | Biodiversity | Machine Learning | Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients | Multiclass Classification

Title: AI-Driven Pre-Identification of Mental Health Issues and Adaptive Learning Tools to Enhance Academic Performance in Students
Abstract: Mental health and emotional well-being are crucial to academic success and workplace productivity. The rising stress levels amongst students due to prolonged exposure to stressors in schools and workplaces calls for early detection and intervention strategies, owing to the demands of modern education and professional settings. Classic evaluation methods, like self-reported surveys, are frequently centered on speculation and omit on-the-spot adaptability. This work introduces a system that employs machine learning models for the evaluation of mental health disorders and their control.For students, it uses the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21) to compute real-time psychological, behavioral and physiological indicators of user stress levels. When detected, automated alerts and intervention strategies (psychiatrist consultations, parental notifications, adaptive learning. In corporate environments, a real-time emotion detection system uses computer vision, speech analysis, and biometric sensors to assess employees' emotional states, allowing for tailored workplace interventions such as personalized workload management and mindfulness initiatives. Moreover, a music recommendation system creates personalized playlists tailored to their needs, curbing workplace stress and improving productivity.
Keywords: DASS-21 | Emotion recognition | Machine learning | Mental health | Predictive analytics | Student stress detection | Workplace well-being

Title: Beyond Traditional Diarization: Enhancing Speaker Attribution Using GenAI
Abstract: Speaker diarization, the process of segmenting and labeling audio recordings by speaker identity, is essential for various applications but remains challenging, particularly in multilingual and noisy environments. This paper investigates the performance of state-of-the-art diarization methods, such as Pyannote, WhisperX, Speechlib, channel split approaches, Azure, and NVIDIA NeMo, on multilingual datasets featuring Thai, Indonesian, and English languages. Comparative Analysis is extensively conducted on these approaches and incorporated novel post-processing solution that integrates Generative AI (GenAI) techniques, specifically large language models (LLMs), to refine the diarization results, addressing common issues such as word errors, missing segments, and unresolved speaker overlaps. This comprehensive comparison of existing techniques and introduction of a new GenAI-based post-processing method demonstrate enhanced performance and accuracy in real-world applications, with broad implications for both academic research and practical applications in multilingual and noisy environments.
Keywords: Generative AI | Large Language Models | Multilingual Speech Processing | NeMo | Noisy Environments | Pyannote | Speaker Diarization | Whisper

Title: A Hybrid AI-Powered Framework for Accurate Urban Flood Prediction and Real-Time Early Warning Systems
Abstract: Urban flooding presents increasing threats to densely populated cities as a result of climate change and urbanisation. Current flood prediction models often show deficiencies in real-time accuracy and do not deliver timely notifications, hence constraining disaster preparedness. This proposed study presents a hybrid AI system that combines Gradient Boosted Decision Trees with a CNN-BiLSTM ensemble to analyse spatial-temporal patterns from different datasets. The system, employing rainfall and water-level data from Kaggle, attains exceptional performance metrics: 97.83% accuracy, 98.15% recall, and an AUC-ROC of 0.993, markedly exceeding baseline models such as Random Forest and LSTM. The framework's real-time alarm distribution improves responsiveness, potentially minimising flood-related damages and fatalities. This methodology enhances flood prediction through the integration of explainability, accuracy, and operational security, providing it an essential instrument for urban disaster management.
Keywords: BiLSTM | CNN | Disaster Management | Flood Risk Assessment | Gradient Boosted Decision Trees | Hybrid AI Framework | Multi-Source Data Integration | Real-Time Early Warning | Spatial-Temporal Analysis | Urban Flood Prediction

Title: Generalization-Oriented Optimization of Music Performance Concentration Models using Deep Transfer Learning and Real-Time Sensors
Abstract: Musical performance is a complex cognitive and perceptual activity, and the level of attention involved directly impacts the stability of the performance and the overall artistic expression. However, traditional attention research relies heavily on questionnaires or behavioral measurements, which makes real-time performance and cross-scenario adaptation difficult. Therefore, this study proposes a framework for music performance attention modeling and generalization optimization based on multi-modal real-time sensor fusion and deep transfer learning. This framework comprehensively utilizes multi-modal signals such as facial landmarks, blink intervals, head posture, performance movements, and musical features. After rotation-scale normalization and robust statistical normalization, the signals are fed into a deep network architecture for low-dimensional feature extraction. Furthermore, a spatial/channel attention mechanism is introduced to highlight key modal information. Furthermore, a multi-objective optimization function is constructed, which includes a classification loss, a domain adaptation loss, a sensor conflict cost, and an energy constraint. The experimental part was based on 120 60-second performance clips from 20 subjects, with a data sampling frequency of 50 Hz. The results show that the average accuracy of the proposed framework reached 86.5% in the three-category task. This result is 5.5% higher than the best baseline model. In regression prediction, the Pearson correlation coefficient increased to 0.72, and the root mean square error decreased to 7.8. In cross-scene testing (rehearsal domain training → stage domain testing), the performance of this model only decreased by 3.4% after introducing domain adaptation optimization. In dynamic time series evaluation, the prediction of a single performance clip was highly consistent with the true curve. For numerical level, the frame-level correlation coefficient reached as high as 0.79, and the average error was approximately ±8 points (0-100 scale).
Keywords: Cognitive State Modeling | Deep Transfer Learning | Generalization Optimization | Music Performance Concentration | Neural Network Adaptation | Real-time Sensors

Title: Design and algorithm optimization of component automatic test system for multi-scene experiment
Abstract: Facing the urgent demand of intelligent manufacturing, aerospace and other fields for high-performance verification of components in multi-physical field coupling environment, this paper proposes a multi-scene automatic test system based on containerization and cloud native architecture, and integrates reinforcement learning and multi-modal deep learning algorithm to realize collaborative optimization of test efficiency and accuracy. Through the concept of "software definition test", the system containerizes 10 kinds of mainstream instrument drivers and services, and the scene reconstruction time is reduced from hour level to minute level; Construct a dynamic parameter optimization model based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), and shorten the testing time by 32.6% in IGBT switch loss testing under the constraint of ± 0.5% accuracy; A multi-source heterogeneous data fusion fault diagnosis engine is developed, and the time series waveform and environmental/static characteristics are extracted by 1D-CNN and fully connected network respectively. Under the condition of small samples (20 faults of each type), the macro-Average F1 value reaches 0.92, which is 18% higher than that of single-source model. The experimental results show that the proposed system and algorithm effectively solve the problems of traditional test flow rigidity, low efficiency and insufficient fault coverage, and provide an extensible and adaptive complete solution for multi-scenario and high-complexity component reliability verification.
Keywords: component automatic test | deep deterministic policy gradient | multi-scene experiment | test system

Title: Multimodal Emotion Recognition Using Acoustic Features and Deep Language Models
Abstract: Emotion recognition makes it possible for systems to respond to users in natural and commiserative ways, emotion recognition is so necessary part of affective computing. To classify emotions more precisely, in this study a framework was devised, including text and voice data. For the audio part, we relied on MFCC based representations (9,793 samples) and popu- lar databases EMO-DB (535 samples) and IEMOCAP (10,190 samples). This involves feeling both at high, low, and neutral levels of intensity excitement frustration and anger sadness etc. We explored models including stacking, multilayer perceptron, voting ensembles and XGBoost with data such as pitch, loudness, MFCCs and chroma. They ranged in accuracy from 39 percent to 45 percent. We used 5,427 labeled samples for 28 fine-grained emotions such as pride, remorse. appreciation, curiosity and admiration for the text modality. We analyzed the transcribed text after performing speech-to-text using BERT and BiLSTM. The text-based models - at nearly a 95% accuracy rate - were better than the audio-only ones. Even back then, we were insulated from relying on any one source. Instead, we combined the-textual and speech-predictions. This stage felt logical since each had its contribution to make: the words themselves would clarify what was said, while the voice would convey how it was presented. Together this gave us a solid base to work from in terms of a consistent, balanced product. The audio signals have value and can pair with text to provide information that allows systems to recognize emotions.
Keywords: Affective Computing | and Speech Processing | Audio Features | BERT | BiLSTM | Emotion Recognition | Ensemble Learning | Multimodal Learning | Natural Language Understanding (NLU)

Title: Enhancing Hindi Speech Recognition Using Regularization Techniques
Abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) for Hindi remains a challenging problem due to limited large-scale annotated datasets. This work presents weight decay and dropout in Hindi Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) using a self-curated dataset. The study fine-tunes the model and analyzes the effect of different weight decay coefficients with and without dropout. The results show that low weight decay without dropout leads to overfitting, unstable precision/recall values, and high Word Error Rates. The optimal balance between underfitting and overfitting is reached with a moderate weight decay of 0.01; this lowers WER and precision/recall. Dropout continuously increases model robustness in all settings, while larger weight decay initially causes underfitting. With the lowest WER and the highest stability across precision, recall, and F1 scores, the optimal overall performance is obtained when 0.01 weight decay and dropout are combined.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Dropout | Hindi Speech Recognition | Weight Decay | WER

Title: Comparative Analysis of Text-to-Speech Synthesis Systems
Abstract: TTS systems have advanced significantly in the last ten years so that computers can produce highly natural sounding and humanlike speech from text. The improvements were due to advancements in speech synthesis architectures, linguistic modelling and deep learning. This paper provides a comparison of several TTS architectures by comparing and summarizing findings of previous research studies and implementations. A variety of techniques will be compared; those include: Seq2Seq (Tacotron-2 + WaveGlow), Non-Autoregressive (FastSpeech 2), Transformer-based (TransformerTTS), Statistical Parametric Speech Synthesis (SPSS, HMM-based), and Concatenative synthesis. The study includes both previously published results and insights from the authors own experiments using different datasets and processing pipelines. The comparison of the techniques will occur in terms of; corpus requirements, preprocessing complexity, feature extraction methods, architecture design, emotional expression, quality of generated speech (MOS or intelligibility), and the trade-offs between strengths and weaknesses. Each technique was analysed using reported performance metrics, data sets, and generation of expressive and intelligible speech under different conditions. The comparative analysis shows that the neural TTS architectures (Seq2Seq, FastSpeech 2, TransformerTTS) consistently achieved higher levels of naturalness and flexibility than all other architectures studied here resulting in better MOS scores than all others, and, the traditional HMM-based and concatenative methods are faster, resource efficient, but less expressive than the neural models.
Keywords: acoustic modeling | deep learning | prosody | speech synthesis | Text-to-Speech

Title: Ai-based offline speech recognition for kazakh, russian and english languages
Abstract: This paper presents a novel full autonomous multilingual audio transcription system tailored to Kazakh, Russian, and English. The proposed solution integrates a language detection module based on SpeechBrain with a transcription engine using Vosk, and employs FFmpeg for robust audio preprocessing. The system automatically detects the language from the initial 10 seconds of an audio stream, selects the corresponding acoustic model, and produces an accurate text transcription. Experimental evaluations on both synthetic and real audio data indicate that our approach achieves competitive performance in terms of accuracy (with word error rates ranging from 5 to 10% under optimal conditions) and processing speed, while operating entirely on local resources without dependency on cloud services. These features make it particularly suitable for applications in digital forensics and other domains that require secure real-time transcription capabilities.
