Keywords: Audio Preprocessing | Digital Forensics | FFmpeg | Kazakh Language Processing | Language Detection | Modular System Architecture | Multilingual Speech Transcription | Offline Speech Recognition | Resource-Constrained Environments | SpeechBrain | Vosk API | Word Error Rate

Title: A Systematic Review of Machine Learning-Based Infant Cry Signal Analysis
Abstract: The current studies on the interpretation and classification of infant cry signals. It focuses on data collection, machine learning classification methods, and cross-domain signal processing. Since infants communicate primarily through crying, interpreting Infant Cry Audio Signals (ICAS) is crucial. Our proposed diagnostic system integrates Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) algorithms with various audio features to identify health-related issues such as discomfort, hunger, or disease. Traditional approaches often fail due to inaccurate interpretation, noise, unpredictability, and limited annotated data. This paper examines recent Neural Network (NN) architectures, preprocessing techniques, feature extraction methods (e.g., MFCC, Spectrograms), and classification algorithms like K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM). It evaluates current advancements and highlights challenges in data collection, annotation, and model performance. The study aims to guide future research toward developing reliable, real-time infant monitoring systems for caretakers and healthcare providers.
Keywords: Audio Features | Data Collection | Deep Learning | Gaussian Mixture Model | Infant Cry Audio Signals | K-Nearest Neighbor | Machine Learning | Support Vector Machine

Title: MuGen-100: A Diverse and Geographically-Rich Dataset for Music Genre Classification
Abstract: In our paper we explore Music genre classification and more precisely the datasets used for that. We noticed that the available datasets used for experiments and research and sometimes even deployed products, there is often a limited cultural perspective [1]. To help this field toward more inclusive and culturally-aware machine learning models, we introduce MuGen-100: A dataset of 100 genres curated from different areas and places of the world. We hope to provide the public with a benchmark resource that provides cultural richness and offers practical and flexible utility. We will also share some baseline performance results to showcase MuGen's potential and how it could be further extended and enhanced in future works.
Keywords: Audio deep learning | CNN | Cultural diversity in machine learning | Dataset | Music genre classification | Music Information Retrieval (MIR) | Random Forest

Title: YOLOv11m-Seg: Real-Time Semantic Segmentation of Instruments and Anatomy in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
Abstract: The understanding of surgical scenes in real-Time plays a crucial role in enhancing patient protection, and operational speed, and robotic surgical system independence. The deployment of robust systems faces three main obstacles: restricted training data availability and unbalanced class distribution, and time-sensitive prediction requirements. This study evaluates YOLOv8m-seg, YOLOv10m-seg, and YOLOv11m-seg models for laparoscopic cholecystectomy segmentation tasks using the CholecSeg8k dataset. The proposed system uses domain-specific augmentation techniques, including blood occlusion simulation and motion blur effects, to boost performance in actual surgical operating conditions. The experimental results demonstrate that YOLOv11m-seg achieves the best performance with 0.92 mAP@0.5, 0.82 mIoU, and 0.91 F1-score while outperforming SegMatch, and SID-RAS and other state-of-The-Art models like RT-DETR and LoViT. This research confirms that YOLOv11m-seg as a dependable and efficient tool for surgical instrument and anatomical segmentation making it suitable for real-Time operating room applications.
Keywords: Computer Vision | Deep Learning | Instrument Segmentation | Operating Room Automation | Phase Recognition | Surgical AI

Title: Hierarchical BiLSTM Encoding for Vocal-Driven Cover Song Detection
Abstract: Cover song detection remains a challenging task due to significant variations in key, tempo, timbre, and arrangement across different versions of the same song. In this paper, we propose a deep learning neural net that leverages isolated vocal stems and extracts multiple complementary low-level beat synchronized audio features - MFCC, Chroma and CQT. These features are processed through a multi-branch BiLSTM-Attention architecture designed to generate musically discriminative embeddings. We use triplet focal loss in training process.The unique combination of BiLSTM and hierarchical sparse attention mechanism improves the embedding separability. Experiments on the SHS100K dataset demonstrate good retrieval performance, achieving a MAP @ 10 of 0.713 and an MRI of 23.7.
Keywords: Attention Mechanisms | Cover Song Detection | Deep Metric Learning | Embedding | Music Information Retrieval | Neural Networks

Title: Integration of Adaptive Hearing Aid Systems with Real-Time Noise Suppression for Enhanced Communication in Dynamic Environments
Abstract: Hearing problems have a substantial impact on communication and quality of life, necessitating the use of modern auditory assistance systems. This study describes a real time smart hearing aid system that uses Digital Signal Processing (DSP) techniques to improve sound clarity and intelligibility in dynamic conditions. The system includes a high sensitivity microphone, a DSP processor for audio processing, and a small speaker for user feedback. Adaptive noise suppression, dynamic range compression, and individualized speech augmentation are key elements that provide excellent performance under a variety of hearing situations. The suggested system uses spectral subtraction for noise reduction, beamforming for directed sound capture, and equalization for frequency amplification tailored to individual hearing profiles. Furthermore, the device includes a simple UI for real-time modifications, allowing users to change settings based on ambient noise levels. The modular architecture allows for smooth interaction with forthcoming technologies like AI-based auditory profiling and Bluetooth connectivity for remote control via smartphones. These innovations make the system very adaptable and accessible to people of all ages and with hearing problems. This smart hearing aid, which combines cutting-edge DSP algorithms with tiny hardware, offers an affordable, portable, and user-centric solution for people with hearing impairment. The proposed methodology bridges the accessibility gap and advances auditory technology, paving the way for the next generation of hearing aids.
Keywords: adaptive filters | digital signal processing | Hearing aids | noise suppression | real-time audio processing | speech enhancement

Title: Deep learning-based Covariance Matrix Reconstruction for Root-MUSIC Algorithm
Abstract: Root-MUSIC is a classical high-resolution DOA estimation algorithm. However, it is based on strict model assumptions, and its performance degrades when model mismatches occur, such as scenarios involving sparse linear arrays (SLAs), coherent signals, or broadband signals. Its performance further deteriorates with limited snapshots and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). To address these challenges, we propose the Residual Covariance Reconstruction Network (RCR-Net), a deep learning framework that reconstructs an ideal, full-rank Hermitian-Toeplitz covariance matrix of a virtual uniform linear array (ULA) for Root-MUSIC. By leveraging the differentiability of the Root-MUSIC algorithm, the proposed framework enables end-to-end training and avoids requiring ground truth labels of the virtual covariance matrix for DOA estimation. The proposed method provides continuous, high-precision estimates and avoids the grid mismatch errors of classification-based approaches. A single network architecture can handle diverse scenarios without modification and successfully estimates more sources than physical sensors. Simulations show that the proposed method outperforms other sparse reconstruction methods and existing deep learning methods in challenging scenarios.
Keywords: broadband signals | coherent signals | deep learning | direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation | Root-MUSIC | sparse arrays

Title: Probabilistic Deep Learning for Musicians' Concentration Recognition from Facial Expressions via Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD)
Abstract: This study proposes a musician concentration recognition algorithm based on probabilistic deep learning and stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics. This algorithm models the state of concentration during performance by using dynamic features of facial expressions. At the algorithmic level, unlike traditional classification models, this algorithm geometrically views the evolution of facial expressions as a stochastic dynamical system on a manifold. It then uses SGLD to implement Bayesian approximate parameter sampling and posterior distribution estimation. This study created a four-layer hierarchical optimization framework in terms of model structure. In particular, the distillation layer uses variational inequalities to guarantee semantic transfer stability, the entropy control layer modifies the temperature and variance of the predicted distribution, the KL layer preserves distribution alignment, and the SGLD layer handles posterior sampling and uncertainty modeling. Efficient studies were carried out on the self-constructed Musicians' Concentration Facial Expression Dataset (MC-FED) to confirm its efficacy. Expert-annotated five-level concentration ratings and 18,000 high-resolution facial photos of ten musicians are included in this database. According to the results, the model outperforms ResNet-18 by 6.6% and conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by 11.3% in terms of classification accuracy. In terms of prediction uncertainty and mean squared error, it also performs the best. Ablation experiments further validate the key role of SGLD, entropy regularization, and distillation loss in improving the model stability and reliability. Time series prediction experiments demonstrate that the model can effectively capture the dynamic changes in concentration during performance.
Keywords: Cognitive State Decoding | Facial Expression Recognition | Musicians' Concentration | Probabilistic Deep Learning | Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD)

Title: Improving Small Object Detection Through Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Attention Mechanisms in Deep Learning Models
Abstract: The detection of small objects has become one of the most difficult problems in the field of computer vision because of the loss of fine-grained spatial information, confusion with a limited number of pixels, and random background, which is common with deep convolutional-based and transformer-based models. To overcome these inadequacies, this paper introduces a new Multi-Scale Attention-Enhanced Small Object Detection (MSAE-SOD) network that combines multi-scale adaptive multi scale feature fusion with hierarchical attention. It starts with an architecture that has a strong foundation based on feature extractions and can maintain low-level spatial details as well as meaningful semantics pattern. Multi-scale feature fusion module is then used to combine features at various depths with learnable fusion weights and this feature is done in a way that the resulting features should have an optimal balance of both texture insight and contextual knowledge. To make the discriminative power even stronger, channel attention, spatial attention, as well as transformer-based contextual attention are added to point out the corresponding channels, focus on the vital spatial areas, and establish long-range relationships. It is tested using the proposed model on the challenging datasets that have a large percentage of small objects such as MS COCO and VisDrone. The experimental output proves that MSAE-SOD beats the state of the art models like Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, YOLOv8, and DETR by a significant margin and improves mAP and specifically AP[[-S]] which will go as high as 7-8 percentage points. Moreover, the model is appropriate in terms of supporting real-time performance of more than 100 FPS, which is why it can be used in real-life applications as UAV surveillance, autonomous navigation, and remote sensing.
Keywords: Attention Mechanisms | Channel Attention | CNN-Transformer Hybrid Models | Deep Learning | Multi-Scale Feature Fusion | Object Detection | Real-Time Detection | Small Object Detection | Spatial Attention | Transformer Attention

Title: An Intelligent Assessment System for Yao Suona Performance Techniques Based on a Cross-Spectral Temporal Adaptive Attention Model
Abstract: Traditional folk instrument assessments suffer from low efficiency, poor consistency, and lack of visual feedback. To address these issues, we propose an end-to-end intelligent assessment and visual feedback system. It aims to enhance accuracy and teaching utility. The system employs a multi-branch convolutional neural network to extract STFT, constant-Q transform, and pitch contour features. A bidirectional gated recurrent unit and an adaptive attention mechanism enable dynamic modeling of individual techniques. Moreover, the accompanying visualization module presents performance differences in pitch, rhythm, and technique. It uses multiscale heatmaps and pitch deviation charts. The module supports segment analysis and interactive zooming. This aids targeted improvements. The system integrates audio input, feature extraction, temporal modeling, prediction, and visualization output. It forms a complete closed loop. Experiments show the framework outperforms traditional methods in accuracy, speed, and user experience. User surveys also indicate strong practicality and instructional value. However, the study also notes room for improvement in data diversity, streaming feedback, and model extension. Future work will explore additional instrument types. We will adopt advanced architectures and integrate with online teaching platforms.
Keywords: Attention Mechanism | Cross-Spectral Temporal Assessment | Deep Learning | Intelligent Teaching System | Multiscale Visual Feedback | Yao Suona

Title: Developing a Strong End-to-End Semantic Approach for Transcribing Spoken Language to Text in Impaired Wireless Conditions
Abstract: As 6G networks advance, semantic communication offers a transformative approach by sending data's fundamental meaning instead of its unprocessed signals. In this context, we introduce DLSC-SR is an end-to-end semantic communication approach employing deep learning that is particularly suitable for speech recognition tasks. Instead of conveying the entire speech waveform, DLSC-SR identifies and sends only the semantic elements relevant to text, reducing bandwidth consumption significantly. The transmitter utilizes convolutional and recurrent neural networks to convert speech spectrograms into compressed semantic features, which are subsequently sent through a wireless communication channel. At the receiving end, a decoder rebuilds these features and retrieves the textual content using a greedy decoding algorithm. The model is tuned. with the connectionist temporal classification (CTC) loss function, enabling effective handling of variable-length sequences. Performance evaluations over AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels demonstrate that DLSCSR achieves improved character and word recognition accuracy, particularly in low-SNR scenarios. Moreover, the model shows resilience to changing channel conditions without needing retraining, making it a strong candidate for 6G applications.
Keywords: 6G Communication | DLSC-SR | semantic communication | speech recognition

Title: Water Quality Classification Using LightGBM: A Machine Learning Approach on a Large-Scale Dataset
Abstract: This research paper revolves around the diversifying water quality in variety range and it's in variety range and its classification, presentation of parameters and machine learning models. The primary purpose of this study is to make a model will be able to use input values and classify water quality. The model is available for anyone who wants to use on their dataset as well. The dataset employed in this investigation is designed to evaluate water quality parameters. Comprising in excess of 2.5 million entries, the extensive volume afforded the LightGBM algorithm the necessary breadth to cultivate robust predictive capacity, culminating in remarkably precise outcomes. Although the inquiry incorporated several alternative classifiers, including logistic regression, LightGBM outperformed all counterparts with an attained accuracy of 98%. The cleaning of dataset features emerged as a determinant of performance. The considerable dimensionality compelled rigorous sanitization to guarantee that the training process ingested reliable measurements. The cleaning regimen entailed duplicate elimination, imputation of missing observations, and the excision of extraneous variables, thereby refining the input supplied to the algorithm. The ramifications of these findings are considerable; the resultant, high-fidelity model represents an effective instrument for the classification of water quality. Practitioners, governing entities, and the research community may leverage its predictive capability to pre-empt and mitigate water contamination hazards, thereby advancing public health and ecological stewardship. Made publicly accessible, the model possesses the capacity to augment ongoing monitoring programmers and inform policy deliberations. In summation, the methodology substantively contributes to the domain of water quality assessment, advancing both theoretical and applied dimensions of the discipline. classification serves as an essential instrument that underpins accurate and comprehensive evaluations of water quality.
Keywords: Classification | LightGBM | Machine Learning | Satellite Images | Water Quality

Title: Adapter-Tuned IndicBERT for Hate and Source Detection in Code-Mixed Indic Texts
Abstract: The spread of hate speech in multilingual online environments especially in low resource, code mixed Indic languages is a serious technical and social issue. In this paper, we introduce a two stage pipeline that encompass hate speech normalization and determine its source of generation. In the first stage, we generate and making a new Indic hate to neutral text rewrite dataset available languages, and fine tune a multilingual encoder decoder model to do context sensitive normalization without changing the semantic intent. During the second stage, we confront the new challenge of AI generated vs human written hate speech detection. Building on adapter-based training on a light Indic language IndicBERT model, obtain a 90.3% accuracy in hate content source attribution, exceeding fully fine tuned MURIL and other baselines. Our finding shows that parameter light-weight, optimized implementations can compete with robust performance in content moderation and AI forensics. This paper provides the first end to end hate normalization analysis with AI vs human source attribution in hybrid Indic code environments, with implications for safer language technologies and accountable AI regulation.
Keywords: Adapter tuning | AI-generated toxicity | hate speech mitigation | Hate speech normalization | Indic languages | IndicBERT | MuRIL | NLP | source attribution

Title: Towards Efficient Speech-Text Jointly Decoding within One Speech Language Model
Abstract: Speech language models (Speech LMs) enable end-to-end speech-text modeling within a single model, offering a promising direction for spoken dialogue systems. The choice of speech-text jointly decoding paradigm plays a critical role in performance, efficiency, and alignment quality. In this work, we systematically compare representative joint speech-text decoding strategies - including the interleaved, and parallel generation paradigms - under a controlled experimental setup using the same base language model, speech tokenizer and training data. Our results show that the interleaved approach achieves the best alignment. However it suffers from slow inference due to long token sequence length. To address this, we propose a novel early-stop interleaved (ESI) pattern that not only significantly accelerates decoding but also yields slightly better performance. Additionally, we curate high-quality question answering (QA) datasets to further improve speech QA performance.
Keywords: conversational AI | Speech language models

Title: Omni-R1: Do You Really Need Audio to Fine-Tune Your Audio LLM?
Abstract: We propose Omni-R1 which fine-tunes a recent multi-modal LLM, Qwen2.5-Omni, on an audio question answering dataset with the reinforcement learning method GRPO. This leads to new State-of-the-Art performance on the recent MMAU and MMAR benchmarks. On MMAU, Omni-R1 achieves the highest accuracies on the sounds, music, speech, and overall average categories, both on the Test-mini and Test-full splits. To understand the performance improvement, we tested models both with and without audio and found that much of the performance improvement from GRPO could be attributed to better text-based reasoning. We also made a surprising discovery that fine-tuning without audio on a text-only dataset was effective at improving the audio-based performance.
Keywords: Audio Large Language Models (LLMs)

Title: KAN-AST: Kolmogorov-Arnold Network based Audio Spectrogram Transformer for Audio Classification
Abstract: Recently, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) have emerged as a promising alternative to enhance the performance of Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs). Instead of relying on traditional linear weights, KANs utilize spline-parametrized univariate functions, significantly improving interpretability and enabling dynamic learning of activation patterns. This novel approach has garnered considerable interest from the AI community and has seen rapid global adoption. While research on applying KANs to Machine Learning and Computer Vision has expanded, their application in audio processing remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we investigate the untapped potential of KANs in improving models for audio tasks. We propose the first Kolmogorov-Arnold Network-based Audio Spectrogram Transformer (KAN-AST) for audio classification. Our study demonstrates how replacing MLPs with KANs enhances the performance of the AST model, highlighting the potential of KANs in advancing audio classification.
Keywords: Audio Classification | Kolmogorov-Arnold networks | Multi-layer Perceptrons

Title: Efficient Speech Watermarking for Speech Synthesis via Progressive Knowledge Distillation
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of speech generative models, unauthorized voice cloning poses significant privacy and security risks. Speech watermarking offers a viable solution for tracing sources and preventing misuse. Current watermarking technologies fall mainly into two categories: DSP-based methods and deep learning-based methods. DSP-based methods are efficient but vulnerable to attacks, whereas deep learning-based methods offer robust protection at the expense of significantly higher computational cost. To improve the computational efficiency and enhance the robustness, we propose PKDMark, a lightweight deep learning-based speech watermarking method that leverages progressive knowledge distillation (PKD). Our approach proceeds in two stages: (1) training a high-performance teacher model using an invertible neural network-based architecture, and (2) transferring the teacher's capabilities to a compact student model through progressive knowledge distillation. This process reduces computational costs by 93.6% while maintaining high level of robust performance and imperceptibility. Experimental results demonstrate that our distilled model achieves an average detection F1 score of 99.6% with a PESQ of 4.30 in advanced distortions, enabling efficient speech watermarking for real-time speech synthesis applications.
Keywords: progressive knowledge distillation | speech privacy | speech watermarking | text-to-speech synthesis

Title: Colloquial-Aware Multimodal Fusion Network for Contextual Speech Formalization
Abstract: The increasing use of informal and colloquial language in user-created content on social media presents a significant challenge for automated comprehension systems. Such study demonstrates that we have to consider multi-modal information (text, audio and Video) to enhance the robust multimodal comprehension for colloquial expressions. The proposed model uses the pretrained Wav2Vec2.0 encoder, and a multi-head fusion transformer for aggregating semantic information across modalities. One of the main contributions is the proposed Colloquial-Aware Cross-Attention Module (CAXA) that dynamically correlates the slang-rich audio transcriptions with the visual or textual context for improved interpretability. CAXA-Net combines a Wav2Vec2.0 encoder for speech processing, a ViT (Vision Transformer) for frame-level image understanding, and a CNN-based visual feature extractor for scene image inputs. These streams are fused using a Cross-Attention Fusion Transformer (CAFT) which enables semantic alignment across modalities. Finally, a T5-based transformer decoder translates the fused colloquial text into its formal equivalent Experimental evaluation was conducted using the MELD (Multimodal EmotionLines Dataset), which contains real-world colloquial dialogues across modalities. The proposed CAXA-Net achieves 92.8% accuracy, 82.7 BLEU score, and 89.1 F1-score on the MELD dataset, demonstrating strong improvements over text-only and multimodal baselines.
Keywords: Colloquial Language Understanding | Cross-Attention Mechanism | Informal Speech Formalization | Multimodal Deep Learning | Vision Transformer | Wav2Vec2.0

Title: Machine Learning Approaches for Acoustic Feature-Based Stress Level Classification
Abstract: Speech signals contain rich acoustic features that can reveal a speaker's emotional and physiological state, including stress levels. In this work, we investigate the effectiveness of three supervised machine learning models-Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN)-for classifying stress levels from speech-derived features. A secondary dataset containing Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC1, MFCC2), Zero Crossing Rate (ZCR), energy, and pitch was pre-processed through normalization and partitioned into training and testing sets. The SVM model aims to maximize the separation margin between stressed and non-stressed classes, the Decision Tree model iteratively partitions the feature space based on information gain, and the ANN model simulates neural information processing through weighted layers. Performance evaluation was carried out using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC analysis. The comparative results mention the strengths and trade-offs of each and every model, providing insights for selecting suitable algorithms in speech-based stress detection applications, and it is the optimal way.
Keywords: Acoustic features | Artificial Neural Network | Decision Tree | Machine learning | Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients | Pitch analysis | Speech processing | Stress detection | Support Vector Machine | Zero Crossing Rate

Title: USAD: Universal Speech and Audio Representation via Distillation
Abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has revolutionized audio representations, yet models often remain domain-specific, focusing on either speech or non-speech tasks. In this work, we present Universal Speech and Audio Distillation (USAD), a unified approach to audio representation learning that integrates diverse audio types - speech, sound, and music - into a single model. USAD employs efficient layer-to-layer distillation from domain-specific SSL models to train a student on a comprehensive audio dataset. USAD offers competitive performance across various benchmarks and datasets, including frame and instance-level speech processing tasks, audio tagging, and sound classification, achieving near state-of-the-art results with a single encoder on SUPERB and HEAR benchmarks.<sup>1</sup>Models: https://huggingface.co/MIT-SLS/USAD-Base
Keywords: knowledge distillation | self-supervised learning | speech and audio representation learning

Title: Utilizing Kolmogorov-Arnold Network in Self-Supervised Learning for Speaker Diarization
Abstract: Speaker diarization is essential in speech processing but remains difficult due to challenges like background noise, far-field audio, overlapping speech, and unknown numbers of speakers. Self-supervised learning (SSL) has recently shown strong performance in neural speaker segmentation (NSS), typically using pre-trained models with Transformer or Conformer decoders connected via a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) adapter. In this work, we enhance the WavLM-Conformer architecture by replacing the MLP with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN), which offers better approximation of multivariate functions. Our KAN-based adapter improves the integration of SSL features into downstream tasks. Experiments show that our model achieves consistent gains over existing approaches, setting new state-of-the-art results on challenging diarization benchmarks such as AMI and AISHELL-4. These results demonstrate the promise of KANs in advancing deep learning architectures for speaker diarization.
Keywords: Kolmogorov-Arnold network | self-supervised learning | speaker diarization

Title: Long-Form Fuzzy Speech-to-Text Alignment for 1000+ Languages
Abstract: Conventional speech-to-text forced alignment typically operates at the utterance level. In practice, however, we do not usually have short segments (e.g., 10 seconds) of audio with exact, verbatim transcriptions (e.g., the LibriSpeech corpus) as in lab conditions. Instead, audio often comes in long-form (e.g., an hour-long lecture recording), and the available transcription may be non-verbatim or include unspoken annotations, making it misaligned with the actual speech. This motivates the need for long-form fuzzy speech-to-text alignment, which has practical applications - for example, preparing segmented supervised audio data for training machine learning models. We demonstrate the Torchaudio long-form aligner, which supports such use cases. Moreover, it can be equipped with any CTC model that predicts frame-wise labels, turning the model into a robust and powerful aligner.
Keywords: CTC | forced alignment | fuzzy | longform | multi-lingual | speech-to-text

Title: Task Assignment AI Assistant: Enhancing Administrative Staff and Fieldworker Efficiency with Reasoning LLMs and Speech Interaction
Abstract: Fieldworkers and administrative staff in grid maintenance face inefficiencies when retrieving task-related information, relying on manual searches through PDFs and databases. This paper presents a Task Assignment AI Assistant that streamlines information access via text and speech interaction. Using Text-to-SQL and a vector database, the assistant delivers factually accurate, context-aware responses while leveraging iterative reasoning for multi-step queries. To enhance accessibility, the solution supports multimodal inputs, integrating Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) models. The ASR model, fine-tuned on IMDA's National Speech Corpus (NSC), improves comprehension of Singlish and local accents, achieving a 3 times reduction in word error rate (WER) compared to the base model. Designed for on-premises deployment, it runs efficiently using Small Language Models (SLMs), improving inference speed by 6 times compared to using a 4-bit quantised LLM, enabling the entire solution to run on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. This enhances real-time usability while maintaining comparable performance.
Keywords: AI Assistant | Small Language Models (SLMs) | Speech Recognition | Text-to-SQL | Vector Databases

Title: SENSE models: An open source solution for multilingual and multimodal semantic-based tasks
Abstract: This paper introduces SENSE (Shared Embedding for Nlingual Speech and tExt), an open-source solution inspired by the SAMUXLSR framework and conceptually similar to Meta AI's SONAR models. These approaches rely on a teacher-student framework to align a self-supervised speech encoder with the language-agnostic continuous representations of a text encoder at the utterance level. We describe how the original SAMU-XLSR method has been updated by selecting a stronger teacher text model and a better initial speech encoder. The source code for training and using SENSE models has been integrated into the SpeechBrain toolkit, and the first SENSE model we trained has been publicly released. We report experimental results on multilingual and multimodal semantic tasks, where our SENSE model achieves highly competitive performance. Finally, this study offers new insights into how semantics are captured in such semantically aligned speech encoders.
Keywords: multilingual speech encoder | multimodal information retrieval | semantic representation | speech translation

Title: Enhanced Voice Pathology Classification Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
Abstract: Early identification is crucial for successful treatment of voice disorders since they can have a substantial impact on communication and general quality of life. This study investigates the use of Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) methods to categorize speech recordings as either problematic or healthy. Key acoustic properties are extracted from a collection of WAV audio recordings and used to train different machine learning and deep learning models. Advanced DL architectures like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are used in conjunction with more conventional ML methods like Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Random Forest (RF). To ascertain how well these models detect irregularities in voice, their performance is systematically assessed using important measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. In order to shed light on the advantages and disadvantages of each strategy, the study compares them, offering insights into the best methods for classifying voice pathologies. DL algorithms learn intricate patterns straight from unprocessed audio data, potentially providing greater accuracy and resilience than ML models, which use feature engineering for categorization. In order to improve early diagnosis and discover the best classification algorithms, this research adds to the expanding field of automated voice disorder detection. The results provide useful direction for the creation of sophisticated diagnostic instruments in clinical settings, which could help medical practitioners evaluate voice health more quickly. For better results in practical applications, future research might concentrate on improving model generalization, extending datasets, and honing feature extraction methods.
Keywords: acoustic analysis | classification | CNN | deep learning | feature extraction | machine learning | SVM | Voice disorders

Title: Hybrid Solar/Diesel Central Heating Experimental Investigation and Control
Abstract: The traditional design of conventional central heating systems typically involves a circulating pump operating at a fixed speed and does not account for ambient variables, hourly/daily changes. On the other hand, Hybrid Solar/Diesel systems that use a preheating process via solar collectors or vacuum tubes also employ similar fixed-flow circulating pumps. This research investigates improvements to hybrid central heating techniques that preheat the inlet fluid to the boiler system using renewable energy sources, such as solar energy. A complete experimental setup of a Hybrid Solar/Diesel system was designed and installed on the Mechanical Engineering rooftop at the University of Jordan. The system includes state-of-the-art Internet of Things instruments capable of accurately measuring the diversity of the required system's process and environmental variables. The research work findings indicated that the tested Hybrid Solar/Diesel performance and efficiencies were strongly correlated with changes in ambient environmental conditions and the system's flow rate for both the Solar and boiler pump loops. When an online closed-loop PLC controller is incorporated to regulate the circulating pumps' speed, accounting for changes in ambient conditions, component degradation, and aging, the system operates in the best performance region. Furthermore, using an AI-based controller and optimizer enables better optimization and operation of the Hybrid Solar/Diesel system.
Keywords: Central Heating | Control | Hybrid Heating Systems | Optimization | Renewable Energy | Solar Energy

Title: PURE Codec: Progressive Unfolding of Residual Entropy for Speech Codec Learning
Abstract: Neural speech codecs have achieved strong performance in low-bitrate compression, but residual vector quantization (RVQ) often suffers from unstable training and ineffective decomposition, limiting reconstruction quality and efficiency. We propose PURE Codec (Progressive Unfolding of Residual Entropy), a novel framework that guides multi-stage quantization using a pre-trained speech enhancement model. The first quantization stage reconstructs low-entropy, denoised speech embeddings, while subsequent stages encode residual high-entropy components. This design improves training stability significantly. Experiments demonstrate that PURE consistently outperforms conventional RVQ-based codecs in reconstruction and downstream speech language model-based text-to-speech, particularly under noisy training conditions.
Keywords: Entropy Decomposition | Neural Speech Codec | Residual Vector Quantization | Speech Enhancement

Title: A Self-Refining Framework for Enhancing ASR Using TTS-Synthesized Data
Abstract: We propose a self-refining framework that enhances ASR performance with only unlabeled datasets. The process starts with an existing ASR model generating pseudo-labels on unannotated speech, which are then used to train a highfidelity text-to-speech (TTS) system. Then, synthesized speech text pairs are bootstrapped into the original ASR system, completing the closed-loop self-improvement cycle. We demonstrated the effectiveness of the framework on Taiwanese-Mandarin speech. Leveraging 6,000 hours of unlabeled speech, a moderate amount of text data, and synthetic content from the AI models, we adapt Whisper-large-v2 into a specialized model, Twister. Twister reduces error rates by up to 20 % on Mandarin and 50 % on Mandarin-English code-switching benchmarks compared to Whisper. Results highlight the framework as a compelling alternative to pseudo-labeling self-distillation approaches and provides a practical pathway for improving ASR performance in lowresource or domain-specific settings.
Keywords: Automatic Speech Recognition | Code-Switching | Pseudo Labeling | Self-Refining | Text-to-Speech | Whisper

Title: MoLEx: Mixture of LoRA Experts in Speech Self-Supervised Models for Audio Deepfake Detection
Abstract: While self-supervised learning (SSL)-based models have boosted audio deepfake detection accuracy, fully finetuning them is computationally expensive. To address this, we propose a parameter-efficient framework that combines Low-Rank Adaptation with a Mixture-of-Experts router, called Mixture of LoRA Experts (MoLEx). It preserves pre-trained knowledge of SSL models while efficiently finetuning only selected experts, reducing training costs while maintaining robust performance. The observed utility of experts during inference shows the router reactivates the same experts for similar attacks but switches to other experts for novel spoofs, confirming MoLEx's domainaware adaptability. MoLEx additionally offers flexibility for domain adaptation by allowing extra experts to be trained without modifying the entire model. We mainly evaluate our approach on the ASVSpoof 5 dataset and achieve the state-of-the-art (SOTA) equal error rate (EER) of 5.56% on the evaluation set without augmentation.
Keywords: Deepfake detection | LoRA | MOE | MoLEx | SSL model

Title: Machine Learning Framework for Audio-Based Equipment Condition Monitoring: A Comparative Study of Classification Algorithms
Abstract: Audio-based equipment condition monitoring suffers from a lack of standardized methodologies for algorithm selection, hindering reproducible research. This paper addresses this gap by introducing a comprehensive framework for the systematic and statistically rigorous evaluation of machine learning models. Leveraging a rich 127-feature set across time, frequency, and time-frequency domains, our methodology is validated on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Results demonstrate that an ensemble method achieves superior performance (94.2% accuracy, 0.942 F1-score), with statistical testing confirming its significant outperformance of individual algorithms by 8-15%. Ultimately, this work provides a validated benchmarking protocol and practical guidelines for selecting robust monitoring solutions in industrial settings.
Keywords: algorithm comparison | audio signal processing | condition monitoring | ensemble methods | fault detection | feature engineering | machine learning

Title: PrediscanNetV2: Early Risk Classification of Coronary Artery Disease via Gated Cross-Attention on Retinal Fundus Images
Abstract: Preventive medicine presently faces challenges in identifying the risk of Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) prior to the occurrence of symptoms. We employ PrediscanNetV2, a method that simply uses basic demographic data and non-invasive fundus photography to estimate Carotid Intima-Media Thickness (CIMT), which is an important sign of atherosclerosis. Most current approaches just integrate tabular and visual information. Our method is different because it uses a Gated Cross-Attention mechanism on top of a Siamese EfficientNet-B3 backbone. This architecture makes it possible to change the weights of visual features based on the patient's age and gender, which is a good way to simulate a clinical setting. We examined the model with the China-Fundus-CIMT dataset (n=2,903) using a strict 5-fold cross-validation procedure. The results showed that the average accuracy was 84.52% and the Area Under the Curve (AUC) was 0.9104. PrediscanNetV2 demonstrates its efficacy as an automated, scalable instrument for assessing cardiovascular risk by statistically surpassing conventional performance benchmarks.
Keywords: CIMT | Coronary Artery Disease | Deep Learning | Gated Cross-Attention | Mul-timodal Fusion | Retinal Fundus Images

Title: Skin Cancer Detection and Classification Using Dermoscopic Imaging with Deep Learning Analysis
Abstract: Early detection and correct classification are the most effective methods for improving patient outcomes in cutaneous cancers such as melanoma. This study introduces a deep learning system capable of autonomously analysing dermoscopy images. It integrates cutting-edge Deep Learning (DL) architectures with comprehensive data pre-processing and augmentation methods. We assembled a curated dataset from public sources including high-resolution dermoscopy images of Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) and benign melanomas. Colour normalisation was used to standardise the photos. To improve the model's generalisability, it was augmented by rotation, flipping, and intensity shifting. This work used stratified five-fold cross-validation to evaluate three fine-tuned deep learning models: VGG19, DenseNet-121, and MobileNet. The MobileNet model achieved a total accuracy of 0.994, surpassing its competitors to detect healthy and abnormal tissues. This strategy far surpasses typical machine-learning techniques. The results indicate that DL-enhanced dermoscopic analysis may assist dermatologists in skin cancer screening. The technique has promise as a decision-support instrument in clinical processes.
Keywords: Classification | Deep Learning | Dermoscopic Imaging | feature extraction | Performance Metrics | Skin Cancer | Technology transfer

Title: A Multi-Modal AI Framework for Real-Time Stress and Sleep Monitoring with Intelligent Interventions
Abstract: Growing instances of stress and sleep disorders in both students and remote workers demand smart and user-friendly mental health tools. This article suggests creating an AI-driven solution that will implement speech analysis, recognition of emotional facial expressions, and behavior patterns to determine the level of stress and propose proper interventions. The assistant uses Whisper in speech-to-text transcription, Deep Face in facial expression recognition, as well as TextBlob in determining the polarity of sentiments. When the stress is high, the system provides real-time warnings based on the Twilio SMS and plays some soothing music or message based on text-to-speech and Pygame. It also shows the long-term stress trend visualization at matplotlib on a Streamlit application. Neither cloud-based heavy APIs nor extensive hardware is required to use the tool that runs in real-time and uses only a microphone and webcam. The simulations of using the system experimentally reveal that it can respond to indicators of stress timely manner and without compromising the privacy of the user. The given solution is inexpensive, scalable, and efficient regarding the promotion of sleep hygiene and psychological well-being.
Keywords: AI mental health assistant | DeepFace | emotion recognition | sentiment analysis | sleep monitoring | Streamlit | Stress detection | TextBlob | TTS | Twilio | visualization | Whisper

Title: VaaniVerse: Low-Latency Speech Translation Using Universal Earphones
Abstract: In multilingual societies like India, language barriers are a major obstacle to effective communication. Due to their reliance on internet connectivity, high cost, poor performance in noisy environments and high latency, existing solutions frequently fail. This paper introduces VaaniVerse, a real-time, multilingual speech translation system with low latency that can be operated with smartphones and standard earphones. The system also integrates an efficient pipeline for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis noise cancellation and context-free translation. VaaniVerse provides accurate and adaptable translations between Hindi, English and Kannada even in noisy environment using lightweight edge AI models like Whisper, Coqui TTS and IndicTrans2. Given that the architecture is optimized for offline use, accessibility and affordability are ensured. The system also futher incorporates several GUI-based novelties that enhances usability and distinguishes it from existing translation applications.
Keywords: Coqui TTS | IndicTrans2 | Low Latency | Speech Translation | Voice Isolation | Whisper

Title: MFCC-Based Multilingual Speech Processing for Depression Classification
Abstract: A relatively underexplored research direction in depression detection involves the utilization of multilingual speech data for model development. Advancing multilingual audio-based depression detection systems is increasingly essential, as such approaches can enhance model robustness, improve cross-linguistic generalizability, and support more equitable mental-health assessment technologies on a global scale. This study conducts a comparative analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) with varying dimensionalities specifically 13, 20, 30, and 40 coefficients in distinguishing depressive and non-depressive speech using two multilingual audio datasets: MODMA and DAIC-WOZ. The extracted MFCC features were used to train three deep learning architectures: LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU. The experimental results show that MFCC-40 consistently achieves the highest performance across models, obtaining an average accuracy of 82.23%, outperforming the lowercoefficient MFCC configurations. Furthermore, among the models trained with MFCC-40, the Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) demonstrates superior classification capability, achieving an average accuracy of 86%. These findings highlight that the combination of MFCC-40 and the BiLSTM architecture provides the most effective framework for multilingual depression detection based on speech.
Keywords: Depression Detection | MFCC | Speech

Title: Transfer Learning Based Deep Learning Framework For Multiclass Brain Tumor Classification
Abstract: Brain tumors are detrimental to health as they generate uncontrolled cellular proliferation. This can disrupt critical cognitive functioning and lead to significant problems, particularly in adults. Early and accurate detection of brain tumors (BT) is crucial as it enhances treatment efficacy and prolongs patient survival. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) remains the superior method for detecting BT, as it provides superior visualization of soft tissue compared to other imaging modalities. However, manually sorting and analyzing MRI data is time consuming and labor-intensive, and varying interpretations may arise among various individuals. Deep learning (DL) has advanced significantly recently particularly via transfer learning (TL). This demonstrates that deep learning may be significantly beneficial for automating complex tasks in medical imaging. This research presents a TL-based framework for the categorization of BTC utilizing pre-trained convolutional neural networks. Following extensive pre-processing, including cropping of the region of interest, enhancement and augmentation, we evaluate the performance of EfficientNetB4 and MobileNetV2 on MRI data. We evaluated EfficientNetB4 and MobileNetV2 on an accessible Kaggle MRI dataset. EfficientNetB4 has a training accuracy of 97.51% and a test accuracy of 98.56%. MobileNetV2 achieved an accuracy of 99.79% during training and 96.67% during testing. These findings indicate that advanced TL structures can enhance our ability to classify brain cancers. This enhances the efficacy and reliability of diagnostic instruments in practical situations.
Keywords: Brain Tumor | CNN | Deep Learning | MRI | Transfer Learning

Title: Integrating Physiological Signals into Music Machine Learning: An HRV-Based Framework
Abstract: Music is widely being recognized as a non-pharmacological intervention for anxiety, yet its physiological mechanisms remain unexplored. This study examines the effect of Kaapi raga (a south Indian classical music) and weightless ambient music on cardiovascular regulation and anxiety reduction using heart rate variability (HRV) and mean arterial pressure (MAP). Twenty participants with high anxiety (HAM-A >25) completed a protocol involving rest, music listening, and attention tasks while ECG and MAP were continuously recorded.HRV features were extracted across time, frequency, and nonlinear domains and analysed using machine learning classifiers. Random Forest and XGBoost achieved the highest performance (70.8% accuracy; AUC up to 0.89), outperforming linear models. Feature ablation revealed non-linear SD2, pNN50, HR mean, and high-frequency power percentage as key predictors of music-induced physiological changes.The findings here demonstrate that ensemble machine learning methods can robustly model music's impact on anxiety, while domain-specific HRV features provide actionable biomarkers for developing personalized, evidence-based music therapy interventions.
Keywords: Feature Ablation | Heart Rate Variability | Machine learning | Music

Title: Detection of Parkinson's Disease by Analysis of Vocal Signals Using Genetic Algorithm & KNN Classifier
Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) represents a slowly advancing neurological disorder often associated with aging. Its progression results in significant motor impairments and a marked decline in daily functioning. Since conventional diagnosis mainly depends on identifying motor abnormalities that arise at later stages, early recognition remains a challenge. To mitigate this, a hybrid diagnostic strategy combining Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based feature refinement and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) classification is presented. The GA process also aids in the selection of important acoustic features and the tuning of the neighborhood parameter of KNN to reduce data dimensions and increase model efficiency. Experimental testing using a freely available Parkinson's speech dataset revealed that the performance of the GA-KNN model surpassed that of the standard classifiers SVM, ANN, and individual KNN with 94.56% mean cross-validation accuracy and 96.61% test accuracy.
Keywords: biomedical voice signals | computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) | feature selection | Genetic Algorithm (GA) | K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) | machine learning | Parkinson's disease

Title: Time-Frequency Conformer and Kalman Filter-Based Speech Enhancement Method
Abstract: The performance of Kalman filters (KF) in speech enhancement is highly dependent on the estimation accuracy of linear predictive coefficients (LPCs). To address the significant estimation bias of LPCs in complex noisy environments, this paper proposes a time-frequency dual-domain Conformer-based Kalman filter speech enhancement method - CAKFNet. The model adopts an encoder-decoder architecture: during the encoding phase, a Dilated DenseNet module is introduced to exponentially expand the receptive field and enhance local feature continuity, thereby achieving multi-scale feature aggregation. Subsequently, dual Conformer modules in both time and frequency domains jointly model the long-term dependencies of speech signals and local convolutional features, fully capturing spatio-temporal correlations. The decoding stage employs a decoupled dual-branch architecture to separately regress the LPC power spectrum (LPC-PS) of clean speech and noise. Building upon this, an autocorrelation matrix is generated via inverse Fourier transform. The Levinson-Durbin recursive algorithm is then employed to compute the clean speech and noise LPC coefficients required for the Augmented Kalman Filter (AKF), along with their prediction error variance, ultimately achieving speech enhancement. The proposed method undergoes systematic experimental evaluation on the publicly available VoiceBank + DEMAND dataset. Results demonstrate that CAKFNet effectively reduces spectral distortion in LPC estimation. Objective metrics, including PESQ and STOI, show significant improvements over baseline methods, while subjective listening tests confirm substantial enhancements in speech quality and intelligibility.
Keywords: Conformer | Deep learning | Kalman filter | Speech enhancement

Title: PatchTST-based Safety Variables Prediction for Severe Accident Progression in Nuclear Power Plants
Abstract: Severe accidents in nuclear power plants progress in complex and non-linear ways, making it difficult for operators to make quick and accurate situational assessment. To support proactive operator decision-making, this study constructed a deep learning model to predict the future behavior of safety variables in multi-steps during a severe accident. Based on the patch time series Transformer model, which shows high performance in time-series prediction, various severe accident scenario data generated by the modular accident analysis program simulation code were used for training. To improve the model's performance and robustness, a complex noise injection technique simulating instrument uncertainty was applied. Furthermore, the prediction uncertainty was quantified using Monte Carlo dropout. Performance evaluation results showed that the proposed model effectively predicted the dynamic behavior of the safety variables. In particular, the model trained with injected noise showed significantly superior robustness on noisy test data compared to the model trained on clean data, suggesting high applicability in real operational environments. In conclusion, the prediction framework proposed in this study confirmed its potential to be utilized as part of an operator support system that provides reliable future information as a decision support tool for operators during a severe accident.
Keywords: nuclear power plants | PatchTST | prediction | severe accident | uncertainty

Title: Integrating Generative AI into Challenge-Based Learning: A Case Study in Preventive Medicine and Public Health Education
Abstract: This study explores the integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into a challenge-based learning (CBL) course on preventive medicine and public health for first-year health students. Implemented at Tecnologico de Monterrey, the course aimed to enhance students' ability to design community based strategies for preventing non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Starting in 2024, students used AI tools to generate and refine proposals aligned with national health guidelines. Academic performance data from 2021 to 2025 showed stable overall grades, but there was a notable improvement in the quality of AI-assisted preventive proposals. Additionally, student motivation-measured using the MUSIC model-was higher in 2025, particularly in terms of empowerment and perceived success. These findings suggest that AI can enhance engagement and support the development of critical and digital skills in health education. Further research is needed to assess long-term impacts and guide the ethical and effective integration of AI in medical training.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Educational innovation | Higher education | Medical Education

Title: The Artificial Intelligence Perception and Literacy Among University Students in the Philippines
Abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, work and everyday life underscores the importance of equipping students with necessary competencies to navigate AI driven environments. This study explored the Artificial Intelligence (AI) literacy level among tertiary students in the Philippines using multidimensional approach that combined demographic data focusing on gender, researcher developed questions on AI platform awareness and five standardized instruments (AI Frequency Use Scale, Two-Dimensional Paradox Scale, AI Performance Perception Scale, AI Risk Perception Scale and AI literacy scale). Data were collected online and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Mann-Whitney U Test.
Keywords: AI | AI Literacy | AI Misinformation | AI Perception | Student Perception

Title: Combination of Traditional Teaching and AI-Guided Self-Directed Learning on Theoretical Learning and Academic Performance in High-Workload Immunobiology Courses
Abstract: This study examined the impact of integrating an AI-guided self-directed learning tool (MagicSchool) into the theoretical module of a high-workload immunobiology course. Academic performance in 2025 was compared with that in 2023 and 2024, and student motivation was assessed using the MUSIC Model of Academic Motivation Inventory. The AI-assisted group achieved higher theoretical module and exam scores than the previous scholar periods (p < 0.0001) and higher final course grades by 2024 (p = 0.0238). The motivation scores were high for usefulness, success, caring, and empowerment, although interest was low, suggesting the need for various learning strategies. These findings indicate that AI can complement traditional teaching to improve performance and support motivation; however, sustaining curiosity requires diverse and interactive methods.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence tool | Educational Innovation | Innovative Learning Strategies | Self-management of knowledge

Title: Swara-Net: A Deep Learning Baseline and Curated Dataset for Five Under-Represented Carnatic Ragas
Abstract: This paper addresses a critical gap in computational musicology: the lack of robust datasets and baselines for specific, under-represented Carnatic ragas. We introduce a new, manually-curated dataset of 638 audio snippets for five prominent ragas: Shankarabharanam, Revathi, Abheri, Brindavanasaranga, and Mayamalavagowla. This collection, sourced from public recordings, is designed to be timbrally diverse. To establish a strong performance benchmark, we compare a standard Support Vector Machine (SVM) against a 3-layer Deep Neural Network (DNN). The results are striking: the SVM achieves only 57.03% accuracy, while our proposed DNN (Swara-Net) achieves 99.0% accuracy. This demonstrates the superior ability of deep learning to navigate the complex, high-dimensional feature space of raga. We further provide a musicological analysis of the model's single misclassification. This work contributes both a valuable, open-source dataset and a reproducible, high-performance baseline, paving the way for more nuanced research on these specific ragas.
Keywords: audio processing | dataset | deep neural networks | Indian classical music | machine learning | Raga classification

Title: Executional Error Detection in Robotic Surgery using a Hybrid Dual Pathway Architecture
Abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery, enabled by systems like the da Vinci Surgical System, enhances minimally invasive procedures through high-definition 3D visualization and precise instrument control. However, executional errors, such as improper needle orientation or loss of instrument visibility, pose significant risks to patient safety. This paper proposes a novel deep learning framework for detecting executional errors in surgical videos using the JHU-ISI Gesture and Skill Assessment Working Set (JIGSAWS) dataset, focusing on suturing and needle-passing tasks. The model integrates a ResNet-50 backbone for spatial feature extraction with a temporal modeling pipeline comprising 1D Convolutional Neural Networks (1D CNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), and self-attention mechanisms. A dualpathway architecture, combining gesture-aware and gesture-agnostic branches, employs dynamic fusion to adapt predictions based on contextual reliability. Evaluated through Group K-Fold cross-validation, the model achieves robust performance with metrics including F1-score (87.2%), Jaccard index (77.2%), accuracy (87.4%), AUC (89.6%), and recall (87.0%). These results highlight its potential for real-time surgical feedback, skill assessment, and enhanced training systems, advancing safer surgical practices.
Keywords: attention mechanisms | deep learning | executional error detection | Robotic surgery | surgical skill assessment | video signal processing

Title: The pedagogical potential of using neural networks in the field of professional music education
Abstract: Introduction. Artificial intelligence is actively used in various spheres of life, including education. Recently, it has begun to be used in music education. This area is of interest, as it helps to improve the learning process and make it more accessible. It is necessary to ensure that these methods really help students and make the learning process more effective. The aim of this study: to conduct a systematic review of scientific papers that examine the pedagogical potential of artificial intelligence (neural networks) in the field of professional music education, implemented at the level of higher or secondary vocational education. Materials and methods. To achieve the stated objective of the study, a systematic literature review method was used. This review was carried out in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 protocol. The study used the Web of Science (WoS), Scopus, and Russian Science Citation Index (RSCI) databases. The final sample size was 31 publications (n = 31). Results. An increase in research interest in this issue has been established since 2022. The greatest activity of Chinese scientists has been revealed. Disproportions have been found between theoretical (19.4%) and empirical (80.6%) works. Six roles of using neural networks in music education have been identified: intelligent learning (48.6%), automated assessment systems (20%), blended learning (17.1%), personalized learning (8.5%), assistive technologies (2.9%), and virtual reality technologies (2.9%). The methods of teaching music (61.3%), control (54.8%), pedagogical communication with feedback (35.5%), assessment (25.8%), educational content (19.4%), and educational environment (16.1%) are most productively transferred to the field of artificial intelligence. The effects of using neural networks in music education include an increase in the quality of education (87%), academic performance (71%), the quality of musical performance in general (38.7%) or individual performance skills, such as musical expressiveness (19.3%), artistic literacy (6.4%), involvement in the educational process, and motivation for students to learn (45.2%). Conclusions. Analysis of the practices of using neural networks in music education shows a deep gap between technological solutions and understanding of the pedagogical potential of these practices. Prospects for further research on this topic can contribute to the formation of digital didactics of music education.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | deep learning | higher education | machine learning | music education | neural network | secondary vocational education | высшее образование | глубокое обучение | искусственный интеллект | машинное обучение | музыкальное образование | нейронная сеть | среднее профессиональное образование

Title: Optimization of Temporal Convolutional Networks Using Harris Hawks Algorithm for Efficient Embedded Speech Recognition
Abstract: Recent advances in embedded speech recognition require models that balance accuracy, efficiency, and low resource consumption. This paper presents a novel approach using Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) optimized by Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) to enhance speech recognition performance on Raspberry Pi devices. The HHO algorithm dynamically tunes key hyperparameters of the TCN models such as convolutional filter sizes, dilation rates, and learning rates - in order to achieve high accuracy while reducing computational overhead. Experiments on benchmark speech datasets demonstrate that the proposed HHO-optimized TCN achieves higher recognition accuracy and faster inference compared to baseline models (e.g., standard LSTM, GRU). The work illustrates the potential of combining bio-inspired optimization with efficient convolutional sequence models to enable real-time speech recognition on resource-constrained edge devices.
Keywords: Embedded AI | Harris Hawks Optimization | Hyperparameter Optimization | Raspberry Pi | Speech Recognition | Temporal Convolutional Networks

Title: Deepfake Audio Detection: Differentiating Modulated and Deepfake Audio
Abstract: The rise in deepfake audio and AI-generated speech has become a very real and serious security issue. The voices that are generated using deepfakes are becoming so realistic that it is difficult to differentiate between a real speech and a deepfake speech. Traditional detection techniques that rely only on audio features will fail in such cases. The paper introduced a hybrid approach to deepfake audio detection that combines modern deep learning with classic audio analysis. The paper uses a Wav2Vec2 embedding to capture speech features and MFCC features to highlight fine details in the sound. It shows that using Wav2Vec2 alone achieves about 81% accuracy, while adding MFCCs boosts performance to 85%, with noticeable improvements in detecting modulated speech. It demonstrates that combining deep embeddings, traditional features, and realistic data augmentations leads to a more reliable detection system.
Keywords: Audio deepfake detection | MFCC | modulated audio | Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) | speech synthesis | Wav2Vec2

Title: Biomimetic Aerodynamic Enhancements and AI Integration for Rocket Vehicle Performance
Abstract: This research investigates the synthesis of advanced aerodynamic principles, biomimetic designs, and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance the efficiency and performance of rocket vehicles. The primary objective is to advance aerodynamic performance by integrating biomimetic features such as shark skin inspired scales on the rocket’s fuselage and double sharklets on the fins. These enhancements aim to reduce aerodynamic drag, improve flight stability, and efficiently utilize turbulence-generated energy to enhance rocket performance. By replicating the texture and structure of shark skin, which includes microstructures that reduce air friction, the application of these scales on the fuselage results in smoother airflow around the rocket, leading to reduced drag and improved fuel efficiency. Additionally, double sharklets on the fins are designed to address vortex-induced drag, thereby enhancing stability and control during ascent. AI is utilized to analyze extensive aerodynamic data, aiding in the development of optimized designs and configurations that enhance the rockets’ overall performance. The AI system processes data, enabling continuous improvements and precise adjustments to design parameters during simulations and testing. The analysis revealed two distinct optimums: a mathematically precise angle of 73.12∘ based on a weighted-sum score, and a more robust, Pareto-optimal angle of 65.32∘ identified by the NSGA-II algorithm, highlighting a critical trade-off in engineering design. From an industrial engineering perspective, this research offers benefits by reducing energy consumption required for launch, thus lowering operational costs and minimizing environmental impact. Furthermore, the application of AI for design optimization shortens the development cycle and enhances the reliability of rocket vehicles, making them more commercially viable and competitive. The incorporation of biomimetic features not only improves aerodynamic efficiency but also introduces innovative methodologies for enhancing rocket performance. By drawing inspiration from natural structures such as shark skin and sharklets, this research pushes the boundaries of traditional engineering and explores new possibilities for rocket enhancements.
Keywords: Aerodynamic efficiency | Artificial intelligence (AI) | Biomimetic designs | Rocket performance

Title: Detecting Early Signs of SLDDs in Preschoolers Using Machine Learning
Abstract: Speech disorders is an important part of clinical diagnosis. Conventional methods that use separate deep learning architectures like GRU, LSTM, and BiLSTM have demonstrated good results, but they typically have trouble finding the right balance between sensitivity and specificity, which may lead to misclassifications and less resilience. architecture that can find temporal correlations while still focusing on speech qualities that are critical for diagnosis. a hybrid GRU-BiLSTM model with an Attention mechanism. This strategy makes use of GRU's capacity to learn in order, BiLSTM's ability to represent context in both directions, and the attention layer's ability to highlight important speech cues, which all help to make classification more accurate. The experimental findings on the dataset show that the suggested model does better than solo models on all assessment metrics. Confusion matrix analysis demonstrates that there are fewer wrong predictions and a more balanced classification, while ROC analysis shows that the model has better discriminative strength. Performance measurements like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score always show that the hybrid model is the best. In conclusion, the GRU-BiLSTM with Attention is a better and more reliable way to find speech disorders than other deep learning approaches.
Keywords: BiLSTM Model | GRU BiLSTM Attention Mechanism | GRU Model | Hybrid deep learning model | LSTM Model | Speech Disorder detection

Title: Optimization of DNNs Using a Hardware Aware Two Stage NAS for Automotive Embedded Targets
Abstract: Deep learning models are widely used in the context of automated driving. Achieving the goal of performance in Automotive Embedded Targets presents numerous challenges due to the trade-off between accuracy and run-time. This paper addresses the task of finding the best candidate that fulfills System-on-Chip (SoCs) constraints using two-stage neural architecture search. We employed this approach to find a balance between accuracy and run-time. Our method can be applied in the context of optimizing deep learning models. Starting from a search space and a neural network, we can automatically create a super-model (by replacing all layers specified in the search space) that can be trained in the first stage of NAS. In the second stage, we use the already trained model to subsample architectures to find the best trade-off between accuracy KPIs and runtime KPIs. These two metrics are not arbitrary; they define the main constraints of SoCs and were used in the construction of the Pareto front from which the users can choose a configuration that satisfies their expectations. We conducted multiple experiments, but the most important ones are: optimizing a YOLOv8s for Texas Instruments (TI) SoC with 8 TOPS per Neural Network Accelerator and a multitask network for RENESAS SoC that has 3.4 TOPS. We ran YOLOv8s experiments on a public COCO dataset and managed to find a neural network that runs approximately 16% faster on TI, with a drop of less than 1.1% in mAP. For the Multitask Network, we conducted experiments on a custom dataset and found a neural network that runs 13% slower on RENESAS, but with an increase of 0.4% in overall evaluation metrics.
Keywords: AutoML | DNN-Deep Neural Network | Multitask Network | NAS-Neural Architecture Search | Neural Network Optimization | Run-Time Prediction

Title: Rootalyx: Stealthy Dynamic Analysis for Linux Malware using Kernel-Level Instrumentation and a Hybrid LSTM-Transformer Model
Abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a stealthy dynamic analysis environment for Linux, named Rootalyx. The system addresses the challenge of evasive malware that can detect and circumvent traditional monitoring tools. Its core component is a kernel module that uses the ftrace subsystem to instrument system calls, integrated with rootkit-inspired hiding techniques to ensure a covert operational profile. The collected behavioral data, including system call arguments, is processed by a hierarchical hybrid model combining the LSTM and Transformer architectures for automated malware classification. Experimental results show that the proposed system introduces lower performance overhead compared to traditional tools for monitoring like strace and successfully evades detection by common security scanners. The machine learning model achieves a classification accuracy of 80.34% on the extracted data, validating the viability of kernel-level stealth monitoring for robust malware analysis.
Keywords: dynamic analysis | kernel module | Linux | lkm | LSTM | machine learning | malware detection | rootkit | Transformer

Title: A TabNet-Based Deep Learning Framework for Predicting Uric Acid Elevation and Kidney Health Risks
Abstract: The rising popularity of high-protein diets, while advantageous in some situations, has been increasingly linked to heightened uric acid levels and renal impairment. These illnesses often go untreated until significant consequences develop, highlighting the need for predictive and preventive healthcare instruments. This paper introduces a TabNet-based deep learning framework for the early identification of hyperuricemia and renal health issues using structured health data. The model utilizes the NHANES dataset, a comprehensive repository of publicly accessible data including biochemical markers, nutritional consumption, demographic characteristics, and comorbidity indicators. Proposed Model Works in 3 stages. Initially, data preparation includes the cleansing, imputation, and modification of pertinent parameters like blood uric acid, creatinine, BUN, protein intake levels, age, and BMI. Secondly, the TabNet architecture is trained, which uses attentive feature selection to comprehend intricate, non-linear interactions while maintaining model interpretability. In the third phase, the model is assessed and contrasted with leading classifiers such as XGBoost, Random Forest, and MLP, while feature significance is shown using TabNet's attention masks. The suggested model had an accuracy of 94.2%, exceeding baseline techniques across all principal performance criteria. Findings indicate that consumption of animal protein, salt, inadequate hydration, and compromised filtration are significant factors in increased uric acid levels. This approach exhibits exceptional prediction accuracy and provides valuable insights for personalized dietary planning. Our technique has potential in enhancing AI-driven preventive healthcare and facilitating scalable, personalized dietary risk assessment systems.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Explainable AI | Kidney Health | NHANES Dataset | TabNet | Uric Acid Prediction

Title: Faint Satellite Streak Detection Using the Raw Output of a YOLO-type Object Detector
Abstract: Space surveillance using optical instruments involves detecting faint streaks from long exposure images. As the space object moves, it creates a line segment trajectory in the image space, against the fixed star background. Clouds, light pollution, or the weak illumination of the object by the Sun may lead to a very small signal to noise ratio. The YOLO family of neural networks is a lightweight solution for detecting various objects from images. Starting from existing streak detection solutions, we have iteratively generated training datasets by a combination of manual and automatic annotation and augmentation. The bounding box output of the neural network detector must be further processed to detect the satellite streak's line segment. The unfiltered output of the neural network, containing multiple overlapping boxes, can be used to indicate the position of the line, without any additional processing cost. The complete processing pipeline can detect faint streaks from any type of input image, with real time performance.
Keywords: computer vision | deep learning | satellite detection | satellite tracking

Title: Seismometers Fault Identification based on Time-series Ambient Noise Analysis using CatBoost Classification
Abstract: Ensuring seismograph reliability is crucial for generating high-quality earthquake parameters. However, early detection of instrument degradation remains a challenge in large seismic networks. This study introduces an automated fault diagnostic that leverages statistical time series features and machine learning classification to identify seismometer malfunctions using background noise recordings from the 2020-2025 Indonesian Tsunami Early Warning System (Ina-TEWS) network. Seismic recordings were preprocessed, segmented into hourly windows, and converted into representative statistical metrics, including availability, Root Mean Square (RMS), median, mode, number of amplitudes, slope, and unique values. These features are labeled according to the seismometer's health status, including normal status and various types of instrument malfunctions. The resulting dataset is then used to train and evaluate a classification algorithm.
