We propose Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) as the primary classifier, with its performance benchmarked against Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). The boosting model consistently produces near-perfect confusion matrices with strong generalization validated through learning curve analysis. CatBoost achieves perfect accuracy (1.00) for normal-abnormal classification and 0.999 accuracy for multi-fault detection. These results confirm that simple statistical features can effectively convert seismometer fault characteristic patterns and that the CatBoost machine learning model is a reliable and scalable solution for automated seismometer fault identification. This framework provides a practical path towards predictive maintenance and data quality improvement for real-time earthquake monitoring.
Keywords: and fault classification | CatBoost | fault detection | machine learning | Seismometer

Title: Research on Fault Detection Method of Airborne Electronic Equipment based on Deep Learning
Abstract: Driven by advancements in deep learning, significant breakthroughs have been achieved in the field of electronic product hardware detection, with related technologies successfully applied to identify functional circuits and component failures in electronic modules. However, existing hardware detection algorithms predominantly rely on general datasets where targets occupy a large proportion in images, leading to suboptimal performance when directly applied to small object detection tasks. To address this, the paper proposes an airborne electronic device fault detection method specifically designed for small targets. It employs pruning techniques, weight clustering, and Huffman coding to implement lightweight design for deep neural networks, thereby reducing network scale and parameter quantity while achieving higher computational efficiency under limited resources. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits notable advantages in identifying functional circuits and critical components within electronic hardware images, effectively meeting the demands for rapid fault detection and localization of airborne electronic components.
Keywords: airborne electronic equipment | deep learning | fault detection | object detection | PVANet

Title: Prostate Cancer Detection Using Deep Learning with Clinical-Structural Data Integration in an EfficientNetV2B3 Framework
Abstract: Prostate cancer continues to be a cause of cancer-related deaths among men and the creation of better diagnostic instruments is needed in this case. This paper lays out a deep learning model called EfficientNetV2B3 architecture to fuse clinical and structural patient data and improve the prediction of prostate cancer. The degree of training and validation occurred in a labeled dataset by placing clinical variables and structural imaging features into the model. Confusion matrix analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and loss/accuracy tracking of 50 epoch were used to measure the performance of the model. The outcomes indicated that the overall ROC AUC was 0.92 with great discriminatory capacity between malignant and benign. The confusion matrix showed accurate prediction of 8 benign and 4 malignant cases with 8 malignant cases being predicted as benign and 0 benign cases as malignant. During the course of training validation accuracy was always above 70 percent and reached well above 90 percent during training. The results make EfficientNetV2B3 promising as deep learning to use multimodal data in prostate cancer diagnostics.
Keywords: Clinical data integration | Deep Learning | Diagnostic accuracy | EfficientNetV2B3 | Prostate cancer detection

Title: Data Processing Algorithm for Bridge Structure Health Monitoring Based on Deep Learning
Abstract: In view of the problem that traditional methods in bridge structure health monitoring are difficult to balance multi-scale damage identification and anti-noise performance, this paper proposes an adaptive multi-scale attention fusion convolutional recurrent network (AMSACRN) algorithm. The algorithm innovatively constructs a three-level collaborative architecture: the adaptive multi-scale feature extraction module captures damage features of different sizes through dynamic weight adjustment, the attention fusion module strengthens key features and suppresses noise, the convolutional recurrent module deeply models the spatiotemporal correlation of data. The experiment uses 86,400 sets of measured data and 16,000 sets of simulation data (including 32 damage conditions) of a cable-stayed bridge, divides the data set into 7: 2: 1, and compares 5 representative algorithms. The results show that the damage identification accuracy of AMSACRN is 98.5%, the precision is 98.2%, the recall is 98.7%, and the F1 score is 98.4%, which are 6.2, 6.4, 6.0, and 6.3 percentage points higher than CNN-LSTM respectively, the RMSE of vibration displacement prediction is 0.023mm, and the MAE is 0. 018 mm, which is more than 30% better than the comparison algorithm, the accuracy is still 94.2% under 10 dB noise, and the performance degradation is only 4.3%. The algorithm has a single sample processing time of 42 ms, which meets the real-time monitoring needs. The research provides a high-precision and strong robust intelligent data processing solution for bridge health monitoring.
Keywords: Attention Mechanism | Bridge Health Monitoring | Damage Identification | Data Processing Algorithm | Deep Learning | Multi-Scale Feature Fusion

Title: Effect of Anxiety Reduction Interventions on Exam Anxiety for Engineering Students Using Physiological Signals
Abstract: Acute test anxiety negatively affects both academic performance and mental well-being in engineering students. Although earlier studies have examined the long-term impact of culturally relevant methods like breathing techniques and Indian classical music, they mostly rely on self-reports, lack real-time physiological data, and seldom offer direct quantitative comparisons. This research investigates the short-term efficacy of guided deep breathing and Indian classical music Raga Bhairavi using wearable biosensors, statistical analysis, and machine learning. The paper randomly assigns sixty undergraduate engineering students with moderate to high anxiety to intervention and control groups. The research measures Galvanic Skin Response (GSR) and Heart Rate Variability (HRV) during the Montreal Imaging Stress Task (MIST), which induces exam-related stress. Non-parametric statistical tests confirm a significant increase in stress for the control group, while both interventions effectively reduce physiological arousal. This paper also implements various Machine learning models (Random Forest, Decision Tree, XGBoost) to classify stress states with high accuracy (>98%), F1 scores (>0.98), and ROC AUC values (>0.96). Integrating culturally grounded interventions with real-time physiological monitoring and AI-based stress classification can offer a scalable, intelligent framework to support student mental health.
Keywords: Blood Volume Pulse | Descriptive Statistics | Electrodermal Activity | Exam Anxiety | Guided Breathing Intervention | Indian Classical Music Therapy | Machine Learning in Stress Detection

Title: A Multimodal Biosensing System for Real-Time Driver Monitoring and Adaptive Feedback
Abstract: This paper presents a multimodal biosensing driver monitoring system for real-time detection of driver drowsiness and psychological stress. The system leverages facial expression recognition, simulated EEG signal analysis, and EMG-based stress detection to assess the driver's physical and mental state. Three different machine learning models are used: a CNN for facial emotion classification, a Random Forest classifier for EEG-based drowsiness detection, and an MLP for EMG-based stress recognition. Each model is developed with a robust preprocessing pipeline and trained using either real or simulated physiological data. The outputs are analyzed by a central decision-making engine that autonomously adjusts the vehicle's music playback via the Spotify Web API, enhancing driver alertness and comfort. This architecture exemplifies the use of affective computing to support road safety, offering an intelligent and adaptive vehicle environment. Experimental results demonstrate reliable performance across all modalities, highlighting the system's potential for practical deployment.
Keywords: driver monitoring | drowsiness detection | EEG | EMG | Multimodal biosensing | stress recognition

Title: Chained Prompting for Better Systematic Review Search Strategies
Abstract: Systematic reviews require the use of rigorously designed search strategies to ensure both comprehensive retrieval and minimization of bias. Conventional manual approaches, although methodologically systematic, are resource-intensive and susceptible to subjectivity, whereas heuristic and automated techniques frequently under-perform in recall unless supplemented by extensive expert input. We introduce a Large Language Model (LLM)-based chained prompt engineering framework for the automated development of search strategies in systematic reviews. The framework replicates the procedural structure of manual search design while leveraging LLMs to decompose review objectives, extract and formalize PICO elements, generate conceptual representations, expand terminologies, and synthesize Boolean queries. In addition to query construction, the framework exhibits superior performance in generating well-structured PICO elements relative to existing methods, thereby strengthening the foundation for high-recall search strategies. Evaluation on a subset of the LEADSInstruct dataset demonstrates that the framework attains a 0.9 average recall. These results significantly exceed the performance of existing approaches. Error analysis further highlights the critical role of precise objective specification and terminological alignment in optimizing retrieval effectiveness. These findings confirm the capacity of LLM-based pipelines to yield transparent, reproducible, and high-performing search strategies, and highlight their potential as scalable instruments for supporting evidence synthesis and evidence-based practice.
Keywords: automation | chain pipeline | literature search | LLM | prompting | search strategy

Title: The Role of AI in Supporting Differentiated Instruction for Primary Education
Abstract: Differentiated Instruction or DI is differentiated pedagogy, curriculum or learning environment to make the learning experience appropriate for individual learners. This is why differentiated instruction in primary education is a key piece of the puzzle, because if there are students of different skill levels, complexities, and paces of learning, than it is critical to ensure that the teacher is providing every student with the kind of instruction that they need to be successful. However, it may be difficult to educators handle it due to various complications, such as insufficient time, resources, responding to the needs of various learners at the same time, and others. Artificial Intelligence has been well known to be an effective instrument that has been offered to other teachers by automation; enhancing differentiated instruction; creating new possibilities of personalized learning experience; streamlining teaching plans; and enriching learning processes and results. The AI-based educational technologies employs data analysis, adaptive learning technologies, and machine learning algorithm to monitor the performance of students and personalize learning pathways that should facilitate the process of differentiated instruction. An example is supporting student performance and needs, based on the intelligent tutoring system, through the application of Artificial Intelligence, which studies the behavior of students and provides tailored instruction and feedback based on the scaffolded support, depending on whether the student is performing well or not. These systems monitor the achievement of the learners and their weakness and provide the appropriate exercises and learning materials, which can be adjusted to the learning pace. This happens because struggling learners can be given the extra time they need and advanced learners can move on at a faster pace. Moreover, AI assessment software allows teachers to track student performance with greater precision. As traditional assessment provide us with a limited view on student learning, AI-driven analytics provide us with deeper insights and details on patterns of understanding and misunderstanding. These tools support teachers' analysis of students' misconceptions and allow them to modify their teaching strategies. And AI enhances formative assessment through more efficient feedback that saves instructors time that can be repurposed from the ponderous task of grading to developing instructional practice.
Keywords: adaptive learning | AI | data privacy | differentiated instruction | formative assessment | gamification | intelligent tutoring systems | machine learning | personalized learning | primary education

Title: Automated Detection of Diabetic Macular Edema Using Deep Learning on Fundus Images
Abstract: The severe diabetic retinopathy complication known as Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) leads to the most common vision loss form in diabetic patients. Automated screening identification of DME in an early stage represents an effective way to prevent complete vision damage. Unlike existing systems, an ensemble deep learning detection system along with Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), a visualizing technique to display the most important image regions for finding DME is introduced in this study. Additionally, a performance comparison of DenseNet121, EfficientNetB3, ResNet50V2 along with InceptionV3 methods for DME has been done. his study utilized the Messidor-2 dataset comprising 1,748 color fundus images with a resolution of 1 4 4 0 × 9 6 0 pixels. High diagnostic capability for DME detection emerges from the developed model which produces 0.946 AUC and simultaneous sensitivity of 94.1% and specificity of 79.6%. The results clearly demonstrate that the ensemble approach proposed in this study outperforms the individual models while delivering a reliable screening instrument which matches well between sensitivity and specificity for clinical DME screening applications. Unlike prior studies using isolated CNN architectures, this work introduces a weighted ensemble framework combining DenseNet121, EfficientNetB3, ResNet50V2, and InceptionV3 for more reliable DME screening. The integration of Grad-CAM provides transparent visualization of clinically relevant retinal regions. The study utilizes the Messidor-2 dataset containing 1,748 fundus images (1440 × 960 px), with a 70: 15: 15 training-validation-test split and a9:91 DME-positive to negative ratio, ensuring reproducibility and robustness.
Keywords: Computer-Aided Diagnosis | Deep Learning | Diabetic Macular Edema | Ensemble Learning | Fundus Imaging | Grad-CAM | Medical Image Analysis | Messidor-2

Title: Detecting Falsified Audio Through Recurrent-Convolutional Neural Network Analysis
Abstract: The advancement of deep fake technology has elevated audio fabrication detection to a critical research priority. Existing frameworks exhibit considerable constraints that hinder their integration into operational autonomous platforms. This investigation introduces an innovative methodology for acoustic data examination to identify contextual information manipulation. The proposed framework combines recurrent and convolutional neural networks within a unified computational structure. Assessment conducted on a proprietary corpus focused on operational intelligence regarding Russia's military campaign in Ukraine demonstrates the framework's exceptional performance compared to conventional approaches, suggesting significant potential for deployment within autonomous vehicle systems.
Keywords: acoustic analysis | cybersecurity | deep learning architectures | pattern recognition | speech processing

Title: AUDIOSCOUT: Precise Audio Retrieval from Consecutive Interpretation Using Speaker Diarization and Natural Language Processing
Abstract: Consecutive interpretation audio clips pose significant challenges for information retrieval due to speaker overlaps, multilingual transitions, and the complexity of pinpointing specific content. This paper introduces AudioScout, a novel system designed to accurately identify timestamps where a speaker addresses a user's query. By integrating Speaker Diarization, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and multilingual embeddings, AudioScout enables precise query-driven retrieval of both textual responses and aligned audio segments. Unlike existing retrieval systems that struggle with alternating speakers and multilingual transitions, AudioScout bridges English-language queries with multilingual audio, ensuring seamless cross-lingual accessibility. Evaluated on a custom dataset of consecutive interpretation recordings, the system achieves high retrieval accuracy while significantly reducing manual search efforts. This work advances AI-driven multilingual speech retrieval, providing a scalable solution for structured access to interpretation-based spoken content.
Keywords: Audio Transcription | Natural Language Processing (NLP) | Query-Driven Audio Retrieval | Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) | Speaker Diarization | Timestamp Mapping

Title: Transformer Based Hybrid System for Speech Transcription and Disorder Detection
Abstract: Stuttering is a fluency disorder of speech that affects communication, and the project presents an AI-powered application that identifies stuttering in real-time based on speech pattern analysis. Through natural language processing and machine learning with libraries like Transformers, PyTorch, and Scikit-learn, the system divides audio using Librosa to identify common stuttering features such as repetitions, prolongations, and abnormal pauses. Pre-trained models are then fine-tuned to identify accurately, and a straightforward Flask interface makes it deployable in speech therapy, communication training, and real-time feedback. The project brings together AI, audio sensing, and health tech in order to facilitate and enhance the monitoring of speech fluency.
Keywords: Audio Feature Extraction | Machine Learning | Natural Language Processing | Real-Time Speech Analysis | Speech Therapy Applications | Stuttering Detection

Title: Application and Optimization of YOLOv11 for Traffic Object Detection
Abstract: In autonomous driving environment perception systems, accurate detection of road targets such as vehicles and pedestrians is a key technology for ensuring driving safety. However, existing methods still face challenges such as missed detection of small targets and insufficient stability in detecting occluded targets in complex scenarios. To address these issues, this study proposes an improved YOLOv11-based model. First, an Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) mechanism is integrated into the detection head, optimizing multi-scale feature fusion via dynamic weight allocation. This enhances the model's performance in detecting objects across different sizes. Next, to boost the detection of small targets, a four-head detection structure is employed, with the addition of high-resolution detection heads improving the retention of small target features. Moreover, a loss function based on the Normalized Gaussian Wasserstein Distance (NWD) is introduced, where bounding boxes are modeled as Gaussian distributions, and their similarity is calculated through distributional similarity, which helps mitigate positional deviations for small targets. Experimental results on both the KITTI and BDD100K datasets show that the improved model not only achieves significant gains in detection accuracy but also maintains its lightweight design. Overall, the proposed approach outperforms existing methods, validating its effectiveness.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Loss Function | Object Detection | YOLOv11

Title: Measuring Reliability and Answering Times for Individual Questions in Digital versus Paper Mode for Inductive Reasoning Assessment Instruments
Abstract: Digital learning and evaluation tools allow researchers to easily capture detailed user behaviour data without compromising the academic experience captured in validated instruments, previously delivered in paper. However, often such instruments migrate to a digital format without testing for reliability of the delivery mode. This study aims to validate the reliability for digital implementation of paper-based inductive reasoning assessment instruments, as well as highlighting the novel benefits of digital delivery, from a behavioural measurement perspective. We replicate an experiment conducted using a subset of exercise items from the Raven Matrices Test, implementing the same format (two different groups, facing a standard or contextual version) both in paper and digital mode, designing and using the easily configurable PoCoPI platform to capture detailed user behaviour data. No significant differences were expected in performance between modes, albeit digital assessment is likely to be shorter. The study was conducted in person, using a convenient sample of university students (N=47), allocated randomly between delivery mode and test version. The mean success rate was 9.3 (out of 10), in average time 7 minutes. Results reveal that university students do not perform better on a contextualized version of the Raven Matrices Test than on the standard version; and confirm that subjects answer faster when the test is delivered digitally. Additionally we track the heterogeneity in response time and hesitation between participants, allowing to explore the discriminant capacity of the test. Further research can extend the validation of PoCoPI in other academic-type assessments.
Keywords: Academic Performance | Contextualized | Digital | Psychometrics | Raven Matrice Test | Time Measurement

Title: Argumentative Academic Writing Through Cluster Analysis: Towards a Typology of Profiles
Abstract: The assessment of academic writing is a key process in educational settings. Although there are instruments designed for this purpose, many of them focus solely on reporting individual results, without considering common performance structures. This study proposes an approach aimed at identifying performance profiles in argumentative academic writing, based on the analysis of collective patterns in texts produced by first-year pedagogy students at the university level. To this end, we worked with records obtained from an analytic rubric that evaluates four dimensions: (1) adherence to the discursive genre of the essay, (2) rhetorical organization of the academic essay, (3) cohesion and coherence relations, and (4) conformity to language norms. A total of 153 rubric records were analyzed. Using unsupervised learning techniques, specifically hierarchical clustering, two groups were identified, whose separation was statistically significant according to Mann-Whitney tests applied to each dimension (p < 0.001 in all cases). Group 2, representing 51.6% of the sample (n = 79), is characterized by higher performance across the four evaluated dimensions, with average scores of 3.85 (dim1), 3.57 (dim2), 3.00 (dim3), and 3.41 (dim4). In contrast, Group 1 (n =74) showed lower averages: 2.70, 2.60, 2.09, and 2.85, respectively. We conclude that students need to develop argumentative writing strategies, as the initial profile displays basic competencies related to textual quality and the development of viewpoints and arguments. To address this, it is necessary to implement didactic sequences that support self-monitoring and the development of critical thinking. In this way, opportunities should be created to foster the construction of written arguments. Additionally, to facilitate the exploration of group formation based on rubric-derived data, we developed a web-based tool that allows for the interactive exploration of new datasets generated by other researchers. Finally, we present ethical guidelines for the use of the tool.
Keywords: academic writing assessment | cluster analysis | rubric-based evaluation | unsupervised machine learning | web-based educational tool

Title: Optimizing Network Security Protocols with Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM) in Wireless Sensor Networks
Abstract: This research aims to analyze how Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM) can enhance network security in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). Considering the fact that WSNs are resource-constrained and are susceptible to security threats, doesn't allow the application of conventional security methods. To accomplish this, the present study proposes the implementation of GBM, a potent ensemble learning procedure, in order to improve the reliability of various security mechanisms in WSNs. The plan is to collect the corresponding data, preprocess it, train a machine learning model, and, finally, implement it in the network in real-time. The use of the GBM model yielded better results than the baseline methods, given high accuracy, precision, and recall rates in analyzing security threats. The study shows that utilization of GBM can enhance the security of WSNs by up to 50%, and thus GBM can be used as an instrument to prevent WSNs in various vital applications, supporting the principles of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) for promoting sustainable innovation and resilient infrastructure in digital communication systems.
Keywords: Ensemble learning | Gradient Boosting Machines | Network Security | SDG | Sustainable Innovation | Wireless Sensor Networks

Title: Research on Pulmonary Nodule Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8: Attention Mechanism and Multi- scale Feature Fusion
Abstract: Early and precise detection of pulmonary nodules is crucial for improving the diagnosis and treatment outcomes of lung cancer. However, manual reading of traditional CT images has limitations such as low efficiency and the tendency to miss small lesions (<3mm), especially when dealing with the weak features of small nodules and their susceptibility to background noise interference. As a mainstream object detection algorithm, YOLOv8, although it has the advantage of real-time performance, has bottlenecks in the detection of small objects in medical images, such as insufficient feature fusion and high missed detection rate of pulmonary micronodules. To this end, this paper proposes a pulmonary nodule detection system based on the improved YOLOv8, which specifically addresses the above-mentioned pain points by integrating the CBAM attention mechanism and multi- scale feature fusion strategy. Specifically, the improved model embeds CBAM modules in the backbone network (CSPDarknet) and the neck network (PANet), using channel attention (CAM) to learn channel weights and spatial attention (SAM) to generate spatial masks, thereby enhancing feature focusing on nodule regions. Meanwhile, the PANet structure is improved by adding a direct path from the shallow high-resolution feature map (such as 80 × 80) to the detection head, and an adaptive weight fusion mechanism (ASFF) is introduced to optimize the fusion effect of deep and shallow features. Furthermore, by adjusting the weights of the CIoU Loss to balance the positive and negative samples, the Focal Loss is added to alleviate the imbalance problem of the categories of large and small nodules. Experiments on the LUNA16 dataset show that the model achieves 92.5% SOTA performance on the mAP@0.5 metric, significantly outperforming benchmark models such as the original YOLOv8 and Faster R-CNN. Moreover, the lightweight design (only increasing by 0.8G FLOPs) achieves a balance between detection accuracy and speed. The ablation experiment verified the effectiveness of the CBAM module and the multi-scale fusion strategy. This study provides radiologists with an efficient auxiliary tool, which is conducive to improving the efficiency of pulmonary nodule screening and promoting the clinical application of AI-assisted early diagnosis of lung cancer.
Keywords: CBAM attention mechanism; Multi-scale feature fusion | Improve YOLOv8 | LUNA16 dataset | Pulmonary nodule detection

Title: Application of the Cascade Method in the Integration of Whisper and Ensemble NLP for Speech Summarization
Abstract: In the era of information overload and due to declined human cognitive skill, efficient comprehension of spoken content has become increasingly important. This study propose a cascade-based speech summarization framework that integrates OpenAI’s Whisper-small model for speech recognition and Ensemble Model that combine T5, Pegasus, and BART for abstractive text summarization process. The CNN/DailyMail News dataset is used for the training and evaluation process. The system aims to transform spoken input into concise, semantically coherent summaries while minimizing transcription and summarizations errors. The methodology consists of two sequential stages, which are Whisper-based ASR for transcription and ensemble model summarization using reranking method. Experimental results demonstrate that Whisper-small achieved an exceptional transcription accuracy with WER of 3.3% and CER of 1.7%. Among individual models, BART obtained the highest summarization performance with ROUGE-L of 0.7498, while the ensemble model achieved balanced performance across all metrics.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Ensemble Model | NLP | Speech Summarization | Whisper

Title: A Weighted Ensemble of Multi-Scale Fusion CNNs for Melanoma Classification
Abstract: The early and accurate diagnosis of malignant melanoma remains a significant challenge in dermatology, largely due to the high visual similarity between malignant and benign skin lesions. This paper introduces a novel classification methodology tested on the challenging and highly imbalanced ISIC 2017 dataset. A custom multi-scale feature fusion head was designed to improve the feature extraction capabilities of standard Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) backbones. Through systematic evaluation, an EfficientNetB6 model equipped with this fusion head was identified as the most effective single-model architecture. To further boost the performance, a weighted ensemble was developed that combines the outputs of our two best fusion models: EfficientNetB6 and DenseNet201. The final proposed model, utilizing a 90/10 weighting scheme, achieved an F1-score of 0.5517, an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.8174, and a clinically significant recall of 75.2%. The experimental results demonstrated that this weighted ensemble of multi-scale fusion models offers a superior balance between precision and recall, establishing an effective strategy for this complex classification task.
Keywords: Computer-Aided Diagnosis | Deep Learning | Ensemble Learning | ISIC 2017 | Melanoma Classification | Multi-Scale Feature Fusion

Title: Speech Enhancement using Sub Convolutional based STCM Model
Abstract: Speech enhancement improves the quality and intelligibility of speech in noisy environments. An effective speech Enhancement model depends on precisely modeling the long range dependencies of noisy speech. Although several recent studies have been performed to enhance speech by capturing long-term contextual information, in this paper we propose that speech enhancement through multistage learning is an effective method for improving various deep learning modules. The proposed model utilizes a multi-stage structure where Sub-convolutional blocks are followed by stacks of Squeezed Temporal Convolutional Network Modules (STCMs) featuring exponentially increasing dilation rates, and improves the parameters. The STCM blocks handle temporal sequence modeling tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed model improves performance over existing baselines with objective metrics being PESQ and STOI.
Keywords: Speech Enhancement (SE) | Squeezed Temporal Convolutional network Module (STCM) | Sub Convolutional Encoder (SCE) | Transformers

Title: Ges-QA: A Multidimensional Quality Assessment Dataset for Audio-to-3D Gesture Generation
Abstract: The Audio-to-3D-Gesture (A2G) task exhibits significant potential across domains including virtual reality, computer graphics, and 3D animation production. However, current evaluation metrics, such as Fréchet Gesture Distance or Beat Constancy, fail at reflecting the human preference of the generated 3D gestures. To cope with this problem, exploring human preference and an objective quality assessment metric for AI-generated 3D human gestures is becoming increasingly significant. In this paper, we introduce the Ges-QA dataset, which includes 1,400 samples with multidimensional scores for gesture quality and audio-gesture consistency. Moreover, we collect binary classification labels to determine whether the generated gestures match the emotions of the audio. Equipped with our Ges-QA dataset, we propose a multi-modal transformer-based neural network with 3 branches for video, audio and 3D skeleton modalities, which can score A2G contents in multiple dimensions. Comparative experimental results and ablation studies demonstrate that Ges-QAer yields state-of-the-art performance on our dataset.
Keywords: AI-Generated Content | Audio-to-3D-Gesture | Quality Assessment

Title: Performance Evaluation of Lyric-Based Music Recommendation Model: Comparison of TF-IDF, Word2Vec, BERT, and Hybrid Model
Abstract: Music recommendation systems play a vital role in enhancing user experience on streaming platforms like Spotify by providing accurate and personalized song suggestions. This study explores and compares different text-based recommendation approaches, including TFIDF, Word2Vec, BERT, and a Hybrid Model, to analyze song lyrics and improve recommendation accuracy. Using a dataset of song lyrics, TF-IDF identifies word frequency similarities, Word2Vec captures semantic relationships between words, and BERT understands lyrical context using deep language modeling. A Hybrid Model combining these approaches is also developed to enhance recommendation performance. The models are evaluated using Precision@5, Recall@5, and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) to determine their effectiveness. The results indicate that TF-IDF has the lowest performance, as it relies only on direct word matching. Word2Vec improves accuracy by recognizing word associations, while BERT significantly enhances recommendation quality by understanding contextual meaning. The Hybrid Model achieves the best performance across all metrics, demonstrating that integrating multiple techniques leads to more precise recommendations. These findings suggest that combining deep learning and NLP methods improves recommendation systems, making them more effective for platforms like Spotify, Apple Music, and YouTube Music. Future research can further optimize these models by incorporating user listening behavior and song metadata for even better personalization.
Keywords: BERT | Hybrid Model | Music Recommendation System | SDG's | TF-IDF | Word2Vec

Title: The Zone Promotion using Binaural Beats
Abstract: Music is widely used in daily life and is essential for commuting, relaxation, and concentration. Especially in sports and learning, music has the effect of increasing concentration and motivation, contributing to improved performance. On the other hand, binaural beats using "swells,"which are certain pattern sounds, are also said to have healing effects and enhance cognitive abilities. Therefore, we examined the effects of listening to music on concentration from biometric measurements. In particular, we created a pseudo "the zone"(a hyper-concentration state: a state of high concentration and a sense of immersion) using binaural beats and verified its effects. Two female and four male subjects in their early 20s were evaluated by acquiring biological data (electroencephalogram (EEG) and electrocardiogram (ECG)) while performing an exercise task (cards tower: making a tower of playing cards) and a thinking task (Kraepelin test) that required concentration while listening to various types of music, and then evaluating the subjects in their lowest concentrated state. The binaural beats were applied to the state in which the subjects were least able to concentrate, and their state was examined to see if it changed. EEG analysis showed an increase in the ratio of the characteristic frequency band, Sensory Motor Rhythm (SMR): (αβ12-15 Hz), and a decrease in the stress level (β intensity/α intensity) in four of the six subjects to whom binaural beats were applied. In addition, the Poincaré plot of R-R interval (RRI) showed a reduction in area (increased density). From these experimental results, we confirmed the possibility that the binaural beats applied and evaluated in the lowest concentrated state promote an exquisite balance state and the zone of the autonomic nervous system.
Keywords: binaural beats | ECG | EEG | heart rate | music | Poincaré plot | RRI | the zone

Title: Masking-Augmentation on Mel-Spectrogram and MFCC for White-crowned Sparrow Vocalization Variants Classification
Abstract: This paper presents a study on the application of masking augmentation techniques on the frequency and time axis of Mel-spectrogram and MFCC features for classifying vocalization variants of the White-crowned Sparrow using MobileNetV3. The dataset consists of 860 audio recordings of nine variation groups recorded in California, USA. The study explores the impact of different masking parameters on model performance, evaluated using aggregated F1-score metrics across ten cross-validation folds. The results indicate that applying masking augmentation on Mel-spectrogram features yields the highest F1-score of 98%, outperforming MFCC features and non-augmented data. However, the study also finds several things that can lead to performance degradation attributed to low and high ranges of certain parameters, such as the number of mels or coefficients used to generate the features and the masking coverage on the augmented data.
Keywords: audio classification | augmentation | birdsong | mel-spectrogram | mfcc

Title: Efficient Realization of Audio Processing on FPGA
Abstract: Field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and advanced embedded computing boards have become essential to attain high performance in modern computing systems. This offers substantial control capability, improves productivity and efficiency across various applications. The current work incorporates audio processing and denoising using accelerated computing. The coefficients of the infinite impulse response (IIR) filter are fine-tuned to get optimal results. The audio signal comprises 64,000 samples, each with 16-bit resolution, having a sampling rate of 16 kHz. The audio processing using Verilog has been executed on two different platforms: the first is a general-purpose computer, and the second is an FPGA. It has been observed that audio processing on an FPGA-based platform offers higher computational efficiency. This can be good in handling real-time, computation-intensive digital signal processing (DSP) applications, such as image and audio denoising, and machine learning, where both performance and resource utilization are critical.
Keywords: Digital signal processing | FPGA | hardware description language | IIR filter | Verilog

Title: NSM's SPOTLIGHT: An Unprecedented Journey into the Transient Universe
Abstract: SPOTLIGHT is a time-domain survey instrument to perform a real-time commensal search for Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) and Pulsars with a PetaFlop system installed at the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) funded under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM). The system executes real-time HPC and AI applications to ensure simultaneous time-domain detection and arc-second imaging localisation of the detected bursts across the GMRT observing band. With an unprecedented sensitivity, SPOTLIGHT is expected to find hundreds of FRBs with possible host galaxy associations, allowing the use of the bursts as cosmological probes. The AI-assisted trigger for genuine astronomical signals enables the capturing of voltage samples spanning the burst duration to study the spectro-temporalpolarimetric properties at microsecond time resolution to probe FRB progenitor models as well as propagation imprints. SPOTLIGHT, an AI-powered big data science project on indigenously developed hardware, enables transformational, high-impact science in time-domain astronomy with the GMRT. The initiative aims to build a robust technological and scientific workforce within the country to enable cutting-edge scientific applications.
Keywords: AI | Big-data | High Performance Computing | Real-time Digital Signal Processing | Time-domain survey

Title: Adopting ChatGPT in Higher Education: UTAUT2 Findings and Student Sentiment from Brunei
Abstract: Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT are rapidly entering higher education, yet the drivers of student adoption remain under-examined outside Western contexts. This study investigates behavioural intention to adopt ChatGPT and students' perceptions in Brunei Darussalam. Using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) as the conceptual lens, we surveyed students from five institutions ($n=378$ for the UTAUT2 model; $n=168$ for the perceptions instrument). Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) established reliability and convergent validity; structural equation modelling (SEM) then tested seven hypothesised paths to behavioural intention (BI). Five of seven were significant-Performance Expectancy, Social Influence, Facilitating Conditions, Hedonic Motivation, and Habit-while Effort Expectancy and Price Value were not. A hybrid sentiment analysis of open-ended responses (lexicon seeding with VADER plus multinomial logistic regression) indicated predominantly positive views of ChatGPT as a study aid, alongside concerns about accuracy and reliability. The results provide context-specific evidence on technology acceptance for generative AI in Brunei higher education and suggest practical levers-supportive infrastructure, peer-led norms, and engaging use cases-for responsible student adoption.
Keywords: Behavioural Intention | ChatGPT | Higher Education | Technology Acceptance | UTAUT2

Title: Improving Sentiment Classification Accuracy using Engagement and Temporal Features from Social Media Data
Abstract: Sentiment analysis has become an important instrument to gain insight on user attitudes, brands and trends in online behavior and digital platforms. This paper addresses this aspect by conducting a recognizable study of an approach encompassing all the available methodologies on classifying sentiment in three categories, i.e. positive, negative and neutral as well as traditional Machine Learning (ML) models, ensemble approaches and a stacking-based combination approach. Different independent classifier models such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Naive Bayes (NB) mode have been tested with Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) features on a sentiment dataset that has undergone preprocessing. Hard voting and extended voting using multiple learners are applied to make a more significant improvement in performance. It shows the biggest benefit in a stacking ensemble model, where LR, NB and SVM are implemented as base learners, and Random Forest (RF) serves as a meta-learner. The findings confirm the usefulness of using hybrid ensemble models in sentiment classification particularly when sparse and moderate sized data sets are involved.
Keywords: Brand Management | Machine Learning | Natural Language Processing | Sentimental Analysis | Social Media | Text Classification

Title: NeuroFusion Advancing Brain Tumor Diagnosis Using CNN Architectures
Abstract: Brain Tumors are a most crucial & life-threatening medical condition for quick & proper diagnosis so that treatment can be done effectively. Conventional diagnostic methods embrace manual interpretation of MRI pictures, that may be tedious and susceptible to human blunders. This study is thrust to establish an AI-driven brain tumor diagnostic system built upon CNNs for improving the accuracy and efficiency of diagnostic. Unlike traditional methods, this work uses deep learning to remove radiologists' dependency on tumor detection and to perceptually decrease the misdiagnosis risks. The proposed NeuroFusion framework employs several CNN structures such as ResNet50, VGG16, DenseNet121 and a custom CNN architecture to employ on the MRI images for distinguishing and categorizing tumor types. dataset get preprocessing such as resizing, normalization, data augmentation to increase robust of model. Experimental results exhibit that DenseNet121 surpasses other models' performance with an accuracy of 98.7%, superior, and indicates that it has the higher classification capability. Moreover, consistency is confirmed by confusion matrix and classification report. It shows that deep learning-based diagnostic instruments are capable to great extent to enhance medical image evaluation such as fast and accurate tumor classification. The future of medical diagnostics with AI is highly likely to make clinical decision making more effective, offering a scalable and cost-effective approach for brain tumor.
Keywords: AI in Medical Diagnostics | Brain Tumor Classification | Convolutional Neural Networks | Deep Learning | MRI Image Analysis

Title: Research on Pointer-Type Scale Instrument Recognition Using Three-Stage Algorithm Framework
Abstract: This paper addresses the automatic reading requirements for pointer-type scale instruments in aerospace launch site environments by proposing an end-to-end recognition methodology based on deep learning. The approach employs a three-stage processing pipeline comprising "detection-correction-recognition", with core components including an optimized YOLOv5-based instrument detection module (YDM), an enhanced spatial transformation network for instrument correction (STM) with implicit offset modeling, and a value acquisition module (VAM) integrating semantic segmentation with sequence recognition. Through optimization strategies including anchor optimization, attention mechanisms, multi-scale training, implicit spatial offset modeling, and multi-task learning with balanced loss weighting, the method effectively handles challenges including complex backgrounds, perspective variations, and illumination changes. Experimental validation demonstrates superior performance in instrument localization, image rectification, and final reading interpretation, satisfying stringent accuracy and robustness requirements for practical deployment.
Keywords: meter recognition | multi-task learning | Pointer instrument | reading interpretation | spatial transformer network | YOLOv5

Title: Deep Learning Based Multimodal Biometric Authentication using Iris and Speech
Abstract: In the rapidly evolving digital era, securing identity verification systems is critical, particularly with the rise in sophisticated cyber threats. This study presents an innovative biometric authentication system based on deep learning, which combines iris recognition with speaker identification. The iris features are extracted using pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) such as ResNet101, while speech features Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), energy, pitch, and frequency are derived using digital signal processing techniques. These features are concatenated and passed to a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for final classification. The system is trained using a synthesized dataset formed from the Iris of the Eye dataset and the CMU ARCTIC speech corpus. It achieves an outstanding 98.5% identification accuracy, outperforming several unimodal and state-of-the-art methods. Robustness is further analyzed under speech noise injection and modality mismatch scenarios. The integration of CNN and LSTM architectures demonstrates superior learning of both spatial and sequential biometric traits, paving the way for more secure and intelligent for significantly strengthen authentication reliability and accuracy.
Keywords: Iris | multimodal biometrics | Performance | ResNet101 | speaker identification

Title: Enhancing Stock Price Forecasts with Random Forests and Simple Moving Average Indicators
Abstract: Accurate stock price forecasting is known to be a challenging problem for financial markets, since the stock price has a volatile and nonlinear nature. This paper conducts a systematic comparison of two machine learning tools, namely, Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Random Forest Regression (RFR), for predicting the next-day adjusted closing prices of stocks. Both models are trained on a simple yet powerful feature set: adjusted close, 5-day and 10-day SMA, and are fitted to historical stock data. The assessment is carried out on two performance metrics: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and the coefficient of determination (R<sup>2).</sup> Results obtained from a wide range of shares show that Random Forest consistently outperforms with larger average R<sup>2</sup> and smaller RMSE values across the board. Although SVR achieves good results in smoother and more stationary trends, it is sensitive to noisy trends and parameter configurations. The ensemble nature of Random Forest is more robust and suitable for capturing complex market behaviors. This comparative study highlights the efficiency of ensemble-based models in financial forecasting.
Keywords: Predictive Modeling | Random Forest | Simple Moving Averages | Stock Price Forecasting | Support Vector Regression

Title: Early Detection of Knee Osteoporosis Using Fine-Tuned VGG19 Model on X-ray Images
Abstract: Usually resulting in major mobility problems and pain, knee osteoporosis (KO) is a common disorder compromising bone strength and raising the risk of fractures. Effective therapy depends on early diagnosis; but conventional techniques include clinical examination and bone mineral density tests can ignore early-stage bone abnormalities. This work uses a customized VGG19 deep learning model to predict knee osteoporosis from X-ray pictures. Leveraging transfer learning, the VGG19 model known for its great performance in image classification was modified for binary classification (healthy against osteoporotic). With both Healthy and Osteoporosis categories, the model was trained and validated on a dataset of knee X-rays including 1,258 training images, 315 validation images, and 472 testing images. With great accuracy of 97.5%, high precision, recall, and F1-scores of 0.97 for both classes, the model performed really remarkably. With just 12 false negatives and low misclassification no false positives the confusion matrix exposed Although sporadic variations in validation loss indicated minor overfitting, the general training and validation accuracy curves showed consistent learning and good generalization. This work validates the ability of deep learning models especially VGG19 in automating knee osteoporosis detection and thereby enhancing diagnosis accuracy. This strategy can greatly improve patient outcomes by giving doctors a strong instrument for early diagnosis. Future research will concentrate on lowering overfitting and enhancing model stability maybe by means of further hyperparameter optimization and regularizing approaches.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Deep Learning | Knee Osteoporosis | Model Training | VGG19 Model

Title: Unveiling Indian Coral Biodiversity and Health Status via Multi-Task Deep Learning on Underwater Imagery
Abstract: The invaluable coral reefs, which are essential for marine ecosystem worldwide and especially in India, face serious threats from global warming, sea water pollution, and increasing sea temperatures. This environmental destruction causes extreme coral bleaching, illness, and ecosystem collapse, damaging sea life and effecting communities in the coastal regions which are dependent on these ecosystems for sustenance. Traditional methods for monitoring coral health, like manual surveys, are slow, costly, and obstructing rapid, comprehensive understanding. To solve this problem, our project presents an automated, efficient approach for coral reef health evaluation using deep learning on underwater images. We started with data collection and expansion, generating a dataset of over 100,000 coral images for model training using image augmentation. During the second phase, ten diverse deep learning models, including custom CNNs and pre-trained architectures like InceptionV3, were created. The third phase focused on fine-tuning these models, resulting in considerable increases in performance. Specifically, models like SimpleCNN and InceptionV3 achieved a remarkable 96% classification accuracy on a 20,000-image test set, successfully solving problems like class imbalance and overfitting. This project provides a strong groundwork for a reliable coral health monitoring system, offering marine experts a fast, accurate instrument for monitoring reef conditions and detecting initial signs of stress indicators, ultimately safeguarding India's invaluable coral reef biodiversity.
Keywords: Coral health | Coral reefs | Deep learning | Image Classification | Underwater Imagerywords

Title: Advancing Earthquake Prediction Accuracy Through Machine Learning: A GBM-Based Study on Diagnostic Performance and Reliability
Abstract: In the study of seismic data, earthquake prediction has proved to be an important issue because of the sophisticated, non-linear, character of the information. In this paper, we discuss the effectiveness of Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM), a strong ensemble learning algorithm, in classifying earthquake events over a well-organized seismic data set. We used stratified data partitions to train and validate our model, which would result in the balancing and confirm appropriate representation of classes. This analysis was done by using various performance measurements and illustrations in order to carry out an effective evaluation. The Confusion matrix indicates a high level of classification of the model, with true positive number of 358 and true negative number of 288, and false negative 34, and false positive 85. The combined accuracy is at 84 percent implying a balanced sensitivity on the model with regard to earthquake and non-earthquake cases. Also, the precision of non-earthquake and earthquake are 0.89 and 0.81 respectively in the classification report whereas recall is high in earthquake cases (0.91) which means high sensitivity and less chance of misses. The high values of the F1-score (0.83 and 0.86, respectively) indicate overall high balance between the precision and recall in classes 0 and 1. The Discriminative strength of the model is further supported by Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve which indicates a good ability to discriminate between the 2 classes with Area under the curve (AUC) score of 0.90. In the learning curve results, training and validation scores improve steadily and converge at the end of the learning curve, and threshold analysis proves that the model is optimized by avoiding either false positive or false negative. This method which is based on GBM shows quite high level of accuracy and strength in earthquake prediction. Due to its capacity to run complicated seismic characteristics, it is being utilized as an invaluable instrument in disaster preparedness, in combination with early warning systems, which portrays a data-based approach to the kind of reliability that results in seismic event predictions.
Keywords: Diagnostic Accuracy | Earthquake Prediction | Gradient Boosting Machine | Machine Learning | Seismic Risk Assessment

Title: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Forecasting NIFTY50 and NIFTY500 Indices using Technical Indicators
Abstract: The stock market forecasting is a challenging issue because of volatility, nonlinear, and dynamic nature. This paper explores the predictive capabilities of three deep learning algorithms: LSTM, GRU, and CNN-LSTM in predicting the weekly closing prices of the primary Indian stock indices such as NIFTY50 and NIFTY500. We developed a custom Weekly dataset having historical features such as Open, High, Low, Close and Volume (OHLCV) data and technical indicators. Technical indicators are derived using OHLCV data like Relative Strength Index (RSI), point difference, percentage difference are used. Evaluation of the models is performed on the basis of such metrics as the Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R<sup>2</sup> score. Findings indicate a superior performance of CNN-LSTM in predicting NIFTY50 and LSTM in predicting NIFTY500, which proves the usefulness of hybrid deep learning models in time series forecasting in the financial sector.
Keywords: CNN | Deep Learning | GRU | LSTM

Title: A GeneSwarm-Enhanced Hybrid Ensemble Model for Predicting Cardiac Outcomes in Kawasaki Disease
Abstract: Kawasaki Disease (KD) is a paediatric vasculitis that may cause coronary artery lesions (CAL) in case it is not diagnosed and treated early. The problem of complicated clinical data and nonspecific markers has complicated proper forecasting of the long-term KD outcomes. This paper suggests a hybrid ensemble machine learning model to use XGBoost, AdaBoost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers and soft voting in order to have robust and interpretable predictions. The GeneSwarm Feature Selector was used to select the features based on the Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization which can optimally identify the most informative and non-redundant clinical and laboratory features. The Babysitting algorithm was used to optimize hyperparameters dynamically and Interquartile Range (IQR) to eliminate outliers and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to deal with class imbalance were used during preprocessing. Assessed on 1,850 paediatric KD cases, the proposed model demonstrated a 97.10% accuracy, 96.50% precision, 96.80% recall, 96.60% F1-score, and a macro-AUC of 97.40% and is better than the current ML methods. Best predictive variables were Complications, Clinical Outcomes, Treatment Approach, Echocardiography, Laboratory Tests, Fever Duration, and Symptoms. These findings indicate that the framework is a reliable, interpretable, and clinically applicable instrument of early KD prognosis, which helps to plan personalized treatment and stratify risks. Through the incorporation of superior feature selection, ensemble learning, and a solid preprocessing, the research will add to an empirical and pragmatic method of enhancing cardiac care in pediatrics.
Keywords: Babysitting Algorithm | Feature Selection | GeneSwarm | Hybrid Ensemble | Kawasaki Disease | Machine Learning

Title: Hybrid Ensemble Machine Learning Framework for Predictive Consumer Food Safety Risk Assessment
Abstract: Food safety is still a global public health issue. Every year, more than 600 million people get sick from foodborne illnesses because of unsafe handling, bad vendor practices, and not enough predictive surveillance. Current studies reveal substantial discrepancies between consumer and vendor knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) and actual contamination outcomes, especially in low- and middle-income nations. To mitigate these constraints, this study introduces an innovative Machine Learning-Driven Framework for Safeguarding Consumer Food Safety, amalgamating behavioral, environmental, and microbiological data into a cohesive predictive model. The suggested system uses hybrid ensemble learning, which combines Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Support Vector Machines, to figure out the risk of contamination and sort hazards into different levels. A dataset comprising 10,000 consumer-vendor interactions and 1,200 microbiological samples was subjected to a 10-fold cross-validation protocol for analysis. The model had an accuracy of 94.6%, an F1-score of 0.93, and an AUC of 0.96 (p < 0.001), which was 8.4% better than baseline models. An analysis of feature importance showed that vendor hygiene compliance, food temperature, and consumer awareness were the most important factors. SHAP-based feature attribution made sure that the model was explainable, which made it easier to understand for policy and regulatory use. The proposed framework offers a scalable, privacy-preserving instrument for early contamination forecasting and evidence-based intervention formulation. Future extensions will investigate federated learning and IoT integration to facilitate real-time monitoring and adaptive risk management in various food systems.
Keywords: Consumer Protection | Explainable AI | Food Safety | Machine Learning | Public Health | Risk Prediction

Title: Multimodal NLP-Audio Approach for Early Alzheimer's Detection Using BERT and Acoustic Embeddings
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease, or AD, requires early diagnosis to intervene and reverse the progression of the condition. In this paper, a strong multimodal scheme is proposed by incorporating Natural Language Processing (NLP) and signal processing of the acoustic signal to detect early indications of AD. The postulated system will use Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) to capture semantic and syntactic information of transcribed speech and acoustic information through Melfrequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) and pretrained sound models like VGGish. The methodology comprises broad preprocessing of the datasets of clinical interviews, extraction of linguistics and acoustic embeddings, and combination of these features through a late-fusion-based design in a deep neural network framework. The pipeline includes the modular sets of steps, such as pre-processing, training, evaluation, and realtime inference using a web interface. Performance was found to be an overall accuracy of 92% on labelled clinical data. Its system allows effortless interaction with the users through uploading audio or inputting text and produces results interpretable with clinical suggestions. In the future, we will extend the dataset with multilingual and nonhomogeneous speech samples, adopt methods of explainable AI, e.g., SHAP and LIME, and also support longitudinal monitoring of cognitive dynamics and the optimization of the framework to run on edge hardware that would allow us to screen people remotely in resource-limited areas.
Keywords: Acoustic Embeddings | Alzheimer's Disease (AD) | Audio Signal Processing | BERT Transformers | Multimodal Learning | Natural Language Processing

Title: Intelligent Smart Metering Framework for Anomaly Detection in Battery Storage Systems and Energy Efficiency Enhancement
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and distributed battery storage into modern power grids necessitates intelligent monitoring mechanisms to ensure reliability and efficiency. Traditional metering systems lack the capability to identify anomalies in storage elements, leading to reduced battery lifespan, unexpected failures, and inefficiencies in grid performance. This study presents an Intelligent Smart Metering Framework designed for anomaly detection in battery storage systems while simultaneously promoting energy efficiency. The proposed framework employs advanced data analytics and machine learning techniques to monitor real-time parameters enabling early detection of irregular charging/discharging patterns, overvoltage, or capacity degradation. The methodology integrates predictive modeling and anomaly detection algorithms with smart meter data, ensuring accurate fault identification and proactive maintenance. The primary objective of this framework is to enhance operational reliability, extend battery life, and optimize the interaction between storage units and the power grid. The outcomes highlight the potential of intelligent smart metering to support sustainable grid operations and energy-efficient consumption in next-generation smart energy ecosystems.
Keywords: Battery Storage Anomaly Detection | Demand-Side Management | Dynamic Pricing | Energy Efficiency | Intelligent Energy Monitoring | Machine Learning | Predictive Maintenance | Renewable Energy Integration | Smart Metering Systems | Sustainable Grid Operations

Title: Automatic Document Classification and Intelligent Archiving System for Academic Administration Based on BERT-TextCNN Fusion Model
Abstract: Efficient management and classification of educational administrative documents is crucial for modern higher education institutions, yet manual archiving remains time-consuming and error-prone. This paper proposes a novel BERT-TextCNN fusion model that integrates global semantic understanding with local n-gram feature extraction for intelligent document classification. The model employs a dual-branch architecture where the BERT branch captures contextual semantics through pre-trained transformers, while the TextCNN branch extracts discriminative local patterns through multi-scale convolutional networks. Two key innovations are introduced: (1) a multi-granularity semantic fusion layer utilizing attention mechanisms to adaptively combine features from both branches, and (2) a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism that automatically balances branch contributions based on document characteristics. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset of 80,000 Chinese educational documents across 12 categories demonstrate that our model achieves 94.7% classification accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines including BERT-base (88.5%) and BERT + BiLSTM (90.1%) by 6.2% and 4.6% respectively, while maintaining 26% faster inference speed (38.6 ms/doc). Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each component, with the attention-based fusion contributing 3.4% and dynamic weighting contributing 1.9% performance gain. The model exhibits exceptional robustness across varying document lengths (93.8%-95.1% accuracy) through adaptive weight adjustment. A 3-month pilot deployment at a major Chinese university processed 12,547 documents with 94.2% accuracy, reducing manual archiving time by 86-89% and achieving 92% user satisfaction. These results demonstrate the practical value of our approach for intelligent educational document management systems.
Keywords: attention mechanism | BERT | deep learning | Document classification | educational administration | natural language processing | semantic fusion | TextCNN

Title: MS-YOLO: A Multi-Scale Method for UAV-Based Insulator and Defect Detection
Abstract: The automatic detection of transmission line insulators is critical to ensuring the reliability and safety of power grids. However, in complex aerial imaging environments, the multi-scale variations in insulators and defect targets pose significant challenges to the detection task. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved object detection model based on YOLOv11, named MS-YOLO. First, in the Neck of the model, the Inter-scale Feature Focusing and Diffusion Pyramid Network (IFDPN) is designed to optimize multi-scale feature extraction and fusion, while improving the utilization of fine-grained features Subsequently, a Dual-weighted Distance (DWD) loss is designed to improve the model's localization performance across multiple scales. Achieving mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 91.8% and 74.3%, respectively, on the self-constructed dataset, MS-YOLO sustains an inference speed of 195 FPS. This validates the effectiveness of MS-YOLO in detecting insulators and defects.
Keywords: Deep learning | Defect detection | Insulator | Object detection | Transmission line

Title: CrowdShield: A Smartphone-Based AIoT Framework for Real-Time Women's Safety Using Emotion-Aware Voice Recognition and LLM-Powered Alert Classification
Abstract: Women's safety in public and private spaces remains a pressing global concern, often exacerbated by the limitations of conventional safety tools that require manual interaction during distress. This paper introduces CrowdShield, a smartphone-based AIoT framework that enables real-time emergency detection and multi-channel alert dissemination using speech emotion recognition and intent classification. The system integrates lightweight on-device convolutional recurrent neural networks (CRNNs) for emotion detection and quantized large language models (LLMs) for contextual intent understanding. Voice inputs are analyzed locally to preserve user privacy, with alerts propagated through a hybrid communication strategy combining Bluetooth mesh, cellular SMS, and cloud messaging. Privacy is ensured through ephemeral audio buffers, anonymization, and end-to-end encryption. Evaluated on standard emotion datasets (RAVDESS, CREMAD) and multilingual voice samples, CrowdShield achieves 91.3% emotion classification accuracy and sub-3s end-to-end alert latency, with low energy overhead. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse use-case scenarios, including public transport and isolated environments. By combining edge AI, ethical design, and resilient communication, CrowdShield establishes a scalable foundation for enhancing women's safety through proactive and privacy-conscious intervention.
Keywords: AIoT | Edge AI | Emotion Recognition | Intent Classification | Large Language Models | MultiChannel Communication | Privacy-Preserving AI | Real-Time Alert Systems | Smartphone Security | Speech Processing | Women's Safety

Title: SmoothGuard: Defending Multimodal Large Language Models with Noise Perturbation and Clustering Aggregation
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance across diverse tasks by jointly reasoning over textual and visual inputs. Despite their success, these models remain highly vulnerable to adversarial manipulations, raising concerns about their safety and reliability in deployment. In this work, we first generalize an approach for generating adversarial images within the HuggingFace ecosystem and then introduce SmoothGuard, a lightweight and model-agnostic defense framework that enhances the robustness of MLLMs through randomized smoothing and clustering-based prediction aggregation. Our method perturbs continuous modalities (e.g., images and audio) with Gaussian noise, generates multiple candidate outputs, and applies embedding-based clustering to filter out adversarially influenced predictions. The final answer is selected from the majority cluster, ensuring stable responses even under malicious perturbations. Extensive experiments on POPE, LLa VA-Bench (In-the- Wild), and MM-SafetyBench demonstrate that Smooth Guard improves resilience to adversarial attacks while maintaining competitive utility. Ablation studies further identify an optimal noise range (0.1-0.2) that balances robustness and utility. These findings establish Smooth Guard as a practical step toward secure and reliable multimodal reasoning, with future work extending the framework to audio-focused benchmarks to validate its generality across modalities. Code is publicly available here: https://github.com/GuangzhiSu/SmoothGuard.
Keywords: adversarial defense | model robustness | Multimodal large language models | trustworthy AI

Title: Identifying Fake Audio Using Social Media Metadata and Audio Features
Abstract: With a rise in AI generated audio, more commonly referred to as audio deepfakes, it has become increasingly important to detect fake audio content especially as it spreads across social media. While most detection methods rely only on analyzing the sound itself, they often miss important clues found in social media engagement data. In this work, we introduce a new approach that combines both audio features (such as, spectrograms, energy levels, tempo, and pitch-related measurements) and social media metadata (such as likes, dislikes, and comment counts) to determine whether an audio clip is real, or AI generated. We developed an ensemble model that brings together five different machine learning methods being, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, and a Neural Network which uses a stacking approach to improve overall prediction. We compared the results acquired from this model to the results of well known papers, including CFAD, Singfake, and ASVspoof 2019. Our model achieved an AUC of 0.847, accuracy of 84.6%, and an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 20.4%, showing that it performs similarly, if not better, than existing methods that use only audio. These results suggest that combining sound with social context offers a promising and practical way to detect deepfake audio, especially in a real world social media setting. While our model achieved moderate performance (AUC of 0.847), it highlights the potential and limitations of combining social and audio features in deepfake audio detection, and opens avenues for future tuning and dataset expansion.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Audio Detection | Binary Classification | DeepFakes | Ensemble Learning | Generated Audio

Title: SOBi-Net: A Soft Ordinal and Bidirectional Fusion Network for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
Abstract: Automated Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) grading is crucial for preventing blindness; however, existing methods face two primary challenges:'Ordinal Blindness' and 'Scale Insensitivity'. To address these issues, a soft ordinal and bidirectional fusion network (SOBi-Net) is proposed. To tackle 'Ordinal Blindness,' a Soft Ordinal learning paradigm is introduced, which explicitly embeds clinical ordinal relationships into the loss function by optimizing a smoothed target probability distribution. For 'Scale Insensitivity,' a Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network is designed to efficiently fuse multi-scale features from the backbone network, enabling the robust identification of lesions ranging from microaneurysms to neovascularization. Experiments conducted on the public APTOS2019 dataset show that the proposed model achieves excellent performance on key ordinal metrics, with a Quadratic Weighted Kappa of 0.9288 and an accuracy of 85.06%. This performance demonstrates its significant potential as an efficient, accurate, and clinicallyaware solution for automated DR grading.
Keywords: BiFPN | Deep Learning | Diabetic Retinopathy | Multi-scale Feature Fusion | Ordinal Regression | SORD Loss

Title: Automated Layout Assessment for Metadata Enrichment via Local Rényi Entropy
Abstract: The paper presents a lightweight virtual instrument for the automatic detection of text blocks, column width, and inter-column space in digitized historical documents (manuscripts) using Local Rényi Entropy (LRE). Unlike computationally intensive deep learning models, the proposed technique works without training data, relying instead on local entropy profiles computed over binarized images to efficiently reveal column structures. By analyzing local entropy profiles along both axis of the page, the instrument reliably detects column boundaries in printed book layouts, even in those with marginalia (both text and iluminations on book margins). In addition to evaluating performance on high-resolution scans, we synthetically degraded the images, by applying blur and contrast reduction, to assess robustness under different archival conditions. Computational cost of the proposed virtual instrument is compared with commonly used methods such as Run-Length Smoothing Algorithm (RLSA), Connected Component Analysis (CCA), Projection Profile, Morpohological filtering and Docstrum. Results confirm that LRE detects layout characteristics efficiently, and preserves discriminative structures even in degraded visual contexts. The proposed virtual instrument can be particularly well-suited for large-scale metadata enrichment tasks in digital heritage repositories as it supports efficient structural analysis for layout-aware OCR, segmentation, and content extraction pipelines. This is valuable for cultural heritage institutions operating without high-end computing infrastructure such as GPUs or machine learning expertise.
Keywords: document layout analysis | entropy profile | historical documents | image binarization | meta-data enrichment | Rényi entropy | text column detection

Title: Enhancing Qur'anic Recitation Skills through an AI-Based Learning Program for Non-Native Arabic Speakers
Abstract: It studies the effectiveness of an AI-based learning program using Tarteel in improving Qur'anic recitation for learners who speak a language other than Arabic. The sample consists of 30 intermediate (B1) female students from Malaysia and Indonesia studying at a Teaching Center for Arabic for Non-Native Speakers at Mansura University, Egypt, for a total of 8 weeks (52 days) of AI immediate feedback, guided practice, and practice with teacher assistance. Assessment of performance was made through the Qur'anic Recitation Skills Observation Card. This has been validated in terms of content and internal consistency (Cronbach's α=0.715). The instrument measures six skill dimensions: pronunciation; differential sounds; application of silent nūn and tanwīn rules; application of silent mīm rules; elongation (madd); and pausing rules. Paired-sample t-tests showed significant improvements in all aspects (p<0.01). Effect size values (η2=0.929-0.993) indicated a strong overall impact of the program. Results clearly indicate that Tarteel, incorporated with a well-planned instructional framework, significantly improves accuracy, fluency, and adherence to Tajwid principles in recitation. It provides a practical model for integrating AI-aided tools into Islamic studies and Arabic language studies.
Keywords: AI-based learning | educational technology | non-native Arabic speakers | Qur'anic recitation | Tajwīd | Tarteel

Title: A Holistic Countermeasure for Imbalanced Audio Deepfake Detection via Uncertainty Mining and Feature Regularization
Abstract: Constructing a large-scale training dataset encompassing representative spoofing attacks is widely recognized as essential for developing effective countermeasures (CMs) in audio deepfake detection (ADD). However, the popularization of audio language models (ALMs) enables low-cost generation of near-infinite spoofed speech data, exacerbating extreme class imbalance (limited bonafide vs. unlimited spoofed), which poses a critical challenge for CM model training. To address this issue, in this work, we propose a holistic CM framework integrating uncertainty-aware hard sample mining and discriminative feature regularization. Leveraging evidential deep learning, the proposal identifies challenging spoofed samples through predictive uncertainty estimation, thereby shifting the training focus from quantity to quality and improving learning efficiency under class imbalance. Furthermore, we impose feature-space constraints to anchor bonafide embeddings into a compact cluster while dispersing diverse spoofed representations. This strategy prevents model overfitting to spoofing representations and preserves intrinsic bonafide structure. The proposed approach synergistically optimizes training efficiency by focusing on high-impact spoofed samples while preserving discriminative feature structures, effectively mitigating performance degradation caused by class imbalance.
