Extensive experiments on Codecfake and ASVspoof datasets demonstrate significant improvements in robustness against unseen spoofing attacks and effective mitigation of data imbalance effects.
Keywords: anti-spoofing | audio deepfake detection | countermeasure | imbalanced learning

Title: Emotion Detection in Indonesian Music Comments Using BERT, Traditional Machine Learning and Their Hybrid Model
Abstract: In the era of digital communication, social media comes as a platform to express honest feelings and opinions, especially in Indonesia where user engagement continues to increase. Music, often related to emotions, gives various reactions in comments on social platforms. However, detecting emotions from Indonesian-language comments is still a challenge due to the use of informal language, emoticons, etc. This research proposes and evaluates three approaches: traditional machine learning employs TF-IDF and SVD for feature extraction, Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, and a hybrid model that combines both. The results show that BERT achieves the highest accuracy (79%). The hybrid model achieves an accuracy of 77% with the training time (0.97 s). Meanwhile, logistic Regression alone offers the fastest performance (0.35 s) with the lowest memory usage but lower accuracy (64%). This study highlights the potential of hybrid approaches to balance accuracy and computational efficiency, contributing to a better understanding of musicrelated emotional expression in Indonesian online communities.
Keywords: BERT | Emotion Classification | Hybrid Model | Indonesian Language | Traditional Machine Learning

Title: Research on the Technical Principles and Performance Verification of SoVITS Speech Synthesis Model
Abstract: In recent years, the naturalness and quality of speech generated by text-to-speech (TTS) framework based on deep learning have been greatly improved. The purpose of synthesizing understandable and natural audio from text has long been the research topic of artificial intelligence, natural language and speech processing. Aiming at the problems existing in traditional text-to-speech (TTS) technology, such as weak training ability with few samples, low naturalness of cross-language synthesis, poor controllability of emotional expression, lack of emotional expression and large amount of target speaker corpus, this paper systematically analyzes the technical framework and operating mechanism of SoVITS speech synthesis model, and focuses on the principle of its acoustic generation part. It aims to transform the emotional state of speech from one to another, while retaining the language information and the identity of the speaker. By designing multi-dimensional experiments involving few samples training and emotion control, the performance of the model is finally verified on LibriSpeech and AISHELL standard data sets, and the joint optimization goal is constructed by introducing reconstruction loss, confrontation loss and semantic alignment loss. The experimental results show that when the training sample duration is only 5 minutes, the naturalness (MOS) of SoVITS synthesized speech is 4.63, and the similarity (COS) of the embedded cosine of the speaker is 0.835. This model provides an efficient solution for the generation of speech synthesis content with low resources and few samples.
Keywords: Emotional Control | Loss Function | Self-Attention Mechanism | SoVITS | Speech Synthesis | Zero-Shot Learning

Title: ROBOAI: Real-Time Multilingual Spam Call Detection with Emotion
Abstract: Spam calls are becoming a bigger issue all around the world. Caller ID spoofing, VoIP technologies, and persuasive speech can all cause big money losses and mental health problems. Current methods of detection, such as metadata-based machine learning, static blacklists, voice-to-text NLP, and rule-based audio analysis, have only had moderate success when used with models like Naive Bayes, Decision Trees, Random Forest, SVM, LSTMand BERT. But these methods can't tell what the caller wants before the call is answered, they don't take into account prosody or emotion, they don't work well with multilingual and accented speech, and they rely on a lot of sensitive data that is processed in a single place. Also, a lot of these existing solutions are computationally high, so they might not work well on mobile devices, which need to be able to handle realtime requirements and new scam strategies that come out over time. This paper suggests a way to deal with these problems: A spam call detection system that works in real time, is aware of prosody, and protects privacy. It does this by combining short-audio analysis (unsupervised), emotion recognition, multilingual NLP, and federated learning. We use Whisper for multilingual transcription, OpenSMILE for prosodic and acoustic feature extraction, and Multilingual BERT for intent classification. The final prediction is made by combining the results of Random Forest and BiLSTM models. It runs on Android and uses Tensorflow Lite. It gets 95.6 % accuracy with 96.2% precision, 94.8 % recall, and less than 0.2. 9 seconds of latency on an offline multilingual dataset of five other languages that was used to set the confidence scores. making a ranking table Federated learning lets you update models in a decentralized way without actually sharing raw user data. This study showed that it was possible to accurately detect intent spam in real-world mobile communication while still keeping privacy using the proposed framework.
Keywords: Emotion Recognition | Federated Learning | Mobile Security | Multilingual NLP | Prosody Analysis | Real-Time Classification | Spam Call Detection | Speech Processing | TensorFlow Lite | Whisper Model

Title: Baseera: An AI-Based Sound Recognition and Visual Alert System for the Deaf
Abstract: Individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing face significant challenges in perceiving environmental sounds that are critical for safety and situational awareness. This paper presents Baseera, an intelligent sound classification system designed to detect and alert users to five high-priority auditory events: fire alarms, sirens, gunshots, car horns, and dog bark. The system follows a structured audio processing pipeline involving data preprocessing, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) feature extraction, and model evaluation using both classical machine learning algorithms - Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Random Forest (RF) - and a deep learning model based on a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN). Experimental results evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the curve (AUC), showed that while SVM achieved comparable overall test accuracy, it failed to produce valid AUC scores under a one-vs-rest setup, indicating limited reliability for multi-class sound classification. In contrast, the 1D-CNN consistently provided high accuracy (96%), balanced per-class performance, and valid AUC values across all classes (ranging from 0.73 to 0.97), demonstrating superior confidence calibration and robustness. Finally, the trained 1D-CNN was successfully deployed into a mobile application that delivers real-time visual and vibration alerts alongside a history log, demonstrating the practicality of the system in real-world scenarios and its potential to enhance safety and independence for individuals with hearing impairments.
Keywords: Accessibility for Deaf and Hard of Hearing | Assistive Technology | Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) | Environmental Sound Recognition (ESR) | MFCC | Mobile Applications

Title: Randomized Neural Network with Multiple Output Layers for Multi-label Classification
Abstract: Multi-label classification (MLC) applications span numerous real-world domains, including music annotation, medical diagnosis, and biological analysis, where instances may be associated with multiple categories simultaneously. However, MLC is a challenging problem due to imbalanced label distributions that exist in multi-label data, making accurate prediction more complicated. In this paper, we propose a Multi-Label ensemble deep Random Vector Functional Link (ML-edRVFL) framework that extends the edRVFL architecture with multiple output layers to multi-label setting by integrating three adaptive thresholding techniques and two ensemble aggregation rules. The framework is evaluated on four benchmark datasets from diverse domains. The experimental results show that the proposed ML-edRVFL models achieve competitive performance in comparison to the baseline methods.
Keywords: adaptive thresholding | edRVFL | ensemble deep learning | multi-label classification | randomized neural network

Title: Thyroid Disease Identification via EfficientNetB2: Leveraging Deep Neural Networks for Early Detection
Abstract: Hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism are thyroid diseases that can harm human health by influencing the brain, heart and ability to have children. Correctly identifying these disorders in the early stages allows patients to recover faster and gets treatment underway more efficiently. Typically, doctors order imaging and blood tests for diagnosis and each can be time-consuming and costly. It is suggested that using a modified version of EfficientNetB2 for deep learning will improve and simplify how thyroid disorders are diagnosed. The model was set up with two divisions - 0 for healthy and 1 for thyroid illness - using photos of more than 7,200 different thyroid conditions. Making some changes to the data, transforming the images, keeping them the same size and enriching it resulted in a robust model. On the assessment of thyroid illness and healthy groups, the EfficientNet B2 model performed extremely well and was accurate 90% of the time. Using a confusion matrix, loss curves and classification criteria, the performance of the model was evaluated, leading to a well-balanced strategy that helps avoid many unneeded positive or negative results. This work supports the healthcare sector by providing easy access to early detection, encouraging health care and encouraging the development of sustainable medical methods. The findings prove the instrument can detect thyroid illnesses early, as EfficientNetB2 is an automation method that runs fast and is capable of scaling up.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | deep learning | EfficientNetB2 | Thyroid disease classification

Title: The Synergy of Consumer Perception and AI Success in Driving Business Optimization
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of information and communication technology marked by the era of digitalization in various sectors, businesses are increasingly adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology to improve operational efficiency and strategic decision-making. Although many studies have explored the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on business performance and consumer behavior separately, there is still limited understanding of how consumer perceptions and AI implementation interactively affect businesses. Most existing studies tend to focus on the technical success of AI devices or on consumer trust and acceptance separately, without examining how these dimensions collectively contribute to measured business outcomes. This study investigates the influence of consumer perceptions and AI implementation on business quality, with a particular focus on the moderating role of AI implementation success. The research method used is a survey with the main instrument in the form of a questionnaire distributed to 120 employees from various companies that utilize AI technology in their companies. Consumer perceptions play a significant role in determining how innovations such as AI are accepted and trusted, which directly affects customer engagement, satisfaction, and loyalty. The implementation of AI devices - such as predictive analytics, intelligent automation, and customer service chatbots - can contribute significantly to internal communication processes and external service delivery. Of the three variables tested against Business Process Optimization, only AI Implementation Success did not show a significant effect, while AI Implementation and Employee Perception of AI were shown to have a positive and significant effect. Thus, AI Implementation does not moderate the relationship between Consumer Perception and AI Implementation on Business Optimization.
Keywords: AI Implementation | AI Success | AI Technology | Business Optimization | Consumer Perception

Title: AI Perceptions and Writing Anxiety: A Correlational Study in the Context of Academic Writing Support
Abstract: This study investigates the relationship between EFL students' perceptions and attitudes toward AI-powered writing tools and their writing anxiety in the context of academic writing. As AI writing tools become increasingly integrated into higher education, understanding their psychological impact on students - particularly regarding writing anxiety - has become essential. The study aims to determine whether students' positive perceptions of these tools correlate with reduced anxiety during academic writing tasks. A quantitative correlational research design was employed. Forty-two undergraduate students in Yogyakarta, Indonesia participated in the study. Participants were selected using purposive sampling, ensuring prior experience with AI writing tools and enrollment in an academic writing course. Data were collected using two validated instruments: a self-developed AI Perception and Attitudes Scale based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and the Second Language Writing Anxiety Inventory (SLWAI). Descriptive statistics, normality testing, and both Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses were conducted using SPSS. Findings revealed that while students generally held positive views toward AI writing tools, there was no statistically significant correlation between AI perceptions/attitudes and writing anxiety levels (Pearson r=-0.211, p=0.180; Spearman's ρ=-0.195, p=0.216). The results suggest that although AI tools are perceived as helpful for writing performance, they do not necessarily reduce the emotional or psychological barriers associated with writing. The study recommends integrating AI tools with pedagogical strategies that explicitly address writing anxiety to support students more holistically in academic writing contexts.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | EFL | perceptions | Technology Acceptance Model | writing anxiety

Title: A Multifaceted Approach Based on Deep Learning Architectures for Dysarthric Speech Recognition
Abstract: Dysarthric speech presents significant challenges to effective communication and overall quality of life. Traditional diagnostic methods are often subjective and time-consuming, limiting both the accuracy and efficiency of detecting this condition. In response, this study proposes a novel automated system for dysarthric speech recognition, designed to improve diagnostic precision and timeliness. The proposed system adopts a comprehensive framework that integrates advanced signal processing techniques, robust feature extraction methods, and cutting-edge deep learning architectures. Multiple acoustic features, including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients 'MFCCs' and Power-Normalized Cepstral Coefficients 'PNCCs', are extracted to capture detailed characteristics of the speech signal. Additionally, speech enhancement algorithms such as Minimum Mean Square Error 'MMSE' based noise reduction are applied to improve input quality, especially under noisy conditions. At the core of the system lies a deep learning model combining Convolutional Neural Networks 'CNNs' with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory 'BiLSTM' networks. This architecture effectively captures both local and temporal dependencies within speech signals. To further enhance performance, the Connectionist Temporal Classification 'CTC' approach is incorporated for word level recognition in dysarthric speech. CTC is particularly beneficial in speech recognition tasks as it enables training sequence to sequence models without requiring strict alignment between input features and output labels. The system's performance has been thoroughly evaluated on the UASpeech dataset, showing notable effectiveness in handling speech with low intelligibility.
Keywords: CTC | deep learning architectures | dysarthric speech recognition | MFCC | PNCC

Title: Efficient and Privacy-Preserving Spoken Language Understanding for Resource-Constrained Microcontroller Unit
Abstract: Speech input is increasingly adopted as an intuitive interface for various embedded mobile devices. Cloud-based solutions provide powerful speech language understanding (SLU) capabilities but introduce privacy risks, as sensitive information may be processed remotely. To address these concerns, disentanglement-based encoders have been developed to strip sensitive data from audio signals, allowing SLU without compromising privacy. However, such encoders are often memory-intensive and computationally demanding, limiting their practicality on resource-constrained devices. Based on extensive experiments, this paper observes a key phenomenon: SLU relies on global information from the entire sentence, whereas the recognition of privacy-sensitive words predominantly depends on local information. We implemented simple encoder designed for efficient privacy-preserving SLU offloading (SILENCE) on an STM32H7 microcontroller and evaluated its performance under various privacy threat scenarios. Results demonstrate that SILENCE provides competitive speech intent classification accuracy and privacy protection compared to more complex encoders. Simultaneously, it achieves a speedup of up to 53.3 times and a reduction in memory footprint by 134.1 times, marking the first time that privacy-preserving SLU services have been realized on a microcontroller with only 1 MB of memory.
Keywords: memory efficient | microcontroller unit | privacy-preserving | resource-constrained devices | speech intent classification | spoken language understanding (SLU) | 内存优化 | 微控制单元 | 语音意图提取 | 语音语言理解(SLU) | 资源受限终端 | 隐私保护

Title: AQGSM: Efficient Multimodal AVQA via Ensemble Transformer Optimization
Abstract: Audio-Visual Question Answering (AVQA) requires reasoning across the interdependencies of the audio and visual modalities, therefore, making the task more challenging than the traditional Visual Question Answering (VQA). Current architectures such as the Collective QuestionGuided Network (CQGN) can perform well on benchmark tasks such as MUSICAVQA; however, these systems are hindered by redundancy in question generation and large computation costs. In response to the short-comings, we propose an augmented CQGN architecture with an Adaptive Question Generation and Selection Module (AQGSM). It is a module that applies an ensemble of transformer encoders, namely, DeBERTa-v3-base, RoBERTa-base, ELECTRA-base, and BERT-base, with the weight of 0.28, 0.25, 0.24, and 0.23 respectively, to make use of context-sensitive question generation and selection.Image representations are acquired through the CLIP ViT-B/32 encoder, whereas audio representations are acquired through Wav2Vec 2.0, and the two modalities are then combined in a multimodal integration component.With a systematic hyperparameter search on a 45,000 instance AVQA corpus, the weighted ensemble accuracy is 93.24 percentage on the validation split, and the expected performance can be improved to 94.7 percent with additional optimization. Additionally, the architecture has lowered inference time to 0.65s/batch.These findings imply an improved efficiency, scalability, and usability over baseline systems like CQGN (77 per cent accuracy) and the MAV-LLM/LAVA pipelines.
Keywords: Adaptive Question Generation | Audio-Visual Question Answering (AVQA) | BERT | DeBERTa-v3 | ELECTRA | Multimodal Fusion | Multimodal Learning | RoBERTa | Transformer Ensemble

Title: Improving ViT Performance for Colon Cancer Histopathological Image Classification Using Transfer Learning
Abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized medical image analysis, particularly the automatic classification of histopathology images. Vision Transformers (ViTs) now surpass convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in modeling long-range dependencies and capturing global features. However, when initialized with random weights, ViTs often struggle to adapt to the varying scales and morphologies of tumor tissues, resulting in suboptimal performance. Transfer learning addresses this challenge by pretraining the model on large datasets to obtain a stronger weight initialization before fine-tuning on the target domain. This strategy has proven especially effective for histology image classification. In this study, we fine-tuned a ViT-B/16 model pretrained on ImageNet-21k by first training it on 75,000 Renal Cell Carcinoma (RCC) patches and then applying it to classify colon tumor subtypes in the Chaoyang dataset. Our proposed method achieves an accuracy of 87.14 %, a precision of 83.59 %, a recall of 82.08 % and an F1 score of 82.77 %, outperforming both a model trained from scratch and one pretrained only on ImageNet. These results underscore the value of domain-specific pretraining for enhancing ViT performance on diverse tumor morphologies in histopathology classification tasks.
Keywords: Colon tumor subtype classification | Deep learning | Histopathology image classification | Transfer learning | Vision Transformer

Title: Research on the Construction Technology of Electric Energy Metering Big Model and Intelligent Agent
Abstract: With the rapid development of smart grid technology, the demand for high precision, real-time performance, and adaptive capability in the field of energy metering is becoming increasingly prominent. This study focuses on the construction of large-scale models and intelligent agents in the field of electric energy metering, and proposes an intelligent metering framework that integrates multimodal data and deep learning technology. By integrating power quality parameters such as voltage, current, harmonic content, as well as multi-source heterogeneous data such as environmental variables and equipment status, a hybrid architecture model based on Transformer and Graph Neural Network (GNN) was constructed to achieve dynamic error prediction and anomaly detection of energy metering data. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the model in harmonic distortion rate prediction task reaches 98.2<sup>%</sup>, which is 21.4% higher than traditional methods. At the same time, it can accurately identify low-frequency anomalies (recall rate 92.3%), verifying its robustness in complex working conditions.
Keywords: Anomaly detection | Deep learning | electricity metering | Intelligent agents | Large model | load forecasting

Title: Predictive Acoustic Analysis of the Graha Medika Ballroom: A Comparative Study of Ecotect Simulation and the Sabine Method
Abstract: Multipurpose spaces, such as the Graha Medika Ballroom at Brawijaya University, face unique acoustic challenges as they must accommodate conflicting reverberation time (RT60) requirements for both speech and music. A research gap exists in the lack of predictive acoustic analysis for this specific ballroom at the design stage. This study, therefore, aims to analyze and predict the space's acoustic performance, focusing on two key parameters: reverberation time and the risk of acoustic defects. The primary focus is on evaluating the RT60 and potential acoustic defects based on the interior design. The methodology used is a quantitative approach comparing digital simulation via Autodesk Ecotect with manual calculation using the classical Sabine method for verification. The simulation yielded an RT60 of 1.52 seconds, while manual calculation gave 1.74 seconds at 500 Hz. This slight difference confirms the validity of both methods, as both results fall within the ideal range. Geometric analysis also revealed no significant acoustic defects, indicating even sound distribution. In conclusion, this ballroom has good acoustic quality for its various functions, especially vocal activities and light music. For further optimization and to align with modern technological trends, a hybrid model combining traditional simulations with machine learning is recommended for more efficient acoustic prediction and dynamic design improvement. We also recommend adding carpet in the stage area and optimizing acoustics in the entrance and behind the ceiling.
Keywords: Acoustic | Ballroom | Ecotect Simulation | Interior Design | Sabine Method

Title: Deep Transfer Learning for Poultry Disease Classification: A Case Study with EfficientNetB3
Abstract: Poultry rearing is a significant food safety and economic stability factor especially among the small to medium sized farmers in the developing nations. However, timeliness and effective diagnosis of chicken illnesses has been the biggest issue because the number of veterinary practitioners and diagnostic centers remains low. The current paper aims at automating the process of detecting the chicken diseases through a deep learning algorithm used on the fecal image image analysis. The data was compiled into an annotated set of 8,067 fecal images (6,453 of which are training images) and 807 validation images and 807 test images. The model applied in this study is the EfficientNetB3 algorithm that has been famous in providing the best balance between performance and computation efficiency. The model was able to achieve the impressive 98% accuracy on test set through extensive training and optimization and had the potential to be a valuable instrument in the diagnosis of disease. This is a technology-driven approach that can be used to provide early diagnosis and prompt treatment, resulting in the improved health of animals, food security and economic growth. Furthermore, sustainable agriculture, responsible consumption and production, and heightened resilience of agricultural systems are other features that such technology promotes - the goal that is consistent with global ambitions to achieve zero hunger, good health and well-being, and industrialization towards innovation.
Keywords: EfficientNetB3 | Fecal image classification | Poultry disease diagnosis | Sustainable livestock management

Title: DeepBindPharma: A Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework with Cross-Attention Integration for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction
Abstract: This study presents DeepBindPharma, an innovative deep learning framework for drug-target affinity prediction. DeepBindPharma integrates multi-modal feature representations, including sequence-based, graph-based, and n-gram features of compounds and proteins, to overcome limitations of existing structure-based and non-structure-based methods. The framework employs four specialized channels: SynapseNet with dilated convolutions for SMILES sequence analysis, Hierarchical Graph Convolutional Network for molecular graph feature extraction, Parallel-Conv Fusion Architecture for multi-scale protein sequence modeling, and Generic Deep Net for processing n-gram protein features. A Cross-Attention Module dynamically balances feature weights between compounds and proteins, mitigating prediction bias. Evaluated on Davis and KIBA datasets, DeepBindPharma outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a 3.54% reduction in MSE, 0.9% improvement in CI, and 1.29% higher correlation index. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each component, particularly the role of Cross-Attention Module in modeling interactions. While demonstrating robustness in five-fold cross-validation, the framework shows slight performance drops on unseen compound-protein pairs, highlighting generalization challenges. This work advances computational drug discovery by unifying diverse biomolecular representations through an interpretable, scalable architecture.
Keywords: Cross-Attention Module | Deep Learning Framework | Drug-Target Affinity | Hierarchical Graph Convolutional Network | Multi-modal Feature Integration

Title: Maximizing Speech Denoising Effectiveness with CNNs: A Focus on Key Architectural Strategies
Abstract: Audio signal denoising is important in speech enhancement. Most traditional methods cannot remove noises thoroughly and models proposed recently still achieve poor performance in denoising under low SNR conditions. This paper proposed a model whose speech denoising performance is higher than that of most models. The model is based on convolutional neural network and is added several strategies to improve its metrics. The importance of strategies like residual connection, batch normalization, Dropout regularization and "encoder-decoder"processing mode in the model is illustrated in the paper. The metrics used in the paper is MSE, SNR, PESQ and STOI. Studies show that the proposed model performs better in the four metrics and over-high or over-low Dropout ratios can affect the performance negatively.
Keywords: deep learning | regularization | residual connection | speech denoising

Title: Dynamic Backdoor Attack Based on Multiscale Local Binary Pattern
Abstract: The data security and integrity of deep learning model is very important. Backdoor attack poses a serious challenge to the security of deep learning system because of its concealment and destructiveness. Most of the existing backdoor attacks rely on static triggers and are easy to be detected by pattern analysis methods. This paper proposes a dynamic backdoor attack (lbpdba) based on multi-scale local binary pattern (LBP). In this method, LBP is used to extract the multi-scale texture features of the image, and the features of different scales are weighted by information entropy to generate dynamic triggers that change with the input image, so as to improve the concealment and adaptability of backdoor attacks. Experiments are carried out on cifar-10 and tiny Imagenet datasets. The results show that compared with badnets, blended and blind methods, lbpdba not only performs better in attack success rate, but also has less impact on the normal performance of the model. In addition, lbpdba can effectively circumvent the mainstream defense methods such as strip and spectre, showing strong concealment and robustness, and providing reference for the research of more effective defense methods.
Keywords: backdoor attack | deep learning security | dynamic trigger | Local Binary Pattern | stealthiness

Title: Comparative Evaluation of Tabnet and Deep Learning Models for Chronic Kidney Disease Diagnosis: Enhancing Interpretability and Predictive Accuracy
Abstract: This study compares TabNet with other deep learning models, including Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), for diagnosing chronic kidney disease (CKD). The work aims to enhance both prediction performance and model interpretability in clinical diagnosis. CKD advances quietly, and hence detection becomes challenging early in the course of the disease using traditional methods such as GFR, creatinine levels, and urinalysis, particularly in wide-ranging patient populations. Machine learning algorithms, implemented across varying datasets - such as clinical, laboratory, and patient data - improve diagnostic specificity. While DNNs and CNNs identify intricate non-linear patterns, interpretability restricts their application in high-risk medical judgments. As opposed to that, TabNet, designed for tabular data, employs sequential attention to mark salient features while deciding, with transparency and accuracy. The data set analysis has shown that Tab Net achieved 94 % which is higher than the existing CNN and DNN algorithms. The research emphasizes TabNet's edge in providing interpretable decision paths, highly important for clinical trust and use. By comparing such models, this paper offers insights into the selection of proper diagnostic instruments, facilitating personalized treatment planning, and the development of explainable AI in nephrology.
Keywords: Chronic Kidney Disorder | Convolutional Neural Networks | Deep Neural Networks | Healthcare Analytics | TabNet

Title: Student Depression Prediction: A Multimodal Machine Learning Approach
Abstract: In today's world, Depression among students has been a critical mental health concern that substantially impacts desired outcomes, productivity, and overall human well-being. Traditional diagnostic instruments involve conventional medical tools, classical diagnostic apparatus, or conventional diagnostic equipment such as the PHQ-9 questionnaire provide effective clinical measures but lack of ease of use in digital-first environments. This paper put forward a plan for multimedia machine learning (ML) framework that integrates behavioral features (mobility, smartphone usage, sleeping patterns) and other feature like linguistics features (related to language text contents from essays and posts on social medias) to estimate depression. A dataset of 820 university students was taken and compared with PHQ-9 scores as ground truth labels. Hereby the functioning of models including BERT, RoBERT, Random Forest, Logistic Regression and a Fusion Ensemble was evaluated. Outcomes show that the fusion approach outperforms unimodal baselines, which brings to a successful conclusion with a veracity of 86% and and of 0.91. Thereafter we give out interpretability results using SHAP, drawing attention to the most influential predictors of depression.
Keywords: BERT | KEY PHRASES- Student depression | machine learning | multimodal learning | PHQ-9 | RoBERTa | SHAP | SMOTE

Title: Exploring the Perceptions of Indian Business Students on the Effective Use of Technology to Enhance Entrepreneurial Intention
Abstract: This paper explores the views of Indian business students on the use of technology to improve their entrepreneurial intention. The study used a qualitative approach and collected data using semi-structured interviews with twenty business students from different institutions in India. It was found that Indian business students positively perceive the application of technology in education and consider it a significant instrument for the improvement of their learning experience and performance, an application that provides diverse advantages, among which include the availability of various resources, motivation, and flexibility in learning. However, barriers have equally been advanced toward effective usage of technology in education, such as inadequacy in its provision, poor Internet connectivity, and technical support.Some participants also feared the possible negative impact of too much technology on the traditional methods of teaching. The study, therefore, advocates that the best way to effectively integrate technology in education is by adopting a total or holistic approach that takes into consideration both students' needs and preferences and all infrastructure and support systems requirements for its usage.This study moves one step further toward better understanding Indian business students' perceptions of and actual usage of technology tools in their educational experiences. It provides an out-of-the-box view regarding the context of India. Policymakers, educators, and technology providers can use this study to create and sustain environments wherein learning is enhanced owing to increased technology use.

Title: Finger Flow: Empowering ASL Communication through Convolutional-Bidirectional LSTM Hybrid Model
Abstract: It is a complex deep learning model framework of analyzing sequential input logically based on the use of convolutional, bilateral, and dense layers on the input sequence of the American Sign Language. The model reveals the massive learning capacity that can identify finer details of patterns in sequential information by taking into account 58 million factors. The convolutional layers are more competent in adding hierarchical features using the bidirectional LSTm to fully topicalize a model and the dense layers to add further alteration. By using the Adam Optimizer with a learning rate of 1e-3, the model demonstrates adaptive learning, which is more important in optimizing the changes in the parameters in the course of training. The virtual model was able to perform exceptionally with more than 20 epochs and mean loss of 0.0065% with a 99 plus accuracy. Accurate testing implies maximum high performance and adjustment to a broad assortment of sequential data workloads. The proposed design comes out as a powerful instrument in enhancing the prospect of deep learning in processing sequence information, and is making an enormous contribution to the ever-growing developments of sophisticated neural network structures.
Keywords: Adam Optimizer | Adaptive Learning | Dense Layers | Hierarchical Feature Extraction | Learning Rate | Loss Function | Model Evaluation | Sequential Data Processing

Title: Tensions and risks in the platformization of public schools in the state of Paraná, Brazil
Abstract: This paper explores the tensions and risks associated with the platformization of public education, focusing on the integration of AI-based digital platforms in basic education in Brazil. Drawing on a critical perspective informed by the literature on educational technology and teacher professionalism, the study examines how the implementation of adaptive learning systems affects the role and working conditions of teachers. The study is based on an analysis of empirical data collected in two public schools in the state of Paraná, Brazil. The Paraná state school system was the first in Brazil to implement the mandatory use of a wide range of digital platforms in basic education. The findings reveal a precarization of teaching work, manifested in the loss of professional autonomy, an increasing workload, and a drastic shift in pedagogical functions toward technical tasks associated with data management. Furthermore, it is observed that EdTech platforms, managed in this case by the government of Paraná, have become instruments of educational governance, reinforcing a model of teacher accountability based on performance metrics and diminishing the space for pedagogical judgment. The paper argues that this transformation challenges fundamental dimensions of education, raising urgent questions about the future of teaching in the age of algorithmic automation.
Keywords: adaptative learning | artificial intelligence | Edtechs | teacher precariousness | teacher role

Title: AI-Driven Simulation and Digital Twin Technologies for Smart Business Planning
Abstract: This research paper explores the intersections between AI-based simulation and digital twin technologies to make intelligent business plans in intelligent business predictive maintenance, process optimization, and decision-making. The concept of a digital twin is developed on four machine learning models, namely- Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and gradual Boosting Machine (GBM) trained on a data set consisting of real-time and historical data of IoT connected industrial equipment such as CNC milling machines. The data include sensor measurements, SCADA data, maintenance data, manufacturing statistics, and environmental data, which are exposed to preprocessing techniques such as noise reduction, missing value filling, normalizing and feature engineering. The models are analysed based on their performance in terms of precision, recall, F1-score, accuracy, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and R2. ANN is the best of the other models with most predictive reliability and accuracy and has highest operations cost saving (22.7) and energy savings (25.6). GBM comes second as it is dependent on boosting mechanisms to make better predictions. RF has the most favorable trade-off between level of accuracy and efficiency. SVM has the worst performance since it is very sensitive to hyperparameter tuning and non-linearity. The findings determine the capabilities of AI-based digital twins to minimize downtime, decrease maintenance costs, and improve industrial processes. The analysis reveals that ANN can be the most suitable model of predictive analytics and business intelligence that are provided in real-time and, therefore, AI-based digital twins are the valuable instrument of industrial automation in the future. The next round of research might explore the field of hybrid AI methods to improve predictive capability and efficiency in smart manufacturing and optimization of business processes.
Keywords: AI-driven digital twin | industrial automation | machine learning models | predictive maintenance | smart business planning

Title: Temporal Multimodal Memory Banks for Agentic Reasoning
Abstract: Current multimodal AI agents process inputs in isolation, lacking the ability to maintain and reason over episodic memories across extended time horizons. We introduce ChronoMem<sup>1</sup><sup>1</sup>https://github.com/TransformerTitan/ChronoMem, a novel architecture that enables agents to store, consolidate, and retrieve multimodal experiences for enhanced temporal reasoning. ChronoMem employs hier-archical memory encoding, cross-modal temporal indexing, and experience-guided retrieval to capture temporal dependencies across visual, audio, and textual modalities. Through comprehensive evaluation on three adapted public benchmark tasks spanning navigation (AVLMaps), human interaction (MTPChat), and scientific assistance (RVTALL), we demonstrate that ChronoMem achieves consistent but modest improvements over memory-augmented baselines: 3.3% average improvement in long-term task performance compared to extended context methods and 3.7% better memory retrieval accuracy compared to systems without persistent memory. Our work addresses fundamental limitations in current agentic systems and provides a principled approach for incorporating episodic memory into mul-timodal AI agents.
Keywords: Adaptive agents | Agentic systems | Benchmark evaluation | Cross-modal indexing | Episodic memory | Experience retrieval | Hierarchical memory encoding | Human-AI interaction | Long-term memory | Memory consolidation | Multimodal AI agents | Multimodal experiences | Navigation tasks | Scientific assistance | Temporal Multimodal Memory Banks (TMMB) | Temporal reasoning

Title: Multimodal Datasets for Studying Expert Performances of Musical Scores
Abstract: In many musical styles, performing a piece of music means to produce an ‘interpretation’ of a score. This interpretation involves performers manipulating musical parameters such as timing, dynamics, timbre, and pitch to communicate their artistic conception of the piece, often to an audience. Much previous research into musical interpretations has examined aspects of expressive performance strategies. However, these studies have largely focused solely on the sounds produced in the performance, investigating players’ manipulation of musical parameters but little of the performance’s broader context and impact. Multimodal datasets, which contain multiple diverse data types offering distinct perspectives on the musical performance (e.g. audio, Musical Instrument Digital Interface, video, motion capture, physiological data), can support more holistic cross- and interdisciplinary study of performers’ interpretative decision-making and its effects on audiences. We propose a taxonomy of modalities relevant to the study of musicians’ interpretations of musical scores. These modalities are distinct facets of the performance or its context through which the performance and musical interpretation can be analysed (e.g. ‘venue acoustics’, ‘performer movements’, ‘performance sound’). We use this taxonomy to systematically review relevant open-access multimodal datasets and the modalities they support. Underrepresented modalities are then highlighted, along with practical suggestions for including data that support these modalities in future datasets. We next examine key challenges of reporting and working with multimodal datasets, emphasising the need for standardisation of data reporting and reliable options for data storage and access. Finally, we summarise the broader interdisciplinary applications of these datasets in artificial intelligence and performance research.
Keywords: dataset standardisation | expressive performance | interpretation | multimodal datasets | music performance | performance analysis

Title: Performance Analysis of Deep Learning-Based Direction Finding in the High-Frequency Band
Abstract: This study comparatively analyzes the performance of the traditional MUSIC algorithm and the deep learning-based CNN for direction finding, particularly for multiple HF band signals. Simulations in environments characterized by complex noise, and additionally by frequency variations and multipath effects, reveal that MUSIC's RMSE significantly increases under low SNR conditions, whereas CNN consistently exhibits lower errors. Furthermore, while MUSIC's RMSE rises with increasing separation angles of the input signals, CNN maintains stable performance. These findings indicate that CNN overcomes grid-based resolution limitations, achieving optimal estimation performance by closely approaching the CRLB under diverse conditions.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network | deep learning | Direction finding | HF band | Multiple-Signal Classification

Title: YOShI: YOLO-ODARIS Ship-Detection Interface-An Innovative Approach to On-Board Data Analysis for Ship-Detection
Abstract: The rapid growth of the demand for low-latency information about time-critical events in the field of remote sensing has become a major focus in the aerospace sector. One solution to this demand, is the possibility to extract key information through automated data analysis on-board the satellite. The availability of state-of-The-Art AI-based tools has strongly catalysed the development of such systems. Within this context, the German Aerospace Center (DLR) develops an "On-Board Data Analysis And Real-Time Information System"with ship-detection used as a reference application for AI-based on-board object detection. Despite this large sector, there is no available standard approach for image processing and data handling in this field of application. As a result, the "Yolo-Odaris Ship-Detection Interface"is proposed for on-board ship-detection suitable for small-to mid-sized satellites with low on-board processing and optical instrument performance.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | image processing | odaris | on-board data handling | on-board data processing | quality of service | remote sensing | ship-detection | software development | system architecture | yolo | yoshi

Title: The Great Coral Reef: Modular AI/ML Task Acceleration for Onboard Data Processing
Abstract: As space missions grow increasingly complex, On-board Data Processing (OBDP) has become essential for enabling autonomy in spacecraft and robotic systems. The growing need for real-Time navigation, terrain analysis, anomaly detection, and adaptive operations makes high-performance, efficient onboard computing a critical requirement. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) offer powerful solutions, but conventional space-qualified processors remain limited in flexibility, power efficiency, and computational throughput.To address these challenges, we introduce The Great Coral Reef, a modular AI acceleration platform that aggregates multiple Google Coral Edge TPUs under a central scheduler to deliver scalable, reconfigurable, and fault-Tolerant onboard inference. The architecture supports parallel workloads, dynamic reassignment under node failure, and power gating for energy efficiency, while maintaining graceful degradation when hardware fails.We validated this approach using the Euclid Early Release Observations (ERO) dataset, extending ESA's reference scripts into a full ML-ready cutout pipeline. Across 20 Euclid VIS and NISP fields, the system generated ~97,000 cutouts, of which 44,987 high-quality samples trained FW-1, a multi-Task convolutional neural network (CNN) that jointly classified astrophysical objects (stars, galaxies, black holes/AGN, gravitational lenses, weak shear patterns, clusters, anomalies) and predicted a composite quality score. The model reached 92.87% accuracy with mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.11. Scaling to ~220,000 cutouts from Euclid, JWST, and HST, FW-2 achieved 95.82% training accuracy and consistently maintained >90% generalization across unseen validation sets, demonstrating cross-instrument portability.Deployment on Coral Edge TPUs sustained ~49,800 cutouts per second at 0.020 ms latency per cutout, with steady-state power consumption near 3.2W per TPU. Thermal management and hardware attrition revealed the fragility of consumer-grade accelerators, yet the scheduler-based design preserved progress through failures and enabled heterogeneous support, including Apple M-series Neural Engines.These results demonstrate that architecture-first modular AI acceleration is a viable path toward next-generation OBDP, with the Coral Reef offering an efficient, fault-Tolerant, and extensible testbed for real-Time scientific processing. While not yet space-ready, this first experimental campaign highlights the importance of scheduler-driven fault tolerance, thermal design, and cross-platform portability in building resilient onboard intelligence for future missions.

Title: ACKurate-DQN: Adaptive Throughput-Based Congestion Control Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: ACKurate-DQN is a Deep Q-Network (DQN) TCP controller that replaces hand-tuned Additive Increase, Multiplicative Decrease (AIMD) logic with a single, scale-invariant reward. A lightweight dual-mode estimator tracks the path's throughput ceiling, and the agent automatically balances throughput and delay to maximize performance, without manual weight tuning. In ns-3 dumbbell-topology tests, ACKurate-DQN sustains more than 95% link utilization and RTT comparable to a recent DQN-AIMD baseline across both static links and a bandwidth-shift scenario with a fixed RTT. This ceiling-aware feedback stabilizes learning and enables more robust operation than existing DQN-based AIMD methods.
Keywords: adaptive throughput estimation | deep Q-network | reinforcement learning | TCP congestion control

Title: FastAFPN: Infrared Surgical Navigation with Adaptive Fusion for Reflective Sphere Localization
Abstract: To resolve environmental noise interference, low localization accuracy, and poor real-time performance in 3D reflective sphere recognition for infrared optical surgical navigation, this paper proposes FastAFPN - a novel detection network integrating a progressive feature pyramid and adaptive fusion mechanism. The method reconstructs YOLOv8n's backbone by replacing its C2f module's Bottleneck with FasterBlock to enhance dynamic feature extraction, and designs an Adaptive Feature Pyramid Network (AFPN) with ASFF-weighted fusion that optimizes cross-scale feature integration while suppressing noise. These innovations significantly improve multi-scale spherical target detection, particularly for small objects. Experimental results demonstrate 96.2% recognition accuracy with real-time efficiency, providing an effective solution for high-precision localization in surgical navigation systems.
Keywords: deep learning | infrared surgical navigation | target identification | target location

Title: AW-BF-MSR: An Image Enhancement Method Based on MSR by Adding BF and AW Module
Abstract: With the rapid development of image processing and deep learning, as raw data for model input, the image dataset's quality can affect the performance of model segmentation, recognition and object detection. For problems such as uneven lighting and low brightness in images, image enhancement techniques are needed to highlight the features of target objects in the image. On the basis of MSR (Multi-Scale Retinex) algorithm, an improved image enhancement method for different fields is proposed in this paper. Firstly, convert the image to be processed to HSI space and extract the I component of the image; Then, when extracting the reflection component using the MSR algorithm, BF (Bilateral Filtering) is introduced; Finally, to address the issue of manually setting weights for multi-scale merging, image information entropy is introduced to adaptively calculate the weight W<inf>k</inf>. The enhanced I component is obtained by multi-scale merging, and the final enhanced image is obtained by merging it with the H and S components. By conducting experiments on images in fields of transportation, industry and power transmission, and comparing them subjectively and objectively with other algorithms, the enhancement effect and universality of the proposed algorithm are verified, which can provide high-quality input data for subsequent image recognition, tracking and understanding.
Keywords: adaptive weighting | bilateral filtering | image enhancement | MSR algorithm | multiple application fields

Title: Chroma Features Based Music Genre Classification Using Machine and Deep Learning Algorithms
Abstract: This study investigates the efficacy of various machine learning and deep learning models for automated music genre classification. Utilizing the GTZAN dataset, a comprehensive collection of audio features was extracted and preprocessed, including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Chroma features, Spectral Centroid, Root Mean Square (RMS), and Spectral Bandwidth. The dataset, comprising 3-second audio segments, was used to train and evaluate K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Decision Tree, Random Forest, and a custom-built Deep Neural Network (DNN). A comparative analysis of model performance, supported by accuracy metrics and confusion matrices, reveals the strengths and limitations of each approach in distinguishing between ten distinct music genres. The findings underscore the importance of robust feature engineering and appropriate model selection for accurate Music Information Retrieval (MIR) tasks, highlighting areas were acoustic similarities challenge classification algorithms.
Keywords: Chroma Features | Deep Neural Network | GTZAN | Music Genre Classification | Music Information Retrieval (MIR)

Title: A Lightweight CNN-based Explainable Approach for Potato Disease Detection with Deep Evaluation Metrics
Abstract: The potato is a major staple food crop across the globe; it plays an important part in food security and sustaining agricultural economies. Potato disease is very dangerous to yield loss when the potato plant infected with diseases like early blight, late blight, etc., as this could cause huge losses when not detected and identified earlier enough. The assessment of diseases is still a manual process performed by agronomists and this approach is slow, inconsistent, and not practical for assessing disease for commercial scale monitoring. This research describes the development of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for the automatic classification of potato leaf disease into early blight, late blight, or healthy. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 98.38%, and does not suffer from degradation in performance having used a lightweight architecture. The model was assessed beyond accuracy; precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix and ROC-AUC curves were used to assess performance, providing a more comprehensive insight into performance for each class. Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) was used to aid the interpretability of the CNN by highlighting regions of the leaf image relative to disease, reminding us of the role and impact of explainable AI (XAI) in agricultural disease detection. Overall, findings indicated that the CNN was accurate, efficient, and had trust; a good proposition for a real-world precision agriculture harvest technology.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) | Explainable AI (XAI) | Grad-CAM | Potato disease detection | Precision agriculture

Title: Intelligent expert system fault diagnosis based on PCA-SPE-CNN classifier
Abstract: Centrifugal compressors are widely used in the oil and natural gas industry for gas compression, reinjection, and transportation. To address the challenges of the difficult separation of data anomalies from equipment failures and limited knowledge acquisition from expert knowledge bases, this article proposes a dynamic fault diagnosis method for centrifugal compressor expert systems, combining convolutional neural networks (CNN) and principal component analysis for statistical process monitoring (PCA-SPE). Realize the combination of expert knowledge and instrument data, and break through the weak links in existing petrochemical instrument safety monitoring technology and traditional expert systems. The method has been validated using process data from centrifugal compressors. The results demonstrate that the method achieved 100% classification accuracy for two types of faults: non-starting of the drive machine and excessively low oil pressure. Combined with the expert system, it reached a satisfactory diagnostic performance.
Keywords: Centrifugal compressor | Condition monitoring | Deep learning | Expert system | Fault diagnosis

Title: Harnessing Legacy Air Platforms Data with NLP for AI Training
Abstract: Challenge of using different test environments in previously developed air platforms is a major obstacle for testing avionics. To train an AI, useful set of data is required. However, every platform has different environment, data and test sets, which are specifically created for specific platform and specific requirements. Since every platform creates distinct test sets, every platform uses same type of test cases and procedures, useful set of data will be increased. This paper introduces novel approach to address challenges to collect relevant data in legacy platforms using in-house developed agents and automated verification software. Aselsan Avionics Verification Communication and Identification Instrument (AVCII) will use legacy platforms' data to create test cases automatically. AVCII parses system requirements and models according to requirement standards with NLP and match with ICD attributes in legacy platforms to create test cases automatically. Tester has configuration field in the software for additional considerations such as test environment configuration, time, resolution and asynchronous continuous tests execution for performance requirements. This way, test cases in legacy platforms are standardized and unified. Additionally, database is utilized to store all system design, development and verification data to feed knowledge database. Structural coverage analysis is also performed after test case generation. After structural coverage analysis, it is seen that %85 requirements are completely covered by test cases for modern platforms, which is higher than previous automated test case generation studies [1] due to strict rules in development and requirement verification in aviation platforms which are used in our study. Additional test cases and procedures were created for achieving complete coverage. Only requirement coverage is aimed in test generation, thus no action is taken for defensive code analysis. Process is repeated for remaining legacy platforms. Then, interface control documents, requirements, test cases and test results of old platforms fed into AI-Based Next Generation Test Tool for training.
Keywords: AI Training | Legacy Systems Reusability | NLP

Title: Automatic Beatmap Generation in Web-Based Rhythm Games: A Systematic Literature Review
Abstract: Rhythm games rely on beatmaps that translate music into interactive visual and timing patterns. Manual beatmap creation is labor-intensive and requires expert knowledge, prompting research into automatic beatmap generation (ABG) to improve scalability and accessibility. This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of 21 studies concerning ABG with an emphasis on web-based deployment. The review identifies the main objectives of prior systems, reducing authoring time, maintaining playability, and supporting educational or cultural purposes. It also summarizes the user-experience (UX) features and algorithmic techniques employed, including rule-based, signal-processing, data-driven, and hybrid models. Efficiency factors such as latency, runtime performance, and browser compatibility are analyzed to evaluate feasibility for real-time interaction on heterogeneous devices. Findings indicate that lightweight and constraint-aware approaches, when combined with optimized deep-learning inference, can achieve human-like playability in browser environments. The study concludes with research directions toward standardized datasets, web-native evaluation benchmarks, and broader integration of traditional and folk-music repertoires in rhythm-game applications.
Keywords: automatic beatmap generation | music information retrieval | rhythm games | systematic literature review | web-based system

Title: Deep Analysis of MFCC, LPC, MEL Spectrogram, and Weighted Features to Classify Stuttered and Non-Stuttered Speech
Abstract: Speech serves as the verbal tool for expressing thoughts, ideas, and emotions, and is essential for human interaction. Stuttering is a speech disorder that impacts millions of individuals worldwide. The determination of whether an individual stutters or does not stutter is conducted through assessments in Speech Language Pathology (SLP). Traditionally, this evaluation involved manually counting the instances of stuttering within speech to classify individuals as either stutterers or non-stutterers. Therefore, the process is time-consuming and susceptible to mistakes. Stuttering speech recognition has been a well-focused area of study within speech signal processing for researchers in recent decades. The present research focuses on identifying stuttered and fluent speech and highlighting its performance in deep learning methodologies. This study examines an in-depth evaluation of the CNN & Bi-LSTM model utilizing MFCC, LPC, and MEL spectrogram features. Additionally, the weighted features of these have also been evaluated by our deep learning methods for the classification of stuttered and fluent speech. A comparison has been carried out on the efficiency achieved from the CNN & Bi-LSTM models utilizing different types of features. Research indicates that the CNN model achieves an impressive accuracy rate of 92% compared to the Bi-LSTM model when utilizing weighted MFCC.
Keywords: Bi-LSTM | CNN | feature extraction methods | SLP | Stuttering

Title: Face-to-Tune: Music Suggestions from Facial Cues
Abstract: Music recommendation systems significantly enhance user experiences by providing content tailored to individual preferences. This study introduces a framework that integrates facial recognition with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze emotions in real time. The proposed system automates music playback by detecting the user’s emotional state through facial expressions and selecting suitable songs, eliminating the need for manual intervention. The system detects emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, and neutrality and maps them to a curated music database, ensuring that the recommendations align with the user’s mood. Unlike conventional methods that rely on user history or preferences, this approach directly connects emotional states with music selection, delivering a highly personalized experience.The use of CNNs enhances the accuracy and reliability of emotion detection, even in complex real-world conditions. By employing deep learning, the system maintains consistent performance and adaptability. This framework redefines music recommendation by directly linking emotions to music, promoting user engagement and emotional well-being. It underscores the transformative potential of AI-powered emotion-aware systems in revolutionizing content delivery and setting new benchmarks in personalized music recommendations.
Keywords: Convolutional Nueral Network | Facial Expression | Music Recommendation | Playlist

Title: Deconstructing AI Detection Tools: Accuracy Limits, Bias, and Human Consequences
Abstract: This is the first study to systematically evaluate AIcontent detectors using dual-direction adversarial edits across multiple genres while simultaneously addressing the ethical gray zone of human-AI collaboration. Nevertheless, there is a critical research gap, as the current literature fails to cover the Gray Zone of the human-AI collaborative authorship and does not have dual-sided adversarial appraisal methods. This study addresses the question raised in the current literature Should the text be considered AI-generated if the AI is used for minor edits. Our two-way evaluation simultaneously evaluates AI-to-human and human-to-AI adversarial changes, applying targeted and strategic changes in order to make human text look like it was produced by AI and the reverse as well with existing commercial AIDetectors as a representative system. The outcomes demonstrate how challenging it is to spot instances of collaborative authorship because even minor typographical adjustments or paraphrases reveal serious flaws in the detection techniques currently in use. Additional algorithmic constraints can be seen in the systemic variation in performance between content types as further shown by genre-specific analysis. The study shows that authorship problems continue even after grammar and style corrections, suggesting that the binary classification method is not effective to capture the complexity of modern human-AI collaboration. Apart from technical criticisms, we also draw focus on practical consequences like academic sanctions for valid work and concerns brought up by institutional policies. It is confirmed by statistical validation that these are systematic limitations rather than problems with implementation. The findings indicate that binary classification is inadequate and that detection tools ought to be reconceptualized as interpretive instruments requiring spectrumbased classifications and human oversight.
Keywords: academic integrity | adversarial robustness | AI-content detection | algorithmic fairness | detection bias | human-AI collaboration

Title: Multimodal Transformer Framework Optimized with Sinusoidal Graylag Goose Algorithm for Performance Analysis of Visually Impaired Adaptive E-Learners
Abstract: Adaptive e-learning systems are designed to provide the significant supporting model for the visually impaired students due to the consideration of resources based on the unique needs. The existing performance analysis approaches depends on unimodal inputs and the models prone to over-fitting and limited prediction accuracy and generalizability. To overcome the challenges, this study proposed a multimodal deep learning framework that integrated speech signals and structured data for robust learner performance analysis. The input speech signals are processed using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) to capture salient audio features and structured data are normalized to enhance compatibility. Finally, the transformer-based model is employed for classifying learners into high, medium, and low performance groups. To optimize learning efficiency of the transformer model, the Sinusoidal Graylag Goose Optimization (SiGO) algorithm is introduced, wherein chaotic sinusoidal mapping within the conventional Graylag Goose Optimization to optimize the loss function.
Keywords: Adaptive elearning | Graylag Goose Optimization | Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients | sinusoidal mapping | transformer | visually impaired students

Title: Analysis of Speech Signals for the Purpose of Neurological Disorders its Detection
Abstract: Standard procedures of Parkinson's disease (PD). detection by a clinical speech therapist have their downsides, mainly because the process is very subjective. Recently, an automatic objective analysis of a speaker’s condition gained in popularity. Researchers successfully based their methods on various machine learning algorithms and handcrafted features. These methods, unfortunately, are not directly scalable to other voice disorders and the process of feature engineering is laborious and thus financially and talent expensive. Based on the previous successes, a deep learning approach might help to ease the problems with scalability and generalization, but an obstacle is a limited amount of training data. This is a common denominator in almost all systems for automated medical data analysis. The main aim of this work is to research new approaches to deep-learning-based predictive modeling using limited audio data sets, focusing especially on voice pathology assessment. This wor is the first to experiment with deep learning in this field and on so far the largest combined database of dysphonic voices, which was created in this work. It provides a thorough examination of publicly available data sources and identifies their limitations. It describes the design of novel time-frequency representations based on Gabor transform and it presents a new class of loss functions, that yield target representations beneficial for learning. In numerical experiments, it demonstrates improvements in the performance of convolutional neural networks trained on limited audio data sets using the augmented target loss function and the newly proposed time-frequency representations, namely Gabor and Mel scattering.
Keywords: detection | monitoring | objective analysis | progress estimation | speech parameterization | speech signal processing

Title: Ta Ka Di Mi: AI for Konnakkol and Rhythm Training
Abstract: We present Ta Ka Di Mi, an AI-powered mobile application designed to make rhythm training and Konnakkol-the South Indian art of vocal percussion-accessible to learners worldwide. Konnakkol is a centuries-old tradition where rhythmic syllables are recited to convey complex tala (time cycles or rhythmic frameworks), often serving as both a pedagogical tool and a performance art. While deeply rooted in South Indian classical music, rhythm itself is a universal language, integral to music, dance, speech, and movement across cultures. Despite this universality, learning Konnakkol has traditionally required close mentorship, consistent practice, and significant exposure to expert practitioners, making it less accessible outside specialized communities. Our system addresses these challenges by combining modern AI technologies with carefully curated pedagogical content to create an interactive, scalable, and user-friendly learning experience for global audiences. The application integrates automatic speech recognition, audio signal processing, and real-time feedback models to evaluate learners across multiple dimensions: rhythmic accuracy, pronunciation fidelity, and tempo consistency. Through gamified lessons, learners can progress from foundational exercises to advanced rhythmic improvisations, guided by structured modules designed in collaboration with renowned artist B.C. Manjunath. The AI-driven evaluation engine provides instant personalized feedback, enabling learners to refine their skills iteratively and at their own pace. In addition, the app incorporates adaptive learning strategies that track a user's growth over time and dynamically suggest exercises tailored to individual strengths and weaknesses. Our demo highlights the unique intersection of cultural heritage and modern AI, showcasing how domain-specific AI/ML techniques can be applied to music education in a globally meaningful way. Beyond traditional music training, Ta Ka Di Mi supports diverse use cases, including rhythm practice for dancers and instrumentalists, therapeutic interventions for speech and motor coordination, and cross-cultural exploration for learners worldwide who seek rhythm as a bridge across traditions. By blending ancient tradition with contemporary technology, the platform not only preserves and disseminates an important cultural practice but also reimagines how rhythm can be taught, experienced, and shared universally. Ultimately, Ta Ka Di Mi demonstrates how AI can democratize access to art forms, enhance pedagogy through personalized insights, and foster global community-building around rhythm. In bridging the gap between ancient tradition and modern technology, the system illustrates the potential of AI-powered education platforms to enrich cultural learning and inspire new creative possibilities across the world. A short demo video is available at: https://youtu.be/LveumJymJ-M.

Title: Animal Sound Source Distance Calculation using Deep Learning
Abstract: In this study, we proposed a deep-learning system for calculating the distance of the Animal sound source mainly focusing on the tiger vocalization. The system utilizes the Google Teachable Machine to train the dataset of tiger sound including the background noise of the forest, people and also the open field making use of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to estimate the distance of the sound source. The system estimates sound source distances by analyzing audio inputs in real-time The system also brings to the notice that it not only detects the animal(Tiger) voice but also the voice of diverse background noise such as Forests, open fields, and human noice where traditional triangulation methods fall short. In this project we have trained and tested the model on the dataset of tiger roars, trying to achieve accuracy in sound classification and mean absolute error of 2.5 meters in distance estimation. The results showed sat- isfactory performance across various environmental conditions, though limitations were observed in highly reverberant settings. The system’s potential application applications include wildlife monitoring and conservation, alerting the people of animal intervention in the human habitat providing real-time data on predator movement. The system has the potential to change the current approaches to wildlife research and conservation efforts also protecting human life from attacks of wild animals and resolving the conflict of humans and wildlife.
Keywords: Acoustic Analysis | Acoustic Signal Processing | Analysis | Animal Sound Detection | Bioacoustic Monitoring | Con- volutional Neural Network (CNN) | Conservation Technology | Data Augmentation | Deep Learning | Distance Estimation | En- vironmental Noise | Google Teachable Machine | Ma- chine Learning | Predator | Real-Time Processing | Sound Source Localization | Sound Triangulation | Tiger Vocalizations | Wildlife Monitoring

Title: Deep Learning for Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection: A Study on Face and Voice Synthesis
Abstract: Currently, deepfake technology is improving the disparity in distinguishing original media from that of synthetic. The work presents a multimodal detection system for deepfakes, utilizing both video- and audio-based modalities for higher classification accuracy. The video processing is done on the DFDC dataset by the provision of metadata, dealing with missing values, and extraction of unique categorical and numerical features. For the audio part, signal processing techniques based on FFmpeg are applied by extracting salient features followed by classification using a Random Forest model with 10-fold cross-validation. Lastly, a model created utilizing deep learning techniques,with an architecture depends on VGG16 is proposed for Fine-tuning the model, allows it to identify important patterns more accurately, which improves overall performance.The last few layers of the neural net for performance. The system is trained over preprocessed datasets and evaluated on several Several evaluation metrics were explored, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), and area under the ROC curve (AUC). This multifaceted approach shows the additional prospect of improving the deepfake detection capability by Predictive modeling approaches and multi-layered AI systems work with diverse types of input in multiple modalities.
Keywords: CNN | Deepfakedetection | Digitalforensics | Fine tune | Multimodalanalysis | Random forest | Spectrogram analysis | VGG16

Title: Predictive Modelling for Oral Cancer Detection using Machine Learning
Abstract: Oral cancer (OC) remains a significant free strength tricky, and primary finding is critical to improving patient outcomes. The research will create multiple ML models to determine OC prediction possibilities based on clinical and demographic information. The data processing phase used label encoding followed by scaling then filled in any absent values in the patient information database. The study evaluated five machine learning (ML) classifiers through training and assessment of Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost and LightGBM as well as Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Logistic Regression (LR). Among them, The XGBoost model produced the best performance with 0.92 ROC AUC score while RF obtained 0.89 and LightGBM demonstrated 0.88. The F1 scores together with the accuracy values varied from 0.80 to 0.90 across evaluated models. Research findings indicate ensemble-based tools especially XGBoost present great potential as diagnostic instruments which help detect oral cancer in its early stages.
Keywords: Hybrid Model | Machine Learning | Oral Cancer | Random Forest | Support Vector Machine

Title: Machine Learning-Based Recommendation Engine for Intelligent Cross-Selling and Upselling in E-Commerce Systems
Abstract: These days, no e-commerce platform is complete without cross-selling and up selling tactics, which boost revenue and delight customers alike. The success of these initiatives depends on accurately gauging consumer opinion. With order to aid with up selling and cross-selling, this study devised a sentiment analysis method for evaluating user-generated material. A comprehensive data cleansing procedure was executed, which comprised tokenization, converting text to lowercase, and removing stop words and punctuation. After the data was cleaned up, it was categorized using the LGCU-CS-DBN model, a DBN based deep learning technique. The GCU-CSO technique was used to optimize the DBN architecture in order to further boost the model's performance. With this method, they were able to fine-tune the activation functions and hidden-neuron count. Achieving a precision of 94.80%, the optimized model demonstrated high sentiment categorization capabilities. Standard performance metrics-based comparative evaluations validated its superiority over more conventional algorithms. These findings show that the LGCU-CS-DBN model is a powerful instrument for e-commerce systems to employ intelligent up selling and cross-selling methods. Because of its flexibility and high accuracy, the model may be used in real-world applications, allowing businesses to make better recommendations and engage customers more effectively.
Keywords: Deep Belief Network (DBN) | Grey linked Chick Update-based Chicken Swarm Optimization (GCU-CSO)

Title: Optimizing Early-Stage Breast Cancer Detection: A Systematic Comparison of Ensemble Methods with Hyperparameter Tuning
Abstract: Breast cancer is one of the leading causes of death among women worldwide, therefore, it requires early detection and appropriate diagnosis to reduce mortality. Reducing mortality depends on early detection and accurate diagnosis, as early-stage treatment is more effective and increases survival rates.
