Early-stage diagnosis of breast cancer still poses a challenge and requires a lot of work on behalf of medical professionals. Machine learning(ML) has become a potent instrument in the diagnosis of chronic diseases, including cancer, in recent years. These ML tools can identify subtle and complicated trends in data that conventional diagnosis techniques might miss. Including such instruments into clinical practice helps doctors to make more accurate and quicker decisions, so improving patient outcomes. In this paper, a comparative study has been conducted using machine learning ensemble methods for breast cancer prediction. Multiple ensemble classifiers—ExtraTreesClassifier, Random Forest, Voting Classifier, Stacking Classifier, XGBoost Classifier, and AdaBoost Classifier with hyperparameter tuning—were trained, and the model's performance was evaluated. Our results show that ensemble approaches greatly enhance prediction performance, and almost all the models performed well. AdaBoost Classifier stands out among all others. Its test accuracy was 98.2%, training accuracy was 100%, and AUC score was also 100%.In proactive healthcare, these instruments can be quite important since they give doctors consistent help for quick diagnosis and treatment planning.
Keywords: accuracy | Breast Cancer | Cancer diagnosis | early detection | Ensemble methods | Machine Learning | prediction

Title: A Method for Zebrafish Egg Viability Identification Based on Improved YOLOv8
Abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of zebrafish egg viability is crucial for high-throughput screening in biomedical research. Although deep learning-based object detectors like YOLOv8 offer feasible solutions, their performance in detecting semi-transparent and small zebrafish eggs within complex microscopic images remains suboptimal. To address this, this paper presents a comprehensively enhanced YOLOv8 model. Specifically, we introduce the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) into the backbone network to enhance feature representation by focusing on salient regions; adopt a weighted Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) for more effective multi-scale feature fusion; and replace the original IoU loss with the EIoU loss function to achieve more accurate bounding box regression. Evaluation on a self-constructed dataset containing 8,992 instances shows that the proposed method achieves an mAP@0.5 of 98.2%, representing a 3.1% improvement over the baseline YOLOv8n model.
Keywords: attention mechanism | biomedical image analysis | viability identification | YOLOv8 | zebrafish eggs

Title: Comparative Analysis of Vgg19 and Efficientnet-B3 for Automated Bird Species Classification Using Deep Learning
Abstract: Bird species identification is a prerequisite to biodiversity tracking, ecological studies, and wildlife conservation. Clearly identifying the species of birds enables researchers to monitor populations, detect changes in habitats, and inform effective conservation measures. However, the classification carried out traditionally by bird experts is usually time-consuming, laborious, and subject to human error, necessitating the use of strong automated mechanisms. In this research, we present a framework based on the use of deep learning techniques to classify bird species based on convolutional neural networks (CNN). VGG19 and EfficientNet-B3 were used, implemented, and analyzed on a dataset comprising 200 bird species with diverse visual features, totaling 2,400 images. Detailed experiments were conducted to determine the output of the competing models based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. VGG19 achieved an accuracy of approximately 79.70 percent, while EfficientNet-B3 delivered superior performance with 98 percent accuracy, demonstrating the benefit of optimized compound scaling and efficient feature extraction. Our results indicate that birds can be automatically recognized very effectively based on the use of deep CNN-based models, representing important instruments used in ecological research as well as biodiversity conservation. This framework is capable of being used to support the conduct of largescale monitoring programs as part of developing smart wildlife management systems. The significant performance gap between the two architectures highlights the importance of model selection in fine-grained classification tasks. Both VGG19 and EfficientNetB3 were fine-tuned using ImageNet pre-trained weights, so as to leverage the transfer learning for better performance on the bird dataset. Such initialization helped the models to retain rich low-level visual features learned from large-scale natural images and accelerated the convergence on our limited dataset. By transferring these generalized representations, the networks required less training samples and resulted in significantly higher accuracy on fine-grained bird species recognition.
Keywords: Accuracy | Bird species | Efficient net | Model comparision | VGG19

Title: Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Meets Machine Learning: Bridging Model-Based Signal Processing and Data-Driven Inference
Abstract: Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation is a core problem in array signal processing with applications in wireless sensing, radar, sonar, acoustics, and robotics. Classical subspace and sparse-reconstruction methods enjoy solid theoretical guarantees, yet their performance can deteriorate under model mismatch, limited snapshots, or coherent multipath. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has achieved strong empirical gains by leveraging high-capacity models and large-scale synthetic data. This work reconciles these lines of research: we review the landscape, articulate complementary strengths and limitations, and present a hybrid framework that integrates physics-based priors with learning-based inference. The approach employs covariance-domain representations, deep unfolding, and transformer encoders together with physics-regularized objectives to enhance robustness to array perturbations and domain shift. Simulations across SNR, source coherence, mutual coupling, and calibration error indicate consistent improvements over classical baselines (MUSIC, ESPRIT, SBL) and representative learning-based models, while maintaining interpretability and sample efficiency.
Keywords: array signal processing | deep learning | deep unfolding | DOA estimation | physics-informed learning | sparse Bayesian learning | transformer

Title: Noise Suppression using Multi Scale Feature Extractor and Channel and Sequence Attention
Abstract: A highly efficient deep neural network architecture is introduced for real-time speech enhancement and noise suppression on resource-constrained devices. The method utilizes a two-phase processing framework with channel-wise feature reorientation and a Channel and Sequence Attention (CSAtt) module to reduce computational cost while retaining state-of-the-art performance. Modified power law compression further optimizes perceptual quality and robust speech estimation. Extensive testing on established datasets demonstrates that the approach matches or surpasses leading solutions such as DeepFilterNet2 with only 25% computational complexity. These results emphasize the potential for deploying advanced deep learning models in IT and IoT environments, aligning with the conference goal of promoting innovative artificial intelligence solutions for real-world applications.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | attention mechanism | deep neural networks | noise suppression | Real-time speech enhancement

Title: Design and Development of an Intelligent Framework for Audio Authenticity Verification in the Digital Era
Abstract: As methods for the generation of non-live audio continue to evolve, the separation of real speech from manipulated voices has emerged as one of the biggest challenges in communication safety and trustworthiness. This work suggests a verification method through deep audio embeddings that is capable of extracting a high-level representation of speech signals. Embeddings are able to extract detailed acoustic and temporal structures efficiently, which are usually not extracted by conventional analysis techniques, allowing for the identification of fine differences in audio between original signals and tampered audio. Then a classification step is used on those embeddings, leveraging the compact representation of audio to feature sets, with no loss of accuracy in real-versus-fake speech discrimination. The experiments show that the suggested framework offers stable and robust system performance across diverse sets of recordings and datasets. Considering the representational power of deep feature extraction and highly effective classification approaches, the framework developed is an appropriate and powerful tool for audio verification and can be used effectively in real-world circumstances, such as security and authentication scenarios.
Keywords: Audio Authenticity | Communication Security | Deep Audio Embeddings | Machine Learning Classification | Speech Manipulation Detection | Voice Verification | Wav2Vec 2.0

Title: Fuzzy-Deep Learning Hybrid Model for Voice and Fluency Assessment in English Literary Performance
Abstract: Reading fluency is an essential component of reading teaching, especially for students encountering literacy difficulties. It differentiates competent readers from those who struggle and serves as a robust indicator of reading comprehension challenges. Upon mastering decoding skills, the subsequent essential stage is to enhance fluency, particularly within the realm of English literary performance. This research presents a technique for evaluating Voice and Fluency in English literary performance utilising FuzzyRNN. The methodology underscores the significance of data preparation and feature extraction, since the calibre of input data profoundly affects model efficacy. Utilising fuzzy numbers for data modelling enables the system to encapsulate human-like perceptions and tackle the uncertainties present in voice and fluency evaluation. The recurrent connections of the FuzzyRNN facilitate a streamlined network architecture while improving its capacity to generalise from fuzzy input. Of the four models evaluated, FuzzyRNN exhibited the highest forecasting accuracy at 94.53%, surpassing its competitors. The results indicate that FuzzyRNN can function as an effective instrument for enhancing fluency assessment in educational settings. The adaptive and perceptual modelling features provide a viable solution for real-time, automated assessment systems, enhancing the efficacy of reading instruction and literary performance evaluation.
Keywords: Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) | Computer Assisted Repeated Reading (CARR) | Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) | Principal Component Analysis (PCA)

Title: Filmfit: Genre Centric Movie Advisor using Hybrid Filtering
Abstract: The evolution of technology has given rise to sophisticated platforms, including Information Gathering, Learning Techniques, the Internet of Things (IOT), and Deep Learning. Because they meet a variety of social demands and encourage the creation of new systems, these technologies are now essential to our day- to-day activities. Among these developments, recommendation engines have become increasingly important in the entertainment, educational, and other sectors of the economy. Users used to have to manually select the books to purchase, the movies to watch, or the music to listen to. Personalized suggestions are now provided by recommendation engines in the modern era to help users. This paper outlines a hybrid recommender system that seeks to improve the quality of recommendations by fusing collaborative filtering with content-based filtering methods. Distinct contrast to conventional systems, our strategy make use of the advantages of both techniques: content-based algorithms prioritize the gathering of materials and quantitative analysis. Conversely, collaborative filtering takes advantage of user choices and behavior. We present a novel approach to feature weight calculation that combines user interactions and a variety of data sources to improve movie representation. Our hybrid model captures the diversity and individuality of user preferences while simultaneously improving recommendation accuracy. We assess the performance of this method, emphasizing its development and future applications in contemporary recommendation systems.
Keywords: Collaborative Filtering | Content-Based Filtering | Feature Weighting | Hybrid Recommendation System | Recommendation Accuracy | User Preferences

Title: Utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks for Image Manipulation Detection
Abstract: The escalating complexity of digital media manipulation methodologies has engendered considerable apprehension concerning the authenticity and reliability of digital content. This investigation confronts the issue of identifying forgeries in images and PDFs through the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), which are particularly adept at discerning subtle modifications via deep feature extraction techniques. In contrast to traditional methodologies, such as metadata examination and watermarking, which frequently encounter difficulties in recognizing sophisticated manipulations, CNNs possess the capability to effectively uncover concealed tampering patterns. The study explores methodologies for detecting altered regions within images, pinpointing anomalies in PDF metadata and content, and scrutinizing modified video frames through both temporal and spatial attributes. Tailored preprocessing pipelines were constructed for each type of content, and CNN models were trained utilizing established datasets. The efficacy of the models was assessed through classification performance metrics, revealing superior outcomes when juxtaposed with conventional methods in terms of both dependability and precision. Furthermore, a user-centric interface was developed employing Django and Streamlit, facilitating the uploading of images and PDFs for instantaneous forgery detection. This practical interface augments the transition from theoretical inquiry to practical implementation, offering a versatile instrument for a wide array of applications. This research addresses challenges such as dataset limitations and computational requirements, proposing recommendations for prospective advancements. By harnessing the capabilities of CNNs, this research presents an effective and scalable solution for forgery detection, contributing to the preservation of digital media integrity in an increasingly manipulated landscape.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) | Deep Learning | Digital Media Forensics | Django Framework | Document Integrity | Forgery Classification | Image Forgery Detection | Media Authenticity | Metadata Analysis | PDF Tampering | Streamlit Interface

Title: Multi-Objective JVM Optimization Framework with Enhanced Machine Learning Techniques: An Automated Approach to Performance Tuning
Abstract: Java Virtual Machine (JVM) parameter tuning is a crucial part of a performance and memory utilisation optimization of application execution in the enterprise environments. This paper outlines a detailed multi objective optimisation model in which the use of Optuna in self-guided tuning of JVM parameters is made. Our approach simultaneously maximises execution latency and memory usage through Pareto front program analysis, thus dealing with the complex trade-offs with which JVM configuration is replete. The framework incorporates a powerful graphical user interface to monitor and provide the necessary decision to determine optimisation progress in real- time. The experimental findings indicate considerable performance improvement: the automated variant achieves a reduction of 56.4 percent in execution time and a reduction by 78.8 percent of memory consumption as compared to the comparative default JVMs. The system provides exhaustive analytics, such as the impact of the parameters assessment, performance trend assessment, and configuration recommendations, thus, making the instrument available to both non-expert and expert users.
Keywords: automated configuration | JVM optimization | memory management | multi-objective optimization | Pareto front | performance tuning

Title: Te-Autoformer: Integrating Astronomical Features for Enhanced Tidal Energy Forecasting
Abstract: Accurate tidal energy forecasting is essential for grid integration and operational planning, yet existing methods struggle to capture the complex multi-periodic dynamics driven by celestial mechanics. This paper proposes the Temporal-Enhanced Autoformer (TE-Autoformer), a physics-informed deep learning architecture that synergistically integrates astronomical domain knowledge with adaptive temporal modeling for long-term tidal forecasting. Our model introduces three key innovations: (1) an Astronomical Feature Extraction module that computes seven celestial parameters including lunar phase and solar-lunar angular separation to provide explicit physical inductive biases; (2) an Adaptive Multi-Scale Decomposition mechanism that dynamically weights semi-diurnal, diurnal, and weekly periodicities through learnable attention; and (3) enhanced auto-correlation mechanisms tailored for tidal signal characteristics. Extensive experiments on the Marine Institute Tide Prediction Dataset demonstrate that TE-Autoformer achieves state-of-the-art performance, reducing Root Mean Square Error by 12 0-15.4% compared to PatchTST and 15.2-20.7% compared to standard Autoformer across 24-72 hour horizons. The model maintains superior accuracy during critical spring-neap transitions, demonstrating robust generalization. These improvements directly translate to enhanced operational reliability for tidal energy systems, enabling more accurate generation forecasting and improved grid integration planning.
Keywords: astronomical features | deep learning | multi-scale decomposition | physics-informed neural networks | renewable energy | Tidal energy forecasting | time series prediction | Transformer

Title: EM-Net: A Deep Learning Model Using Enhanced Attention and Multi-Scale Feature Fusion for Text Image Forgery Detection
Abstract: In this paper, we propose an EM-Net for detecting the tiny regions of subtle features, which includes three stages. First, a Multi-scale Feature Extraction module (MSFE-module) is used to extract multi-scale and multi-layer feature information. A Feature Enhanced (FE-module) catches the key information in different scales and refines the results by assigning more weights to forgery areas. Therefore valuable features can be enhanced while irrelevant information is suppressed. As the network is constantly downsampling the image, the resolution becomes small. To restore the size, in the Feature Fusion decoder module (FFU-module), the multi-level information by integrating the global features and location details, so as to improve the performance of locating the forgery areas. To demonstrate the validity of our model, we compare the performance of the proposed EM-Net with state-of-art methods. The results show that our performance was excellent on the testing dataset.
Keywords: deep learning | finance forensics | image processing | text image forgery detection

Title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection and Classification of Ovarian Cancer from Medical Imaging
Abstract: Ovarian cancer remains one of the most lethal types of gynaecological cancer because it advances asymptomatically and is often identified at an advanced stage. Early and precise identification is a critical to maintain health. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), especially deep learning (DL), have shown significant potential for enhancing computer-aided diagnosis and medical picture analysis. This study presents a DL-based system for the automated detection and classification of ovarian cancer utilising medical imaging techniques. The extraction of distinguishing features and categorisation of benign and malignant cases with high precision is achieved through the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning techniques. The proposed approach is evaluated using publicly accessible datasets and clinical datasets, demonstrating superior performance relative to traditional machine learning (ML) methods in accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. DL models possess the capability to serve as valuable, dependable, and scalable instruments that can aid radiologists in the early detection and classification of ovarian cancer. This will ultimately enhance patient outcomes and facilitate tailored treatment planning. The results underscore the potential of deep learning methods.
Keywords: Classification | Deep Learning | Health | Ovarian cancer | Performance Metrics | Technology transfer

Title: A Lightweight Attention Convolutional Network for End-to-End Monaural Speech Separation
Abstract: Existing single-channel speech separation methods often rely on complex deep neural network architectures, such as convolutional neural network and recurrent neural network. These approaches suffer from high model complexity and poor real-time performance, especially in resource-constrained scenarios. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight attention convolutional network (LAC-Net), centered around a Lightweight Multi-Branch Attention Block (LMBA Block). This module integrates Ghost Module, Channel Split and Channel Shuffle operations, as well as an improved Convolutional Block Attention Module. It significantly reduces model parameters and computational cost while effectively enhancing speech feature modeling and separation performance. Extensive experiments were conducted on WSJ0-2mix, Libri2Mix, and the selfconstructed Chinese datasets NJUST603-2Mix and NJUST6033Mix. The results demonstrate that LAC-Net consistently outperforms several classical baseline models in terms of SDRi and SI-SNRi. While maintaining a compact model size, LACNet exhibits stable performance in multi-speaker scenarios and achieves favorable results in real-time evaluations, highlighting its strong generalization ability.
Keywords: attention mechanism | deep learning | lightweight network | speech separation

Title: The Future of Precision Medicine and Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery: A Comprehensive Analysis of Instruments and Methods
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionised drug discovery and development by improving the speed, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness of the traditional method of finding novel therapeutic candidates. Computational and meta-analytical findings are used in this review to assess AI's effectiveness at different phases of drug discovery. It highlights important AI technologies like natural language processing (NLP), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL), which are being used more and more in precision medicine, virtual screening, pharmacological target identification, and repurposing. A quantitative synthesis of 12 independent studies using random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird method) revealed a pooled accuracy of 0.57 (95% CI: 0.38-0.76) in predicting drug-target interactions (DTIs). Furthermore, the study incorporates mathematical formulations for AI model performance evaluation, including Mean Squared Error (MSE), Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) area, and precision metrics. Despite challenges such as data heterogeneity, model interpretability, and ethical governance, the integration of explainable AI (XAI), multi-omics data fusion, and real-time analytics promises to restructure the future of pharmaceutical innovation.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Deep Learning | Drug Discovery | Drug Repurposing | Machine Learning | Meta-analysis | Precision Medicine

Title: Transformer-aided Subspace Method for Near Field Localization
Abstract: With the development of technologies such as largescale MIMO and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, spatial information processing in the near-field region has emerged as a significant research topic in wireless communication and intelligent sensing. Existing model-based deep learning methods, such as covariance matrix-based subspace methods, while performing high estimation accuracy and robustness under severe conditions like sources correlation and limited snapshots, their performances are sub-optimal, particularly in feature extraction and longcontext understanding, present significant potential for further optimization. Therefore, a novel near-field DOA estimation method is proposed that integrates Transformer structure with subspace method, named NFTranSNet. This method utilizes a Transformer network to extract spatial correlations and temporal features from the received signals and constructs a surrogate covariance matrix. Combined with the 2D-MUSIC algorithm, it achieves joint estimation of the angle and distance of near-field signal sources. Simulation results demonstrate that NFTranSNet significantly outperforms traditional subspace methods and existing deep learning models in complex scenarios such as multisource, coherent signals, low SNR, limited snapshots, and array perturbations.
Keywords: Deep learning | Near-Field DOAs | Subspace method

Title: The Influence of Denoising Pre-processing on the Performance of Kulkul Sound Classification Using Transformers
Abstract: The kulkul, a traditional Balinese slit drum, is a vital communication tool for relaying community messages. Automating the classification of distinct sounds offers significant potential for cultural preservation and modernizing community information systems; however, ambient noise in real-world recordings poses a substantial challenge to model reliability. This study systematically evaluated the influence of denoising pre-processing on the performance of a transformer-based model for classifying three kulkul sounds: bulus (danger), sangkep (assembly), and kematian (death). Using a dataset of 318 recordings, we compared a baseline (no denoising) with traditional signal processing methods (Spectral Subtraction, Wiener Filter, Spectral Gating) and an advanced deep learning approach, CycleGAN. Our results show that CycleGAN-based denoising yields superior performance, achieving an F1-score of 86.34
Keywords: CycleGAN | denoising | kulkul | sound classification | transformer

Title: UAV Small Object Detection via Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Adaptive Attention Mechanism
Abstract: An advanced object detection approach grounded in the RT-DETR framework is developed to enhance small object identification in UAV imagery, effectively mitigating challenges related to poor feature expressiveness, scale-level semantic inconsistency, and hardware constraints during real-world deployment. At the feature extraction level, a lightweight convolutional feature extraction structure (LCFE) is constructed, which employs an improved Conv3XCC3 module to effectively capture fine-grained low-level features of small objects while significantly reducing computational complexity. At the crossscale modeling level, a Scale Sequence Attention Module (SSAM) is designed, integrating the GSConv and ScalSeq mechanisms to achieve dynamic dependency modeling across scales and enhance semantic perception in complex scenes. At the feature fusion level, a Dynamic Adaptive Feature Fusion Module (DAFM) is proposed, which leverages the Zoom-cat operator and an adaptive gating mechanism to accomplish multi-scale semantic alignment and small-object feature enhancement, effectively mitigating information conflicts and detail loss during the feature fusion process. Performance evaluation reveals that the optimized network attains a 2. 1% increase in mAP and a 1. 8% rise in mAPs compared with the baseline, respectively, on the VisDrone2019 dataset, while reducing the weight file size by 17.28%, which demonstrates the proposed model's capability and effectiveness.
Keywords: Adaptive Feature Fusion | Deep Learning | RT-DETR | Small Object Detection

Title: High-Bit Implementation of PDM-to-PCM Conversion Based on Depthwise Separable Convolution
Abstract: Digital micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) can output pulse density modulation (PDM) signals with high sampling rates, but in the field of audio signal analysis, they usually tend to handle pulse code modulation (PCM) signals. Therefore, before analyzing the audio signal, converting the PDM signal to a PCM signal is a necessary step. Currently, onedimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNN) can efficiently achieve 8-bit accuracy reconstruction in the conversion from PDM to PCM and have a relatively low inference delay. However, in the face of widely used 16-bit audio signals, the abovementioned method, due to the limited model expression ability, is difficult to accurately restore high-resolution waveforms, which limits its application in high-quality audio processing. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight neural network architecture based on Depthwise Separable Convolution (DSC), which enhances the feature expression ability by introducing a learnable channel expansion mechanism. Combining the calculation method of Half-Precision Floating-Point Format (float16), the overflow and rounding errors in the conversion of high-bit wide signals are effectively alleviated to improve the reconstruction quality of 16-bit PCM signals. This method was successfully deployed on the Xilinx Zynq-7020 FPGA platform. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.00218 on the self-built PDM speech dataset. The Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) reached 65.72dB, which was significantly superior to the existing neural network methods. Although its performance is still inferior to that of dedicated industrial-grade audio conversion chips, the construction of a highly reusable technical path on a generalpurpose FPGA platform has verified the feasibility of deep learning models in high-bit PDM-to-PCM conversion, providing a reproducible and transferable implementation example for the research of reconfigurable and adaptive audio systems.
Keywords: CIC filter | Deep learning | Depthwise Separable Convolution (DSC) | PDM to PCM

Title: CD-TA-RTM: A Dual-Pathway Deep Learning Architecture for Rainfall Estimation Using Commercial Microwave Links
Abstract: Commercial microwave links (CML) create opportunities for rainfall sensing by leveraging signal attenuation patterns as indicators. However, existing CML-based rainfall estimation methods face several challenges. These include difficulties with complex spatiotemporal precipitation patterns, fixed parameter dependencies, poor regional adaptability, and systematic underestimation of heavy rainfall events. To address these challenges, we propose CD-TA-RTM, a dual-pathway deep learning architecture which exploits Convolutional Downsampling (CD) for spatial pattern extraction, Temporal ion (TA) for multi-scale temporal dynamics, and Raw Temporal Modeling (RTM) for preserving original sequence information. To balance contributions of imbalanced rainfall intensities during training, we also introduce an Adaptive Rainfall-Intensity Weighted (ARIW) loss function that dynamically addresses underestimation bias during heavy precipitation events with small proportion in the dataset. Experiments based on dual-frequency E-band CML data demonstrate that our approach achieves excellent prediction performance across the entire test dataset with PCC of 0.8915 and R2 of 0.7805 while maintaining remarkable robustness to noise.
Keywords: Adaptive Loss Function | Commercial Microwave Links | Deep Learning | Rainfall Estimation | Signal Attenuation | Signal Processing

Title: VisionAid Edge: Design and Technical Feasibility Study of a Multimodal Assistive System for Visually Impaired Individuals
Abstract: Vision impairment affects 2.2 billion people worldwide, while existing assistive technologies face fragmentation through single-modality approaches, privacy concerns from cloud dependency, or cost barriers exceeding Rs. 3 lakh. This paper presents VisionAid Edge, a cyber-physical system integrating multimodal artificial intelligence on low-cost edge hardware while preserving privacy through on-device processing. The architecture combines object detection (YOLO11n via NCNN), Indian currency recognition (ONNX), ultrasonic ranging with haptic feedback, offline voice control, and Global Positioning System (GPS) alerts on Raspberry Pi 4. To address thermal and power constraints, adaptive input resizing, two-frame temporal filtering, and priority-based audio queuing are applied. Technical characterization over five 100-minute trials demonstrates currency recognition accuracy of 87.3 percent on 900 test images, median text-to-speech latency of 275 milliseconds, sustained throughput of about two to three frames per second (FPS), and 3.2-hour battery life on 37 Wh power. Face encodings use PBKDF2-derived AES-256 encryption. Results establish that low-cost edge platforms (Rs. 10,400) can support integrated assistive functionality with acceptable performance. Complete implementation is opensourced to enable user studies and deployment.
Keywords: assistive technology | computer vision | edge computing | sensor fusion | visual impairment

Title: Multi-Track Audio Fusion for Emotion Recognition Using Machine and Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract: Emotion recognition from audio signals is essential for human-computer interaction, affective computing, and mental health monitoring. However, traditional single-track systems often fail to capture the full range of emotional nuance in complex audio environments. Motivated by this challenge, we propose a multi-track audio fusion-based approach to improve emotion classification accuracy. Using Bangla song recordings, we extract Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, spectral, and temporal features, then apply feature-level fusion to build enriched audio representations. These features are classified using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and compared against classical machine learning models, including SVM, RF, and CatBoost. The CNN model achieved superior performance, with a 99.45% accuracy rate on multi-emotion classification. Our results confirm the robustness of multi-track fusion and deep learning in building more precise and scalable emotion recognition systems.
Keywords: Audio Signal Processing | Deep Learning | Emotion Recognition | Feature Extraction | Machine Learning | Multi-Track Audio Fusion

Title: LLM-Guided Multimodal Scene Captioning via Prompt-Based Fusion of Visual and Auditory Descriptions
Abstract: Understanding complex scenes in real world environments often demands more than visual analysis alone it requires the integration of both visual and auditory cues. This study investigates whether prompt-based fusion using large language models (LLMs) can effectively combine modality specific outputs for zero-shot scene captioning. We propose a modular framework that leverages BLIP-2 for visual captioning, Whisper for audio transcription, and FLAN-T5 for prompt-driven fusion. To simulate multimodal caption pairs, we augment the COCO image caption dataset with text-to-speech (TTS) generated audio and incorporate filtered real-world audio-image samples. Unlike prior approaches requiring joint training or architectural modification, our pipeline operates entirely in zero-shot mode with no model retraining. Evaluation using BLEU, ROUGE-L, and cosine-based semantic similarity reveals that our fusion strategy, despite its simplicity, achieves semantically coherent captions across modalities. This work demonstrates the feasibility of LLM-guided fusion for assistive AI and offers a reproducible, low-resource solution for applications such as smart narration, AR/VR accessibility, and navigation aids for visually impaired users.
Keywords: Assistive AI | Audio Captioning | BLIP-2 | FLAN-T5 | Large Language Models | Low-resource Deployment | Multimodal Learning | Prompt-based Fusion | Scene Captioning | Semantic Similarity | Text-to-Speech | Visual Captioning | Whisper | Zero-shot Learning

Title: Bangla Speech to IPA Transcription: A Multi-Stage Transformer-Based Approach
Abstract: The International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) provides an exact way to represent speech sounds across different dialects, making it crucial for tasks like linguistic research and pronunciation-focused applications. Precise IPA transcription plays a significant role in areas such as speech therapy, language education, and the preservation of endangered languages. This paper presents a multistage approach for transcribing Bangla speech into IPA, aiming to improve phonetic accuracy and offer a modular solution tailored for low-resource language contexts. The pipeline consists of two stages: speech-to-text transcription and grapheme-to-phoneme IPA conversion. We used two curated Bangla datasets with diverse phoneme coverage, addressing limitations in existing datasets. The first stage employs a customized automatic speech recognition (ASR) model based on transformer architectures, inspired by recent multilingual ASR advancements. To assess generalization, we evaluated our model on a dataset lacking prior benchmarks, obtaining a WER of 0.2625 and CER of 0.0787, high-lighting the challenges of domain transfer. The second stage uses a sequence-to-sequence grapheme-to-phoneme model to generate IPA transcriptions, followed by a scoring layer that assesses pronunciation consistency and model confidence, achieving a WER of 1.7% and a CER of 0.414%. By decoupling stages, our framework ensures greater control over linguistic fidelity. Experimental results demonstrate strong phonetic transcription capabilities, offering flexibility for applications such as speech recognition, pronunciation assessment, and language documentation in low-resource settings. Our modular approach provides a scalable solution for Bangla and similar languages, paving the way for robust speech processing systems.
Keywords: automatic speech recognition (ASR) | Bangla speech processing | grapheme-to-phoneme | International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) | low-resource languages | phonetic scoring | speech-to-text | transformer models

Title: Emotion Detection in Speech Using Lightweight and Transformer-Based Models: A Comparative and Ablation Study
Abstract: Emotion recognition from speech plays a vital role in the development of empathetic human-computer interaction systems. This paper presents a comparative analysis of lightweight transformer-based models, DistilHuBERT and PaSST, by classifying six core emotions from the CREMA-D dataset. We benchmark their performance against a traditional CNN-LSTM baseline model using MFCC features. DistilHuBERT demonstrates superior accuracy (70.64%) and F1 score (70.36%) while maintaining an exceptionally small model size (0.02 MB), outperforming both PaSST and the baseline. Furthermore, we conducted an ablation study on three variants of the PaSST, Linear, MLP, and Attentive Pooling heads, to understand the effect of classification head architecture on model performance. Our results indicate that PaSST with an MLP head yields the best performance among its variants but still falls short of DistilHuBERT. Among the emotion classes, angry is consistently the most accurately detected, while disgust remains the most challenging. These findings suggest that lightweight transformers like DistilHuBERT offer a compelling solution for real-time speech emotion recognition on edge devices. The code is available at: https://github.com/luckymaduabuchi/Emotion-detection-.
Keywords: CNN-LSTM | DistilHuBERT | Edge AI | PaSST | Speech Emotion Recognition | Transformers

Title: Toward Early Detection of Prediabetes in Children: A Multimodal Analysis of Oral, Cutaneous, and Metabolic Indicators
Abstract: Early detection of pre-diabetes in children and adolescents is essential to prevent its progression to type-2 diabetes. In paediatric settings, conventional diagnostic approaches relying on invasive blood tests often pose practical and psychological challenges. This study investigates the feasibility of using external physiological indicators, specifically tongue and skin features, as non-invasive markers of early metabolic alteration. To support this objective, a tri-modal screening framework integrating clinical parameters with machine-learning-based image analysis is proposed to enable patient-friendly assessment. The dataset comprises 127 synthetically generated clinical image cases, with a mean participant age of 14.13 years. From these images, a total of 152 quantitative features were extracted, including GLCM-based texture metrics, colour-distribution descriptors, and high-dimensional deep-learning representations. These visual features were analysed alongside metabolic indices such as HbA1c and fasting blood glucose. The ensemble model that combined all modalities achieved an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.94, with a sensitivity of 92% and specificity of 88%, demonstrating strong diagnostic potential. Overall, the findings support the use of visual cues as a viable, non-invasive approach for early pre-diabetes screening in paediatric populations. Validation on larger, real-world, and demographically diverse cohorts will be essential for future clinical adoption.
Keywords: image analysis | machine learning | metabolic markers | non-invasive diagnosis | paediatric screeing | Pre-diabetes

Title: Intelligent Human Scream Detection for Crime Control Using Audio Signal Processing and Machine Learning
Abstract: The human scream detection system is increasingly useful for fostering safety in public transport, urban, homely, and school settings. Conventional surveillance cameras often fail to discern distress signals when visual coverage is obscured, or when a person cannot trigger an alarm manually. In such scenarios, the automatic detection of vocal distress would be a useful boost. This paper presents a method to detect and classify human vocalization into screams or non-screams by signal processing and machine learning. Mel spectrograms are used to preprocess the audio for subsequent extraction of relevant sound features. Three models were developed and tested: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The performance of these models was assessed on a realtime basis using a dataset of 27 scream audios and background noise, giving a realistic impression of their performance. CNN-based detection achieved 88.6% accuracy, while that of SVMs and RFs was 80.1% and 81%, respectively. The method exhibits level flexibility across different acoustic settings and adds to the overall detection reliability. Along with its high accuracy, the system is promising in emergency response frameworks, smart surveillance systems, and public safety setups. It has assisted in the development of smart safety systems that identify distress signals and trigger timely intervention quickly.
Keywords: convolutional neural network (CNN) | Detection of human screams | machine learning | mel spectrogram | random forest (RF) | signal processing | support vector machine (SVM)

Title: Evaluation of Accuracy, Information Quality, and Readability of Artificial Intelligence Based Chatbots in Pediatric Oral Surgery: A Comparative Analysis Based on the AAPD Clinical Guideline
Abstract: Objectives: Chatbots powered by artificial intelligence are increasingly used as tools for obtaining medical and dental knowledge. This study aimed to assess and compare the performance of four AI chatbots in providing evidence-based information on pediatric oral surgery topics, with reference to the American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry (AAPD) clinical guideline. Materials and Methods: This descriptive observational study evaluated four AI chatbots (ChatGPT-5, Gemini, Copilot, and DeepSeek) by posing 20 questions derived from the AAPD Guideline on Management Considerations for Pediatric Oral Surgery. Responses were assessed for accuracy using the grading system, for quality using the 16-item DISCERN instrument and for readability using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) formula. Non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment were employed for statistical comparisons (p < 0.05). Results: Significant differences were observed among chatbots in all outcome measures. Gemini and ChatGPT-5 achieved the highest accuracy scores (1.30 ± 0.47 and 1.40 ± 0.60, respectively; p = 0.001), whereas DeepSeek and Copilot showed lower accuracy. In terms of information quality, DeepSeek produced the highest DISCERN scores (52.90 ± 3.73; p < 0.001), followed by Copilot. ChatGPT-5 and Gemini yielded more readable outputs (10.73 ± 1.98 and 11.68 ± 1.91, respectively), though readability differences were not statistically significant (p > 0.05). Conclusions: Of the models evaluated, Gemini and ChatGPT-5 produced the most accurate responses, while DeepSeek generated the highest-quality content. While AI chatbots show promise as supplementary tools for patient education and clinical learning in pediatric oral surgery, their reliability varies considerably across platforms. Continuous validation and guideline-based evaluation are essential prior to clinical integration.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | hekimliği | oral cerrahi | oral surgery | pediatric dentistry | yapay zekâ | Çocuk diş

Title: A Unified Analytical Framework for Systematically Comparing Classical and aI Approaches in Radar Systems
Abstract: The paper conducts a systematic analysis and comparison of signal processing and object identification methods used in radar systems for intelligent transportation. We propose a unified analytical framework that evaluates classical model-based algorithms, subspace methods, and modern deep learning-based approaches. Our analysis synthesizes these paradigms through consistent performance metrics, computational complexity, and robustness, offering a new perspective for assessing practical trade-offs. We examine a range of problems, including detection, parameter estimation, and vehicle classification. The results are organized to provide engineers and researchers with practical guidance on selecting optimal processing architectures, identifying unresolved issues, and exploring promising research directions in the field of autonomous transportation systems.
Keywords: Automotive radar | CFAR | CNN/YOLO | DOA | FFT | FMCW | MUSIC/ESPRIT | range-Doppler | STAP

Title: Deep Neural Networks Analyzing Age and Fat Component Correlation in Kyrgyz Women
Abstract: This paper examines the relationship between age and fat factors in Kyrgyz females based on the deep neural network (DNN) approach. A feed forward model of neural network is used to examine structured data, such as age, body fat percentage, BMI, and lifestyle factors. Normalization and standardization are some of the data preprocessing that are employed to bring consistency to the features. The model of DNN is trained on Adam optimizer and assessed with the help of Mean Squared Error (MSE) to estimate the percentage of fat by age. Cross-validation of models is used to verify their performance in order to prevent overfitting. The research tries to extract major trends in age role in fat composition and gives insight on the application of deep learning on analysis of data concerning health. The findings reveal that DNN model is useful in capturing the complex relationship between age and components of fat and provides a potent instrument of health research of diverse groups of people.
Keywords: Age | Body Fat Percentage | Data Preprocessing | Deep Neural Networks | Fat Composition | Kyrgyz Women | Machine Learning

Title: Detection of Apple Mosaic Disease Based on YOLOV5 Model
Abstract: The apple industry occupies an important position in the global agricultural economy, but the yield and quality of apple mosaic disease are seriously threatened, and it is urgent to achieve accurate and efficient detection of the disease. In order to solve the problem of insufficient accuracy of traditional detection methods due to complex shape characteristics (such as irregular patches, twisted leaf veins and scattered punctate lesions) of apple mosaic diseases, an optimization solution based on YOLOv5 deep learning model was proposed. Firstly, a large-scale disease image dataset covering major production areas, multiple climatic conditions and growth stages in the world was constructed, focusing on the collection of leaf characteristic data with different environmental backgrounds and disease levels. Then, by improving the network structure parameters, optimizing the multi-scale feature fusion strategy and adjusting the weight of the loss function, the ability of the model to capture subtle disease features was significantly improved. The experimental results show that the optimized YOLOv5 model has achieved breakthrough detection performance in complex orchard scenes: The detection accuracy of irregular plaque lesions has been improved, the recall rate of twisted leaf vein lesions has been greatly improved, and the key indicators are significantly better than those of the comparison model. This achievement provides high-precision technical support for the intelligent monitoring of orchard diseases, and effectively solves the problem of identifying complex disease spot features.
Keywords: apple mosaic virus | deep learning | disease detection | Feature extraction | YOLOV5

Title: Scalable VLSI Design for Edge AI Acceleration in Real-Time Audio-Visual Processing Systems
Abstract: The high rate of Edge AI application development requires scalable streamlined energy-effective hardware solutions, which can handle real-time audio-visual processing at the edge with little latency and consumption. Current accelerators such as GPUs and FPGAs frequently do not support multimodal data streams which is utilizing high energy, with an efficient synchronization. In a bid to avoid these constraints, the proposed Scalable VLSI Design Framework to Edge AI Acceleration in Real-Time Audio-Visual Processing Systems is a synthesis of hierarchical dataflow-based VLSI architecture, systolic array-based parallel computing, and dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) as means of optimizing performance. Swift compression-conscious interconnects and dynamic hardware division are also built in to the design in order to create the efficient synchronization of audio and visual channels. The proposed model is analysed with 7 nm CMOS technology that demonstrates the notable enhancements in throughput processing and efficiency of power along with interference latency estimation which is less than 10 ms per frame and accuracy enhancement of 13% which is better than the other existing frameworks. The obtained results are clearly depicting that the proposed framework is well suitable for real time applications such as smart surveillance, UAVs and in HMIs.
Keywords: AI application | Audiovisual processing | CMOS | dynamic voltage and frequency scaling | FPGAs | throughput | VLSI design

Title: Scene Classification of High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images via CNN-Transformer Feature Fusion
Abstract: High-resolution remote sensing (HRRS) images hold considerable application worth in domains like urban planning and natural disaster surveillance. Nevertheless, their notable intra-class variation and strong inter-class resemblance present substantial hurdles for scene classification. Conventional machine learning approaches depend on manually designed features and exhibit poor generalization, whereas standalone CNN or Transformer models find it difficult to effectively integrate multi-scale and global-local information. To tackle these shortcomings, this study puts forward a scene classification approach that combines CNN and Transformer architectures. First, four cascaded Transformer encoder blocks are adopted: linear spatial self-Attention is utilized to lower computational costs, and convolutional feed-forward layers are employed to refine positional encoding, thereby extracting features across four distinct scales. Next, spatial and global attention mechanisms are introduced to suppress redundant content and amplify critical features. Finally, global average pooling is leveraged to learn dynamic weights, enabling linearly weighted integration of multi-scale features and thus reinforcing the guidance offered by scale-related information. Experiments carried out on the UCM dataset indicate that our approach attains an overall accuracy of 98.51%, surpassing other state-of-The-Art algorithms. Ablation experiments verify that the feature enhancement and adaptive fusion modules lead to significant performance improvements. This approach provides an innovative solution for HRRS images classification and i is highly suitable for scenarios such as urban planning and disaster surveillance.
Keywords: Adaptive fusion | High-resolution remote sensing image | Multi-scale feature | Scene classification | Transformer

Title: Music Popularity Prediction Platform
Abstract: Predicting the popularity of songs has long been a challenge in the music industry due to rapidly changing listener preferences and evolving production practices. This is an empirical study with a deployed prototype. It applies machine learning techniques to audio features and temporal metadata spanning six decades of music to predict whether a track will achieve commercial popularity. Four models were developed and evaluated, including a tuned Random Forest with decade encoding, which demonstrated superior performance in terms of F1-score and ROC-AUC. Stratified sampling and per-decade validation ensured robustness against temporal bias, while feature importance analyses revealed danceability, instrumentalness, and acousticness as key predictors. SHAP-based explainability methods provided transparency into model decisions, enhancing trust and interpretability. A Streamlit-based application was also deployed to offer an interactive interface for exploring predictions, enabling threshold tuning and scenario testing. Results suggest that integrating temporal context with acoustic features improves predictive accuracy and provides actionable insights for playlist curation, artist scouting, and trend forecasting. The platform's ranking, calibration, and explainability support practical Artist scouting, repertoire triage and playlist curation, offering measurable screening efficiency and transparent decision support for labels and distributors
Keywords: Acoustic Features | API | CRISP-DM | Feature Engineering | Interpretability | Machine Learning | MIR | Music Popularity Prediction | Random Forest | SHAP | Spotify | Streamlit Deployment | Temporal Analysis | XGBoost

Title: Radionuclide Identification System Based on Embedded Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Traditional radionuclide identification systems suffer from large volume, poor real-time performance, and low identification efficiency in low count rate, making it difficult to meet the requirements for miniaturization and intelligence of equipment in the fields of nuclear safety, security, and facility decommissioning. This paper proposes and implements a radionuclide identification system based on embedded artificial intelligence, aiming to provide a highly efficient and portable solution. The hardware platform adopts the STM32H750 microcontroller, combined with analog front-end circuits and peak-finding algorithms for precise acquisition, and directly accumulates the collected peak voltages into a energy spectrum feature vector. Then it is fed into the core identification algorithm using a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model, achieving end-to-end embedded intelligence from data acquisition to radionuclide identification. Experimental results show that the system exhibits excellent accuracy in front-end signal processing, and the constructed nuclear energy spectrum is highly consistent with the results of traditional methods, with clear characteristic peaks. The MLP model deployed on the STM32H750 can accurately identify multiple radionuclides such as Am, Cs, Co and their mixture, verifying the feasibility and practical value of this system in improving identification efficiency and achieving equipment miniaturization.
Keywords: Embedded artificial intelligence | Energy spectrum analysis | Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) | Peak extraction | Radionuclide identification

Title: Transparent and Efficient Fraud Detection in Power-Grid Smart Metering with Explainable AI
Abstract: Smart meters in power grids enable data-driven operations, yet electricity theft and tampering cause major non-technical losses. Many machine learning (ML) models achieve high accuracy but act as black boxes, limiting operator trust. We present an explainable AI (xAI) framework that augments supervised (Random Forest, CatBoost) and unsupervised (VAE, LSTM-AE) baselines with attribution-driven feature selection. Using daily readings from more than 40,000 customers over three years, we show that xAI reduces dimensionality and inference latency without degrading detection quality. The method highlights abnormal consumption, sudden drops, and time-of-use anomalies, surfacing customers and days for field inspections. CatBoost and LSTM-AE emerge as most effective supervised and unsupervised baselines, respectively, with about 400 selected features balancing accuracy and speed. Explainability is introduced without performance loss, supporting faster, auditable, and trusted utility operations.
Keywords: anomaly detection | critical infrastructure | Explainable AI (xAI) | fraud detection | non-technical losses (NTL) | power grids | smart metering | time-series analysis

Title: Deep Learning for Predicting Drug-Drug Interactions and Patient Safety in Dental Clinical Trials
Abstract: This paper introduces a new model, named Deep Federated Transformer Graph Attention Network (DFT-GAT), to predict drug-drug interaction (DDIs) to improve patient safety in dental clinical trials. The proposed model is based on the PyTorch 2.x and includes multimodal data sources: molecular structures, clinical records, and treatment notes, which are processed with the help of an attention-based fusion mechanism to learn features holistically. With the federated learning paradigm, model training can be done in more than one dental center, and the data privacy and adherence to the clinical rules must be provided. Graph attention module focuses on capturing the inter-drug associations, whereas SHAP-based explainability enables easy understanding of the results of decisions, enhancing clinical trust and interpretability. Experimental analyses showed better performance with accuracy of 93.8% and AUC-ROC of 0.962 and exceeding the current deep learning benchmarks. These findings indicate that the framework can provide scalable, interpretable, and privacy-aware predictions and that DFT-GAT is a powerful AI-based instrument in dental pharmacological analysis to provide safe and efficient predictions.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Drug-Drug Interaction | Explainable AI | Federated Learning | Graph Attention Network | Patient Safety | Transformer Network

Title: Efficient-DEIM: An Enhanced DEIM Framework for Small-Target Detection in UAV Aerial Imagery
Abstract: To address the limited detection performance of small objects in aerial imagery, this study proposes an improved DEIM-based deep learning detector. First, the feature extraction network replaces conventional depthwise separable convolution with a partial convolution structure, effectively reducing computational redundancy and enhancing multi-scale feature representation. Second, we introduce a novel multi-scale feature fusion module that integrates a meta-operations mixer and a convolutional gating unit, enabling deep fusion of multi-level features through adaptive weighting to substantially improve the model's ability to capture global contextual information. Experiments on the VisDrone2019 dataset show that, relative to a baseline model, the proposed approach achieves a significant improvement in detection performance, with mAP50 rising by 5.8 percentage points and mAP50:95 rising by 3.4 percentage points. Compared with existing mainstream algorithms, the method demonstrates superior performance for aerial small-object detection tasks.
Keywords: DEIM | feature fusion | small-object detection | UAV

Title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Cryptocurrency Trend Prediction via Candlestick Charts and Technical Indicators
Abstract: The growth of Bitcoin cryptocurrency with large fluctuations has aroused the interest of large investors, leading to the need for institutional investors to be at the forefront of short-term cryptocurrency trend prediction technology. To address the complexities caused by nonlinearity, this paper proposes a fusion model combining the MobileNetV2 model to capture candlestick chart morphology, OHLCV series with technical indicators modeled by GRU for short-term dependencies, and nonautoregressive encoder (NAR) to extract long-term context. Then, the features of each model are merged into the XGBoost model for classification (Bull/Bear/Neutral), which is mapped into trading signals while integrating the Uncertainty gating decision mechanism to increase reliability. Using the 15minute BTC/USDT dataset from Binance, divided into 70%/15%/15% ensembles, the merged model achieved an accuracy of 74.3 %, macro-F1 of 0.7429, and MCC of 0.4867, outperforming the single-method and baseline methods. The trust-aware gating results further improved the reliability, raising the accuracy and F1 to over 81% with a coverage of 67.74%, with a high threshold exceeding 98% accuracy for selective predictions. The above results demonstrate that the combination of multi-methods with the Uncertainty gating decision mechanism provides a reliable and practical forecasting tool for the volatile cryptocurrency market.
Keywords: Candlestick chart analysis | Cryptocurrency forecasting | Feature fusion with XGBoost | Multimodal deep learning | technical indicators

Title: Research on Microphone Array Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Techniques Based on Deep Learning
Abstract: The microphone array direction finding technique is widely used in the problem of DOA estimation, in which the representative MUSIC algorithm can realize highresolution unbiased estimation. Still, the performance is reduced in complex acoustic environments. The deep learning technique is expected to overcome the limitations of traditional algorithms and bring new development opportunities to this field. Concretely, this paper applies the multilayer perceptual machine model and proposes deep learning-based gridded and ungridded MUSIC algorithms from multi-label classification and regression perspectives, respectively. Simulation experiments show that the proposed algorithms have high estimation accuracy and interference resistance, and under the same conditions, the running time of direction measurement with an eight-element line array is shortened to one-sixth of the original running time; under the condition of a low number of snapshots, the mean-square error of the improved algorithm of deep learning decreases by about 80 % compared with that of the original MUSIC algorithm; under the condition of low signal-To-noise ratio, the mean-square error of the proposed algorithm, MLP-WMUSIC, is always significantly lower than that of the MUSIC algorithm.
Keywords: deep learning | direction of arrival | multi-label categorization | multiple signal classification | regression models

Title: Robot Target Recognition Algorithm with Dual-Layer Deep Feature Fusion
Abstract: Aiming at the problem of insufficient accuracy and real-Time performance of robot target recognition in complex environments, this paper proposes a dual-layer deep feature fusion algorithm. The bottom layer uses an improved convolutional neural network to extract multi-scale basic features, and the upper layer uses the channel and spatial attention mechanism to mine contextual semantic information, and integrates dual-layer features through weighted fusion and adaptive parameter optimization strategies. Experiments were conducted on COCO, self-built warehousing and industrial inspection datasets, with Faster R-CNN, YOLOv5 and other algorithms as controls. The results show that the mAP of this algorithm on the warehousing dataset reaches 92.3%, which is 7.8% higher than YOLOv5; the mAP in the industrial inspection scene is 90.5%, which is 10.2% higher than Faster RCNN. Faced with complex conditions such as lighting changes and 30%, and the average inference time is only 0.08s, meeting the real-Time requirements. Ablation experiments show that two-layer feature fusion and adaptive parameter optimization increase mAP by 5.6% and 3.2% respectively. The algorithm provides an efficient solution for robot target recognition.
Keywords: attention mechanism | deep learning | real-Time performance | Robot target recognition | two-layer feature fusion

Title: Enhancing Content-Based Video-Music Matching using Attention Mechanisms
Abstract: In digital storytelling and multimedia production, background music plays a crucial role in shaping the emotional and perceptual experience of viewers. However, selecting appropriate music for video content remains a manual and often subjective process, lacking scalability and contextual sensitivity. To address this, we propose a content-based video music retrieval system that automatically recommends background music based solely on visual input. Our approach leverages deep learning models to extract high-level semantic features from both video and music, enabling perceptually aligned matches without relying on metadata or user input. Specifically, EfficientNet-B5 is used for visual feature extraction, and attention mechanisms are incorporated to enhance the model's focus on emotionally and semantically rich regions of the video. These enriched representations are matched with audio embeddings derived from a VGGish network using cosine similarity in a shared latent space. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed system significantly improves retrieval performance, offering a scalable solution for intelligent music recommendation in video editing and media production.
Keywords: Attention Mechanisms | Multimodal Deep Learning | Video Music Retrieval

Title: Inspecting Deep Learning Techniques for Music Transcription
Abstract: Music Transcription describes the procedure of transforming audio recordings into symbolic formats such as musical notation or scores. This survey explores key methodologies and architectures of symbolic representations, with a focus on feature extraction and deep learning techniques. It begins with rhythm-based and jSymbolic features, followed by advanced frameworks like PiRhDy, MusicBERT, MIDI2vec, and MusicAOG that enhance symbolic music understanding. A comparative analysis of CNN, DNN, and GNN highlights their respective performance and strengths, while RNN are recognized for capturing temporal dependencies and hierarchical structures. Transformer-based models are discussed in terms of optimization strategies, and diffusion techniques are analyzed. Hybrid models that integrate multiple architectures are also reviewed. Core transcription tasks pitch detection, onset/offset estimation, and polyphonic transcription are emphasized for their foundational role. Lastly, the survey covers key datasets and tools essential for benchmarking and advancing symbolic transcription. The observations herein are intended for a wide audience of researchers, engineers, musicians, educators, and music technology developers among others.
Keywords: CNN | Diffusion | DNN | Features | GNN | RNN | Transformer

Title: Academic Confidence in the Age of AI: A Study on Chatbot-Assisted Learning Among Graduate Learners in Hospitality and Tourism Management
Abstract: This study examines the relationship between chatbot-assisted learning and academic confidence among graduate students in Hospitality and Tourism Management programs in Metro Manila. Grounded in Bandura's Self-Efficacy Theory, the research employed a quantitative, descriptive-correlational design involving 350 Master's and PhD students. Data were gathered using adapted Likert-scale instruments and analyzed through Pearson correlation and linear regression. Findings revealed no significant correlation between chatbot usage and academic confidence, suggesting that while students frequently engage with AI tools, such interactions may not meaningfully influence their self-belief in academic performance. These results challenge assumptions about AI's impact on learner psychology and highlight the limitations of current chatbot systems in fostering self-efficacy. The study contributes to the discourse on digital learning by emphasizing the need for emotionally intelligent, feedback-rich AI integration. Future research should explore mediating variables to uncover the nuanced dynamics between technology and learner confidence.
Keywords: academic confidence | Chatbot-assisted learning

Title: Hear little and Help big - LSTM Enhanced Temporal signal Processor for Infant Vocalization Analysis
Abstract: Hear Little and Help Big' proposes an LSTMbased Temporal Signal Processing pipeline for real-time infant cry analysis, aiming intelligent neonatal monitoring and early detection of distress. The system is based on spectrogrambased preprocessing and extraction of MFCC features to convert cry audio into formatted temporal representations, which are analyzed by a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network involved in classifying the cries into hunger, pain, or discomfort categories. Integrated with a context sensing decision engine, the model translates classifications into prescriptive caregiving actions and sends automatic notifications via an integrated notification module. Built for low-latency systems, the framework exhibits strong performance on noisy datasets and provides a scalable solution for AI-augmented infant care in clinical and home environments. Yet, this model could be constrained by the sample size and demographic makeup of the training dataset, potentially imposing biases on generalization over heterogeneous infant populations. Although early results are encouraging, wider assessment and comparison with current state-of-the-art cry analysis systems would be necessary to establish its full efficacy.
Keywords: Audio signal processing | Emotion recognition | LSTM | Parenting assistant and Neonatal monitoring

Title: A Real-Time Multi-Modal Fatigue Detection System Using Deep Learning and Facial Behavior Analysis
Abstract: Fatigue and drowsiness are significant contributors to road accidents, with studies suggesting they account for about 10-20 percent of cases worldwide. Similar trends are also observed in India, where around one-fifth of accidents involve drivers who are sleep-deprived or fatigued. These conditions can also reduce productivity during prolonged periods of screen use, showing that their impact extends beyond transportation safety. To address this problem, this research proposes a multimodal detection system that integrates physiological signals with real-time monitoring of facial features, including the eyes, mouth, and head. By combining signal processing and deep learning algorithms, the system is designed to be robust and responsive while providing timely audio-visual alerts. The proposed approach supports deployment on portable and embedded devices, making it suitable for real-life applications. This work proposes a solution to improve road safety and promote digital well-being by addressing challenges in camera reliability, multimodal integration, and real-time performance.
Keywords: Computer Vision | Deep Learning | Digital Well-being | Driver Drowsiness Detection | EEG Analysis | Fatigue Monitoring | Multimodal Fusion | Physiological Signals | Real-Time Processing | Road Safety

Title: From Noise to Clarity: Emerging Trends in Speech Enhancement for Real-Time Communication
Abstract: Real-time communication demands speech that is both intelligible and natural, even in noisy environments. This paper traces the progression of speech enhancement from traditional DSP techniques-such as spectral subtraction and Wiener filtering-to modern deep learning and diffusion-based models. While classical methods offer low latency and interpretability, they falter in complex, non-stationary noise. Deep neural networks, including CNNs, RNNs, and transformers, brought adaptive, data-driven noise suppression with superior performance. Most recently, diffusion models have redefined the state-of-the-art, enabling high-fidelity speech reconstruction from heavily corrupted inputs. We present a comparative analysis of these approaches in terms of effectiveness, latency, and deployment feasibility, and highlight the promise of hybrid models that unify DSP precision with generative AI power.
Keywords: deep learning | diffusion models | GANs | generative models | neural audio processing | noise suppression | selfattention | Speech enhancement

Title: From Encoded Features to Quantifying Disfluency: A Deep Learning Approach for Stuttering Severity Classification
Abstract: Stuttering is a speech disorder marked by interruptions in the natural flow of speech, affecting millions globally. Accurately assessing its severity-categorized as mild, moderate, or severe is essential for guiding effective interventions and enhancing speech therapy outcomes. In this study, we address the task of stuttering severity classification using two publicly available datasets: FluencyBank Timestamped and LibriStutter. We extract diverse feature representations from Whisper, Wav2Vec2.0, and MFCCs to capture both learned and handcrafted speech characteristics. These features are evaluated using three deep neural network classifiers: CNN, ResNet50 and Transformer. Among the combinations tested, Whisper-Small embeddings paired with ResNet50 yielded the highest performance, achieving an overall accuracy of 82.1% and an F1 score of 0.778. While, the other Whisper variants also performs fairly competitive with an accuracy of 77.7% on Base and 76.6% on tiny model using ResNet50. Our proposed setup establishes a strong benchmark and a potential state-of-the-art-for future research in automatic stuttering severity assessment.
Keywords: Deep neural network | Handcrafted features | Severity | Stuttering | Wav2Vec2.0 | Whisper

Title: Automating Photometric Measurements Using LabVIEW-Python-Based AI: Enhancing Precision in Luminous Intensity, Responsivity, Illuminance, and Flux Analysis at Saudi Standards, Metrology, and Quality Organization-SASO-KSA
Abstract: - This work explores the automation of a photometry laboratory by integrating LabVIEW as the primary control and data acquisition platform, coupled with a Python-based artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm for intelligent analysis and optimization. The system is designed to measure and analyze critical photometric parameters such as luminous intensity, luminous responsivity, illuminance, and luminous flux—all of which are essential for evaluating the performance of light sources like tungsten halogen lamps, LEDs, displays, and optical sensors. By automating traditionally manual processes, the system enhances both the accuracy and efficiency of photometric testing. LabVIEW provides an intuitive graphical interface to control instruments, log data, and visualize results in real time. Meanwhile, the Python AI component improves decision-making by learning from historical data, predicting trends, and detecting anomalies or inconsistencies in measurements. The AI model optimizes calibration routines, reduces human error, and enables adaptive testing scenarios based on environmental conditions or device behavior. Together, LabVIEW and Python form a powerful, flexible platform that brings modern intelligence to photometry labs, making them faster, smarter, and more reliable. This approach demonstrates how combining industrial automation tools with machine learning can revolutionize traditional optical testing environments, paving the way for advanced lighting technologies and robust quality assurance systems.
Keywords: AI | Algorithms | Automation | Flux | Illuminance | NMCC | Photometry | Python | Responsivity | SASO

Title: Synthetic Speech Detection via Multi-Generator GANs with Anomaly Detection Architectures
Abstract: Advancement in text-to-speech and voice conversion have enabled highly realistic synthetic voices, resulting in threats to cybersecurity, and fraud prevention. Classic classifiers and deep learning models often struggle to generalize across diverse spoofing conditions. In this work, we propose two improved anomaly detection architectures for synthetic speech detection: Enhanced D-AnoGAN (eD-AnoGAN) and Multi-generator RESGANomaly (RES-MGANomaly). eD-AnoGAN removes the bandit prior by directly assigning clusters to generator-encoder branches and incorporates a latent consistency loss during training, while RES-MGANomaly extends RES-GANomaly by introducing multiple residual-attention generators with shared encoders. On WaveFake, eD-AnoGAN with latent consistency achieves the highest performance with an AUC of 0.9211 and F1 of 0.8957, while RES-MGANomaly also performs strongly with an AUC of 0.9030. In cross-dataset evaluation on ASVspoof2019 LA, eD-AnoGAN attains the best generalization with an AUC of 0.8428 and F1 of 0.7956. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of multi-generator anomaly detection in improving robustness against synthetic speech attacks.
Keywords: Anomaly detection | Anti-spoofing | Generative adversarial networks | Speech processing | Speech synthesis

Title: Human Personality Analysis and Enhancer using AI
Abstract: This research explores the application of logistic regression for classifying individuals into five distinct personality types: responsible, serious, extraverted and lively and dependable. The classification is based on a dataset comprising 709 individuals, each of whom is evaluated on five key personality traits: PEN affiliative traits include: openness to experience, negative emotionality, conscientiousness, agreeableness, and extraversion. These traits are known in psychology as the important factors that define behaviour and predispositions of the persons. The logistic regression analysis, often used and easy to explain, is applied to the analysis of the links between these personality traits and the respective personality type. The model aims at identifying personality type given certain interaction and level of importance of the traits in question. An important advantage of using logistic regression is the provision of probability values for each class, with results in class predictions as well as their likelihood. For its assessment, the model uses more than one key performance indicator: accuracy, precision, recall, and F1score which provide an objective picture of the effectiveness of the model. The proposed logistic regression classifier produces an overall accuracy of 76 percent with reasonable precision and recall rates for each of the five personality classes. These outcomes lead to the conclusion that logistic regression can be considered as an effective and accurate instrument of personality classification.
