In addition, the model comes with interpretability, the ability to explain the outcomes of each trait with regards to the probability of a certain personality classification.
Keywords: AI-based system | Big Five Personality Traits | career advice | machine learning | personal growth | personality prediction | psychological evaluations

Title: Leveraging domain-adaptation to improve chlorophyll-a estimates from satellite derived multispectral data.
Abstract: — Monitoring the health of essential freshwater and coastal ecosystems like lakes and estuaries requires estimating water quality indicators (WQIs) like chlorophyll-a from remote sensing data. Machine learning (ML)-based regression tools are a popular choice for this estimation task. Training such models requires a labeled dataset comprising of co-located measurements of remote sensing variables and WQIs. To address this need, practitioners primarily use co-located in situ measurements of remote sensing reflectance and WQIs to train ML models. While these ML models outperform other analytical/empirical methods for the chlorophyll-a estimation tasks on labeled in situ datasets, their performance deteriorates quite significantly when applied to satellite datasets. Using satellite-based training datasets is infeasible given the paucity of co-located measurements of satellite-derived variables and WQIs, especially for newer sensors. To address the discrepancy between the training (in situ) datasets and application (satellite) datasets, we will leverage domain adaptation (DA), i.e., an ML trick to transfer knowledge from a source (in situ) domain with abundant labeled examples to a related target domain with little or no labeled data (satellite). To demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, we implement Domain Adaptation for REgression by aligning inverse GRAM matrices (DARE-GRAM) for the chlorophyll-a estimation task. This regression-specific domain adaptation technique uses the labeled source (in situ) data and unlabeled satellite data (i.e., only the remote sensing reflectance) to build a model with improved chlorophyll-a estimation for satellite datasets. We test this approach using data from two popular multispectral sensors, namely, Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI) and Sentinel-3 Ocean and Land Colour Imager (OLCI). The DARE-GRAM shows improvements of between 20-50% across a wide range of regression metrics, indicating a comprehensive improvement in the estimation performance relative to classical ML methods. The DARE-GRAM method also shows significantly improved agreement for chlorophyll-a estimates from near-simultaneous acquisitions from the different sensors. This improved harmony is expected to be an important step in creating consistent cross-sensor products.
Keywords: chlorophyll-a | domain adaptation | machine learning | multispectral | remote sensing | water quality indicators

Title: Audio Recognition-based Method for RF Transmitters Classification using CNN-LSTM model
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Radio Frequency transmitter classification that adapts audio recognition techniques to enhance device identification accuracy. By leveraging Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) and spectral characteristics traditionally used in audio processing, combined with a hybrid CNN-LSTM deep learning architecture, our method achieves 93.6% classification accuracy across 8 devices in same-scenario testing. The approach demonstrates strong initial performance comparable to state-of-the-art RF fingerprinting methods, while also providing insights into cross-scenario challenges under varying operational conditions. Our experimental results, conducted using a dataset of commercial RF transmitters, highlight both the potential of audio-inspired features for RF fingerprinting and the persistent challenge of maintaining classification reliability across different operational conditions. This work contributes to the growing field of physicallayer security by demonstrating how cross-domain adaptation of proven audio processing techniques can enhance RF device identification.
Keywords: audio recognition | CNN | LSTM | MFCC | physicallayer security | RF fingerprinting

Title: Precision in Sound: A Comprehensive Framework for Advanced Gender Recognition from Audio Data
Abstract: Gender recognition from audio data has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its wide-ranging applications in security, surveillance, and human-computer interaction. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for gender recognition solely from audio inputs, addressing the complexities and challenges inherent in audio-based gender classification. The framework encompasses a multi-faceted approach, integrating sophisticated audio processing techniques with state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms. Key components of the framework include data preprocessing, model training, and real-time inference, facilitated by PyAudio for audio input/output, Librosa for feature extraction, and TensorFlow/Keras for deep learning. Moreover, the framework incorporates utility functions to streamline data manipulation and model construction tasks, enhancing efficiency and scalability. The proposed framework undergoes rigorous evaluation across diverse datasets and real-world scenarios to assess its robustness and efficacy. Experimental results demonstrate the framework's capability to achieve high accuracy in gender classification, outperforming existing methods. Notably, the framework exhibits resilience to noise and variability in audio inputs, showcasing its adaptability to challenging environments. Additionally, real-time inference capabilities enable seamless integration into interactive systems, further extending its utility across various applications. Furthermore, this paper provides an in-depth analysis of the framework's performance, highlighting its strengths, limitations, and avenues for future research. Insights gained from the analysis contribute to the ongoing refinement and enhancement of gender recognition technology. The framework's applicability extends beyond academic research to practical implementation in real-world scenarios, offering a valuable resource for practitioners and researchers in audio signal processing and machine learning domains. In conclusion, this research presents a significant advancement in gender recognition from audio data, offering a comprehensive and effective framework that addresses the complexities of audio-based gender classification. By leveraging advanced audio processing techniques and machine learning algorithms, the framework represents a significant step forward in the development of robust and reliable gender recognition systems.
Keywords: Audio data analysis | Deep learning | Gender recognition | Librosa | Machine learning | PyAudio | Real-time inference | TensorFlow/Keras

Title: Research on the Application of Transformer, GAN and Q-learning in Piano Improvisational Accompaniment Teaching
Abstract: In recent years, the integration of cloud computing and artificial intelligence technologies has brought revolutionary changes to the field of education. This study proposes a cloud-based AI framework, leveraging Transformer, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), and Q-learning technologies, aiming to optimize the efficiency and personalized experience of piano improvisational accompaniment teaching. Through Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), the digital conversion of audio signals into MIDI format is achieved, and digital information processing technology is used for feature extraction. The methods include system architecture design supported by distributed cloud computing, sequence modeling with Transformer, stylized accompaniment generation with GAN, and reinforcement learning optimization with Q-learning. Experiments were conducted using Muqam-style musical score data for testing, verifying the framework's adaptability under different emotional styles. The experimental results indicate that the framework significantly outperforms traditional teaching methods in terms of feedback accuracy (96.1%±1.2%), learning efficiency (improved by 34.7%±3.5%), model stability (variance 0.015), and response time (0.22 seconds). This research provides a new paradigm for the engineering application of AI technology in the field of music education. Future work may further optimize performance in high-concurrency scenarios.
Keywords: Cloud-based AI Framewor | Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) | music education | piano improvisational accompaniment | Q-learning | transformer

Title: AI-Driven Data Cleansing and Representation Learning for CRM Optimization: A Webly-Supervised Approach
Abstract: In modern CRM systems, maintaining high-quality data while handling large-scale, weakly labeled information remains a notable difficulty. This study introduces Momentum Prototypes (MoPro), a novel AI-driven approach created to improve data accuracy, classification, and prognostic modeling in customer relationship management (CRM). Leveraging websupervised learning, MoPro efficiently corrects noisy labels and eliminates out-of-distribution data, guaranteeing cleaner and more dependable and trustworthy datasets for Salesforce AIdriven automation instruments like Einstein Analytics. The proposed model shows superior performance in customer segmentation, guidance scoring, and automated decision-making by learning strong and durable representations from varied and distinct, unstructured datasets.... predictive accuracy, making it a valuable addition to Salesforce's AI ecosystem. In a Q2 Salesforce org managing 5 million leads, MoPro identified 8% mislabeled state entries, enhancing primary conversion AUC by 0.04. This CRM-oriented augmentation reinforces MoPro's real-world impact beyond common and nonspecific benchmarks.
Keywords: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) | Einstein Analytics | Forecasting analysis | Information accuracy | Momentum Prototypes (MoPro) | Noisy Label Correction | Out-ofDistribution Data | Salesforce | Webly-Supervised Learning

Title: Multi-Task Frequency Attentive Network for Lightweight Small Aerial Target Classification
Abstract: Accurate classification of low-altitude, slow-moving, small radar cross-section aerial targets, such as drones and birds, is essential for radar surveillance. Among existing studies, traditional machine learning methods often struggle with performance, while popular deep learning models, such as ResNet and YOLO, tend to be overly complex and computationally intensive. To achieve a balance between model performance and complexity, this paper proposes a lightweight multi-task frequency attentive network that leverages 128-point fast Fourier transform spectral features derived from radar echoes. The proposed network architecture integrates a convolutional encoder-decoder with a lightweight classification head, where input features are first extracted by the encoder with adaptive frequency attention using multi-scale depthwise convolutions. Latent features are then jointly optimized within a collaborative multi-task framework involving both the decoder and the classifier, enabling compact and efficient end-to-end learning. Experiments show that the proposed model achieves promising results with a mere 0.23M parameters and 4.53M FLOPs.
Keywords: attention mechanism | convolutional neural network | lightweight | small aerial target classification

Title: Vox2Brief: Summarizing Conversational Medical Narratives
Abstract: This paper provides a thorough analysis and evaluation of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) capacities, in this case the performance of the OpenAI Whisper Medium model. We describe the end-to-end system architecture for audio processing and transcribing, and its rigorous assessment using industry-standard jiwer library metrics: Word Error Rate (WER), Character Error Rate (CER), and Match Error Rate (MER). Experimental performance on a well-chosen audio sample, we show the model's exceptional ability to translate spoken English into text. We also use a Flan-T5-based summarization module to translate medical accounts into patient-readable accounts. The strong performance obtained indicates the extensive value of large-scale pre-trained models in bridging the gap between human speech and digital text across many applications. In addition, the paper explains the implications of such great accuracy for real-world deployments and specifies directions of future research, such as large-scale evaluation on multiform datasets and investigation of real-time ASR systems. This paper adds to the increasing amount of knowledge about state-of-the-art ASR model performance in real-world cases and their ability to improve human-computer interaction.
Keywords: ASR | Automatic Speech Recognition | CER | Deep Learning | Machine Learning | Natural Language Processing | Speech-to-Text | WER | Whisper Model

Title: VocalMorse: Voice-to-Morse-Code Generation
Abstract: Speech-to-text systems and Morse code serve critical roles in assistive and constrained communication. Building a bridge between multilingual spoken input and symbolic Morse output is technically challenging due to language variability and noise. The model propose a modular pipeline using Whisper for speech transcription, NLP for text refinement, and a custom Morse converter for final output. The system achieved over 92.1% conversion accuracy in tests across Hindi and English speech samples. Our solution demonstrates real-time, accurate, and scalable multilingual speech-to-Morse conversion with practical applications in accessibility and emergency systems.
Keywords: accessibility technology | assistive communication | low-bandwidth communication | Morse code generation | multilingual speech processing | natural language processing(NLP) | Real-time audio processing | Speech recognition | Whisper model

Title: LIGHT-CONE FEATURE SELECTION IN METHANE HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGES
Abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) capture detailed spectral information across numerous contiguous bands, enabling the extraction of intrinsic characteristics of scanned objects and areas. This study focuses on the application of light-cone feature selection in quantum machine learning for methane detection and localization using HSIs. The proposed method leverages quantum methods to enhance feature selection and classification accuracy. The dataset used includes HSIs collected by the AVIRIS-NG instrument captured in geographically diverse locations. In this study, we investigate the performance of support vector machine classifiers with different classic and quantum kernels. The results indicate that the quantum kernel classifier, combined with light-cone feature selection, provides in one metric, superior performance when compared to the classic techniques. It demonstrates the potential of quantum machine learning in improving the remote sensing data analysis for environmental monitoring.
Keywords: classification | Earth observation | feature selection | methane detection | Quantum Machine Learning

Title: DDUNet: Dual Dynamic U-Net for Highly-Efficient Cloud Segmentation
Abstract: —Cloud segmentation amounts to separating cloud pixels from non-cloud pixels in an image. Current deep learning methods for cloud segmentation suffer from three issues. (a) Constrain on their receptive field due to the fixed size of the convolution kernel. (b) Lack of robustness towards different scenarios. (c) Requirement of a large number of parameters and limitations for real-time implementation. To address these issues, we propose a Dual Dynamic U-Net (DDUNet) for supervised cloud segmentation. The DDUNet adheres to a U-Net architecture and integrates two crucial modules: the dynamic multi-scale convolution (DMSC), improving merging features under different reception fields, and the dynamic weights and bias generator (DWBG) in classification layers to enhance generalization ability. More importantly, owing to the use of depth-wise convolution, the DDUNet is a lightweight network that can achieve 95.3% accuracy on the SWINySEG dataset with only 0.33M parameters, and achieve superior performance over three different configurations of the SWINySEg dataset in both accuracy and efficiency. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/Att100/DDUNet.
Keywords: cloud segmentation | deep learning | dynamic convolution | reception field | U-Net

Title: Evaluating a Convolutional Neural Network Calibration Model with Laboratory Data
Abstract: In-orbit calibration of Smallsat and Cubesat sensors can be challenging due to fluctuations arising from sensitivity to solar radiation and imperfect calibration sources. In order to maintain low revisit times and minimize downtime, Cubesat instruments are often powered off during eclipse, or rapidly power cycled on and off to reduce average power consumption. Power cycling during eclipse can result in a steep transient curve when the instrument is powered back on, and while rapid power cycling can produce continuous measurements, it is done so at the cost of increased measurement uncertainty due to the same transient effect at each turn-on. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model has been demonstrated to calibrate over the turn-on transient effect in a synthetic radiometer calibration dataset with greatly improved accuracy and precision compared to a conventional linear least-squares regression (LSR) calibration algorithm [1]. In order to validate these results in a practical setting, a laboratory radiometer is used to produce two-point calibration data in a laboratory setting with liquid nitrogen (LN2) as a contrasting target to a blackbody target at ambient room temperature. A calibration dataset for CNN training is created using an optical chopping wheel to create alternating cycles of observations between the two calibration targets. The CNN model is then compared to a conventional LSR model by evaluating both models an on independent test dataset, generated in the same manner as the initial training dataset. The results of this experiment will be presented to validate the performance of a CNN calibration model in a practical laboratory setting.
Keywords: machine learning | microwave | power cycling | radiometer | smallsat

Title: Edge Machine Learning for Forest Acoustic Monitoring Implementation
Abstract: Forest preservation faces significant threats from illegal logging and fires, demanding effective real-time monitoring solutions in remote environments. Conventional approaches often struggle with heavy data transmission burdens or compromise model performance due to limited edge device resources. This paper proposes a low-cost, real-time forest acoustic monitoring system that leverages on-device machine learning for efficient event detection. Our solution employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with the YAMNet model as a feature extractor, fine-tuned on a curated subset of the ESC-50 dataset to classify six critical forest-related sounds, including 'chainsaw', 'footsteps', 'crackling-fire', 'rain', 'engine', and 'hand-saw'.The system acquires audio segments, processes them in 1 -second windows, and classifies acoustic events directly on a Raspberry Pi 3. To ensure reliable data transmission in challenging remote conditions, the classified event outputs are encoded into compact messages and transmitted via LoRaWAN. The fine-tuned model achieved promising performance with an 88.3% accuracy, 88.5% precision, 88.3% recall, and an F 1-score of 87.9% on the test set. This approach demonstrates the feasibility of deploying highlevel audio classification on resource-constrained edge platforms, enabling real-time alerting and enhancing forest preservation efforts in real-world scenarios.
Keywords: Acoustic Monitoring | Environmental sound classification | LoRa | Machine Learning

Title: DIGITAL ELEVATION MODEL ESTIMATION FROM RGB SATELLITE IMAGERY USING GENERATIVE DEEP LEARNING
Abstract: Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are vital datasets for geospatial applications such as hydrological modeling and environmental monitoring. However, conventional methods to generate DEM, such as using LiDAR and photogrammetry, require specific types of data that are often inaccessible in resource-constrained settings. To alleviate this problem, this study proposes an approach to generate DEM from freely available RGB satellite imagery using generative deep learning, particularly based on a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (GAN). We first developed a global dataset consisting of 12K RGB-DEM pairs using Landsat satellite imagery and NASA’s SRTM digital elevation data, both from the year 2000. A unique preprocessing pipeline was implemented to select high-quality, cloud-free regions and aggregate normalized RGB composites from Landsat imagery. Additionally, the model was trained in a two-stage process, where it was first trained on the complete dataset and then fine-tuned on high-quality samples filtered by Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) values to improve performance on challenging terrains. The results demonstrate promising performance in mountainous regions, achieving an overall mean root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.4671 and a mean SSIM score of 0.2065 (scale -1 to 1), while highlighting limitations in lowland and residential areas. This study underscores the importance of meticulous preprocessing and iterative refinement in generative modeling for DEM generation, offering a cost-effective and adaptive alternative to conventional methods while emphasizing the challenge of generalization across diverse terrains worldwide.
Keywords: Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) | Digital Elevation Model (DEM) | Generative Deep Learning | RGB Satellite Imagery

Title: Task-Based Forecast Evaluation for Model Selection in Make-to-Order Manufacturing
Abstract: In the face of persistent uncertainty in sales forecasting, companies must navigate forecast errors to support effective decision-making. Aligning forecast evaluation with concrete planning tasks is therefore crucial for actionable sales forecasts in make-to-order (MTO) SMEs. We present a four-step framework: (1) Task Definition, where decision contexts are identified based on the Hannover supply-chain model and complementary sources; (2) Metric Mapping, which pairs each task with tailored error families - scale-invariant measures (MASE, sMAPE), bias indicators (MPE), probabilistic scores (Pinball Loss, CRPS), and decision-driven metrics (Cost-Weighted MAE, Service-Level Penalty, Inventory Holding Score); (3) Model Benchmarking, deploying five algorithms (ETS, SARIMA, Gradient Boosted Trees, Random Forest, LSTM) on a ten-year monthly demand series from a consumer-durables SME; and (4) Multi-Criteria Ranking, ranking model performance based on a configurable set of evaluation criteria. This structured approach ensures forecast metrics directly reflect user needs, streamlines evaluation, and delivers measurable business impact in resource-constrained industrial settings.
Keywords: Benchmarking | Demand Volatility | Machine Learning Forecasting | Make-to-Order Production | Sales Forecasting | Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises

Title: Enhancing Digital Strategic Performance in Higher Education through AI-Enabled Strategic Capabilities
Abstract: This study aims to discover how strategic capabilities supported by AI tools contribute to achieving digital strategic performance, which is assessed from financial, stakeholder, internal operations, AI enablers, education and research, learning and development, and institutional image perspectives in higher education and particularly in private universities. The descriptive analytical strategy was utilized for the presentation, analysis, and interpretation of research data, as it facilitates the collection of extensive information pertinent to the research problem. The study was executed in private universities and colleges within Anbar Governorate, targeting a population of 90 senior and midlevel Managerial leaders, including the university president, vice presidents, deans and their deputies, department heads, and division directors. A comprehensive enumeration method was employed, resulting in the distribution of 90 questionnaires, of which 87 valid responses were received for statistical analysis, yielding a response rate of 97%, The researcher utilized the questionnaire as the primary instrument for data collection. To analyze the data, various statistical methods were employed, including the mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, variance, Pearson correlation coefficient, simple regression, and multiple regression, utilizing the SPSS V. 28 and AMOS V. 28 software programs. The researcher found results that mostly matched the research predictions, showing strong connections between the strategic capabilities and its parts within the strategic performance, as well as a clear positive impact of the AI strategic capabilities on the digital strategic performance in private universities and colleges in Anbar Governorate.
Keywords: Digitalization | Higher education | SDG4 | Strategic capabilities | strategic performance

Title: A Biochemical Reaction Anomaly Detection System Based on Stage-Awareness and Spatiotemporal Features
Abstract: Biochemical reaction instruments are vital for nucleic acid testing, but anomalies like uneven liquid stratification, bubble interference, or mechanical failures during extraction can cause experimental errors and resource wastage. Traditional sensorbased monitoring faces limitations in coverage, cost, and realtime performance. This study presents a video-based anomaly detection system for nucleic acid extraction, tested on a laboratorydeveloped instrument. The system combines ResNet18 for adaptive video segmentation, CLIP ViT-B/32 for robust visual feature extraction, Bi-LSTM for temporal dependency modeling, and PU learning to address data imbalance, enabling real-time anomaly detection. Evaluated on a self-constructed dataset with simulated anomalies, the model achieves a ROC AUC of {0. 7 7 8 4, } {8 0} percent accuracy, and zero false negatives, ensuring clinical safety. This work's core value lies in developing an integrated stageaware spatiotemporal framework (ResNet18+CLIP+Bi-LSTM) to address sensor-based monitoring limitations, designing a weighted loss and adaptive threshold for clinical safety, and enabling early intervention within the 6 -minute extraction phase-reducing reagent waste by 90-95 percent, saving 45-90 minutes per detection, and offering a scalable solution for high-throughput testing and other biochemical instruments.
Keywords: Biochemical Reaction Instruments | Deep Learning | Time series model | Video Anomaly Detection

Title: Explainable Deep Learning Approach for Automated Classification of Retinal Diseases Using OCT Images and Grad-CAM
Abstract: The retinal conditions cause the most vision loss across the globe, and it is necessary to diagnose the retinal disease properly and in time. Optical Coherence Tomography, also known by the initials OCT, is a non-invasive imaging test of the retina characterized as being in high-resolution, cross-sectional imaging, and through it, the detection of disease is possible. The proposed approach was a deep learning-based solution to automating the classification of retinal OCT images into four classes, including CNV, DME, DRUSEN, and NORMAL. Daily, a huge amount of approximately 85,000 labeled OCT images was used to develop and train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. A massive preprocessing was done on the dataset involving resizing the images, converting the RGB values, and data augmentation to improve model robustness and generalization. The CNN model proposed was trained by Adam optimizer and took 10 epochs to attain 96% accuracy in terms of classification performance, appreciable precision, recall, and F1-score in all categories. Grad-CAM visualization was performed to enhance interpretability; areas relevant to disease were highlighted in OCT images, and the manner in which the model reached its decision provided visual decisions. The findings prove the potential of deep learning techniques, with the help of explainability methods, to be a fruitful and trustworthy instrument in the diagnosis of retinal disease and help ophthalmologists during clinical decision-making.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) | Deep Learning | Image Classification | Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) | Retinal Diseases

Title: Smart Lab 360- Accelerating Lab Performance Through Smart Integration of Instruments, LIMS, and AI-driven Insights
Abstract: This paper presents the transformative journey of ADNOC Central Lab as it leverages integrated digital platforms and AI-driven technologies to redefine laboratory efficiency and data integrity. By seamlessly connecting advanced laboratory instruments with a robust Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) and incorporating smart AI assistants and IoT-enabled devices, the lab has established a foundation for real-time data flow, automated analytics, and heightened regulatory compliance. The approach ensures secure, end-to-end sample management, agile workflow assignments, and advanced quality control, supporting ADNOC's commitment to operational excellence and innovation in the era of intelligent laboratories.

Title: Intelligent Multi-Well Lithofacies Identification Using Adaptive Wavelet Networks with Dynamic Domain Alignment: A Case Study of Carbonate Reservoir in the Mesopotamian Basin
Abstract: Accurate lithofacies identification from well logs remains a critical challenge in reservoir characterization in the Mesopotamian Basin, Middle East, particularly when extending models across multiple wells, given the varying geological conditions and logging tool responses between well locations. Traditional machine learning approaches suffer from significant performance degradation when applied to new wells, typically experiencing 30-40% accuracy reduction due to inter-well data distribution shifts. This limitation necessitates extensive manual recalibration and limits the practical deployment of automated interpretation systems. To address these challenges, this study presents an innovative Adaptive Geo-Wavelet Network with Dynamic Domain Alignment (AGW-DDA) that integrates multi-scale geological features with intelligent cross-well adaptation mechanisms. The proposed AGW-DDA framework employs a three-branch architecture to extract complementary geological features from well log data. The first branch utilizes lifting-based adaptive wavelet transforms to capture multi-scale stratigraphic patterns, automatically adjusting decomposition parameters based on local geological characteristics. The second branch applies continuous wavelet transform specifically to spontaneous potential (SP) curves, revealing sedimentary rhythms at scales ranging from individual beds to sequence boundaries. The third branch digitalizes traditional petrophysical relationships through correlation analysis of key log pairs, incorporating domain expertise into the learning process. These features are intelligently fused using attention mechanisms before undergoing dynamic domain adaptation, which selectively aligns only mid-frequency components to preserve crucial geological information while correcting for instrument-related variations. Application to a 46-well dataset with Mishrif, Rumaila, Ahmadi, Wara, and Mauddud formations of the Mesopotamian basin demonstrates the effectiveness of the AGW-DDA approach in maintaining cross-well performance. While conventional methods show 30-40% performance degradation on new wells, the proposed method maintains over 85% of its training performance for every individual well through dynamic adaptation. Specifically, the system achieves an average lithofacies classification accuracy of 87.3% across all test wells, with boundary detection precision improving by 25% compared to baseline methods. The multi-scale analysis reveals previously undetected thin interbeds and complex lithological transitions, particularly in heterogeneous carbonate sequences. Computational efficiency analysis shows that the three-branch architecture can process a typical well log suite in under 2 minutes using standard GPU hardware, making it suitable for real-time applications. This research introduces a novel integration of adaptive wavelet analysis with dynamic domain adaptation for multi-well lithofacies identification. The AGW-DDA framework successfully bridges traditional geological interpretation methods with modern deep learning techniques, providing both high accuracy and interpretability. The approach offers a practical solution for automated well log interpretation across diverse geological settings, with particular relevance for mature fields requiring consistent interpretation across numerous wells.
Keywords: Adaptive Wavelet Transform | Case Study | Dynamic Domain Adaptation | Intelligent Lithofacies Identification | Multi-Well Analysis

Title: Predictive Analytics and Machine Learning for Real-Time Emotion Detection and Employee Well-Being Optimization
Abstract: Surveys, performance evaluations, and basic HR analytics, the usual instruments for tracking employee well-being, are subjective, slow, and incapable of capturing quick emotional changes. Stress, weariness, or burnout have already had an impact on productivity and satisfaction; therefore, such reactive systems operate in such a way. The predictive approach, utilizing multimodal data and machine learning, surmounts these limitations by enabling immediate identification of emotions and enabling action in situations where emotions are at their peak. Long-term monitoring uses neural models with a unique architecture that includes facial expressions, voice tone, text sentiment, wearable data, and behavioral patterns. Predictive analytics anticipates possible dangers such as burnout, allowing time to act by balancing workloads, motivating staff to take mindfulness breaks, or having HR reach out. The experimental evaluation demonstrates considerable gains over previous methods in total emotion recognition (93.6%), burnout risk (47.2%), and stress detection (92.5%). It has major implications for improving workplace well-being.
Keywords: Employee Well-Being | Predictive Analytics | Real-Time Emotion Detection | Sentiment Analysis | Stress Prediction | Workplace Optimization

Title: A Comprehensive Survey on Machine and Deep Learning Techniques for Genre Prediction in Folk Songs
Abstract: Music genre prediction, particularly for folk songs, has become an important area in Music Information Retrieval (MIR), combining computational methods with cultural preservation. This paper evaluates Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques applied to folk song classification, showcasing progress and remaining gaps. Traditional models such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Narve Bayes, and Decision Trees are still used but result in limited scalability and cannot capture complex audio patterns. In contrast, modern architectures, including Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), and Transformers, deliver stronger performance in genre identification. Analysis of over thirty publications suggests transformer-based models like BERT, DistilBERT, Wav2Vec2, and Audio Spectrogram Transformers (AST) achieve higher accuracy in music genre classification. However, dataset imbalance and underrepresentation of folk music remain challenges. The review concludes by analyzing contributions, datasets, techniques, and limitations across studies, recommending future work focus on multimodal feature integration, transfer learning, and solutions for low-resource folk music domains to ensure improved performance and cultural inclusivity.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Folk Songs | Machine Learning | Music Genre Classification | Music Information Retrieval | Transformers

Title: A Novel Deep Learning Model for Enhancing Chest X-Ray Assessment Using CXRIA-Net
Abstract: A key diagnostic technique for recognizing several lung diseases gives pneumonia, TB, and COVID-19 chest X-ray (CXR) imaging is Manual interpreting CXR pictures, on the other hand, might be laborious and prone to inter-observer variation. This paper presents CXRIA-Net, a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) meant to improve chest X-ray picture assessment precision as well as effectiveness. Employing advanced deep learning technology, the approach simplifies feature extraction, enhances disease classifying, and reduces diagnostic mistakes. The above technique trains CXRIA-Net on a sizable dataset of identified chest X-ray images using transfer learning together with data augmenting to maximize performance. The model shows better precision, sensitiveness, and specificity in finding anomalies when compared to functioning state-of-the-art CNN architectures. Experimental investigations indicate that CXRIA-Net demonstrates excellent diagnostic precision capabilities which establish it as a promising instrument to assist radiologists and healthcare employees during medical imaging assessment. This paper demonstrates how deep learning integration with medical imaging technology reveals AI applications which benefit patient results and radiological task operations. The proposed CXRIA-Net model demonstrates excellent potential to help detect diseases early which enables better clinical decisions and operates with enhanced healthcare system efficiency.
Keywords: chest X-ray | Convolutional neural network | CXRIA-Net | deep learning | disease diagnosis | healthcare | Medical Imaging

Title: Real-Time Forgery Detection via Dynamic Frequency-Domain Selection and Phoneme Alignment
Abstract: The proliferation of deep learning-based video forgery, known as DeepFakes, poses a significant threat to information integrity and digital security, particularly in real-time communication scenarios. Existing detection methods often struggle with three critical challenges: performance degradation due to video compression, a limited capacity to detect subtle audio-visual semantic inconsistencies, and excessive computational latency for real-time deployment. This paper introduces a lightweight, multi-modal framework designed to address these limitations. Our method employs a dual-stream architecture for parallel analysis of visual and auditory signals. Key contributions include: a novel dynamic frequency band selection module that adaptively isolates and enhances faint forgery artifacts from heavily compressed video streams; a phoneme-aligned cross-modal verification system that precisely quantifies lip-audio temporal desynchronization to detect semantic mismatches; and a lightweight hybrid architecture integrating ResNet3D and Mamba for efficient spatiotemporal modeling. Validated on benchmarks like CelebDF and FaceForensics++, our method achieves a state-of-the-art trade-off, delivering accuracy competitive with leading methods at a fraction of the computational cost, thus enabling practical real-time deployment.
Keywords: deepfake detection | frequency domain | multi-modal analysis | phoneme-viseme mismatch | real-time systems | state-space models

Title: AFTR-HAR-Net: Adaptive Fusion and Temporal Reasoning Network for Robust Human Activity Recognition
Abstract: In this era, Human Activity Recognition (HAR) has become a crucial component in healthcare monitoring, fitness tracking and smart IoT applications. Specifically, attaining accurate classification still struggles with various challenges where the deep learning approaches have limitations with multimodal fusion and efficient temporal modelling that leads to suboptimal performance on sensor data. Therefore, to resolve these limitations, this research proposes an Adaptive Fusion and Temporal Reasoning Human Activity Recognition Network (AFTR-HAR-Net) which is a lightweight robust framework that combines adaptive sensor fusion, a dilated Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) encoder and an Attention-guided GRU temporal reasoning module. In particular, the adaptive fusion mechanism learns modalityspecific significance weights which assists to improve resilience to sensor imbalance, then the dilated CNN captures multi-scale temporal features with minimal computational cost. Further, the GRU and attention layers helps to refine temporal dependencies which improves the discrimination of overlapping activities. The proposed AFTR-HAR-Net acquired higher results with 98.12% accuracy and 97.89% F1-Score when compared with the existing hybrid model namely CNN with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory.
Keywords: adaptive fusion | convolutional neural network | gated recurrent unit | human activity recognition | temporal reasoning

Title: A Network with High-Frequency Feature Extraction and Feature Recalibration Mechanisms for Chinese Speech Recognition
Abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, speech recognition has become an important form of humancomputer interaction. Chinese speech recognition faces unique challenges due to tones, homophones, and dialect differences. To enhance recognition performance and robustness, a novel network named LCHANet was proposed. A DSCSE module that combines depthwise separable convolution (DSC) and squeeze-andexcitation (SE) networks, along with a lightweight-improved attention mechanism (FECA), is included in this model to achieve efficient feature extraction and channel recalibration. Compared with the baseline model, the LCHANet proposed in this paper has reduced the character error rate (CER) by 13.45% on the THCHS-30 dataset. Ablation studies further validate the contribution of each module, demonstrating that both the FECA and DSCSE modules play crucial roles in performance improvement. The proposed method delivers an efficient and precise solution for Chinese speech recognition, showcasing remarkable performance.
Keywords: Chinese Speech Recognition | Deep Separable Network | DSCSE | FECA | LCHANet | SE

Title: Spoken Language Recognition for Indonesian Local Languages Using Deep Learning
Abstract: This paper presents a spoken language identification (LID) system for seven Indonesian local languages: Acehnese, Balinese, Batak Toba, Javanese, Sundanese, Yawa, and Rote. The dataset was constructed from audio.sabda.org, with recordings standardized, normalized, and segmented into 3-second utterances to ensure consistent input. Three deep learning architectures were evaluated: a baseline CNN, ResNet-50, and DenseNet-121, trained on multiple acoustic features including MFCC, log-Mel spectrograms, and shifted delta coefficients (SDC). Hyperparameters were optimized using random search, resulting in nine best-performing configurations. Experimental results show that deeper architectures substantially outperform CNN, with ResNet-50 trained on SDC achieving the highest overall performance (81 % accuracy, FRR 0.19, EER 0.07, C avg 0.11). Per-class analysis reveals that Balinese and Rote are recognized with near-perfect accuracy, while Batak Toba and Javanese exhibit higher error rates due to phonotactic similarities. Compared to prior work, the proposed system achieves competitive performance despite being trained on a relatively small dataset. The findings confirm that residual networks combined with temporal features provide a robust backbone for low-resource spoken language identification, and highlight promising directions for extending research on Indonesian languages.
Keywords: Indonesian Local Languages | Low-Resource Speech Processing | Random Search | ResNet-50 | Spoken Language Identification

Title: Fast and Labor-Efficient Visual Algorithm for Automated Reading of Water Treatment Instrumentation
Abstract: In water treatment facilities, routine inspection of instruments such as pressure gauges and flow meters is essential yet relies on manual, labor-intensive, and error-prone visual checks. While small computer vision models offer an automation solution, they require large annotated datasets, making them costly and impractical for industrial use. To address these challenges, this research proposes a fast and labor-efficient multimodal solution for automated instrument reading. Leveraging multimodal technology, the approach reduces annotation efforts and accelerates deployment. The study compares performance between multimodal and non-multimodal models using an industrial dataset. A practical visual system is developed, achieving acceptable accuracy with minimal manual input, thus demonstrating a scalable, cost-effective approach for real-world industrial applications.
Keywords: Automated Instrument Reading | Industrial AI | Labor-Efficient AI | Multimodal Vision

Title: GDPA: A Parameter-Efficient Gated Dual-Path Spatiotemporal Adapter for Surgical Workflow Recognition
Abstract: Automated surgical workflow recognition is a key enabler for context-aware computer-assisted surgery. Due to the scarcity of labeled surgical videos, training models from scratch or fully fine-tuning large vision architectures is often resourceintensive and can lead to overfitting. To alleviate this bottleneck, we insert a lightweight spatiotemporal adapter module into an image-pretrained backbone to inject temporal reasoning capability into the backbone and fine-tune the entire network. This not only preserves the backbone's original strong spatial representation capability, but also enables the model to learn such issues as the characteristic long-range temporal dependencies in surgical scenarios and the fine-grained interactions between instruments and organs, thereby achieving robust transfer to surgical video understanding tasks. Specifically, we propose a parameter-efficient Gated Dual-Path Spatiotemporal Adapter (GDPA) for surgical workflow recognition. GDPA is a lightweight module inserted into a frozen image-pretrained backbone to enable parallel spatial and temporal modeling. Within each GDPA block, the spatial and temporal branches operate in parallel, and their outputs are fused by an adaptive gating mechanism. This gating mechanism adaptively allocates the contributions of the two branches according to phase-dependent requirements for fine-grained spatial semantics and long-range temporal cues. Compared with previous methods, GDPA requires only a small number of trainable parameters and low computational cost. By retaining the backbone's pretrained visual knowledge and training only lightweight adapters in an end-to-end manner, it achieves higher accuracy even in data-limited scenarios. We evaluate our method on the Cholec80 and AutoLaparo surgical video benchmarks. The results show that even with a parameter budget far below that of full fine-tuning, GDPA still achieves competitive or even superior performance.
Keywords: Deep Learning | ParameterEfficient Fine-Tuning | Surgical Workflow Recognition | Vision Foundation Model

Title: A General Classification Framework for Detecting AI-Generated Voices
Abstract: The rapid advancement of deepfake voice synthesis technologies has led to increasing misuse cases, including impersonation, misinformation, and fraud. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-generated voices offer legitimate benefits, their misuse poses growing cybersecurity threats. This paper presents a general classification framework for detecting AI-generated voices across Sinhala, Tamil, and English languages. Publicly available datasets for multilingual deepfake voice detection, particularly in low-resource languages such as Sinhala and Tamil, remain limited, with most existing models focused primarily on English. To address this gap, an acoustic dataset covering Sinhala, Tamil, and English was created using real voice samples either recorded or sourced from public datasets and synthetic samples generated through Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Voice Conversion (VC) techniques, including tools such as Google Translate and Resemble AI. A hybrid CNN-LSTM model was developed to classify voices as real or synthetic. Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) were extracted and fed into separate CNN-LSTM models trained for each language. The proposed system achieved over 95% test accuracy across all three languages, demonstrating robust cross-linguistic performance. The findings offer a foundation for scalable, AI-driven deepfake voice detection frameworks adaptable to diverse linguistic and regional contexts.
Keywords: AI-generated voice detection | Artificial Intelligence | Audio Deepfake Detection | CNN-LSTM | MFCC

Title: Real-Time Financial Risk Modeling Using Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract: — Traditional financial risk modelling methodologies frequently fail to capture complicated, nonlinear patterns in real-time data in the age of highfrequency trading and turbulent global markets. In order to improve forecast accuracy and responsiveness, this article investigates the incorporation of deep learning techniques into real-time financial risk modelling. We create models that can interpret large, dynamic financial datasets in real-time by utilising cutting-edge architectures like Transformer models, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Real-time trading signals, sentiment analysis from news and social media, and macroeconomic factors are added to previous market data to train these models. Significant gains in predicting accuracy and risk identification are seen when the study compares the performance of DL models to traditional risk models like Value at Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR). We also discuss issues such managing noisy, non-stationary data, latency limitations, and model interpretability. The findings show that DL techniques can greatly improve the accuracy and promptness of risk forecasts, providing financial organisations with an effective instrument for proactive risk control. Deep learning may revolutionise real-time risk assessment and decision-making, as this study shows, adding to the expanding field of Al-driven finance. A realtime, adaptive deep learning-based financial risk modelling framework proposed in the proposed study has a fundamental contribution to the current state-of-the-art practices. In contrast to classical statistical or batch-trained machine learning models which assume fixed data and require time to inquire about it, this literature uses streaming deep learning models, namely the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), to perpetually learn on-the-fly based on real-time data streams in the market.
Keywords: Deep learning | Financial risk

Title: PREDICTION OF DISSOLVED ORGANIC CARBON IN INLAND WATERS USING MACHINE LEARNING METHODS: A CASE STUDY OF LAKE ERKEN, SWEDEN
Abstract: Dissolved Organic Carbon (DOC) is a key component of the inland water carbon cycle, playing a critical role in water quality, aquatic ecosystem dynamics, and carbon flux assessments. In this study, we combine Sentinel-2 Multi-Spectral Instrument (MSI) data with in-situ water quality, meteorological, and temporal variables to predict DOC concentrations in Lake Erken, Sweden. Three Machine Learning (ML) models, eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest Regression (RFR), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), are evaluated. XGBoost achieved the best performance with a MAPE of 3.46% and RMSE of 0.45 mg C/L. To enhance interpretability, we applied SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, which identified that the year (Y), total phosphorus (TP), total nitrogen (TN), and Sentinel-2 Band 2 (B2) were the most influential predictors of DOC. These results demonstrate the potential of integrating remote sensing and ML techniques for accurate DOC prediction in inland waters, thereby improving our understanding of the carbon cycle and providing insights to support sustainable water management.
Keywords: DOC | Inland waters | ML | Sentinel-2 MSI | SHAP | XGBoost

Title: Classification of Binaural Audio for Sound Immersion Assessment in TV 3.0
Abstract: In recent years, advances in artificial intelligence have enabled new approaches to evaluating sound immersion. This study proposes a machine learning-based method for assessing audio immersion by classifying binaural recordings captured with a dummy head. The classification aims to identify the reproduction system employed, thereby indirectly indicating the immersion level. A dataset was constructed by convolving the test audio signals provided by the SBTVD Forum with binaural room impulse responses from the SADIE II database. This process followed the MPEG-H standards and simulated 2.0, 5.1, and 5.1+4H reproduction configurations, as specified by the Brazilian TV 3.0 standard. The resulting binaural signals were segmented into 5-second samples and transformed into image-like representations using spectrograms and phase differences. A convolutional neural network based on the VGG-16 architecture was trained to classify four audio formats: monophonic, stereophonic, 5.1 surround, and immersive 5.1+4H. Using transfer learning, the model achieved a validation accuracy of 92.21% on synthetic data. A real-world test was conducted using a physical loudspeaker array and a calibrated dummy head to evaluate generalization. The classification performance significantly declined under these conditions, particularly for the monophonic and surround formats. This decline underscores the need for hybrid training strategies that integrate both synthetic and real-world data to improve model robustness.

Title: Explainable Spectro-Temporal Modeling for Indian Raga Classification Using Hybrid Neural Network
Abstract: Indian classical music, rich in emotional and melodic depth, poses a unique challenge for computational analysis - especially in the precise identification of ragas. In this study, we propose a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network(CNN)-(Long Short Term Memory(LSTM)) model that effectively combines spectral and temporal features extracted via Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) to classify Hindustani ragas. To enhance transparency, we integrate SHAP explainable AI to uncover how individual audio features influence predictions of ragas. Our model, trained on a curated dataset of ten raga classes, achieved a classification accuracy of 95.56%, demonstrating robust performance. Beyond high accuracy, the SHapley Additive exPlanations(SHAP) visualizations allowed us to interpret model decisions by highlighting the most influential MFCC coefficients. This dual focus on performance and interpretability offers a promising path forward for musicological tools that are not only accurate but also explain their reasoning - opening new doors in education, archiving, and cultural analysis of Indian classical music.

Title: Bringing Llama-3 to the Edge: End-to-End Quantized Conversational AI on Raspberry Pi 5
Abstract: Deploying conversational AI systems on resource-constrained edge computing devices requires sophisticated optimization techniques to ensure computational efficiency without compromising performance quality. This paper presents a comprehensive study on the optimization and deployment of an end-to-end conversational AI pipeline - comprising Whisper automatic speech recognition (ASR), a 3-billion parameter Llama-3 large language model (LLM) and lightweight text-to-speech (TTS) - running entirely on a Raspberry Pi module. Multiple quantization levels are benchmarked across two inference stacks, Ollama and the lower-overhead llama.cpp. The evaluation is conducted in two phases: first, by analyzing the metrics for individual components and second, by assessing the overall pipeline. The results show that implementing a lower bit quantized version of llama.cpp within the pipeline yields significant improvements in latency and energy consumption compared to the higher bit baseline, with only a marginal reduction in coherence. Similar results are observed for the Ollama deployment. These findings demonstrate that strategic quantization and runtime optimizations facilitate the practical deployment of conversational AI systems on edge devices, maintaining high conversational quality while paving the way for locally executed, privacy-preserving AI applications.
Keywords: ASR | conversational AI | edge devices | LLM | quantization | Raspberry Pi 5 | single-board computers | TTS

Title: Hybrid Deep Learning with ConvNeXt and Self-Attention for Pulmonary Disease Classification
Abstract: Pulmonary lung detection represents a critical challenge in modern neuroimaging, with significant implications for timely medical intervention. In this study, we use the IQ-OTHNCCD lung cancer classification dataset to introduce a novel hybrid deep learning architecture that combines Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) with ConvNeXt-inspired convolutional blocks for effective lung disease classification. The proposed model captures both local spatial features and long-range dependencies that are necessary for spotting subtle and scattered problematic patterns. Following a sequence of convolutional layers with Layer Normalization for initial feature encoding, ConvNeXt-style blocks that integrate depth-wise convolution, Gaussian Error Linear Unit (GELU)-activated multi-layer perceptron's (MLPs), and residual connections are used. Tokenized spatial depictions are moderate to MHSA in order to improve global contextual comprehension. The proposed method shows superior performance in multi-class pulmonary lung classification with 98.4% accuracy, 96.3% precision, 97.0% F1-score, and 97.7% recall without compromising computational efficiency. These findings demonstrate the stability and generalizability of our approach, which makes it an optimistic instrument for automatic clinical pulmonary lung disease identification.
Keywords: Classification | Down-sampling | Malignant | Medical Images | Pulmonary Nodules

Title: Recording Environment and Microphone Recognition in Cymbal Audios Using Machine Learning
Abstract: Although machine learning techniques are commonly used in audio forensic analysis to identify recording devices and environments, the music industry can also benefit from this type of application, mainly because it is a little-explored approach. In this sense, this work aims to use this type of approach to assess whether different recording conditions - specifically microphones and environments - contribute to increasing the variability of audio signals in a way that simulates similar musical instruments, increasing the number of samples in a limited set of instruments. A dataset of cymbal audio recordings was analyzed using a logistic regression model combined with Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (RFECV) to evaluate the classification of microphones and environments. Results indicate that the recording environments significantly impacted signal variability, achieving classification accuracy of 99%, whereas the influence of microphone types was minimal, with classification performance around 52%.

Title: Novel and Efficient Information-Theoretic Weighted CAT Boost Framework for Complex Multi-Scale Stock Price Prediction
Abstract: In this research the long-standing problem of stock price prediction and propose a information gain weighted CatBoost (IGW-CatBoost) approach which orchestrates dynamic feature weighting and sophisticated ensemble learning. In contrast to many traditional and deep learning models which can either consider all TA indicators equally or cannot interpret its learned weights, the method uses information gain to allocate adaptive data driven weights to engineered features to best contribute to the prediction accuracy. These weights are fine-tuned using a gradient-based optimization and then used within a robust CatBoost regression framework. Empirical evaluation of popular NASDAQ stocks (AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOG, TSLA) on daily, hourly, and monthly intervals shows the superiority of IGW-CatBoost in comparison to the state-of-the-art models like CNN-LSTM Hybrid, TFT and N-BEATS (up to 4% higher (R2) (R)R2 and 20% lower error rates). This evidence endorses the predictive effectiveness of dynamic feature weighing and enhances the interpretability and generalization of financial forecasting systems. These results are a significant step toward real-world application, from both a methodological perspective and in terms of practical risk management and algorithmic trading.
Keywords: CatBoost | feature weighting | information gain | Stock market prediction

Title: Harnessing Grey Wolf Optimization for Early Thyroid Cancer Prediction
Abstract: Thyroid cancer is an increasing worry for medical professionals, who recognize that early identification is crucial for effective treatment. Machine learning (ML) advancements have generated significant prospects for improving the speed and precision of thyroid cancer detection. The current diagnostic instruments' lack of accuracy and clarity obstructs prompt patient care. Thus, improving clinical decision-making in this domain requires optimizing prediction models. This study assesses a hybrid diagnostic model that incorporates feature selection methods, such as sequential feature selection and recursive feature removal, enhanced by grey wolf optimization (GWO), using the Kaggle Thyroid Cancer Disease Dataset. The objective is to determine the most efficient prediction models for the early and precise identification of thyroid cancer. The suggested hybrid technique demonstrated outstanding performance, with an accuracy of 98.87%, precision of 100%, sensitivity of 94.84%, specificity of 100%, and F-measure of 97.33% across several assessment criteria, setting it apart from the nine hybrid models examined. The results suggest that machine learning models can substantially enhance the accuracy of thyroid cancer detection by GWO-based feature selection and optimization. This technology may improve patient outcomes and reduce strain on healthcare systems by enabling the creation of more efficient and accurate diagnostic tools.
Keywords: grey wolf optimization | Machine learning | recursive feature elimination | sequential feature selection | Thyroid cancer

Title: Automated Multi-Class Fault Diagnosis of Photovoltaic Panels Using Lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: The performance of the photovoltaic (PV) systems continues to be part of the sustainable energy production, however, it is often compromised by a range of environmental and physical defects. Even though the automated monitoring methods have a significant potential, previous studies have focused on binary classification, which usually distinguishes between clean and dusty panels. The range of conditions that require special maintenance is not considered in such models. This shortcoming is addressed in the current paper by suggesting and testing a multi-class fault diagnosis system of solar panels. Two lightweight and very efficient deep-learning(DL) models, MobileNetV3Small and EfficientNet-B0, are used to classify PV-panel images into six categories which are operationally very critical, namely Clean, Dusty, Snow-Covered, Bird Droppings, Physical Damage, and Electrical Damage. These models are fine-tuned on this subtle task with the help of transfer learning and data augmentation on a publicly-available dataset. The performance is outstanding as the MobileNetV3Small scored a test accuracy of 98.61% and the EfficientNet-B0 scored a test accuracy of 99.11%. The fact that EfficientNet-B0 outperforms its competitors, as well as having a reduced computational cost, highlights the success of compound scaling in coming up with strong and discriminative feature extractors. In turn, the research confirms the practicality of an automated multi-class diagnostic instrument and preconditions the idea of intelligent condition-based maintenance that can significantly increase the energy output, reliability, and economic performance of solar power plants.
Keywords: condition based maintenance | data augmentation | deep learning | EfficientNet-B0 | MobileNetV3Small | multi class fault diagnosis | Photovoltaic (PV) systems | transfer learning

Title: A Deep Learning-Based Method for Detecting Foreign Objects Attached to Electric Poles
Abstract: With the advancement of power system intelligentization, foreign objects attached to electric poles (e.g., plastic bags, kites, and debris) pose significant threats to the safe and stable operation of power grids, potentially inducing faults such as short circuits and tripping. Traditional manual inspection methods are constrained by low efficiency and limited coverage, failing to meet the requirements of large-scale real-time grid monitoring. Existing deep learning-based detection methods exhibit three critical limitations: poor feature adaptability to multi-scene and multi-scale foreign objects, difficulty in balancing lightweight deployment and detection accuracy, and inadequate capability in detecting small-target foreign objects. To address these issues, this study proposes a Multi-Module Synergy Pole Foreign Object Detection Network (MSPFOD-Net). This network integrates three core modules: a multi-scale feature perception enhancement module, a separate weight cascaded lightweight module, and a dual-convolution multi-pooling small-target detection module. By fusing spatial and semantic features of pole images, MSPFOD-Net achieves accurate detection of foreign objects, providing a robust technical solution for intelligent power inspection. Experimental results on a self-constructed dataset of pole-attached foreign objects demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional models in both detection accuracy and real-time performance, verifying its academic value and practical applicability. (Abstract)
Keywords: Lightweight Network | MSPFOD-Net | Multi-Scale Feature | Small-Target Detection (key words)

Title: Advancing Inclusive Education and Accessibility Through Regional Flexibility in TTS Systems by Indian English Accent Detection
Abstract: This study examines the application of machine learning techniques for recognizing and differentiating regional accents in Indian English, with the broader aim of improving the inclusivity and contextual suitability of speech technolo-gies in India's linguistically diverse environment. Using the Indic TTS dataset from IIT Madras, we analyzed speech samples from male and female speakers across eight states, resulting in 16 distinct accent classes. Mel-Frequency Cep-stral Coefficients (MFCC) were employed for acoustic feature extraction, and multiple classifiers-including Support Vector Machines, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest, and XGBoost-were trained and evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation. XGBoost achieved the highest reported accuracy of 99.02 %, followed closely by Random Forest (98.86 %) and CNN-LSTM (98.70 %). These results underscore the potential of accent-aware models to enhance recognition performance and cultural adaptability in speech systems. Beyond improving general speech recognition, the system has applications in accent-specific speech synthesis, personalized voice assistants, call-center automation, and educational tools for language learning and pronunciation feedback.
Keywords: Cross Validation | Feature Extraction | Indian English Accent Recognition | Machine Learning | Mel frequency cepstral coefficients | Speech Pro-cessing

Title: A Machine Learning Approach for Predictive Financial Analysis: Enhancing Fraud Detection and Investment Strategies
Abstract: There is a multitude of investment-related opportunities where advanced prediction analysis can be applied within machine learning algorithms, particularly in the fields of finance and investment fraud. The current paper explores the detail and construction of a machine learning model which can be applied to analyzing and comprehending complex and voluminous data sets in the finance domain to optimize security and profitability. To discover anomalies which may suggest some transactional data is fraudulent, we employ both supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms such as neural networks, decision trees, support and cluster machines, and random forests. To achieve goal-oriented investing, we implement a combination of forecasting market dynamics through advanced deep learning and decision-making systems to formulate and execute Fact Based Investing (FBI) methodologies. We possess better models than the standard statistical methods simply because the real-world financial data is experimented to measure how these strategies perform. While return on investment (ROI) and risk-adjusted returns quantify the models' influence on investment outcomes, key performance indicators including precision, recall, and F1-score are utilised to confirm the models' efficacy in fraud detection. This study demonstrates how ML may revolutionise financial analytics by providing strong instruments for strategic investment planning and early fraud detection, which will help make financial decision-making safer and more intelligent.
Keywords: financial analysis | fraud detection | Machine learning

Title: Leveraging Machine Learning for Speech-Based Dementia Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Review
Abstract: Dementia is a progressive neurodegenerative disease in which early diagnosis continues to be a challenge as a result of constraints of the traditional, invasive diagnosis procedures. The use of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models (RNNs, CNNs, and Transformer-based architectures) to classify dementia based on speech data are systematically assessed in this review. Multimodal models with diagnostic accuracy of over 90 have been built using benchmark datasets such as Dementia Bank and ADReSS and have very efficient feature integration strategies which combine acoustic (MFCCs, jitter, shimmer) and linguistic (semantic embeddings) features. The review is quantitative in cost-benefit improvements in methodology and presents systematic issues such as the lack of diversity of datasets and lack of interpretability of the models, and research gaps in multilingual adaptation and clinical scalability. This work made a contribution in terms of a summarized analysis of the performance and a series of guidance on the overall progress of speech-based, non-invasive, and explainable dementia diagnosis to effective clinical implementation.
Keywords: cognitive and linguistic deterioration | Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) | deep learning (DL) | machine learning (ML) | multimodal systems | Neurodegenerative disease | Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) | speech-based diagnosis | Transformer models

Title: Smart Diagnostic System for Multiple Respiratory Diseases Using Lung Sounds
Abstract: In the present world pollution is increasing rapidly, which is causing health issues in human beings. The major issue is with respect to the lung. The problem is also due to bad habits like smoking. To identify the problem in the preliminary stage we are proposing a 'Smart diagnostic system for the automated classification of multiple respiratory diseases using lung sound recordings'. Motivated by the limitations of traditional auscultation, the system employs a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model trained on Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) extracted from the ICBHI 2017 Respiratory Sound Database. The proposed architecture effectively captures both spatial and temporal features in respiratory signals, enabling accurate detection of conditions such as Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Pneumonia, Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (URTI), and Bronchiolitis. Extensive preprocessing, including noise reduction, segmentation, and data augmentation, improves model robustness against real-world acoustic variability and class imbalance. The system achieves a classification accuracy of 93.2%, with strong performance on COPD and Pneumonia classes. The findings suggest the model's potential as a lowcost, scalable tool for AI-assisted pulmonary diagnostics, particularly in resource-constrained environments.
Keywords: Audio Signal Processing | Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) | Deep Learning | Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) | ICBHI Dataset | Lung Sound Classification | Medical Diagnostics | Mel Spectrogram | MFCC | Respiratory Diseases

Title: Adaptive Music Recommendation Platform for Elderly via Web-Based AI
Abstract: The elderly experience a wide range of changes covering physical, social, and psychological domains. These experiences are diverse and influenced by individual factors, health status, socioeconomic conditions, and cultural contexts. Music is a soothing solution to all these life problems. With most of the elderly being computer literate this paper attempts a web-based Music Recommendation Platform based on Signal Processing and Artificial Intelligence techniques. The data set is a combination of Million Song dataset and the Spotify dataset to provide better leverage to the system. The special feature of the Recommendation system includes user information like age, gender, genre, year of release of song, popularity of the song and artist. Based on the. Signal processing features such as MFCC (Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients), pitch, timbre, rhythm, and spectrogram audio signals are categorized and effectively classified using three machine learning models namely Decision tree, K Nearest Neighbor and Random Forest respectively. The performance metrics for these models are evaluated and Random Forest is observed to stand out compared to the other two models in all aspects. Bidirectional Encoder for Representation Transformer (BERT) is used for predicting songs by implementing the textual features to find the characteristics like Artists, Genre as a replacement for the ML model.The best performing KNN is ported to the webpage to provide an MRS to the elderly. A mobile app is under development to test the effectiveness of the system employing the KNN.
Keywords: BERT Model | Decision Tree | K Nearest Neighbor | Machine Learning | Pitch | Random Forest | Timbre

Title: Embodied Conversational Virtual Humans in 3D Environments: Towards Scalable and Immersive AI Interactions
Abstract: We present a fully automated conversational virtual human system developed in Unity, designed for scalable and immersive human-AI interactions in 3D environments. The system integrates real-time voice activity detection for automatic turn-taking, speech-to-text transcription, text response generation, and text-to-speech synthesis with synchronized lip animation. Unlike prior systems, our approach facilitates fluid, naturalistic dialogue in customizable 3D environments. To provide initial validation, we conducted a study with 17 participants evaluating conversational experiences in both virtual reality and PC. Results indicate the system achieves low latency (mean 2.30s total response time) and is perceived positively by users regarding speed, likeability, and accuracy, while highlighting areas for improved clarity. Although conversational realism ratings were comparable or favored PC, participants preferred the VR modality, citing immersion and co-presence as key factors. These findings demonstrate the system's usability and the significant role of immersion in enhancing embodied conversational AI interactions.
Keywords: Conversational AI | Dialogue systems | Large Language Models | Speech Processing | Unity | Virtual Humans

Title: Enhancing Store Sales Forecasting Accuracy with Hybrid Deep Learning and LSSVM-Based Models
Abstract: Precise sales forecasting is essential for retail enterprises to facilitate effective inventory management, reduce losses, and enhance customer happiness. Conventional statistical models and independent deep learning methods fail to adequately represent the intricate temporal patterns and deviations present in retail sales data. This study introduces a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates neural networks using convolution (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and a Least Squares Support Vector Machine (LSSVM) regressor to enhance forecasting precision. The CNN-LSTM layers extract profound temporal and spatial patterns, but the LSSVM component improves generalisation and rectifies nonlinear residuals. The model was assessed utilising real-world datasets obtained from Kaggle, specifically the Rossman Store Sales and M5 Forecasting datasets. Experimental findings indicate the model's superiority compared to baseline methods like ARIMA, XGBoost, Prophet, and LSTM-only models. The proposed model attained an RMSE of 204.35, MAE of 156.21, MAPE of 3.98%, and a R<sup>2</sup> score of 0.981, surpassing all comparing baselines. These findings confirm the hybrid system's resilience and scalability for real-time retail forecasting applications. The research introduces an innovative and practical forecasting instrument to the domain of intelligent retail analytics.
Keywords: ARIMA | Business Intelligence | CNN-LSTM | Demand Forecasting | Ensemble Learning | Feature Engineering | Forecast Accuracy | GRU | Hybrid Deep Learning | LSSVM | Machine Learning | Nonlinear Regression | Python | Retail Analytics | RNN | Sales Forecasting | Store Sales | Temporal Modeling | Time Series Prediction | XGBoost

Title: Artificial Intelligence Based Digital Writing Pen Technology
Abstract: This Pen PC technology offers a flexible platform for collaboration, productivity, and creative expression. It is a ground-breaking combination of traditional instruments for writing and digital computing capabilities. This abstract explores the cutting-edge field of Pen a personal computer technology, following its development from early systems based on styluses to sophisticated digital pens with inbuilt sensors and CPUs. It has a wide range of uses in business, education, healthcare, and entertainment. Even with its revolutionary potential, issues like latency and accuracy still need to be addressed, which motivates continuous R&D to improve performance and user experience. The future of Pen PC technology is extremely promising, as new developments like AI-powered handwriting detection and AR-enabled interactions have the potential to completely alter the nature of digital writing. In summary, Pen PC technology is a paradigm change in human-computer interaction that enables users to achieve previously unimaginable levels of productivity and creativity. By enabling users to annotate papers, draw ideas, and interact in real-time, Pen PC technology is being integrated into hybrid devices like smartphones and 2-in-1 laptops to improve efficiency and creativity. Pen PC technology makes interactive learning experiences possible in educational environments by letting students interact with virtual classrooms, annotate digital texts, and solve math problems.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | augmented reality integration | education technology | handwriting recognition | wireless connectivity

Title: Speech-to-Image Generation Using Audio Embeddings and Latent Diffusion Models
Abstract: Speech-driven image generation is an emerging multimodal learning task that enables the creation of visual content directly from spoken descriptions. Most existing systems depend on intermediate text transcription or require large paired audio-image datasets, limiting their applicability in realistic environments. This paper presents a deep learning framework for end-to-end speech-to-image generation using an audio-CLIP encoder integrated with a latent diffusion model.
