The proposed method extracts semantic and prosodic features from raw speech using an audio embedding network and maps them to the latent space of a pretrained diffusion generator through a hybrid feature-fusion module. This design allows the model to utilize both linguistic information and paralinguistic cues that conventional ASR-based pipelines often discard. Experiments conducted on the Flickr8k Audio Caption Corpus and SPEECH-COCO datasets demonstrate improved semantic alignment and visual quality compared to baseline ASR → text → image approaches, with notable gains in CLIP similarity and perceptual metrics. The results highlight the effectiveness of direct audio conditioning and establish a strong foundation for future speech-native multimodal generation systems.
Keywords: Audio embeddings | Deep learning | Latent diffusion models | Speech-to-image generation

Title: Advanced Harmonic Feature Utilization in Ensemble Learning for Guitar Chord Classification
Abstract: Guitar chord classification problem has been explored and experimented in more than one dimension for music recognition, classification and recommendation models. Musical notes created by different instruments are just sound waves but harmonised. Mathematically, these sound waves can be represented in both time domain and frequency domain. This mathematical representation becomes necessary for the purpose of analysis and developing recommendation systems for music. Frequency domain representation leads to generation of harmonics which are basically different frequency components contained in an audio specifically music file in our research. The objective of this research paper is to present an optimised ensemble learning on different harmonics generated by guitar playing and subsequently classifying the chord as major or minor guitar chord. Having said that, selection of harmonics is one crucial aspect of this research, where we have also explored the harmonics which are relevant and the ones which are not relevant and can conveniently be dropped. This also helps in dimensionality reduction and controlled computation and time complexity involved in the process of guitar chore classification task. The preprocessing of guitar chords audio into numerical data is computationally extensive. During the preprocessing stage the harmonics are generated in large numbers and the effect of higher order harmonics is explored in some previous works. In this paper we have attempted to implement ensemble machine learning algorithm with tuned hyper parameters. To achieve this we have considered two classification algorithms vis-a-vis Decision Tree and Random Forest algorithms.
Keywords: ensemble learning | harmonics | machine learning | music recognition | music recommendation system

Title: Research related to audio processing based on adaptive strategies and deep learning
Abstract: In the field of digital audio, the balance between efficient file storage and high-quality sound quality optimization is the core challenge. To address this issue, this paper proposes an audio processing framework integrating adaptive strategies and deep learning, aiming to solve the key technical problems of comprehensive evaluation of audio formats and sound quality prediction. Firstly, the Quality-Size Index Model (QSI model) was constructed. Through the planning and processing of the three elements of audio file size, audio quality fidelity and encoding and decoding complexity, combined with adaptive weight allocation, the balance relationship between storage efficiency and audio quality fidelity of different audio formats (WAV, MP3, AAC) was quantified. Then, in this paper, a deep learning sound quality prediction model based on multi-layer neural networks is established to conduct nonlinear fitting of multi-dimensional parameters such as sampling rate, bit rate, depth and encoding format, so as to achieve the prediction of sound quality score and the recommendation of the best parameters. The experimental results show that the QSI model can effectively distinguish the advantages and disadvantages of file formats in typical scenarios such as mobile devices and professional recording. Among them, the AAC format has a score ranging from 0.633 to 1.104 in the mobile device scenario and has the best balanced performance. Under the sound quality prediction model based on deep learning, the recommended optimal parameters for speech content and music content are AAC format (44.1kHz,96kbps) and WAV format (16.0kHz or 8.0kHz, 16-bit), respectively. The research provides an optimization method for audio processing that takes into account both storage efficiency and sound quality. The model is adapted to multi-parameter nonlinear dynamic scenes and has significant advantages in balanced optimization, laying a technical foundation for subsequent audio coding optimization and intelligent processing.
Keywords: adaptive strategy model | audio format evaluation | deep learning | QSI index model | sound quality prediction

Title: Decentralized Optical Music Recognition Using YOLO and FedGP for Music Education
Abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative model training, where data remain on local devices. Leveraging this capability, we explore privacy-aware Optical Music Recognition (OMR) by coupling a state-of-the-art YOLOv9c detector with FedGP, a genetic-programming-based aggregation strategy tailored to highly non-IID client distributions. We cast OMR as the end-to-end transcription of printed and handwritten four-part harmony scores into structured MusicXML, a task complicated by symbol variability, staff-line distortions, and non-musical artifacts. To support this formulation, we assembled a hybrid corpus of 1 810 page images - 810 augmented handwritten exercises and 1000 automati-cally annotated digital scores-comprising 112024 bounding-box annotations across 166 symbol classes. The pages are deliberately partitioned in a non-IID manner among ten virtual clients. Training proceeds by freezing the first 22 layers of the pre-trained YOLOv9c backbone and fine-tuning the detection head for 160 local epochs per client. Parameter updates are transmitted every 20 communication rounds and aggregated over 500 global epochs. Comprehensive experiments show that FedGP consistently outperforms the canonical FedAvg baseline. At communication round 8, FedGP attains a mean mAP50 of 0.6775±0.0179, significantly exceeding FedAvg's 0.6467±0.0095. These findings demonstrate that genetic-programming-driven aggregation mitigates client heterogeneity while preserving data locality and imposing modest computational demands on edge devices. Overall, the study confirms the viability of FL for large-scale, privacy-conscious OMR and establishes FedGP as a robust alternative to standard aggregation schemes under challenging non-IID conditions.
Keywords: 4-part harmonization | FedAVG | Federated Learning | FedGP | Optical Music Recognition | YOLOv9

Title: Hybrid CNN-RNN Model for Identifying and Classifying Literary Themes and Structures in English Novels
Abstract: The automated analysis of literary themes and structures in English novels presents a significant task due to the complicated interplay of stylistic patterns and long-range narrative relationships. Current models often inadequately represent both local and global features., resulting in minimized classification accuracy. The proposed study presents a hybrid CNN-RNN model that integrates convolutional layers for n-gram pattern recognition with bidirectional GRU layers for sequence modelling., resulting in enhanced performance in literary analytics. Experiments utilizing unique datasets from Kaggle illustrate the model's effectiveness., attaining 98.6% accuracy., 97.9% precision., 98.2% recall., and a 98.0% macro Fl-score. Comparative evaluations demonstrate significant improvements over baseline models., including independent CNN., Bi-GRU., and BERT fine-tuning. The suggested methodology markedly enhances the current capabilities in literary theme and structure identification., providing a powerful instrument for digital humanities and automated educational systems. This study establishes a basis for subsequent efforts in multimodal and multilingual literary analysis.
Keywords: Automated Literary Analytics | BERT Fine-Tuning | Bidirectional GRU | Computational Literary Analysis | Convolutional Neural Network | Deep Learning | Hybrid CNN-RNN | Literary Theme Detection | Narrative Structure Classification | NLP | Sequence Modelling | Text Classification

Title: AS-ASR: A Lightweight Framework for Aphasia-Specific Automatic Speech Recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes AS-ASR, a lightweight aphasiaspecific speech recognition framework based on Whisper-tiny, tailored for low-resource deployment on edge devices. Our approach introduces a hybrid training strategy that systematically combines standard and aphasic speech at varying ratios, enabling robust generalization, and a GPT-4-based reference enhancement method that refines noisy aphasic transcripts, improving supervision quality. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple data mixing configurations and evaluation settings. Results show that our fine-tuned model significantly outperforms the zero-shot baseline, reducing WER on aphasic speech by over 30% while preserving performance on standard speech. The proposed framework offers a scalable, efficient solution for realworld disordered speech recognition.
Keywords: AIoT | Aphasic Speech Recognition | Fine-Tuning | Healthcare | Whisper

Title: Exhaust Gas Guidance Model to Enhance Combustion Efficiency for Power Plant Boilers Using Partial Least Squares Regression
Abstract: The steel industry is a highly power-consuming, meeting its power demands by operating in-house power generators and purchasing electricity from external sources. Consequently, improving combustion efficiency in power generation significantly reduces rising electricity purchase costs and subsequently lowers production expenses. This study aims to develop an optimal model that guides O<inf>2</inf> and CO levels in exhaust gas using machine learning (ML) to enhance the combustion efficiency of power boilers. First, 367 data points were collected and preprocessed from the power plant boiler of Steel Plant A. Subsequently, an Exhaust Gas Guidance Model (EG-GM) was developed to guide O<inf>2</inf> and CO levels using the Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR) algorithm. The test results of the model showed a guidance accuracy of 83.1% for O<inf>2</inf> and 53.3% for CO. Although the accuracy for CO was relatively lower, over 90% of the guided values fell within a 10% margin of error, indicating high reliability within the evaluation criteria. This suggests the potential for the model to serve as an alternative tool in cases of instrument failure or decreased reliability. It is expected to contribute to optimizing equipment performance and enhancing operational efficiency in the future.
Keywords: combustion efficiency | exhaust gas guidance | exhaust gas guidance model | machine learning | partial least squares | power plant in steel industry | regression

Title: FreqFormer: Frequency-Aware Multi-Scale Transformer with Gated Temporal Fusion for Robust Time Series Forecasting
Abstract: Time series forecasting remains a fundamental challenge in real-world applications due to the complex characteristics of non-stationarity., multi-scale dynamics., and evolving predictive dependencies. Existing deep learning models often adopt static architectures that fail to adapt to the intrinsic spectral and temporal structure of diverse sequences. To address this limitation., we propose FreqFormer., a novel Transformer-based framework that unifies multi-scale patch construction., frequency-aware Scale Router., and Temporal Boundary Gated Fusion. FreqFormer first constructs patch representations at multiple temporal granularities and aligns them to a common sequence length. It then dynamically weights and fuses these multi-scale embeddings via the input's global low-frequency energy ratio., a metric that directly reflects the balance between long-term trends and short-term fluctuations to guide adaptive scale selection. Finally., a boundary-aware refinement module enhances the encoder output by assigning adaptive importance to patches near the prediction horizon. Evaluated on four standard benchmarks., FreqFormer achieves state-of-the-art performance., particularly on long-horizon and non-stationary forecasting tasks., demonstrating its robustness and adaptability.
Keywords: Frequency-aware adaptation | Multi-scale modeling | Spectral-guided scale fusion | Time series forecasting

Title: Voice Conversion: Transformation Through Deep Learning
Abstract: Voice conversion is a technique that converts a speaker's voice into another while retaining the original content. The main goal of this research is to enhance the quality of voice conversion system that well exhibits speaker identity while ensuring naturalness and intelligibility. To accomplish this, we introduce a three-stage pipeline using a deep learning-based approach. The Encoder draws speaker-specific features from the input speech, the Synthesizer produces mel spectrograms that maintain the linguistic and acoustic features of the target speaker, and the Vocoder synthesizes the final waveform to generate natural-sounding speech. The method is trained on varied speech datasets to achieve robustness over various speakers. Experimental outcomes confirm that the system efficiently alters speaker identity without losing speech clarity and prosody, resulting in high-fidelity voice conversions. The results highlight the capabilities of deep learning in progressing voice transformation technology. Future studies will aim at optimizing real-time performance, enhancing prosody conservation, and furthering speaker similarity, paving the way for use in personalized voice assistants, speech synthesis, and assistive technology.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Mel Spectrograms | Real-Time Processing | Speaker Embeddings | Speaker Similarity | Speech Synthesis | Voice Conversion

Title: Air Condition Diagnosis System in Laser Directed Energy Deposition Based on Deep Learning
Abstract: In the air condition diagnosis system of laser directed energy deposition, equipment failures can lead to transient contamination, which in turn causes oxygen levels to rise by hundreds of ppm quickly, surpassing the requirement of ≤qslant 2 0 ppm for high-end components and thus degrading product performance. To address this issue, this paper constructs a fault diagnosis model based on a lightweight CNN (Convolutional Neural Network)-Transformer hybrid network to provide basic diagnostic capabilities for the system. It takes a five-dimensional atmospheric sensor sequence, including intake flow rate, exhaust flow rate, chamber pressure, and oxygen content (sensors 1 and 2), as input. It extracts local mutation features through convolution and then uses a single-layer Transformer encoder to characterize the global coupling relationships among multiple parameters. At the data level, for the difficult-to-classify category, Z-score anomaly removal, Robust Scaler independent standardization, and class weight enhancement are implemented to alleviate the problem of class imbalance. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 97.99%, a Macro-F1 value of 97.94%, and the F1 value for the difficult-to-classify category increases to 1.000, significantly outperforming other baseline models, such as 1D-CNN and CNN-RNN. This establishes a basis for monitoring and diagnosing laser additive manufacturing processes and other complex atmospheric systems.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Fault Diagnosis | Multi-Class Classification

Title: Transformer-Based Bispectral Fusion: Enhancing UCA DOA Estimation in Low SNR
Abstract: Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation using deep learning (DL) for uniform circular arrays (UCAs) demonstrates significant potential in complex environments. However, DL-based methods inherently sacrifice resolution for robustness due to heightened sensitivity, which exacerbates spurious peaks in low-SNR scenarios and leads to inaccurate estimates. To address this limitation, we propose a Transformer-based dual-spectrum fusion model (SFD-Net). Specifically, multiple-snapshot data are processed in parallel by the Transformer encoder backbone, and the extracted features are fed into subsequent branches. Subsequently, one branch integrates the MUSIC algorithm by substituting its key high-complexity operations with neural networks, achieving computational efficiency while preserving high resolution. Meanwhile, the other branch employs attention mechanisms combined with residual networks to enhance feature extraction, enabling comprehensive target verification across all angles. Simulations demonstrate SFD-Net's superior performance in low-SNR, reducing angular estimation error by 77% at SNR = -18dB. The model also generalizes to scenarios with varying numbers of targets while significantly suppressing spurious peaks.
Keywords: DoA estimation | Low SNR | Transformer | uniform circular array

Title: Audio-Visual Cross-Attention for Improved Deepfake Video Detection and Forgery Localization
Abstract: With the emergence of multi-modal generative models, synthesized videos are becoming increasingly realistic, making the detection of deepfakes extremely challenging. While several video deepfake detection models have shown promising performance, their focus has been primarily on the visual modality. To overcome this limitation, we propose a dualstream framework that fuses visual and auditory information via cross-attention computed between embeddings extracted from pre-trained video and audio encoders. Additionally, we design a weakly-supervised forgery localization head that infers frame-level forgery scores from coarse segment-level labels, minimizing the need for fine-grained annotations and allowing for forgery location characterization. In this paper, we describe our preliminary results showing the proposed model outperforming state-of-the-art detectors on both frame-level localization and sequence-level deepfake detection tasks. Ongoing work focuses on investigating the complementarity between the visual and auditory modalities to improve model robustness and explainability.
Keywords: audio-visual | crossmodal attention | Deepfake detection | forgery | generative AI

Title: A Cross-Attentive Multi-Scale Speech Framework for Mental Health Risk Prediction using VocalMind-Net
Abstract: In modern era, Mental health disorders such as stress, anxiety, and depression affect daily functioning and often go undetected due to overlapping symptoms and limited diagnostic tools. Conventional mental health prediction assessment is time-consuming and involves expert participation in tests, making early detection difficult. However, there are no scalable, non-contact systems that can accurately measure psychological stress with the help of natural indicators such as speech. Most existing models frequently use facial expressions or other physiological signals that can be unreliable or influenced by external factors. This research aimed to develop a speech-based system for detecting psychological stress using Deep Learning (DL) techniques namely, VocalMind-Net, with the aim of categorizing stress and non-stress speech signals by analyzing vocal features linked to emotional states. It is based on multi-scale wavelet denoising, spectral and nonlinear feature extraction, combinatorial feature selection, bidirectional crossattention fusion of speech and metadata, and Multiscale Orthogonal Independent Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit (MODE-Bi-GRU) temporal modeling. The MODE-Bi-GRU block uses three parallel Bi-GRU streams with different strides to capture the phoneme-, syllable-, and phrase-level dependencies. The proposed VocalMind-Net model achieved an average classification accuracy of 98.8 % and 98.79 % for 959 DAIC-WOZ and MODMA datasets thereby demonstrating strong performance and reliability.
Keywords: bidirectional cross-attention fusion | deep learning | mental health disorder | metadata multiscale orthogonal independent bi-directional gated recurrent unit | speech signals | stress

Title: MERCI: A Multimodal Dataset for Personalised and Emotionally-Aware Dialogues
Abstract: The integration of conversational agents into daily life has become increasingly common. However, sustaining deeply engaging and natural interactions remains challenging due to a lack of multimodal datasets capturing personal and emotional nuances. In this paper, we introduce MERCI (Multimodal dataset for Emotionally-aware peRsonalised Conversational In-teractions), a dataset derived from user-robot dialogues involving thirty participants who completed user profile questionnaires covering ten personal topics (e.g., hobbies, music). A conver-sational system called PERCY then engaged with each partici-pant in open-domain conversations, leveraging GPT-4, real-time facial-expression and sentiment analysis to generate contextu-ally appropriate, empathetic responses. MERCI contains 1860 utterances, equating to about 12.5 hours of aligned audio, three-view video, transcripts with timestamps, emotion labels, and sentiment scores. This dataset serves as a reproducible test-bed for tasks such as emotion-aware response generation, multimodal affect recognition, and personalised policy learning. Baseline performance results have been established using advanced models such as BERT, T5, BART, and GPT-3.5/4/4o-mini across gener-ation, regression, and classification. Evaluations through human and automated methods have demonstrated strong naturalness, relevance, and consistency in responses while indicating areas for enhanced personalisation and empathic depth. We expect that MERCI will enhance the development of emotionally intelligent, user-centric conversational AI applications, potentially ranging from social robotics to mental health support.
Keywords: dialogue systems | empathetic conversational agents | human-robot interaction | multimodal dataset | personalisation

Title: Iot-Driven Infant Care System: Real-Time Monitoring and Automated Parental Alerts
Abstract: This work discusses the design and development of an Intelligent Baby Cradle System utilizing Internet of Things (IoT), data science, and Android-based solutions to monitor the comfort and safety of infants. The system employs an ESP32 microcontroller with a variety of sensors such as a microphone, humidity and temperature sensors, and an object detection sensor to monitor the infant's surrounding and behavior incessantly. The system analyzes real-time sensor information to determine the causes of distresslike crying caused by discomfort or environmental issues-and takes action independently by playing soothing music and alerting caregivers via a specialist Android application. The application provides minute-to-minute alerts during crying and sends alerts if the ambient air is above safe levels. Machine learning procedures are used to classify the causes of distress of an infant and facilitate predictive and proactive parenting intervention. The performance shows high precision in environmental sensing and distress identification with real- time responses and efficient hardware and software integration. The system facilitates proactive and smart infant care and provides a basis for smart parenting solutions in contemporary homes.
Keywords: Android Application | Baby cry Detection | Environmental Sensors | ESP32 | Internet of Things (IoT) | Smart Cradle System

Title: Phonetic Analysis of Real and Synthetic Speech Using HuBERT Embeddings: Perspectives for Deepfake Detection
Abstract: The growing sophistication of speech generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI) has introduced new challenges in audio deepfake detection. Text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC) technologies can now produce convincing synthetic speech with high quality and intelligibility. This poses a serious threat to voice biometric security systems, such as automatic speaker recognition. It also increases the risks associated to the spread of spoken disinformation, where synthetic voices can be used to disseminate malicious content. In this study, we conduct an analysis of real and synthetic speech at phonetic and word levels. For that, a parallel dataset comprising real and synthetic speech signals were developed based on a subset of the LibriSpeech ASR corpus. Synthetic speech samples were generated using two TTS and one VC systems: Coqui TTS, VITS TTS, and StarGANv2 VC. We adopted HuBERT, a self-supervised speech model, to extract speech embeddings. The motivation for using this model stems from its ability to recognize sound units corresponding to the so-called pseudo phonemes. Our analysis is based on the KL divergence (KLD) between the distributions of synthetic and real phonemes, which allowed us to rank synthetic phonemes based on their alignment with their real counterpart. We also trained several classifiers per phoneme to distinguish between real and synthetic samples. We then compute the correlations between KLD and accuracies per phoneme. Besides showing a list of phonemes that are more discriminative, our findings suggest that vowels correlate better with the classifiers' performance, suggesting that the KLD can be an indicator of the most distinguishable phonemes for deepfake detection.
Keywords: Audio DeepFake Detection | Hu-BERT | Phoneme and word Embedding | Self-Supervised Speech Representation

Title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for Indonesian Speech Emotion Recognition Using the IndoWaveSentiment Dataset
Abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) significantly improves human-computer interactions by enabling computers to interpret emotional nuances of speech. Although popular datasets like EmoDB and SAVEE have been extensively utilized, they often fall short when applied to non-Western languages such as Indonesian. This research introduces and evaluates IndoWaveSentiment, a specialized data set tailored specifically to recognize emotions in Indonesian speech. The study applied various machine learning and deep learning approaches to classify five emotional states: neutral, happy, surprised, disgusted, and disappointed. Traditional machine learning models, including LightGBM and Random Forest, achieved notable accuracies of 83% and 80%, respectively. However, a deep neural network, optimized using Optuna, delivered superior performance with an accuracy of 86.67%, along with robust F 1 scores in individual emotional categories. These results underscore the efficacy of both conventional machine learning and advanced deep learning methods in emotion recognition tasks for low-resource languages. Importantly, deep learning methods demonstrated greater adapt- ability to complex emotional speech patterns. This research advances the development of culturally sensitive AI solutions and proposes further studies, particularly exploring multimodal ap- proaches and transformer-based models to improve SER systems
Keywords: Emotion classification | IndoWaveSentiment | Optuna hyperparameter tuning | Speech Emotion Recognition (SER)

Title: Deep Learning-Driven Recommendation Framework for Personalized College Vocal Music Education
Abstract: In recent years, Vocal music recommendation systems have developed crucial components of digital learning platforms that supports the personalized content delivery in educational settings. However, traditional models significantly depend on user listening history often fail to deliver accurate recommendations for new users leads to cold-start limitations. Hence, this research proposes an enhanced hybrid recommendation framework that incorporates the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to overcome these challenges. Initially, user behavioral data were gathered from public music datasets in the form of play counts and audio content. Then, the behavioral data were normalized and converted into a user-music interaction matrix, while audio signals were preprocessed into Log-Mel spectrograms. After that, the processed data were fed into CNN model to extract high-level acoustic features from the spectrograms for creating the compact content embeddings for each song. Further, a VAE-based preference modeling approach was employed to learn latent user distributions and make initial preference vectors for new users without interaction history. Finally, the proposed CNN-VAE framework produced top-n recommendations by matching audio content features with created user embeddings. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed CNN-VAE framework attained greater performance in terms of accuracy of 0.94% compared to existing CNN model.
Keywords: convolutional neural network | log-mel spectrograms | user-music interaction matrix | variational autoencoder | vocal music recommendation system

Title: A Falsetto Detection Algorithm for Enhancing Voice Gender Recognition
Abstract: This paper presents a novel falsetto detection algorithm designed to enhance the performance of Voice Gender Recognition (VGR). By incorporating Signal Processing techniques with insights from vocal pedagogy, our algorithm identifies falsetto in singing voice data to reduce gender identity ambiguity in vocal analysis. We used a pre-trained Deep Learning VGR model to assess the effectiveness of our algorithm. Experiments with various parameter settings demonstrate that the proposed algorithm reduced false positives in male voice detection and improved the VGR F1 score by a maximum of 5.3% for male voices and 2.6% for female voices. Our findings also highlight potential advancements in falsetto detection and provide insight for improving applications such as Voice Age Detection.
Keywords: falsetto | falsetto detection | signal processing | singing voice analysis | voice gender recognition

Title: HAF-Net: Hierarchical Attention Fusion Network for Multimodal Image Fusion
Abstract: Fusing medical images from diverse modalities like MRI, PET, and SPECT helps improve diagnostic precision by combining their complementary features. However, existing deep learning-based fusion methods often suffer from limited detail preservation and inefficient attention modeling across spatial and channel dimensions. This study introduces an innovative framework called hierarchical attention fusion network (HAF-Net) for robust and high-quality medical image fusion. The proposed model incorporates a hierarchical feature aggregation (HFA) module to extract scale-adaptive features, and a residual attention convolution (RAC) block to enhance fine-grained details using gradient-aware spatial and frequency-domain information. Furthermore, a multispectral frequency-aware channel attention (MFCA) mechanism is introduced to capture discriminative features across multiple frequency bands, and a cross-interaction attention module (CIAM) is designed to jointly model spatial-channel relationships. An adaptive fusion weighting (AFW) strategy is employed to dynamically combine multi-scale features based on their contextual relevance. Extensive experiments on standard PET/MRI and SPECT/MRI datasets demonstrate that HAF-Net achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art fusion methods. The results validate the effectiveness of the proposed modules in preserving structural integrity and enhancing detail in fused medical images.
Keywords: Deep learning | hierarchical feature aggregation | image enhancement | multimodal medical image fusion

Title: Privacy-Preserving Real-Time Conversation Summarization with Local AI on Wearable Devices
Abstract: Real-time conversation summarization is increasingly vital for professionals across domains such as healthcare, legal, and corporate communications. This paper presents a privacy-preserving wearable system that captures spoken conversations, performs on-device preprocessing using an ESP32 microcontroller, and transmits the audio to a locally hosted AI server for realtime summarization. The proposed architecture integrates Web Sockets for efficient data transfer, OpenAI Whisper for robust speech-to-text conversion, Pyannote for speaker diarization, and Ollama LLM for abstractive summarization. All processing is performed locally to eliminate external data exposure. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the system's effectiveness in achieving low latency, high transcription accuracy, and coherent summarization, establishing its applicability for secure and context-aware conversation analysis.
Keywords: ESP32 | Local AI | PrivacyPreserving Computing | Real-Time Summarization | Speaker Diarization | web Sockets | Whisper

Title: Development of a K-Nearest Neighbor - Based Indoor Alert System Using Vibration Engines and LCD Displays in Wrist for Deaf Individuals
Abstract: The challenges experienced by deaf individuals include maintaining safety and situational awareness in daily life due to their inability to perceive sound. To address these challenges, this study proposes a machine- learning based system utilizing a K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) model for sound detection and classification of indoor sounds, including telephone rings, doorbells, dog barks, fire alarms, and car horns, and provides haptic and visual alert feedback through vibration motors and an LCD display. The alert system achieved its highest classification accuracy for Dog barking sounds (95.00), followed by Phone ringing and Fire alarms (90.00), Doorbells (85.00), and Car horns (75.00). Despite these challenges, the system attained an overall accuracy of 86%, demonstrating improved accuracy results over the previous model. Additionally, the system demonstrated strong performance metrics, with a precision score of 85.11 and an F1-score of 91.95, further highlighting its effectiveness in accurate sound classification.
Keywords: Alert System | Indoor Sounds | K-Nearest Neighbor | Sound Classification | Sound Detection | Sound Localization

Title: WIP: A Scoping Literature Review on Survey Instruments Used to Examine STEM Graduate Students' Mental Health Experiences
Abstract: This research WIP paper will detail a scoping literature review on mental health survey instruments used to examined science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) graduate students' mental health experiences. The challenges faced by graduate students, including intense coursework, heavy rigorous research requirements, and high levels of competition, can significantly affect their mental well-being. Understanding these mental health challenges is crucial for developing effective support systems and improving the overall well-being of students. The objective of this research is to examine what and how survey instruments are used to assess mental health issues among graduate-level STEM students, guided by our overarching research question: how have survey instruments been used to assess STEM graduate students' mental health experiences? To answer this question, a scoping literature review is being conducted. Data sources included five research databases searched (EBSCO: CINAHL, EBSCO: PsycINFO, ProQuest: ERIC, PubMed, and Scopus) on May 31, 2024 and an existing scoping review on engineering graduate students' mental health experiences. We will detail our inclusionary and exclusionary criteria, how these were leveraged to conduct this review, and where we are at in the screening process. As data extraction is ongoing, preliminary findings from the 29 studies currently included will be provided. Our findings will highlight the landscape of work done, and detail areas for future work. By proactively addressing mental health concerns in graduate-level students, educational institutions can enhance student retention, academic performance, and overall quality of life.
Keywords: graduate | mental health | scoping literature review | STEM | survey

Title: Mitigating Exam Barriers for Neurodivergent Students: A Study on Sensory Adaptations in Computing Assessments
Abstract: This Work-in-Progress (WIP) study explores the impact of sensory-adapted examination environments on neurodivergent students in a postgraduate computing module within an MSc Software Development program. As concerns about generative AI increase pressure to reintroduce invigilated exams in higher education, there is a renewed urgency to ensure such environments are accessible for all learners. Neurodivergent students - including those with autism, ADHD, dyslexia, and dyspraxia - often face unique sensory and cognitive challenges that are not fully addressed by standard accommodations such as extra time or separate rooms. The module included three examinations throughout the course. While the first two were completed under typical conditions for students in the specialised quiet room, the final exam - weighted at 50% - introduced a set of tailored, sensory-friendly adjustments. These included: (1) noise-cancelling headphones with the option of white noise, music, or silence; (2) a fixed overall exam duration, incorporating extra time and rest breaks to reduce time-related anxiety; and (3) an editable digital exam format to support accessibility and executive functioning. Eleven neurodivergent students opted into the specialised quiet room setting. Post-exam surveys and interviews revealed that all students rated their experience of the adjustments at the highest level (5/5), reporting improvements in focus, reduced anxiety, and greater comfort during the exam. Performance data indicated a 2.0% increase in average scores following the adjustments, compared to a 0.9% increase across the overall cohort. While the small sample size limits statistical generalisation, these results suggest that sensory-adapted environments may offer meaningful benefits for neurodivergent learners. This study underscores the value of moving beyond conventional accommodations toward more holistic and personalised approaches to exam accessibility. Further research is needed to assess the scalability of such interventions across larger and more diverse student populations.
Keywords: feedback | Gen AI | Neurodivergent | programming | university

Title: Blending Technology and Tradition: Perception on AI, Local and Native Teachers in English Learning
Abstract: Integrating with AI in the education sector is becoming crucial and impactful for students' English performance and analyzing junior high school students' perceptions of teaching effectiveness across AI, local, and native English teachers in Taiwan, there is still limited empirical evidence on how students perceive on this, without such understanding the attempt of Bilingual 2030 policy which might limited alignment with students need. This study employs a qualitative approach, conducting interviews with a total of 357 junior high school students in Taiwan. Moreover, this study developed a structured questionnaire assessing students' experiences regarding learning outcomes. Data were collected through in-depth interviews guided by instruments which has been designed from the literature and pilot testing, with participants who have engaged with AI-enhanced, local, and native teachers in Taiwan. The study also examines the perceived strengths and limitations of AI, local, and native teachers in fostering language acquisition, students' motivation, and personalized learning. The findings suggest that a blended instructional teaching model, which integrates AI tools, local, and native teachers in learning English, can enhance students' language acquisition and cultural relevance in Taiwan's English Education System. Furthermore, this study provides new insights into students' preferences for AI, local teachers, and native teachers.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | English Learning | Local Teacher | Native Teacher | Students

Title: Predicting Wellbeing and Academic Risk from Gaming Behavior among Saudi University Students: A Machine Learning Approach
Abstract: Gaming has become one of the fastest-growing entertainment and digital industries in Saudi Arabia, supported by large-scale national investments and esports initiatives under Vision 2030. This study investigates the relationship between gaming behavior, psychological wellbeing, and academic performance among Saudi university students using a data-driven machine learning framework. A cross-sectional survey (N = 267) was conducted across multiple Saudi universities, incorporating validated psychometric instruments: the WHO-5 Wellbeing Index, GAD-7 Anxiety Scale, and IGDS9-SF for Internet Gaming Disorder. Behavioral indicators such as gaming hours, platform type, sleep quality, and self-reported GPA were also collected. Logistic regression and random forest classifiers were trained to predict low wellbeing (25.8% of students) and academic risk (8.6% of students). Predictive accuracy was modest (ROC-AUC ≈0.52 for wellbeing and 0.38 for academic risk), indicating that gaming and lifestyle variables alone provide limited predictive power. However, clustering analysis (k=3; silhouette=0.197) revealed distinct gamer typologies: Moderate Gamers (43.1%), High Wellbeing Recreational Gamers (36.0%), and Heavy High-Hour Gamers (21.0%), differing significantly in wellbeing, gaming disorder scores, and sleep quality. The findings suggest that while problematic or excessive gaming can impair wellbeing, moderate and balanced play may coexist with positive psychological outcomes. This study contributes novel regional evidence using predictive modeling and unsupervised learning, providing a data-informed foundation for digital wellbeing and esports strategies within Saudi higher education.
Keywords: academic risk | GAD-7 | Gaming behavior | IGDS9-SF | machine learning | Saudi Arabia | wellbeing | WHO-5

Title: A Comprehensive Review of Deepfake Audio Detection Techniques: Advances, Challenges and Future Directions
Abstract: The exponential growth of deepfake audio generated by artificial intelligence presents unprecedented security challenges across multiple domains, ranging from personal identity security to national intelligence. This review paper reviews recent developments in deepfake audio detection methods, with a focus on real-time detection systems. We discuss the shift from classical signal processing techniques to deep learning solutions, noting the advent of hybrid detection frameworks, which exploit complementary strengths of both areas. By conducting an in-depth performance analysis of several detection systems, we provide a comparative assessment of accuracy rates, computational time, and real-world usability in different deployment contexts. From our research, it is apparent that integrated designs that synchronize convolutional neural networks with dedicated signal processing methods hold the current best detection framework with accuracy rates higher than 94 % and processing times below 150 ms. Yet, key challenges remain, such as the quick development of deepfake technology, adversarial attacks on detection algorithms, and limitations in cross-cultural generalizability. We outline a research agenda to meet these challenges with adaptive learning systems, multimodal fusion, explainable AI paradigms, and edge-specialized architectures. This review consolidates existing understanding of audio deepfake detection and offers researchers and practitioners a complete basis for designing next-generation forensic tools to counter more advanced audio manipulation technologies.
Keywords: Adversarial | Artificial Intelligence | Audio Forensics | Deep Learning | Deepfake | Neural Networks

Title: Advances in Bird Bioacoustics Using Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Review of Vocal Mechanisms, Acoustic Communication, and Conservation Application
Abstract: Recent advances in deep learning (DL) have transformed bird bioacoustics by allowing for automated analysis of vocal signals on unprecedented scales. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), residual models (BirdNET), and hybrid C N N-R N N architectures can now classify hundreds to thousands of species based on their calls. These methods uncover acoustic features associated with bird vocal organs (syrinx physiology) and communication function, while also significantly improving conservation monitoring (species inventories, habitat assessment, population tracking). Selfsupervised learning, data augmentation (mix-up, background noise), and transfer learning are all complementary approaches that help improve model generalization. Modern bioacoustics indices and sensor networks work together with machine learning pipelines to generate ecological indicators. This review discusses key technical advances (BirdNET ResNet, CNN-LSTM models, transformers, and self-supervised methods) with performance metrics, as well as their implications for understanding bird vocal mechanisms and acoustic communication. Conservation applications such as population tracking, biodiversity indexing, and endangered species detection now benefit from machine learning-driven passive acoustic monitoring (PAM), mobile apps, and dense sensor networks. The review also discusses key challenges such as noise interference, data imbalance, and model generalization, and suggests future directions centered on standardized datasets and multimodal fusion. Future directions include the development of standardized datasets, the enhancements to transfer learning protocols, and long-term studies of vocal learning.
Keywords: Bird Bioacoustics | Convolutional Neural Network | Deep Learning | Passive Acoustic Monitoring | Temporal Signal Processing | Unsupervised learning

Title: Fostering Musical Partnership: A Human-Centric Robotic Co-Player for Accessible and Adaptive Piano Learning
Abstract: Meaningful human-robot interaction in creative domains requires systems that can adapt not just to tasks, but to the user's style, skill, and emotional state. In the context of piano playing, this challenge is acute for both users with disabilities and beginners. We introduce a human-centric robotic co-player engineered to transcend mere accompaniment and become a collaborative musical partner. Our system architecture integrates a machine learning model for real-time adaptation to player tempo and harmony with a biomimetic robotic hand that provides tangible, expressive feedback. A user study involving one-handed pianists (N=10) and novice learners (N=10) was conducted to evaluate the system's impact on accessibility, learning, and user experience. Quantitative analysis revealed significant gains in playing synchronization and a dramatic increase in the ability of disabled users to approach complex repertoire. Qualitative feedback strongly corroborated these findings, with participants reporting a profound sense of empowerment, engagement, and partnership. This work contributes a validated design for adaptive robotic systems that enhance human capability and foster collaborative creativity. Creating genuine musical partnership between humans and robots requires a shift from pre-programmed accompaniment to real-time, predictive collaboration. Current systems often fail to adapt to a user's style and intent, posing a significant barrier for learners and individuals with motor impairments. This paper introduces a human-centric robotic co-player whose core intelligence is a Transformer-based neural network designed for live harmonic prediction. By analyzing a user's melodic MIDI input in real-time, the model generates a musically coherent accompaniment that dynamically adapts to the human's timing and expression. This AI-driven musical response is physically rendered with low latency by a 6-DoF manipulator featuring a custom, bio-inspired hand, creating a closed-loop interactive system. We validated this architecture through a formal user study involving one-handed pianists (N=10) and novice learners (N=10). The system yielded significant objective performance gains, including a 45.4% reduction in average synchronization error. Critically, qualitative feedback confirmed that users overwhelmingly perceived the system as a collaborative partner, not merely a tool. This work contributes a validated architecture for embodied AI systems that successfully fosters creative partnership and enhances musical accessibility.
Keywords: Assistive Robotics | Deep Learning for Music | Embodied AI | Human-Centric AI | Human-Robot Collaboration | Piano Accessibility | Transformer Models

Title: Comparative Analysis of SVM and Random Forest for Smart Grid Stability and Reliability Prediction
Abstract: The escalating complexity of smart grid systems, propelled by variable energy demands and heightened incorporation of renewable sources, has intensified the want for precise and prompt stability forecasting. This paper performs a comparative examination of two prevalent machine learning (ML) algorithms Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest (RF) to forecast the stability of smart grids. The research utilizes the Smart Grid Stability and Reliability Dataset from Kaggle, comprising 1000 samples with 24 numerical features that denote key physical and operational elements of the grid. The preprocessing stages encompassed normalization and stratified dataset split to provide balanced training and evaluation. Both models were designed to categorize the grid condition as either stable or unstable. Results indicate that RF achieved a superior prediction accuracy of 98.66%, improving SVM, which reached an accuracy of 94.33%. The exceptional performance of RF is ascribed to its ensemble architecture and capacity to adeptly describe complex nonlinear interactions. This investigation highlights the efficacy of RF as a dependable ML instrument for predicting smart grid reliability. Its exceptional precision renders it ideal for implementation in real-time decision support systems designed to uphold grid reliability and avert system failures.
Keywords: Classification | Grid Forecasting | Power Systems | Random Forest (RF) | Reliability Assessment | Smart Grid | Stability Prediction | Support Vector Machine (SVM)

Title: InstaScript: Convert Voice Notes to Summarized Smart Notes using NLP
Abstract: In recent years, the increasing volume of audio-based content in academic and professional environments has necessitated efficient tools for automated note-taking and summarization. The paper presents InstaScript, a novel web-based application that leverages automatic speech recognition (ASR) and natural language processing (NLP) to transcribe voice recordings and generate structured summary notes. Built using OpenAI's Whisper model for robust transcription and state-of-the-art text summarization algorithms, InstaScript provides a seamless pipeline from audio input to concise, downloadable bullet-point summaries. The system is designed with user-centric features, including support for multiple audio formats, real-time processing, and PDF export of results. Emphasis is placed on maintaining transcription accuracy, relevance of summarized content, and delivering an intuitive user interface. The proposed system demonstrates significant utility in educational, research, and corporate settings, where rapid information retrieval from spoken content is essential.
Keywords: Audio Transcription | Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) | Deep Learning | Natural Language Processing (NLP) | Productivity Tools | Smart Notes | Streamlit Application | Text Summarization | Voice-to-Text | Whisper Model

Title: Leveraging Ensemble Methods for Accurate Credit Card Fraud Detection
Abstract: Credit card fraud presents a risk to financial institutions and individuals, resulting in substantial monetary losses and critical security concerns. Detecting fraudulent transactions in real-time is challenging due to the prevalence of valid transactions and the infrequency of fraud within the entire dataset. Moreover, offenders continually alter their methods. This work established the feasibility of developing an ensemble system utilizing machine learning algorithms, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, and Boost, integrated with the soft voting classifier for the detection of credit card fraud. The algorithms were utilized on both authentic transaction data and generated data to assess their performance according to several metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. The experimental results indicated that the ensemble-enhanced outcomes are relatively higher than singular algorithm predictions, reducing false positives while augmenting real positives. This technology is a reliable and adaptable instrument designed to identify probable fraud situations for banks and financial organizations, safeguarding their clients' assets.
Keywords: K-means clustering and Decision Tree | Machine learning techniques

Title: Research on audio signal feature recognition and classification based on machine learning
Abstract: Audio signal classification holds significant application value in multimedia information processing, intelligent surveillance, human-computer interaction, and related fields. This paper proposes a machine learning-based method for audio signal feature extraction and classification. The approach first extracts time-frequency domain features through signal processing techniques such as Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and Mel Frequency Cospectra (MFCC). A support vector machine (SVM) algorithm is then employed to construct the classification model. Experiments conducted on the UrbanSound8K dataset, which contains 10 categories of common urban environmental audio, demonstrate that the SVM model combining comprehensive features achieves an 89.7% classification accuracy rate on the test set. Notably, MFCC and its differential features show the most significant performance improvements. This study validates the effectiveness of traditional machine learning methods in audio signal classification tasks, providing theoretical foundations and technical references for the design of intelligent audio analysis systems.
Keywords: Audio signal processing | feature extraction | machine learning | signal classification | support vector machine

Title: Noise Reduction Strategies For Optimising Speech Signal Clarity: A Comprehensive Review
Abstract: Dealing with speech signal quality in communication systems is a significant challenge due to environmental and channel noise. Reduced intelligibility and communication effectiveness are the inevitable result of this constant battle against noise. However, if advanced technologies can be harnessed to minimise it in helpful ways, then that might remain a bridge too far. This review examines advanced noise reduction strategies aiming to maximise speech signal intelligibility. A complete analysis of various noise reduction techniques, including spectral subtraction, Wiener filtering, and more recent deep learning-based ones, is given. Special attention is paid to creating effective models of noise suppression, which employ the Short-Time Fourier Transform spectrogram as an essential tool in their construction process. These models maximise speech quality by removing noise while preserving central speech features. Performance metrics such as Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) and Short-Time Objective Intelligibility (STOI) are used to evaluate how well these methods work. Also, honesty is introduced regarding whether the study is based on traditional or state-of-the-art techniques, with recent breakthroughs highlighted and then put into context for real-time communication systems. Finally, the research provides a helpful overview of current research approaches, including their strengths and weaknesses and possible future work. It is an essential reference tool for researchers and practitioners seeking to improve speech signals' clarity in noisy work environments.
Keywords: Noise Reduction | Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) | Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) | Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) | Speech Signal Enhancement

Title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Models and Optimization Techniques for Financial Fraud Detection
Abstract: Every day machine learning in financial systems is increasing with financial institutions taking every steps in their power to detect and block counterfeit transactions. Today, modern electronic payment instruments and financial facilities are becoming more and more susceptible to new methods of fraud which are unobtrusively reproducing the activities of legitimate interests to the detriment of the economy which is losing incalculable sums of money. In order to overcome this the combination technique of quantum and classical methods of calculating the data is a great way to enhance the reliability and accuracy of the fraud detection. It is applied by means of Quantum Support Vector Machine, Variational Quantum Classifier, the classical algorithms of Support Vector Machine and K-Nearest Neighbor with an ensemble based on Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization. These algorithms are used together to scan a stream of transactions in real time and classify what is legitimate behaviour and what is unfavourable behaviour. The work provides evidence to prove that hybrid quantum-classical techniques can improve on the performance of classical systems using improved recall, less false negatives and the speed of detection of new types of frauds. It is shown that the integration of quantum intelligence based upon classical methods of analysis is a powerful and fruitful means to enhance levels of secure financial practice and help combat large scale financial frauds in modern digital environments.
Keywords: K-Nearest Neighbor | Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization | Quantum Support Vector Machine | Support Vector Machine | Variational Quantum Classifier

Title: Research on the Application of Machine Learning in Computer Vision Object Recognition
Abstract: To address the challenges of insufficient accuracy and real-time performance of traditional CNN object recognition algorithms in complex scenarios, this study designed a multi-scale attention fusion convolutional neural network (MSA-CNN). This model optimizes feature extraction through a multi-scale feature fusion module (parallel extraction of 3×3/5×5/7×7 convolution kernels + dynamic weight allocation) and an attention mechanism module (channel-wise + spatial feature filtering). Experiments were conducted on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and COCO 2017 datasets using an Intel Core i7-12700K and RTX 3090 GPU using the PyTorch 2.0 framework. The model was compared with the Faster R-CNN and YOLOv5 algorithms, and ablation experiments were conducted. Results show that MSA-CNN achieves a mean average performance (mAP) of 89.2% on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset, representing improvements of 6.7 and 2.4 percentage points over Faster R-CNN (82.5%) and YOLOv5 (86.8%), respectively. Its small object performance on the COCO 2017 dataset reaches 42.8%, a 7.6 percentage point improvement over the competing algorithms. In terms of real-time performance, it achieves 38 frames per second (FPS) and 26.3 milliseconds inference time at 416×416 resolution, meeting the requirements of scenarios such as autonomous driving. Ablation experiments show that removing the multi-scale and attention modules reduces mAP by 4.1 and 3.5 percentage points, respectively, validating the effectiveness of these core modules.
Keywords: COCO dataset | computer vision | experimental simulation | Machine learning | multi-scale attention fusion convolutional neural network (MSA-CNN) | object recognition | PASCAL VOC dataset | real-time performance | recognition accuracy

Title: Enhanced Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through LightGBM and Advanced Feature Optimization
Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) refers to a complicated neurodevelopmental disorder that influences social interaction, verbal communication, and adaptability of behaviour. This is important because early diagnosis can greatly enhance the long-term. Nonetheless, conventional machine learning methods and traditional approaches to diagnosis are prone to redundancy of attributes, high dimensionality, reduced generalization, and lower diagnostic accuracy. To overcome the difficulties, the current research proposes an ASD detector in the form of Light GBM. As the primary dataset, the ASD Children Traits Dataset, which comprises Behavioral indicators and demographic information, is utilized. During the preprocessing phase, numerical variables are normalized to stabilize and accelerate convergence. The extraction of features is used to realize the underlying Behavioral patterns. Further, the feature selection procedure is applied to extract the most informative features (Sequential Feature Selection (SFS). This helps to reduce redundancy of features and to increase their interpretability. Lastly, LightGBM was used as a classifier option, including Exclusive Feature Bundling (EFB) and Gradient-based One-Side Sampling (GOSS) to easily work with structured data. The experimental assessment showed good performance with an accuracy of 0.99 %, precision of 1.0 %, recall of 0.99%, F1-score of 0.99 %, and ROC-AUC of 1.0%. These findings substantiate that LightGBM has better predictive performance and can be regarded as an advanced and highly reliable predictive instrument to detect ASD in its initial stages.
Keywords: ASD Children Traits Dataset | autism spectrum disorder (ASD) | Early Diagnosis | Feature Selection | LightGBM | Machine Learning

Title: Brainwave-Driven Emotional Speech Analysis using Adversarial Networks and Combined Deep RL Approaches for Improved Recognition Performance
Abstract: Recognition of emotions in speech is a complex problem because of the inconsistency in vocal expressions and the absence of the trusted internal emotional expressions. This paper presents Brainwave-Driven Emotional Speech Analysis, a composite system combining adversarial synthetic EEG generation and deep reinforcement learning-based classifier in order to improve the accuracy of emotion recognition. It begins by extracting high-level acoustic features of input speech and then uses a Progressive Growing Generative Adversarial Network (PG-GAN) to produce synthetic EEG signal energies that are related to emotions. The resulting EEG signal is denoised with a Savitzky Golay denoising filter followed by additional processing by a combined deep learning network comprising of LSTM, GRU and Deep Q-network models to provide strong emotion classification in positive, negative and neutral affective states. Experimental analysis proves better recognition results than traditional audio only models, with emphasis on the merits of the use of synthesized neural patterns as auxiliary emotional signals. The given solution offers a new avenue of improving affective computing systems through the application of adversarial brainwave synthesis to supplement scarce real EEG data and enhance the processing of emotional context in speech-based applications.
Keywords: affective computing | deep reinforcement learning | EEG synthesis | hybrid neural networks | Progressive GAN | speech emotion recognition

Title: Real-Time Voice Signal Classification for Identifying Emergency Scenarios using Deep Learning
Abstract: Screams are among the distinctive auditory cues that are often produced during emergencies such as violent incidents, medical crises, and public disturbances. Public safety and quick emergency response depend on the timely detection of these sounds. Manual reporting is the foundation of traditional emergency response systems, resulting in inefficiencies and delays. This study suggests a real-time voice signal classification system that analyses auditory signals to identify emergency situations to overcome this limitation. The system divides sound into emergency and non-emergency categories using deep learning techniques. To enable precise classification, melspectrogram representations of audio signals are subjected to temporal and spatial feature extraction using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. A carefully selected dataset of emergency and nonemergency sounds is used to train the model, and features are pre-processed and normalized prior to training. The proposed system is designed for real-time performance, ensuring quick detection and automated SOS alert generation.
Keywords: audio classification | convolutional neural network (CNN) | Emergency sound detection | real-time sound recognition

Title: EffWhiS: A Proposed Efficient Approach for Speech-to-Text Streaming Whisper
Abstract: Whisper Streaming is an emerging approach for real-time automatic speech recognition (ASR), extending OpenAI’s Whisper model, and using local agreement to commit transcriptions. However, its reliance on fixed chunk sizes and local agreement often causes unnecessary delays or premature outputs. To address this, we propose an efficient Whisper Streaming (EffWhiS), a refined streaming algorithm that enhances Whisper’s responsiveness and accuracy through two key strategies: (1) majority-vote commit, which commits a word if it appears in at least two of the last three decoding passes; and (2) segment consistency constraint, which allows commits only when consecutive segment predictions agree. The benchmark ESIC corpus and two hours of recordings of actual Vietnamese meetings are used to evaluate our proposed EffWhiS. The findings show that, in comparison to the original Whisper Streaming, EffWhiS achieves a lower Word Error Rate and a significantly lower Average Commit Latency. Notably, EffWhiS maintains high accuracy even at a short chunk size of 0.5 seconds, confirming its robustness for practical streaming ASR deployments. These improvements are consistent across various chunk sizes in both English and Vietnamese, highlighting the generalizability of our proposed approach. With its balance between accuracy and latency, EffWhiS offers a potential path for effective and deployable streaming ASR systems.
Keywords: Automatic Speech Recognition | Efficient Streaming | Speech to Text | Whisper streaming

Title: Designing Musical Instrument Identification Systems Using Lightweight Machine Learning Architectures
Abstract: Musicology is a vast field in which the use of electronic instruments has increased significantly with the development of digital audio workstations and virtual instruments. Selecting the appropriate instrument is crucial for producing high-quality music. The traditional approach to identifying musical instruments relies on manually listening to audio recordings, which is time-consuming and inefficient. Therefore, musical signal processing has become one of the most important tasks in audio signal processing. It enables the identification of instruments in music based on their acoustic features. The proposed work focuses on extracting audio features from WAV files and developing an ensemble model that combines Random Forest and Support Vector Machine classifiers using a voting strategy to identify the instruments used in music. The findings highlight the potential applications of this research in music information retrieval systems and contribute to the growing field of computational musicology by providing a scalable and accurate approach to musical instrument identification, achieving an accuracy of 95%.
Keywords: Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients | Persian Instruments | Support Vector Machine | Time-Frequency Domain | Voting Classifier

Title: DPMNet: Frequency-Aware Dual-Path Modulation for Robust Scene Text Detection
Abstract: Scene text detection is crucial for applications like document analysis, autonomous driving, and instant translation. Despite progress in deep learning, existing methods struggle with geometric diversity and multi-scale text due to ineffective feature fusion and context modeling. Traditional approaches often naively combine high-level and low-level features, losing fine details in small text and overemphasizing high-level semantics, reducing detection accuracy. To mitigate these constraints, DPMNet is presented, a novel network with two key modules: The Frequency-Aware Dual-Path Modulation (FADPM) module, which adaptively refines features by enhancing high-frequency details while optimizing low-frequency semantics. The Multibranch Adaptive Fusion (MAF) module leverages multi-scale dilated convolutions and spatial weight allocation to improve context integration. We evaluated the proposed methods TotalText, CTW1500 and ICDAR19 ArT. Extensive experiments have demonstrated the state-of-the-art performance and our method's exceptional robustness.
Keywords: adaptive fusion | Frequency-Aware | text detection

Title: Deep Learning and Adaptive Large Language Model for Speech Denoising and Performance Enhancement
Abstract: Noise suppression is a vital signal processing technique that relies on precise estimators and parameters. Conventionally, deep learning-based speech-denoising methods have required noise-free speech signals for training, limiting their practicality in real-time scenarios. In this study, we develop an innovative self-supervised learning approach that significantly enhances speech denoising in real-world audio environments without noise-free speech signals. Our method outperforms Wiener filtering by ∼ 33% on SNR and ∼ 75% on Segmental SNR (SSNR) metrics and introduces a large language-based model (LLM) for denoising, improving the output sound quality.
Keywords: Large Language Model (LLM) | MEL filter bank (MFB) | Noise Suppression | Performance Indicators | Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) | Speech Signals

Title: An Improved ResNet50-based Speech Recognition System
Abstract: To address the limitation of low accuracy in traditional machine learning-based speech recognition, this paper innovatively proposes a speech recognition system based on an improved ResNet50 model. The initial ResNet50 model is enhanced by incorporating the CBAM module and the ReliefF feature selection algorithm. Experiments demonstrate that the ResNet50-CBAM-ReliefF model achieves a recognition accuracy of 94%, significantly outperforming traditional machine learning methods. To improve the model's anomaly detection capability, the negative branch training method is introduced. Experimental results show that the negative branch regularization method has minimal impact on recognition accuracy, thereby enhancing the model's anomaly detection ability without compromising its recognition performance.
Keywords: CBAM | component: Speech recognition | Negative branch regularization | ReliefF | ResNet50

Title: PAPR Reduction Method for CPM-OFDM System Based on AF-HDC-CPMNet
Abstract: To address the high Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) issue in Continuous Phase Modulation Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (CPM-OFDM) systems, which causes power amplifier nonlinear distortion, this paper proposes a novel deep learning network named AF-HDC-CPMNet. Its core is an Attention-enhanced Hybrid Dilated Convolution (AF-HDC) module, which employs coprime dilation rates to capture multi-scale phase dependencies and a branch attention mechanism to dynamically weight features critical for global phase continuity. Additionally, a phase-preserving decoder using nearest-neighbor upsampling is designed to mitigate phase distortion. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves a significant PAPR reduction to 3.3 dB at a CCDF of 10<sup>-3</sup> while maintaining excellent Bit Error Rate (BER) performance, outperforming traditional and other deep learning-based schemes.
Keywords: attention mechanism | CPM-OFDM | deep learning | hybrid dilated convolution | peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction | phase continuity

Title: Machine Learning for Flow Rate and AICD Status Prediction Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
Abstract: In this work, we present machine learning (ML) models for predicting bulk flow rate through a pipe and inflow from Autonomous Inflow Control Devices (AICDs) along the pipe using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) data. The proposed methods consist of four steps: pre-processing the acoustic data, extracting the relevant acoustic features, conditioning the data for use in ML, and utilizing machine learning models for the prediction and classification of the flow rate and AICD status, respectively. The acoustic features used for training the machine learning models involve different time- and frequency-domain features of the measured DAS data. The performance and the relative importance of the proposed features are investigated across various frequency bands using statistical analysis to determine their correlation with the flow-induced signal. The most dominant acoustic signature generated by bulk flow is found to be at low frequency (∼1 – 100 Hz.), meanwhile the acoustic signature generated by inflow through an AICD is dominant at frequencies higher than 1 kHz. Regression and classification models using different techniques including multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and Light Gradient Boosting are supplied with the time- and frequency-domain features to predict flow rate and classify AICD status, respectively. We investigated the effectiveness of processing the acoustic data into features for machine learning through a series of various optional pre-processing steps (including channel averaging, normalizations, selection of specific frequency bands, filtering, etc.), calculation of temporal and frequency band features, and final post-processing for training and testing within a ML model. DAS data acquired from a comprehensive laboratory campaign, comprising both single-phase water and single-phase oil flowing conditions, was used to train and validate the machine learning models. Regression models estimate the bulk flow rate with average percentage error = 7-10 % and AICD flow rate with average percentage error = 4-5 %. The classification model predicts the AICD status with nearly 100% accuracy. This work demonstrates the viability of a ML-based DAS monitoring strategy for bulk flow rate estimation, AICD inflow rate (and allocation) estimation, as well as AICD status evaluation.

Title: A Multilayer Perceptron Approach to Detecting Mental Health Conditions from Music Preferences
Abstract: Early identification of mental health disorders is essential to allow timely interventions and improve overall well-being. This study explores the potential of using Machine Learning (ML) to detect mental health conditions, specifically depression, anxiety, insomnia, and Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD), based on individual preferences of the music genre. The dataset containing anonymized music listening behavior and self-reported mental health statuses was collected and preprocessed. Four ML classifiers, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naive Bayes (NB), Random Forest (RF), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), were used and evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation and an 80:20 train-test split. The experimental results indicated that MLP produced the highest classification accuracy for depression is 58% and anxiety is 60%, while NB demonstrated superior performance in detecting OCD with 81% of accuracy and insomnia with 66% accuracy value. These results highlight the feasibility of using music preferences as noninvasive indicators for mental health screening. Future research should aim to incorporate heterogeneous data sources and conduct clinical validation to enhance the accuracy and reliability of the proposed approach.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Machine Learning | Mental Health | Music Genre

Title: Hybrid AI-Physics Framework for Lost Circulation Zone Diagnosis: A Data-Driven Iterative Approach Integrating Drilling-Logging Big Data with Theoretical Models
Abstract: This paper develops a hybrid AI-physics framework designed to enable real-time, cost-effective diagnosis of loss zones in complex formations. The framework integrates drilling and surface logging big data with physics-based models to address two critical industry challenges: (1) the high uncertainty of manual theoretical calculations and (2) the delays and costs of post-event instrument-based measurements. By using real-time data, it rapidly determines loss zone characteristics (depth, channel type, and fracture dimensions), enhancing treatment success rates and holding the potential to reduce operational costs. A Sichuan Basin database was constructed from over 100 wells using an event-based approach, capturing time-series data around lost circulation events. Theoretical models for determining loss zone depth, identifying lost circulation channel types, and estimating fracture width were evaluated through statistical error analysis. AI optimization methods tailored to each theoretical model were selected, and corresponding AI-physics hybrid models were developed independently, followed by training and validating these models on a database randomly split with 80% allocated for training and 20% for validation. These hybrid models were embedded into the Engineering Intelligent Support Center (EISC) with real-time drilling and surface logging parameters to establish loss zone diagnostic framework. A machine learning-enhanced drilling hydraulics model was developed to calculate the loss zone depth using real-time drilling and surface logging parameters, achieving a test set mean error of 4.06%-4.87%, representing a 10%-48% reduction compared to theoretical models. A convolutional neural network-based intelligent classification model was established to identify lost circulation channel types, leveraging geometric features of loss rate vs. time and mud pit volume vs. time curves to distinguish natural fractures, induced fractures, microfractures/high-permeability pores, and medium-to-large fractures/caverns, with a test set accuracy exceeding 94%. An ensemble learning model integrating AdaBoost with solid- and liquid-phase lost circulation dynamics was constructed to invert fracture width, utilizing drilling fluid or lost circulation material slurry flow data, reducing test set mean errors to 12.07%-42.73%, an improvement of up to 73.46% over theoretical methods. Field trials across over 20 wells in the Sichuan Basin demonstrated that, following post-lost circulation events, engineers could access real-time drilling and surface logging data via the field-deployed Framework connected to the EISC, rapidly determining the loss zone depth, channel type, and fracture width to inform lost circulation control strategies. The framework achieved a field-validated diagnostic accuracy exceeding 85%, with ongoing updates to lost circulation data expected to further enhance precision. This work introduces the first EISC-integrated hybrid AI-physics framework for loss zone diagnosis. It bridges the gap between data-driven AI and physics-based models, enabling rapid, cost-effective diagnosis with acceptable accuracy and without additional downhole instrumentation. The framework offers engineers a practically validated tool for decision-making in lost circulation treatment, balancing theoretical rigor with AI adaptability.

Title: Conformer-Driven Nonnegative Matrix Factorization: A Unified Optimization Framework for Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement
Abstract: A hybrid architecture integrating Conformcr encoders with multichannel Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF) is proposed for speech enhancement.
