The model leverages the global-local feature extraction capabilities of Conformer blocks while preserving the interprctablc spcctrospatial decomposition of NMF through differentiable multiplicative update rules. This study derive a unified optimization framework based on the majorization-minimization of the multichannel Itakura-Saito divergence, enabling joint learning of spectral and spatial parameters in an end-to-end manner. The proposed approach effectively combines the strengths of deep learning and traditional probabilistic modeling: the Conformer encoder captures long-range contextual dependencies and complex acoustic patterns, while the NMF structure ensures interpretability and stability in spectro-temporal decomposition. Experimental results on the CHiME dataset demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance across multiple objective metrics, including SDR, PESQ, and STOI, validating its effectiveness in real-world multi-channel speech enhancement tasks.
Keywords: Conformer | Multi-Channel speech enhancement | nonnegative matrix factorization

Title: Research on Data Feature Processing Model Based on Hierarchical Analysis and STFT
Abstract: This paper proposes a comprehensive evaluation model of audio formats integrating entropy weighting and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), a parameter optimization model based on regression analysis, and an adaptive noise suppression model combining short-time Fourier transform (STFT), focusing on the algorithmic implementation of multidimensional audio feature quantization, coding parameter optimization, and noise intelligent processing. Firstly, the performance ranking of audio formats is realized by constructing an entropy weighting-AHP weighting model, quantifying the indexes such as storage efficiency and signal fidelity, calculating the weights by using a judgment matrix and establishing a Comprehensive Performance Index (CPI) model. Secondly, the Quality Scoring Index (QSI) is introduced, the mapping relationship between parameters and performance is established through regression analysis, and the combination of coding parameters is optimized using linear regression and machine learning methods. Finally, the time-frequency domain noise features are extracted based on STFT, the noise types are identified by combining the minimum statistics algorithm with peak detection, the narrowband noise is suppressed by IIR trap filter, the background noise is eliminated by Wiener filter, and the transient noise is handled by adaptive thresholding. The model system realizes the whole process of processing from format evaluation to noise suppression through the synergy of multiple algorithms, and has the advantages of multidimensional quantitative analysis, scene adaptive optimization and accurate identification of noise types, providing systematic algorithmic solutions for audio processing.
Keywords: analytic hierarchy process | entropy weight method | noise suppression | regression analysis model | short-time Fourier transform

Title: From Reactive to Proactive: How IoT Re-Imagines Healthcare Delivery Systems
Abstract: The purpose of this study is to assess how Internet of Things (IoT) technologies have revolutionized healthcare delivery, with an emphasis on resource optimisation, clinical results, and operational efficiency. In three crucial areas-hospital asset management, smart medical equipment utilization, and remote patient monitoring-the major goal is to compare healthcare organizations that have implemented IoT technologies with those that have not. In order to do this, the study examines how IoT-enabled systems are implemented in operating rooms and examines how they affect procedural efficiency and surgical safety. In order to create a responsive and integrated healthcare environment, the project also investigates the integration of IoT devices designed for patients and surgical personnel. IoT, which sits at the nexus of medicine and technology, is being studied as a tactical instrument to tackle enduring issues in healthcare, including medication shortages, medical blunders, system overloads, and disruptions caused by pandemics. The approach uses a framework for innovation that is problem-oriented and emphasises workable solutions that encourage cooperation between healthcare professionals and IoT developers. The study measures gains in operational throughput, response time, and data correctness using simulated performance datasets and Python-based predictive modelling. The results highlight how preventative treatment, allocation of resources, and overall clinical effectiveness are all greatly improved by real-time IoT integration.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Biosensors | Healthcare | Internet of Things (IoT) | Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) | Sustainable Development Goal

Title: Fine-Tuning Wav2Vec2 for Low-Resource Kichwa Automatic Speech Recognition
Abstract: In recent years, advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have significantly accelerated the development of natural language processing and automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems for high-resource languages, raising concerns about the marginalization of ancestral and underrepresented languages. In this context, this work explores the fine-tuning of the Wav2Vec 2.0 model, developed by Meta AI, for ASR in Kichwa-a low-resource language spoken in the Ecuadorian Andes. The training process utilized two datasets totaling approximately 8 hours of audio, segmented into clips ranging from 1.5 to 5 seconds, with manually aligned transcriptions created using ELAN software. Fine-tuning was performed using the Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss function. After multiple experiments, a two-tailed Wilcoxon signed-rank test revealed no statistically significant improvement when applying SpecAugment. The best-performing model, trained without data augmentation, achieved promising results on the test set: a Word Error Rate (WER) of 0.262, a Character Error Rate (CER) of 0.120, and a Match Error Rate (MER) of 0.401. These findings d emonstrate the viability of adapting pre-trained self-supervised models to low-resource settings and underscore the potential of ASR technologies to support greater linguistic inclusivity in artificial intelligence.
Keywords: Audio | Automatic Speech Recognition | Connectionist Temporal Classification | Deep Learning | FineTuning | Kichwa

Title: Design of Indicators for the Logistic Control of Products in a Commercial Company Based on Business Intelligence
Abstract: In different types of companies and in different parts of the world, the integration of ICT with product logistics management has several advantages. The overall objective of this research study is to design performance indicators to monitor logistics and product distribution in a company based on business intelligence. The methodology used was a review of the literature, observation of other models found in the articles, induction, deduction, modelling and a digital survey technique. Nineteen relevant scientific articles were included that helped answer research questions focused on transport as the most widely used logistics activity, the role of the distributor as the main participant, business intelligence as the most widely used information technology, and service improvement as the main objective pursued by research models. A three-layer model was proposed: Data Source, Processing-Storage, and Presentation, which helps obtain real data and enables decision-making and improved operations. In the survey, an average of 89% of experts agree and strongly agree that the tools, IoT devices, proposed indicators, dimensions mentioned, and table of facts are appropriate elements for the model. Experts also mentioned other indicators, dimensions, and facts that could be added to the model.
Keywords: Business Intelligence | Indicators | Information Technologies | Product Logistics Control

Title: Automated Detection of Low Carbon Technologies from Electricity Smart Meter Data
Abstract: The proliferation of Low-Carbon Technologies (LCTs), such as electric vehicles, heat pumps, and solar panels, poses a challenge for distribution system operators (DSOs). LCTs are installed within the household premises, i.e., behind the meter, and do not usually require a formal registration process. Since DSOs are generally unaware of their presence, automated detection techniques that can identify LCTs from electricity smart meters (SMs) measurements are becoming essential for network planning. Recent advances in Machine Learning (ML) have shown the potential of supervised learning techniques in energy demand forecasting, load profiling and segmentation, and smart metering. ML models can identify and classify usage patterns, providing immediate data insights and real-time feedback. This paper investigates the application of supervised learning approaches in LCT detection and develops two classifiers that can reliably detect their presence in SM profiles. The performance of both classifiers is demonstrated using a publicly available dataset SM measurements collected in Belgium and compared with other state-of-the-art techniques. Additionally, the generalisation ability of each classifier is examined on an unseen dataset from Ireland.
Keywords: energy profiling | low-carbon technologies | machine learning | smart meters

Title: Audio Watermarking Using Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Transform (DTCWT) for Robustness Against Compression
Abstract: Audio watermarking serves a double purpose as a technique which adds invisible metadata to audio files to protect copyright elements and establish content accuracy. This research analyses a strong watermarking approach that implements Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Transform (DTCWT) because of its impressive time-frequency localisation capabilities and shift-invariance properties. Current watermarking solutions show inadequate resistance against the lossy compression techniques MP3 and AAC because these algorithms cause significant damage to embedded watermarks. This work develops a new framework by combining Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Transform with Deep Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Network (U-Net). By training its U-Net model, the system builds the ability to place watermarks intelligently throughout mid-frequency DTCWT coefficients, resulting in compression-resistant watermarked audio with maintained sound quality. The proposed embedding method builds protectable and robust watermarks into music and speech signals with superior hidden quality and retrieval performance despite compression processes. Our approach generates better Bit Error Rate (BER) results with improved audio quality compared to conventional watermarking systems, according to experimental evaluations.
Keywords: Audio Watermarking | Compression Robustness | Deep Learning | DTCWT | etc | Signal Processing | U-Net

Title: Development of Snow Cover Product from Scatterometer Using Google Earth Engine
Abstract: The Western Himalayas are an important source of fresh water that impact agriculture, hydroelectricity production, and natural disaster management and the variability of snow over Himalayas may affect these domains. Most the traditional approaches to remote sensing can't work properly either because of persistent cloud cover or give poor performance while examining changing snow-cover areas. Hence, this study has attempted the development of SCATSAT-1 scatterometer data integration with the Google Earth Engine and neural network for the binary classification of the snow/non-snow zones. The proposed approach achieved 97% of accuracy, validated through highly correlated MODIS datasets. Thus, the proposed approach provides an efficient framework for the highly accurate mapping of snow cover areas that may facilitate better resource management and disaster mitigation strategies in high-altitude, snow-fed regions.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Google Earth Engine | Neural Network | SCATSAT-1 | Snow | Western Himalayas

Title: Speech-GAN: Black-Box Attack against Automatic Speech Recognition Systems
Abstract: Today, most Automatic Speech Recognition systems rely on Deep Learning to convert human speech to text and interpretable commands. However, such systems can be deceived by specially crafted adversarial audios, misleading them to incorrect audio transcriptions, and exposing technologies using these systems to security flaws. Hence, knowing the weaknesses of these systems is crucial if they are to be used in safety-critical and security-sensitive applications. In this work, we present Speech-GAN, a Generative Adversarial Network that aims at creating adversarial audios deceiving Deep Learning-based Automatic Speech Recognition models in a black-box setting, without drastically altering the audio quality. With a success rate of 100%, and signal-to-noise ratios averaging -9.47 dB, our black-box untargeted attack is experimentally validated on a Wav2Vec2.0 Automatic Speech Recognition model, for 1,000 audio samples spanning 10 command words.
Keywords: Adversarial example | Audio | Automatic Speech Recognition | Black-box attack | Generative Adversarial Network

Title: Encrypted Malicious Traffic Detection with Limited Data Based on Active Learning
Abstract: Accurate encrypted malicious traffic detection is crucial for improving network service quality. Existing methods leverage the widespread application of machine learning (ML) to distinguish encrypted malicious traffic from normal traffic by learning the statistical characteristics of traffic. However, the scarcity of high-quality annotated encrypted malicious traffic data, especially malicious traffic samples, limits the performance of these supervised learning methods. Additionally, annotating network traffic is challenging as it requires domain-specific expert knowledge. Therefore, this paper proposes an encrypted malicious traffic detection framework based on the active learning method. This framework achieves high recognition rates using a limited number of samples. It employs a hybrid weighted uncertainty sampling strategy that utilizes the independence coefficient method to weight uncertainty measurements across multiple scales. This improves the reliability during the automatic instance selection process. In the experimental section, we achieved a detection accuracy exceeding 93 % using a data subset comprising only 1 % of the original dataset. Furthermore, we validated the robustness of the proposed framework through calibration rate measurements in the experiments.
Keywords: Active Learning | Deep Learning | Encrypted Malicious Traffic Detection | Machine Learning

Title: Hybrid model using both LSTM and attention mechanism along with emotion and genre embeddings for recommendation of songs
Abstract: This research models a better neural network, combining sequential data together with categorical variables like genre and emotion into a model to predict which songs will popularize. The model incorporated an attention mechanism that pays more attention to the most important segments of the input sequence, along with LSTM layers that can record temporal dependencies in song metadata. Since the embedded feature vectors of emotion and genre data could well compactly represent meaningful concepts, we can predict the composite song success score much more accurately by bringing them together. Using an extensive song dataset, we measure its effectiveness and even get documentable gains in precision and applicability over typical models. In fact, the performance metrics of Mean Squared Error, R<sup>2</sup> score, ROC curve, and Precision-Recall curve indicate how reliable the method is. Then, we proceed to success predictions specified for specific genres, revealing the versatility of the model in musical style identification. This fresh combination of LSTM, attention, and embeddings presents a powerful method to predict song popularity and also infer interesting components driving music success.
Keywords: Attention mechanism | Deep learning | Emotion analysis | Feature embeddings | Genre classi- fication | LSTM | Machine learning | Multimodal input | Music industry | Music popularity | Neural networks | Predictive modeling | Sequential data | Song success prediction

Title: Exploring initial refractive lens designs in a sandbox-based learning environment
Abstract: Machine learning, particularly reinforcement learning, enables the exploration of diverse initial designs for refractive lens systems, overcoming traditional limitations i.e. predefined lens sequence. Preliminary results demonstrate that optimising the generated designs leads to diffraction-limited performance.

Title: Multimodal Multilingual Translation System with Text, Voice, and Visual Outputs
Abstract: As the world becomes more globalized, multilingual communication interfaces are a necessity to bridge language differences across various fields of study like education, tourism, and access. This paper introduces a multilingual translation model that can take in text and voice inputs and output the result as translated text, synthesized speech, and a visual representation thereof. The model is built using the Facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M, supporting more than 200 languages, with performance and accessibility at its core. The approach combines auto language detection from the langdetect library, text-to-speech (TTS) conversion from Google TTS, and speech-to-text (STT) functionality from Whisper tiny/base models with low-latency audio processing. For graphical representation, Stable Diffusion XL is used to produce images consistent with the translated text. To make the model efficient, quantization and FP16 precision are used, which greatly accelerates inference speed and allows hardware with low memory resources to deploy the model. A translation memory with the previous five translations and a secure login authorization system enhance usability even further. In this project, we are also developing a user-friendly interface that enables easy interaction with the system, permitting users to enter queries and obtain outputs in multiple modalities with ease. The innovation in the system is the integration of multimodal output (image, audio, text) with an optimized translation framework and user-friendly UI, providing quick, precise, and scalable results for real-world use. It is a leap ahead in accessible, human-oriented translation technology, which can be made feasible for various communication requirements all over the world.
Keywords: Edge AI | FP16 Precision | Google Colab Deployment | GPU Memory Optimization | HuggingFace Cache | Model Efficiency | Multimodal Translation | NLLB-200 | Speech Recognition | Stable Diffusion XL | Whisper ASR

Title: A Decoupled Biophysically-Inspired Architecture for Speech Enhancement
Abstract: The aim of biophysically-inspired speech enhancement models is to replicate the robustness of the human auditory system. However, these models often fall short due to being computationally expensive or monolithic "black box"systems. This paper introduces d-CoSE, a decoupled architecture that separates the biophysical auditory feature enhancement and waveform synthesis tasks, which are implicitly coupled within its monolithic predecessor. To demonstrate the advantages of this architectural change, the proposed system is systematically compared against the original CoSE framework. The decoupled design enables advanced training strategies, such as a hybrid loss function and a final fine-tuning stage, which are not possible in a coupled model, allowing the d-CoSE system to surpass the baseline in perceptual quality (PESQ 2.42 vs 2.33). The results validate the decoupled approach, showing the architectural separation provides inherent benefits of modularity, transparency and potential for superior performance.
Keywords: auditory modelling | biophysically-inspired features | decoupled architecture | deep learning | speech enhancement

Title: Benchmarking Wav2Vec and Traditional Speech Recognition in Speech Transcription
Abstract: This study presents an empirical benchmarking comparison of two distinct speech-to-text approaches under identical conditions: the Speech Recognition module, which utilizes the online Google Web Speech API, and the offline Wav2Vec model developed by Facebook AI. Both approaches facilitate the transformation of spoken language into written language, although they demonstrate unique characteristics in terms of reliance on the internet, speed, and precision. This study utilizes the LJ Speech dataset, which contains short audio segments of a single reader supplemented by their corresponding transcriptions. Both examined models acquire text from the identical dataset and subsequently assess its similarity to the texts within the dataset. Our analysis reveals that wav2vec outperforms the speech recognition model in both accuracy and performance, suggesting the use of wav2vec in speech-to-speech implementations.
Keywords: natural language processing | speech recognition | speech-to-text | wav2vec

Title: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Dysarthria Severity Detection using Balanced Speech Data
Abstract: Automatic assessment of speaker severity levels plays a crucial role in diagnosing and monitoring speech disorders. This paper presents a deep learning based approach for classifying speaker severity levels using acoustic features extracted from speech recordings. This study investigates four deep learning models - Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and a hybrid CNN+BiLSTM model to classify speaker severity into four levels: very low, low, moderate, and high. The models are trained and evaluated on the UA-Speech dataset, comprising audio recordings from speakers with diverse speech impairments. Acoustic features, including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Chroma vectors, and Spectral Contrasts, are extracted and serve as the input to all models. The results demonstrate that the best-performing model, CNN+BiLSTM, achieved the highest accuracy of 99.61%, outperforming the other models. The standalone CNN model's performance was also strong, reaching a test accuracy of 99.34%. Furthermore, analyzed the models' performance using various evaluation metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices, and visualized the learned representations using t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) plots to gain insights into the separability of different severity levels.
Keywords: BiLSTM | CNN | Deep Learning | Dysarthria | LSTM | Severity Detection | Speech Processing | t-SNE

Title: CNN-Based Vision-to-Speech Recovery: Training with Chirp, Testing with Speech
Abstract: Vision-based remote sound recovery is an emerging technology that reconstructs sound by extracting sub-pixel level intensity variation in video frames of vibrating surfaces induced by acoustic waves. State-of-the-art methods rely on computationally intensive motion extraction algorithms, which limits their practicality. In this paper, we propose a novel approach using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to directly extract vibrations from video frames. The conventional machine learning methods that used for audio signal processing is trained using speech or audio data set. Here, the CNN model is trained using chirp signals instead of speech signal, which provide a controlled and complete representation of frequencies across the spectrum. This training strategy ensures robust vibration extraction and enhances the ability of the system to generalize across diverse sound sources. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in sound recovery quality and computational efficiency, setting a new benchmark for vision-based sound recovery. This work highlights the effectiveness of chirp signals for training and provides a flexible framework for real world applications.
Keywords: CNN | motion extraction | sub-pixel level vibrations | Vision-based sound recovery

Title: Unsupervised Indoor Relative Positioning and Group Proximity Prediction Based on CIR Graph Convolutional Network and MDS Embedding
Abstract: Accurate modeling of proximity relationships between individuals and groups in urban spaces is critical for public safety alerts, emergency evacuation planning, commercial flow analysis, and urban planning optimization. Existing indoor localization techniques-including TOA/TDOA/AoA geometry-based methods, visual SLAM, inertial navigation (PDR), and RSSI/UWB fingerprinting-Achieve high accuracy in static environments but rely heavily on large-scale manual labeling, strict clock synchronization, or dense anchor deployment, and struggle to accommodate both trajectory continuity and dynamic environmental changes. To address these limitations, we propose a dual-modal deep learning framework based on Graph Convolutional Networks and Multidimensional Scaling embedding. First, channel feature similarities are computed from CIR sequences sampled continuously by mobile terminals, and an attentionenhanced proximity graph is constructed. Then, the graph adjacency matrix is fed into the MDS algorithm to recover the relative low-dimensional layout of observation points, enabling robust reconstruction of crowd density and flow topology. To mitigate class imbalance and manage positive and negative pair ratios both within and across trajectories, we introduce a spatiotemporal pair generation strategy and employ a weighted binary crossentropy loss during training. Simulation results demonstrate that under sparse sampling and dynamic conditions, our method significantly outperforms traditional thresholding and existing unsupervised baselines in both precision and recall, and approaches the performance of supervised methods under moderate label noise. This framework offers an efficient, annotation-free solution for indoor crowd density estimation and flow analysis.
Keywords: channel impulse response | crowd density estimation | graph convolutional network | multidimensional scaling | proximity relationship prediction | unsupervised deep learning

Title: Automatic Code-switched Academic Tunisian Arabic Speech Recognition
Abstract: Aiming to support researchers by answering their questions, this paper presents the first module of a virtual assistant for Tunisian Arabic (TA): Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). Given the specialized lexicon used, which is characterized by a high rate of Code-Switching (CS), our primary objective is to create a new dataset, Tunacad, tailored to this context. Tunacad comprises 1 2. 5 6 hours of CS spontaneous speech in the academic domain. Additionally, we experiment with our proposed CS corpus on predefined ASR models, Whisper and Wav2vec2-XLR-S. To enhance ASR performance on our corpus, we apply several techniques, such as automatic orthographic correction, normalization, and prompt-based correction. Additionally, we incorporate human evaluation to assess transcription quality beyond surface-level accuracy. Through these experiments and CS errors analysis statistics, we highlight the persistent challenges in processing TA speech.
Keywords: Automatic speech recognition | Code-Switching | In-domain speech resources | Tunisian Arabic | Virtual assistant | Wav2vec2-XLS-R | Whisper

Title: Multilingual Audio-Based Depression Detection using Audio Augmentation and Data Efficient Image Transformer
Abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that speech analysis is increasingly being utilized as an objective biomarker in artificial intelligence (AI) applications designed to complement clinical assessments, improve diagnostic accuracy and treatment response monitoring, enhance healthcare quality, facilitate remote patient monitoring, and reduce the cost and time associated with the assessment of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). This study employs audio augmentation techniques including pitch shifting, time shifting, and noise addition to address the issue of data imbalance between Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and Healthy Control (HC) labels identified in previous research. To mitigate this imbalance, oversampling is applied to the MDD class, which contains fewer samples than the HC class. The augmented data are then used to train two variations of the DeiT model, namely deit-base-patch16-224 and deit-small-patch16-224. Both models achieved an accuracy of approximately 70 percent across the training, validation, and testing phases. Although the deit-small-patch16-224 exhibited slightly lower accuracy compared to the deit-base-patch16-224 model, this performance was attained with only half the training time required by the deit-base-patch16-224. Furthermore, the proposed framework, which incorporates audio augmentation techniques, outperforms prior related studies by achieving a 14.82 percent performance improvement.
Keywords: Audio Augmentation | Audio Classification | DeiT | Depression Detection | Multilingual Audio

Title: Noise-Robust Speaker Verification With Attenuated Speech Restoration and Consistency Training
Abstract: Even though the performance of speaker verification (SV) has been significantly improved with deep learning approaches, it may degrade severely in the presence of background noises. Simple approaches to relieve this issue would be multi-condition training (MCT) and adopting a speech enhancement (SE) module as a pre-processor. However, whether joint-trained with the SV module or not, the SE module may occasionally incur speech attenuation which leads to the partial loss of speaker information. To address this problem, in this paper, we propose a noise-robust SV system with the SE front-end incorporating a speech restoration module using lost information aggregation and consistency training. In the speech restoration module, the lost information obtained from the noisy and enhanced latent representations processed with different sizes of the receptive field is aggregated to produce restored speech features using a loss function penalizing speech attenuation. Moreover, to further improve the robustness to the background noises and unseen data, we adopt consistency training to make the speaker embeddings for the noisy speech similar to those for the clean speech obtained by a pre-trained SV model. Our experimental results demonstrated that the proposed system significantly improved the performance of the speaker verification for the VoxCeleb dataset mixed with environmental noises, and exhibited the generalization capability in the experiment on the CHiME-4 dataset.
Keywords: consistency training | noise robustness | Speaker verification | speech enhancement | speech restoration

Title: mAP-C: A Coverage-Based Metric for Robust Cross-Instrument Sunspot Detection Using YOLOv8
Abstract: Sunspot detection is critical for mitigating space weather impacts, yet evaluating models across datasets with divergent annotation granularities remains challenging. Traditional IoU-based metrics often misrepresent performance when predicted and ground truth bounding boxes differ in precision (e.g., tight predictions vs. loose annotations). We propose Coverage-based Mean Average Precision (mAP-C), which measures the fraction of a predicted box overlapping any part of a ground truth region, enabling fairer cross-instrument evaluation. Using YOLOv8 trained on two datasets (OGAUC: tight annotations; ROB: loose annotations), we demonstrate that models trained on OGAUC achieve mAP-C@0.6 > 0.81 on ROB—indicating robust detection—while traditional IoU metrics fall to <0.12 due to strict geometric alignment requirements. Training on a fusion of both datasets yields balanced performance (mAP-C@0.6: 0.77 on OGAUC, 0.80 on ROB). These results validate mAP-C as a more reliable metric for multi-instrument sunspot detection, supporting consistent evaluation in operational space weather monitoring.
Keywords: Coverage-based mAP | Cross-Instrument Generalization | Solar Image Analysis | Sunspot Detection | YOLOv8

Title: Explainable Hate Speech Detection from Audio using Deep Learning
Abstract: Majority of the current research studies focused on detecting hate speech require improvements. This is because most studies used textual datasets in English language to train traditional classifiers which are opaque and black-box in nature. This research study proposes a novel and explainable hate speech detection framework from audio for Kiswahili and English languages to curb the above limitations. We utilize a hybrid, complex and robust deep learning architectures consisting of the attention-based LSTM (AT-LSTM) classifier and AT-LSTM-GCNN (Graph CNN) ensemble classifier. An audio hate speech dataset for both languages was manually created by collecting videos from YouTube. After converting the videos to audio, various audio features were extracted to train the deep learning classifiers. Experimental results demonstrate that the AT-LSTM-GCNN ensemble classifier achieved exceptional results in both languages compared to the standalone AT-LSTM. Furthermore, we integrate the attention mechanism and the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) explainability techniques to provide a more granular yet detailed explanation of the predictions achieved by the AT-LSTM classifier.
Keywords: Attention mechanism | Audio | Explainable AI (XAI) | GCNN | Hate Speech | Kiswahili | LSTM | MFCC | SHAP

Title: EEG Channel Selection via h-index-Based Centrality Measures of Complex Networks for Music Genre Classification
Abstract: The intrinsic characteristics of music affect the brain by activating specific areas that alter its electrical activity. Understanding this behavior can support relevant applications, but high dimensionality hinders model interpretability, performance, and generalization. Therefore, selecting the most informative channels would reduce complexity, lower computational cost, and potentially improve classification performance. In this paper, we propose an approach to identify the musical genre associated with an acoustic stimulus based on the analysis of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals, aiming to overcome the high dimensionality of the data. To this end, we computed the functional connectivity (graph G) between EEG channels using techniques from various analysis domains, and mined the most representative channels (nodes i). To achieve dimensionality optimization, we propose two centrality measures based on the h-index and degree-strength centrality (DSC) metrics: (1) global ks-index (h<inf>ks</inf>), and (2) local l<inf>ks</inf>-index (l<inf>ks</inf>). High values of h<inf>ks</inf>(G) helped to select the most representative networks, while the computation of l<inf>ks</inf>(i) enabled the identification of the most relevant channels. The selected networks and channels were then mined: the former using global topological measures, and the latter using conventional time-series metrics. In the experiments, we varied the number of the most relevant networks and channels, as well as the DSC type, and used five classifiers with repeated k-fold cross-validation. Our best classification accuracy was 60.1%, achieved with one graph, two channels, and an artificial neural network. The results showed that the new indices helped distinguish subtle structural variations between nodes, select the most relevant channels, and surpass the state of the art in the accuracy–channel ratio.
Keywords: Electroencephalography | Graph theory | Machine Learning | Topological measures

Title: Comparative Study of Complex Network Centrality Measures for EEG Channel Selection in Music Genre Classification
Abstract: Music is a complex auditory stimulus capable of evoking distinct neural responses, measurable through electroencephalographic (EEG) signals. However, its high dimensionality compromises both computational performance and the generalizability of classification models. Therefore, appropriate channel selection becomes essential to improve performance. This study analyzes the use of centrality measures from complex brain connectivity networks for selecting relevant channels in music genre classification. For such a purpose, we constructed Functional Connectivity (FC) networks using correlation, Phase-Locking Value (PLV), and Granger Causality (GC), and evaluated various centrality measures. In addition to conventional centralities, we considered a degree-strength-based metric, which also served as the basis for the development of a new one, named Bonacich Degree-Strength (BDS), with three variants. The feature vector was composed of attributes extracted from the most central channel, combined with topological metrics. Using repeated Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) resampling (10 iterations) and various classifiers, we conducted several experiments with each FC method and each centrality measure. The results showed that with an artificial neural network, GC, and only one channel, the channel selection guided by the betweenness centrality measure improved classification performance in most FC types and classifiers, achieving a maximum accuracy of 60.4%. Furthermore, the BDS variant based on a basal vector and a degree-strength adjacency matrix exhibited discriminative power comparable to the corresponding conventional measure. Additionally, our best model outperformed most state-of-the-art models in terms of the trade-off between accuracy, number of channels, and total number of features. These findings reinforce the role of complex networks as a robust tool in the analysis of neurophysiological signals.
Keywords: Biological Signal Classification | Centrality Measures | Complex Networks | Machine Learning

Title: THE ROLE OF GENERATIVE AI CHATBOTS IN HIGHER EDUCATION: A STUDENT-CENTRIC CONCEPTUAL ANALYSIS OF BENEFITS, ETHICS, AND PRIVACY CONCERNS
Abstract: Generative AI chatbots, such as ChatGPT, are reshaping higher education by offering personalized tutoring, administrative support, and enhanced research capabilities, while simultaneously raising ethical and privacy concerns. This study examines their role from a student-centered perspective, focusing on benefits, risks, and institutional implications. A pilot study was carried out with 300 undergraduate students and 120 faculty members from five European universities. Participants engaged in semi-structured interviews, perception surveys, and controlled academic tasks designed to evaluate chatbot performance. Instruments included standardized student satisfaction questionnaires, expert review rubrics, and quantitative performance metrics (perplexity, response latency, context window, SWE-bench accuracy). Data were analyzed through descriptive statistics, ANOVA tests, and thematic coding of interviews. Results reveal that ChatGPT and Claude achieved the best balance between pedagogical clarity and privacy compliance, while Gemini excelled in technical capacity but showed weaker ethical safeguards. Student satisfaction was strongly associated with transparency in data policies and pedagogical usefulness rather than raw technical performance. These findings highlight the need for universities to adopt generative AI technologies under robust ethical and privacy frameworks. Future research should extend this pilot into longitudinal studies and institutional case analyses.
Keywords: Chatbots | Ethics | Generative AI | Higher education | Privacy | Student perceptions

Title: Perception and Exception Detection of Road Pavement based on an Enhanced DETR model
Abstract: Accurate and efficient detection of road pavement distress is essential for AI-driven maintenance systems in modern infrastructure management. Pavement distress exhibits significant size variability while maintaining similar local characteristics, necessitating detection models that can effectively capture both local and global features. However, existing approaches relying solely on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) or Transformers often result in either global feature loss or inefficient feature extraction processes. To address these limitations, we propose PD-DETR, a novel pavement distress detection model that integrates the advantages of real-time object detection Transformer (RT-DETR) architecture. Our method incorporates an optimized NextViT backbone enhanced with Depthwise Separable Convolutions (DSConv) and a fine-tuned MLP ratio, enabling superior capture of both global and local characteristics of pavement distress while maintaining model efficiency. Furthermore, we introduce an innovative AttentionGate mechanism within the hybrid encoder, which facilitates more effective multi-scale feature fusion through channel weighting after feature concatenation. Extensive experiments on the challenging RDD2022 dataset demonstrate the superior performance of PD-DETR, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 64.27% with a compact parameter size of 30.0M. The proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models, including YOLOv5s (57.85%) and YOLOv9s (60.12%). This work represents a significant advancement in Transformer-based architectures for pavement distress detection, particularly in complex real-world scenarios, offering both improved accuracy and computational efficiency for practical road maintenance applications.
Keywords: Exception Detection | Object detection | Transformer

Title: Machine Learning Models for Student Stress and Academic Performance Prediction: A Systematic Literature Review
Abstract: This study aims to identify and analyze trends, techniques, and findings from recent research on predicting student stress and academic performance using machine learning. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted following the PRISMA protocol, focusing on articles published between 2019 and 2025 from Scopus and other academic databases. Twenty relevant studies were reviewed, covering algorithm types, data preprocessing, feature types, and model performance. Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Neural Networks emerged as the most frequently used algorithms. Predictive features included psychological, behavioral, and physiological data collected from standardized instruments (e.g., DASS-42, PHQ-9), wearable biosensors, and facial expression analysis. Common preprocessing steps included text cleaning, tokenization, normalization, and dimensionality reduction. To handle class imbalance, most studies implemented SMOTE or undersampling techniques. Model optimization was typically conducted using grid search or Bayesian optimization, with some models achieving up to 97% accuracy. Geographically, India, China, and Indonesia were the most active contributors. Research was categorized into stress prediction (10 studies), academic performance prediction (5), and combined models (5). This review provides valuable insights into the use of intelligent systems for improving student well-being and academic success and highlights the need for explainable AI and multimodal data integration in future predictive modeling.
Keywords: Academic performance | Machine learning | PRISMA | Stress prediction | Systematic Literature Review

Title: Cross-Platform Speaker Diarization: Evaluating the Scalability and Flexibility of Maleo
Abstract: Maleo is a cutting-edge, cross-platform speaker diarization system that integrates advancements in speech processing and machine learning. This paper details Maleo's architecture and evaluates its performance. The system's purpose is to provide a flexible and scalable diarization solution deployable across diverse hardware. The methodology involves a pipeline beginning with audio processing (PCM Mono 16-bit 16kHz conversion) to standardize input. The standardized audio is then analyzed using two core models: Whisper for times-tamped speech recognition and Pyannote for neural network-based speaker segmentation. The combined model is exported into the ONNX format to ensure compatibility across CPU, GPU, and WebGPU environments. The system's performance was evaluated on 10 diverse audio files from the VoxConverse dataset. The results show an average diarization error rate (DER) of 9.217% and an average Jaccard error rate (JER) of 24.982%. This study highlights Maleo's ability to overcome diarization challenges by showcasing its efficiency, adaptability, and ability to function optimally in varied computing environments, presenting a practical solution for real-world applications.
Keywords: cross-platform | evaluating | maleo | performance | speaker diarization

Title: Achievable Rates of Full Duplex Cooperative Relay Selection-Based Machine Learning
Abstract: Machine learning (ML) is an advanced artificial intelligence technology that addresses the ever-growing complexity in communication signal processing. In this paper, the concept of ML-based classification model to choose the best relay is investigate in a full duplex (FD) cooperative system. Specifically, a K-nearest neighbors (KNN)-based relay selection is applied to accurately predict and evaluate the achievable rate of the optimal FD relay. The core idea of the multi-class KNN is to identify the optimal relay that yields the highest achievable rate performance by utilizing a large set of offline training data derived from the channel state information (CSI), ensuring that no further training is required during system processing. The results indicate that the KNN-based FD relay selection can achieve an achievable rate comparable to the optimal exhaustive search method with lower computation complexity.
Keywords: Cooperative communication | Full duplex (FD) | k-nearest neighbors (KNN) | machine learning | relay selection | supervised learning

Title: Research on the Time-Frequency Evolution Law of Coal-Rock Electromagnetic Radiation Based on CPO-CNN-BiLSTM and Quadratic Decomposition
Abstract: This article proposes a warning method combining quadratic mode decomposition and optimized deep learning to address the issues of non-stationary, strong noise, and difficult feature extraction of electromagnetic radiation signals from loaded coal and rock in coal mine rockburst warning. The experiment takes the "rock coal rock"three-layer standard sample as the object, and uses the RTR-4600 rock mechanics system and NF-5035 electromagnetic instrument to collect EMR signals at loading rates of 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5mm/min. Firstly, the original signal is decomposed using ICEEMDAN to obtain IMF and residual components. By combining sample entropy and Kmeans, IMF is classified into high, medium, and low frequency categories; 2=Then use VMD quadratic decomposition on highfrequency components to refine frequency characteristics; Finally, a CPO CNN BiLSTM model is constructed for training. The results showed that the R of all three operating conditions in the test set exceeded 95%, with the lowest MAE of 0.33966 and the lowest MAPE of 0.057666; The ablation experiment confirmed that secondary decomposition and CPO optimization improved the model performance by 15% -83% compared to CNN and BiLSTM alone. This method can effectively capture the time-frequency evolution law of EMR signals, providing technical support for ground pressure warning.
Keywords: CNN-BiLSTM | CPO algorithm | Electromagnetic radiation signal | K-means | Secondary decomposition

Title: Convolutional Neural Network-Based Transfer Learning for Indonesian Wind and String Instrument Image Classification
Abstract: Indonesia is a country that has a variety of cultural heritages, including traditional musical instrument that reflect the uniqueness of a region. However, interest in traditional musicals instrument has decreased and is difficult to accept in society due to lack of knowledge and information about it. To overcome this, image classification of traditional musical instruments based on deep learning, especially with its derivative Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), to recognize traditional Indonesian musical instruments in several regions. This study focuses on the classification of wind and string instruments through several CNN models, such as VGG16, VGG19, ResNet50V2, ResNet101V2, ResNet152V2, InceptionV3, Xception, and MobileNetV2. By applying transfer learning, this study develops an image recognition technique for traditional Indonesian musical instruments. The dataset used includes images of musical instruments from various regions in Indonesia, where the recognition process is preprocessed such as resizing, grayscale, cropping, background removal, and data augmentation to improve model performance. Based on the experiment, the VGG16 model showed the best performance, with the highest accuracy and showed effective learning with minimal up to 100% followed by the ResNet50V2, VGG 19 and Inception V3 models which have an average accuracy of 98%. This shows that the approach process to recognize several Indonesian musical instruments has been running well.
Keywords: CNN | Inception V3 | musical Instrument | ResNetV250 | traditional | VGG16

Title: Hybrid Machine Learning Algorithms for Solving the Multi-class Classification Problem of Liver Damage Stages
Abstract: This comprehensive methodology leveraging hybrid machine learning is proposed for the processing of incomplete medical datasets and the prediction of concurrent liver fibrosis (F1-F4) and steatosis (S1-S4). The core of our contribution is a three-stage system combining hybrid imputation (KNN+MICE), PLS-neural network-based factor analysis for identifying significant biomarkers (ALT, AST, bilirubin), and an optimized Voting classifier ensemble (SVM, RF, k-NN) with automatic weight tuning, yielding an F1-score of 0.96. Experimental validation on 104 patient records confirmed a statistically significant performance advantage over isolated methods, with a 15.9% increase in accuracy (p<0.05). The practical relevance of this research is embodied in a high-precision diagnostic instrument with an interactive web interface, designed for seamless clinical deployment and forming a foundation for unified clinical decision support systems in hepatology.
Keywords: classification | data imputation | ensemble learning | hybrid machine learning methods | incomplete medical data | liver fibrosis | medical decision support system | steatosis

Title: Detecting AI-Generated Music: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models
Abstract: The rapid evolution of deepfake music has emerged as a significant challenge for musicians and the music industry. Generative models such as Suno and Juno can produce highly realistic AI-generated music that closely mimics the style and voice of real artists, making it difficult for human listeners to distinguish between synthetic and authentic compositions. This capability raises serious legal and ethical concerns. In response, numerous studies have explored deep learning approaches for deepfake music detection. The primary objective of this study is to examine the limitations of current detection models and evaluate the performance of three deep learning architectures: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Audio Spectrogram Transformers (AST), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks (BiLSTM). A balanced dataset comprising 10,000 AI-generated songs and 10,000 human-composed songs from YouTube was collected. These were segmented into approximately 700,000 five-second mel spectrogram segments for training and evaluation. All three models achieved strong performance, each attaining an F1-score, precision and recall of 1.0, suggesting potential dataset simplicity or overfitting. Among the models, CNN recorded the lowest final test loss (0.07%) and the highest test accuracy (99.7%), outperforming AST and BiLSTM in terms of convergence and generalization. These findings highlight the effectiveness of deep learning in detecting AI-generated music, while also emphasizing the importance of addressing potential data leakage, enhancing dataset complexity, and conducting real-world validations to ensure robust and reliable model deployment.
Keywords: AI-generated music | AST | audio deepfake detection | BiLSTM | CNN | deepfake music | spectrogram

Title: Integration of Conformal Prediction in Automated Forex Trading Systems: Development and Evaluation
Abstract: Automated trading systems are widely used in the forex market to make decisions based on predictions from machine learning models. However, these models often produce point predictions without clear information about their uncertainty. This can lead to risky trades and financial losses. This study investigates the integration of Conformal Prediction (CP) into our forex trading bot to handle this issue. CP may be a statistical strategy that makes expectations interim rather than giving point estimates, which highlights the degree of vulnerability in the figures. This helps reduce ineffective or harmful trading actions by enabling the algorithm to execute trades only when it has high confidence. The inspiration for this study is to enhance the security and reliability of robotized forex trading by employing a strategy that tells the framework designed to measure the level of confidence associated with its predictions. The most significant commitment of this work is the advancement of a forex trading bot that combines CP with price prediction models and trading decision rules. It interfaces specifically to the MetaTrader 5 platform, making real-time trading decisions based on both predicted prices and their associated volatility levels. This study evaluates the framework using empirical data from the XAU/USD (Gold/US Dollar) instrument. The findings indicate that the use of CP contributes to avoiding trades in uncertain market conditions and enhances the accuracy of trading signals. In future work, this study extends framework validation to additional currency pairs, optimizes forecasting accuracy, and analyzes alternative volatility metrics to enhance model performance.
Keywords: Automate Trading System | Conformal Prediction | Forex Trading | MetaTrader 5 | Prediction Uncertainty | XAUUSD

Title: A SHAP-Based Explainable AI Approach for Dropout Prediction Using Ensemble Stacking Models
Abstract: Student dropout is a critical issue in higher education, affecting both academic achievement and institutional performance. Many existing predictive models lack the required accuracy and interpretability for timely interventions. This study proposes a stacking ensemble model integrated with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to increase the transparency of the model and prediction accuracy. The ensemble includes Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests (RF), and LightGBM as base learners, with Logistic Regression (LR) acting as the meta-learner. The dataset was partitioned using stratified sampling to ensure a balanced class distribution between testing and training subsets. The proposed model achieved excellent performance, with an accuracy of 98.34%, precision of 99.32%, recall of 96.61%, F1-score of 97.95%, and AU-ROC of 99.92%. SHAP analysis identified critical predictors like the quantity of approved curricular units, tuition payment status, and scholarship eligibility as highly influential in estimating the risk of dropout. The incorporation of SHAP enabled interpretability on a local and global level, providing valuable perspectives on how the model comes to its conclusions. In conclusion, the proposed framework delivers high predictive performance along with interpretable outputs, making it a useful instrument for early warning systems in higher education.
Keywords: Explainable AI | Model Interpretability | SHAP | Stacking Ensemble | Student Dropout

Title: A Novel Voice-Processing Method Leveraging Polyphonic Audio for Instrument Recognition Using Machine Learning
Abstract: In this research, a novel polyphonic voice recognition system for instrument identification, pitch detection, and chord detection based on machine learning techniques is presented. The system utilizes python and its large set of data analytics libraries to provide efficient and realistic audio recognition. Some of the main techniques involve Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) for feature extraction and classification models like k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) and hidden Markov models (hmm). MFCC s have been used to efficiently extract the spectral features of the audio signals, whereas K-NN classifiers (k=3) and hmm models (8 gaussian states) yield high instrument identification and sequential pattern audio analysis. The system also presents high accuracies of 58% using K-NN and 67% using hmm in classifying 8 instruments namely acoustic guitar, bass drum, cello, clarinet, double bass, flute, hi hat, saxophone, snare drum, violin. A stratified shuffle split strategy and a balanced dataset guarantee fair training and testing. The frontend, coded in html, CSS, and JavaScript, supports dynamic audio visualization and easy user interaction through web audio Api, whereas the backend, implemented with python and flask, processes real-time audio and machine learning operations. Iterative feedback-based updates enhance system flexibility even further, which makes it worthwhile for use in music education, production, transcription, and research applications. In spite of difficulties in overlapping sound separation and intricate polyphonic audio analysis, this research emphasizes the revolutionary potential of intelligent audio processing in developing music technology.
Keywords: audio signal processing | bass drum | cello | clarinet | double bass | flute | hi hat | hmm | K-NN | machine learning | MFCC | polyphonic voice recognition | real-time note identification acoustic guitar | saxophone | snare drum | violin

Title: TAM reveals AI negativity bias in VR music performances
Abstract: Virtual reality concerts are gaining traction, yet very little is known about its experience. The present study employs the Technological Acceptance Model (TAM) to assess user perception and enjoyment of virtual reality (VR) concerts. More specifically, it aims to investigate the so-called AI negativity bias in the context of VR concert adoption. An experiment was conducted in which one group of participants believed the concerts were generated by artificial intelligence (AI), while another group believed the musical performances were live recordings translated into VR environments. Afterwards, participants evaluated their stance towards VR concerts. Results showed that the TAM measures of Perceived Enjoyment, Perceived Ease of Use, and Perceived Usefulness significantly differed across conditions, with higher scores for the live recording condition. Moreover, general attitude towards VR, as well as immersive tendencies, correlated with technological acceptance. Differences between participant groups could not be explained by familiarity or liking of the artists and songs, strengthening the theory of an AI negativity bias. As such, this study adds to the literature on perceptions of AI usage, extending it into the domain of virtual concert experiences.
Keywords: artificial intelligence (AI) | concert experience | music | technological acceptance model (TAM) | virtual reality (VR)

Title: Deep Learning-Based Early Detection of Harmful Algal Blooms in Jakarta Bay Using High Resolution Satellite Imagery
Abstract: Over the past two decades, Jakarta Bay has experienced recurring harmful algal bloom events, with a noticeable increase in their frequency, intensity, and duration in recent years. These blooms have resulted in considerable ecological degradation, including widespread fish mortality, and have negatively affected local fisheries, tourism, and other coastal economic sectors. The intensification of such events is widely attributed to escalating anthropogenic pressures, including urban runoff and industrial effluents from surrounding areas. In response to this growing concern, the present study proposes an early detection framework that integrates high resolution satellite imagery with deep learning techniques. Multispectral data from Sentinel-3A and Sentinel-3B Ocean and Land Colour Instruments, acquired during the early months of 2023, particularly in were utilised. The analysis focused on spectral bands sensitive to chlorophyll and phytoplankton concentrations, specifically Band 6 at 560 nm, Band 8 at 665 nm, Band 11 at 708 nm, Band 12 at 753 nm, Band 17 at 865 nm, and Band 21 at 1020 nm. Ground truth data from Copernicus Marine Environment Monitoring Service (CMEMS) collected during the same period were employed for validation. A convolutional neural network was developed to extract and classify spatial and spectral features associated with harmful algal bloom presence. The input data underwent rigorous pre-processing, including atmospheric correction and spatial alignment. The proposed model demonstrated robust predictive performance, achieving a classification accuracy exceeding 91%, with high precision, recall, and F1 score. These findings underscore the potential of combining artificial intelligence and satellite-based Earth observation to enable timely and accurate monitoring of harmful algal blooms. This approach offers a scalable and operationally viable tool for supporting proactive coastal management in ecologically and economically vulnerable marine environments such as Jakarta Bay.
Keywords: Chlorophyll detection | Convolutional Neural Network | Harmful Algal Bloom | Jakarta Bay

Title: A Comparative Evaluation of Speech Separation Models on Multi-Speaker Child Speech Recordings
Abstract: The task of separating overlapping sounds, known as the cocktail party problem, becomes even more challenging when applied to children's voices, which have higher acoustic variability and spontaneous articulation. While deep learning-based models such as Conv-TasNet, DCCRN, DPRNN, and SepFormer have demonstrated strong performance on adult voice data, their robustness to children's voices remains rarely explored. In this study, we present a comparative evaluation of four speech separation models using a specialised dataset constructed from overlapping recordings of elementary school children speaking. These models were pre-trained using the LibriMix dataset with noise from WHAM! and then fine-tuned on synthesised child voice mixes. Evaluations were conducted using real classroom recordings involving two to five simultaneous speakers. The SI-SNRi metric was used as the primary measure, complemented by qualitative analysis using spectrograms and waveforms. Our results show that SepFormer consistently outperforms the other models, achieving up to 14.1 dB SI-SNRi with two speakers and maintaining 9.4 dB with five speakers, followed by DPRNN (13.2-8.5 dB). Conv-TasNet and DCCRN performed lower, particularly under heavy overlap. Qualitative observations confirm that the transformer-based architecture provides better harmonic reconstruction capabilities and temporal accuracy in the context of child speech. These findings emphasise the importance of long-term modelling for speech separation tasks in educational settings and real-world applications for children.
Keywords: Conv-TasNet | DCCRN | DPRNN | SepFormer | speech separation

Title: The IEEE-IS2 2025 Music Packet Loss Concealment Challenge
Abstract: We present the IEEE-IS<sup>2</sup> 2025 Music Packet Loss Concealment Challenge. Building on the foundations laid in the inaugural edition, this second installment of the challenge introduces improved evaluation metrics and a newly curated test set. In this paper, we outline the challenge rules, detail the construction of the validation and blind test sets, discuss the evaluation methodology used to benchmark participant submissions, and present the results. Continuing to bridge the communities of signal processing, machine learning, and networked music performance, the IEEE-IS<sup>2</sup> 2025 Music Packet Loss Concealment Challenge further advances the state of the art in packet loss concealment for music signals and promotes the development of robust, perceptually-aware algorithms suitable for real-world immersive audio applications.
Keywords: audio packet loss concealment | networked immersive audio | networked music performance

Title: Machine Learning-Driven Angle of Arrival Estimation for a Moving Signal Source
Abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks for robust single-source Angle-of-Arrival (AoA) estimation. The model is trained on a synthetic RF dataset and evaluated on both real-world acoustic signals from the LOCATA Challenge and a live over-the-air (OTA) RF testbed. Experimental results show that the proposed CNN-BiLSTM model achieves real-time AoA tracking on a CPU-only system with inference latency under 20 ms per frame. It closely tracks the theoretical Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) at low SNR and outperforms traditional deep learning baselines across SNRs. Compared to the classical MUSIC algorithm, the proposed approach achieves superior performance at low SNR and significantly lower cumulative RMSE when averaged across all conditions. Importantly, the CNN-BiLSTM model maintains constant inference complexity, making it suitable for deployment in time-sensitive or large-scale antenna array systems.
Keywords: Angle of Arrival (AoA) | CNN-BiLSTM | Interference Localization | Machine Learning | MUSIC Algorithm | Signal Processing | Spectrum Management

Title: Real-Time Tracking of Instrument Motion to Enable Machine Learning Approaches to Laparoscopy Training
Abstract: Laparoscopic approaches to surgery have become widely adopted, due to several advantages over open surgery. However, as an unavoidable consequence of the nature of the laparoscopic setup, skills are more difficult to acquire and sufficient quality feedback on simulator training is costly to procure. We propose a real-time algorithm to track instrument trajectories in 3D within traditional physical laparoscopic simulators. This enables feedback and performance assessment via machine learning techniques. The algorithm has been characterised using a robotically controlled laparoscopic setup as a ground truth and achieves dual instrument tracking up to 60 frames per second at ≈ 5mm accuracy.

Title: CNN-Based Mineral Classification: Epoch Performance Analysis and Web Usability Evaluation
Abstract: This study addresses the challenge analyze system mineral identification, which traditionally relies on manual observation and expert interpretation - methods that are often subjective and time-consuming. While several machine learning models have been applied to image-based mineral classification, limited research has explored how training dynamics, particularly epoch variation, affect model performance. To bridge this gap, we present a web-based mineral classification system using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), enabling users to upload mineral images and receive instant predictions via an accessible interface. The model is evaluated using five different epoch values (10, 25, 50, 75, 100) to analyze its learning behavior over time. The dataset consists of 5,610 labeled images from seven mineral classes, divided into 80% training and 20% validation sets. The model achieves its highest accuracy of 0.74 at epochs 10 and 50, with stable performance across other epochs. Weighted precision and recall reach 0.78 and 0.74, respectively, outperforming macro metrics due to class imbalance. Usability testing with five participants was conducted using Single Ease Question (SEQ), System Usability Scale (SUS), and Net Promoter Score (NPS). SEQ results ranged from 5.4 to 6.0, SUS scored 81.5 (excellent), and NPS recorded 100% promoter responses. These findings demonstrate the system's potential for reliable classification and positive user experience, particularly for educational applications in geoscience.
Keywords: AI | CNN | epoch | machine learning | mineral

Title: Accuracy Enhancement of Arabic Handwritten Signature Verification: A Case Study of Mobilenet-V2
Abstract: The verification of Arabic handwritten signatures is an important research area in the fields of computer vision, machine learning, and deep learning. It is essential to distinguish between genuine and forged signatures due to their significance in preventing fraud and forgery, as well as in various legal contexts. Handwritten signatures vary due to several influencing factors, such as mood, writing surface, and writing instrument. In this research paper, three different datasets were utilized: the first dataset (Dataset1) is an English signature dataset known as CEDAR; the second dataset (Dataset2) is an Arabic signature dataset specifically created for this research; and the third dataset (Dataset3) combines the CEDAR dataset with the Arabic signatures. These datasets were utilized to develop a transfer learning model for signature recognition called MobileNet-V2, which is a deep neural network (DNN) model developed by Google, aimed at achieving a balance between accuracy and performance speed. It is primarily designed for image classification tasks in resource-constrained environments. Standard training and k -fold cross-validation (CV) methods were applied to evaluate the model's performance. The model achieved an accuracy of 97.74% on the CEDAR dataset, 98.49% on the Arabic dataset, and 99.49% on the combined dataset.
Keywords: Deep learning | Handwritten Signatures | Machine learning | MobileNet-V2 Model | Offline Recognition | Transfer learning

Title: Audio Forgery Detection via Combined Recurrent-Convolutional Neural Network Architecture
Abstract: The advancement of deep fake technology has elevated audio fabrication detection to a critical research priority. Existing frameworks exhibit considerable constraints that hinder their integration into operational autonomous platforms. This investigation introduces an innovative methodology for acoustic data examination to identify contextual information manipulation. The proposed framework combines recurrent and convolutional neural networks within a unified computational structure. Assessment conducted on a proprietary corpus focused on operational intelligence regarding Russia's military campaign in Ukraine demonstrates the framework's exceptional performance compared to conventional approaches, suggesting significant potential for deployment within autonomous vehicle systems.
Keywords: acoustic analysis | cybersecurity | deep learning architectures | pattern recognition | speech processing

Title: The Use of AI Chatbots in Enhancing Customer Satisfaction in the E-Commerce Industry
Abstract: AI chatbots are becoming widely used due to the e-commerce industry's explosive growth and the increased demand for quick and effective customer service. These systems aim to improve service efficiency and lower operating costs by providing real-time, automated support through machine learning and natural language processing. This study integrates the DeLone & McLean IS Success Model (D&M) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) to examine how AI chatbot features affect customer satisfaction in the e-commerce industry. Three hundred sixty-five purposefully chosen e-commerce users who had previously interacted with AI chatbots were given a quantitative survey. The research instrument evaluated constructs such as Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, Trust, Information Quality, System Quality, Service Quality, Customer Satisfaction, and Intention. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4.0 to verify the measurement model and investigate the relationships between variables. The study provides a thorough framework for comprehending the factors influencing chatbot adoption and how they affect customer satisfaction in the e-commerce industry.
Keywords: AI Chatbots | Customer Satisfaction | E-commerce | PLS-SEM | UTAUT

Title: Poster - A Preliminary Music Data Collector for Networked Music Performance
Abstract: Networked Music Performance (NMP) is an emerging domain that enables geographically distributed musicians to perform together in real time. Despite its growing potential, the quality of NMP experiences remains highly dependent on network conditions and user perception, making reliable evaluation and optimization challenging. This paper introduces MusiQoED, a novel data-collection application specifically designed for NMP environments. The system integrates real-time network monitoring, user feedback acquisition, and contextual information gathering into a modular architecture, producing structured datasets organized into traces and sessions. These datasets provide a valuable foundation for Quality of Experience (QoE) analysis and machine-learning–based adaptation in NMP scenarios.
Keywords: Application | Data collection | Jamulus | Musician quality of experience (MQoE) | Networked music performance (NMP) | Quality of service (QoS)

Title: A Hybrid Deep-Learning-Statistical Approach for Large-Scale Time-Series Forecasting
Abstract: Accurate and stable forecasting of large-scale time series data is crucial for various applications. This paper presents a hybrid approach that integrates deep learning and statistical modeling to enhance forecasting performance. We employ Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to capture non-linear features and long-term dependencies in the time series data. Subsequently, the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model is utilized to model the residuals from the LSTM predictions, correcting systematic biases. An adaptive weighting strategy is then applied to combine the strengths of both models, dynamically allocating weights based on their respective prediction errors in different data segments. This approach minimizes local prediction biases and enhances overall consistency. To address the challenges posed by large-scale time series data, we incorporate a lightweight LSTM network architecture and a block parallel processing mechanism. Experimental results on power load and industrial equipment energy consumption datasets demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms individual models, achieving a 15.2% reduction in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and an 8.7% reduction in Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) compared to LSTM, and a near 10 percentage point increase in prediction accuracy compared to ARIMA, reaching 92.5%. The results validate the effectiveness of our method in improving prediction accuracy, stability, and generalization ability, offering a reliable solution for time series forecasting in energy management, industrial production, and other fields.
Keywords: adaptive fusion | ARIMA | hybrid model | large-scale data | LSTM | time-series forecasting

Title: Towards Explainable Music Emotion Recognition for Guitar Improvisations
Abstract: Explainability has gained significant attention across various domains, yet it remains relatively underexplored in the field of music, particularly in Music Emotion Recognition. This paper presents XMERApp; a web application designed to provide interpretability for a deep learning model that classifies classical and acoustic guitar into four emotional states. Our system employs a deep learning architecture trained on improvised musical performances to classify emotions, while providing comprehensive explainability through multiple complementary approaches. The application offers users three levels of interpretability: (1) detailed breakdowns of prediction probabilities across different emotion categories, enabling users to understand the confidence and uncertainty in model predictions; (2) temporal visualization of emotion evolution throughout the improvisation, revealing how the model's understanding of emotional content develops over time; and (3) LIME-based explanations that highlight specific spectrogram regions most influential to the model's decisions within focused time windows. Additionally, users can listen to the specific spectrogram regions identified as critical for the emotion classification, gaining insights into which parts of the performance and frequency ranges contributed the most to the model's output. The web-based nature of XMERApp enables deployment across many devices, including smart musical instruments, enhancing the interpretability of intelligent features embedded within them.
Keywords: Emotion Recognition | Explainable Artificial Intelligence | Music Information Retrieval

Title: A MUSIC-Based Adaptive Beamforming Approach for Mobile Jamming Mitigation in 5G Networks
Abstract: Mobile jammers pose a critical threat to 5G networks, particularly in military communications. This paper investigates an anti-jamming framework that enhances a strong adaptive beamforming baseline comprising Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) for Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation and Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) for interference suppression with a lightweight machine learning (ML) model for predictive error correction. Extensive simulations in a realistic highway scenario demonstrate that the integrated system achieves a high DoA estimation accuracy of up to 99.8% and an average Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) improvement of 9.58 dB. Analysis reveals that the MUSIC-MVDR baseline alone accounts for the vast majority of this performance gain (9.46 dB), indicating that the primary benefit of the simple ML model lies in correcting outlier estimates rather than providing a substantial systemic SNR increase. The framework's computational efficiency validates the effectiveness of the core beamforming approach and highlights the critical trade-off between ML model complexity and practical performance gains for securing 5G communications in contested environments.
Keywords: 5G | Adaptive Beamforming | Anti-Jamming | Barrage Jamming | Direction of Arrival | Minimum Variance Distortionless Response | Multiple Signal Classification

Title: Multichannel Speech Enhancement Method Using Dilated Semi-Dense Convolutional Network
Abstract: This paper proposes a dilated semi-dense convolutional network for multichannel speech enhancement using machine learning. The baseline, SpatialNet, employs a Conformer for narrowband processing but uses a simple 3-layer CNN block, limiting local information extraction. To improve performance, we replace the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) block with dilated convolution, dilated dense convolution, and the proposed dilated semi-dense convolution.
Keywords: Convolutional Network | Denoising | Dereverberation | Machine Learning | Speech Enhancement | Speech Separation

Title: AI-Based Primary Schools Teachers' Professional Competency Assessment Tool
Abstract: In the era of Industrial Revolution 5.0 and digital transformation, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is known to play a crucial role in improving the effectiveness and efficiency of education, specifically in public and private elementary schools where teachers greatly influenced students' learning experiences. Therefore, the present research focused on developing an assessment tool to measure teachers' performance driven by AI. Professional competency centered on three dimensions, technical, pedagogical, and ethical. The use of a quantitative method was due to the presence of 150 elementary teachers from public and private schools in Yogyakarta, selected through cluster random sampling. The data acquired through a 10-item Likert scale questionnaire, was validated through expert review and field testing.
