The Multilayer Perceptron model achieved the best result with an accuracy rate of 74.5% when principal component analysis was not used. The study conducted a comparative analysis of machine learning and deep learning algorithms using acoustic features extracted from audio signals. Model performance and generalization capabilities were extensively investigated using methods such as data preprocessing, dimensionality reduction, and hyperparameter optimization. This presented a novel and comprehensive Artificial intelligence-based approach for stress and anxiety detection.
Keywords: anxiety detection | artificial intelligence | hybrid model | Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients | psychotherapy applications | stress detection | voice analysis

Title: TurkAds-Emotion: Analyzing Emotional Impact in Turkish Advertising Audio and Text
Abstract: Modeling the subjective effects of advertising is inherently challenging, particularly for morphologically rich and low-resource languages such as Turkish. To address this gap, we introduce and publicly release TurkAds-Emotion, a novel dataset comprising 2,500 Turkish commercials. Each advertisement in our dataset includes both textual transcripts and audio recordings, annotated with scores (0-10 scale) across five functional dimensions: call-to-action (harekete geçirici), trustworthiness (güven verici), cliché (klişe), entertaining (eǧlenceli), and emotional (duygusal). To establish strong performance benchmarks, we first evaluated unimodal models to understand the predictive power of text and audio separately. For text, we compared sentiment-aware BERT and general-purpose RoBERTa models; for audio, emotion-driven Wav2Vec2 and noise-resistant Whisper models were assessed. Our experiments utilized a rigorous 5-fold cross-validation strategy, providing robust evaluation metrics. The fully fine-tuned RoBERTa model emerged superior for rhetorically complex labels, such as harekete geçirici (0.7146 F1). Conversely, the fine-tuned Wav2Vec2 model significantly outperformed other audio models on non-linguistic labels like eǧlenceli (0.700 F1). Leveraging these complementary strengths, we then developed a multimodal fusion architecture employing cross-modal attention, which integrates text and audio modalities synergistically. This fusion model notably enhanced prediction performance for functional labels such as eǧlenceli and güven verici (0.7478 F1), surpassing our strongest unimodal baselines. However, the multimodal approach did not consistently yield improvements across all labels, specifically underperforming on the klişe and duygusal labels. This study contributes both a valuable new resource and demonstrates the efficacy and nuanced potential of multimodal approaches for comprehensively analyzing complex emotional and persuasive effects in advertising.
Keywords: Advertising | Audio Processing | BERT | Deep Learning | Multimodal Deep Learning | Natural Language Processing | Sentiment Analysis | Turkish Language | Wav2Vec2

Title: Thermal imaging-based fault detection and energy efficiency analysis in a 1.6 MW photovoltaic system in Bağyurdu OIZ, Türkiye
Abstract: The present study assesses the influence of thermal imaging defect detection on the energy efficiency of a 1.6 MW solar power facility in the Bağyurdu Organized Industrial Zone (OIZ) in İzmir, Turkey. Thermal imaging has demonstrated efficacy in detecting serious problems in photovoltaic (PV) panels, including hot spots, inoperative modules, faulty connections, and shadowing, which substantially impact system performance. A comprehensive investigation revealed that around 15% of the photovoltaic panels displayed defects, resulting in a 16% decrease in system performance and an estimated yearly energy loss of 0.35 GWh. The study emphasizes the benefits of thermal imaging compared to conventional fault detection techniques, including its capacity for swift and non-invasive identification of localized overheating, which may lead to fires, and its ability to discern fluctuations in energy output due to shading or malfunctioning modules. The results underscore the necessity for routine thermal evaluations and maintenance to guarantee photovoltaic systems’ operational efficacy and dependability. This study enhances the sparse data on large-scale photovoltaic systems in Türkiye and illustrates the effectiveness of thermal imaging as an economical and accurate diagnostic instrument. Future studies should amalgamate thermal imaging with sophisticated diagnostic techniques, like electroluminescence testing and machine learning, to augment fault detection precision and optimize photovoltaic system efficacy.
Keywords: dc/ac ratio optimization | energy efficiency | fault detection | photovoltaic systems | solar energy | thermal imaging

Title: Toward a Hermeneutic Model for Digital Art and Cross-Disciplinary Performance
Abstract: This paper proposes a hermeneutic model for digital art practice, developed through a comprehensive review and reflection on a cross-disciplinary performance project that integrates digital technology, visual art, and classical music. The project centered on the visualization of René Magritte’s artworks within a live concert setting, employing digital technologies not as spectacle, but as subtle and flexible mediators that could bridge artistic disciplines. While the musical compositions were pre-selected and the visual references predetermined, the central challenge of the project lay in the interpretive task: how to deeply understand both media to enable meaningful technological mediation and construct a coherent and immersive experience for the audience. This study translates the praxeological insights from our collaborative creative process into a hermeneutic model designed to inform and inspire future cross-disciplinary artistic practices. By emphasizing the interpretation of distinct layers – elementary, semiotic, rhetorical, contextual, and speculative – the model enables artists and designers to articulate a shared metaphorical framework across disciplines. This layered approach offers a vocabulary through which technology, music, and visual art can engage in mutual dialogue during the compositional process. In parallel, the hermeneutic framework is positioned as a philosophical response to issues of authenticity in digital art. As digital reproduction and AI-generated media increasingly permeate artistic domains, questions surrounding meaning, authorship, and originality demand new theoretical grounding. Our model argues that, through thoughtful, critical, and creative interpretation, even technologically mediated works – such as reproductions or reinterpretations – can retain or generate philosophical and aesthetic depth. Rather than diminishing authenticity, digital media, when guided by reflective hermeneutic practice, can serve to extend the expressive potential of traditional art forms in ways that remain conceptually grounded and artistically coherent.
Keywords: cross-disciplinary art | digital art | Gesamtkunstwerk | hermeneutics | technological media

Title: Mitigating Temperature Effects in Rogowski Coils' Accuracy Through Physics-Informed Model
Abstract: Low-Power Instrument Transformers (LPITs) are increasingly being deployed across power networks, either to replace or operate alongside traditional inductive instrument transformers. While LPITs offer several advantages, they are also known for their sensitivity to various influencing factors. This research focuses on one specific type of LPIT-the Rogowski coil-and examines the influence of temperature on its performance, considering both the ratio error and phase displacement components. Leveraging standardized testing procedures as defined by IEC standards, the study captures the coil's behavior at three controlled temperature points. These empirical results are then used to train a physics-informed deep learning (DL) model capable of generalizing the coil's accuracy indices across a continuous range of temperatures. The proposed approach enables the estimation and compensation of temperature-induced errors without requiring real-Time thermal calibration or additional sensing hardware, thereby reducing complexity and cost. By embedding physical knowledge into the data-driven model, the methodology ensures that predictions remain robust and interpretable, even outside the originally tested temperature points. The results demonstrate that the integration of domain knowledge with modern DL tools can significantly mitigate one of the most critical error sources in Rogowski coils, enhancing their reliability for grid monitoring, protection, and control applications. This work paves the way for more resilient LPIT deployments in smart grid environments.
Keywords: accuracy | compensation | deep learning | instrument transformer | Rogowski coil | temperature

Title: Integration of a photoplethysmogram sensor to a single-board computer with cBP-Tnet edge AI for continuous blood pressure estimation
Abstract: Deep learning (DL) methods for continuous blood pressure (BP) monitoring utilizing photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals have been confined only to research modeling and not applied. Recently, research on the weighing-scale-based system proved potential DL practical deployment (Edge AI) as existing systems rely on the Pulse Transit Time (PTT) method. The PTT method depends only on manual feature extraction, limiting its performance, and requires inconveniently one additional sensor per method (electrocardiogram, ballistocardiogram, and impedance plethysmography). This study deployed a DL model, cBP-Tnet Edge AI, into a single clip-on BP measuring system mounted on the sensor bar of a body-fat weighing scale, aiming for practical use case. This setup ensures familiar and secure skin contact minimizing motion artifacts. Specifically, we evaluated the performance of integrating a PPG sensor (MAX30102) to single-board computer (Raspberry Pi 5), deployed with cBP-Tnet edge AI for continuous BP estimation. To validate, we recruited 10 volunteer participants and compared cBP-Tnet Edge AI's performance to established PTTbased and traditional cuff oscillometric BP measurement methods. In comparison to PTT-based, cBP-Tnet Edge AI attained Pearson correlations of r=0.788 for systolic blood pressure (SBP) and r = 0. 8 4 1 for diastolic blood pressure (DBP). When compared to traditional cuff-based BP, measurements were preliminarily feasible (SBP: p=0.063; DBP: p=0.791). The mean absolute errors were 9.7 mmHg for SBP and 6.3 mmHg for DBP, with overall accuracies of 91.7 % and 91.2 %, respectively. Thus, cBP-Tnet Edge AI is comparable in performance to both established PTT-based and traditional cuff-based methods, providing potential to include SBP and DBP measurements to commercial body-fat scales.
Keywords: Body-fat Weighing Scale | Deep Learning | Multitask Transformer Network | Pulse Transit Time | Raspberry Pi

Title: Real-Time Fall Detection Based on Deep Learning
Abstract: Falls that occur among elderly adults or individuals with mobility challenges may provide certain health hazards. Due to this, effective fall detection systems need to be designed that are accurate and real-time. The classic methods of fall detection are threshold-based methods and rule-based methods that are less suited to diverse environments and generate too many false alarms. To improve on these disadvantages, this research develops a deep learning-based hybrid model employing CNN and LSTM networks to obtain increased fall detection performance. This model integrates both vision-based data and sensor-based data; it learns on benchmarks. This boosts the detection rate. The experiments prove that the suggested CNN-LSTM model is superior in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The model's accuracy reaches 96.4 % and also has substantially lower false positive and false negative rates than state-of-the-art ones. The comparison with 3D-CNN, Bi-LSTM, and Hybrid DNN models indicated that our system excels in real-time latency and robustness in various situations. The proposed system can be used for geriatric monitoring, smart health care systems, and autonomous emergency response. However, the study has several drawbacks, such as being computationally expensive and requiring big and diverse datasets to generalize properly. Future studies will work on merging several types of sensors, learning capabilities, and edge-based computers so as to shorten real-time detection. The outcomes of this research can help in the design of AI-based medical instruments that are safer for sensitive parts.
Keywords: CNN-LSTM | deep learning | elderly care | Fall detection | healthcare technology | realtime monitoring | sensor-based systems

Title: Enhancing Cryptocurrency Market Forecasting Through Advanced AI-Driven Predictive Analytics
Abstract: Cryptocurrency market forecasting remains a challenging task due to high volatility (3-7 % daily price fluctuations), sentiment-driven market behavior, and decentralized trading environments. This research presents an AI-driven predictive analytics framework utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, sentiment analysis (BERTbased classifiers), and blockchain analytics to improve forecasting accuracy. The proposed LSTM model achieves a precision of 0.96, recall of 0.97, and F1-score of 0.96, significantly outperforming conventional models such as CNN (F1-score: 0.82), ARIMA (F1-score: 0.79), and Transformerbased models (F1-score: 0.90). The Mean Squared Error (MSE 0.001), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE0.03), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE 2%) validate the model's superior predictive capabilities. The Sharpe Ratio (1.5) further confirms its effectiveness in risk-adjusted market forecasting. A wide dataset of 500,000+ daily tweets related to cryptocurrency, Binance historical price, and on-chain transaction data were used to optimize model performance. The findings reveal that short-term (24 -hour) forecasting leads AI-based cryptocurrency predictions (68.6 %), whereas longterm forecasting (120 -day) is underutilized (1.4 %). The hybrid AI architecture combines deep learning, financial sentiment analysis, and blockchain analytics and results in 18 % increased forecasting accuracy compared to current methodologies. This research sets the stage for LSTM-based neural networks as a more effective forecasting instrument, opening doors to future development in real-time AI-based financial prediction.
Keywords: AI-Driven Predictive Analytics | Blockchain Analytics | Cryptocurrency Market Forecasting | Financial Sentiment Analysis | LSTM Neural Networks

Title: Integrated Channel Estimation and Phase Optimization in RIS-Assisted MIMO Network: An End-to-End Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: Downlink channel estimation and achievable rate optimization are critical challenges in current RIS-assisted MIMO systems. The two issues are studied separately: deep learning is used for channel estimation, and convex optimization is employed for rate maximization. But the step-by-step execution will lead to an increase in computational complexity and algorithmic complexity due to the separate handling of each task. To overcome these limitations, we propose an end-to-end integrated deep learning framework that jointly executes channel estimation and optimizes phase configuration to improve system performance. Specifically, a two-stage deep neural network architecture is introduced, which is trained using a multi-task optimization strategy. Moreover, the optimal network structure was explored by adjusting the scale of each stage and the training weight ratio. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining high system performance.
Keywords: channel estimation | deep learning | phase optimization | Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)

Title: MixedG2P-T5: G2P-Free Speech Synthesis for Mixed-Script Texts Using Speech Self-Supervised Learning and Language Model
Abstract: This study presents a novel approach to voice synthesis that can substitute the traditional grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) conversion by using a deep learning-based model that generates discrete tokens directly from speech. Utilizing a pretrained voice SSL model, we train a T5 encoder to produce pseudo-language labels from mixed-script texts (e.g., containing Kanji and Kana). This method eliminates the need for manual phonetic transcription, reducing costs and enhancing scalability, especially for large non-transcribed audio datasets. Our model matches the performance of conventional G2P-based text-tospeech systems and is capable of synthesizing speech that retains natural linguistic and paralinguistic features, such as accents and intonations.

Title: Accuracy Improvement of Automatic Chord Recognition with Source Separation Preprocessing
Abstract: Automatic chord recognition is a fundamental research topic in music information retrieval (MIR) and has been applied to various tasks, including cover song retrieval and music key detection. In recent years, several methods based on deep learning have been proposed, enabling easier and more accurate recognition. In this study, we focused on the bi-directional Transformer for musical chord recognition (BTC), a chord recognition method based on Transformers, and evaluated its performance. The experimental results showed that the chord recognition accuracy for the triads was 75.52%, which is insufficient for realworld music applications. To improve the recognition accuracy, we focus on the differences in volume between instruments within a song. We propose a method that emphasizes sounds from chord-relevant instruments by applying source separation as a preprocessing step. By amplifying the volume of pitched instruments, such as a piano and guitar, we confirmed that the proposed method successfully corrected more than 2,000 misrecognized chord frames and improved the overall recognition accuracy compared with the conventional method.

Title: Dementia Prediction From Speech Signal Using Optimized Prosodic Features
Abstract: Early detection of dementia, a general term for cognitive decline, is vital for enhancing patient care and management. Conventional clinical assessments and cognitive tests require expert clinicians and are time-consuming. Therefore, developing rapid and reliable in-house detection methods is highly desirable. Prior studies have identified speech-based early markers of dementia, motivating the application of machine learning for automated detection. This study investigates the effectiveness of optimized prosodic features, with a focus on pause-related metrics, for dementia classification. Experimental evaluation of 15 selected features shows that pause and formant features are the most discriminative, achieving improved classification performance over the original 45-feature set. These findings suggest that concise, targeted feature sets can enhance automated speech-based dementia detection.

Title: Retinex-Fusion: A Novel Paradigm for Ultra-Low Light Image Enhancement
Abstract: This study presents a robust algorithm for low-light image enhancement, specifically designed to address unevenly illuminated images. The proposed method integrates several key techniques, including denoising, multi-scale Retinex, power-law (gamma) transformation, and illumination estimation and correction through color balancing. Following these stages, a multi-scale pyramidal fusion approach is employed to fuse intermediate images with their respective weight maps derived from contrast, saturation, well-exposedness, dark channel, and entropy information. The performance of the proposed framework is evaluated using the LOw-Light (LOL) dataset, which comprises extremely dark images for testing purposes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses several state-of-the-art techniques, outper-forming many machine learning-based approaches in both no-reference and full-reference image quality metrics. These findings suggest that the method holds significant promise for applications in surveillance, medical imaging, and smartphone-based imaging systems.
Keywords: image fusion | Low-light image enhancement | multi-scale Retinex

Title: An Ensemble Framework for an Effective Feature Extraction and Classification of Chinese Ethnic Music Styles
Abstract: China's vast and ancient cultural landscape encompasses 56 ethnic groups with distinct musical traditions, presenting significant challenges for automated Feature Extraction and classification due to subtle tonal variations, diverse instrumental timbres, and limited digitized archives. With the usage of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) algorithms, classification performance still can be enhanced for an efficient Feature Extraction. However, these models suffers from poor feature extraction methods to understand the complex Chinese music tones. To solve this above problem, this research presents a comprehensive framework for intelligent classification of Chinese ethnic music styles using Mel-Frequency cepstral Co-efficient(MFCC) extraction, and Optimized Kolomorgy Arnold training networks. The suggested model are used for classification of Chinese Music variants The comprehensive training was carried out using the Kaggle Chinese Ethnic Music datasets and validated using enactment boundaries such as accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1-score are measured and evaluated. The extensive evaluation is carried out and performance of the proposed framework demonstrated its superiority over the other existing frameworks, achieving the accuracy rate of 98.56%, precision of 98.3%, recall of 98.2% and F1-scoreof 98.4% in Feature Extraction and classifying the different Chinese music styles.
Keywords: chinese ethnic music styles | mel frequency cepstral co-efficient | optimized kolomorgy arnold networks

Title: Research on Noise Reduction Technology of Digital Conference Power Amplifiers Based on AI Algorithms
Abstract: With the increasing demand for speech clarity and system stability in small public spaces such as conference rooms and training centers, traditional audio amplification systems have shown clear shortcomings in dealing with environmental noise and signal failures. To address these issues, the integration of AI-based noise reduction and automatic signal switching technologies into digital conference power amplifiers has emerged as a key solution for enhancing system performance. By leveraging deep learning techniques to detect and suppress both continuous and transient noises, combined with real-time signal monitoring and switching algorithms, this approach effectively resolves problems such as audio distortion and signal dropout. The technology not only improves the acoustic environment for conferencing but also provides robust support for remote control and system reliability, showing great promise for intelligent upgrades in small-scale conference audio systems.
Keywords: AI noise reduction | deep learning | digital conference | power amplifier | signal switching

Title: EUROPEAN APPROACHES TO DIGITAL JUSTICE IN CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE AND THE BALTIC TATES,WITH PERSPECTIVES FOR UKRAINE
Abstract: Background: This article examines European approaches to digital justice, focusing on how supranational regulatory models—ranging from digital rights principles to operational e-justice instruments—shape national practices across Central and Eastern Europe and the Baltic States. The study conceptualises digital justice as a multidimensional phenomenon that integrates technological tools, institutional design, data governance, and human-centred values. Particular attention is given to how these European developments may inform Ukraine’s justice sector reforms as the country progresses toward alignment with the EU acquis. Methods: The research employs a doctrinal legal methodology combined with comparative analysis. It systematically examines EU regulatory frameworks, CEPEJ instruments, and the Digital Decade monitoring architecture alongside civil procedure legislation and e-justice platforms in eleven EU Member States. Empirical insights are drawn from the EU Justice Scoreboard 2024-2025 and Digital Decade CountryReports. This methodological approach enables the identification of patterns, divergences, and implementation models, forming a basis for assessing Ukraine’s digital justice trajectory.Results and Conclusions: The findings demonstrate that the European Union has developed a coherent, value-oriented architecture of digital justice that unites legally binding standards, interoperable technological solutions, and principles of inclusiveness, transparency, and human oversight—particularly in the context of high-risk AI. The Baltic States provide the most integrated and technologically advanced model, whereas Central and Eastern European jurisdictions exhibit more gradual or fragmented pathways. Systemic integration—characterised by mandatory electronic filing, unified data-exchange infrastructures, and machine-readable judicial data— correlates with stronger performance across EU indicators. Conversely, fragmented or parallel systems constrain accessibility, interoperability, and data-driven justice. Ukraine has achieved notable progress through UJITS, automated case management, and electronic document flow; however, substantial gaps persist in interoperability, machine-readability, user-centred design, and AI governance. Structural fragmentation and the absence of a comprehensive digital justice strategy limit its convergence with EU standards. Drawing on comparative insights, priority directions for Ukraine include full implementation of machine-readable formats (XML/JSON and ECLI), consolidation of fragmented subsystems into a unified ecosystem, mandatory digital procedures for professional participants, and the development of a rights-based AI governance framework aligned with the EU AI Act. Ensuring that digitalisation enhances-rather than restricts —access to justice requires balancing technological innovation with procedural safeguards, institutional resilience, and user inclusion.
Keywords: AI | Baltic States | Central and Eastern Europe | civil procedure | court decision | digital justice | digital principles | digital rights | e-justice | European Union | human-centred digital transformation | protection of rights | Ukraine

Title: Segment Transformer: AI-Generated Music Detection via Music Structural Analysis
Abstract: Audio and music generation systems have been remarkably developed in the music information retrieval (MIR) research field. The advancement of these technologies raises copyright concerns, as ownership and authorship of AI-generated music (AIGM) remain unclear. Also, it can be difficult to determine whether a piece was generated by AI or composed by humans clearly. To address these challenges, we aim to improve the accuracy of AIGM detection by analyzing the structural patterns of music segments. Specifically, to extract musical features from short audio clips, we integrated various pre-trained models, including self-supervised learning (SSL) models or an audio effect encoder, each within our suggested transformerbased framework. Furthermore, for long audio, we developed a segment transformer that divides music into segments and learns inter-segment relationships. We used the FakeMusicCaps and SONICS datasets, achieving high accuracy in both the short-audio and full-audio detection experiments. These findings suggest that integrating segment-level musical features into long-range temporal analysis can effectively enhance both the performance and robustness of AIGM detection systems.

Title: The Application of Computer Software and Hybrid Learning Framework in Chemical and Chemical Engineering Data Processing
Abstract: Chemical Engineering and Chemical analyses poses a significant challenges due to device-specific variations, inconsistent peak identification, specification of spectral noises across the different instruments, which limiting the crossplatform and analytical reliability. Hence application of computer software in chemical and chemical engineering data processing has become vital for enhancing efficiency, accuracy, and predictive capabilities in modern industries. The proposed model incorporates spatial embeddings, temporal decomposition, and an attention-based feature fusion strategy with a region-aware hybrid random forest ensemble. To boost the quality of inputs, dimensionality reduction is achieved by Relief), whereas Wavelet Transform eliminates economic time series noise. The structure of the model is fine-tuned with Bayesian hyperparameter tuning for enhanced generalization. Experiments have been performed on Kaggle's Raman Spectroscopy devices from the different manfacturers. The suggested model proposed obtained an R<sup>2</sup> value of 0.964 and RMSE of 0.031, which is higher than what conventional models such as ARIMA, SVR, and XGBoost would obtain. The feature importance analysis came up with catalyst efficiency, reaction temperature control, and material purity levels as the most influential drivers. The framework provides chemical engineers and process designers with a strong and interpretable forecasting, early warning, and targeted process optimization tool.
Keywords: attention mechanism | chemical analysis | chemical engineering | machine learning | time series prediction

Title: A Comparative Study of Statistical Features and Deep Learning for Orchestral Texture Classification
Abstract: Orchestral texture, which reflects the interaction of instruments in ensemble music, is central to understanding multitrack music; however, symbolic texture classification has not been widely studied. This study addresses the task of assigning textural roles to individual track-bar units (i.e., each bar of each track) in symphonic movements. We evaluate a range of features and models, including random forest, convolutional neural networks, hybrid approaches, and pre-trained models, on the Orchestration and S3 datasets. The results show that duration-related statistical features are the most informative, while identifying melodic roles remains challenging. Overall, our findings suggest the potential of symbolic texture classification, and highlight key challenges in melody extraction for multi-track music and ensuring labeling consistency across datasets.

Title: End-To-End Multi-Channel Speaker Extraction and Binaural Speech Synthesis
Abstract: Speech clarity and spatial audio immersion are the two most critical factors in enhancing remote conferencing experiences. Existing methods are often limited: either due to the lack of spatial information when using only one microphone, or because their performance is highly dependent on the accuracy of direction-of-arrival estimation when using microphone array. To overcome this issue, we introduce an end-to-end deep learning framework that has the capacity of mapping multi-channel noisy and reverberant signals to clean and spatialized binaural speech directly. This framework unifies source extraction, noise suppression, and binaural rendering into one network. In this framework, a novel magnitude-weighted interaural level difference loss function is proposed that aims to improve the accuracy of spatial rendering. Extensive evaluations show that our method outperforms established baselines in terms of both speech quality and spatial fidelity.

Title: Research on the Construction of Graphene Oil-Water Separation Material Characteristic Database and Intelligent Monitoring System
Abstract: First, this paper obtains the physical and chemical property data of graphene oil-water separation materials, such as hydrophilicity, lipophilicity, separation efficiency, etc. through experimental measurement, and standardizes the data. Then, a relational database management system (such as MySQL) is used to design the database structure, establish data tables, define data fields and relationships, and realize data storage, query, update and deletion functions. The IoT-based intelligent monitoring system architecture is designed, including the sensor layer, data transmission layer and data processing layer. Suitable sensors are selected and reasonably arranged on the surface of graphene materials. WSN is adopted to collect and transmit data in real time. The data are processed and analyzed by machine learning algorithms to evaluate the performance of materials. A friendly user interface is developed to display real-time monitoring data and analysis results to provide decision support. In this paper, a performance test platform for graphene oil-water separation materials is built in a laboratory environment, and necessary instruments and equipment are configured. Oil-water separation experiments under different conditions are designed to test the performance indicators of graphene materials such as separation efficiency and stability. Data is obtained through experiments, entered into the database for storage and analysis, and material performance is evaluated. The graphene oil-water separation process was simulated using computer simulation software to predict material properties. The constructed database can effectively store and manage the characteristic data of graphene oil-water separation materials, and the intelligent monitoring system can evaluate the material properties in real time and provide accurate decision support.
Keywords: characteristic database | deep learning | Graphene | intelligent monitoring system | oil-water separation

Title: Enhancing Speech Emotion Recognition through Domain-Aware Data Augmentation and Model Explainability
Abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) constitutes a vital technology for enhancing the naturalness and intelligence of human-computer interactions. However, its performance is often constrained by noise interference and data scarcity in real-world contexts. To address these challenges, this study systematically investigates the construction of high-precision and interpretable SER models utilizing the Toronto Emotional Speech Set (TESS) dataset. A data augmentation strategy, rooted in domain knowledge, is developed, encompassing dynamic signal-to-noise ratio adjustment, emotion label-guided speech rate modification, and pitch transformation, to produce emotionally congruent augmented samples. Subsequently, a comprehensive 134dimensional acoustic feature vector is extracted, incorporating Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Mel spectrogram, spectral contrast, and chroma features. The classification performance of six models - Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory, and Transformer - is rigorously evaluated based on these features. Empirical findings indicate that the Extreme Gradient Boosting model achieves superior performance, with both accuracy and macro F1 score surpassing 99.4%. Further Shapley Additive Explanation identifies the Mel spectral energy distribution as the most critical discriminative feature for the model, followed by the MFCC, aligning with the physiological acoustic mechanisms of speech production. This study not only highlights the exceptional potential of lightweight machine learning models in this domain but also offers an empirical foundation and critical guidance for developing reliable and transparent SER systems through its comprehensive framework of data augmentation, feature engineering, model selection, and decision interpretation.
Keywords: Data augmentation | Deep learning | Machine learning | Shapley additive explanations | Speech emotion recognition

Title: Binary Classification of Capuchin Bird Calls via Spectrogram-Enhanced Frequency-Aware Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Automated recognition of bird vocalizations plays a critical role in ecological research, particularly in challenging environments. In this paper, we propose a frequency-aware Deep Learning (DL) framework for the binary classification of Capuchinbird vocalizations using a tailored Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and smart spectrogram preprocessing. The model was trained and evaluated using a curated subset of the Z by HP Unlocked Challenge 3-Signal Processing dataset, focusing on short audio clips ranging from 2 to 5 seconds. The preprocessing pipeline included duration standardization, zero-padding, and a novel smart cropping method that emphasizes low-frequency energy concentrations relevant to bird calls. Spectrograms were generated using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and normalized to enhance biologically informative regions. The CNN achieved outstanding performance, with 99% accuracy, 99.5% precision, 98% recall, and a 98.5% F1-score. Visualization tools, along with confusion matrix analysis, confirmed the robustness, generalization, and minimal overfitting of our model. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our frequency-aware CNN approach for real-world bioacoustic classification tasks. The ability of the framework to reliably detect rare vocalizations under realistic conditions also makes it a valuable tool for scalable wildlife monitoring.
Keywords: Bioacoustic monitoring | Bird call classification | Capuchinbird detection | Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) | Spectrogram preprocessing

Title: COVID-19 Chest X-Ray Analysis Using an MPI-Based HPC Platform: Improving Machine Learning for Medical Diagnosis
Abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the necessity for rapid diagnostic tools in the medical field, which prompted the creation of multiple disease detection algorithmic models. Even though these models are rather simple to construct, a large amount of data, storage, and resources are needed for their training, which might not be appropriate for use by healthcare facilities or might require more expertise than what most people have, who require these tools the most. This study presents a platform for machine learning (PyTorch) and message passing interface (MPI) that uses high-performance computer technology to help medical diagnosis applications. Retraining a deep learning model that was previously published serves as validation for this platform. (COVID-Net) using fresh data, demonstrating how the model's performance is enhanced by these optimizations that revealed the best possible training. The model's per-class accuracy may increase when the MPI and PyTorch are used instead of parameters selected using conventional approaches, particularly for COVID-19 and pneumonia. Additionally, training time may significantly decrease as resources rise, according to training speed-up studies. The platform that has been built aims to offer healthcare professionals a technological setting for creating innovative, portable artificial intelligence-based diagnostic instruments.
Keywords: COVID-19 | Deep learning | High-performance computing | Image-based diagnostics | Message passing interface (MPI) | PyTorch

Title: An Ensemble-based Approach for Accurate Classification of Astronomical Objects using Deep Learning
Abstract: With the rapid growth of telescopic technologies and space exploration missions, the amount of astronomical data captured as images, videos, and audio from satellites has increased significantly. Manually classifying such large datasets is no longer practical, making automated solutions necessary. Most existing studies focus on limited binary or three-class classification tasks, which leaves a gap in models that can handle a wider range of celestial objectsIn this paper, we propose a novel five-class ensemble deep learning model for the classification of planets, comets, asteroids, black holes, and constellations. Our method combines the advantages of VGG19, which is renowned for its effective layered feature extraction, with ResNet101V2, which is known for its residual connections and capacity to train deep networks effectively. The ensemble achieves a validation accuracy of 95.7% and a training accuracy of 99.7% using a soft voting technique. These outcomes show how well the model performs in classifying multi-class astronomical images and offer a potent instrument for enhancing automated analysis in space exploration.
Keywords: Ensemble Model | Image Classification | ResNet101V2 | Soft Voting | VGG-19

Title: A Comprehensive Review of Infant Cry Audio Signal Analysis and Recognition using Machine Learning Approaches
Abstract: This paper reviews recent research on interpreting and classifying infant cry signals, focusing on data collection, machine learning methods, and signal processing techniques. Since crying is a baby's main form of communication, accurate interpretation is essential to identify needs such as hunger, discomfort, or illness. Challenges include noise, variability, and limited labeled data. The review highlights current approaches and their limitations, aiming to guide the development of reliable cry-based monitoring systems. This paper looks at how newly built Neural Network (NN) architectures are used in newborn cry research. It also looks at how preprocessing, feature extraction (e.g., Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Spectrograms), and classification using algorithms like K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) are currently done. They evaluate recent advancements, highlighting both the achievements and shortcomings of data collection, tagging, and model performance. This project aims to focus future research on creating a reliable, real-time infant monitoring system to assist caretakers and healthcare providers in making urgent choices.
Keywords: Gaussian Mixture Model | Infant Cry Audio Signals | K-Nearest Neighbor | Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients | Neural Network | Spectrograms | Support Vector Machine

Title: Bidirectional ASL Communication Platform using Whisper Ai and Real-Time Gesture-to-Speech and Speech-to-Gesture Conversion
Abstract: Bridging the communication gap between hearing-impaired individuals and non-signers remains a critical challenge in inclusive technology. This paper presents a real-time, bidirectional communication platform that translates between American Sign Language (ASL) gestures and spoken English. The system integrates a gesture-to-speech module using MediaPipe and a Random Forest classifier trained on ASL alphabet data, alongside a speech-to-gesture module powered by OpenAI's Whisper AI for robust speech transcription. Recognized text is matched to corresponding ASL gestures using a predefined dictionary and displayed through an interactive interface developed with Streamlit. The platform achieves 94.7% accuracy in gesture recognition and 96% speech transcription accuracy in quiet environments, with end-to-end latency ranging from 1.3 to 1.8 seconds. Unlike traditional one-way assistive tools, this system supports real-time two-way communication, making it suitable for use in education, healthcare, and public service settings. The results demonstrate the feasibility of combining AI-driven speech and vision models in a practical, scalable solution for accessible communication.
Keywords: Accessibility Technology | ASL | Bidirectional Communication | Deep Learning | Gesture Recognition | Human-Computer Interaction | Real-Time Translation | Speech-to-Gesture | Speech-to-Text | Whisper AI

Title: Augmented Transfer Learning for Synthetic Speech Detection
Abstract: Speech synthesis models pose significant risks, as modern text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC) systems can generate highly realistic synthetic voices that can be exploited for fraud, impersonation, or disinformation. In this paper, we focus on a single, highly effective transfer learning solution: a pretrained EfficientNetV2 backbone model using augmented spectrogram inputs. We employed and evaluated a suite of spectrogram augmentation techniques (adaptive resizing, SpecAugment, and Mixup), regularization methods (dropout, stochastic depth, label smoothing, selective layer freezing), as well as a progressive resizing approach and optimization and learning rate strategies. For the Fake-or-Real (FoR) dataset, a reference benchmark in the field, comprising speech samples both genuine and generated by modern TTS/VC models, our system achieves 97.2% validation accuracy and 91.1% test accuracy, surpassing prior performance by up to 19.6%, reducing the generalization gap, and indicating that focused augmentation on a single pretrained network yields state-of-the-art performance with minimal complexity increase.
Keywords: data augmentation | deep neural networks | EfficientNetV2 | Fake-or-Real dataset | synthetic speech detection | transfer learning

Title: Enhancing Stock Market Forecasting with LLMs, Sentiment Analysis and Technical Indicators
Abstract: Forecasting stock market trends remains a complex and demanding endeavor due to the intricate and dynamic nature of financial markets. This study explores the combination of sentiment analysis with technical indicators to improve the accuracy of stock price predictions. The research incorporates stock market and news data spanning from January 2015 to June 2023, ensuring a well-aligned and comprehensive dataset. Data was sourced using the Google News API and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), followed by rigorous preprocessing, which involved handling missing values and standardizing sentiment scores for accuracy and consistency. To analyze sentiment, tools like VADER, TextBlob, and the Gemini-1.5-Flash API were employed, with sentiment scores aggregated at the stock level. Simultaneously, key technical indicators including the Relative Strength Index (RSI), Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), Bollinger Bands, and Exponential Moving Averages were derived from stock price patterns. These diverse data points were integrated to predict 14-day closing stock prices, leveraging the Gemini1.5-Flash model for forecasting. The model s performance was assessed using various error metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE). The results indicated strong predictive accuracy for stable stocks while pointing out challenges in forecasting highly volatile stocks. Ultimately, the findings suggest that combining sentiment analysis with technical indicators strengthens stock market trend predictions, offering a solid foundation for future advancements in real-time financial analytics.
Keywords: Gemini-1.5-flash | multimodal data | sentiment analysis | Stock market prediction | technical indicators

Title: Deep Learning based Spectrogram Analysis for Music Genre Classification
Abstract: The large prevalence of digital music has created a pressing need for efficient and accurate automatic music genre classification systems. Traditional approaches rely on manual feature extraction, thus limiting scalability and generalizability across diverse genres of music. The project aims to address the problem of ineffective genre classification by using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to learn hierarchical audio features end-to-end from raw audio. The aim is to enhance accuracy, flexibility, and real-time performance of music classification systems. The system converts audio waves into Log-Mel spectrograms, thus extracting temporal and frequency features necessary for genre discrimination. CNNs automatically detect intricate patterns from these visual representations without human intervention with improved performance across a wide range of genres. The novelty is in the combination of spectrogram-based preprocessing with state-of-the-art CNN architectures and performance optimization methods that reduce training time with improved robustness. Experimental outcomes show impressive improvements in accuracy and scalability, thus placing the system on the road towards deployment in today's music platforms.
Keywords: Audio Signal Interpretation | Deep Learning | Digital Music | Genre Recognition | Intelligent Systems | Music Classification | Spectrogram Analysis

Title: Music Genre Classification Using Spectrograms and AlexNet: A Deep Learning Approach with MFCC and Spectral Features
Abstract: Music, an art form that blends vocal and instrumental sounds to create beauty, harmony, and emotional depth, significantly influences both the fields of music and dance as well as everyday life. This study explores the classification of 10 music genres using the GTZAN dataset, using Mel frequency spectral coefficients (MFCC) and spectral features, namely centrion, bandwidth, contrast and roll-off, to construct a 450-dimensional feature vector. Deep learning models, specifically VGG16 and AlexNet, along with traditional machine learning classifiers, to assess classification performance.AlexNet outperforms all of them with the highest accuracy of 97.4% even though more common CNNs are trained. The results imply that deep learning models work well on spectrograms for the purpose of genre classification. Nevertheless enables broader datasets method development facilitates dataset bias and limited research generalisability across styles; prompting larger datasets need development. Not only does this research contribute to the state of the art in audio classification, it also addresses a societal and humanitarian concern that aligns with UN SDG 17 of promoting technological advancements and international partnerships to make music accessible to everyone.
Keywords: Adam Optimizer | AlexNet | Audio Genre Classification | Linear Predictive Coding (LPC) | Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) | Music Analysis | RMSprop Optimizer | Spectrogram Images | VGG16

Title: Hypothesis Testing to Adapt Measurement Noise Covariance for Smartphone GNSS Positioning
Abstract: Smartphone-based Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning has advanced considerably with the introduction of dual-frequency chips and raw measurement APIs. However, raw measurements from smartphone GNSS receivers remain noisy and biased, with limited antenna performance and strong susceptibility to multipath and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) effects. These issues degrade the performance of tightly coupled GNSS/IMU solutions that rely on precise modeling of measurement noise covariance. This paper introduces a hypothesis testing-based adaptive Kalman filter, where standardized innovations are subjected to a t-test to adaptively scale measurement noise covariance based on carrier-to-noise (C/N0)-based weighting. The statistical approach avoids arbitrary thresholds and accounts for dynamic variations in smartphone measurements. The method is evaluated using datasets from the Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge (2021-2023) across multiple devices (Xiaomi Mi8, Pixel 5, Pixel 7 Pro). Results show that the proposed approach reduces horizontal positioning error by 35-45% at the 50th and 95th percentiles compared to weighted least squares, consistently suppressing extreme outliers. The findings highlight the importance of statistically grounded adaptiveness for robust smartphone GNSS positioning and demonstrate progress toward decimeter-level accuracy. Future work will investigate process noise adaptation and machine learning-based covariance modeling.

Title: Assessing Concentration Levels in Interactive Digital Tests Through Portable EEG Technology
Abstract: The increasing prevalence of hybrid education has underscored the need for strategies to evaluate student concentration across both in-person and remote settings. Within Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) contexts, monitoring attention during various learning tasks has been identified as a critical factor influencing academic outcomes. Although prior research has demonstrated the utility of electroencephalography (EEG) for assessing mental states, the application of low-cost, portable EEG devices for concentration monitoring in educational environments remains limited.This study aimed to examine the feasibility of using EEG signals recorded from a Muse 2 Headband to distinguish between tasks requiring different levels of concentration. A total of forty-one participants completed a series of digital tasks while EEG data were collected. The dataset was processed and analyzed using three machine learning algorithms: Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and KNearest Neighbors. The objective was to classify concentration versus non-concentration states based on EEG features and selfreported focus levels. The Random Forest model achieved the highest classification accuracy, outperforming comparable methods and supporting the validity of using the Muse 2 Headband as a real-time, cost-effective tool for concentration assessment in HCI-driven educational scenarios. These findings suggest that portable EEG devices may serve as effective instruments for tracking concentration in hybrid learning environments. Their integration could offer timely feedback to students and educators, contributing to improved academic performance. Future work will explore multimodal approaches by combining EEG data with other physiological signals to enhance the robustness of concentration assessment models.
Keywords: Concentration | Educational Monitoring | EEG | HumanComputer Interaction | Hybrid Education | Machine Learning | Multimodal Learning Analytics | Physiological Data

Title: Sing My Syllabus: Use of Suno Artificial Intelligence as a Gamification Strategy in Engineering Students
Abstract: This study examines the use of Suno, a musicbased AI platform, as a gamification tool in engineering education. Based on cognitive and motivational theories, it investigates whether musical storytelling enhances students' understanding, engagement, and satisfaction. A quasiexperimental study with 50 biotechnology engineering students compared a control group to a group using Suno, where students turned scientific concepts into songs and reviewed them repeatedly. Results showed significant learning gains in the experimental group on topics such as heat transfer and mass transfer, while the control group showed modest improvements. Surveys indicated high engagement, positive perceptions of usability and enjoyment, though self-efficacy scores were slightly lower, highlighting the need for more scaffolding. Instructor support was key to satisfaction, but some students were uncertain about Suno's direct impact on their performance. Overall, findings support the potential of integrating Gen-AI in gamified higher education, fostering creativity, understanding, and emotional engagement with scientific concepts. Future research should focus on scalability, AI literacy, and alignment with assessments to increase academic value, contributing to AI-enhanced pedagogy in STEM education.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Biotechnology | Educational Innovation | Gamification | Higher Education

Title: Gold price forecasting using ML and DL models
Abstract: The economic value of gold leads to its global market position as a commodity because it acts as a trading instrument that protects against market volatility. Precise prediction of gold prices serves essential purposes for investors alongside state managers and commodity market analysts. This study investigates the performance of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models to predict gold prices through Investing.com gold futures data from April 2025 to April 2025. The dataset contains six features, which include date alongside open, high, low, close (price), volume, and percent change. This work evaluated two ML models, Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Random Forest Regressor (RFR), and two DL models, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), for gold price prediction. An 80/20 split into training and testing was used to evaluate the models before using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and \boldsymbol{R}^{2 score as key regression metrics for their assessment. The LSTM model proved to be the most accurate model in this study because it generated an R2 score of 0.99279, which demonstrated its excellent capacity for detecting sophisticated temporal patterns in gold price data. Results demonstrate that deep learning techniques demonstrate better performance than machine learning methods in the task of predicting gold prices. Advanced predictive models receive essential insights through this study as to their effectiveness in commodity market applications.
Keywords: Commodities | Deep Learning | Gold Price | Machine Learning | Prediction

Title: Deep Transfer Learning for Indian Classical Music Genre Classification
Abstract: A transfer learning approach for Indian music genre classification is presented, leveraging a fine-tuned Wav2Vec2 model. The system achieves 88.7% (best performance at epoch 89) accuracy across five genres (Bollypop, Carnatic, Ghazal, Hindustani, Qawwali) on a curated dataset of 115 audio recordings with a final model accuracy of 85%. A comprehensive evaluation is provided, including confusion matrix, per-class accuracy, and classification report and genre-specific challenges and model strengths are discussed. The results highlight the promise of speech-based deep models for culturally rich, underrepresented music traditions.
Keywords: Audio Analysis | Classification Report | Confusion Matrix | Deep Learning | Indian Classical Music | Music Genre Classification | Per-Class Accuracy | Transfer Learning | Wav2Vec2

Title: CRUSE-cMGAN: a Conditional Metric GAN Framework for Real-Time Speech Enhancement Algorithms
Abstract: Denoising speech signals can be a difficult task especially if the background noise is non-stationary. Deep Neural Network (DNN) models provide an excellent performance in speech enhancement, yet they require a substantial computational effort during the inference process, as well as an enormous data basis. We propose a novel approach to optimize real-time supervised learning algorithms semi-supervised by adding a discriminator to the optimization process as well as a non-feature based objective function with phase awareness. We use a Convolutional Recurrent U-net for Speech Enhancement (CRUSE) to build up a conditional generative adversarial training framework. To reduce the computational complexity we train the generator exclusively on the magnitude spectrum and the metric discriminator returns the influence of the disturbed phase. Our findings show that CRUSE-cMGAN outperforms the existing supervised trained CRUSE based on the same architecture. Furthermore the semi-supervised learning manner allows a reduced training database for the optimization process. Experimental results are provided to prove the advantages of the conditional metric GAN framework.
Keywords: deep learning | generative adversarial network | metric discriminator | real-time applications | Speech enhancement

Title: Speech Emotion Recognition: A Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Approach with Wav2Vec2
Abstract: Speech emotion recognition has become a critical area in affective computing and is used in human-computer interaction, mental health monitoring, and adaptive AI. This research utilizes Wav2Vec2 embeddings as feature vectors and constructs a hybrid deep neural network with the inclusion of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks, and residual connections. The model is trained using a Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation strategy with Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) for addressing the class imbalance in the EMODB database. The model applies residual connections to improve feature propagation, convolutional layers for spatial feature extraction, and BiLSTM layers to learn temporal dependencies in speech signals. Training is carried out with an Adam optimizer having learning rate scheduling, and validation of performance on several folds is ensured for robustness. The experimental results reflect the substantial increase in accuracy for emotion classification and confirm the ability of the suggested approach to well-capture fine-grained speech-based emotional states.
Keywords: BiLSTM | CNN | Cross-Validation | Residual Networks | Speech Emotion Recognition | Wav2Vec2

Title: dit dah delta token: Statistical Models of Music and Language Interfering via Morse Code
Abstract: dit dah delta token is a live-coding performance using statistical machine learning models and Morse code as material. In the piece, a large language model and a MIDI model co-generate a text which is also a musical rhythm, combining probabilities over each durational element. In this paper, we explain the method in detail and reflect on the composition as a piece of music.

Title: Interactive Music Co-Creation with an Instrumental Technique-Aware System: A Case Study with Flute and Somax2
Abstract: This paper presents a significant advancement in the co-creative capabilities of Somax2 through the integration of real-time recognition of a broad range of flute Instrumental Playing Techniques (IPTs). Building on the concept of interactive systems for musical co-creation, this implementation enables the recognition and response to diverse IPTs, enhancing the depth of interaction during live performance. The approach was tested in collaboration with a professional flutist performing Cassandra’s Dream Song by Brian Ferneyhough, a piece renowned for its complex intrication of extended playing techniques. Through this experiment, the artificial agents demonstrated the ability to adapt and engage with the performer’s techniques, creating a more dynamic and responsive experience. This functionality relies on a CNN-based flute IPT recognition model, which informs the agents’ real-time responses. The paper examines the broader implications of these innovations for music co-creation, interactive performance, and human-AI collaboration, offering new workflows for creative musical systems and potential applications in composition and live improvisation.

Title: VibroTempo: Feel the Beat with Vibrational Metronomes for Musicians
Abstract: This study investigates VibroTempo, a wearable device designed to enhance musical performance through tactile feedback. The device provides vibrational cues to help musicians maintain a consistent tempo and reduce cognitive load. We conducted a study with 24 participants that evaluated the effectiveness of the vibrational metronome compared to traditional auditory metronomes. Participants’ performances were assessed using key metrics such as Inter-Beat Interval (IBI) Consistency, tempo drift, and tempo variability. While initial findings indicated significant variability with the vibrational metronome due to unfamiliarity, the results showed potential for improved performance with further training. In addition, accented beats were introduced to influence timing and technique, which led to measurable timing adjustments. The device also demonstrated the ability to reduce cognitive load, allowing musicians to focus more on their performance. Reduced cognitive load was moderately correlated with improved memory recall and timing consistency, suggesting performance benefits beyond tempo control. Future research will involve hardware and AI improvements, as well as a counterbalanced experimental design to minimize familiarity effects. This study highlights the effectiveness of the vibrational metronome and identifies areas for further research and refinement.

Title: SCALE-Sim V3: a Modular Cycle-Accurate Systolic Accelerator Simulator for End-To-End System Analysis
Abstract: The rapid advancements in AI, scientific computing, and high-performance computing (HPC) have driven the need for versatile and efficient hardware accelerators. Existing tools like SCALE-Sim v2 provide valuable cycle-accurate simulations for systolic-array-based architectures but fall short in supporting key modern features such as sparsity, multi-core scalability, and comprehensive memory analysis. To address these limitations, we present SCALE-Sim v3 (GitHub Repository), a modular, cycle-accurate simulator that extends the capabilities of its predecessor. SCALE-Sim v3 introduces five significant enhancements: multi-core simulation with spatio-temporal partitioning and hierarchical memory structures, support for sparse matrix multiplications (SpMM) with layer-wise and row-wise sparsity, integration with Ramulator for detailed DRAM analysis, precise data layout modeling to minimize memory stalls, and energy and power estimation via Accelergy. These improvements enable deeper end-to-end system analysis for modern AI accelerators, accommodating a wide variety of systems and workloads and providing detailed full-system insights into latency, bandwidth, and power efficiency. A 128 × 128 array is 6.53 × faster than a 32 × 32 array for ViTbase, using only latency as a metric. However, SCALE-Sim v3 finds that 32 × 32 is 2.86 × more energy-efficient due to better utilization and lower leakage energy. For EdP, 64 × 64 outperforms both 128 × 128 and 32 × 32 for ViT-base. SCALE-Sim v2 shows a 21 % reduction in compute cycles for six ResNet18 layers using weight-stationary (WS) dataflow compared to outputstationary (OS). However, when factoring in DRAM stalls, OS dataflow exhibits 30.1% lower execution cycles compared to WS, highlighting the critical role of detailed DRAM analysis.
Keywords: cycle-accurate | multi-core | sparsity

Title: Virtual Ensemble: Exploring Musicking Through Networked Digital Score
Abstract: This paper explores the concept of the Virtual Ensemble through a networked digital score, redefining musicking in a technologically mediated environment. By leveraging real-time brainwave data and remote collaboration, performers distributed across different locations contribute to a shared musical experience without physical presence. The networked digital score acts as an interactive medium, dynamically shaping sound based on the participants’ neural and instrumental input. The work challenges traditional notions of time in performance, introducing nonlinear temporal structures that reflect both individual agency and collective synchronization. Inspired by the idea of “The bright moon shines over the sea, and from far away we share this moment together,” this study takes Shared Moment: The Bright Moon as a case study to illustrate these concepts. This composition embodies a new paradigm of ensemble performance where connectivity replaces co-location. Through this research, we investigate how digital networks, AI, and brain-computer interaction redefine the perception of musical time, presence, and collaboration in contemporary music-making.

Title: Utmori: Korean Music Composition using Machine Learning and Latent Spaces Navigation
Abstract: This study introduces UTMORI, a project that reinterprets Korean traditional music through machine learning, not as a tool for replication but as a framework for expanding its compositional possibilities. Rather than treating AI as an autonomous creator, UTMORI defines it as a system for generating and manipulating new musical objects—sonic elements that can be structured and reconfigured within a composition. By reexamining the interaction between rhythm, timbre, and form within a generative framework, the project challenges conventional notions of musical structure and introduces alternative methodologies for AI-driven music creation. Instead of fully automating composition, UTMORI emphasizes the composer’s agency in shaping and refining the generative process, allowing for greater control and exploration. This approach not only redefines how machine learning interacts with traditional music but also proposes new ways to conceptualize sound as compositional material. By integrating computational models with musical intuition, UTMORI demonstrates how AI can function as a medium for reimagining musical language, fostering innovative modes of composition and performance while maintaining a deep connection to cultural heritage.

Title: AI Heart Sound Denoising at the Edge
Abstract: Cardiac auscultation with a digital stethoscope is an important method for early diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), especially in resource-constrained settings. However, its utility is often impaired by unwanted noise (e.g., lung sounds, ambient speech) obscuring critical heart signals in the recordings. This paper addresses the challenge of denoising heart sounds in noisy environments and performing this processing on-device for minimal delay and improved data privacy and security. We propose a deep learning-based denoising method using U-Nets based on the Spleeter architecture, which separates heart sound signals from noise in the time-frequency domain. The models are implemented on two edge computing platforms-a Raspberry Pi 4 B and a Qualcomm RB3 Gen 2-demonstrating the feasibility of AI-driven heart sound denoising at the edge. We further optimize the models via quantization to Int8 precision to leverage the RB3 Gen 2's neural processing unit (NPU) for acceleration. Experimental results show that the denoisers achieve significant enhancement in signal quality, with each yielding an average improvement in scale-invariant signal-To-distortion ratio (SI-SDR) exceeding 10 dB. The edge deployment meets real-Time constraints, with the quantized model on the RB3 Gen 2 executing denoising substantially faster (at least 17 times faster than the Raspberry Pi implementation) and at lower power compared to the full-precision model, all without appreciable loss in denoising performance-0.06 dB being the largest drop. These results demonstrate the potential of deploying advanced AI denoising on edge devices for immediate, on-device heart sound denoising.
Keywords: AI accelerators | cardiovascular diseases | deep learning denoiser | digital stethoscope | edge AI | edge computing | heart sound denoising | phonocardiogram | short-Time Fourier transform | signal processing | spectrogram | U-Net architecture

Title: Wavelet-Enhanced CNN-Transformer Hybrid Network for Semantic Segmentation of Multi-Scale Geospatial Objects
Abstract: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing imagery has achieved pixel-level precision in land cover classification through deep learning and computer vision technologies, providing automated and high-accuracy interpretation solutions for environmental monitoring, urban planning, and disaster assessment. However, the complex backgrounds, significant scale and orientation variations, and high intra-class variance inherent in remote sensing images often limit the performance of conventional segmentation methods. To address these challenges, this work proposes a novel Semantic-Enhanced Network (SEnetformer) for high-resolution remote sensing image segmentation, which integrates wavelet-transform convolution and transformer-based attention mechanisms to tackle the critical issues of spectral-spatial ambiguity and multi-scale object variability in geospatial analysis. The proposed architecture introduces three key innovations: a wavelet-transform guided decoder that hierarchically enhances low-level texture representation while suppressing high-frequency noise, a Multiscale Weighted Transformer Block (MWTB) that establishes long-range dependencies through local-global class-aware feature alignment, and a Hierarchical Multiscale Attention (HMA) mechanism for stochastic fusion of cross-scale encoder-decoder features to dynamically adapt to object size variations. Extensive experiments on the LoveDA, ISPRS Vaihingen, and UV-Beijing datasets demonstrate that these components collectively enable precise boundary delineation and robust semantic reasoning in complex scenarios.
Keywords: Hybrid Architecture | Multiscale Fusion | Remote Sensing | Semantic Segmentation

Title: Realizations & Expansions Performance Cases of an Open Work using Artificial Intelligence Generative Tools
Abstract: This research explores the performance of John Cage's Solo for Sliding Trombone using artificial intelligence (AI) generative tools within the Somax2 environment. By integrating AI agents as virtual performers and employing techniques like "coloring the silence" and "expansions," the project investigates the interplay between human interpretation, AI-assisted performance, and Cage's concepts of silence, indeterminacy and unintentionality. The research highlights how AI can recontextualize musical relationships, creating "listening topologies" that transcend traditional linear structures. This approach, termed "playing with music," challenges conventional performance practices while raising crucial questions about copyright, authorship, and the ethical implications of AI in musical creation.

Title: Dynamic Generalized Parametric Control of Digital Music Instruments
Abstract: This paper discusses a general approach to mapping the parameters of a digital music instrument (DM1) with a focus on Virtual Studio Technology (VST) plug-ins. This approach is characterized by its simplicity of implementation, its general applicability to existing DMl signal processing algorithms, and its ability to produce rich, dynamic timbres for musical performance. The focus is on VST plug-ins because there are many thousands of VSTs in existence, but the techniques described here can be applied to DMIs coded in Csound, Max, Pd, SuperCollider, or any other acoustic compiler. High-level control is applied to the DMl through interpolation of its parameters, which can create a constantly changing timbre environment for performers. Despite the simplicity of the method, a surprising amount of sonic variety and musical behaviors can be generated that would be difficult or impossible to produce through more traditional manipulation of DMl parameters. The implications of this approach for machine learning are also discussed.

Title: Music As Natural Language: Deep Learning Driven Rhythmic Creation
Abstract: Symbolic music generation has been widely explored using deep learning techniques, yet capturing rhythmic structures with coherence and variation remains a challenge. In this work, we propose a Transformer-LSTM+FNN hybrid architecture that integrates self-attention for long-range dependencies with recurrence-based sequential modeling. This architecture enhances rhythmic consistency while maintaining computational efficiency. Our approach represents drum sequences as symbolic tokenized events, leveraging a language modeling framework for structured generation. We evaluate its performance through both quantitative and qualitative analysis, demonstrating superior results over the Transformer baseline in rhythmic stability and diversity. Additionally, we explore real-world applications by implementing this approach in robotics and mechatronic arts, enabling real-time adaptive drumming systems. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of hybrid language modeling techniques for expressive and coherent symbolic music generation.

Title: Generalization in Audio Deepfake Detection: Evaluating ASR Encoder-Based Feature Extraction
Abstract: Audio deepfakes are artificially generated audio recordings that are used to create inauthentic imitations of a person's utterances. In the context of the increasing utilisation of artificial intelligence, the recognition of these recordings is becoming increasingly important. Thereby, the generalization of the detectors is a major challenge in audio deepfake detection (ADD). We analysed six feature representations: MFCC, LFCC, Wav2Vec2.0 and three pre-Trained encoders of automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems (Whisper, SpeechT5, Canary) for ADD. For evaluating their generalizability, we trained the models on the ASVspoof 2019 LA train set and tested on the in-The-wild (ITW) test set. Furthermore, we evaluated the training time of the models, analysed the effect of additional (newer) training data and performed a correlation analysis. The ASR encoders were outperformed by using simple MFCC features, achieving an EER of 17.96% on the ITW test set with the lowest training time (7 min. per epoch). The best results were calculated using Wav2Vec 2.0 (+MFCC) with an EER of 17.60%, but using additional training data, and a training time of 135 min. per epoch. Wav2Vec also showed the highest correlations in varying training settings, indicating the best predictability of the model's performance.
Keywords: Audio Deepfake Detection | Automatic Speech Recognition | Generalizability | Learning Rate | MFCC

Title: A Real-Time Gesture-Based Control Framework
Abstract: We introduce a real-time, human-in-the-loop gesture control framework that can dynamically adapt audio and music based on human movement by analyzing live video input. By creating a responsive connection between visual and auditory stimuli, this system enables dancers and performers to not only respond to music but also influence it through their movements. Designed for live performances, interactive installations, and personal use, it offers an immersive experience where users can shape the music in real time. The framework integrates computer vision and machine learning techniques to track and interpret motion, allowing users to manipulate audio elements such as tempo, pitch, effects, and playback sequence. With ongoing training, it achieves user-independent functionality, requiring as few as 50 to 80 samples to label simple gestures. This framework combines gesture training, cue mapping, and audio manipulation to create a dynamic, interactive experience. Gestures are interpreted as input signals, mapped to sound control commands, and used to naturally adjust music elements, showcasing the seamless interplay between human interaction and machine response.

Title: Cloud Conversations Virtually Recreating the Musical Resonances of Costa Rican Outdoor Performance Spaces
Abstract: Room resonance is often seen as an extension of our musical instruments. As musicians, artists and acoustic researchers, built environments such as churches, cathedrals, and large performance halls have functioned as sites for research and digital modelling. However, these spaces can be noninclusive and gated as they are often tied to specific theologies, wealth, and social status. In an effort to broaden this field of study, this paper examines the possibility of inclusive community performance spaces beyond built structures through a case study of the open-air stages in the cloud forest of Costa Rica. In addition, to promote access this project explores options for recreating those spaces virtually. Conventional modelling techniques involving impulse responses and convolution reverb software prove ineffective for outdoor spaces, and instead, the resonance of these spaces is inferred through auditory responses of surrounding birdsong using Somax2 generative AI musical agents. As a means of further exploring this resonance, a composition/instrument entitled Cloud Conversations was created by combining a guitar composition and Somax2 agents, providing a virtual overlap of spaces and resonances. This novel approach to modelling the sonic resonances of outdoor performance spaces expands the field of study to support future community-oriented practices that can be shared both in the field and online.

Title: NEOLIGHTNING: A MODERN REIMAGINATION OF GESTURE-BASED SOUND DESIGN
Abstract: This paper introduces NeoLightning, a modern reinterpretation of the Buchla Lightning. NeoLightning preserves the innovative spirit of Don Buchla's "Buchla Lightning" (introduced in the 1990s) while making its gesture-based interaction accessible to contemporary users.
