Keywords: AI-Driven | AI-Tools | Artificial | Artificial Intelligence (AI) | Barriers | Benefits | Challenges | Commercial Banks | Human Resources Management (HRM) | Intelligence | Jordan | Jordanian Banks

Title: Data-Driven Spatial Dynamics Decoding for Remote Health Monitoring
Abstract: Remote health monitoring instrument, leveraging noncontact sensing device for achieving high convenience, is of great potential to establish long-term continuous big data toward precision medicine. The challenge arises in the quick decaying of the signal when propagating from the human body to the sensor remotely placed. Targeting this challenge, we propose a novel data-driven spatial dynamics decoding framework for mining the remotely captured array signals with health dynamics encoded. More specifically, the innovative framework leverages the two-stage deep learning architecture, which first boosts the array signal fidelity through the deep autoencoder-based distortion suppression and afterward extracts the spatial patterns and yields the inference results through the convolutional learning of the boosted array signals. Furthermore, the framework leverages the data-driven approach to avoid the need of the reference signal that is usually required in the communication system and also to boost the minority class given the imbalanced dataset. To evaluate the system, we have performed experiments on sleep apnea detection, with our customized on-bedframe sensing device and with the proposed deep learning framework. Through comprehensive comparison with the state of the art, we have demonstrated the superior performance of the proposed novel instrument that can achieve a detection accuracy of 94.4%, even with the decayed signal remotely captured. This study will greatly advance remote health monitoring instrument through innovations in off-body array signal perception and mining.
Keywords: Array sensor | deep learning | health monitoring instrument | sleep apnea

Title: Semi-Supervised Sound Event Detection Based on Multi-Scale Attention
Abstract: Sound event detection (SED) involves identifying the onset and offset times as well as the categories of acoustic events within an audio signal. In practical real-world situations, sound events frequently exhibit temporal overlap and substantial duration variability, making SED a crucial research area in audio signal processing. Although deep learning has significantly advanced SED performance, several challenges remain unresolved. The intrinsic diversity of sound events leads to significant disparities in their time-frequency features, making numerous current models ineffective for reliable event detection. To tackle these limitations, this research puts forward a semi-supervised learning framework for SED incorporating multi-scale attention mechanisms. The proposed model enhances discriminative capability across heterogeneous sound events through a dedicated multi-scale attention module. Furthermore, frequency-adaptive dynamic convolution is employed to improve the model's physical congruence with time-frequency patterns within acoustic events. Experimental validation on the DCASE 2021 Task 4 (DESED) dataset demonstrates the superior performance of our approach compared to existing methods.
Keywords: frequency dynamic convolution | multi-scale attention | semi-supervised learning | Sound event detection

Title: Integrating Advanced Machine Learning Techniques for Enhanced Customer Lifetime Value Prediction
Abstract: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) forecasting is implemented by organizations as a core business strategy for customer interaction enhancement, marketing investment optimization, and sustained revenue generation. Accurate CLV predictions enable customer engagement adaptation, improved business decisions, and resource distribution optimization. Traditional CLV systems utilizing national data series with simple command-based models frequently failed in evolving consumer behavior analysis. Predictive performance, system responsiveness, and strategic business value are now significantly boosted by recent Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) advancements. Sophisticated AI-based CLV prediction technology has been implemented in this study, uniting customer segments with multi-dimensional data, predictive analytics, and immediate response mechanisms. Transaction records, behavioral indicators, and demographic factors are incorporated into the model, with precise CLV calculation achieved through ensemble techniques, time-series forecasting, regression, and deep learning models. The study's key focus is formed by behavioral pattern analysis, with purchase frequency, engagement scores, retention probability, and churn risk being assessed. The value-based clustering and micro-segmentation results in focused marketing efforts by narrowing down what kind of customers can be applied. The value is estimated in terms of the financial value based on the projections of revenues, the cost of acquisition and the forecasted profitability. The real-time feedback loops adapt the CLV forecast scale to the changes of behavior. The predictive interaction modeling is quantified by customer touch point analysis, the cross-channel activities as well as the messaging strategies. Ethical AI development precludes biases when it comes to preserving privacy. The policies of the world, the uses of industry to different industries, the quality of data, the complex calculation in use, and explainable AI (XAI) are explored. AI-based CLV prediction instrument generates long-term business development and competitive advantages in the market transformation.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | behavioral pattern analysis | customer lifetime value | explainable artificial intelligence | machine learning | value estimation

Title: Investigation of the Performance of Different EEG Channel Sets for Imagined Word Classification
Abstract: This study evaluates the impact of classification architecture and EEG channel configuration on imagined word recognition using data from the 2020 International BCI Competition. EEG signals corresponding to five imagined phrases were preprocessed and transformed into topographic brain maps, which were classified using a hybrid deep learning model combining 3D-CNN and LSTM layers. Two classification approaches were compared: a direct multi-class model and a nested framework that separates single and compound words. While both approaches showed comparable accuracy, the direct model demonstrated superior efficiency. In parallel, four EEG channel sets were analyzed to assess their influence on classification performance. The best-performing set, selected using subject-specific utility metrics, included electrodes spanning frontal, temporal, central, parietal, and occipital regions. This configuration achieved an average accuracy of 36.8% in multi-class classification and ranged between 31.1% to 39.1 % in the nested classification. These findings emphasize the value of optimized model structure and targeted channel selection in enhancing imagined speech decoding from EEG signals.
Keywords: Channel selection | deep learning | EEG-based BCI | imagined speech | topographic maps

Title: Design and Application of Music Cloud Teaching Platform based on Artificial Intelligence Algorithm
Abstract: The rapid evolution of intelligent education platforms has greatly transformed traditional teaching methodologies, especially in music education. However, existing digital platforms do not offer adaptive, efficient, and context-sensitive learning experiences. To address these limitations, this research develops an adaptive cloud-based music education system powered by a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) algorithm. By modeling the sequential and temporal dependencies of musical elements, the proposed system supports real-time analysis of learner interaction patterns and enhances intelligent content delivery. The dataset used in this study comprises a diverse collection of user interaction data, audio features, and performance evaluations gathered from an online music learning environment. The BiLSTM model was employed to predict user skill levels and generate personalized learning paths. Experimental results demonstrated an accuracy of 98.2%, outperforming other learning models and confirming its effectiveness in addressing individual learner needs. Additionally, Precision (97.8%), Recall (98.1%), Specificity (97.9%), and F1-Score (97.9%) highlight the efficiency of the proposed method. The model is deployed within a cloud-based infrastructure, enabling seamless access to educational content, real-time monitoring of learner performance, and scalable delivery across institutions. This research represents a significant advancement in intelligent music education management, offering a robust and adaptive AI-powered learning environment suitable for large-scale academic deployment.
Keywords: adaptive learning systems | BiLSTM | cloud platform | music education | personalized learning | user interaction analysis

Title: Comparison of MFCC and Spectrogram Analysis in Improving the Accuracy of CNN Models for Song Clip Prediction
Abstract: The performance of automatic music recognition models largely depends on the chosen feature extraction method. This study compares two widely used techniquesMFCC and Spectrograms-to determine which works better with CNNs for classifying short song clips. The audio data was first preprocessed, segmented, and augmented, and then features were extracted using both MFCC and Spectrogram approaches. Separate CNN models were trained on each type of input. While the MFCC-based model performed reasonably well, achieving 84.2 % accuracy on the test set, the model trained with Spectrograms performed significantly better, reaching 96 % test accuracy along with higher precision, recall, and F1 Score. In conclusion, Spectrograms are more effective at capturing the intricate patterns in audio because they are more accurately classify songs.
Keywords: audio classification | CNN | deep learning | feature extraction | MFCC | music recognition | song clip prediction | spectrogram

Title: Enhanced Skin Cancer Classification with VGG-16 Using Dermoscopic Image Analysis
Abstract: One of the most often occurring cancers globally, skin cancer depends on early identification for efficient treatment. Often time-consuming and prone to human variability are traditional diagnostic techniques. This work improves skin cancer classification using dermoscopic image analysis using the VGG-16 deep learning (DL) model. 25,000 dermoscopic images from publicly accessible sources were utilized in a dataset; images were pre-processed using resizing, normalizing, and augmentation to enhance model generalizing. Transfer learning helped to refine the pre-trained VGG-16 model for binary classification benign against malignant. The experiment's results showed the proposed model's exceptional performance, which showed 100% accuracy. The technique also reduced false positives and negatives, providing ideal early detection. These results highlight the possibilities of DL in dermatology as they provide a quick and accurate AI-assisted diagnostic instrument. Real-time clinical validation and multimodal data integration will be the main emphasis of the next projects to improve model performance.
Keywords: Dermatology | Early Detection | Image Augmentation | Skin Cancer Classification | VGG-16

Title: A Novel Prediction of Tourism Economic Development Trends based on Machine Learning
Abstract: Tourism economic forecasting is a critical exercise hindered by cyclical variations, unforeseen factors, and multiple-variable interdependence. Conventional methods like regression and ARIMA are inadequate in capturing non-linear relationships and massive data streams. This study presents a prediction model based on neural networks that identifies intricate correlations among variables such as tourist arrival, seasonal patterns, consumption, and investment in infrastructure. A feedforward neural network with multiple layers is trained on past tourism data, optimized by backpropagation and data normalization. The output of the model predicts future growth rates and revenue of tourism. Accuracy and Precision score are used for performance benchmarking. The neural network provides 97.2% greater accuracy than conventional models. This facilitates informed decision-making by policymakers and tourism boards for resource allocation, advertisement campaigns, and infrastructure development. The solution presents a useful instrument for tourism economics strategic planning.
Keywords: feedforward neural network | performance benchmarking | tourism economic forecasting | tourism economics strategic planning

Title: A Machine Learning based Intelligent Evaluation Technique for Information Literacy of Foreign Language Teachers
Abstract: Assessing information literacy of foreign language teachers is critical in improving teaching effectiveness and academic achievement. Current assessment frameworks, however, depend on qualitative surveys and conventional statistical models that are not flexible and not accurate. Conventional models, including rule-based and linear regression models, cannot identify nonlinear relationships among complex literacy indicators. This paper proposes a Radial Basis Function (RBF)-based deep learning model to overcome such constraints. The proposed model is efficient in handling intricate, multidimensional data with high generalization and increased convergence. Comparative study against conventional backpropagation neural networks and support vector machines shows the excellence of the proposed RBF model in performance with 96.2% accuracy and 95.8% F1-score, being superior to others by 6-10%. The system takes information behaviour measures, digital resource use, and cognitive ability indices as input parameters. The performance mechanism guarantees interpretability and stability and is thus an effective instrument for dynamic and data-driven literacy assessment. This methodology not only improves the accuracy of assessments but also facilitates targeted intervention training for educators.
Keywords: cognitive indicators | deep learning | evaluation model | foreign language teachers | information literacy | RBF neural network

Title: Transformer-EKF for UWB Positioning: A Benchmark Against CNN and BiLSTM Models
Abstract: Ultra-Wideband (UWB) indoor positioning systems suffer significant accuracy degradation in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) conditions, where multipath distortions in the Channel Impulse Response (CIR) lead to biased range estimates. While deep learning (DL) models have shown potential in predicting such errors from CIR data, most prior studies focus on isolated architectures and static pipelines, without evaluating their broader integration into full positioning systems. This work presents a comparative study of three DL models - Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks (BiLSTM), and Transformer - for CIR-based range error prediction, integrated into both Weighted Least Squares (WLS) and Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) frameworks. In WLS, predicted errors are used as adaptive weights to suppress unreliable measurements; in EKF, they dynamically scale the measurement noise covariance for more accurate filtering. We evaluate all models across four realistic indoor environments using a public UWB dataset. Our results show that Transformer-EKF achieves the best performance, reducing mean positioning error to 0.59m in Environment 2 (severe NLoS/multipath) while maintaining real-time inference at 0.059 milliseconds per position. These findings establish a comprehensive benchmark for learning-based UWB positioning and demonstrate the value of fusing data-driven range correction with model-based tracking.
Keywords: BiLSTM | CIR | CNN | EKF | Indoor Positioning | Transformer | UWB | WLS

Title: Segmentation Network with Strip⁃Like Feature Enhancement for Lithium Battery Electrode CT Images
Abstract: Objective The internal structure of lithium batteries, particularly the precise geometry and arrangement of their electrodes, is critical to their performance, safety, and lifespan, which directly affects the viability of new energy vehicles. Computed tomography (CT) provides high-resolution 3D imagery for inspecting these internal structures, enabling the assessment of key quality parameters such as electrode overhang and alignment. However, accurately segmenting individual electrodes in CT images presents significant challenges due to their strip-like geometry, dense packing, the presence of image artifacts, and low contrast inherent in CT scans of lithium battery materials. Existing instance segmentation models, including both established architectures and recent general-purpose or large-scale pre-trained models, often exhibit inefficient feature representation for these specific targets, leading to suboptimal segmentation accuracy, poor edge delineation, and connectivity issues. To address these limitations, we develop a novel deep learning network, Batt-Mask2Former, specifically optimized for the high-precision instance segmentation of these electrodes within CT images, thereby providing a reliable basis for subsequent quantitative quality assessment. Methods We propose Batt-Mask2Former, a novel instance segmentation network designed for the high-precision segmentation of electrodes in lithium battery CT images. Batt-Mask2Former enhances the Mask2Former framework by incorporating two key innovative modules: the cascaded multi-scale strip convolutional encoder (CMSCE) and the alternating path aggregation feature pyramid network (APAFPN), both specifically engineered to address the unique challenges of electrode feature extraction. The CMSCE module employs a cascaded architecture of multi-scale strip convolutional encoders. Each CMSCE, through its core multi-scale channel-weighted stripe convolutional attention mechanism, utilizes parallel branches with varying-kernel-size strip convolutions and channel-wise attention to effectively capture the elongated geometry and multi-scale contextual information of electrodes. The cascaded structure facilitates progressive feature refinement and cross-group information interaction. Following the CMSCE, the APAFPN integrates the processed multi-scale features using a three-stage alternating path strategy. Key components within the APAFPN include a dynamic upsampling module (DySample) for feature upscaling and standard downsampling convolutions. A specialized feature fusion module is also included, which combines standard convolutions with strip convolutions to further enhance the representation of slender electrode structures during the multi-level feature integration process. Results and Discussions The proposed Batt-Mask2Former is validated on a dataset derived from open-source lithium-ion battery CT scans, featuring pouch and 2170 cylindrical cell images (Fig. 8), as well as on a self-scanned blade lithium-ion battery CT dataset (Fig. 12). Performance of the proposed Batt-Mask2Former is benchmarked against several representative state-of-the-art instance segmentation methods, including SparseInst, SCNet, Cascade R-CNN, QueryInst, Mask2Former, Co-DETR, and DI-MaskDINO. On the pouch and 2170 cylindrical cell dataset (Table 2), Batt-Mask2Former demonstrates superior performance, achieving an mAP (mean average precision) of 46.8%, mAP50 [mAP at intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.5] of 87.7%, mAP75 (mAP at IoU of 0.75) of 44.4%, and mAR (mean average recall) of 57.4%. These results represent improvements of 3.5%, 1.4%, 5.8%, and 2.5% in mAP, mAP<inf>50</inf>, mAP<inf>75</inf>, and mAR, respectively, over the Mask2Former baseline. While the inference speed is 14.1 frame/s, the quantitative gains highlight the effectiveness of Batt-Mask2Former for electrode segmentation. Visual comparisons on pouch (Fig. 9) and 2170 cell (Fig. 10) images further corroborate these findings. Ablation studies systematically validate the contributions of the proposed modules. The combined use of the CMSCE and the APAFPN proves optimal, achieving the peak mAP of 46.8% (Table 3). To assess generalization capabilities, Batt-Mask2Former is evaluated on the self-scanned lithium-ion battery CT dataset. On this distinct dataset, our method also achieves state-of-the-art results, with an mAP of 61.3%, an mAP<inf>50</inf> of 99.4%, an mAP<inf>75</inf> of 70.5%, and an mAR of 68.5% (Table 7). This performance confirms Batt-Mask2Former’s strong adaptability to different battery types and imaging conditions. Visual results on the blade lithium battery dataset (Fig. 12) further support this conclusion. Conclusions We address the significant challenge of accurately segmenting slender, high-aspect-ratio electrodes in lithium battery CT images, a critical task for non-destructive quality assessment and safety assurance. Existing instance segmentation models often struggle with inefficient feature representation for such specific geometries and are adversely affected by CT image artifacts. To overcome these limitations, we propose Batt-Mask2Former, a novel deep learning network. Batt-Mask2Former enhances the Mask2Former framework with two core innovations: a CMSCE designed to specifically capture elongated structural features and multi-scale contextual information, and an APAFPN engineered for effective fusion of multi-level features while preserving detail. Comprehensive evaluations on public pouch and 2170 cylindrical cell CT datasets, as well as a self-scanned blade lithium battery dataset, demonstrate that Batt-Mask2Former significantly outperforms several mainstream and state-of-the-art instance segmentation models in key metrics, including mAP, mAP<inf>50</inf>, mAP<inf>75</inf>, and mAR. The proposed method shows clear advantages in accurately delineating electrode edges and maintaining segmentation integrity across diverse battery types. While Batt-Mask2Former achieves superior segmentation accuracy, its introduced network complexity leads to a moderate inference speed. Future research will therefore focus on optimizing the model’s computational efficiency to better balance accuracy and real-time performance for industrial deployment.
Keywords: deep learning | instance segmentation | lithium-ion battery | Mask2Former | strip convolution

Title: Design and Implementation of an AI-Enhanced Teaching of Signals and Systems Course*
Abstract: This paper presents a three-year pedagogical reform study investigating the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and adaptive learning technologies on student outcomes in the Signals and Systems course at Hefei University of Technology (HFUT). Approximately 130 sophomore students majoring in Measurement and Control Technology and Instruments were divided into an experimental group receiving AI-enhanced instruction and a control group receiving traditional teaching. The study implemented and evaluated three key AI-driven interventions: (1) a machine learning-based cognitive blind-spot detection system using YOLO object detection models to automatically identify typical error patterns in circuit design and frequency spectrum analysis tasks, (2) adaptive virtual laboratory exercises with dynamically adjustable difficulty levels and incorporating real case studies based on individual student performance and feedback, and (3) a rigorous assessment framework employing NI Multisim practical exams evaluated with a detailed rubric. Results demonstrated that the AI-assisted cohorts demonstrated substantially improved performance. Notably, the AI-assisted group exhibited an approximately 32% lower error rate in the NI Multisim practical exam compared to the control group, a statistically significant improvement. Additionally, students in the AI-enhanced group showed higher engagement and confidence in tackling complex signal processing problems. The study concludes that integrating YOLO-based error detection and adaptive virtual labs significantly enhances learning outcomes. It contributes a validated pedagogical model for AI-driven personalized feedback in engineering education, supported by empirical evidence and an evaluation rubric, offering a framework for broader adoption in similar courses.
Keywords: adaptive learning | engineering education | object detection | signals and systems | YOLO

Title: AI-Driven Predictive Optimization for Data Center Efficiency: a Web-Based Calculator with Machine Learning Integration
Abstract: New optimization solutions are needed for existing current data center energy utilization levels. The predictive AI optimized technology is used within the designed framework as it operates within the framework of a web based calculator system to analyze data center performance efficiency. A machine learning methodology for power usage prediction and thermal signatures recognition is done by a computer system with various machine learning methods including regression models, deep neural networks and reinforcement learning for finding the optimal workload allocation and unsupervised learning to detect anomalies of the system. This method was demonstrated three performance evaluations across various data center scenarios, saving 25-40% of energy while attaining a PUE 15- 30%, and reducing the operation cost 30-45%. This adaptation takes 2-5 minutes and performs better than 87 to 93% compared with standard strategies. This online interface allows an expert of any background to use sophisticated optimization tools through its conversion of complex metric information into visual presentations. Research showed that the cost benefit of implementing this approach lie in the range of 9 to 14 months per research findings depending on the setup of data center, making this approach economically viable across the board. Through its novel method of obtaining sustainable data centers with computational capacity retention, the research considerably decreases major deficiencies in existing solutions.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Data Center Optimization | Energy Efficiency | Machine Learning | Predictive Analytics | Web-Based Calculator

Title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Music Genre Classification Using Spectrogram Analysis
Abstract: Recognizing and categorizing musical genres is a well-known and long-standing problem in music information retrieval, generally regarded as a black box problem among deep learning pipelines. This paper presents a new interpretable architecture for genre classification by using CNNs, and combining with the novel scripts related to explainability, to extract meaning from spectrograms in order to differentiate genres of music. We used the GTZAN dataset, and implemented three architectures-VGG19, ResNet18 and a custom CNN- and fine-tuned each model using the Mel spectrograms as input. Importantly, we inserted explainability via Grad-CAM, which provided explanatory visualizations, showing transparency into what each model is doing internally to arrive at their final decisions. The most successful performing model was VGG19, which yielded a peak validation accuracy of around 82%, followed by a Custom CNN model at 77.50%, while the ResNet18 had a moderate performance of 75.50%. ResNet18 model exhibited unique interpretability as seen in Grad-CAM. The Grad-CAM visualizations revealed interesting learning behavior: the VGG19 and Custom CNN models were often activated on the negative space in high-frequency regions, which was particularly for blues tracks, which suggests some sort of structural attention beyond the rhythmic contours. The ResNet18 model relied more on some consistent texture patterns. This study provides a general understanding of which frequency regions are most implicated in genre categorization which serves as an important link between the success of deep learning and human understanding of music.
Keywords: CNN | Grad-CAM | ResNet18 | VGGNet19 | XAI

Title: Detecting Process Equipment Failures Using Acoustic Data and Machine Learning
Abstract: Nuclear power plant (NPP) process equipment such as fans, motors, valves, and pumps generate frequent or continuous noise, and deviations from the normal operational sounds made by this equipment can indicate potential issues. These deviations can be identified via automated acoustic anomaly detection, which involves using acoustic sensors (i.e., microphones) alongside detection algorithms to continuously monitor for changes in acoustic signatures. This task is made challenging by the substantial background noise that exists, such as operators opening and closing doors, manipulating valves, and conversing-in addition to typical plant noises. In collaboration with a nuclear power utility partner, this effort assessed the efficacy of acoustic anomaly detection when using a specific acoustic sensor that compresses data into a fixed set of features that are transferable over a standard Internet of Things communication protocol, thereby improving usability but potentially degrading detection performance. Two methods of performing automated acoustic anomaly detection were evaluated: one-class support vector machine (OC-SVM) and isolation forest (iForest). To enable the use of high-quality acoustic data encompassing both normal and anomalous conditions, the study utilized the publicly available Malfunctioning Industrial Machine Investigation and Inspection dataset, which includes real measured acoustic sensor data for a range of equipment types, model numbers, and signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), along with a benchmark set of detection results. Using this dataset, the methods were tested and then compared against the benchmark results. The results indicated that although the specific acoustic sensor did not enable as rich a feature set extraction, the proposed methods with the limited feature set performed just as well. This provides solid justification for both the methods and the use of the proposed acoustic sensor.
Keywords: acoustic data | anomaly detection | machine learning

Title: Experimenting Active and Sequential Learning in a Medieval Music Manuscript
Abstract: Optical Music Recognition (OMR) is a cornerstone of music digitization initiatives in cultural heritage, yet it remains limited by the scarcity of annotated data and the complexity of historical manuscripts. In this paper, we present a preliminary study of Active Learning (AL) and Sequential Learning (SL) tailored for object detection and layout recognition in an old medieval music manuscript. Leveraging YOLOv8, our system selects samples with the highest uncertainty (lowest prediction confidence) for iterative labeling and retraining. Our approach starts with a single annotated image and successfully boosts performance while minimizing manual labeling. Experimental results indicate that comparable accuracy to fully supervised training can be achieved with significantly fewer labeled examples. We test the methodology as a preliminary investigation on a novel dataset offered to the community by the Anonymous project, which studies laude, a poetical-musical genre spread across Italy during the 12th-16th Century. We show that in the manuscript at-hand, uncertainty-based AL is not effective and advocates for more usable methods in data-scarcity scenarios.
Keywords: Active Learning | Cultural Heritage | Object Detection | Optical Music Recognition | YOLOv8

Title: Tiny Noise-Robust Voice Activity Detector for Voice Assistants
Abstract: Voice Activity Detection (VAD) in the presence of background noise remains a challenging problem in speech processing. Accurate VAD is essential in automatic speech recognition, voice-to-text, conversational agents, etc, where noise can severely degrade the performance. A modern application includes the voice assistant, specially mounted on Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) devices such as cell phones, smart glasses, earbuds, etc, in which the voice signal includes background noise. Therefore, VAD modules must remain light-weight due to their practical on-device limitation. The existing models often struggle with low signal-tonoise ratios across diverse acoustic environments. A simple VAD often detects human voice in a clean environment, but struggles to detect the human voice in noisy conditions. We propose a noise-robust VAD that comprises a light-weight VAD, with data pre-processing and post-processing modules to handle the background noise. This approach significantly enhances the VAD accuracy in noisy environments and requires neither a larger model, nor fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves a notable improvement compared to baselines, particularly in environments with high background noise interference. This modified VAD additionally improves clean speech detection.
Keywords: Noise Robustness | Speech Recognition | Voice activity Detection

Title: Predicting alcohol use disorder risk in firefighters using a multimodal deep learning model: a cross-sectional study
Abstract: Introduction: Firefighters constitute a high-risk occupational cohort for alcohol use disorder (AUD) due to chronic trauma exposure, yet traditional screening methodologies relying on self-report instruments remain compromised by systematic underreporting attributable to occupational stigma and career preservation concerns. This cross-sectional investigation developed and validated a multimodal deep learning framework integrating T1-weighted structural magnetic resonance imaging with standardized neuropsychological assessments to enable objective AUD risk stratification without necessitating computationally intensive functional neuroimaging protocols. Methods: Analysis of 689 active-duty firefighters (mean age 43.3±8.8 years; 93% male) from a nationwide occupational cohort incorporated high-resolution three-dimensional T1-weighted structural MRI acquisition alongside comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation utilizing the Grooved Pegboard Test for visual-motor coordination assessment and Trail Making Test for executive function quantification. The novel computational architecture synergistically combined ResNet-50 convolutional neural networks for hierarchical morphological feature extraction, Vision Transformer modules for global neuroanatomical pattern recognition, and multilayer perceptron integration of clinical variables, with model interpretability assessed through Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping and SHapley Additive exPlanations methodologies. Performance evaluation employed stratified three-fold cross-validation with DeLong's test for statistical comparison of receiver operating characteristic curves. Results: The multimodal framework achieved 79.88% classification accuracy with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 79.65%, representing statistically significant performance enhancement relative to clinical-only (62.53%; p<0.001) and neuroimaging-only (61.53%; p<0.001) models, demonstrating a 17.35 percentage-point improvement attributable to synergistic cross-modal integration rather than simple feature concatenation. Interpretability analyses revealed stochastic activation patterns in unimodal neuroimaging models lacking neuroanatomically coherent feature localization, while clinical feature importance hierarchically prioritized biological sex and motor coordination metrics as primary predictive indicators. The framework maintained robust calibration across probability thresholds, supporting operational feasibility for clinical deployment. Discussion: This investigation establishes that structural neuroimaging combined with targeted neuropsychological assessment achieves classification performance comparable to complex multimodal protocols while substantially reducing acquisition time and computational requirements, offering a pragmatic pathway for implementing objective AUD screening in high-risk occupational populations with broader implications for psychiatric risk stratification in trauma-exposed professions.
Keywords: alcohol use disorder | firefighters | multimodal deep learning | neuroimaging biomarkers | occupational psychiatry | structural MRI

Title: Child Speech Assessment Through Large Language Model Speech Synthesis: Preliminary Results
Abstract: Mispronunciation detection and/or diagnosis (MDD) plays an important role in computer-aided language learning (CALL) systems. It remains a research challenge mainly because of the great variability that speech has. A major part of MDD research works base their approaches on models trained for automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, ASR tends to hide nuanced differences in speech for the sake of a higher recognition rate, while these differences could be vital for MDD. In this work, we propose a novel way to derive phoneme-level scores for MDD using large language model based text to speech (TTS) systems. Our proposed method is simple and efficient because speech generation from the synthesizer is not required. The results on the child speech dataset CMU-kids show that our method is comparable in performance to traditional HMM-GMM based systems for the MDD task.
Keywords: automatic speech assessment | child speech | GOP | L2 | MDD | text-to-speech

Title: Multimodal Framework for Deep Fake Detection and Content Moderation Using CNN, ViT, and Audio-Visual Analysis
Abstract: This paper presents a multimodal framework for deepfake detection and content moderation, integrating audio, video, and text analysis to improve detection accuracy and robustness. The framework consists of seven key components: audio extraction, deepfake detection using CNN, audiovisual deepfake detection, metadata and caption extraction, advanced feature extraction using CNN and ViT, text-to-speech transcription in Bengali, and hate speech detection from images. Audio and video features extracted using CNN and ViT are combined to compute a probabilistic score for deepfake detection, while OCR and NLP models analyze transcribed text for hate speech. The system is designed for real-time multimedia analysis, making it suitable for social media content moderation, forensic investigations, and misinformation detection. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets such as Celeb-Df, and DFDC demonstrate high detection accuracy, outperforming traditional single-modal approaches. The framework is optimized for scalability and efficiency, enabling large-scale multimedia analysis with minimal latency. By integrating advanced video processing, speech analysis, and text recognition, this work contributes to multimodal AI research, offering a comprehensive and scalable solution for detecting manipulated media and ensuring digital content integrity in real-world applications.
Keywords: Bengali speech-to-text | CNN | Content moderation | Deep fake detection | Multimodal analysis | OCR | Vision Transformers

Title: Air Pollution Forecasting with Machine Learning: A Step Toward Proactive Environmental Management
Abstract: Urban air pollution is still a critical environmental and public health issue, fueled by increasing levels of fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5), Ozone (O<inf>3</inf>), and Sulfur Dioxide (SO<inf>2</inf>). Current monitoring systems, though accurate in real-time measurement, are inadequate in predicting pollutant levels, which prevents proactive decision-making. This project suggests a data-driven solution based on Multitask Learning (MTL) to forecast hourly concentrations of major air pollutants up to 24 hours ahead. Building on past meteorological observations and pollution records, we compare the performance of a variety of algorithms - Random Forest, Extra Trees, Lasso Regression, and Support Vector Machines - in the MTL setting. To provide temporal consistency in the predictions, we add regularization methods like temporal smoothness penalties. Model training and model performance measurement are done on an open-source urban air quality dataset, and the metrics used are Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and R-squared (R<sup>2</sup>). The MTL architecture facilitates the concurrent forecasting of different pollutants and, thus, reduces computational time and enhances inter-pollutant correlation capture. This study offers a replicable method for short-term air quality forecasting, with relevance to urban planning, emergency management, and environmental policy. The findings show the potential for the application of machine learning in air quality management as a scalable instrument for cities that seek to reduce pollution-related health hazards.
Keywords: Air Pollution | Air Quality Index | Machine Learning | Meteorological Data | Multitask Learning | Particulate Matter

Title: A Lightweight Multi-Feature Fusion Attention Network for Single-Channel Speech Separation
Abstract: Speech separation is a fundamental task in speech signal processing and plays a critical role in applications such as automatic speech recognition. Although deep learning has led to significant progress in single-channel speech separation, challenges persist in feature extraction, phase reconstruction, and computational efficiency. In this paper, we propose a lightweight multi-feature fusion attention convolutional network (LMFA-Net) for end-to-end single-channel speech separation. The encoder integrates a deterministic Multi-Phase Gammatone Filterbank (MP-GTF) with a Convolutional Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) module to enhance time-frequency feature representation. The separation module employs Ghost Module-based lightweight convolutional blocks to reduce model size and complexity while maintaining strong separation performance. In the decoder, outputs from transposed convolution and the pseudo-inverse MPGTF are fused via an attention-based weighting mechanism to reconstruct waveforms. Experimental results on WSJ0-2mix, Libri2Mix, and a self-built Chinese dataset, NJUST603-2Mix, show that LMFA-Net achieves superior SDRi and SI-SNRi scores with fewer parameters, demonstrating its effectiveness and strong generalization capability.
Keywords: Attention Mechanism | Deep Learning | Lightweight Network | Multi-Feature Fusion | Speech Separation

Title: TRANSFORMER-BASED SPEECH EMOTION RECOGNITION USING SYNTHETIC BONE-CONDUCTED SPEECH
Abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is a rapidly growing field, with recent advancements utilizing deep learning techniques to improve accuracy and robustness. In this study, we explore the prospect of transformer-based learning methods for SER using synthetic bone-conducted (BC) speech. This research builds on the unique properties of BC speech, which emphasize low-frequency components crucial for emotional expression by transforming air-conducted (AC) speech into BC speech using an infinite impulse response (IIR) filter. Due to their built-in self-attention mechanism, transformers are highly effective in picking up on elaborate spectral and temporal patterns found in speech signals. We augment the synthetic BC speech dataset and preprocess the data to maintain essential low-frequency components, which are the key to emotional expression in speech. Our proposed transformer-based model incorporates positional encodings to handle temporal information in speech data and multi-head self-attention layers to extract global dependencies across the input sequence. The model aims to address the challenges of quiet emotional state recognition and improve accuracy for subtle emotions like fear and surprise. Experimental results show that the transformer model significantly outperforms conventional deep learning approaches, achieving an accuracy of 99% for synthetic BC speech, compared to 72.50% achieved by convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and 69.83% for AC speech using existing models. The superior performance is attributed to the transformer's ability to capture intricate temporal and spectral patterns that are critical for emotional expression. This research highlights the transformative impact of applying attention-based models to SER tasks with synthetic BC speech. Future work will include comprehensive evaluations of the transformer architecture against other state-of-the-art methods, exploring its robustness across diverse datasets and real-world situations. These initiatives will facilitate more efficient applications in assistive technologies, human-computer interaction, and emotion-driven AI systems.
Keywords: bone-conducted speech | transformer learning

Title: A Precision BMI Monitoring System with Real-Time Alerts using SHAP and XGBoost based Interpretability
Abstract: The aim is to develop an Enhanced Sensitivity BMI Calculator that uses machine learning, specifically XGBoost, for accurate BMI predictions and SHAP for model transparency. The system provides real-time BMI analysis and personalized health notifications to improve individual health management. Group 1 estimates body fat percentage using Random Forest Regressor, while Group 2 develops a BMI prediction model with XGBoost, using SHAP for feature selection and interpretability, and delivers real-time personalized health feedback through real-time notifications. The model achieved high accuracy with MAE = 1.22, RMSE = 1.56, and R2 = 0.92, indicating strong performance in predicting BMI. SHAP analysis identified weight, age, and physical activity as the most influential factors in predictions. User feedback on the mobile app was highly positive, with ratings of 4.7/5 for accuracy and 4.8/5 for overall experience. In this work, it combines high-accuracy BMI predictions using XGBoost with transparent insights through SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis, offering real-time, personalized health notifications.
Keywords: BMI Calculator | BMI prediction | component | feature | health management | machine learning | mobile app | real-time notifications | SHapley Additive exPlanations | user feedback | XGBoost

Title: Enhanced Smart Hearing Aid Simulation with Scene Classification and Frequency Compression
Abstract: Contemporary hearing aids do not have the capability to learn intelligently from dynamic real-world scenarios and do not provide personalized hearing improvement for people with varied hearing loss types. This paper introduces an improved, real-time smart hearing aid system that incorporates acoustic scene classification, frequency compression, and multi-user personalization on the BioAid framework. Complementing the shortcomings of existing literature, this research suggests an improved and more scalable method for assistive hearing.The system starts with live audio recording with low-latency input devices and extracts Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and spectral features to identify the acoustic scene based on machine learning algorithms like Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Random Forest classifiers. Upon identification of a scene, the system picks a personalized hearing aid preset from a broadened list of BioAid options, dynamically correlated with each individual's hearing profile and preferences.To confront the universal issue of high-frequency hearing loss, an FFT-based frequency compression module is proposed. This module relocates critical high-frequency elements into lower, more accessible frequency bands and increases speech intelligibility without acoustic context distortion. The inference pipeline of the model is engineered for real-time performance and efficient deployment in TensorFlow Lite or TinyML and is thus ideal for deployment on edge devices like Raspberry Pi or bespoke embedded hearing hardware.The system is tested with public datasets like DCASE2017 for environmental sound and LJ Speech for clean voice, and a custom multi-user dataset to personalize preset mapping. Experimental results show better accuracy in scene classification, real-time adaptability, and successful frequency compression. This work advances intelligent assistive technology by providing a usable and efficient solution for real-world hearing aid deployment
Keywords: Acoustic Scene Classification | Assistive Technology | BioAid | Frequency Compression | Machine Learning | MFCC | Personalized Preset Mapping | Real-Time Audio Processing | Smart Hearing Aid | TinyML

Title: A Secure Web-based Application for Predicting Parkinson Disease using Speech Signal Features and Machine Learning Techniques
Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder affecting motor control, including the muscle responsible for speech. Alterations in voice, such as reduced vocal stability and amplitude variation often appear in early and mid-stages of PD. Speech feature extraction provides a non-invasive, cost-effective, and scalable approach for remote screening of PD using minimal equipment. This study presents a secure, web-based application that predicts whether an individual has PD using speech recordings. Vocal biomarkers are extracted and used to train multiple binary classifiers, including Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors, CatBoost, XGBoost, AdaBoost and Multiplayer Perception. Model outputs are combined using an ensemble based Stacking approach, achieving an overall accuracy of 95%. The application allows users to upload speech samples and instantly receive a PD likelihood prediction, making remote and accessible screening possible. This demonstrates the potential of speech-based machine learning systems for reliable Parkinson's detection.
Keywords: Machine Learning | Neurodegenerative Disorders | Parkinson's Disease | Speech Signal Processing | Web-based Application

Title: Human Dignity and the Metaphysical Crisis in Postmodern Ethics
Abstract: The concept of human dignity is frequently invoked in contemporary ethical, legal, and political discourse, yet often remains ungrounded in any coherent ontological framework. This article argues that the contemporary fragility and fragmentation of the idea of dignity stem from a deeper metaphysical crisis: the abandonment of a realist conception of human nature and the rise of nominalism. By contrasting nominalism with Aristotelian-Thomistic realism, it shows that human dignity cannot be coherently sustained without recognizing a stable and objective human essence. Through historical and philosophical analysis, the article traces how modern thought has increasingly severed the link between language and being, replacing the classical understanding of personhood with functional, procedural, or relational definitions. As a result, dignity is frequently tied to contingent attributes such as autonomy, sentience, or cognitive performance—criteria that exclude the most vulnerable members of the human family. The article examines how this metaphysical shift affects bioethical deliberations in areas such as embryonic research, end-of-life care, artificial intelligence, and transhumanism. It argues that without a stable ontological foundation, dignity becomes a rhetorical construct, vulnerable to technocratic reductionism and moral relativism. In response to contemporary objections—including pluralism, autonomy, and historicism—the article defends the ongoing relevance of a realist metaphysics. Far from suppressing freedom or diversity, it provides the necessary framework for dialogue, responsibility, and moral coherence. It concludes that defending human dignity in the postmodern age requires more than legal instruments or ethical consensus: it demands a renewed inquiry into the being of the human person, and the metaphysical foundations that make dignity not only intelligible but inviolable.
Keywords: Aristotelian-Thomistic anthropology | bioethics | human dignity | nominalism | personhood | philosophy of health care and ethics

Title: An intelligent cloud-based architecture for music classification and recursive metadata management in digital libraries
Abstract: The rapid growth of digital music collections has made accurate metadata classification essential for effective organisation and retrieval. This study presents a cloud-based architecture for music genre recognition that leverages recent Deep Learning advances through a Frequency-Aware Transformer with Learnable Adaptive Positional Encoding (LAPE), Frequency-Adaptive Multi-Head Self-Attention (FA-MHSA), and layer-wise residual gating. Audio inputs undergo Spectral Flux-Based Dynamic Segmentation, amplitude normalisation, and silence trimming, while hierarchical features are extracted via multi-resolution Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and Mel-spectrograms, combined through a Learnable Weighted Fusion process. Experiments on the GTZAN dataset demonstrate exceptional performance, achieving 99% accuracy, 98.98% precision, 99.07% recall, and 99.02% F1-score—surpassing existing methods. The model maintained an average accuracy of 99% across ten genres, with class-wise accuracy ranging from 97% to 100%, indicating strong generalisation without bias. Further validation through confusion matrices, ROC curves, and training dynamics confirms the model’s capability to capture complex time–frequency dependencies in music. Overall, the proposed system provides a highly accurate, robust, and scalable solution for real-time music genre classification and metadata management in large-scale digital music libraries.
Keywords: frequency adaptive multi-head self-attention | Frequency-Aware Transformer | mel-frequency cepstral coefficients | mel-spectrograms | Music genre classification

Title: User-Centered Evaluation of Smart Musical Instruments with Embedded Real-Time Pattern Detection
Abstract: The emerging class of Smart Musical Instruments (SMIs), which embed onboard intelligence and wireless connectivity, has opened new avenues for creative possibilities for musicians. This paper addresses the challenge of real-time polyphonic audio pattern detection embedded into SMIs, which are used to trigger control messages to external devices upon the pattern identification during a live performance. We describe a real-time algorithm based on deep learning that recognizes a set of predefined polyphonic patterns from an incoming audio stream. We embed such an algorithm into smart electric guitar and smart keyboard prototypes connected to external peripherals, and assess the detection accuracy, latency, and user satisfaction with a user study involving 22 musicians. Qualitative results showed that the musicians enjoyed using the system, and they expressed interest in integrating deep learning-based tools into their performances. The user study resulted in a precision of 0.72, a recall of 0.67, and an F1 score of 0.66. We also describe and discuss a musical performance that incorporated two smart musical instruments with real time pattern detection capabilities, which were used to trigger external peripherals which included stage lights, smoke machines, mixed reality headsets, and haptic wearable devices.
Keywords: Internet of Musical Things | Music Information Retrieval Pattern Recognition | Smart Musical Instruments

Title: Implementation of Machine Learning Techniques for Real-Time Deep Fake Voice Detection
Abstract: Growing numbers of audio material made by computers, also called "deep fake voices,"are very dangerous to people's privacy, the security of information, and computers. Aiming to correctly identify fake voice changes, this study demonstrates and analyzes real-time machine learning (ML) methods. Specifically, a special dataset with 15,000 audio clips (50 percent real and 50 percent fake) was created and used for testing. Multiple machine learning models could be fully analyzed using features like Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), pitch, and spectral difference that were extracted. Random Forest (91.7%) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithms were beaten by Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), which got 96.2% accuracy. Based on real-time application tests, CNN recognition delay was an average of 0.45 seconds per 5-second audio section, proving that it is suitable for use in real-world situations. CNN clearly did better than the other models that were tried, as shown by its positive Area Under Curve (AUC) score of 0.97 in a Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis. With precision and memory rates of 95.4% and 94.8%, respectively, CNN's better performance and stability are further demonstrated. When compared to high recognition rates, the model had a 3.8% false-positive rate, showing that it needs to be improved. Results show that CNN-based machine learning models can be useful for fighting deep fake audio risks, which could lead to better real-time security solutions. For better precision and fewer false findings, it is suggested that future study combine multi-modal data analysis with advanced signal processing methods.
Keywords: CNN | Cybersecurity | Deep Fake Voice Detection | Machine Learning | Real-Time Analysis

Title: SFE-DETR: Small Feature Enhanced DETR for Infrared Small Target Detection
Abstract: Infrared Small Target Detection (ISTD) holds significant application value in multiple domains. However, current deep learning neural networks struggle to effectively extract the weak features of infrared small targets against complex backgrounds. To enhance detection capability, this paper proposes an improved algorithm based on RT-DETR: the Small Target Feature-Enhanced DETR (SFE-DETR). We introduce a Feature Channel Modulation (FCM) module to enrich spatial information via channel splitting and fusion; present the SpecPolar-AIFI Transformer encoder to fuse frequency enhancement with linear attention; propose an extended PsConv8D convolution to extract multi-directional infrared target features; and develop a Dynamic Shape-IoU (DSIoU) loss to dynamically adjust shape-distance weighting by target scale. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate that the proposed SFE-DETR significantly improves detection accuracy compared to state-of-the-art infrared small target detection methods, while maintaining excellent real-time performance.
Keywords: infrared small target | PolaLinear Attention | RT-DETR | target detection

Title: GETMusic: Generating Music Tracks with a Unified Representation and Diffusion Framework
Abstract: Symbolic music generation aims to create musical notes, which can help users compose music, such as generating target instrument tracks based on provided source tracks. In practical scenarios where there's a predefined ensemble of tracks and various composition needs, an efficient and effective generative model that can generate any target tracks based on the other tracks becomes crucial. However, previous efforts have fallen short in addressing this necessity due to limitations in their music representations and models. In this paper, we introduce a framework known as GETMusic, with “GET” standing for “GEnerate music Tracks.” This framework encompasses a novel music representation “GETScore” and a diffusion model “GETDiff.” GETScore represents musical notes as tokens and organizes tokens in a 2D structure, with tracks stacked vertically and progressing horizontally over time. At a training step, each track of a music piece is randomly selected as either the target or source. The training involves two processes: In the forward process, target tracks are corrupted by masking their tokens, while source tracks remain as the ground truth; in the denoising process, GETDiff is trained to predict the masked target tokens conditioning on the source tracks. Our proposed representation, coupled with the non-autoregressive generative model, empowers GETMusic to generate music with any arbitrary source-target track combinations. Our experiments demonstrate that the versatile GETMusic outperforms prior works proposed for certain specific composition tasks.

Title: AdaMixT: Adaptive Weighted Mixture of Multi-Scale Expert Transformers for Time Series Forecasting
Abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting involves predicting future values based on historical observations. However, existing approaches primarily rely on predefined single-scale patches or lack effective mechanisms for multi-scale feature fusion. These limitations hinder them from fully capturing the complex patterns inherent in time series, leading to constrained performance and insufficient generalizability. To address these challenges, we propose a novel architecture named Adaptive Weighted Mixture of Multi-Scale Expert Transformers (AdaMixT). Specifically, AdaMixT introduces various patches and leverages both General Pre-trained Models (GPM) and Domain-specific Models (DSM) for multi-scale feature extraction. To accommodate the heterogeneity of temporal features, AdaMixT incorporates a gating network that dynamically allocates weights among different experts, enabling more accurate predictions through adaptive multi-scale fusion. Comprehensive experiments on eight widely used benchmarks, including Weather, Traffic, Electricity, ILI, and four ETT datasets, consistently demonstrate the effectiveness of AdaMixT in real-world scenarios.

Title: CompLex: Music Theory Lexicon Constructed by Autonomous Agents for Automatic Music Generation
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence in music has made significant strides, yet it still falls short of the substantial achievements seen in natural language processing, primarily due to the limited availability of music data. Knowledge-informed approaches have been shown to enhance the performance of music generation models, even when only a few pieces of musical knowledge are integrated. This paper seeks to leverage comprehensive music theory in AI-driven music generation tasks, such as algorithmic composition and style transfer, which traditionally require significant manual effort with existing techniques. We introduce a novel automatic music lexicon construction model that generates a lexicon, named CompLex, comprising 37,432 items derived from just 9 manually input category keywords and 5 sentence prompt templates. A new multi-agent algorithm is proposed to automatically detect and mitigate hallucinations. CompLex demonstrates impressive performance improvements across three state-of-the-art text-to-music generation models, encompassing both symbolic and audio-based methods. Furthermore, we evaluate CompLex in terms of completeness, accuracy, non-redundancy, and executability, confirming that it possesses the key characteristics of an effective lexicon.

Title: Learning Neural Vocoder from Range-Null Space Decomposition
Abstract: Despite the rapid development of neural vocoders in recent years, they usually suffer from some intrinsic challenges like opaque modeling, and parameter-performance trade-off. In this study, we propose an innovative time-frequency (T-F) domain-based neural vocoder to resolve the above-mentioned challenges. To be specific, we bridge the connection between the classical signal range-null decomposition (RND) theory and vocoder task, and the reconstruction of target spectrogram can be decomposed into the superimposition between the range-space and null-space, where the former is enabled by a linear domain shift from the original mel-scale domain to the target linear-scale domain, and the latter is instantiated via a learnable network for further spectral detail generation. Accordingly, we propose a novel dual-path framework, where the spectrum is hierarchically encoded/decoded, and the cross- and narrow-band modules are elaborately devised for efficient sub-band and sequential modeling. Comprehensive experiments are conducted on the LJSpeech and LibriTTS benchmarks. Quantitative and qualitative results show that while enjoying lightweight network parameters, the proposed approach yields state-of-the-art performance among existing advanced methods. Our code and the pretrained model weights are available at https://github.com/Andong-Li-speech/RNDVoC.

Title: AI-Assisted Human-Pet Artistic Musical Co-Creation for Wellness Therapy
Abstract: This paper explores AI-mediated human-pet musical co-creation from an interdisciplinary perspective, leveraging recent advancements in animal-assisted therapy. These advancements have shown significant psychosocial benefits, especially in reducing anxiety and enhancing social engagement. Building on these findings, this study innovatively employs pet vocal timbres as'digital avatars' to enhance emotional investment during the music creation process. We propose PetCoCre, a novel system that applies pet vocal timbres in three distinct character paradigms within AI music creation: (1) PetRhythm: using pet voices as rhythmic percussion through beat synchronization. (2) PetMelody: enabling pet voices to act as melodic instruments via pitch-shifting alignment. (3) PetVocalia: utilizing pet vocal timbres as the target timbre for SVC (Singing Voice Conversion), where the converted singing voice replaces the original singer's voice, thus preserving the original semantic content. Beyond these character paradigms, our technical innovation lies in proposing SaMoye, the first open-source, high-quality zero-shot SVC model that effectively overcomes existing methods' zero-shot limitations by employing mixed speaker embeddings for timbre enhancement and leveraging a large-scale singing voice dataset. In our experiments, we collected dog and cat vocalization data from pet stores and conducted experiments with 30 participants. Results demonstrate that the human-pet co-creation mode led to significant enhancements in pleasure and creative satisfaction compared to solo AI music generation, along with a significant reduction in participants' anxiety levels. Through collaborative art creation, this research pioneers new paradigms for animal-assisted therapeutic interventions and expands the boundaries of AI-assisted creative collaboration.

Title: Cross-Level Feature Fusion for Music Emotion Recognition: Integrating Mel-Spectrogram, High-Level Musical Descriptors and Symbolic MIDI Data with Attention Mechanisms
Abstract: Even though recent deep learning techniques are achieving good performance using low-level acoustic features, symbolic-level data such as MIDI remain less explored and less frequently blended with spectral or temporal features. We introduce an end-to-end multi-modal neural framework that combines Mel spectrogram, low-level descriptors (LLDs), highlevel musical features, and symbolic MIDI data using targeted encoders and through a cross-modal attention mechanism to connect the two modes. Experimental results on three benchmarking datasets prove the efficacy of the proposed model. On DEAM and PMEmo, the Trans+HF model achieves the best RMSE scores on valence (0. 1 0 2) and arousal (0. 0 9 7), and on EMOPIA, the Mel+HF model achieves 68.15% accuracy and 0.662 Macro-F1, outperforming state-of-the-art models such as MIDIGPT and MIDIBERT-Piano. Ablation studies further confirm that each modality contributes uniquely to emotional prediction and that their integration enhances performance and generalizability. These findings validate the potential of crossmodal, cross-level feature fusion in advancing robust and expressive MER systems.
Keywords: Affective Computing | CNN-BiLSTM | Feature Fusion | High-Level Musical Features | Mel Spectrogram | Multi-modal Learning | Music Emotion Recognition | Symbolic Representation | Transformer

Title: Weakly-Supervised Movie Trailer Generation Driven by Multi-Modal Semantic Consistency
Abstract: As an essential movie promotional tool, trailers are designed to capture the audience's interest through the skillful editing of key movie shots. Although some attempts have been made for automatic trailer generation, existing methods often rely on predefined rules or manual fine-grained annotations and fail to fully leverage the multi-modal information of movies, resulting in unsatisfactory trailer generation results. In this study, we introduce a weakly-supervised trailer generation method driven by multi-modal semantic consistency. Specifically, we design a multi-modal trailer generation framework that selects and sorts key movie shots based on input music and movie metadata (e.g., category tags and plot keywords) and adds narration to the generated trailer based on movie subtitles. We utilize two pseudo-scores derived from the proposed framework as labels and thus train the model under a weakly-supervised learning paradigm, ensuring trailerness consistency for key shot selection and emotion consistency for key shot sorting, respectively. As a result, we can learn the proposed model solely based on movie-trailer pairs without any fine-grained annotations. Both objective experimental results and subjective user studies demonstrate the superior performance of our method over previous works. The code is available at https://github.com/Dixin-Lab/MMSC.

Title: Research on Secure Intelligent Vision Algorithm Based on Multi-Scale Image Enhancement
Abstract: Aiming at the problems such as insufficient brightness, blurred details and severe color cast of transmission line images in the power system, a multi-scale adaptive enhancement algorithm for transmission line images based on Retinex theory is proposed. Based on the traditional multi-scale Retinex algorithm, this algorithm introduces adaptive gamma correction to adjust brightness and color balance, achieving adaptive distribution of multi-scale weights. The experimental results show that compared with the classical multi-scale Retinex algorithm, the algorithm proposed in this paper has improved to varying degrees in multiple evaluation indicators, and the average processing time of the algorithm is also better than that of similar classical algorithms. Qualitative analysis further verified the significant effect of this algorithm in detail retention and color restoration. This method demonstrates excellent performance in both image enhancement quality and efficiency, and has high potential for engineering application.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | computer vision | fault diagnosis | power transmission lines

Title: A Machine Learning Dyslalia Mispronunciation Detection Framework for Interactive Speech Therapy
Abstract: Speech disorders, such as dyslalia, are highly prevalent among children. Traditional speech therapy methods are constrained by limited accessibility, and low engagement. In this paper, we investigate the use of machine learning (ML) in enabling real-time pronunciation practice and feedback. A synthesized dataset that includes both correct and dyslalia-affected pronunciations was developed. Our ML framework incorporates comprehensive preprocessing and feature extraction using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC). Multiple classifiers were evaluated, and three training approaches were explored. To demonstrate the practical utility of the system, we integrated the framework into a virtual reality (VR) game, LingoLand, which provides engaging speech therapy for children. The classification results achieved accuracies ranging from 83% to 95 %, with the best performance observed using the support vector machine (SVM) and XGBoost.
Keywords: Dyslalia | LingoLand | Machine Learning | Speech Disorder | Speech Recognition | Virtual Reality

Title: Improving Ml-Based Dysarthria Detection in Speech by Variation of Acoustic Features
Abstract: Dysarthria, a speech disorder affecting millions worldwide, poses significant challenges in clinical diagnosis and early detection. This paper presents a machine learning framework for detecting dysarthria in speech through multiple algorithms and feature extraction techniques. In this research, four different machine learning models were tested (Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), and XGBoost), trained on acoustic features extracted from the TORGO database. The results indicate high performance, with accuracy consistently surpassing 90%. Various feature extraction techniques were implemented to enhance the performance, including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), spectral features, and prosodic characteristics. The influence of different train-test split ratios (80/20 and 70/30) and cross-validation configurations (5-fold and 10-fold) on model performance is also evaluated. The best results of the system are achieved using an 80/20 train-test split. The best performing model (SVM) achieved a test F1-score of 0.96, outperforming some deep learning approaches, which shows that with the right feature extraction techniques, machine learning models achieve exemplary results in medical speech classification tasks.
Keywords: cross-validation | dysarthria | feature extraction | machine learning | MFCC | speech disorder detection | TORGO dataset

Title: Exploring the Trade-Offs: Quantization Methods, Task Difficulty, and Model Size in Large Language Models From Edge to Giant
Abstract: Quantization has gained attention as a promising solution for the cost-effective deployment of large and small language models. However, most prior work has been limited to perplexity or basic knowledge tasks and lacks a comprehensive evaluation of recent models like Llama-3.3. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation of instruction-tuned models spanning 1B to 405B parameters, applying four quantization methods across 13 datasets. Our findings reveal that (1) quantized models generally surpass smaller FP16 baselines, yet they often struggle with instruction-following and hallucination detection; (2) FP8 consistently emerges as the most robust option across tasks, and AWQ tends to outperform GPTQ in weight-only quantization; (3) smaller models can suffer severe accuracy drops at 4-bit quantization, while 70B-scale models maintain stable performance; (4) notably, hard tasks do not always experience the largest accuracy losses, indicating that quantization magnifies a model's inherent weaknesses rather than simply correlating with task difficulty; and (5) an LLM-based judge (MT-Bench) highlights significant performance declines in Coding and STEM tasks, though it occasionally reports improvements in reasoning.

Title: Real-Time Prediction of Infectious Disease Based on Edge Lightweight MLP-SEIR-D
Abstract: In today's highly interconnected social network, infectious disease is no longer a simple linear diffusion, but exhibits a complex pattern of 'short-term exponential and longterm long-tail'. To achieve early warning in scenarios with limited edge computing power, this paper constructs a 'SEIR-D + Lightweight Graph Neural Network' fusion framework: the dynamics of five types of populations, namely susceptible, latent, infected, recovered, and deceased, are characterized by classical SEIR-D equations, and the microscopic topological features such as node degree and clustering coefficient are input into a 3-layer MLP to realize topology-parameter dual-channel real-time optimization. The experiment was completed in 160-day dynamic simulation in three networks of 500 people and 100 nodes, ER, WS, and BA. The results show that the increase of infection rate makes the infection peak significantly advance, and the tail decay of BA scale-free network is the most persistent; after embedding network features, the peak prediction error is reduced by about 27 %, and the model weight is only 5 kB, which can be run in milliseconds on an edge node with 256 kB RAM. The study confirms that the combination of small-parameter models and network features can still balance accuracy and real-time performance in resource-constrained environments, providing public health decision-making with low latency, highly reliable decision support.
Keywords: Complex network model | Machine learning | SEIR-D infectious disease model

Title: Modelling the complex dynamic effect of L2 speaking anxiety in metaverse on students' academic enjoyment, pronunciation anxiety, speaking performance, and task load
Abstract: This study examines the intricate relationship between second language (L2) speaking anxiety and its subsequent impacts on pronunciation anxiety, perceived task load, speaking performance, and academic enjoyment within the context of metaverse-mediated English language learning, amidst the changing landscape of immersive technologies. The study examines a crucial issue: how virtual environments, despite promoting genuine interaction, may unintentionally exacerbate emotional barriers to L2 oral proficiency. A total of 117 high school students, aged 14–17 and possessing B1–B2 proficiency levels, participated in a structured debate task on Spatial.io, a three-dimensional metaverse platform that simulates a virtual conference hall featuring personalized avatars and spatial audio. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected through validated instruments and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4, with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) employed to address non-normal distributions. The findings suggest that increased L2 speaking anxiety is a significant predictor of heightened pronunciation anxiety and perceived task load, while also having substantial negative impacts on speaking performance and enjoyment of academic activities. These pathways highlight the metaverse's socio-technical affordances as a double-edged sword: they boost engagement through immersive embodiment while increasing anxiety due to real-time evaluative pressures, ultimately compromising fluency and positive affect. As a result, the findings support the implementation of innovative interventions, including AI-integrated scaffolding and anxiety-reducing protocols (such as pre-task mindfulness modules or adaptive avatar feedback), to enhance metaverse platforms for equitable L2 oral development.
Keywords: academic enjoyment | extended reality | L2 speaking anxiety | metaverse | pronunciation anxiety | speaking performance | task load

Title: Deep Neural Network and SVM-Based Multiclass Musical Instruments Classification Using MFCC, STFT, and Related Acoustic Features
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized the field of music analysis by enabling advanced sound recognition and classification techniques. In the recent year, the music industry has had transformative evolution in recent years, significantly impacting user engagement, creativity, and technological innovation across various domains, including entertainment, education, and therapy. Musical instrument recognition is an emerging field within this landscape that could be used in applications such as automated music transcription and intelligent recommendation systems and adaptive music generation. Using Deep Learning (DL) alongside Artificial Intelligence has dramatically improved how we hear things as it has become a robust analytics tool for patterns in audio. The intricate signals from audio data together with overlapping frequencies and instrument diversity present significant challenges to accurate musical instrument prediction and classification. Traditional structured machine learning models cannot be applied successfully to dealing with complicated patterns, in contrast DL models possess superior designed system architectures and stronger feature extracting ability. Through the integration of these DNN with default layers with support vector machines, an instrument recognition framework is presented in this research, on publicly available dataset of diverse instruments with three second clips combined with Mel Spectrogram and its audio features. The standard measures are used for measuring performance of models such as accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score.
