In order to evaluate the effectiveness of applied student motivation methods, the authors conducted a training in which different choral groups studied according to different learning strategies. The results of the ANOVA confirm the existence of statistically significant differences between the control and experimental groups after the training intervention. This indicates the effectiveness of the innovative program, which involved the use of AI, in the development of key cognitive functions. In addition, the students of the experimental group were motivated to create choral improvisations. The results obtained can be used in the professional training of choirmasters, in the extracurricular work of vocal groups, in inclusive music education, and in the implementation of distance forms of choral education.
Keywords: Choral improvisation | motivation of choristers | multimedia technologies | musical development | public performances

Title: Enhancing Adult Income Prediction Using PSO-Tuned LightGBM and Explainable AI
Abstract: Economic disparity, especially in the distribution of income and wealth, continues to be a major issue in the US and the world. Accurate income forecasting is critical for the creation of focused policies aimed at alleviating poverty and eliminating social inequality. However, class imbalance and weak validation techniques, among others, remain an issue in many of the currently available machine learning research works, affecting their models' dependability. To overcome these limitations, this study proposed a strong predictive model that utilizes the Tomek Links undersampling to rebalance the dataset and stratified K-fold for a rigorous evaluation. A combination of ensemble models, such as CatBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, and Decision Tree, was used, and model hyperparameters were tuned using PSO. On the UCI Adult Dataset, the best model of our approach, LightGBM, achieved an accuracy of 86.96% outperforming the previous best result of 85.256%. In the interest of transparency, Explainable AI(XAI) was applied in terms of feature importance analysis and performed a meticulous fairness analysis based on SHAP values. The proposed approach not only increased the performance on the minority class but also provided fairness in the model's behaviour across demographic groups. These improvements offer policymakers an actionable, interpretable instrument for identifying at-risk populations and ensuring fair, data-driven economic planning.
Keywords: CatBoost | Decision Tree | LightGBM | PSO (Particle Swarm Optimization) | Random Forest | stratified crossvalidation | Tomek Links undersampling | XAI(Explainable AI) | XGBoost

Title: Lightweight MATLAB GUI for Real-Time Voice Biometric Authentication
Abstract: This paper presents a real-time, text-dependent voice biometric authentication system designed using MATLAB App Designer. The system utilizes Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) for feature extraction and cross-correlation for temporal matching, enabling efficient and accurate speaker verification. Tailored for environments with limited computing resources, the approach offers a streamlined alternative to complex techniques such as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC). Operating in the frequency domain, the system achieves 95.3 % authentication accuracy. A user-friendly graphical interface supports seamless interaction, real-time user enrollment, and secure logging of verification attempts. With its focus on simplicity, speed, and effectiveness, the solution proves well-suited for practical deployment. Future improvements will explore the integration of deep learning models and adaptive noise suppression methods to enhance performance in dynamic, real-world conditions.
Keywords: Biometrics | CrossCorrelation | FFT | MATLAB GUI | Real-Time Authentication | Signal processing | Speech Recognition | Voice authentication

Title: Design and Development of Automatic Generation of Dance Moves Using Ensemble Networks
Abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has made it possible to generate dance movements automatically through combining deep learning with multimodal learning to learn the projection of music features into human-like coherent motion sequences. Nevertheless, current systems suffer from the following challenges: being poorly synchronized with rhythm, not being naturally smooth, having limited adaptability to different dance genres, and having lower generalization when tested on unseen audio patterns. Legacy methods such as rule-based choreography models and RNN-based sequence generators have the drawbacks of generating stiff, repetitive, and less expressive outputs, and GAN-based methods have the setbacks of training instability and motion collapse. To overcome this aforementioned challenge, Residual Attention Temporal Gated Networks (RAST-Gated Networks) is introduced, which integrates residual temporal learning, attention-based feature fusion, and transformer-based sequence modelling to learn long-term dependencies between audio and motion with realism. The model is trained on huge Kaggle Dance datasets with spectral augmentations and pose-based augmentations and is benchmarked with accuracy and F1-score against baseline architectures. Experimental results prove that performance is better with 97.6 % accuracy and 96.8 % F1-score, proving the robustness of the model in rhythm alignment, motion fluidity, and cross-genre adaptability, thus guaranteeing a more expressive and human-like dance movement generation mechanism.
Keywords: dance movement generation | motion synthesis | residual attention gated networks

Title: Design and Development of Modified Swin Transformer Based Digital Cultural and Creative Designs for Enhancing the Style Transfer Mechanism
Abstract: Digital cultural and overwhelming creative designs has attracted more significant intensity of momentum in imparting digital practices such as art, music and cultural heritages. These practices need more intelligent algorithms for the enhancing the transferring the mechanism. The recent advancements in Machine learning and Deep Learning algorithms have shown remarkable potential in analysing and generating culturally rich visual contents. However, achieving the high accurate performance in existing models remains to be real challenge to an efficient style transfer and exact art generation. This research article explores the advantages of Swin transformer and proposed Enhanced Swin Transformer Model integrated with Deep Weighted Feed Forward Networks to support the cultural design tasks including style classification and segmentation process. The suggested Swin transformer model was trained and validated with Kaggle Digital Art and Cultural datasets which contains 1 0, 3 6 5 cultural images which is useful for enabling multi-model cultural representation. The experimental framework evaluates performance of method through metrics like PSNR, SSIM, DICE, accuracy, precision, recall and F 1-score are calculated. The suggested model has achieved PSNR of 35.92,SSIM of 0.92, DICE of 0.93 and accuracy of 0.987 respectively. The study demonstrates that proposed mdoel not only facilitates cultural preservation but also fosters innovative creative practices, bridging the gap between heritage and modern design.
Keywords: creative designs | deep learning | machine learning | style classification | swin transformer

Title: A Machine Learning Approach for Identifying Mental Health Risk Factors Among University Students in Bangladesh
Abstract: Mental health concerns among university students in Bangladesh are rising, with depression presenting as one of the most prevalent challenges. This study employs machine learning techniques to identify key factors associated with self-reported depression, used as a proxy for bipolar disorder in the absence of clinical diagnostic data. Data were collected through structured surveys covering academic stress, lifestyle habits, emotional well-being, and social relationships. To address class imbalance in the target variable, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied. A comparative analysis of six supervised learning modelsRandom Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Naïve Bayes-was conducted to determine the most effective approach for classification. The models were evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC metrics. In addition to classification performance, feature importance scores and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) were used to interpret individual predictions and identify influential features such as suicidal ideation, social stress, and academic burden. The findings underscore the value of interpretable, data-driven methods in enhancing mental health awareness and guiding early interventions. Although limited by the use of selfreported diagnoses and non-clinical instruments, this study provides a scalable analytical framework for supporting student mental health in low-resource academic settings.
Keywords: Academic Stress | Data-Driven Intervention | Depression Prediction | Lifestyle Factors | Machine Learning | Mental Health Analytics | Psychological Wellbeing | Random Forest | SMOTE | University Students

Title: Design and Development of Intelligent Music Evaluation and Learning Platform Using Hybrid Fractal Recurrent Networks
Abstract: As digital technologies increasingly influence human lives, the incorporation of Web-based platforms in the music education arena has been imperative to offer interactive, accessible, and intelligent learning environments. The broad idea is to exploit Web technology to develop a network platform that facilitates real-time collaboration, personalized learning, adaptive feedback, and sharing of resources in music education. Yet, current systems are plagued by inefficiencies like low interactivity, inefficient recommendations, poor scalability, and absence of intelligent performance measures. Standard systems, being dependent on static databases, simple content delivery, and rule-based evaluations, cannot cater to the dynamic and individualistic learning needs. In this context, this research paper proposes the novel fractal Long short Term memory(LSTM) model and Deep Extreme Learning Networks for effective evaluation of different music notes from individuals. The proposed framework introduces the MelFrequency Correlation Co-efficients(MFCC) for better feature extraction process and aids for the better evaluation. The extensive experimentation has been carried out using MUSICNETS and various performance metrics were calculated. Comparative evaluation with traditional techniques shows enhanced outcomes, with an accuracy of 0.988, precision of 0.98, recall of 0.979 and F1-score of 0.986, marking the system's high resilience in recommendation, evaluation, and interaction. superiority performance guarantees scalability, real-time adaptability, and individualized user-centric learning, setting a standard for future music learning systems.
Keywords: fractal recurrent networks | long short term memory | mel frequency correlation co-efficients | music education

Title: Beyond Accuracy: Explainable Multimodal Deepfake Detection Through Cross-Modal Feature Analysis and Dynamic Attention Weighting
Abstract: The advent of deepfake technology in recent years has significantly transformed the domain of video synthesis, facilitating the production of convincing synthetic films. The study explains a method for detecting deepfakes that uses both visual and sound analysis with special neural networks and a technique that combines the two types of information. We have a system that uses an EfficientNetB0- based CNN to analyze face images and a bidirectional LSTM to process audio features, showing that combining both types of data makes detection stronger than using just one type. Our research on the AVLips dataset shows that different types of data learn in different ways-visual features help with quick learning at first but are more likely to overfit, while audio features lead to a more consistent learning process. Using explainable AI methods, we find that visual deepfake signs are mainly seen around the eyes and mouth, while specific MFCC coefficients (specifically 2 and 9) offer important distinguishing information in the audio part. The fusion model attains an accuracy of 87.25 %, surpassing the visual-only model at 85.25 % and the audio-only model at 81 %. In addition to performance measurements, our study offers important information regarding feature relevance across modalities and illustrates how attention mechanisms may adjust modality contributions depending on the reliability of individual samples. This study improves the field by highlighting the benefits of understanding multimodal methods and identifying specific patterns across different types of data that characterize deepfake content.
Keywords: AVLips | CNN | Deepfake Detection | EfficientNetBO | LSTM | MFCC | Multimodal

Title: A Single Channel Speech Enhancement Framework Based on Input-Information Enhanced Conformer
Abstract: Recently, the Convolution-augmented transformer (Conformer) has shown competitive results in speech applications. However, Conformer faces problems such as insufficient signal information, difficulty in processing long sequence information, and poor performance in tasks that require modeling complex temporal dynamics in single channel speech enhancement research. LSTM can have better performance in longer sequences. Stacking several audio frames into one block (SAB) in preprocessing allows the network to read more information once, which can compensate for the insufficient contextual information in single channel speech enhancement. Therefore, this paper proposes a single channel speech enhancement framework based on input-information enhanced Conformer, Nesting Conformer with LSTM, the input signal is first processed by SAB and LSTM before being input into the Conformer module. The experiment shows that compared with previous methods using the same dataset and parameters, the proposed framework's perception evaluation of speech quality (PESQ) increases by 19.0% under different signal-to-noise ratios.
Keywords: conformer | deep learning | information enhancement | LSTM | speech enhancement

Title: Deep Learning Approaches for Facies Prediction in Subsurface Seismic Data
Abstract: Hydrocarbon exploration and production depend on the classification of seismic facies, a basic component of subsurface reservoir characterization. Conventional interpretation techniques mostly rely on subjective, time-consuming, and inconsistent manual examination of seismic data. Automated methods have become effective instruments for increasing seismic interpretation efficiency and accuracy as deep learning has advanced. In this work, a deep learning framework for classifying seismic facies using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based on U-Net is presented. To assess the model's prediction power, it was tested on an unlabeled dataset after being trained on labeled seismic data. To improve model performance, data preprocessing methods such as one-hot encoding, normalization, and image scaling were used. Because of the magnitude of the dataset and the computational complexity, training was done on Google Collab. Techniques for data augmentation were also used to enhance generalization. Numerous performance measures were used to assess the algorithm, proving its efficacy in classifying facies. The findings show that by automating classification, decreasing manual labor, and enhancing the dependability of subsurface analysis, deep learning considerably improves seismic interpretation. The trained model's potential for scalable deployment in oil and gas exploration was demonstrated by the fact that it was preserved for later use.
Keywords: computation complexity | Convolutional neural network | Hydrocarbon exploration | model | normalization | One-hot encoding | Seismic facie | subsurface analysis

Title: Evaluation Singing Art Voice Quality Using Siamese Gated Recurrent Extreme Learning Networks
Abstract: The quick evolution of artificial intelligence and deep learning has provided new chances for singing art voice quality assessment, where exact evaluation of the vocal performance is critical to training, music education, and intelligent feedback systems. Current methods tend to depend on hand-engineered acoustic features, rule-based processing, or shallow machine learning models that do not handle intricate temporal-spectral dependencies present in singing signals and exhibit weak generalization and weak adaptability to varied voice types. Conventional methods like MFCC-based classification, simple CNN architectures, and recurrent networks have demonstrated some progress but are faced with high computation, overfitting, and inadequate robust attention mechanisms. To cope with the above challenges, a Siamese Gated Recurrent Extreme Learning Networks (SGRELN) is proposed by incorporating gated recurrent units, extreme learning machines and Siamese modules for emphasizing prominent vocal features. Experimental results clearly show noteworthy superiority, where RAT-CNN attains 98.8% accuracy and 97.7 % F1-score compared to traditional models. Comparative mechanism emphasizes the efficacy, strength, and interpretability of the model proposed, with greater reliability in real applications of singing quality evaluation in the real world with superior performance, scalability, and domain adaptability.
Keywords: residual attention | SGRELN | singing art | temporal modelling | voice quality evaluation

Title: Deciphering Speech Through Vision: A Deep Learning Lip Reading System
Abstract: Lip-reading bridges computer vision and speech processing by recognizing spoken words from visual lip movements alone. This study presents a streamlined framework combining facial landmark detection, image enhancement, and deep spatiotemporal modeling. We use MTCNN to detect and align lip regions, enhanced by Real-ESRGAN for higher resolution and finer detail. The enhanced images feed into a 3D CNN with timedistributed layers and bidirectional LSTM, trained using CTC loss for effective spatial-temporal feature learning and alignmentfree transcription. Evaluated on the GRID corpus, our model achieves a character error rate (CER) of 2.3% on seen speakers and 5.2% on unseen speakers. Overall, it delivers state-of-the-art performance with a 5.2% CER and 95.8% accuracy, improving CER by 18.8% over LipNet. Notably, for unseen speakers, it reduces CER from LipNet's 9.4% to 5.2%, a 44.7% relative decrease, showcasing superior generalization and robustness. These results highlight that combining super-resolution with deep temporal modeling substantially enhances visual speech recognition accuracy and reliability.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network | Deep learning | Long Short-Term Memory | Multi-Task Cascaded Convolutional Networks | Super Resolution Generative Adversarial Network

Title: Provable Performance Bounds for Digital Twin-Driven Deep Reinforcement Learning in Wireless Networks: a Novel Digital Twin Evaluation Metric
Abstract: Digital twin (DT)-driven deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for wireless network optimization, offering safe and efficient training environment for policy exploration. However, in theory existing methods can hardly guarantee real-world performance of DTtrained policies before actual deployment. In this paper, we propose the DT bisimulation metric (DT-BSM), a novel metric based on the Wasserstein distance, to quantify the discrepancy between Markov decision processes (MDPs) in both the DT and the corresponding real-world wireless network environment. We prove that for any DT-trained policy, the sub-optimality of its performance (regret) in the real-world deployment is bounded by a weighted sum of the DT-BSM and its sub-optimality within the MDP in the DT, and a modified DT-BSM based on the total variation distance is introduced to avoid the prohibitive calculation complexity of Wasserstein distance for large-scale wireless network scenarios. Numerical experiments validate this first theoretical finding on the provable and calculable performance bounds for DT-driven DRL.
Keywords: bisimulation metric | deep reinforcement learning (DRL) | Digital twin | Markov decision process (MDP) | transfer learning

Title: AI-Based Vulnerability Scanners: A Cross-Sectional Survey Analysis
Abstract: One major innovation in improving organizations’ security measures is the adoption of AI-based vulnerability scanners within the cybersecurity space. The paper analyzes cross-sectional survey research identifying factors that influence the acceptance and use of such advanced tools among cybersecurity professionals. The primary method of gathering data was a structured survey questionnaire that used Likert-scale questions to quantify the participants’ opinions objectively. It contained 20 questions based on established models, including TAM, UTAUT, and IDT. In this research, the total number of people who responded to the survey was 49, comprising cybersecurity professionals working in various industry domains. This instrument has measured perceived usefulness, ease of use, performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, and the stages of adoption, including awareness, interest, evaluation, trial, and adoption. Our results provide insight into factors that drive or hinder the adoption of AI-based vulnerability scanners, focusing on the significant role of perceived benefits and organizational support. The present paper offers valuable implications for practitioners and researchers who aim to foster AI-driven security solutions within organizational contexts.
Keywords: AI models | AI-based vulnerability scanners | cybersecurity | false positives | integration | user survey

Title: Optimizing academic engagement and mental health through AI: an experimental study on LLM integration in higher education
Abstract: Background: In alignment with UNESCO's Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG4), which advocates for inclusive and equitable quality education, the integration of Artificial Intelligence tools—particularly Large Language Models (LLMs)—presents promising opportunities for transforming higher education. Despite this potential, empirical research remains scarce regarding the effects of LLM use on students' academic performance, mental well-being, and engagement, especially across different modes of implementation. Objective: This experimental study investigated whether a guided, pedagogically grounded use of LLMs enhances students' academic writing quality, perceived mental health, and academic engagement more effectively than either unguided use or no exposure to LLMs. The study contributes to UNESCO's “Futures of Education” vision by exploring how structured AI use may foster more inclusive and empowering learning environments. Method: A total of 246 undergraduate students were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: guided LLM use, unguided LLM use, or a control group with no LLM access. Participants completed a critical writing task and standardized instruments measuring academic engagement and mental well-being. Prior academic achievement was controlled for, and writing quality was assessed using Grammarly for Education. Results: Students in the guided LLM condition achieved significantly higher scores in writing quality and academic engagement compared to the control group, with large and moderate effect sizes, respectively. Modest improvements in mental health indicators were also observed. By contrast, unguided use yielded moderate gains in writing quality but did not produce significant effects on engagement or well-being. Conclusion: The findings highlight the critical role of intentional instructional design in the educational integration of AI tools. Structured guidance not only optimizes academic outcomes but also supports students' wellbeing and inclusion. This study offers empirical evidence to inform ongoing debates on how digital innovation can contribute to reducing educational disparities and advancing equitable learning in the post-pandemic era.
Keywords: academic writing | AI-assisted learning | educational technology | guided instruction | higher education | Large Language Models | mental health | student engagement

Title: Neuroanatomy-Informed Brain–Machine Hybrid Intelligence for Robust Acoustic Target Detection
Abstract: Sound target detection (STD) plays a critical role in modern acoustic sensing systems. However, existing automated STD methods show poor robustness and limited generalization, especially under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions or when processing previously unencountered sound categories. To overcome these limitations, we first propose a brain–computer interface (BCI)-based STD method that utilizes neural responses to auditory stimuli. Our approach features the Triple-Region Spatiotemporal Dynamics Attention Network (Tri-SDANet), an electroencephalogram (EEG) decoding model incorporating neuroanatomical priors derived from EEG source analysis to enhance decoding accuracy and provide interpretability in complex auditory scenes. Recognizing the inherent limitations of stand-alone BCI systems (notably their high false alarm rates), we further develop an adaptive confidence-based brain–machine fusion strategy that intelligently combines decisions from both the BCI and conventional acoustic detection models. This hybrid approach effectively merges the complementary strengths of neural perception and acoustic feature learning. We validate the proposed method through experiments with 16 participants. Experimental results demonstrate that the Tri-SDANet achieves state-of-the-art performance in neural decoding under complex acoustic conditions. Moreover, the hybrid system maintains reliable detection performance at low SNR levels while exhibiting remarkable generalization to unseen target classes. In addition, source-level EEG analysis reveals distinct brain activation patterns associated with target perception, offering neuroscientific validation for our model design. This work pioneers a neuro-acoustic fusion paradigm for robust STD, offering a generalizable solution for real-world applications through the integration of noninvasive neural signals with artificial intelligence.

Title: Robust Retinal Vessel Segmentation for Pathology Screening Using Advanced Deep Learning Methods
Abstract: Accurate segmentation of the retinal blood vessels is crucial for the early recognition and monitoring of numerous retinal illnesses, including age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, and retinal vein occlusion. The intricacies of retinal images, such as precisely identifying thin arteries and controlling noise, can be challenging for traditional segmentation techniques. In this study, advanced deep learning approaches like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and U-Net improve the separation of retinal vessels and, as a result, detect retinal diseases. The goal is to present a novel method for deep learning that combines attention mechanisms, such as spatial and channel-wise attention modules, with multi-scale feature extraction methods such as pyramid pooling or dilated convolutions. By capturing contextual data at both the local and global levels, the deep neural network architecture will improve the identification of vessels with different widths and levels of complexity. To guarantee stable performance on various retinal image datasets, the model makes use of supervised learning in conjunction with sophisticated data augmentation approaches. This method provides a trustworthy instrument for automated retinal image processing and helps with the early detection and monitoring of retinal disorders by precisely segmenting retinal vessels. This study emphasizes the value of deep learning techniques in clinical applications for early illness identification and treatment planning, particularly CNNs, RNNs, and U-Net, and underlines their promise in retinal vascular segmentation. The findings show notable gains in segmentation sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy, especially in the identification of diseased areas and small arteries. To further improve clinical value, future research will concentrate on network architecture optimization and real-time segmentation capability exploration.
Keywords: Attention mechanism | Deep learning | Diabetic retinopathy | Multi-scale feature extraction | Retinal diseases | Retinal vessel segmentation

Title: Agriculture Crop Waste to Biochar: Extreme Learning Machine-Based Prognostics for Higher Heating Values
Abstract: This study investigates the potential of machine learning models to predict the Higher Heating Value (HHV) of biochar derived from agricultural crop waste, specifically focusing on food grain crops such as wheat, rice, and corn. Using three machine learning methods—random forest (RF), gradient boosting regressor (GBR), and extreme learning machine (ELM)—the aim was to provide consistent prognostics. For both training and testing sets, the models were scored using mean squared error (MSE), R<sup>2</sup>, and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). With the lowest Train MSE (0.0053) and Test MSE (0.4253) together with a high Train R<sup>2</sup> (0.9997) and Test R<sup>2</sup> (0.99336), ELM showed the best performance, per results. ELM also has the lowest MAPE values; hence, it is the most accurate model for biochar HHV prediction. While GBR showed overfitting tendencies with an exaggerated Train R<sup>2</sup> of 0.9991 but a much smaller Test R<sup>2</sup> of 0.8857, RF also performed well with a Test R<sup>2</sup> of 0.9576. These findings show ELM’s potential as a strong instrument for biochar energy output prediction, thereby supporting the optimization of biomass-to-biochar conversion techniques.
Keywords: Biochar | Biomass | Extreme learning machine | Machine learning | Prognostics | Waste to energy

Title: Voice Activated Platform for Video Lectures
Abstract: This project focuses on developing a deep learning-based neural network architecture for automatic timestamp generation in video content, leveraging both audio and visual inputs. The system aims to accurately detect and mark relevant video segments by analyzing synchronized audio-visual data, such as speech and corresponding facial movements. The input comprises audio features like Spectral Feature Extraction Based on Mel-scale Frequencies and visual features such as pixel data or facial landmarks, which are processed through a series of fully connected hidden layers to learn complex temporal relationships. The neural network predicts timestamps for significant video events, offering precise synchronization of video frames with audio signals. To enhance performance, advanced models like Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are integrated, addressing temporal dependencies across video sequences. The primary applications of this system include automatic subtitle generation, dialogue extraction, and lip-sync accuracy for multimedia content. This approach aims to improve efficiency and accuracy in video processing tasks, particularly in areas that require precise temporal alignment between audio and visual elements. In the future, this model can be further optimized for real-time video applications and extended to support multi-modal video processing in various languages and environments.
Keywords: Automatic annotation | Deep learning | Video segmentation | Video timestamping | Video transcripts | Voice commands

Title: Integrated transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq analysis identifies CLCNKB, KLK1 and PLEKHA4 as key gene of AKI-to-CKD progression
Abstract: Background: Studies have demonstrated a significant connection between acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). The purpose of this study was to identify biomarkers linked to the advancement of AKI and CKD, aiming to offer new targets and insights for treating and intervening in these conditions. Methods: Initially, candidate genes were identified by overlapping the results from differential expression analyses of AKI and CKD. Biomarkers were subsequently identified using machine learning algorithms, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, expression analysis and experimental verification. Functional enrichment, drug prediction analyses and immune cells infiltration were conducted to investigate the functional mechanisms of the identified biomarkers. Furthermore, single-cell analyses were performed to examine the trends of biomarker expression across different cell types. Results: CLCNKB, KLK1 and PLEKHA4 were identified as biomarkers by the screening. Subsequently, enrichment analysis showed that CLCNKB was notably enriched in oxidative phosphorylation and the degradation of valine, leucine, and isoleucine in both AKI and CKD datasets. CLCNKB, KLK1 and PLEKHA4 were found to be significantly associated with multiple immune cell types. The regulatory network indicated that PLEKHA4 might play a more important role in the progression of AKI and CKD. Furthermore, it was discovered that CLCNKB, KLK1, and PLEKHA4 are commonly targeted by tetrachlorodibenzodioxin. Finally, in the single-cell data analysis, Type A intercalated cell and Collecting duct-principal cell were identified as the key cells. It was observed that the expression trends of these biomarkers were different under different differentiation states of the key cell subpopulations. Conclusion: CLCNKB, KLK1 and PLEKHA4 were identified as biomarkers related to the development of AKI and CKD in this study, and new ideas were provided for the research on the potential mechanisms of the progression of AKI and CKD.
Keywords: acute kidney injury | biomarkers | chronic kidney disease | drug prediction | single-cell RNA sequencing

Title: Transforming Music Streaming with Blockchain and Machine Learning
Abstract: The objective of the music platform focuses on using blockchain and machine learning to revolutionize the music industry in terms of fairness in compensation to artists and quality of music for the listeners. Through the platform, artists are able to upload songs, distribute the royalties automatically using smart contracts and store the content safely by using the IPFS. Adjustable royalty pay-out structure applied based on streaming data provides a fair and equitable compensation. The proposed decentralized music platform also introduces Time-Bound NFTs and gives artists tools to deliver timely content that users can access or renew for a fee using NFTs, creating new monetization paths. The platform also embeds a highly effective recommendation system leveraging a hybrid of TF-IDF and Cohere embeddings to generate musical recommendations closely aligned to the users’ profile. In order to protect the content’s originality, The platform uses a simple audio fingerprinting for the detection of duplicates leading to improvement of the platform’s credibility. The artists can as well get a full statistic analysis on a particular song for instance to diagnose its performance. Furthermore, using a machine learning-driven notification system takes the initiative to let the users and artists know what songs are popular, which NFTs are selling the fastest, and when they are getting royalty payments. These innovations place the platform as the crystal-clear ecosystem offering advanced solutions to artists and delivering the unique fun and personal environment for listeners, paving the way for change in the music streaming and sales industry.
Keywords: Audio fingerprinting | Blockchain | Content authenticity | Decentralized music platform | Dynamic royalties | IPFS | Machine learning | Music analytics | Music streaming | NFT marketplace | Personalized recommendations | Royalty distribution | Smart contracts | Time-bound NFTs

Title: Advanced Deep Learning Approaches for Segmenting Kidney Vasculature in Phase-Contrast Tomography Images
Abstract: Automated blood artery segmentation is a crucial work in biomedical image processing, and it faces several obstacles due to intricate vascular systems, anatomical variances, and a lack of annotated datasets. This paper provides an extensive literature analysis on machine learning methods for medical image segmentation, with a focus on the most recent approaches for different organs. The objective is to create a solid foundational model for vascular segmentation in Hierarchical Phase-Contrast Tomography (HiP-CT), a new imaging modality with high-resolution 3D imaging capabilities. Let’s move on to the more general setting of medical image segmentation, where deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), namely the UNet architecture, have become widely used due to recent advances. Nevertheless, UNet difficulty in capturing long-range dependencies leads to restrictions. In response, a unique model that combines the best features of transformers and CNNs is put forth in this paper. An attention gate, channel attention, and spatial normalization are three ways that the three-level attention (TLA) module is incorporated into the architecture to improve feature representation. Deep supervision and revised skip connections improve model performance by tackling issues like low-contrast tissue settings and hazy borders. The suggested model shows steady progress on various datasets, such as ultrasound and CT scan pictures, indicating its potential as a cutting-edge instrument for medical image segmentation.
Keywords: Attention UNet | Kidney blood vessels | UNet | Vessel segmentation

Title: AI-Driven Intrusion Detection Systems: Enhancing Network Security with Machine Learning Algorithms
Abstract: Over the years, a vast amount of statistics has been produced over numerous networks since the technological transformation. The network's ability to identify assaults employing appropriate approaches has made analyzing statistics more challenging. To defend computer networks against assaults and unwanted accessibility, identifying intrusions is a crucial component of network security. Safeguarding facilities and networks against malevolent assaults requires the implementation of intrusion detection systems (IDSs). Methods depending on machine learning (ML) have demonstrated encouraging outcomes in detecting undiscovered harmful attempts. This study presents a unique ML approach for identifying attacks that are built on a collection. Several studies were conducted and assessed for assessing different ML algorithms using the KDD99 intrusion database. The efficiency of the suggested method will be assessed using a variety of ensemble-based ML algorithms and a large number of publicly available databases. Principal components assessment (PCA), shared data, and correlational examination are used to choose the most pertinent characteristics for identifying intrusions. With improved performance measures like Accuracy, precision, recall, F1-value, etc., this study utilizing various combined techniques shows that the suggested technique employing the Random Forest algorithm beats conventional algorithms FPR, and accuracy, is frequently greater than 99%. This tactic might be a helpful instrument for enhancing network and system security against new web-based risks.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | Cyber attacks | Intrusion detection system | Machine learning | Random forest

Title: Thermogram Based Diabetic Foot Ulcer Analysis Using Graph Neural Network
Abstract: Diabetes is a chronic disease which can lead to Diabetic Foot Ulcer (DFU), which has been the subject of much research. In the past, many studies have used Convolution Neural Network (CNN) to analyze DFUs. However, recent research has explored Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are more suited for analyzing data that has complex relational structures, such as the thermogram data used in DFU studies. By using GNN, both local and global information about the data were incorporated, allowing the model to make more accurate predictions. In this study, we have preprocessed the existing thermogram dataset and applied a two-layer graph convolution network. Our research compares the performance of GNN model with three machine learning models–Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, and Naive Bayes, over diabetic foot ulcer thermogram data for DFU classification. The Graph Neural Network model demonstrated stable and superior performance compared to the Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, and Naive Bayes models. The GNN model achieved an overall accuracy of 90.82%, recall of 90.71%, and an F1 score of 90.77%, along with a sensitivity of 96% and a specificity of 85.42%. Overall, the study aimed to demonstrate the potential of using GNN to analyze DFU.
Keywords: Diabetes | Diabetic foot ulcers | Graph neural network | Plantar | Thermogram

Title: Research on the Audio Data Transmission Security of Artificial Intelligence Voice Interaction Engine Devices in Smart Home
Abstract: At present, when smart homes are widely used, the security of voice interaction is very important, and the secure transmission of voice data is the key to ensuring user privacy and system security. This study for intelligent home voice interaction engine audio data transmission security problems, put forward based on deep learning and pattern recognition security strategy, through the improved CNN model learning audio features and adopts the new encryption algorithm coding after a large number of real environment test, can ensure the accuracy of the interaction at the same time improve transmission security. Research also discusses the different noise backgrounds of voice interaction engine performance, comparative analysis of the common security protocol efficiency, data show that the strategy in the environment of dynamic noise robustness is better than the traditional method, verified its innovative and practical, the future is expected to be widely used in smart home products to ensure the user information security.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence voice interaction | Audio data security | Deep learning | Pattern recognition | Smart home

Title: Cross-Domain Landscape Restoration and Fusion Based on Hybrid Deep Learning Model
Abstract: With the widespread adoption of image acquisition devices and the increasing complexity of application scenarios, motion blur and multi-source blur issues in landscape imagery have become increasingly prominent, making it challenging for traditional methods to meet high-precision restoration demands. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a cross-domain landscape restoration and fusion method based on a hybrid deep learning model. The approach integrates a globally aware generative adversarial network (GAN), a spatial detail enhancement module, a multi-scale feature fusion network, and a weighted spatial pyramid feature fusion network (WSPF-Net), enabling comprehensive utilization of features across different scales and regions. Experimental evaluations conducted on the UrbanScapes, NatureScapes, and HDR_Landscape datasets demonstrate that WSPF-Net achieves PSNR values of 30.87 dB, 31.02 dB, and 29.14 dB, respectively, with significant improvements over comparative models. The SSIM metrics all exceed 0.89, and visual quality scores are consistently above 4.5 points. The system exhibits outstanding performance in image sharpness, detail fidelity, and color reproduction. The proposed method demonstrates superior image restoration capabilities and strong cross-domain adaptability in complex scenarios, offering a novel technical pathway for landscape image processing.
Keywords: Cross-Domain | Deblurring | Deep Learning | Feature Fusion | Image Restoration

Title: Stock Market Prediction Using Spider Feline Swarm Optimization Based Hybrid Gated Recurrent Unit and Bidirectional LSTM Model
Abstract: Stock market forecasting is about predicting future trends in financial markets, such as stock prices and trading volume levels, utilizing sentiment analysis tools. Sentiment analysis is a very popular technique nowadays to extract significant information based on suggestions and reviews of users from raw data available on the internet, which also classifies the sentiment as positive, negative, and neutral. The existing models suffer from the limitations of the market’s complexity, domain-specific language, non-availability of a large labelled dataset, volatility, noise, and unpredictability for stock prediction based on sentiment analysis. Moreover, this research developed a new model - Spider Feline Swarm Optimization based hybrid Gated Recurrent Unit and Bidirectional Long-Short Term Memory (SFS based GRU-BiLSTM) to overcome these challenges. The model integrates the SFS algorithm into the hybrid GRU and BiLSTM models, which is a revolutionary step in the application of deep learning techniques for stock market forecasting and time-series analysis. The capability of the SFS model to systematically search the problem domain and intelligently find out the most promising area is one of the reasons that the hybrid model method could successfully pinpoint the complex temporal patterns present in financial data. Moreover, due to the adaptivity of SFS, it can quickly adapt its search strategies according to the changes in market conditions, and this ensures its good performance even in turbulent times. In the usage of the SFS characteristics integrated with the hybrid GRU-BiLSTM model, the traders and investors obtain a sophisticated instrument that helps them to make correct decisions in a turbulent environment. The findings show that the performance is significantly better than traditional methods in terms of accuracy, MCC, precision, and recall when looking at a training percentage of 90 on the stock market sentiment dataset, with results of 96.95%, 93.91%, 96.36%, and 97.58% respectively.
Keywords: BiLSTM | Feature extraction | Hybrid gated recurrent unit | Spider feline swarm optimization | Stock market prediction

Title: Speech Feature-based Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approach for Assamese Dialect Identification
Abstract: Dialect identification helps identify various dialects within a certain language. The Assamese language is spoken widely across Assam, India, and its neighboring states. Identifying dialects within a language is important in gaining insights into its social, cultural, and historical context. The broadly recognized dialects in Assamese include Central, Lower, and Upper Assamese dialects. Recent developments in Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) have shown promising results in dialect identification in various languages, rather than relying on traditional methods that are labor intensive and require manual intervention. Features of speech signals play a vital role in their respective task. This paper explores the use of Random Forest and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models for the automatic identification of Assamese dialects. By leveraging our proposed dataset of three dialects, extracting relevant features such as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Energy, Formants (F1, F2, F3), and Spectral Flux, and ML/DL architectures, this study contributes to the development of automatic dialect identification of Assamese dialects. The results showed that both the Random Forest and LSTM models achieved an accuracy of 97%, indicating good performance with limited availability of data.
Keywords: Dialect Identification | LSTM | Machine Learning | Random Forest | Speech

Title: Research on Stage Vocal Classification Based on Long Short-Term Memory Artificial Neural Networks
Abstract: With the continuous advancement of artificial intelligence technology, stage vocal classification has become increasingly prevalent in the fields of music and speech processing. In response to the complex sound data and realtime classification requirements in stage performance environments, this paper proposes a stage vocal classification method based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks. First, the paper deeply analyzes the audio features of stage vocals, focusing on extracting parameters closely related to vocal characteristics, such as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), formant frequencies, pitch, and timefrequency domain features. These features can comprehensively capture both temporal and spectral information of the human voice, providing effective input for the LSTM model. Secondly, considering the advantages of LSTM networks in handling time-series data, the paper constructs an LSTM-based stage vocal classification model that leverages its ability to learn temporal dependencies and sequence patterns. This model not only accurately captures pitch variations, speech rhythm, and environmental noise interference in stage performances but also effectively distinguishes between different singing styles. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional machine learning methods in stage vocal classification accuracy, especially in complex stage environments, achieving higher classification accuracy and robustness.
Keywords: audio features | long short-term memory | machine learning methods | singing styles | Stage vocal classification

Title: New Method for Intent Recognition Based on Audio and Text Multimodality
Abstract: This paper introduces an innovative intent recognition approach that leverages the complementary strengths of audio and text multimodalities. Initially, the method captures the user's raw voice data and transcribes it into textual information. Subsequently, the Roberta text intent recognition model is employed for extracting textual features and discerning intent, where the first cross-entropy is computed. In parallel, the unsupervised pre-training model wav2vec is utilized to extract audio features directly from the original voice information, and intent is recognized, resulting in the second cross-entropy. Furthermore, the method integrates intent recognition by concatenating the extracted text and audio features, yielding the third cross-entropy. The ultimate intent recognition is achieved through a weighted calculation of these three cross-entropies. The weights are derived through training the Roberta text intent recognition model in conjunction with the wav2vec unsupervised pre-training model. This approach, particularly pertinent to the field of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), minimizes the risk of error propagation from inaccurate textual transcriptions, thereby enhancing the precision of downstream tasks. By advancing the interface between linguistic and acoustic data analysis, this method highlights the transformative impact of integrating advanced natural language processing and audio signal processing technologies in HCI applications. The proposed method underscores the significance of applying sophisticated audio-visual integration techniques in engineering disciplines to achieve robust and accurate intent recognition in modern interactive systems.
Keywords: Deep learning | Human-computer dialogue system | Intent recognition | Multi-modal | Natural language understanding

Title: PsychoLLAMA3-R1: A Large-Scale Adaptive Testing Model Based on LLAMA3 Large Language Model with CoT and DPO
Abstract: Psychological assessments play a pivotal role in comprehending individual psychological states, yet they often grapple with the intricacies of complex data management. To surmount these obstacles, we have developed PsychoLLAMA3-R1, an expansive psychological assessment model grounded in the LLAMA3.2-8B-Instruct framework. This model amalgamates a distinctive 50 K dataset along with the Chain of Thought (CoT) Alpaca dataset, both subjected to stringent verification processes involving human expertise and AI technologies to guarantee data excellence and variety. The refinement of PsychoLLAMA3-R1 was accomplished through a combination of supervised Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) methodologies. It is capable of offline deployment, thereby safeguarding data privacy and security, and has undergone optimization to minimize energy consumption. Findings indicate that PsychoLLAMA3-R1 delivers superior performance in psychological assessments, yielding precise and pertinent responses. The offline functionality ensures the security of sensitive data, and the energy optimization mitigates the operational load. PsychoLLAMA3-R1 signifies a considerable leap forward in the realm of psychological evaluations, presenting a robust instrument for tailored education and clinical decision-making. Subsequent endeavors will concentrate on further bolstering the model's performance and broadening its applicability.
Keywords: DPO | large language model | LLAMA3 | psychological assessment | RL

Title: Virtual Human Dance Movement Generation Technology Based on Transformer and VITON Network
Abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of computer vision and deep learning technologies, virtual human technology has been widely applied in fields such as entertainment, education, gaming, and metaverse. But the existing methods still have deficiencies in movement fluency, music matching and naturalness of virtual human posture. In order to improve the quality of virtual human dance generation, the study proposes a movement generation technique based on Transformer and virtual try-on network. By constructing a dance video dataset, the encoder-decoder structure is used to establish the mapping relationship between audio and dance movements. Virtual human dance synthesis is realized. The experimental results show that the matching rate of this method increases rapidly with the increase of the dataset, and gradually tends to stabilize after the dataset size exceeds 10, with the matching rate close to 0.93. Its smoothness and matching degree of the movements are 0.9 and 0.88, respectively. In terms of the generating speed, the fastest generating speed is 0.50 ~s / frame. The study shows that this technology has good performance and can effectively improve the accuracy and realism of virtual human dance generation, providing support for applications such as virtual idol and intelligent entertainment.
Keywords: computer vision | dance movement key points | deep learning | movement generation | transformer networks

Title: Robust Optical Power Forecasting Across Temperatures: A New L-I Model with Enhanced Temperature Dependence
Abstract: This study presents a new L-I Model, an optimized optical power prediction model that incorporates temperature-dependent efficiency (η(T)), linear temperature-dependent thermal resistance (R<sup>th</sup>). ReLU activation is applied to ensure non-negative predictions. Using the RMSprop optimizer with a small learning rate (2e-12), the model achieves an R2 of 0. 6 9 9 2, MSE of 0.2004 and MAE of 0.3826 significantly outperforming previous models. The model demonstrates robust performance in predicting optical power across a range of temperatures (10°C. to 90° C). Key improvements include enhanced temperature dependence modeling and ReLU activation, resulting in more accurate predictions and stable training.
Keywords: lasers | machine learning | optical communications | optical power prediction | ReLU activation | RMSprop optimizer

Title: THE IMPACT OF FINANCIAL TECHNOLOGY (FINTECH) ON ENHANCING FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE: AN APPLIED STUDY IN THE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY
Abstract: The enhancement of financial performance within insurance companies fundamentally relies on achieving a balance between premium income and the compensatory disbursements made in response to policyholder claims. This study investigates the extent to which financial technology (FinTech) contributes to the improved financial performance of the Iraqi National Insurance Company. To address this objective, the research outlines the core problem and integrates findings from existing literature concerning both FinTech adoption and strategies for financial enhancement. A conceptual framework was established to examine the relationship between FinTech utilisation and financial performance improvements. To empirically validate the research hypothesis, a structured questionnaire was designed and distributed to a purposive sample of 150 employees drawn from the information systems, finance, and sales/customer service departments of the Iraqi National Insurance Company. The data were analysed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), with a Likert-scale instrument applied to measure relevant constructs. The results revealed a significant positive correlation (R = 0.621) between FinTech implementation and financial performance, with technological factors accounting for 38.6% of the variance in performance outcomes. These findings support the hypothesis that FinTech exerts a direct and measurable impact on the financial efficiency of the company. The study concludes that there exists a strong and direct association between the integration of FinTech solutions and the enhancement of financial performance within the Iraqi National Insurance Company.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Financial Performance Improvement | FinTech | Insurance Tech | Internet of Things

Title: Discovery of Deepfakes in Art
Abstract: The proliferation of deepfakes-AI-generated or manipulated media-has transformed the landscape of contemporary art. Deep generative models, including GANs, VAEs, diffusion models, and Transformers, have enabled artists to explore new creative realms while simultaneously raising critical questions around authenticity, ethics, and detection. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of deepfake technologies across five key media modalities: image, video, text, speech, and music. We examine the architectures that enable content creation, and the state-of-the-art techniques used for detection. Further, we evaluate detection accuracy, robustness, and practical implementation, incorporating diagrams, comparative tables, and performance formulas. This work aims to provide a balanced perspective on the opportunities and challenges posed by synthetic media in the artistic domain.
Keywords: Art Forensics | Deepfakes | GANs | Generative Models | Multimedia AI | Transformers

Title: Applying transfer learning and data augmentation to image recognition models for music emotion classification
Abstract: In this study, we propose a method to construct an image recognition model with a single-channel input using transfer learning and data augmentation for music emotion classifi-cation. The data augmentation method generates a variety of spectrogram images by varying the STFT window size in small increments. This method ensures data equivalent to five times the amount of the original data and prevents degradation of classification performance due to insufficient data. The model construction method using transfer learning for grayscale images is designed to adapt the pre-trained EfficientNetV2 model, which was originally trained on ImageNet. The constructed model through transfer learning and our proposed data augmentation method achieved a classification accuracy of 94.8% on the 4Q Audio Emotion Dataset. Thus, our construction method using transfer learning for grayscale images, combined with the proposed data augmentation method, is effective in achieving music high-accuracy emotion classification.
Keywords: CNN | data augmentation | deep learning | music emotion classification | transfer learning

Title: Synthetic index for the evaluation of territorial poverty in the municipalities of Querétaro, Mexico
Abstract: Introduction/Objectives: Poverty is a multidimensional phenomenon that affects various aspects of well-being across territories. This study aims to develop a Synthetic Municipal Poverty Index (SMPI) for the state of Querétaro, with the objective of assessing socioeconomic disparities among municipalities and prioritizing areas for public policy intervention. Methodology: A quantitative approach with a deductive, non-experimental design was employed. Socioeconomic data from 16 municipalities in Querétaro were collected from official sources such as INEGI and CONEVAL. The SMPI was constructed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), a technique applied to determine the weights of selected indicators. Index validation was carried out through hierarchical clustering and the XGBoost machine learning model, ensuring the robustness and accuracy of the index. Results: The findings reveal significant disparities in poverty levels across the analyzed municipalities. Income and food-related sub-indices emerged as the main determinants of poverty. Validation using the XGBoost model demonstrated high predictive performance of the SMPI, reinforcing its value as an analytical tool. Conclusions: The SMPI serves as a reliable instrument for measuring multidimensional poverty at the municipal level. Its application supports the identification of priority areas and contributes to the design of more targeted and effective public policies. This index provides a solid framework for evidence-based decision-making and the development of comprehensive strategies to reduce poverty at the territorial level.
Keywords: clustering | Poverty | principal component analysis | Querétaro | supervised learning | synthetic index

Title: Impact of Machine Learning on the Development of Mathematical Operations Using Scratch
Abstract: This research focused on analyzing the impact of Machine Learning (ML) applied through the Scratch platform on the development of mathematical operations in secondary school students. The quantitative, descriptive, and field-based study was conducted with a sample of 30 students from public schools in educational zone three. A survey technique was used with a questionnaire validated by education experts, and the instrument’s reliability was measured with a Cronbach’s Alpha of 0.89. The results obtained from pretest and posttest, as well as the application of the t-student test and ANOVA analysis, demonstrated that the experimental group, which used Scratch with ML, showed significant improvements in their mathematical performance compared to the control group. Additionally, the impact analysis based on Cohen’s D revealed a considerable effect on academic performance, reinforcing the effectiveness of the proposal. These findings not only highlight the importance of incorporating emerging technologies in education but also suggest that the use of interactive and adaptive approaches can optimize the learning of mathematics. The research concludes that integrating ML and Scratch in mathematics education is an effective tool for enhancing students’ understanding and developing critical skills.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Education | Machine Learning | Mathematics

Title: Enhanced piano audio feature recognition: a novel MFCC-based method with F-HRSF and convolutional neural network
Abstract: In piano audio processing and analysis, while the traditional Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) feature extraction method is extensively utilized in audio recognition, its recognition accuracy often falls short when applied to piano audio due to its inability to capture the intricate dynamic features of such audio fully. To address this limitation, this article enhances the MFCC feature extraction method by integrating the Fisher half rising sine function (F-HRSF) with a multilayer convolutional neural network, aiming to achieve precise recognition of piano audio features. Initially, we employ the Fisher ratio for subband screening to isolate components with strong characterization ability from the audio subband components, segmenting the MFCC features by dimensions and calculating the Fisher ratio. Subsequently, we develop an improved MFCC feature extraction method based on F-HRSF. The normalized 2D feature values obtained are then used as inputs for the multilayer hierarchical convolutional neural network. Experimental results demonstrate that the model developed in this article achieves accuracy rates of 92.15%, 92.83%, 91.57%, and 92.13% in classification accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively, on the GTZAN dataset, with a consistently stable performance in audio feature recognition. This study not only refines the MFCC feature extraction method and enhances audio feature recognition accuracy but also introduces novel ideas and approaches for piano audio processing and analysis.
Keywords: Algorithms and Analysis of Algorithms | Algorithms and Analysis of Algorithms | Artificial Intelligence | Artificial Intelligence | Audio feature recognition | Brain-Computer Interface | Brain-Computer Interface | Data Mining and Machine Learning | Data Mining and Machine Learning | Deep learning | Fisher ratio | MCFF | Multilevel convolutional neural network | Neural Networks | Neural Networks | Subband screening

Title: A comparative evaluation of Deep Learning models for tumor segmentation: Identifying the optimal framework for clinical integration
Abstract: Accurate tumor segmentation is crucial for effective radiotherapy planning and surgical applications through 3D models and patient-specific instruments. Manual delineation is labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability, driving the need for robust automated solutions. This study evaluates the performance of four Deep Learning frameworks - U-Net, SegResNet, UNETR, and SwinUNETR - implemented via the MONAI framework. A comprehensive dataset of 126 pelvic tumors was employed for training and validation. Quantitative metrics (Dice Similarity Coefficient, Hausdorff Distance and Average Surface Distance) and qualitative evaluation were used to assess segmentation performance. Our results indicate that, although each model shows potential, U-Net delivers superior segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency, making it the most viable candidate for integration into clinical workflows. These findings underscore the transformative role of Deep Learning-based segmentation in enhancing treatment planning efficiency in clinical practice.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Deep Learning | MONAI | Pelvic Tumors | Radiotherapy | SegResNet | Surgical Planning | SwinUNETR | Tumor Segmentation | U-Net | UNETR

Title: Enhancing LLMs with Indian Multi-Lingual Audio Understanding for Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) Advancement
Abstract: The creation of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) includes training machines to understand human communication in the style of real-time conversations. In this paper, the shortcomings of Large Language Models (LLMs) in processing audio data of various languages and contexts, especially in linguistically diverse environments like India, are identified and pose the challenge of phonetic variations, tones, and nuanced contextual usage. With the integration of pre-trained text-based LLMs with multi-lingual and multi-task audio perception, the process includes ongoing pre-training based on audio encodings of Indian multi-lingual data. With the usage of sophisticated audio handling methodologies and multimodal data, the model is trained to provide high-quality transcriptions and resilient contextual understanding. A multi-step framework of dataset curation, preprocessing, and model training focuses on metrics like Word Error Rate (WER) and BLEU scores. Outcomes show a significant lowering of WER by 15% and an increase in BLEU scores by 20% with improved transcription accuracy and audio understanding. The paper adds to the AGI mission by creating an adaptive, culture-sensitive AI system with effective multi-lingual communication, supporting applications like voice assistants, real-time translation, and accessibility aid, while addressing the computational efficiency and diversity of data challenge.
Keywords: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) | Computational Efficiency | Data Diversity | Dataset Curation | Large Language Models (LLMs) | Multi-Lingual Audio Understanding | Multimodal Data

Title: Physically Parameterized Differentiable MUSIC for DoA Estimation with Uncalibrated Arrays
Abstract: Direction of arrival (DoA) estimation is a common sensing problem in radar, sonar, audio, and wireless communication systems. It has gained renewed importance with the advent of the integrated sensing and communication paradigm. To fully exploit the potential of such sensing systems, it is crucial to take into account potential hardware impairments that can negatively impact the obtained performance. This study introduces a joint DoA estimation and hardware impairment learning scheme following a model-based approach. Specifically, a differentiable version of the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm is derived, allowing efficient learning of the considered impairments. The proposed approach supports both supervised and unsupervised learning strategies, showcasing its practical potential. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method successfully learns significant inaccuracies in both antenna locations and complex gains. Additionally, the proposed method outperforms the classical MUSIC algorithm in the DoA estimation task.
Keywords: DoA estimation | Hardware impairments | ISAC | Model-based machine learning

Title: Automated Lung Sound Classification using Multi-Scale Contextual Attention with Adaptive Feature Scaling
Abstract: Respiratory sound is one of the major things that give us information about healthy and unhealthy lungs through the breath that is inhaled and exhaled. If any abnormal sound is detected in the lungs, then it is a thing, that should be seriously dealt with. Lung disease is known to be the third most common cause, which makes the people die. So it is essential to detect and classify the abnormalities that are happening in the lungs through the signal waves. Nowadays, various artificial intelligence (AI) techniques are playing a crucial role in image and signal processing. This technique offers promising result in image (or) video recognition, and audio signal processing. In those AI techniques, deep learning has played a vital role over decades for accurately detecting the disease than the other learning models. Although, it is hard to classify the abnormalities present within it. Hence, this study proposes a Multi-scale contextual attention with an adaptive feature scaling algorithm to classify the lung sound and detect abnormalities. For filtering the signal, the total variation denoising technique is used. Following this Short-Term Fourier Transform along with Zero Crossing Rate is used for feature extraction and PCA with relief is used for reducing the dimensionalities. Further, the proposed classification algorithm is also compared with the other existing algorithms, such as R-CNN, LSTM, and E-LSTM for better results. Moreover, accuracy, precision, and recall comparisons are also made to evaluate the performance of the proposed model in the detection of lung sounds through signal waves.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence (AI) | Deep Learning | Lung sound | Multi-scale contextual attention with adaptive feature scaling | Signal Processing | Total Variation Denoising

Title: A High-Performance Malware Detection Using Extra Tree Classifier and Logistic Regression on TUNADROMD Dataset
Abstract: Precise malware identification is essential for enhancing cybersecurity frameworks against advancing threats. This study introduces an enhanced malware detection framework utilizing machine learning methods on the TUNADROMD data set from Kaggle, which comprises 4,465 instances and 242 instances. A selection of 23 high-impact attributes was identified through feature relevance analysis to enhance classification accuracy reduce computing complexity. Two models-Extra Tree Classifier and Logistic Regression-were assessed for their classification efficacy. The Extra Tree Classifier exhibited enhanced accuracy, attaining 97.42% in training and 97.23% in testing, surpassing the Logistic Regression model, which recorded 94.84% and 93.67%, respectively. The Extra Tree Classifier has superior predictive performance and reduced computational expense compared to current methodologies, positioning it as a dependable instrument for real-Time malware detection. This work emphasizes the capability of machine learning to offer scalable and resilient solutions for malware analysis and detection, establishing a basis for future progress in automated threat mitigation.
Keywords: Automated Malware Analysis | Cybersecurity | Extra Tree Classifier | Feature Selection | Logistic Regression | Machine Learning | Malware Detection | Threat Mitigation | TUNADROMD Dataset

Title: Automatic Key Modulation Monitoring and Tonicization Detection with Hierarchical Clustering
Abstract: In a wide range of tasks involving tonal music, key annotation is essential. Among these, the handling of modulation remains a blind spot in most existing approaches. As a result, music analysis often struggles to cope with highly modulating and tonally diverse material. Moreover, with the growing trend of artificial intelligence researches in music generation and style transfer, there is an increasing demand for datasets containing more precise key information. This paper proposes an unsupervised algorithm capable of rapidly and effectively detecting the key of symbolic music, while also addressing any instances of modulation or tonic deviation. We evaluate the method on diverse samples, both with and without modulation, across multiple musical styles. Comparative analysis with established algorithms demonstrates its promising performance.
Keywords: beam search | hierarchical clustering | key detection | key modulation | symbolic music

Title: An Automated Interference Detection System for FDMA Based Satellite Communication Networks Using Multi-Scale Wavelet Technique
Abstract: Current satellite communication interference detection systems face significant challenges including high false alarm rates in conventional energy detection methods, computational complexity in machine learning approaches requiring extensive training datasets, and inability of single-scale analysis techniques to handle heterogeneous carrier characteristics in Frequency Division Multiple Access networks. Recent advances in deep learning-based signal classification demonstrate improved accuracy but suffer from limited adaptability to operational networks and high computational overhead. Statistical anomaly detection methods assume specific signal models that inadequately address the diverse spectral signatures found in operational satellite systems. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a novel automated interference detection system employing multi-scale wavelet transforms with adaptive thresholding and cross-scale weighted voting mechanisms. The primary objective is to develop a robust, real-time interference detection framework capable of identifying multiple interference types including co-channel, adjacent satellite, and unauthorized transmissions while maintaining low false alarm rates. The system processes spectrum analyzer data at regular intervals, implementing scale-dependent threshold adaptation and weighted cross-scale integration to distinguish anomalous interferers from normal communication signals. Experimental validation demonstrates detection accuracy exceeding 85% with median response times under 20 seconds, implemented in an operational Carrier Monitoring System (CMS) for ISTRAC's satellite communication network. Results indicate superior performance compared to conventional single-scale frequency-domain techniques, with 23% reduction in false alarms and enhanced detection capability for low signal-to-interference ratio conditions. The interference detection system was implemented to detect real-time anomalies in multiple satellite transponder spectrums simultaneously by incorporating RF switching in a round-robin fashion. The RF switch and the Spectrum Analyzer are controlled in a coordinated manner in the Carrier Monitoring System.
Keywords: Carrier Monitoring System | carrier segmentation | Frequency Division Multiple Access | interference detection | satellite communications | spectrum monitoring | wavelet analysis

Title: Performance Evaluation of Speech Emotion Recognition Using Hybrid Feature Selection and Machine Learning
Abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) plays a crucial role in human-computer interaction, offering insights into user emotions, particularly in environments with complex acoustic interactions such as songs. Traditional machine learning classifiers struggle with these complexities, especially when distinguishing emotions in the presence of vocals and background music. This study proposes a hybrid feature selection strategy to enhance SER accuracy for six distinct emotions: neutral, calm, happy, sad, angry, and fearful. Using the RAVDESS database, consisting of 1,012 recordings, we extracted 33 time-frequency features, including energy, spectral descriptors, MFCCs, and chroma. A hybrid framework combining filter-based (chi-square) and embedded (random forest importance) methods was implemented. Four classifiers K Nearest Neighbors (K-NN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Gradient Boosting (GB) were evaluated across three paradigms: filter-only, embedded-only, and hybrid. The hybrid feature selection method outperformed the others, with SVM achieving a peak accuracy of 83.55% (RBF kernel) and K-NN showing a 6.25% improvement over baseline performance (81.91%). These results demonstrate that hybrid feature selection enhances traditional machine learning classifiers, allowing them to achieve performance comparable to deep learning models while maintaining computational efficiency. This approach is particularly advantageous for deploying SER in resource-constrained environments, offering a balance between accuracy and efficiency in emotion recognition applications.
Keywords: Deep Learning | ML Classifiers | RAVDESS | SER | Time-Frequency Features

Title: Implementation of Multiscale Conv-GRU-based Efficient Emotion Recognition Framework using Speech Signals based on Federated Learning
Abstract: In real-life communication, nonverbal elements including laughter, crying, and other emotional interjections play a key role in conveying feelings. Emotions are essential for human interactions, aiding in mutual understanding. To enhance human-computer interactions and advance speech-based emotion recognition technologies, it is crucial to accurately identify emotions. Extracting emotional context from speech remains a significant challenge in the domain of AI. Building datasets for speech emotion recognition is a demanding and expensive task, resulting in limited data availability and uneven emotion representation. This imbalanced dataset can affect the performance and dependability of emotion detection systems. Innovative approaches are necessary to address the limitations of traditional emotion recognition methods. In this study, a novel deep learning-based speech-emotion recognition framework incorporating the principles of federated learning is proposed. In the initial phase, required speech signals for the validations are sourced from the benchmark resources. Next, from the collected speech signals, ensemble features like Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), spectral features and sparse autoencoder-based deep features are extracted.
