Research limitations/implications – The sample is limited to peer-reviewed literature (2000–2023) with English-language emphasis; database coverage and methodological heterogeneity may bias topic prevalence. Future work should widen non-English sources, replicate with alternative models (e.g. BERTopic) and couple macroreviews with microdata on product performance and inclusion outcomes. Practical implications – Guidance for regulators on mutual recognition and Shariah governance harmonization; for institutions on embedding digital Shariah controls, cybersecurity and AI assurance; and for issuers on robust KPI/impact frameworks for green Sukuk. Social implications – Digital Islamic finance can advance financial inclusion and sustainable development goals if paired with credible impact verification, consumer protection and equitable data-use practices. Originality/value – Combines a systematic review with machine-learning topic discovery, bibliometric validation and qualitative evidence to deliver an integrated map of Islamic finance’s evolution, a conceptual ecosystem framework and a concrete agenda linking fintech, governance and sustainability.
Keywords: Islamic banking | Islamic finance | Shariah-compliant finance | Sukuk | Systematic review

Title: AFR-Net: Attention-Based Channel-Spatial Feature Refinement Network for Small Object Detection
Abstract: Small object detection (SOD) is a critical yet challenging area in computer vision. Deep learning-based object detection techniques have achieved remarkable progress, however, identifying small objects continues to be a challenging task due to factors such as scale variations, object deformation, and interference from complex backgrounds. The Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) partially mitigates these challenges and significantly enhances detection performance, but existing FPN-based approaches often face substantial information loss at different levels of the pyramid, limiting the effectiveness of multi-scale feature utilization. To address these challenges, we propose AFR-Net to improve small object detection by augmenting the functionality of feature pyramid networks. AFR-Net comprises three primary modules. Multi-scale Deformable Feature Extraction (MDFE) leverages deformable convolution to enhance feature extraction at the deepest FPN level, generating more accurate feature maps. During the feature fusion process, Channel-Spatial Feature Refinement (CSFR) module employs attention mechanisms to refine important feature information. Wise Intersection over Union (WIoU) emphasizes small objects by assigning appropriate weights to different scales. We evaluate AFR-Net on benchmark datasets, including MS COCO and VisDrone, demonstrating that it achieves superior performance compared to existing FPN-based detection methods. Furthermore, AFR-Net’s design makes it applicable to various feature-refinement-based tasks in computer vision, enabling improved performance across multiple domains.

Title: Using AI in Analysing Satirical Drawings in Commercial Advertisements
Abstract: Satirical drawings have served as an effective instrument in commercial ads, where humor and irony can help mold public perception. Yet, satirical content can be subjective and hard to recognize in an automated way or to analyze. This study investigates using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze satirical reconnaissance in commercial advertisements through a multimodal image and text processing analysis. The CNN model effectively identifies and classifies satirical content with high accuracy by leveraging deep learning and natural language processing techniques. Empirical results show that multimodal CNN could achieve much better classification performance than single-mode models, achieving a 91 of AUC-ROC. The study notes the use of AI in content moderation, ad optimization, and audience engagement tactics. Despite prevalent issues with deciphering elaborate humor, this groundbreaking study offers an initial structure for automated recognition of satirical content, setting the stage for more profound proficiency in computational humor analysis as well as advertising intelligence.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | CNN | Commercial Advertisements | Content Moderation | Deep Learning | Humor Recognition | Marketing AI | Multimodal Analysis | Satirical Drawings

Title: An Ensemble Learning Approach to Predict Breast Cancer Disease
Abstract: The concept of Machine Learning is used now a days to describe the diagnosis and prognosis of many kinds of cancer. This forecast reduces subsequent surgical procedures. The prediction of breast cancer is the main subject of this paper. The incidence of deaths from breast cancer has recently declined due to early diagnosis, breast screening and improved treatment. In this research, the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC) dataset is used to offer a robust Stacking Ensemble Learning framework for breast cancer prediction. Four different supervised Machine Learning algorithms as base learners: Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree and Multi-Layer Perceptron and Logistic Regression as the meta model have been employed to integrate each of their separate predictions. To improve model performance, extensive preprocessing procedures were carried out. In comparison to individual classifiers, the stacked model outperformed them with an accuracy of 97.37%, highlights how well the suggested Ensemble approach improves diagnostic precision and show that it has the potential to be a significant instrument for clinical judgment in the identification of breast cancer.
Keywords: breast cancer | decision tree | ensemble technique | logistic regression | machine learning | multi layer perceptron | naive bayes | random forest | stacking

Title: The Integration of Artificial Intelligence and the Contributions of Behavioral Economics into Public Management in Morocco: Towards a Transformation of Administrative Practices and Public Decision-Making
Abstract: In the era of digital native and growing demands for public performance, the purpose of this study is to investigate the role of AI and behavioral economics in public management in Morocco. The goal is to study to what extent such innovations can modernize administrative processes and improve public decision-making factors, while respecting local institutional and cultural conditions. The key question is whether these instruments can reinforce the effectiveness, transparency and accountability of public action, notwithstanding the organizational and ethical challenges they also pose. They find that AI is very cost effective to use to optimize decisions (prediction, automation), while nudges improve compliance of citizens with public policies. But the study also points to major drawbacks: institutional resistance, digital skills gaps and ethical risks associated with algorithmic opacity. The vision emphasizes the need for futurological governance, customized training, and strong regulations for an inclusive transition. This study paves the way for further investigations into the territorial appropriation of these new practices and the potential implications of these innovations for the inequality of access to public services.
Keywords: Algorithmic governance | Behavioral economics | Digital transformation | public management

Title: Is AI a Threat to Human Music? (a neo-Deweyan Perspective)
Abstract: As the artificial intelligence (AI) wave washes over more and more traditional forms of human experience, music-makers and audiences disagree about the value of generative artificially intelligent music (GAIM) relative to more traditionally human forms of composition and performance. My answer to my title question is no and yes. No, in that GAIM, lacking consciousness, cannot literally threaten anything; but also yes, in that certain human uses of musical artificial intelligence threaten human music. Situating this thesis within a neohumanist and experientialist view of art, I draw on key themes in John Dewey's Art as Experience and in his broader experimental-pragmatist approach to problem-solving and learning. Particularly relevant is Art as Experience's argument that any kind of art, including music, is a form of fully embodied human experience that involves human agency, aesthetic phenomenology, and mutual recognition among human artists and their audiences. Equally relevant is Dewey's pragmatist account of reconstructive inquiry into "indeterminate situations."This idea provides a strategically useful frame for parents and teachers who seek to create new ways of teaching young children the pleasures of hearing and making human music before they become habituated to the easy, agency-eroding pleasures of GAIM-fueled streaming platforms and music-generating programs.

Title: Predicting Economic Quads Through Asset Returns Using Ensemble Machine Learning
Abstract: This study explores the predictive capacity of financial asset returns in forecasting macroeconomic regime shifts, specifically the transition among Inflation, Expansion, Stagflation, and Deflation (IESD) quadrants. While traditional economic indicators such as GDP, CPI, and interest rates are commonly used to define these regimes, their delayed release limits real-time applicability. Motivated by the forward-looking nature of markets, we develop two Machine Learning (ML) models: a Neural Network and an Ensemble Learning classifier combining Random Forest and Gradient Boosting. These models are trained on a ten-year dataset comprising 22 financial instruments, including equity sector Exchange-Traded Fund (ETFs), bonds, commodities, and volatility indices. To enhance predictive robustness, the study incorporates extensive feature engineering, such as logarithmic returns, rolling volatilities, and moving averages, alongside dimensionality reduction via Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Evaluation is conducted through K-Fold cross-validation and performance metrics including accuracy, F1-score, and ROC AUC. Results indicate that the Neural Network achieves an accuracy of 57% on first predictions, rising to 78% when considering the top-two predicted quads. The Ensemble model outperforms with a 96% accuracy, exhibiting consistent classification across all quadrants. The findings highlight the practical potential of ML models to identify economic cycles using asset return behavior. By treating asset returns as early-warning indicators, the study bridges the gap between market signals and delayed macroeconomic statistics, contributing a novel approach to economic state prediction.
Keywords: asset returns | Economic quads | ensemble learning | neural networks

Title: An All-Inclusive CNN-Based Pneumonia Detection Method
Abstract: Particularly in children, elderly, immunocompromised adults, pneumonia, a serious respiratory illness including inflammation of the lung air sacs, still causes a significant health risk in this research report. Both efficient treatment and improvement of patient outcomes depend on a proper diagnosis. Among the traditional diagnostic instruments whose subjective fluctuations could result in misdiagnoses and delayed therapy are clinical tests and chest X-rays. This paper investigates a CNN-based method to increase chest X-ray image pneumonia detection accuracy. We use a dataset of 624 high-resolution X-ray pictures from Kaggle to implement the CNN model under MobileNetV2 architecture. With a fantastic total accuracy of 92.6%, the model achieves outstanding accuracy (91%), recall (94%), and F1-score (92.5%). Design, performance evaluation of CNN models, and training technique expose their ability to differentiate between normal lung states and pneumonia. By automating image processing, lowering diagnosis mistakes, and enhancing clinical decision-making, this approach presents enormous opportunities to assist radiologists. Such developments guarantee excellent healthcare, help to improve world access to healthcare and inspire medical technical innovation. Future work will concentrate on improving CNN architecture, strengthening data augmentation methods, and investigating hybrid models to incrementally improve generalizability and diagnostic accuracy.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | CNN Model | Deep Learning | Model Training | Pneumonia Detection

Title: AI in Art Industry: Will It Be Accepted in Creative Industries and Change the Market?
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) is text, images, and even music-generated content generated by artificial intelligence technology. This innovation has significantly improved efficiency in content production, but it also raises concerns about its potential impact on creativity and the workforce within the creative industries. Many face challenges in understanding and adopting AIGC technologies, fearing that they may disrupt traditional creative processes and risks related to quality and originality. This study aims to evaluate the acceptance of AIGC technology in the Indonesian creative industry. The model framework used is the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), which consists of behavioral intention, performance expectancy, effort expectancy, facilitating condition, and social influence variables. There is also an addition of variables analyzed, such as perceived risk and perceived anxiety. This study analyzes the factors that influence the adoption of AIGC. The author collected data through a survey of creative industry players. Data was collected by distributing online questionnaires, and creative industry players in Indonesia recruited 176 respondents. This study used non-probability sampling techniques, specifically purposive sampling techniques. The data was processed using SMART-PLS3 software to carry out further analysis. The results of this research are expected to provide insight for entities within the creative industry in implementing AIGC technology, as well as increase understanding of the acceptance of AI technology in sectors that depend on creativity.
Keywords: AIGC | Creative Industry | Perceived Anxiety | Perceived Risk | UTAUT

Title: Dysarthric Speech Data Augmentation using Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Both the issue of data scarcity and the problem of class imbalance are factors that hinder the performance of automated dysarthric speech recognition (ADSR) systems. The use of data augmentation allows for the creation of synthetic speech samples, which helps to reduce the effects of data scarcity and class imbalance issues. Traditional statistically-based data augmentation approaches, on the other hand, have shown that ADSR systems have less than satisfactory speech intelligibility and accuracy. The purpose of this study is to provide the augmentation of dysarthric speech data via the use of a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) that maintains the fluctuations in quality, prosodic variations, and intonation across the synthetic samples. The Mel Log Frequency Spectrogram (MFLS) features and the Deep Convolution Neural Network (DCNN) are used in order to verify the results of the system for the DSR. Mean square error (MSE) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) are the metrics that are used to assess the efficacy of the system on the UASpeech dataset. After applying the GAN-based data augmentation, the total PSNR was determined to be 36.59, the MSE was 48.53, and the MAE was 18.24. An enhanced accuracy of 95.2%, recall of 95.2%, precision of 95.7%, net present value of 94.8%, and selectivity of 95.7% were all provided by the DCNN-GAN solution.
Keywords: and speech recognition are some of the terms that are used in this context | component | deep learning | dysarthria | Generative adversarial network | voice pathology

Title: Deep Learning-Based Text-Independent Speaker Verification for Channel and Language Mismatch in Indian Scenarios
Abstract: This work presents an innovative deep neural network-based speaker verification (SV) model. SV is an authentication process that confirms whether a speaker is authorized. Text Independent Speaker Verification identifies who is speaking, not what is being said. India's diverse linguistic and cultural landscape introduces challenges such as dialect and accent variations, multilingualism, multi-speaker scenarios, and varying quality of voice data recorded. Literature hints that the EER of the speaker verification model shoots up if tested with multi-language and multi-channel data; we have used the IITG-MV dataset, which has these variations captured specially for Indian conditions. Currently, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown encouraging results in speaker verification. Our work presents CNN combined with the LSTMs, where CNN is a feed-forward neural network, and LSTMs are a recurrent neural network. The pipeline extracts the acoustic characteristics from the input speech signal using MFCC and fed into models based on deep neural networks like VGG-16. However, the raw speech signal is fed into the SincNet model. The CNN-LSTMs model demonstrates significantly superior accuracy to SincNet and VGG16, making it the most effective approach for text-independent speaker verification in diverse Indian languages and channels. Despite using a basic deep neural network, the results demonstrate the efficiency of our proposed architecture. CNN-LSTM's state-of-the-art performance is closer to that of the ECAPA-TDNN model.
Keywords: aggregation | attention mechanisms | channel attention | propagation | Speaker verification | TDNN

Title: A Novel Approach To Music Genre Classification Through Deep Learning
Abstract: All kinds of music genres are classified into some common categories such as pop, electronic dance music, metal, jazz, blues, country, rock, and hip-hop. The most demanding task in the music information retrieval (MIR) process is organizing different music files based on these genres. Automatic music genre classification is a very important study for music platforms such as Spotify, Wynk, and Saavn that have a great impact in terms of personalized recommendations and offerings. Today's deep learning techniques like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are very successfully applied to a large variety of data by learning and inferring patterns and trends. Different techniques are reviewed for music genre classification using CNN. Further fine-tuning and additional development of VGG16 would help improve classification accuracy by learning complex feature representations of audio spectrograms and being trained on initial datasets. It is indicated that VGG16 is efficient for learning genre-specific patterns and so can serve as a flagship framework for automatic music genre classification. To improve automatic classification of music genres, ResNet-18 with the residual learning architecture was also tried for boosting classification performance in automatic music genre classification. The efficiency with which ResNet-18 can avoid the vanishing gradient problem because of the skip connections further improves the lend of deep architectures and advances automatic classification of music genres.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network | Music Genre Classification | ResNet-18 | Sound Spectrogram Representations | VGG16 Model

Title: Adaptive Mathematics Lesson Planning for Personalized Learning
Abstract: Mathematics is crucial in learning core sciences and resolving everyday problems. However, conventional teaching methods frequently cannot cater to the specific needs of learners, especially in subjects with high complexity levels like mathematics, leading to disengagement and poor performance. This study introduces a machine learning-based adaptive learning system that individualizes learning mathematics using four fundamental components. Collaborative learning is enhanced through hierarchical math lesson preference and peer study prediction, with XGBoost being 88.4% accurate on lesson preference and 85.7% accurate on peer prediction. Cognitive behavior analysis is conducted through gamification with Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) clustering students based on cognitive traits, effectively reducing quantization error under 10,000 iterations. Support Vector Machines (SVMs) are 81.4% accurate for cognition level prediction. Stress detection, using voice and facial expression analysis, is 85.3% accurate, with the stress relieved through music recommendation based on K-Means. Finally, individualized lesson planning is being optimized using classification techniques and obtained over 90% accuracy from SVM. Future work involves real-world deployment and its impact on student achievement.
Keywords: adaptive learning | artificial intelligence | collaborative learning | gamification | mathematics education | personalized learning

Title: Content-Based Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Classical Music Recommendation
Abstract: Indian Classical Music (ICM) is characterized by intricate melodic and rhythmic structures, making its analysis and recommendation a challenging task. Unlike Western music, ICM relies on raga based improvisation, requiring specialized feature extraction techniques for meaningful representation. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning framework combining Convolutional Autoencoders (CAE) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for content-based recommendation ICM. The CAE extracts spectral features from Mel-Spectrograms, while the LSTM learns temporal dependencies to enhance feature representations. The learned embeddings are utilized for music classification (classical vs. non-classical) and recommendation based on cosine similarity of extracted features. Performance is measured using Mean Precision@K and Mean Reciprocal Rank demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed model in retrieving similar classical compositions.
Keywords: Convolutional Autoencoders(CAE) | Cosine Similarity | Indian Classical Music (ICM) | Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) | Mel-Spectrograms

Title: Research on quality detection method of high-performance fiber thin web based on machine vision
Abstract: With the growing demand for nonwoven materials in high-end applications, traditional offline basis-weight measurements interrupt continuous production, and in-line weight-detection systems on carding machines only provide coarse, localized weight profiles (typically at centimeter-scale resolution), and cannot resolve fiber- or pore-level distribution uniformity. This paper proposes an online quality-inspection method for nonwoven fiber webs using machine vision and deep learning. High-resolution images captured on a bespoke inspection platform are preprocessed via wavelet transforms and image-enhancement techniques. A convolutional neural network regression model then estimates web basis weight in real time. To quantify fiber-distribution uniformity, this paper introduces a porosity-based metric and demonstrates that its coefficient of variation (CV) correlates strongly with the CV of measured web basis weight. The proposed approach delivers data-driven support for real-time adjustment of carding-machine process parameters, thereby overcoming the technical challenge of online uniformity monitoring in high-end nonwoven fabric production.
Keywords: deep learning | fiber distribution uniformity | machine vision | Nonwoven | porosity | weight estimation

Title: Predicting the rapid progression of coronary artery lesions in patients with acute coronary syndrome based on machine learning
Abstract: Purposes: Rapid coronary artery lesions (RCAL) are strongly linked to major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This work developed a public online prediction platform for RCAL (OpRCAL) by comparing the performance of nine machine learning models. Methods: We retrospectively examined the clinical data of 324 patients with ACS who received percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Using both univariate and multivariate analyses, the potential independent risk factors for RCAL were studied. Following the screening of all variables using Lasso regression, multiple machine learning models were constructed. The optimal model was then chosen and validated using an external cohort. Furthermore, to elucidate the contribution of each feature to the model, the shapley additive explanation (SHAP) values of the variables were calculated. Finally, a prediction platform for RCAL in patients with ACS following PCI was established. Results: The number of coronary lesions, systolic blood pressure (SBP), N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), QRS interval, and platelet count were found as independent risk factors for RCAL. Among the nine machine learning models constructed after identifying twelve different variables using Lasso regression, the random forest (RF) model performed best in the training cohort and showed good generalization in the external test cohort, with area under curve of 0.774 (95%CI: 0.640–0.909). Finally, we constructed an online platform named OpRCAL for clinicians to predict RCAL in patients with ACS following PCI based on the RF model. Conclusions: The RF model exhibits high accuracy and generalizability in predicting RCAL, thereby providing a valuable instrument to assist clinical decision-making.
Keywords: acute coronary syndrome | machine learning | PCI | random forest | rapid progression

Title: AIoT-Driven Harmonic Lifecycle Assessment and Predictive Analytics for Green Music Production Supply Chain Systems
Abstract: —Traditional carbon footprint measurement approaches fail to address the unique requirements of green music production, where conventional lifecycle assessment methods cannot accommodate the dual imperatives of environmental impact reduction and acoustic performance preservation. Existing carbon accounting frameworks lack the granularity to capture real-time operational variations in creative environments, while standard IoT monitoring systems ignore the acoustic signatures that indicate both energy efficiency and production quality. This article introduces harmonic music carbon assessment and prediction (HMCAP), a novel dual-phase methodology that harmonizes environmental impact assessment with acoustic performance requirements throughout green music production supply chains. The first phase divides the music production supply chain into five distinct stages and develops corresponding measurement models enhanced with acoustic-sensitive AIoT sensor networks, enabling quantitative carbon footprint evaluation across raw materials, manufacturing, distribution, usage, and end-of-life (EOL) stages. The second phase constructs a long short-term memory (LSTM) networks-based prediction framework with parallel processing pathways for acoustic and energy features, creating a specialized carbon emission forecasting system for green music production environments. We validated our approach using two years of operational data from a leading music equipment manufacturer and showed a 99.4% prediction accuracy. Implementation resulted in 14.6% carbon intensity reduction across manufacturing operations and 22.3% decrease in recording session emissions, with 92% of artists reporting no perceptible quality difference—confirming HMCAP’s capacity to balance sustainability with creative excellence in green music production.
Keywords: AI-based IoT | carbon footprint | lifecycle assessment | long short-term memory (LSTM) networks | music production supply chain

Title: hERG-MFFGNN: An Explainable Deep Learning Model for Predicting Cardiotoxicity Using Multi-feature Fusion and Graph Neural Networks
Abstract: Drug-related cardiotoxicity, most notably arrhythmia, represents a major challenge in drug development. Inhibition of hERG potassium channel by certain compounds has the potential to delay cardiac repolarization, manifested as QT interval prolongation, thereby elevating the risk of severe cardiac arrhythmias like torsades de pointes (TdP). Accurate assessment of compounds’ impact on hERG channels is crucial. Traditional methods are costly and inefficient for large-scale screening. Therefore, developing efficient and accurate computational methods for hERG inhibition prediction is critical. In this study, we present a deep learning framework, named hERG-MFFGNN, aimed at accurately predicting hERG channel blockers while providing model interpretability. To improve both accuracy and generalizability, we implement a multi-feature fusion strategy that systematically integrates molecular structural information. Initially, multiple molecular fingerprint features and molecular descriptors are fused to construct an initial feature representation. Then, graph neural networks are used to extract molecular topological features. These two sets of features are weighted and fused using an attention mechanism to form the final compound representation, enabling a more comprehensive expression of molecular features. The performance of hERG-MFFGNN is assessed using fivefold cross-validation on the benchmark dataset and external validation datasets. The results demonstrate that hERG-MFFGNN achieves AUROC of 0.909 and ACC of 0.854, highlighting its robust predictive capabilities for hERG activity across diverse datasets. We believe that may function as an effective instrument for the early prediction of hERG channel blockers in the phases of drug discovery and development. The complete source code is publicly accessible at https://github.com/zhaoqi106/hERG-MFFGNN.
Keywords: Cardiotoxicity | Deep learning | Graph neural network | Multi feature fusion

Title: A Map-Free Deep Learning-Based Framework for Gate-to-Gate Monocular Visual Navigation Aboard Miniaturized Aerial Vehicles
Abstract: Palm-sized autonomous nano-drones, i.e., sub-50 g in weight, recently entered the drone racing scenario, where they are tasked to avoid obstacles and navigate as fast as possible through gates. However, in contrast with their bigger counterparts, i.e., kg-scale drones, nano-drones expose three orders of magnitude less onboard memory and compute power, demanding more efficient and lightweight vision-based pipelines to win the race. This work presents a map-free vision-based (using only a monocular camera) autonomous nano-drone that combines a real-time deep learning gate detection front-end with a classic yet elegant and effective visual servoing control back-end, only relying on onboard resources. Starting from two state-of-the-art tiny deep learning models, we adapt them for our specific task, and after a mixed simulator-real-world training, we integrate and deploy them aboard our nano-drone. Our best-performing pipeline costs of only 24 M multiply-accumulate operations per frame, resulting in a closed-loop control performance of 30 Hz, while achieving a gate detection root mean square error of 1.4 pixels, on our ∼20 k real-world image dataset. In-field experiments highlight the capability of our nano-drone to successfully navigate through 15 gates in 4 min, never crashing and covering a total travel distance of ∼ 100 m, with a peak flight speed of 1.9 m/s. Finally, to stress the generalization capability of our system, we also test it in a never-seen-before environment, where it navigates through gates for more than 4 min.

Title: Bypassing Audio reCAPTCHA with Automatic Speech Recognition Models
Abstract: CAPTCHAs are challenges designed to distinguish humans from automated bots. However, with the growing capabilities of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models, these challenges are increasingly vulnerable to automated resolution. In this paper, we evaluate the feasibility of bypassing the audio versions of CAPTCHAs. We automate the collection and transcription of Google audio CAPTCHAs and compare the performance of several models, including Google Speech-to-text, DeepSpeeach, Whisper, Azure AI Speech, and Deepgram, focusing on accuracy, speed, and cost. The performance results highlight how easily audio CAPTCHAs can be bypassed, in one second for the fastest methods. We also discuss possible countermeasures that could be deployed. We make all collected audio files and results available to the community at: https://gitlab.com/lepolodiou/data-set-bypass-audio-captcha.
Keywords: Audio reCAPTCHA | Automatic Speech Recognition | Whisper

Title: An Interpretable Framework for Stock Market Forecasting Using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Networks with SHAP - Explainable AI (XAI) Method
Abstract: Predicting stock market movements is a challenging and ever-changing process because it is by a variety of unpredictable elements. In this study, we explore the use of deep learning, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, to estimate the upcoming stock prices of HDFC Bank. The training process of the model utilizes past stock closing prices to learn patterns and make future predictions from 2020 to 2025, sourced from Yahoo Finance. The time series data is preprocessed using normalization techniques, and sequences of past observations are structured to train the LSTM architecture effectively. To make the model's predictions easier to understand and explain, Explainable AI methods, particularly SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), are employed. The proposed model demonstrates strong predictive performance, achieving a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.0246, indicating that the average difference between the predicted and actual values is quite low. Additionally, the R<sup>2</sup> (coefficient of determination) score was 0.9489, suggesting that approximately 94.89% of the variability in the actual values is explained by the model's predictions. These results highlight the model's capability to accurately capture trends in stock price movement while also providing valuable insights into feature contributions. Unlike traditional statistical models, LSTM networks can retain long-term dependencies, enabling them to detect time-based patterns effectively. The integration of explainability not only adds transparency to the predictions but also enhances the trustworthiness of the model in real-world applications. Furthermore, this approach can be adapted to other financial instruments or extended with external indicators for broader market analysis. The combination of LSTM and SHAP enables a robust, interpretable framework for stock market forecasting that supports data-driven investment strategies.
Keywords: Explainable AI | Long Short-Term Memory | Quality | Root Mean Squared Error

Title: Towards Intelligent Home Monitoring: A CNN Framework for Environmental Sound Event Detection
Abstract: Environmental sound recognition is an active area of research within the broader field of machine listening, yet most existing studies have primarily focused on speech and music domains. This paper proposes a framework for a home-based machine listening system capable of detecting and classifying non-speech environmental sound events using deep learning techniques. The system leverages a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture alongside Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) for feature extraction, enabling a robust representation of audio signals captured in typical household environments. A dataset composed of 2,000 five-second audio samples, spanning 50 different sound classes commonly found in home settings, was used to train and evaluate the model. These classes include a diverse range of domestic, animal, and other external sounds. The CNN was implemented with a sequential model incorporating convolutional, pooling, and dropout layers to improve generalization and reduce overfitting. The model achieved an average accuracy of 73% using five-fold cross-validation, demonstrating promising performance in classifying real-world environmental audio. The proposed framework has potential applications in intelligent home monitoring, particularly for safety, security, and emergency scenarios where visual systems alone may be insufficient. Additionally, a graphical user interface (GUI) was developed to support live recognition, and monitoring of sound events in real time. Future work will explore multi-audio input, real-time system deployment, and enhanced classification using additional acoustic features.
Keywords: acoustic monitoring | audio signal processing | convolutional neural network (CNN) | deep learning | feature extraction | machine listening | smart home systems | sound event detection

Title: Machine Learning-Optimized Design of 3D-Printed Cylindrical Luneburg Lenses
Abstract: Designing a Luneburg lens is challenging due to its radially graded permittivity, which introduces fabrication complexity, material constraints, bandwidth limitations, and high costs. This work presents a machine learning-optimized 3D-printed multishell Luneburg lens using air voids in polylactic acid (PLA) to emulate ideal performance. A cylindrical prototype with a 100 mm diameter and 30 mm thickness is designed for X-band operation, closely matching the performance of a near-ideal 1000-shell lens. The proposed method provides a cost-effective and practical solution for high-performance antenna lenses, overcoming traditional manufacturing limitations.
Keywords: Effective Refractive Index | GRIN | Luneburg lens antenna | ML | Parallel EM Waves | TIR

Title: eHealth literacy and attitudes towards use of artificial intelligence among university students in the United Arab Emirates, a cross-sectional study
Abstract: Introduction: With the rapid digitalization of healthcare information and the increasing dependability on online health resources, it has become crucial to understand digital health literacy and the use of emerging AI technologies like ChatGPT among stakeholders. This is of particular importance in the United Arab Emirates which has the highest internet penetration rates. Method: This study aimed to assess eHealth literacy and the factors influencing it among university students in the United Arab Emirates. Their attitudes towards ChatGPT use were also explored. Data from participants, studying in the public universities of UAE, was collected between April–July 2024 using eHEALS and TAME Chat GPT instruments. Results: Results indicated a mean eHealth literacy score of 29.3 out of 40, with higher scores among females and those in health–related disciplines. It was also found that students with higher eHealth literacy perceived ChatGPT as more useful in healthcare, despite their concerns about its risks and potential to replace healthcare professionals. Discussion: The findings from the study underscore the need of development of tailored digital health curricula, to enhance eHealth literacy particularly in subgroups showing lower literacy scores. Moreover, it is also imperative to develop guidelines for responsible and ethical AI use in health information seeking.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | chatGPT | eHealth literacy | healthcare | higher education | United Arab Emirates

Title: Text-and-timbre-based speech semantic coding for ultra-low-bitrate communications
Abstract: To address the contradiction between the explosive growth of wireless data and the limited spectrum resources, semantic communication has been emerging as a promising communication paradigm. In this paper, we thus design a speech semantic coded communication system, referred to as Deep-STS (i.e., Deep-learning based Speech To Speech), for the low-bandwidth speech communication. Specifically, we first deeply compress the speech data through extracting the textual information from the speech based on the conformer encoder and connectionist temporal classification decoder at the transmitter side of Deep-STS system. In order to facilitate the final speech timbre recovery, we also extract the short-term timbre feature of speech signals only for the starting 2s duration by the long short-term memory network. Then, the Reed-Solomon coding and hybrid automatic repeat request protocol are applied to improve the reliability of transmitting the extracted text and timbre feature over the wireless channel. Third, we reconstruct the speech signal by the mel spectrogram prediction network and vocoder, when the extracted text is received along with the timbre feature at the receiver of Deep-STS system. Finally, we develop the demo system based on the USRP and GNU radio for the performance evaluation of Deep-STS. Numerical results show that the accuracy of text extraction approaches 95%, and the mel cepstral distortion between the recovered speech signal and the original one in the spectrum domain is less than 10. Furthermore, the experimental results show that the proposed Deep-STS system can reduce the total delay of speech communication by 85% on average compared to the G.723 coding at the transmission rate of 5.4 kbps. More importantly, the coding rate of the proposed Deep-STS system is extremely low, only 0.2 kbps for continuous speech communication. It is worth noting that the Deep-STS with lower coding rate can support the low-zero-power speech communication, unveiling a new era in ultra-efficient coded communications.
Keywords: low coding rate | semantic communication | speech recognition | speech synthesis

Title: Choral harmony: the role of collective singing in ritual, cultural identity and cognitive-affective synchronisation in the age of AI
Abstract: Purpose: This study examines how choral singing functions as a mechanism for sustaining ritual practice and reinforcing cultural identity. By integrating perspectives from musicology, social psychology, and cognitive science, it explores how collective vocal performance supports emotional attunement, group cohesion, and symbolic memory in culturally diverse contexts. Materials and Methods: A mixed-methods approach was applied, combining ethnographic observation, survey-based data, and cognitive measures with AI-informed frameworks such as voice emotion recognition and neural synchrony modeling. Case studies included Anglican cathedral choirs, Tibetan Buddhist chant groups, and Indigenous community choirs in Northern Canada. Results: Findings demonstrate that choral structures—such as harmonic entrainment and rhythmic alignment—foster affective convergence, enhance psychological resilience, and strengthen group synchrony. Participation in choir singing was also shown to increase self–other overlap and reinforce cultural continuity across traditions. Conclusions: The study affirms choral singing as both a symbolic and embodied practice of shared identity in the algorithmic era. It highlights the potential for AI-informed feedback systems to contribute to participatory music education and communal healing, providing a theoretical foundation and data reference for future interdisciplinary applications.
Keywords: affective synchrony | AI-enhanced ethnomusicology | Choral singing | cultural identity | neuropsychology of music | ritual cognition

Title: A Lightweight Network Architecture for Enhanced Music Recommendation
Abstract: Music recommendation systems (MRS) have improved the listening experience for many users by offering personalized suggestions, enhancing their mood, and increasing productivity. Machine learning (ML) techniques are powerful tools in deciphering user preferences, and MRS were able to offer users personally tailored suggestions. MRS needs to be installed on handy devices like mobiles thus the recommendation models need to be lightweight. This research introduces a new lightweight neural network architecture, the 3-Layer Dense Neural Network (3DLNN), which is optimized for efficient and precise music recommendations. For evaluation, its effectiveness was compared with traditional techniques such as Content-Based Filtering (CBF), Collaborative Filtering (CF), Context Filtering, and Hybrid Systems. Using the Free Music Archive (FMA) dataset, a database containing over 100,000 audio tracks with extensive metadata, the results show the 3DLNN's superiority in terms of precision (0.8), F1-score (0.889), and RMSE (6.462). The model was superior to the others in ranking accuracy and error minimization and outperformed all other methods, while CBF had the lowest performance, with a precision of 0.4 and F1-score of 0.571. Findings indicate that 3DLNN is a strong and scalable framework for music recommendation systems for the next generation and enable new ways toward adaptive neural network-based personalization.
Keywords: Content-Based Filtering | Deep Neural Networks | Hybrid Systems | Machine Learning | Music Recommendation Systems

Title: Indian sign language to voice using ESP32_Cam for hand tracking and MediaPipe for hand gesture detection
Abstract: Communication gaps experienced by people with hearing and speech disabilities continue to be a major issue in the modern world, particularly when communicating with people who are not familiar with sign language to bridge this gap, this study introduces a real-time Indian Sign Language (ISL) to Voice translation system based on an ESP32-CAM module for capturing hand gestures and Media-Pipe for precise hand landmark detection and gesture recognition. The system identifies ISL alphabets and numbers using effective hand tracking and gesture segmentation, providing smooth conversion of sign language to text as well as synthesized speech output. Media-Pipe's hand tracking improves the precision of gesture recognition by capturing 21 critical hand landmarks while a light machine learning model determines the gestures. The identified text is then converted to voice with the help of text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis, enabling clear communication for the hearing and speech-impaired. Differing from conventional systems depending on heavy hardware or being confined to English speech, this project focuses on an embedded, cost-effective solution via ESP32-CAM, thereby being portable. In addition, the flexibility in the system will enable future enhancement for multilingual, even regional languages such as Malayalam, to extend inclusivity. This paper describes the architecture, implementation, and experimental performance of the system, showing its efficiency and accuracy in real-time ISL gesture recognition and voice generation. The system proposed here has great potential in filling the communication gaps, enabling independence and social inclusion of hearing and speech disabled individuals.
Keywords: ESP32-CAM | Hand Gesture Recognition | Indian Sign Language (ISL) | Machine Learning | Media-Pipe | Random Forest | Text-to-Speech (TTS)

Title: Deep Learning Techniques for Voice Disorder Detection: A Transfer Learning and Data Augmentation Approach
Abstract: Voice disorders are among the most prevalent problems affecting a huge proportion of the population, with the majority of them resulting in communication issues and a deterioration in quality of life. Early detection leads to more effective treatment. Thus, better approaches for accurately diagnosing vocal abnormalities are essential. Machine learning techniques such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Random Forests, and transfer learning approaches have all proven useful in this discipline. CNNs offer incredible audio signal processing capabilities, since they can convert raw voice data into spectrograms and automatically extract key properties. CNNs can detect minor patterns associated with numerous voice disorders, improving classification accuracy. Random Forest is a technique used in ensemble learning to enhance robustness and accuracy in classification tasks. The utility of this approach stems from its capacity to overcome existing data processing issues, making it a substantial contribution to the area. Thus, we propose the system with CNN and Random Forest as the classification models and obtained the 97.31% accuracy for transfer learning model.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) | Random Forest | Transfer Learning | Voice Disorder | well-being

Title: AI-Powered Smart Glasses for Real-Time Speech-to-Text Transcription
Abstract: This project introduces AI-powered smart glasses designed to enhance real-time communication and accessibility through speech-to-text transcription. Utilizing an ESP32 microcontroller, a microphone, and a compact OLED display, the system provides live transcription of spoken language, displayed within the user's field of vision. The solution employs a Flutter-based application leveraging the Flutter Speech-to-Text API for accurate and efficient transcription, optimized for low latency. Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) ensures seamless connectivity with a smartphone, which processes the data while keeping the hardware lightweight. These smart glasses have broad applications, from assisting individuals with hearing impairments to facilitating conversations in diverse environments.
Keywords: Accessibility | AI-Driven Design System | Real-Time Transcription | Speech-to-Text | Wearable Technology

Title: RTrans-D3Net: Music Source Separation with Multi-Dilated Convolutions and Transformer
Abstract: Music source separation aims to isolate individual sound sources from mixed music signals. To address this task, we propose a novel deep learning model, RTransD3Net. The model is based on an encoder-decoder architecture and innovatively integrates D3 Block, Res Path, and Transformer modules to overcome the limitations of existing methods, such as restricted receptive fields, feature semantic gaps, and insufficient long-term dependency modeling. Specifically, the D3 Block expands the receptive field and avoids aliasing effects through densely connected multi-dilated convolutions; Res Path reduces feature discrepancies between the encoder and decoder by introducing convolutional layers; and the Transformer module embedded in the bottleneck enhances long-term contextual modeling capabilities. Experiments on the MUSDB18 dataset demonstrate that RTrans-D3Net achieves an average SDR of 6.09 dB, outperforming some existing time-domain and frequency-domain separation methods in terms of separation performance.
Keywords: DenseNet | Frequency-Domain Modeling | Music source separation | Transformer

Title: A Novel Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Early Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease Using MRI Data
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a chronic brain disorder that affects neurons resulting in a decline in cognitive abilities; timely and accurate diagnosis of AD has a significant impact on delaying its progress and enhancing patient management. Old-fashioned, clinical or and or neuropsychological assessment procedures are inadequate and lack the efficiency of early diagnosis. This study aims at highlighting an innovative deep learning model to diagnose AD in its early stages based on MRI data. This model combines both the CNNs for the spatial feature extraction as well as the RNNs for the temporal sequence learning. The model was trained using images from open access datasets, and the results show a high increase in the performance as compared to conventional methods. The model is significantly more sensitive, specific, and accurate than current methods in correctly classifying cell-metastasis levels based on gene expression patterns. It also achieves good results in different stages of CKD, thereby proving the model's practicality. Such studies may be useful for the creation of new effective diagnostic instruments to support the physicians in the early identification of Alzheimer's disease.
Keywords: Alzheimer's disease | cognitive decline | convolutional neural networks | diagnostic accuracy | disease progression | early diagnosis | hybrid deep learning | machine learning | MRI | neural networks | neurodegenerative disorder | recurrent neural networks

Title: Multimodal Emotion Recognition with Balanced Audio and Video Feature Extraction Under Text Modality Residuals
Abstract: With the rise of social media and digital communication, sentiment analysis has become an important part of artificial intelligence. In this paper, we study the problems of insufficient inter-modal correlation and inefficient feature extraction in multimodal sentiment recognition. Based on the self-MM model and combining with the attention mechanism, we propose a model named VAMM-FQM, which deepens the correlation between the two modalities through the self-attention mechanism and improves the model efficiency through the feedback mechanism. The performance of this model is improved by about 5% over the original model, and the correlation is improved by more than two times. Next, by optimising the feature extraction part and replacing the sLSTM method with EfficientNet and Wav2vec 2.0 for the visual and audio parts of the feature extraction, respectively, a model called VAMM-WE is proposed, which ensures that detailed features of both domains can be captured. In addition, Transformer is used as a decision-level fusion operator to facilitate information exchange between the two modalities, achieving a significant error rate reduction. Compared to the original model, the new model reduced the error rate by 60% on each dataset.
Keywords: deep learning | feature fusion | multimodal sentiment analysis

Title: Towards Sustainable Oceans: Deep Learning for Plastic Detection in Subaquatic Environment
Abstract: Marine biodiversity and the health of the environment worldwide are seriously threatened by the fast buildup of plastic garbage in aquatic environments. The use of automated solutions is required since traditional techniques for identifying plastic waste under water are time-consuming and not scalable. Advanced sensor and computing capabilities on Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) are making them essential instruments for detecting underwater garbage. Deep learning arose as a key component of these automated systems due to its exceptional performance in image identification tasks. While U-Net and DeepLab are excellent in segmenting plastic debris at the pixel level, models like YOLOv8m, YOLOv8n, YOLOv8s and SSD are being used in our work for real-time object identification. These models use strong feature extraction and data augmentation strategies to tackle underwater obstacles, such as low visibility and changing surroundings. Metrics like Precision, Accuracy, F1-Score, and Recall are considered to assess performance and provide information on the correctness and dependability of the model. Real-time mapping, monitoring, and intervention in marine settings are ensured by integrating these technologies with AUVs. This study establishes the foundation for sustainable marine ecosystem management and highlights the abilities of deep learning to transform detection plastic waste in underwater.
Keywords: deep learning | environmental monitoring | marine pollution | SSD | underwater plastic detection | YOLOv8

Title: Advancing Low-Resource Urdu Speech Emotion Recognition: Employing Deep Learning with Unidirectional and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units on Mel-Spectrogram Acoustic Features
Abstract: In the growing field of artificial intelligence, identifying emotions in Urdu speech presents distinct challenges. This work adopts a novel approach using unidirectional (Uni-GRU) and bidirectional (Bi-GRU) gated recurrent units to examine the acoustic characteristics of the Mel-spectrogram for emotion classification. We propose a speech emotion recognition (SER) method based on these specific recurrent neural network architectures. Initially, the Uni-GRU model processed the Melspectrogram and effectively captured emotional patterns in URDU dataset samples, achieving 98.33% training accuracy, 75.00% validation accuracy, and 81.25% testing accuracy. Subsequently, the enhanced Bi-GRU model surpassed the Uni-GRU by more accurately identifying complex emotions, attaining a training accuracy of 98.75%, validation accuracy of 78.75%, and testing accuracy of 87.50%. Our evaluation on a representative Urdu corpus shows that GRU-based models substantially improve SER performance. This modeling strategy highlights the advantages of using Uni-GRU and Bi-GRU architectures with Mel-spectrogram features, offering insights into emotion recognition in low-resource languages. The findings demonstrate the potential of deep learning to support speech processing in underrepresented linguistic contexts and lay the groundwork for extending SER applications across a broader range of language environments.
Keywords: Bi-GRU Model | Low-Resourced Language Processing | Mel-Spectrogram Analysis | Urdu Speech Emotion Recognition

Title: Intelligent Inspection System for Optical Lens Surface
Abstract: Defect detection in optical lenses is challenging due to reflections, surface curvature, and the low contrast of defects. This study presents an intelligent inspection system for optical lens surface defects with four main steps. Firstly, a customizable imaging acquisition system is proposed to enhance defect visibility by capturing multiple frames of optical lens under static and dynamic lighting conditions. By applying frame averaging, unwanted lighting reflections are minimized while preserving the defect structure. Second, an adaptive energy-based algorithm is proposed for efficient defect detection. Third, a novel hybrid wavelet-gradient processing-based multi-stage defect enhancement algorithm is proposed to highlight defect details. Finally, deep learning models (VGG16, etc) are used to classify five types of defects accurately. Experimental validation on 40 optical lens samples demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed method in defect detection and classification, significantly improving the automated optical inspection process and quality management.
Keywords: adaptive energy analysis | classification | Defect detection | frame averaging | wavelet transform

Title: Analysis and Reconstruction of Laryngectomised Speech using GAN Models
Abstract: Communication through whispering is crucial for individuals who have undergone laryngectomy, a surgical procedure involving the partial or total removal of the voice box or larynx. Whispering, which lacks fundamental frequency, often results in hushed and unintelligible speech for these patients, necessitating prosthetics or treatments. These treatments pose a risk of getting infections, and the resulting speech sounds unnatural.Recently, in a computational framework, deep learning-based methods have been developed for a whisper-to-speech conversion that could be useful for laryngectomy patients as well. In this paper, we analyse GAN-based methods for the reconstruction of laryngectomised speech, using a laryngectomy dataset that we collected in New Zealand. Based on this analysis, we propose modified architectures and loss functions specifically tailored to laryngectomy patients. The proposed models are trained on both the wTIMIT and laryngectomy patient datasets. Evaluations show improved performance in both spectral features and speech intelligibility compared to existing models.
Keywords: Deep Learning | GAN | Laryngectomy | Speech Reconstruction

Title: A Machine Learning based Approch to Classify Emotions from Music
Abstract: Music has the profound ability to evoke a wide spectrum of emotions, from joy and excitement to sadness and melancholy. A vital field of study with uses in advertising, film soundtracks, music therapy, and emotional analysis, emotion classification in music is the identification and classification of these emotional reactions. This work investigates how machine learning methods might precisely categorize musical emotions into happy, sad, calm, and energetic groups. Key audio features including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), spectral contrast, and rhythm-based characteristics are the main emphasis of the feature extracting process. We apply Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM) among other supervised machine learning techniques to assess classification performance. Cross-valuation guarantees model dependability; performance is measured with accuracy, F1-score, recall, and precision. Experimental findings show that the suggested method provides a strong basis for emotional-based music analysis since it efficiently labels music files with great accuracy.
Keywords: Emotions | Machine Learning Algorithm | Music classification | Music files | Subjective Tests

Title: A Duoethnographic Study of Writing-With as a Mode of EFL Teacher Professional Development Practice in the Age of AI
Abstract: As digital tools become increasingly embedded in teacher professional development (TPD), teacher reflection is often mediated by institutional platforms, algorithmic suggestions, and artificial intelligence–assisted tools. This study explores how Writing-With, a self-developed stance toward dialogic teacher reflection, can reorient these tools from instruments of compliance into spaces of co-presence and ethical inquiry. Through a duoethnographic exchange, the authors reflect on three episodes involving learning management systems, teacher use of ChatGPT, and platform-based feedback. The duoethnographic exchange surfaced emotional labor, pedagogical ambivalence, and moments where digital tools both constrained and provoked insight. Rather than positioning technology as inherently limiting or liberating, the study shows how Writing-With enabled dwelling in dissonance, reclaiming teacher judgment, and reframing feedback as a relational practice. Findings suggest that Writing-With supports a form of TPD grounded not in performance metrics, but in mutual noticing, ethical presence, and care.
Keywords: CALL-Mediated Professional Development | Dialogic Pedagogy | Duoethnography | Teacher Reflection | Writing-With

Title: Operationalising the definition of general-purpose AI: assessing four approaches
Abstract: The European Union’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act is set to be a landmark legal instrument for regulating AI technology. While stakeholders have primarily focused on fixed-purpose AI applications (also known as narrow AI), more attention is required to understand the nature and regulatory implications of highly and broadly capable systems. During the AI Act policymaking process, several definitions for general-purpose AI (GPAI) were considered, each attempting to distinguish between systems with and without a fixed purpose. This distinction is crucial, as it influences the allocation of regulatory obligations. In this article, we operationalise these differences through the concept of ‘distinct tasks’ and examine four approaches (quantity, performance, adaptability, and emergence) to determine whether an AI system should be classified as a GPAI. We suggest that EU stakeholders use the four approaches as a starting point to discriminate between fixed-purpose AI and GPAI.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | European Union | general purpose AI | technology risk management

Title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of Music's Physiological Effects Using Muse2 Heart Rate, Mind Calm, and Stillness
Abstract: The use of music therapy has shown results in improving both physiological and psychological health. In this research, we applied deep learning methods to forecast how calming music affects individuals. Our study involved creating a model using a dense neural network (DNN) to analyze data collected from a Muse2 device, which tracks metrics like heart rate, mind calm, and stillness before and after listening to music. By utilizing the TensorFlow and Keras frameworks, we processed time series data to explore the impact of music therapy on these responses. Our discoveries demonstrate that soothing music significantly reduces heart rate and improves calmness and stillness scores. We developed a structured data processing and analysis pipeline, including careful data preprocessing, dense neural network (DNN) model design, and rigorous performance evaluation. We established an approach for predicting shifts in these Muse2-tracked metrics following music therapy sessions. This study contributes to crafting settings that can enhance overall well-being with potential applications in fields such as psychology, medicine, and consumer electronics. By bridging theory with application, our research lays the foundation for targeted and efficient use of music-based interventions aimed at promoting relaxation and better health through specific physiological and mental indicators.
Keywords: Brain Sensing | Deep Learning | Heart Rate | Machine Learning | Mind Calm | Muse2 | Music | Neural Network | Regression | Relaxation | Relaxing | Stillness

Title: SyntheticPop: Attacking Speaker Verification Systems With Synthetic VoicePops
Abstract: Voice Authentication (VA), also known as Automatic Speaker Verification (ASV), is a widely adopted authentication method, particularly in automated systems like banking services, where it serves as a secondary layer of user authentication. Despite its popularity, VA systems are vulnerable to various attacks, including replay, impersonation, and the emerging threat of deepfake audio that mimics the voice of legitimate users. To mitigate these risks, several defense mechanisms have been proposed. One such solution, 'Voice Pops', aims to distinguish an individual's unique phoneme pronunciations during the enrollment process. While promising, the effectiveness of VA+VoicePop against a broader range of attacks, particularly logical or adversarial attacks, remains insufficiently explored. We propose a novel attack method, which we refer to as SyntheticPop, designed to target the phoneme recognition capabilities of the VA+VoicePop system. The SyntheticPop attack involves embedding synthetic 'pop' noises into spoofed audio samples, significantly degrading the model's performance. We achieve an attack success rate of over 95% while poisoning 20% of the training dataset. Our experiments demonstrate that VA+VoicePop achieves 69% accuracy under normal conditions, 37% accuracy when subjected to a baseline label flipping attack, and just 14% accuracy under our proposed SyntheticPop attack, emphasizing the effectiveness of our method.
Keywords: audio synthesis | automated speaker verification | biometrics | data poisoning | deepfake audio | machine learning | replay attack | spoofing | voice authentication

Title: Optimizing Neural Architectures for Hindi Speech Separation and Enhancement in Noisy Environments
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of Hindi speech separation and enhancement using advanced neural network architectures, with a focus on edge devices. We propose a refined approach leveraging the DEMUCS model to overcome limitations of traditional methods, achieving substantial improvements in speech clarity and intelligibility. The model is fine-tuned with U-Net and LSTM layers, trained on a dataset of 400,000 Hindi speech clips augmented with ESC-50 and MS-SNSD for diverse acoustic environments. Evaluation using PESQ and STOI metrics shows superior performance, particularly under extreme noise conditions. To ensure deployment on resource-constrained devices like TWS earbuds, we explore quantization techniques to reduce computational requirements. This research highlights the effectiveness of customized AI algorithms for speech processing in Indian contexts and suggests future directions for optimizing edge-based architectures.

Title: Sarcasm Detection using Bert Embeddings and Hybrid LSTM-CNN Architecture
Abstract: Irony, a prevalent literary device, often appears in online writings and dialogues, complicating sentiment analysis. Sentiment analysis seeks to ascertain the emotional tone of a digital test-positive, negative, or neutral, rendering it an effective instrument for comprehending individuals' ideas and feelings in settings such as social media, reviews, and emails. This research concentrates on identifying irony in text via the use of breakthroughs in Natural Language Processing. We present a hybrid model that integrates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to assess, store, and identify irony in phrases. Furthermore, we use BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) for pre-training, augmenting the model's capacity to comprehend contextual linkages. Our results indicate that sarcasm detection markedly improves with the presence of contextual similarity across phases, underscoring the importance of linguistic and emotional subtleties. The model's performance, with an accuracy of 0.7750, highlights its applicability in sentiment analysis across various datasets. These observations have ramifications for improving automated text comprehension in areas such as consumer feedback, social media analysis, and conversational artificial intelligence.
Keywords: BERT | CNN | Deep Learning | Hybrid Architecture | LSTM | Sarcasm Detection

Title: Comparative Study of the Working of Various AI Classifiers for Identifying Ragas of Indian Classical Music
Abstract: Music is an art of melody and sound. Classical music provides a framework for creating melodies and musical compositions. The most popular methods are Western classical music and Indian Classical Music (ICM). In ICM, the melodic pattern is called a Raga. Each Raga is classified based on the notes present, the order of the notes and the emotion (Rasa). Identifying a Raga is necessary for various music analyses. The objective of this research paper is to conduct a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) specifically to compare the working and performance of all the classifiers used in AI models proposed in previous research. The work involves a systematic literature review and a meta-analysis of all the AI classifier models used in ICM Raga Identification. The purpose of this study is to provide knowledge of the best performing AI classifier in Raga identification of ICM. The detailed analysis indicates that the model using Time Delay Neural Network (TDNN) displays the best performance over a large data set. This classifier can be considered for all further studies involving Raga identification which still in its nascent stage of research.
Keywords: Indian Classical Music | Notes | Raga | Rasa | Systematic Literature Review | Time Delay Neural Network

Title: CoPlay: Audio-agnostic Cognitive Scaling for Acoustic Sensing
Abstract: Acoustic sensing manifests great potential in various applications like health monitoring, gesture interface, by utilizing built-in speakers and microphones on smart devices. However, in ongoing research and development, one problem is often overlooked: the same speaker, when used concurrently for sensing and other traditional audio tasks (like playing music), could cause interference in both, making it impractical to use. The strong ultrasonic sensing signals mixed with music would overload the speaker's mixer. To confront this issue of overloaded signals, current solutions are clipping or down-scaling, both of which affect the music playback quality, sensing range, and accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose CoPlay, a deep learning-based optimization algorithm to cognitively adapt the sensing signal and run in real-time. It can 1) maximize the sensing signal magnitude within the available bandwidth left by the concurrent music to optimize sensing range and accuracy and 2) minimize any consequential frequency distortion that can affect music playback. We design a custom model and test it on common types of sensing signals (sine wave or Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave FMCW) as inputs alongside various agnostic types of concurrent music and speech. First, we micro-benchmark the model performance to show the quality of the generated signals. Secondly, we conducted 2 field studies of downstream acoustic sensing tasks on 2 devices in the real world. A study with 12 users proved that respiration monitoring and gesture recognition using our adapted signal achieve similar accuracy as no-concurrent-music scenarios, whereas baseline methods of clipping or down-scaling manifest worse accuracy. A qualitative study also justifies that CoPlay leaves music untouched, unlike clipping or down-scaling that degrade music quality.
Keywords: acoustic sensing | audio generation | wireless perception

Title: Machine Learning Based Caloric Expenditure Prediction for Personalized Exercise Soundtracks
Abstract: In today's world, with a growing awareness of maintaining a healthy lifestyle, exercise plays an important role. The expanding market of smart wearables and the inclusion of music into workouts, utilises the potential of technology to transform exercise. The domains of music and exercise cohesively have the potential to enhance exercise experience. However, there is a gap that exists between the two domains, with an absence of a platform that effectively combines both to yield a powerful system. This study proposes a novel machine learning solution that aims to bridge this gap, by utilising its user's real-time smartwatch data and music preferences to dynamically regulate the pace of exercise of the user through personalised music playlists. The proposed solution also provides a diet-centric chatbot based on Natural Language Processing, thus resulting in a wholistic health solution. This innovative approach aims to elevate user motivation, improve performance, and ultimately make exercise more enjoyable.
Keywords: Classification | Exercise | Large Language Model | Machine Learning | Music | Regression

Title: A Multi-Scale Lightweight 1D-CNN for Efficient CAN Intrusion Detection
Abstract: The Controller Area Network (CAN) bus is widely used in modern vehicles, but remains vulnerable to various cyberattacks due to its lack of built-in security mechanisms. Machine learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs) have been proposed to detect anomalies. However, many existing approaches rely on deep or recurrent architectures that are computationally intensive and difficult to deploy on resource-constrained automotive environments. To this end, we propose a multi-scale lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) designed specifically for efficient CAN intrusion detection. Unlike previous studies, we consider that realistic attacks can be complex and may not exhibit regular patterns, often displaying diverse temporal behaviors. We design and employ multiple depthwise separable Conv1D branches with varying kernel sizes, enabling more effective handling of such attacks. To further improve the performance, rather than concatenating feature maps or using computationally expensive fusion modules, we introduce scale gate, a parameter-free softmax gating mechanism that adaptively re-weights each branch's output based on the input. We evaluate the proposed IDS using real CAN traffic collected from different cars. The model achieves satisfying accuracy under our most challenging attack strategy with approximately 30 K parameters and 2.7 M FLOPs. Our ablation studies further confirm that both the multi-scale design and scale gate contribute to detection performance, demonstrating the effectiveness and efficiency of the approach for automotive environments.
Keywords: automotive security | CAN bus | in-vehicle networks | intrusion detection system | lightweight deep learning model

Title: Predicting Cognitive Decline: A Multimodal AI Approach to Dementia Screening from Speech
Abstract: Recent progress has been made in detecting early stage dementia entirely through recordings of patient speech. Multimodal speech analysis methods were applied to the Prediction and Recognition Of Cognitive declinE through Spontaneous Speech (PROCESS) Signal Processing Grand Challenge, which requires participants to use audio recordings of clinical interviews to predict patients as healthy control, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia and regress the patient's MiniMental State Exam (MMSE) scores. The approach implemented in this work combines acoustic features (eGeMAPS and Prosody) with embeddings from Whisper and RoBERTa models, achieving competitive results in both regression (RMSE: 2.7666) and classification (Macro-F1 score: 0.5774) tasks. Additionally, a novel two-tiered classification architecture is utilized to better differentiate between MCI and dementia. Our approach achieved strong results on the test set, ranking seventh on regression and eleventh on classification out of thirty-seven teams, exceeding the baseline performance.
Keywords: Early-stage Dementia Detection | Machine Learning | Multimodal AI | Speech and Audio Processing

Title: A Deep Learning Framework for Insect Sound Classification Integrating STFT and Log Mel Spectrogram with CNN
Abstract: Sound-based insect categorization has emerged as a practical method for monitoring biodiversity and ecological health. In order to classify insect species, this research presents a deep learning framework that combines the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), log mel spectrograms, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). To train and assess the model, 24 insect species that belong to the family Orthoptera, have been used. To transform the time-domain signals into frequency-domain representations, the suggested method starts with preprocessing the raw audio data using STFT. From the STFT outputs, log mel spectrograms are subsequently produced, which provide a more perceptually meaningful depiction of the insect sounds. These spectrograms are what the CNN model uses as input features. The spectrograms intricate patterns and properties are efficiently captured by the CNN architecture, allowing for precise classification of insect species. The model's resilience is demonstrated by the performance evaluation, which yields a classification accuracy of 98.66%
Keywords: Acoustic monitoring | Bioacoustics | Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) | Deep learning | Insect sound classification | Log mel spectrograms | Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) | Species identification

Title: A Moving Source Angle-of-Arrival Estimation in Real-Time Using Machine Learning
Abstract: This paper presents a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM model for accurate Angle of Arrival (AoA) estimation in dynamic signal environments. The proposed model achieves an overall root mean square error (RMSE) of 4.77 degrees for a single moving source, demonstrating superior robustness in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions (-20 dB), where the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm's performance significantly deteriorates. Additioanly, over-the-air (OTA) test validate the real-world applicability of our approach, where our model achieves an RMSE of 5.10 degrees compared to MUSIC's 34.99 degrees. The results highlight the advantages of machine learning over traditional subspace-based methods for AoA estimation in challenging environments.

Title: An Investigation of Machine Learning Solutions to Demonstrate Black Box Software Conformity in Regulated Measuring Instruments
Abstract: Modern regulated measuring instruments are mostly driven by sophisticated software with simple hardware sensors, where the software conformity with legal requirements is usually demonstrated via the version numbers and cryptographic hashes over executable binaries. Such conformity assessments quickly reach a bottleneck, when the actual software functionalities remain hidden from the view of authorities, i.e., in black box scenarios. In this article, we develop extensions to a machine learning approach that allows software modeling as automata in quasi-black box settings.
