This article presents a novel data-driven methodology for modeling nonlinear transducers within the power quality (PQ) frequency domain. Traditional modeling approaches often depend on predefined analytical formulations or efforts to derive them, which can restrict adaptability to varying operating conditions. In contrast, this method leverages machine learning to eliminate the need for prior analytical knowledge. Central to this methodology is utilizing artificial neural networks (ANNs) to precisely characterize the relationships between harmonic components in input and output signals (I/O) exhibiting distinct harmonic patterns. The resulting data-driven model closely aligns with source data, preserving statistical intricacies observed in both simulated and real-world measurements, with deviations typically within a few parts in 10<sup>−5</sup>
Keywords: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) | data-driven modeling | instrument transformers (ITs) | nonlinear network analysis | power system harmonics | transducers

Title: A Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model for Flashover Alert on Polluted Insulators Using UHF and Acoustic PD Signals
Abstract: Insulators are critical components in the transmission of electrical energy, and their correct operation is essential to guarantee the safety and continuity of the electrical supply. However, their constant exposure to environmental conditions such as pollution can affect their performance and lead to costly power outages. Proper monitoring and maintenance of this equipment are essential to avoid unexpected failures. Although significant progress has been made in the implementation of new monitoring methodologies and instruments, a solution that enables accurate and reliable online monitoring remains a challenge. This work presents a novel insulator flashover alert system that uses an acoustic sensor and an ultrahigh-frequency (UHF) antenna to detect partial discharge (PD) activity and generate alerts in three different states. The system uses hybrid deep learning models that combine a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network that process the information provided by the sensors and generate local alerts to produce the general decision. This system can indicate whether the monitored insulator is in a normal state, an attention state, or an alarm state, which could help specialists take preventive measures and avoid sudden insulator failures.
Keywords: Acoustic measurement | deep learning | flashover analysis | insulators | partial discharge (PD) | ultrahigh-frequency (UHF) measurement

Title: Mobile Application for Managing Anxiety using Machine Learning Model
Abstract: Anxiety before and after cardiac surgery is a critical factor that can negatively affect patients' recovery and clinical outcomes. This study presents Kora, a mobile application that combines mobile health (mHealth) strategies with a machine learning model to recommend relaxation techniques tailored to each patient's anxiety level. The proposed system uses physiological data - such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, and sleep duration - along with State-Trait Anxiety Inventory assessments (STAI), to classify users into anxiety categories and recommend appropriate interventions (music therapy, guided meditation, or breathing exercises). Three machine learning models - Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Gradient Boosted Trees - were trained and evaluated using the LifeSnaps dataset (7,411 records), with Gradient Boosted Trees achieving the highest performance, reaching 80.76% accuracy and 82.33% F1-score. Additionally, validation with clinical experts confirmed the app's usability and relevance in healthcare settings. These results suggest that Kora is a promising digital tool to support the emotional well-being of cardiac surgery patients through personalized relaxation techniques.
Keywords: anxiety | machine learning | mHealth | relaxation techniques | TensorFlow

Title: Effective Denoising in Music-Present Pubs with Efficient Channel Attention
Abstract: Music denoising aims to filter out unwanted noise while preserving the original quality of the music signal. In particular, noise generated in crowded environments such as pubs or streets varies widely in both type and intensity. In these settings, conventional denoising techniques often fail to perform effectively, leading to a degradation in music quality. There are a few related works, such as Band-Split RNN (BSRNN), typically involve dividing the signal into frequency bands and processing each band individually. However, they face several limitations. For instance, BSRNN’s high model complexity results in increased computational costs, and its reliance on manual frequency band selection can lead to suboptimal performance. Furthermore, it struggles with separating overlapping frequency bands in complex environments. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes the MusicBsECA method, which combines Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) with a band-splitting approach. Our method reduces model complexity and computational costs by focusing on critical features through ECA, while also leveraging LSTM and Transformer networks to capture both local and global dependencies in the signal. This custom approach allows for more precise separation of similar frequency bands and better performance in noise-heavy environments. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance in complex and noisy environments compared to existing techniques.
Keywords: Deep learning | Denoising | ECA | Music separation

Title: 3D On-chip Network Structure and Routing Algorithm for Large-scale Neuromorphic System
Abstract: The development of artificial intelligence enables instruments to cope with more complex and diverse measurement tasks. Inspired by the human brain, large-scale neuromorphic systems can optimize the architecture of measurement systems in terms of data processing capabilities and methods. They are typically composed of multiple chips, and on-chip network technology is crucial for supporting high-performance parallel and distributed computing. Inspired by the morphological structure of cortical microcircuits, this study proposes a three-dimensional on-chip network structure with multi-level clustered mesh and routing algorithm that is specifically designed for Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). The proposed approach is validated on a neural morphological system consisting of 40 FPGAs. Compared to traditional on-chip network structures, the proposed structure exhibits higher saturation injection rates and lower resource consumption, which reduces communication latency and improves scalability. This advancement facilitates the coordinated operation of large-scale Spiking Neural Network (SNN) systems and multi-brain area microcircuits, paving the way for future optimization of measurement and data processing in instruments and devices from the perspective of large-scale brain-inspired computing.
Keywords: FPGA | network-on-chip | neuromorphic system | routing algorithm

Title: Deep machine learning for identifying time-series functions of regulated measuring instruments
Abstract: Modern measuring instruments regulated by legal requirements such as in Legal Metrology are subject to conformity assessment and require a certification to ensure the compliance of instruments during use. However, such conformity assessment is usually version specific and a continuous monitoring or functional identification of these instruments during use could potentially replace repetitive conformity assessments and reverifications in the field. In this paper, we develop an extension to a state-of-the-art deep machine learning framework to interpret and analyze system logbooks describing the time-dependent behavior of regulated measuring instruments, realizing continuous quality control of such instruments via continually monitoring and identifying the instruments' behavior. We also evaluate the performance and investigate the advantages of the approach. It is envisioned that the approach could be added as an acceptable solution to legal regulations and could facilitate fully automatic quality control of modern measuring instruments.
Keywords: Automatic quality control | deep machine learning | functional identification | Legal Metrology | regulated measuring instruments | software conformity | time-series analysis

Title: A Comparative Analysis of OpenAI's API Performance: Insights from AI Response Statistics
Abstract: Generative AI models have the capability to produce a wide range of new content based on the data they are trained on. These models can generate not just text, but also various types of multimedia content, including images. In recent years, they have become increasingly popular due to their significant impact across multiple fields. They are used in various applications, from text and image generation to music creation, as well as in education, healthcare, robotics, finance, education, autonomous vehicles, and more. However, these models face numerous challenges, such as overfitting the outputs, inconsistency in the results, response time, and token usage. This study presents a comparative analysis of the performance of OpenAI's API, focusing on insights gleaned from AI response statistics. The evaluation encompasses various performance insights on different model approaches, such as response tokens, processing speed, and result token efficiency. Using quantitative metrics and qualitative assessments, the research identifies trends and patterns in API performance, highlighting strengths and areas for improvement. The study concludes with recommendations for optimizing API functions, contributing to the broader discourse on advancing AI integration in real-world applications.
Keywords: API Response | Generative AI | OpenAI Models | Prompt Engineering | Token

Title: LABIIUM: AI-Enhanced Zero-configuration Measurement Automation System
Abstract: The complexity of laboratory environments requires solutions that simplify instrument interaction and enhance measurement automation. Traditional tools often require configuration, software, and programming skills, creating barriers to productivity. Previous approaches, including dedicated software suites and custom scripts, frequently fall short in providing user-friendly solutions that align with programming practices.We present LABIIUM, an AI-enhanced, zero-configuration measurement automation system designed to streamline experimental workflows and improve user productivity. LABIIUM integrates an AI assistant powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate code. LABIIUM's Lab-Automation-Measurement Bridges (LAMBs) enable seamless instrument connectivity using standard tools such as VSCode and Python, eliminating setup overhead.To demonstrate its capabilities, we conducted experiments involving the measurement of the parametric transfer curve of a simple two-transistor inverting amplifier with a current source load. The AI assistant was evaluated using different prompt scenarios and compared with multiple models, including Claude Sonnet 3.5, Gemini Pro 1.5, and GPT-4o. An expert solution implementing the Gradient-Weighted Adaptive Stochastic Sampling (GWASS) method was used as a baseline.The solutions generated by the AI assistant were compared with the expert solution and a uniform linear sweep baseline with 10,000 points. The graph results show that the LLMs were able to successfully complete the most basic uniform sweep, but LLMs were unable to develop adaptive sweeping algorithms to compete with GWASS. The evaluation underscores LABIIUM's ability to enhance laboratory productivity and support digital transformation in research and industry, and emphasizes the future work required to improve LLM performance in Electronic Measurement Science Tasks.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | Automation | Electronic engineering | Large language models | Test and measurement

Title: Detecting Fake Reviews for E-Commerce Platform Using Machine Learning
Abstract: We suggest an effective, machine learning-based approach intended to fight the growing proliferation of deceptive reviews on online marketplaces. With customer reviews emerging as a major decision-making instrument for online consumers, review content manipulation poses a mounting risk to consumer confidence and marketplace reputation. This paper targets detecting deceptive reviews with conventional supervised learning methods, along with natural language processing (NLP) techniques. Based on Amazon's verified purchase data as an effective benchmark, we obtain linguistic features by means of Count Vectorizer and TF-IDF techniques and test the performances of three classifiers, namely Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Logistic Regression (LR). Logistic Regression with Count Vectorizer performed optimally among the three, thereby qualifying for deployment in real time. The concluding model is integrated into a web application to provide user-friendly, real-time prediction of review genuineness. This solution is for platform transparency and improves the online consumer experience.
Keywords: Count Vectorizer | Fake Reviews | Logistic Regression | NLP | Review Authenticity | SVM | Text Classification

Title: An Intelligent System for Real-time Skin Disease Detection and Medication
Abstract: Skin diseases are one of the leading diseases affecting humanity at large and across the globe, with no discrimination by age, gender, or ethnicity. These diseases, if not diagnosed early or treated appropriately, can be very detrimental, and dermatological services are hard to come by in many places. This paper proposes a system that combines achievements in machine learning, image processing, and mobile computing to detect skin diseases in real time and recommend the appropriate medications. It uses a deep learning convolutional neural network based on a large database of dermatological images to diagnose manifold diseases with high accuracy. Connecting with mobile and web-based applications, the system enables patients to take photos of the damaged areas of the skin and obtain diagnostic results instantly. In addition, the system gives a unique prescription of medication for the identified condition from a large library of therapeutic regimens and pharmacopeia. Systematic testing was performed to assess its performance, which yielded more than 90% satisfactory results in identifying the four most frequent conditions: acne, eczema, psoriasis, and melanoma. Moreover, the user testing also confirmed the system's implementation aspect, which gives the developed system the potential to fill the gaps in dermatological services, especially in low-income areas. In this paper, I describe the system's architecture, the process of implementation, the assessment of its accomplishments, and potential future improvements, which can be seen as a perspective instrument in dermatology and public health.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) | Deep Learning | Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) | Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) | Medical Image Processing | Real-time Diagnosis System | Skin Analysis | Skin Disease Detection

Title: Emotion Aware Speech Recognition System Using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Emotions play a critical role in conveying context, intent, and meaning in human communication. However, most speech recognition systems lack the capability to detect emotional cues, limiting their effectiveness in applications requiring situationally aware responses. This paper presents an Emotion-Aware Speech Recognition System utilizing deep learning techniques for integrated speech processing and emotion detection. The proposed system employs the TESS dataset for audio feature extraction using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), and utilizes Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to classify input speech into one of seven emotional states: sad, happy, surprised, angry, disgusted, fearful, or neutral. The dataset was partitioned into training (80%) and testing (20%) subsets, achieving a classification accuracy of 95%. Performance evaluation was conducted using precision, recall, F1-score, and a confusion matrix, demonstrating robustness across all emotional categories. The results highlight the potential applications of emotion recognition in domains such as customer service, healthcare, virtual assistants, and education by enhancing conventional speech processing models. This work contributes to the advancement of multimodal emotion recognition, facilitating the development of emotionally intelligent AI systems.
Keywords: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) | Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) | Toronto Emotional Speech Set (TESS)

Title: LSTM-based Financial Trend Prediction: Exploring the Use of Trend and Momentum Indicators
Abstract: The ability to forecast financial time series is critical for informed investment strategies and proactive risk control. This paper offers a proposed LSTM-based model for the Classification of the Stock Market as Bullish, Neutral, or Bearish with some Technical Indicators such as Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs), Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), and Relative Strength Index (RSI). The incorporation of several features in feature engineering assists in recognizing significant patterns, and LSTM layers capture The interconnected patterns in stock price fluctuations. The Training and Testing of the model employed a five-year dataset of historical stock prices. The experimental results proved that the model attained an impressive 98% accuracy in predicting market trends reliably. Confusion Matrices and Classification Reports validated its performance over various market conditions. This work highlighted the importance of technical indicators in the prediction process and provided a robust framework for financial time series analysis. The results emphasize the promise of deep learning methods, particularly LSTM networks, to improve forecasting reliability in financial markets.
Keywords: EMA | LSTM | MACD | RSI | Stock Trend

Title: Cloud Integrated System for Audio Processing and Automated Lecture Transcription
Abstract: Accurate speech transcription fulfills essential functions like accessibility and documentation and automated communication while background noises cause major obstacles to the accuracy rate. The research presents a speech-to-text system which combines edge computing with deep learning and cloud services to deliver better transcription results. An edge device based on a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B handles the process of audio capture and pre-processing. The noise reduction capabilities of the RNN model use LSTM units for dynamic disturbance filtering to enhance speech clarity. The service Amazon Transcribe receives refined audio data which it uses to generate text with high accuracy through its cloud-based speech recognition capabilities. AWS S3 provides secure high-scale storage that depends on encryption features alongside versioning and access authorization tools. A MERN stack-based dashboard that combines MongoDB, Express.js, React.js, Node.js lets users conduct interactive searches and filtration operations and transcription administration through an interface. Traditional noise suppression techniques break down when sound environments change but the adaptive RNN model both learns new information and enhances itself thus leading to better speech recognition accuracy in multiple real-life situations. This system functions best for lecture recording as well as corporate meeting recordings and accessibility tool applications and automatic documentation system processing. This study achieves a versatile high-sensitivity and cost-optimized transcription system through its real-time edge computing tech and AI noise filtration systems and scalable cloud platform design.
Keywords: Automatic Speech Recognition | Cloud Computing | Edge Computing | LSTM | MERN Stack | Noise Reduction | RNN | Speech-to-Text

Title: Black-box conformity tests on regulated measuring instruments: A machine learning approach
Abstract: The conformity of modern measuring instruments regulated with legal requirements is usually demonstrated by verifying software version numbers and cryptographic hashes over executable binaries. Regulated measuring instruments in Legal Metrology could also pass this conformity test, if the functional behavior of devices in the field and certified prototype is identical, thereby giving rise to the need for more efficient monitoring and identification methods in many legally regulated industries, especially when the functionalities of devices remain hidden from the view of authorities, i.e., in black box scenarios. In this paper, we extend a risk-based software monitoring algorithm by developing and integrating a model learning algorithm that works in quasi-black-box settings. We also analyze the performance of the algorithm and compare it with state-of-the-art approaches. If successfully implemented, manufacturers of measuring instruments could introduce software updates and monitor potential abnormalities, without resubmitting the software for new conformity assessment or certification.
Keywords: automata learning | Automatic quality control | functional identification | Legal Metrology | software conformity

Title: A Comprehensive Exploration of Machine Learning Models for Banknote Authentication
Abstract: Banknotes are legally issued instruments that represent monetary value and are sanctioned by governmental authorities. However, their high value and widespread use have made them a frequent target for counterfeiting. Due to the striking similarity between genuine and counterfeit notes, accurately distinguishing between the two poses a considerable challenge. This study aims to evaluate the performance of various machine learning models using the Banknote Authentication dataset, with the objective of identifying the most effective model for classifying banknotes as genuine or counterfeit. The models employed include Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbor, XGBoost Classifier, and Naive Bayes. Model robustness was validated using a Train-Test split methodology, with accuracy serving as the primary evaluation metric. Among the models tested, the XGBoost Classifier demonstrated the highest accuracy of 99.7273%, followed by K-Nearest Neighbor, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, and Naive Bayes. The findings of this research provide valuable insights that may inform the development of more accurate and reliable predictive systems for banknote authentication.
Keywords: Banknote Authentication | Banknote Recognition | K-Nearest Neighbor | Visualization | XGBoost Classifier

Title: A Lightweight Speech Enhancement Model with Parallel Processing of Magnitude and Phase Spectra
Abstract: Recent advancements in deep learning have led to substantial improvements in speech enhancement over traditional methods. However, these models typically involve a large number of parameters and require considerable computational resources, which limits their applicability on edge devices for real-world use. In this paper, we propose MPCRN, a novel model that simultaneously addresses both magnitude and phase denoising by incorporating GTCRN. MPCRN is optimized for computational efficiency, containing only 1.31 million parameters. Experimental evaluations show that MPCRN exhibits comparable performance to the current leading model, demonstrating strong competitiveness. A comparison of MPCRN with MP-SENet reveals that the former has an advantage in terms of memory utilisation efficiency and the effective reduction of training time.
Keywords: convolutional recurrent network | lightweight model | parallel denoising | speech enhancement

Title: Thyroid Disease Detection through EfficientNetB2: Enhancing Early Diagnosis with Deep Learning
Abstract: Thyroid diseases - including hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism - can seriously damage human well-being influencing cognitive ability, heart health, and fertility. Early, correct identification of these disorders guarantees both better patient outcomes and efficient treatment. Among the standard diagnoses are imaging and blood tests; both may be costly and time-consuming. This work suggests applying deep learning to increase diagnostic accuracy and efficiency by means of a modified EfficientNetB2 model for the automated categorization of thyroid disorders. Divided into two groups - healthy (0) and thyroid illness (1) - the model was taught using a collection of 7,288 thyroid-related photos. Pre-processing, picture resizing, standardizing, and enriching the dataset assured model robustity. Precision, recall, and F1-scores of 0.94, 0.88, and 0.91 for class 1 (thyroid illness) and 0.86, 0.93, and 0.90 for class 0 (healthy) the EfficientNet B2 model exhibited an outstanding accuracy of 90% in identifying thyroid abnormalities. By use of a confusion matrix, loss curves, and classification criteria, the model's performance was assessed, thereby exposing a well-balanced strategy to lower false positives and negatives. By means of better access to early detection techniques, encouragement of well-being, and support of the creation of creative medical solutions fit for sustainability objectives, this work promotes healthcare. The results demonstrate the potential of the instrument for early thyroid illness identification since EfficientNetB2 presents a scalable and computationally fast automated medical diagnostics solution.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | automated healthcare | deep learning | early diagnosis | EfficientNetB2 | machine learning in healthcare | medical imaging | Thyroid disease classification

Title: Speech Recognition Integration for Improved Learnability and Intelligibility in Point-Of-Care Systems
Abstract: This study focuses on the application of Automatic Speech Recognition to improve the learnability and intelligibility in PoC devices. The increased generation of data and the development of artificial intelligence make speech recognition technologies the necessary elements of healthcare systems. Non-Blocking speech interpretation is achieved through an LSTM-CNN computer system accompanied by Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) for feature analysis. Other forms of implementation include the use of mobile nets which only combine the two for better depiction in resourceful but limited mobile devices. It also responds to shortcomings of regional accents, dialectal variation, and background noise through high-performance voice activity and extraction of prosodic features. Extension of Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) promotes alignment-free transcribing which in turn reduces word error correction and improves the transcription effectiveness. The experimental findings confirm the feasibility of the system for recognizing different types of language inputs and the achieved level of intelligibility and speaker recognition. It establishes the feasibility of using speech recognition computer technologies for data entry in clinical contexts, and therefore, for secure and efficient communication between corresponding entities. This work provides the foundation for further developments in smart, environment-aware spoken-dialogue systems within healthcare settings.
Keywords: Connectionist Temporal Classification | Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients | Natural Language Processing | Voice Activity Detection

Title: Perception of Essential Sound in Cochlear Implants: Prediction Using Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract: Cochlear Implant (CI) is the intricate electronic gadget that offers the auditory sense for people who were afflicted with sensorineural hearing loss. It differs from the other hearing aid devices by its acoustic output signal and emulates the herbal listening to function the inner ear through digital stimulation. It stimulates the auditory nerve by applying electric signals to the electrodes which are present inside the cochlea. The auditory nerve sends those signals to the brain to recognize as sound. The performance of CI is sufficient good in the quiet environment, but they are facing more challenges in the noisy environment due to multi-talker and unwanted obstructions. The background noise degrades the functionality of these devices. The hearing ability of CI users depends on the sound stream segregation in the real world listening environment namely, monaural and binaural cues. Hence the CI users require more advanced strategies and algorithms to enhance the hearing ability. This paper provides a detailed review upon the sound recognition algorithms and sound coding strategies which are implemented to improve the intelligibility scores. In the further context of sound quality improvement, music perception, residual acoustic hearing, etc. we analysed the development and present a conceptual frame work to address these issues by focusing on recent works made for achieving higher intelligibility scores, ease of listening using Deep Learning techniques. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive exploration predominantly in the advancement of sound recognition techniques for CI users in reverberation environment through Deep Neural Network implementation.
Keywords: Cochlear implants | Deep learning | Speech intelligibility

Title: Generating Music With Retention Based Latent Transformer Models
Abstract: This paper introduces a new approach of music generation by combining Contrastive Language-Audio Pre-training (CLAP) for text encoding, retention-based transformers for audio synthesis, and Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoders (VQVAE) to compress the audio. The quality of generated output improves and computation needs decline with comparison to a base transformer architecture. In this experiment, several model configurations have been tried, which dif- fer by the number of transformer blocks or hidden layer sizes. The configurations are rated by metrics derived from the Friedrich Audio Distance combined with training loss. The best performing model used 16 transformer blocks, along with a hidden dimension of 512, to achieve good performance while cutting training by a time of 10 times and inference by 20 times compared with the standard transformers.The MusicBench dataset was used, where both the training and testing employed the same dataset, using varied music samples accompanied by textual descriptions. This dataset offered a massive test of the model's ability to produce music in various styles and genres. The current study adds great value to the AI-generated music domain by presenting a strong architecture that will endure high-quality output while overcoming computational challenges most often cited as being associated with music generation models.
Keywords: Music Generation | Retention-based Transformers | Text-conditioned Audio Synthesis | Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoders (VQ-VAE)

Title: Unsupervised Change Detection in multitemporal Satellite Images: A VMamba-Driven Cross-Scale Feature Decoding Network
Abstract: Unsupervised change detection based on deep learning has received wide attention on remote sensing image analysis. However, a critical challenge that limits the accuracy of change detection, is how to establish the global and local feature representations of multitemporal remote sensing images in complex scenarios. To address this challenge, a VMamba-driven cross-scale feature decoding (VCFD) unsupervised change detection network is proposed. VCFD employs two weight shared VMamba encoders to extract multi-scale features from multitemporal remote sensing images, which models the global context and local details of change features. Meanwhile, we design a cross-scale upsampling decoding module to progressively reconstruct high-resolution feature maps. The experiment on the OSCD dataset shows the superior performance of proposed method, which achieves a new existing state-of-the-art(SOTA) in unsupervised change detection.
Keywords: change detection | multi-scale features | remote sensing | vmamba

Title: Hybrid AI Framework for Dyslexia Detection Using MFCC Features, Optimized SVM, and Reinforcement-Based Assistive Learning
Abstract: A pervasive neurodevelopmental disorder, dyslexia has a substantial influence on reading, writing, and cognitive processing, which impacts everyday living as well as academic achievement. This work offers a hybrid AI-driven method for detecting dyslexia that combines adaptive reinforcement learning, speech signal analysis, and EEG-based biomarkers to improve diagnosis accuracy and offer individualized assistance. To enhance classification performance, the suggested system uses optimal Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers with sophisticated preprocessing methods, such as feature extraction and noise reduction. Real-time processing, scalability, and accessibility are guaranteed by a Raspberry Pi-based design, which makes it appropriate for a range of clinical and educational applications. The system's capacity to differentiate between dyslexic speech patterns and neurophysiological signals is confirmed by experimental evaluations, guaranteeing precise early diagnosis. Additionally, by tailoring interventions to each student's requirements, the adaptive reinforcement learning module increases engagement and enhances learning results. The results demonstrate the approach's promise as a thorough, economical, and successful method of dyslexia screening and assistance.
Keywords: Adaptive reinforcement learning | Advanced machine learning | Dyslexia diagnosis | Edge computing with Raspberry Pi | SVM classifiers

Title: Real-Time Human Joint Locations with Move Net for Interactive and Enhanced Motion Analysis
Abstract: With an emphasis on its makes use of in movement evaluation and augmented reality (AR) systems, this has a look at investigates MoveNet, a deep learning community for real-time role detection. With its outstanding precision and efficiency, MoveNet - that is primarily based totally at the MobileNetV2 architecture - is suitable for real-time posture estimation, even on cell devices. It presents complete insights at the posture and motion of the human frame through detecting 17 crucial frame markers. The have a look at explains how MoveNet may be used to music keypoints for comparing shape and overall performance in movement evaluation for sports, fitness, and rehabilitation. Additionally, the model's application in AR structures is highlighted, in which specific stance identity permits for dynamic interplay with digital objects, enhancing consumer reports in health and gaming packages. According to experimental data, MoveNet outperforms extra mounted posture detection strategies like OpenPose in phrases of performance and latency, mainly while processing in actual time. The model's adaptability for dynamic programs is confirmed with the aid of using its resilience in a number of scenarios, which includes altered lighting fixtures and partial occlusions.
Keywords: Augmented Reality | Convolutional Neural Network | Deep learning | Emotion Analysis | MobileNet | Virtual Reality

Title: ProLEACH: A Novel LEACH Improved with Multi-Head Attention Mechanism and Graph Convolution Network for Wireless Sensor Network
Abstract: In today's information age, Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN s) playa crucial and multifaceted role in our daily lives. From the smartphones to various precision instruments and testing equipment, WSNs provide essential support, enabling seamless communication, data collection, and intelligent automation. However, traditional WSN routing strategies, such as the Low-Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy (LEACH), face several significant limitations, including uneven node energy consumption, suboptimal path planning, and weak adaptability to dynamic environments. These shortcomings lead to inefficient energy usage, reduced network lifespan, and poor overall performance. To address these challenges, this paper integrates deep learning techniques into the existing LEACH routing protocol, introducing a novel ProLEACH routing method that leverages both the Multi-Head Attention (MHA) mechanism and Graph Convolutional Network (GCN). Specifically, the proposed approach first employs the MHA mechanism to intelligently select cluster heads based on multiple factors rather than random selection, ensuring a more balanced energy distribution across nodes. Then, GCN is utilized to optimize the data transmission path, allowing for more efficient and reliable communication between cluster heads and the base station. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed ProLEACH method significantly outperforms traditional LEACH routing in terms of two key performance metrics: node mortality rate and energy decay rate. By mitigating the negative effects of random cluster head selection, ProLEACH ensures a more uniform energy distribution among sensor nodes, effectively prolonging the network's lifespan. Additionally, the optimized transmission path reduces the communication overhead of cluster heads, further enhancing data transmission efficiency while lowering overall energy consumption. These improvements make ProLEACH a promising solution for energy-efficient and intelligent WSN routing in real-world applications.
Keywords: deep learning | Graph Convolution Network | Multi-Head Attention | WSN

Title: Steel Surface Defect Detection Algorithm Based on DM-YOLOv11
Abstract: To address the issues of multi-scale steel surface defects and the poor multi-scale feature processing of existing algorithms, this study proposes an improved detection modeling algorithm, called DM-YOLOv11. Firstly, the C3k2 module of the backbone network is integrated with the Dynamic Weight Reparameterization (DWR) module, expanding the receptive field at higher network levels to enhance multi-scale target recognition. Secondly, the Multi-path Coordinate Attention (MPCA) is integrated into the backbone network, enhancing the localization and discrimination of multi-scale defective features. Lastly, the Wise-IoUv2 loss function is employed to dynamically adjust the gradient modulation factor and incorporate non-monotonic gradient focusing, enhancing regression robustness. The experimental results demonstrate that the mean average precision (mAP) of DM-YOLOv11 on the NEU-DET and GC10-DET datasets improves by 4.1% and 2.6%, reaching 80.6% and 71.4%, respectively. The proposed method is highly effective for steel defect detection in industrial settings, showcasing its strong potential for robust generalization performance.
Keywords: attention mechanism | deep learning | steel defect detection | WIouv2 | YOLOv11

Title: Deep Learning Based Audio Classification Using Multi Feature Fusion Techniques
Abstract: This research explores the classification of environmental sounds using the UrbanSound8K dataset, introducing a novel feature fusion technique that combines spectrograms, scalograms, and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) - a combination not previously explored in existing literature. While individual features such as spectrograms, scalograms, and MFCCs achieved accuracies of 92%, 89%, and 89%, respectively, the fusion of these features led to a significant improvement in accuracy, reaching 97%, with a notable 5-8% performance gain. The proposed method harnesses the complementary nature of these features, effectively capturing temporal, frequency, and perceptual characteristics of audio signals, enabling more robust and comprehensive representations. The fused features are processed through an enhanced AlexNet architecture, customized to handle multi-dimensional inputs. The model demonstrated excellent noise robustness, faster convergence, and superior generalizability compared to models trained on individual features. The findings pave the way for future applications, including real-time environmental sound classification integrated with IoT devices, mobile applications, and broader domains such as wildlife monitoring and industrial noise detection systems.
Keywords: AlexNet | Classification | Environmental Sound | Feature Fusion | MFCC | Scalogram | Spectrogram

Title: A Study on Correcting English Pronunciation for Non-English Major Students Based on Artificial Intelligence Speech Recognition Technology
Abstract: This paper introduces a speech recognition and pronunciation correction system based on the Transformer model. The Transformer model uses the self-attention mechanism to capture the pronunciation timing and context information, and uses an end-to-end method to map the pronunciation signal to the correction suggestion. The model identifies the error type by calculating the pronunciation difference and generates personalized feedback. To improve performance, optimization strategies such as data enhancement and adding self-attention structure are adopted. The experiment uses a dataset containing 1,000 student samples and compares it with the recurrent neural network (RNN) and long short-term memory network (LSTM) models. The results show that the Transformer model-based system outperforms the traditional model in terms of accuracy (94.2%), recall (91.5%), F1 value (92.8), correction rate (87.6%), and other indicators, with an average response time of only 0.75 seconds. After using the system, students' pronunciation accuracy improved by more than 30%, and the improvement was more significant in the intermediate and advanced groups. More than 90% of students were satisfied with the system experience. In quiet and background noise environments, the Transformer model has strong stability and anti-interference ability, showing high robustness and practicality.
Keywords: AI speech recognition | non-English majors | pronunciation self-correction | self-attention mechanism | Transformer

Title: Vidtext Retriever
Abstract: This system in YouTube videos reflects an automatic text extractor, a response to the ever-rising demand for effective processing of digital media content. It fetches downloaded videos, converts audio into FFmpeg, and makes the transcription accurate with Google's Speech Recognition API. This feature enables the conversion of videos into text, thereby streamlining the content extraction processes and facilitating easy access to video content for consumers. Most content consumers, researchers, and educators, who require the fast transcription of large-scale video data to facilitate easier video understanding, would greatly benefit from this scalable solution.
Keywords: audio processing | speech recognition | text extraction | transcription | YouTube

Title: Multi-Modal Detection and Classification of Diabetic Retinopathy
Abstract: Early detection and precise severity analysis of diabetic retinopathy are crucial to preventing vision loss and improving patient outcomes. To address this challenge, an advanced deep learning model for improved detection and severity analysis of diabetic retinopathy has been proposed, capable of classifying the condition into five severity levels, ensuring higher accuracy and interpretability. To start with, the EfficientNet and GoogLeNet ensemble model was built and tested that reached 95.6% accuracy, which shows the model's stability. Additional improvements were made by adopting attention layers, stacking approaches and HbA1c% levels to increase the accuracy to 98.6%, thus offering a more comprehensive insight into the progression of the disease. The use of explainable AI was performed for interpretability, along with the feature of segmentation of affected retinal regions that helps make accurate medical assessment and decision planning. A user-friendly interface is created to support real time prediction where the clinician can upload the retinal images and get the report back with prediction. This vast framework helps not only to enhance diagnostic efficacy involving diabetic retinopathy, but also equip healthcare practitioners with the crucial instruments for decision-making regarding the results, thus providing a prospect for enhanced control over the disease.
Keywords: attention layers | Deep learning | detection | diabetic retinopathy | EfficientNet | ensemble models | explainable AI | five severity levels | GoogLeNet | HbA1c% levels | segmentation | stacking | user-friendly interface

Title: Classifying Music Genre and Recommending songs using various ML Algorithms
Abstract: The task of music genre classification in the realm of Music Information Retrieval is considered very challenging because audio features have varied complexity and overlapping nature. This paper addresses the issue by employing, comparing, and experimenting on diverse machine learning and deep learning models, including XGBoost, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The experiments are conducted on the GTZAN dataset, which has widely been used as a benchmark for music genre classification. Among the models implemented, the XGBoost demonstrated the best performance in predictions of the genre labels, acquiring a higher degree of accuracy as compared to the classical machine learning techniques. Besides, the study includes the development of a music recommendation system that suggests songs based on the input audio. It indicates that machine learning methods, like XGBoost, are highly effective for genre classification, but further enhancements, such as feature optimization and dataset expansion, could improve the performance of more traditional models.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Networks | K-Nearest Neighbors | Music Genre Classification | Music Information Retrieval | Random Forest | Support Vector Machines | XGBoost

Title: Music Genre Classification using Large Language Models
Abstract: This paper investigates the zero-shot capabilities of pre-trained large language models (LLMs) for music genre classification. The proposed approach splits audio signals into 20 ms chunks and processes them through convolutional feature encoders, a transformer encoder, and additional layers for coding audio units and generating feature vectors. The extracted feature vectors are used to train a classification head. During inference, predictions on individual chunks are aggregated for a final genre classification. We conducted a comprehensive comparison of LLMs, including WavLM, HuBERT, and wav2vec 2.0, with traditional deep learning architectures like 1D and 2D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and the audio spectrogram transformer (AST). Our findings demonstrate the superior performance of the AST model, achieving an overall accuracy of 85.5%, surpassing all other models evaluated. These results highlight the potential of LLMs and transformer-based architectures for advancing music information retrieval tasks, even in zero-shot scenarios.
Keywords: convolutional neural networks | Music genre classification | music information retrieval | transformers

Title: A Data-Driven Approach to Bankruptcy Prediction Using Machine Learning
Abstract: A crucial component of financial risk management, bankruptcy prediction aids in the informed decision-making of investors, companies, and other stakeholders. Accurately forecasting bankruptcy is one of the major obstacles in this field, particularly when the data is unbalanced. This endeavor is further complicated by the fact that bankrupt enterprises (the minority class) are frequently underrepresented in such statistics. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling strategy (SMOTE) is a strategy used in this work to correct this imbalance and improve bankruptcy prediction utilizing machine learning approaches. We use seven distinct algorithms, such as Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and MLP Classifier, on a financial dataset in order to evaluate the efficacy of various machine learning models. We make two contributions: first, we use important metrics like accuracy, recall, precision, and F1-score to assess the performance of these models before and after using SMOTE. The findings demonstrate that Random Forest and Gradient Boosting outperform the other models in recall with a score of 0.8 and are especially good at identifying failing companies. Our method's unique feature is the way we combine SMOTE with numerous classifiers to increase the model's capacity for accurate prediction and generalization. The prediction models' performance is much improved by this combination, providing a more trustworthy instrument for financial decision-making.
Keywords: Classifier | Financial Risk Management | Machine Learning | Prediction | SMOTE

Title: Kannada Music Genre Classification Using Audio Analytics, Machine Learning and Deep Learning
Abstract: Recommender systems have become popular in many business systems, including the entertainment and music industries. Music apps like Spotify, YouTube Music, Amazon Music, and Apple Music have embedded recommendation engines to enhance user base and customer experience. Kannada music, largely known to Indians and a bit less known to the international community, has a wide musical audience. It has a rich musical heritage with many great singers and musicians contributing to its vast musical repertoire spanning various genres. Current recommendation systems in most music apps are based on metadata classification using album, movie, singer, year, etc. They lack abilities to finer genre classification for soft Kannada music types like ‘Janapada’, ‘Bhavageethe’, and ‘Classical’, missing to attract a certain segment of the musical audience. According to the study survey, there hasn’t been any noteworthy work done on the genres of soft music, nor has there been any use of contemporary methods for classifying genres or the availability of datasets for experimenting. The proposed work is aimed at the Music Genre classification of Kannada soft music. The methodology involves the creation of a Kannada music audio dataset, application of audio analytics for feature extraction, feature analysis, and training of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models. Techniques of hyperparameter tuning, cross-validation, feature importance analysis, and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) have been applied to optimize the trained models. Through this work, a Kannada soft music dataset of 1500 audio clips is created. Various ML and DL models are trained, and the performance of models is compared. and a classification accuracy of 96.05% is achieved. Proposed applications include a music recommendation system and Teacher-in machines.
Keywords: Audio analytics | Bhavageethe | Classical | Deep learning | Indian music | Janapada | Kannada soft music | Machine learning | Music genre classification | Recommender system

Title: DenseViT: Densely Connected Vision Transformers for Visual Recognition
Abstract: Dense connection structures have garnered considerable interest in the deep learning domain due to their efficient feature reuse capabilities. However, their potential within Transformer architectures remains underexplored. To address the issues of feature collapse and inadequate multi-scale learning capabilities in classical Vision Transformers (ViT), we propose a feature learning method integrating dense connections, learnable weight matrices, and pyramid convolutions. The approach achieves efficient multi-layer feature reuse through dense connection structures while employing weight matrices to regulate the influence of different layers on final attention scores. We conducted experiments on four benchmark datasets: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Oxford-Flowers-102, and Oxford-IIIT Pet. The consequences exhibit that the densely connected ViT exhibits superior performance in classification tasks and significantly improved multi-scale learning capabilities compared to baseline models.
Keywords: Dense Connection | Image Classification | Pyramid Convolutions | Vision Transformer

Title: Innovative Sensing and Data Processing for Deformation and Texture Classification in Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Surgery
Abstract: Tactile feedback is crucial in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery (RAMIS), especially for surgeons palpating subsurface tumors and other organ structures. This research introduces a novel approach to tactile perception in RAMIS, focusing on deformation and texture detection. The proposed solution involves the design of a sensory system and two main data processing phases: feature extraction and recognition. During feature extraction, data is gathered from two micro-electromechanical (MEMS) sensors and a force-sensitive resistor (FSR) sensor attached to an EndoWrist thoracic grasper instrument compatible with the da Vinci Surgical System. Digital signal processing techniques are then applied to process the acquired data. In the recognition phase, the extracted features serve as inputs for training and testing two advanced machine learning algorithms: Reflex Fuzzy Min-Max Neural Network (RFMN) and Time Series Classification - Learning Shapelets (TSC-LS). These algorithms aim to accurately classify objects with varying softness and roughness into corresponding deformation or texture labels. The research presents preliminary experiments and results analyzing the performance metrics of the two machine learning algorithms.

Title: Innovating Education with ChatGPT: Strategies for Greater Engagement and Critical Thinking
Abstract: This research documents the implementation of the artificial intelligence tool ChatGPT in higher education settings as a learning instrument rather than a content creator. The tool was utilized in two online courses targeting students aged 18-21 pursuing diverse disciplines in Social Sciences and Government: "Global Citizenship: Diversity and Tolerance" and "Mexican Politics: Evolution and Challenges". The activities included dialogue sessions on migration and analysis of selected decisions of the Supreme Court of Mexico, presenting moral and legal dilemmas. ChatGPT was employed to gain further insights into these rulings and the background that prompted their outcomes. To assess the effectiveness of these initiatives, students participated in an online mixed (quantitative and qualitative) survey. Data related to participation, academic performance, critical reflection, and tool interaction were collected. The research findings offer suggestions and considerations for creating activities utilizing artificial intelligence, such as ChatGPT, while identifying areas needing improvement. This study underscores the importance of incorporating artificial intelligence tools in traditional educational settings to leverage their advantages and explore varied AI applications. The purpose of these applications was not knowledge production but rather the utilization of AI as a tool for the learning process.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | ChatGPT | Higher Education | Technology

Title: Intelligent Automatic Editing System Based on SpringBoot Framework - Helping Cultural Inheritance
Abstract: This paper introduces an intelligent editing system based on artificial intelligence technology, which is specially designed for the field of Chinese history and cultural heritage, and supports the acquisition, processing, editing and distribution of a variety of video materials. The system adopts MEANR-VC speech recognition model and DFCNN-CTC acoustic model, which is capable of recognizing speech of different languages and accents, and provides customized output speech conversion technology. Meanwhile, the system provides rich editing functions and supports automatic generation of editing schemes to improve editing efficiency. Through efficient algorithms and optimization strategies, the system ensures fast processing of video clips with good scalability.
Keywords: customized output | DFCNN-CTC | editing function | intelligent editing system | MEANR-VC | performance optimization | speech recognition | video processing

Title: Heterogeneous AI Music Generation Technology Integrating Fine-Grained Control
Abstract: As artificial intelligence algorithms continue to advance, researchers have increasingly harnessed their capabilities to generate music that resonates with human emotions, offering a novel means of alleviating the escalating pressures of contemporary life. To tackle the persistent issue of low accuracy in current emotion recognition and music generation systems, an innovative approach was proposed that fused a graph convolutional neural network with a channel attention mechanism for emotion recognition. This integrated model was subsequently paired with a Transformer architecture, creating a sophisticated framework capable of fine-grained control and heterogeneous music generation. In comparing the performance of the emotion recognition model against other leading models, the results underscored its exceptional accuracy across five distinct electroencephalogram signal bands: 97.3%, 95.8%, 96.9%, 98.4%, and 97.6%, respectively. Crucially, all these accuracy metrics exceeded the 95% benchmark, clearly demonstrating superiority over the comparative models. Additionally, a rigorous performance assessment was conducted to evaluate the music generation model's capabilities against alternative approaches. The findings revealed that the suggested model achieved an average mean square error of 0.27 and an average root mean square error of 0.24. These error rates were notably lower than those of the competing models, highlighting the enhanced precision and fidelity of the music generated. Together, these results validated the effectiveness of both the emotion recognition and music generation models developed in this research. This research not only propelled the existing frontiers of emotion detection and musical composition forward, but also laid a robust theoretical framework to facilitate subsequent investigations into the emerging field of emotion-aware music generation.
Keywords: channel attention | emotion recognition | Graph convolutional neural network | music generation | transformer

Title: Music Style Recognition using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients and Principal Component Analysis Enhanced Features with Support Vector Machine
Abstract: Music style recognition is a key application in audio classification, recommendation systems, and music information retrieval. Most conventional approaches depend on handcrafted feature extraction or neural networks with the need for extensive training and large datasets. Nevertheless, current systems have low accuracy when handling overlapping genres or noisy audio signals. This study puts forward the hybrid classification system that integrates Support Vector Machine (SVM) with Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) feature extraction and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for reducing dimension, which is more effective and efficient. SVM is utilized because it is strong in dealing with small and high-dimensional data sets. The proposed system is compared with standard classifiers KNN and Decision Trees. Results demonstrate the new system attains 97.4% accuracy and an F1-score of 96.8%, which is significantly higher than conventional models. The improved performance can be credited to the discriminative nature of MFCC features and PCA's capacity to remove redundant data, allowing the SVM classifier to have better distinction between genres. This hybrid model exhibits enhanced generalization, accuracy, and reliability in music style classification tasks.
Keywords: audio classification | F1-score | genre detection | machine learning | MFCC | music style recognition | PCA | support vector machine

Title: Research on Music Course Teaching Resource Recommendation based on Convolutional Neural Network
Abstract: The fast development of online education calls for smart recommendation systems that can improve personalized music learning experiences. This paper introduces a Hierarchical Multi-Modal Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based recommendation model that can be specifically designed for the teaching resources of music courses. Current recommendation systems are plagued by low accuracy, poor contextual understanding, and limited adaptability to the distinctive auditory and structural properties of music-oriented data. Classic models like collaborative filtering and content-based ones tend to be ineffective in representing profound semantic relations between musical resources. However, the proposed architecture digs out hierarchical features from multi-modal music data (textual, audio, and visual inputs) to predict learner preferences accurately and provide relevant recommendations. Experimental results illustrate that the proposed model performs better than baseline models such as conventional CNNs and matrix factorization methods, reaching 94.2% accuracy and 93.5% F1-score, with superior performance in precision and recall trade-offs. The model's resilience and flexibility attest to its applicability in practical situations in dynamic learning environments, providing an intelligent and effective means for resource recommendation in music learning.
Keywords: accuracy | deep learning | F1-score | music education | personalized learning | teaching resource recommendation

Title: Enhanced Lung Disease Classification Using CALMNet: A Hybrid CNN-LSTM-TimeDistributed Model for Respiratory Sound Analysis
Abstract: Lung diseases, such as asthma, pneumonia, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), pose considerable global health issues, making early diagnosis essential for effective treatment. Traditional diagnostic techniques for these ailments, especially auscultation using a stethoscope, are subjective and susceptible to inaccuracies. This study introduces CALMNet, a deep learning model that uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and a TimeDistributed layer to accurately analyze lung sounds by considering both their spatial and time-related features. The model is trained and assessed utilizing the ICBHI dataset, which encompasses a varied collection of lung sounds from patients with various respiratory ailments. Preprocessing techniques, including double denoising (FFT and high-pass filtering), were utilized to enhance the audio data quality, while feature extraction methods such as Mel Spectrograms, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), and Chroma Short-Time Fourier Transform (ChromaSTFT) were employed to capture the fundamental characteristics of lung sounds. The results show that CALMNet achieves an impressive accuracy of 97.65%, with an F1-score of 0.909, precision of 0.911, and recall of 0.90, outperforming other models like CNNs and LSTMs. CALMNet exhibits enhanced efficacy in differentiating various lung illnesses, as evidenced by the confusion matrix and ROC curve analysis. The model’s exceptional accuracy and strong performance indicate its promise as an effective instrument for the automated classification of lung illnesses, providing a dependable, objective, and scalable option for clinical use. Future endeavors will concentrate on augmenting the dataset, enhancing model interpretability, and executing real-time diagnostic applications to further elevate its applicability in healthcare environments.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence | CALMNet | respiratory diseases | respiratory sound analysis | sound processing. lung sound classification

Title: Wavelet Augmented Phase Coherence Features for EEG-Based Imagined Speech Classification
Abstract: Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) provide direct communication between the brain and external devices. Using electroencephalogram (EEG) sensors, BCIs are applied in assistive technologies and neuroprosthetics. Among various BCI paradigms, imagined speech-based BCI aims to decode internal speech representations from EEG signals, enabling silent communication. Decoding imagined speech is challenging due to the nonstationarity, intersubject variability of EEG signals and low signal-to-noise ratio. The proposed method uses a multilayer perceptron (MLP) integrated with a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) to enhance feature learning by refining spatial and channel-wise attention. To further improve performance, wavelet-based augmentation enhances data diversity. Phase and coherence-based functional connectivity features capture interchannel dependencies critical for imagined speech classification. The proposed wavelet-augmented phase coherence features with MLP-CBAM (WaveCoh-MLP-CBAM) framework is evaluated on an imagined speech dataset. The WaveCoh-MLP-CBAM shows superior classification accuracy, F1-score, and Cohen's kappa compared to conventional approaches. Results highlight the importance of augmentation, functional connectivity features, and attention in improving EEG-based imagined speech decoding.
Keywords: coherence | electroencephalogram (EEG) | imagined speech | machine learning | phase | Sensor signal processing | sensor signal processing

Title: Dynamic Multi-Image Weighting for Automated Detection and Diagnosis of Abnormal Urinary Tract on Voiding Cystourethrography with a Deep Learning System: A Retrospective, Large-Scale, Multicenter Study
Abstract: We aimed to develop a voiding cystourethrography (VCUG) diagnostic artificial intelligence model (VCUG-DAM), which relies on a novel architecture to automatically segment and diagnose the bladder, urethra, and ureters using a single VCUG image, while dynamically assessing the relative importance of each image. A total of 7,899 VCUG images from 1,660 patients across 15 Chinese hospitals were collected between 2021 and 2023. In stage 1, we assessed the performances of the VCUG-DAM model. The patient-level area under the curve (AUC) of VCUG-DAM was 0.8772, 0.7752, 0.9443, and 0.9342 for bladder, urethral, left, and right vesicoureteral reflux (VUR), respectively. In stage 2, we explored whether the VCUG-DAM model could improve the diagnostic ability of clinicians. VCUG-DAM improved the clinician’s diagnostic performance, with mean AUCs increasing from 0.8185 to 0.9456 for the bladder, 0.6507 to 0.7943 for the urethra, 0.6288 to 0.9641 for the left VUR, and 0.7305 to 0.9506 for the right VUR (all P < 0.0001). In stage 3, the consistency of the VCUG-DAM for VUR grading was validated. VCUG-DAM improved inter-clinician agreement for VUR grading. The fully automated VCUG-DAM demonstrated high accuracy, reliability, and robustness in multitask diagnoses of urinary tract abnormalities across multiple VCUG images, while improving the diagnostic ability of clinicians as an auxiliary tool.

Title: YouTube Comments Spam Detection Model Comparison with Selective Feature Vectors and a Hybrid Metric
Abstract: There has been a noticeable surge in spam and illegitimate comments with the booming growth of digital footprints on social media platforms leading to a great inconvenience to moderators and content administrators. Here, we present a comprehensive study of YouTube comment classification using machine learning models. Our dataset comprises 50,744 comments extracted from 21 Music Videos. With selective feature vectors and manually curated datasets, we use SVM, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and KNN Classifier models and Hybrid metric to assess each model performance. The intention of this research is to provide a view of large-scale data with intuitive insights and knowledge-based analysis when selective features are used.
Keywords: Big data | Comment classification | Data analytics | Feature vectors | Natural language processing | Spam detection

Title: Optimized Heart Disease Detection Using Hybrid Brave-Hunting Algorithm with SVM-Integrated Deep CNN
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease is one of the leading causes of death in the human population. Every year, this illness is responsible for the deaths of a great number of people. It is estimated by the World Health Organisation that 17.9 million individuals lose their lives each year due to heart disease. Imaging has become increasingly useful in the detection of cardiac illness, because to the different instruments and methodologies that have been developed. In the fields of pattern recognition and computer vision, one of the most essential tasks is the assignment of one or more labels to images. It is now much easier to recognise patterns in images thanks to machine learning, and deep learning has made it more accurate than the previous methods of image categorisation. This research aims to develop a deep learning-based image classification technique to diagnose heart disease. Deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) are the most common image recognition classifier. Additionally, there is no other method that is more frequently employed. The results can be improved even further with the use of classification. Image classification is a major challenge now. The UCI heart disease dataset is used to evaluate the proposed model. The dataset has 14 features and 1050 patients. We gathered a collection of easily available features from the dataset containing heart diseases, and we considered this feature vector to be the input for a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) in order to evaluate whether or not an instance belongs to the category of heart disease or healthy. A number of performance metrics, such as accuracy, precision, recall, and the F1 measure, were utilised in order to assess the efficacy of the technique that was suggested. With a validation accuracy of 91.7%, our model was successful. The results of the experiment demonstrate how effective the method that was suggested is when applied in a real-world environment.
Keywords: and heart disease are all topics that are commonly discussed | Computer vision | deep convolutional neural network | deep learning technique | image classification

Title: A transfer deep residual shrinkage network for bird sound recognition
Abstract: Bird sound recognition has important applications in bird monitoring and ecological protection. However, in complicated environments, noise and insufficient sample data are the major factors affecting recognition accuracy. We proposed a bird sound recognition method based on a developed transfer deep residual shrinkage network. First, a deep residual shrinkage network with noise resistance was constructed based on the structural characteristics of the residual shrinkage module, multi-scale operations, and the characteristics of bird sound Mel spectrograms. Then, the deep residual shrinkage network was pre-trained using a bird sound dataset, applying an unfreezing finetuning strategy, to mitigate the impact of insufficient training data. A transfer learning alleviated the problem of data scarcity by utilizing pre-trained models, while the deep residual shrinkage network enhanced the performance of the model in a noisy environment by optimizing the network structure. Experimental results showed that this method achieves high recognition accuracy under noise and small data sets. It has advantages over the compared methods and is suitable for ecological monitoring fields such as bird population monitoring. The method has good application prospects.
Keywords: audio signal processing | bioacoustics | bird sound recognition | deep learning | deep residual shrinkage network | ecological monitoring | machine learning | transfer learning

Title: DeePet: A Deep Learning Based Pet Comforting and Feeding System Using Internet of Things Technologies
Abstract: This paper designs and implements a deep learning based pet comforting and feeding system, called DeePet, to achieve comprehensive pet care services through IoT technologies. The DeePet system provides functions of activity recognition, instant feeding, music/sound playing, pet soothing, and exercise encouragement. The pet activity recognition model is developed based on densely connected neural networks to accurately identify pet status (e.g., eating, anxious, drinking, or agitated). In addition, the pet can be conditionally feeded as it performs sufficient roller rotations for encouraging exercise. Furthermore, the scent of the owner can be extracted beforehand and released to alleviate the anxiety of the pet as necessary. To validate the feasibility and performance of DeePet, an Android-based prototype with the IoT device is developed. Experimental results show that DeePet outperforms existing methods and can significantly improve the accuracy of pet activity recognition.
Keywords: Activity Recognition | Deep Learning | Internet of Things | Mobile Device | Pet Care

Title: FDMamba-Net: Feature-Decoupled Mamba Network for Efficient Flight Trajectory Prediction
Abstract: Accurate flight trajectory forecasting is crucial for air traffic management and UAV navigation. However, the task is highly challenging due to complex spatiotemporal dependencies in long sequences and computational constraints. Thus, we propose FDMamba-Net, a novel deep learning-based framework for trajectory prediction that achieves both high efficiency and precision. It combines feature decoupling, spatiotemporal attention fusion, state - space modeling, and spatial - enhanced decoding. The framework first uses a feature decoupling module to divide raw inputs into independent subspaces to eliminate feature interference. Then, spatiotemporal attention fusion is applied to model dynamic temporal relationships. Next, multi-layer Mamba blocks conduct multi-scale temporal modeling. Finally, spatial features are optimized through adaptive weight - enhanced decoding. Experiments show that FDMamba-Net surpasses baseline methods. Compared to Transformer-based approaches, it achieves better performance with 55.5% fewer parameters, making it a promising solution for efficient trajectory prediction.
Keywords: Flight trajectory prediction | Mamba | Spatiotemporal Modeling

Title: DB-MFNet: A Dual-Branch Cross-Modal Fusion Network for High-Resolution Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: Combining land cover semantic segmentation with deep learning neural networks and applying it is a very important research direction. In the past few years, The multimodal fusion model has made great progress and attracted extensive attention. Most models achieve this by integrating visual Transformers with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), This results in an increased overall computational load and potential loss of contextual data, particularly during feature fusion. The self-attention mechanism’s inherent deficiency in local receptive field constraints hinders precise localization of high-frequency spatial patterns. To further improve the effect of network in remote sensing segmentation, this paper proposes a dual-branch multi-scale fusion network (DB-MFNet). In feature-level fusion, a novel multi-scale attention module (MSAF) is used to construct a multi-scale feature fusion module (MFF), which extracts modality-specific features at different scales and combines them with channel-space mixed attention for dynamic weighted fusion. Furthermore, this paper introduces a spatial-channel mutual fusion aggregation module (SCMFA) and, through testing, develops an encoder (SCMF-Former) capable of spatial-channel mutual fusion of high-level features. Finally, a dynamic upsampling module (Dysample) is introduced into the decoder, forming a dynamic upsampling cascade decoder that adaptively focuses on important areas. Experimental results of DB-MFNet on the Potsdam and Vaihingen datasets indicate that this approach demonstrates good performance in remote sensing semantic segmentation.
Keywords: Deep Learning | Multimodal | Remote Sensing | Semantic Segmentation

Title: Chlorophyll-a Prediction Based on Machine Learning and Satellite Data in the South Sea of Korea
Abstract: Chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) is a critical indicator of phytoplankton biomass, offering key insights into changes in marine ecosystems, including algal blooms and nutrient cycling. However, predicting Chl-a concentrations using numerical models remains challenging due to the intricate interplay of climatic and geographical factors. Moreover, conventional studies relying heavily on localized marine measurement instruments face limitations in both scope and generalizability. To address these challenges, this study integrates high-resolution satellite imagery with advanced machine learning (ML) techniques to develop a robust and scalable model for predicting Chl-a concentrations in the South Sea of Korea. Multiple linear regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting models were evaluated, along with an averaging ensemble that combines their predictions. A feature ablation study was also conducted to assess the contribution of individual input variables. The results showed that the Ensemble model achieved the highest performance, with R<sup>2</sup> values of 0.821 for 1-day predictions, 0.750 for 2-day predictions, and 0.713 for 3-day predictions. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating high-resolution (250 m) satellite data with ML to achieve accurate and wide-scale predictions of Chl-a concentrations. These advancements are expected to provide foundational data for applications in marine environmental monitoring, sustainable aquaculture management, and harmful algal bloom prediction.
Keywords: Chlorophyll-a | ensemble | feature ablation study | machine learning (ML) | satellite data | South Sea of Korea

Title: Interpretable Machine Learning Techniques for Audio Source Separation
Abstract: Recent advancements in deep learning have revolutionized audio source separation, addressing challenges like the cocktail party problem. This study explores the efficacy of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), specifically the Conv-TasNet architecture, for separating vocals, drums, bass, and other instruments from mixed audio using spectrogram-based methods, and deep learning models. Leveraging the MUSDB18 dataset, these models were trained and evaluated, and the best model achieved significant performance metrics such as an accuracy of 0.93, Signal-to-Distortion Ratio (SDR) of 13.2 dB, Signal-to-Interference Ratio (SIR) of 14.6 dB, and Signal-to-Artifact Ratio (SAR) of 10.5 dB. Additionally, explainability techniques like SHAP and Integrated Gradient were employed to enhance model interpretability. These findings contribute to advancing more efficient and interpretable audio processing systems.
Keywords: Audio source separation | Deep learning | Machine learning | Spectrograms | Target sound extraction | XAI

Title: Harmonising code and composition: computational design strategies for multimedia classical concerts
Abstract: There are growing intersections between classical music performance, its tradition, acoustic fidelity, and advanced computational technologies, creating immersive multimedia concert experiences. We discuss how classical concert design is advanced by integrating real-time audio processing, machine learning models, generative visual engines, and audience interaction frameworks. A modular architecture was developed and tested through two case studies (Beethoven 360° and Bach Rewired), demonstrating two separate use cases of artificial intelligence, real-time rendering, and biofeedback systems. Sensor-based audience input has been used to learn about the adaptive performance elements, and musical structure was mapped to visual output using deep learning models. Results showed that audience immersion increased from an average of 5.4 to 6.8, while system latency was less than 25 ms.
