The article's primary contributions are twofold: firstly, we present an objective aesthetic evaluation method tailored for music performance; secondly, we introduce ten fundamental music features and four aesthetic music features. Experimental results demonstrate that our method excels in performance assessment.
Keywords: birkhoff's measure | computational aesthetics | music features | music performance evaluation

Title: RP1M: A Large-Scale Motion Dataset for Piano Playing with Bimanual Dexterous Robot Hands
Abstract: It has been a long-standing research goal to endow robot hands with human-level dexterity. Bimanual robot piano playing constitutes a task that combines challenges from dynamic tasks, such as generating fast while precise motions, with slower but contact-rich manipulation problems. Although reinforcement learning-based approaches have shown promising results in single-task performance, these methods struggle in a multi-song setting. Our work aims to close this gap and, thereby, enable imitation learning approaches for robot piano playing at scale. To this end, we introduce the Robot Piano 1 Million (RP1M) dataset, containing bimanual robot piano playing motion data of more than one million trajectories. We formulate finger placements as an optimal transport problem, thus, enabling automatic annotation of vast amounts of unlabeled songs. Benchmarking existing imitation learning approaches shows that such approaches reach promising robot piano playing performance by leveraging RP1M<sup>?</sup>
Keywords: Bimanual dexterous robot hands | dataset for robot piano playing | imitation learning | robot learning at scale

Title: Face Anti-Spoofing Using Chainlets and Deep Learning
Abstract: Now-a-days, biometric technology is widely employed for many security purposes. Facial recognition is one of the biometric technologies that is increasingly utilized because it is convenient and contactless. However, the facial recognition system has become the most targeted by unauthorized users to get access to the system. Most facial recognition systems are vulnerable to face spoofing attacks. With the widespread use of the internet and social media, it has become easy to get videos or pictures of people’s faces. The imposter can use these documents to deceive facial authentication systems, which affects the system’s security and privacy. Face spoofing occurs when an unauthorized user attempts to gain access to a facial recognition system using presentation attack instruments (PAIs) such as photos, videos, or 3D masks of the authorized users. Therefore, the need for an effective face anti-spoofing (FAS) system is increased. That motivated us to develop a face anti-spoofing model that accurately detects presentation attacks. In our work, we developed a model that integrates handcrafted features based on Chainlets (as motion-based descriptor) and the convolutional neural network (CNN) to provide a more robust feature vector and enhance accuracy performance. Chainlets can be computed from deep contour-based edge detection using Histograms of Freeman Chain Codes, which provides a richer and rotation-invariant description of edge orientation that can be used to extract Chainlets features. We used a benchmark dataset, the Replay-Attack database. The result shows that the Chainlets-based face anti-spoofing method overcome the state-of-art methods and provide higher accuracy.
Keywords: chain code | Chainlets | CNN | contour | face anti-spoofing | handcrafted features | Presentation attacks

Title: Texture Feature and Mel-Spectrogram Analysis for Music Sound Classification
Abstract: The categorization of music has received substantial interest in the management of large-scale databases. However, the sound of music classification (MC) is poorly interesting, making it a big challenge. For this reason, this paper has proposed a new robust combining method based on texture feature with Mel-spectrogram to classify Arabic music sound. A music audio dataset consisting of 404 sound recordings for different four classes of Arabic music sounds has been collected. The collected data became available for free on the Kaggle website. Firstly, music sound is transformed into a Mel spectrogram, and then several texture features are extracted from these Mel spectrogram images. A two-dimensional Haar wavelet is applied to each Mel-spectrogram image, and Local Binary Patterns (LBP), Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM), and Histogram of Oriented Gradient (HOG) are utilized for feature extraction. K-nearest neighbors (KNN), random forest (RF), decision tree (DT), logistic regression (LR), AdaBoost, extreme gradient boosting (XGB), and support vector machine (SVM) classifiers were utilized in a comparative analysis of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms. Two different datasets have been employed in order to evaluate the effectiveness of our approach: the collected dataset that the authors had gathered and the global GTZAN dataset. Our method demonstrates superior performance with a five-fold cross-validation. The experimental findings indicated that the XGB exhibited a high accuracy with an average performance of 97.80% for accuracy, 97.72% for F1-Score, 97.75% for recall, and 97.81% for precision.
Keywords: MC | Mel-spectrograms | ML | texture features

Title: Knowledge Graph-Based Badminton Tactics Mining and Reasoning for Badminton Player Training Pattern Analysis and Optimization
Abstract: As the global emphasis on sports data analysis and athlete performance optimization continues to grow, traditional badminton training methods are increasingly insufficient to meet the demands of modern high-level competitive sports. The exploration and reasoning of badminton tactics can significantly aid coaches and athletes in better comprehending game strategies, playing a vital role in the analysis and optimization of training methods. By utilizing knowledge graph-based badminton tactics mining, an approach involving heterogeneous graph splitting is employed, coupled with the incorporation of a cross-relational attention mechanism within relational graph neural networks. This mechanism assigns varying weights based on the importance of neighboring nodes across different relations, facilitating information aggregation and dissemination across multiple relationships. Furthermore, to address the challenges posed by the complexity of large-scale knowledge graphs, which feature numerous entity relationships and intricate internal structures, techniques such as training subgraph sampling, positive-negative sampling, and block-diagonal matrix decomposition are introduced. These techniques help to reduce the computational load and complexity of model training, while also enhancing the model's generalization capabilities. Finally, comparative experiments conducted on a proprietary badminton tactics dataset demonstrated the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model improvements when reasonable parameters were applied. The case study shows that this approach holds considerable promise for the analysis and optimization of badminton players’ training strategies.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | attention mechanisms | Badminton tactical analysis | graph neural networks | heterogeneous graph splitting | training pattern optimization

Title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Student Academic Performance in Higher Education
Abstract: In recent years, educational institutions have increasingly sought to leverage data-driven approaches to enhance student success and retention. While numerous machine learning algorithms have been created to forecast academic performance, their efficacy differs among datasets, domains, and institutional contexts. The optimal algorithm for particular settings in higher education remains uncertain. This study aims to compare multiple algorithms such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, and K-Nearest Neighbors to identify the most effective model for predicting student academic performance in higher education institutions (HEIs). This paper also introduces the application of SMOTE, which focuses on addressing class imbalance. Evaluation of multiple models comparing their performance across metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-Score was present in this paper. The results of the comparative analysis showed that Random Forest outperforms other algorithms, particularly when SMOTE is applied, with an accuracy of 97%, demonstrating its robustness and adaptability in handling imbalanced datasets. This paper underscores the capacity of machine learning to furnish educational stakeholders with novel instruments for predicting student outcomes, facilitating prompt interventions to enhance academic performance.
Keywords: Algorithm Analysis | Educational Data Mining (EDM) | Higher Education | Machine Learning | Prediction Algorithm | Random Forest | SMOTE

Title: Enhancing Cardiovascular Health through Gradient Boosting Classifier-Based Risk Prediction
Abstract: Predicting heart disease is an important field of medical research that seeks to find those who are at risk and offer prompt care. Because of its better performance in robustness and predictive accuracy among machine learning algorithms, the Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC) has become a top model. In order to assess the GBC's predictive power against other widely used models such Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, and Neural Networks, this work compares them. A large dataset including age, blood pressure, cholesterol, and electrocardiographic findings is used in the study. Results show that the GBC beats other models in terms of F1-score, accuracy, precision, and recall. GBC is a very trustworthy model for heart disease prediction since of its intrinsic capacity to manage complicated non-linear interactions and its efficiency in reducing overfitting by boosting methods. These results emphasize the Gradient Boosting Classifier's promise as a useful instrument in clinical settings for the early identification and treatment of heart disease.
Keywords: cardiac disease | healthcare | Heart disease | Machine learning

Title: Emotion Detection Mastery: EEG Signal Analysis with Balanced vs. Unbalanced Data
Abstract: Emotion is crucial in daily life, influencing stress levels, decision-making, relationships, and overall mental health. Recognizing emotions accurately is valuable across sectors like healthcare, education, and beyond. This paper presents a comparative study on emotion recognition, applying various deep learning models with the DEAP dataset, which includes EEG recordings from 32 participants who watched 40 short music video clips. We extracted time-domain, frequency-domain, and wavelet features from the preprocessed EEG data to capture nuanced patterns within the signals. The models assessed in this study include convolutional neural networks (CNN), long short-term memory networks (LSTM), gated recurrent units (GRU), and hybrid architectures, each trained on both balanced and unbalanced datasets. To address class imbalance, data was augmented using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). Results indicate that the Attention GRU model achieved slightly higher performance by utilizing its attention mechanism to capture extended dependencies within the data. Additionally, model accuracy improved by 5-9% when trained on balanced datasets, underscoring the importance of data balancing in enhancing classification outcomes.
Keywords: DEAP Dataset | Deep Learning Models | Electroencephalogram (EEG) | Emotion Recognition | Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE)

Title: Deep Learning Based DOA Estimation in Low SNR and Multipath Scenarios
Abstract: Deep Learning (DL) has revolutionized Signal and Image processing in complex environments where it is difficult to accurately define the signal model. The convolutional neural network (CNN) is DL technique that learns high level features directly from the data. By using different DL approaches, various studies have been done on direction of arrival (DOA) estimation of acoustic sources. While high-resolution algorithms MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) have been studied in literature for DOA estimation, the performance of these algorithms is limited by constraints such as low Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR), antenna element spacing and multipath scenarios. In this paper, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based technique is proposed for DOA estimation in noisy and multipath environment. It is shown that the proposed technique is robust towards these typical constraints even in scenario of closely spaced sources. Simulation results show that the proposed CNN algorithm outperforms MUSIC algorithm in low SNR, multipath environment while being computationally less intensive.
Keywords: CNN | Compressive Sensing (CS) | DL | DOA | FC | Machine Learning | Multipath | MUSIC | RMSE | SNR | Subspace | Tensor

Title: Dynamic Emotion Regulation through Reinforcement Learning: A Neurofeedback System with EEG Data and Custom Wearable Interventions
Abstract: Neurofeedback, a form of biofeedback that uses brainwave activity to provide real-time feedback, is a powerful approach for emotion regulation. Recent advancements in affective computing and machine learning offer new possibilities for improving the efficacy of neurofeedback systems, particularly through adaptive algorithms for personalizing the intervention process. This study presents an innovative neurofeedback mecha-nism that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to regulate emotions. The system uses Q-learning algorithm to dynamically adjusts its intervention strategies based on sampled EEG data from the DEAP dataset that monitors brain activity associated with emotional states. The therapeutic interventions consist of a mix of music therapy sessions, mindfulness exercises, and tactile feedback provided by a custom-built wearable device. The device utilizes tactile vibration as a neurofeedback signal to help users become more conscious of and effectively regulate their emotional well-being. The system's performance was evaluated through detailed analysis of the Q-learning process and observing how various states, actions and rewards influenced effective emotional regulation. Using sampled EEG data from the DEAP dataset enabled comprehensive testing and refinement of the system's algorithms in a controlled environment, thereby setting the stage for potential future use with real time EEG devices. The results of this study highlight the power of RL-based neurofeedback to help transform emotional wellbeing, while also showcasing the potential to expand the spectrum of neurofeedback tools to be more responsive and adaptive to individual users, ultimately promoting improved mental health.
Keywords: EEG Signal Processing | Emotion Regulation | Neurofeedback | Reinforcement Learning (RL) | Wearable Device

Title: Fine-tuned Generative Adversarial Network-based Model for Medical Image Super-Resolution
Abstract: In the field of medical image analysis, there is a substantial need for high-resolution (HR) images to improve diagnostic accuracy. However, it is a challenging task to obtain HR medical images, as it requires advanced instruments and significant time. Deep learning-based super-resolution methods can help to improve the resolution and perceptual quality of low-resolution (LR) medical images. Recently, Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) based methods have shown remarkable performance among deep learning-based super-resolution methods. Real-Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (Real-ESRGAN) is a practical model for recovering HR images from real-world LR images. In our proposed approach, we use transfer learning technique and fine-tune the pre-trained Real-ESRGAN model using medical image datasets. This technique helps in improving the performance of the model. We employ the high-order degradation model of the Real-ESRGAN which better simulates real-world image degradations. This adaptation allows for generating more realistic degraded medical images, resulting in improved performance. The focus of this paper is on enhancing the resolution and perceptual quality of chest X-ray and retinal images. We use the Tuberculosis chest X-ray (Shenzhen) dataset and the STARE dataset of retinal images for fine-tuning the model. The proposed model achieves superior perceptual quality compared to the Real-ESRGAN model, effectively preserving fine details and generating images with more realistic textures.
Keywords: Deep learning | Generative adversarial network | Medical images | Super-resolution | Transfer learning

Title: Revolutionizing Endoscopic Diagnostics: A Comparative Study of DC-UNet and MC-UNet
Abstract: Endoscopic imaging plays a pivotal role in diag-nosing and managing gastrointestinal diseases, where precise segmentation of images is essential for accurate disease detection and treatment. Traditional image segmentation methods often struggle with the complexities inherent in endoscopic images, prompting the development of advanced deep-learning models. This paper compares two novel architectures designed to improve segmentation performance: the dual-channel U-Net (DC-UNet) and the multi-channel U-Net (MC-UNet). The DC-UNet model builds on the traditional U-Net framework by incorporating dilated convolutions and residual modules to enhance feature extraction and improve segmentation accuracy. Dilated convo-lutions increase the receptive field without sacrificing spatial resolution, while residual modules facilitate better information flow across the network's layers. In addition, we present the MC-UNet, which extends the DC-UNet architecture by integrating multi-channels to capture features at varying resolutions and improve the detection of structures of different sizes. We evaluate the performance of both models on two challenging endoscopy image datasets: Kvasir-Instrument and CVC-ClinicDB. The DC-UNet achieved an accuracy of 97.34% on Kvasir-Instrument and 97.98% on CVC-ClinicDB, while the MC-UNet demonstrated slighter better performance with 98.25% and 98.19% accuracy, respectively. Our results highlight the potential of the DC-UNet and MC-UNet models to revolutionise endoscopic diagnostics by providing more accurate and reliable segmentation results, ultimately improving clinical outcomes.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Networks | Deep Learning | Dual-Channel U-Net (DC-UNet) | Endoscopy | Gastrointestinal Diseases | Image Segmentation | Medical Imaging | Multi-Channel U-Net (MC-UNet) | U-Net

Title: Analyzing the Futuristic Scope of Artificial Intelligence in the Healthcare Sector in India
Abstract: With the use of enormous databases, artificial intelligence (AI) methods are transforming the evaluation of illnesses by recognizing trends and building trustworthy systems. This method, along with the availability of large healthcare records enables physicians in India to establish more reliable diagnostic instruments, optimizing the outcomes of patients. The study examines the application of AI on information associated with liver and cardiac illnesses. A novel nutcracker search- driven kernelized support vector machine (NS-KSVM) framework is presented in this work to effectively analyze liver and cardiac illnesses. In the framework, the NS optimization strategy is employed to enhance the KSVM's parameters. To train the NS-KSVM method, datasets are initially collected from public sources. Then, a min-max scalar is applied to raw data samples for normalizing purposes. After that, linear discriminant analysis (LDA) is employed to extract the significant features from the normalized data. Then, the illness prediction process is carried out by the proposed method. This research is implemented in a Python tool to analyze the NS- KSVM's performance in terms of various metrics. It demonstrated that our proposed method achieved better performance in the healthcare sector than other existing methodologies.
Keywords: AI | diseases | Healthcare | nutcracker search-driven kernelized support vector machine (NS-KSVM) | prediction

Title: An Intelligent User-specific Music Recommendation Engine-using Machine Learning
Abstract: This research delves into the design and functionalities of a music recommendation system, encompassing user interaction, an optional emotion recognition module, and the core recommendation process leveraging user data and music features. Stressing the significance of user feedback and iterative learning for ongoing enhancement, the study also delves into metrics for evaluating system performance and discusses potential contributions and implications. By prioritizing user preferences and engagement, music recommendation systems aim to deliver personalized experiences for heightened satisfaction. Ethical considerations and a commitment to continual learning through user feedback are highlighted. Additionally, Support Vector Machines (SVM) are employed to recommend music based on user emotions, enriching the system's ability to tailor recommendations to individual emotional states. This research lays the groundwork, offering insights for further evolution and exploration in the dynamic landscape of music recommendation systems.
Keywords: Design and Functionalities | Iterative Learning | Music Features | Music Recommendation System | User Data | User Feedback | User Interaction

Title: A Deep Learning Approach to Glaucoma: CNN Role in Early Detection
Abstract: Leveraging a strong Kaggle dataset of 16,642 retinal pictures classified into glaucomatous and healthy classes, this research paper presents a thorough investigation on glaucoma diagnosis using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. Leading cause of irreversible blindness, glaucoma silently advances usually undetectable until major vision loss results. The work focuses on improving early detection using the VGG16 model, which is well-known for its deep architecture able to extract complex characteristics from retinal images. Resizing, normalizing, and data augmentation among preprocessing methods helped to raise model generalization and accuracy. With sensitivity and specificity measures proving its capacity to clearly separate glaucomatous from healthy eyes, the model attained a classification accuracy of 76%. Using F-1 scores, AUC values, and ROC curves, performance was further assessed to validate the model's glaucoma detection ability. This work highlights the possibilities of CNNs in automating glaucoma diagnosis, therefore offering a strong instrument for early management. The results support the continuous efforts to diagnose glaucoma and provide a scalable solution to be included into clinical settings to stop vision loss and maximize patient outcomes.
Keywords: AUC values | automated diagnosis | blindness prevention | classification accuracy | clinical application | Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) | data augmentation | deep learning | early diagnosis | F-1 score | Glaucoma detection | healthcare innovation | image preprocessing | Kaggle dataset | medical AI integration | ophthalmology | retinal images | ROC curves | sensitivity | specificity | sustainable development | vision loss prevention

Title: Deep MVDR: A High Resolution DoA Estimation Method against Array Gain-Phase Error
Abstract: Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation is a critical issue in array signal processing, and several classical methods such as Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) and Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC), have been proposed to solve this problem and have achieved remarkable results. However, these DoA estimation methods suffer performance degradation under model mismatches such as gain-phase errors. Deep learning (DL) methods have strong capability to learn the mapping from received data to true angles directly, achieving notable performance in model mismatches scenarios, but their performance tends to degrade in different SNRs or snapshots scenarios. To address these issues, a high-resolution DoA estimation method named Deep MVDR is proposed in this paper, which consists of covariance-enhanced autoencoder, DoA estimator and super resolution modules. These modules can utilize the feature extraction capabilities of neural networks to improve performance and refine spatial spectrum. Simulation results demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method across various target numbers, SNRs and snapshots with gain-phase errors, and show that Deep MVDR outperforms other existing methods in terms of spatial resolution.
Keywords: autoencoder | deep learning | Direction of arrival | MVDR | neural network

Title: Emotion-Aware Music Recommendations: Evaluating Custom CNN vs. VGG16 and InceptionV3
Abstract: This study conducts a comparative analysis of various pretrained models for detecting emotions from facial expressions, introducing a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) designed to enhance accuracy. We evaluate the performance of well-known models such as VGG16 and InceptionV3 alongside our proposed CNN architecture to determine the most effective model for incorporating facial emotion detection into music recommendation systems. Our system utilizes facial expressions captured through webcams or images to deliver personalized music suggestions that reflect users' current emotional states, aiming to enhance user engagement on music streaming platforms. By outlining methodology, including dataset compilation and preprocessing strategies, we test and validate our CNN architecture, revealing its superiority over existing models in accuracy. The integration of sophisticated facial emotion detection into recommendation systems offers a transformative way to improve the user experience by providing emotionally attuned music suggestions. Our findings demonstrate that this advancement holds promise for applications in digital music streaming, enhancing user engagement and personalization. By leveraging facial expression analysis, we can create more effective music recommendation systems that cater to individual users' emotional needs, leading to increased user satisfaction and loyalty.
Keywords: Advanced Recommendation Systems | Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) | Deep Learning | Emotion Recognition Accuracy | Facial Expression Recognition | Image Processing Techniques | Neural Network Architecture | Personalized Music Streaming | Pre-trained Models | Real-Time Emotion Analysis

Title: Sentiment-Based Insights Into Amazon Musical Instrument Purchases
Abstract: The project aims to analyze Amazon music instrument reviews to understand customer satisfaction in terms of key sentiments related to the products. Online shopping has made customer reviews increasingly relevant for both buyers and sellers. The project analyzes unprocessed text data using Natural Language Processing (NLP), which includes steps like text cleaning, tokenization, stop-word removal, stemming, and lemmatization. Word embeddings or term frequency-inverse document frequency (tf-idf) are used to encode the large dataset. A method of sentiment analysis on user reviews is described, with the dataset going through preliminary NLP work. Sentiments are classified using various models, evaluated based on accuracy, cross-validation scores, and classification reports. Visualization graphics depict sentiment distribution, emphasizing the potential of NLP for better sentiment analysis performance.
Keywords: Machine Learning Models | Model Evaluation and Visualization | NLP | Sentiment Analysis | Text Classification

Title: Using Transformer Models to Separate and Reduce Noise in Speaker Voice in Noisy Conference Scenarios
Abstract: Nowadays, online meetings have become an important way for people to communicate at work. With the application popularization of this meeting form and the emergence of various new functions, people's requirements for voice quality are also continuously rising. Especially in the case of noisy backgrounds and multiple speakers, obtaining clear speech signals and accurately separated speech is still a problem that needs to be solved today. To solve this problem, this study proposes a multi-speaker speech separation and noise reduction system based on the pre-trained model of the SpeechBrain library. This system combines the SpectralMaskEnhancement model and the SepformerSeparation model, respectively used for speech denoising and multi-speaker speech separation in complex noise environments. By combining the advantages of the two models, the separation and denoising effects are effectively improved. The experiment used the LibriMix dataset, and the results showed that this method achieved 18.0 dB in signal-to-noise ratio improvement (SI-SNRi) and 18.3 dB in source-to-distortion ratio improvement (SDRi), significantly improved compared to the traditional Wavesplit and the separate Sepformer model. Through experimental comparison, the fusion model outperformed conventional methods in denoising and speech separation performance, especially in complex scenarios with multi-speaker overlap and strong background noise. The method in this study can effectively improve the voice quality of the conference in noisy backgrounds and multi-speaker scenarios, and play a role in other audio fields.
Keywords: Audio processing | Computer vision | Machine learning | Speech noise reduction

Title: The Role of Digital Humanities and Machine Learning in Enhancing Critical Thinking among Select B. Tech ESL Students: A Case Study
Abstract: The paper examines how digital humanities & Machine Learning have influenced student critical thinking performance in the language classroom. Participants in this study include students from the 'The Apollo University (TAU)', Chittoor, located in Andhra Pradesh, who are all learning English as a second language. The objective of this research is to investigate the role of digital humanities in assisting students' capability on critical thinking to flourish in the academic environment. The study looks into a prospective direction for future research designs including the introduction of technological approaches into the arena of academic inquiry. To assess the impact of digital humanities on first year B. Tech students, we must examine how teachers use it in the classroom and how students feel about it. The study takes a qualitative method, analyzing the viewpoints of both students and teachers on the usage of digital humanities in the classroom. The findings of this study support the notion that traditional classroom learning should be augmented with digital resources. Both instructors and students were keen to try out new methods to education made feasible by the development of AI technology instruments. They think that this sort of environment is more favorable to learning than more traditional ones.
Keywords: AI &Digital Humanities | Critical Thinking | ESL Students | Learning and Classroom tools | Machine Learning

Title: Wavelet Decompositions, Hierarchical Encoding and Convolutional Neural Network Integrated Lossless Audio Codec
Abstract: In this paper, a lossless audio codec is proposed by leveraging Wavelet transformation, Hierarchical encoding with Convolutional Neural Network architecture. In the first phase, three level 1D wavelet decomposition is applied on the input audio for generating approximation and detail coefficients. In the next phase, the approximation and detail coefficients are transformed into binary streams by utilizing the proposed dynamic hierarchical encoding algorithm. In this encoding technique, coefficients are converted to binary by dynamically accumulating the binary path values. In the subsequent phase, the binary stream is transformed into image patterns and further compressed by reducing the dimensionality by the proposed convolutional neural network(CNN) model. The model’s effectiveness is evaluated against current conventional lossless audio benchmarks and machine learning-based methods. Experiment results demonstrate that the method shows better performance than existing lossless audio techniques.
Keywords: approximation coefficients | CNN | detail coefficients | hierarchical encoding | lossless audio compression | MAE | MSE

Title: Attention-based multi-views and multi-scale temporal information fusion convolutional neural network for motor imagery EEG decoding
Abstract: In this paper, we propose an innovative deep learning architecture called Attention-based Multi-view and Multi-scale Temporal Information Fusion Convolutional Neural Network (AMMFCNN) for decoding motor imagery EEG signals. AMMFCNN effectively captures global dependencies and multichannel, multi-temporal information. The model applies spectral filtering to the EEG data and uses channel attention mechanisms to redistribute feature weights across frequency bands. Multi-scale temporal and spatial convolutions are then applied to extract both temporal and spatial features, which are further processed using multi-head self-attention modules. These features are fused using element-wise addition before being passed to a fully connected layer for classification. Our method was validated on the BCI Competition IV 2a dataset and achieved superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its effectiveness for motor imagery EEG decoding. The results show that AMMFCNN outperforms previous models, such as EEGNet, FBCNet, IFNet, and Conformer by 9. 0 2 %, 6. 3 2 %, 2. 6 6 %, and 3.51% respectively. The source code can be found at the following link: https://github.com/Qiantoulv/ADMMFCNN.
Keywords: Attention Mechanism | EEG Decoding | Motor Imagery EEG | Multiscale Convolution

Title: Improving Early Diagnosis: An AI-Powered Method for Precise Skin Cancer Identification
Abstract: An important development in medical diagnostics is the use of artificial intelligence (AI) helps to investigate the creation and application of the system intended to detect skin cancer using pictures of skin lesions. The method uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), a type of machine learning technique, to identify lesions as benign or malignant based on its analysis of dermatoscopic pictures. Expert dermatologists gather and annotate a sizable dataset of photos of skin lesions as the first step in the procedure. Preprocessing techniques such as segmentation, normalisation, and augmentation are used to these pictures in order to increase the analysis's focus and quality. The colour, texture, and form characteristics of the lesions are analysed using feature extraction techniques, which are essential for precise categorization. CNN gains the ability to identify trends and characteristics linked to various forms of skin cancer. After training, a different set of pictures is used to verify the model and evaluate its performance in terms of ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteristic - Area Under Curve), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. After that, the AI system is incorporated into an intuitive user interface, giving dermatologists and medical professionals a trustworthy instrument for screening for skin cancer. The system's accessibility is further increased via a mobile application version, which makes initial screenings possible in underserved and rural places. Dense Net 201 performs best in training and test accuracy as well as training loss, despite being the deepest and having the most parameters. With fewer layers and parameters than Dense Net 201 and Inception V3, VGG16 performs admirably as well, particularly in training accuracy and loss. Finally, the Dense Net 201 performs the best in terms of training and test accuracy as well as training loss. Dense Net 201 is the best effective model if training time and computer resources are not limited.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Networks | Deep Learning | Dermatoscopic Images | Diagnostic Accuracy | Early Detection | Feature Extraction | Image Preprocessing

Title: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Techniques for Fake News Detection
Abstract: The proliferation of fake news has been accelerated by the growth of social media and online news outlets, which poses serious risks to social harmony, political stability, and public confidence. The research examines and compares various deep learning techniques, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model, to detect fake news. It assesses the effectiveness of these models using a sizable dataset of news reports with authenticity and falsity labels. Important performance parameters including recall, accuracy, precision, and F1-score are considered for analysis. The outcomes show that BERT networks perform better than CNN and LSTM models, with 98.17% accuracy and 98.0% F1-score. The work demonstrates how well BERT captures intricate semantic linkages in text, which makes it a potent instrument for identifying false news. It also offers insights for further research in this area and highlights the power of sophisticated deep learning approaches in improving the effectiveness of false news detection systems.
Keywords: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) | Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) | Deep learning | Fake news | Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)

Title: SEMI-SUPERVISED PIANO TRANSCRIPTION USING PSEUDO-LABELING TECHNIQUES
Abstract: Automatic piano transcription (APT) transforms piano recordings into symbolic note events. In recent years, APT has relied on supervised deep learning, which de-mands a large amount of labeled data that is often limited. This paper introduces a semi-supervised approach to APT, leveraging unlabeled data with techniques originally introduced in computer vision (CV): pseudo-labeling, consistency regularization, and distribution matching. The idea of pseudo-labeling is to use the current model for producing artificial labels for unlabeled data, and consistency regularization makes the model’s predictions for unlabeled data robust to augmentations. Finally, distribution matching ensures that the pseudo-labels follow the same marginal distribution as the reference labels, adding an extra layer of robustness. Our method, tested on three piano datasets, shows improvements over purely supervised methods and performs comparably to existing semi-supervised approaches. Conceptually, this work illustrates that semi-supervised learning techniques from CV can be effectively transferred to the music domain, considerably reducing the dependence on large annotated datasets.

Title: A Machine Learning Based Approach for Post Manufacturing Performance Sensing in Analog Circuits
Abstract: As CMOS technology advances towards miniaturization for enhanced performance, the impact of process uncertainties on analog circuits becomes increasingly pronounced, often resulting in degraded performance. In order to ensure proper functionality, the fabricated analog circuits are subjected to performance check during the production test where these are interfaced with high end Automated Test Equipment (ATE), leading to higher test cost. This work introduces a low-cost Machine Learning (ML) based non-intrusive sensing strategy for performance estimation of process perturbed analog circuits. The sensor outputs, termed as signatures are used for performance prediction using a pre-trained ML model. These sensors are placed close to the Circuit Under Test (CUT), provides an image of process variations, without actually loading it. A systematic approach for identification of sensor signatures is proposed using Recursive Feature Elimination Technique. The proposed performance sensing approach is validated on a current-starved voltage-controlled oscillator (CSVCO), where a neural network-based regression model predicts the key performance metrics in a CSVCO.
Keywords: Machine Learning | Non-intrusive Sensor | Post Manufacturing | Process uncertainties

Title: A Case Study of AI Application in Singing Research
Abstract: In the interpretation and performance style of the song "Chun Hua Qiu Yue He Shi Liao"(•) the four singers, YiJie Shi, Sen Ren, AI for YiJie Shi, and AI for Sen Ren, exhibit various differences in their approach of singing the same piece due to their diverse educational backgrounds, vocal training methods, and aesthetic perspective. We try to find the differences about different ages, educational background, singing experience between people and people, people and machines on the work of the second creation by analyzing the singing of the two singers and their robot AI, which is extracted and imitated by their timbre, and highlights the difference in the treatment of the works of the two singers. The audio recordings of these four singers (two of them are AI) were selected and imported into music visualization analysis software. Using pitch processing, tempo processing, dynamics processing, and timbre processing as entry points, the different performance approaches of these four singers were quantitatively analyzed and compared. Based on quantitative analysis, a scientific interpretation of their singing styles is provided, which opens new research methods and perspectives for sing research. It is a typical case study of AI technology enhancing learning and teaching.
Keywords: AI | dynamics processing | pitch processing | tempo processing | timbre processing

Title: Music Emotion Recognition Using Ensemble Learning
Abstract: Music has been a part of human experience for centuries and continues to serve not only as entertainment but also as therapy. As music evolves through generations, new genres and subgenres emerge, making it a highly subjective experience. Despite the challenges in determining the emotional content of music, technological advancements offer promising possibilities. This study aims to enhance the accuracy of Music Emotion Recognition (MER), targeting an improvement from the standard 73.1% accuracy achieved by previous models. To accomplish this, an ensemble model is proposed, combining three machine learning architectures: (1) ResNet50, (2) DenseNet121, and (3) VGG16. The study utilizes the DEAM dataset, which comprises 1,802 songs (including 58 full-length tracks and 1,744 excerpts of 45 seconds) from various Western popular music genres (e.g., rock, pop, electronic, country, jazz). Each piece is characterized by two numerical values representing Valence and Arousal, based on Robert Thayer's traditional circumplex mood model, which classifies emotions into four categories: (1) Happy, (2) Calm, (3) Angry, (4) Sad, and four additional emotions. The model's performance will be evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The proposed model obtained an accuracy score of 86.13%, a precision score of 85%, a recall score of 84% and an F1- score of 84%. The results show that the proposed ensemble model was able to better classify the emotion in music than the individual CNN models. Keywords - circumplex mood model, DEAM dataset, DenseNet121, ensemble model, machine learning, music emotion recognition, ResNet50, VGG16, Western popular music genres.
Keywords: CNN | DEAM dataset | Ensemble Learning | Music Emotion Recognition | Robert Thayer'sModel | Western pop

Title: A Decision-Making Framework for Financial Trading Using Linear Tree-Based Kernel Support Vector Machine Classifier
Abstract: In today's rapidly evolving financial landscape, numerous investors and hedge funds have gravitated towards stock markets, captivated by their extensive range of instruments and lucrative investment opportunities. Despite their allure, navigating the stock market landscape is intricate. It demands financial traders to remain vigilant, identifying thriving firms and diligently tracking stock price oscillations to devise potent trading strategies. In recent times, cutting-edge technological advancements like artificial intelligence and machine learning have revolutionized stock price predictions. Machine learning (ML) algorithms, especially Support Vector Machines (SVM), have become instrumental in predicting stock movements. However, an often-underacknowledged limitation of SVM is its susceptibility to overfit in the presence of noisy and intricate datasets. Addressing this gap, our research introduces the innovative Linear Tree-based Kernel Support Vector Machine (LT-KSVM) for enhanced stock market price forecasts. We empirically validated our approach by creating a portfolio of stocks from the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul). Simulated trades over a span of 3.7 years were deployed to assess the portfolio's predicted performance. We meticulously executed three preprocessing phases to enhance stock price movement forecasts. Remarkably, our proposed framework demonstrated astounding potential, boasting over 90% returns.
Keywords: financial trading | Stock market | stock price forecasting | support vector machine

Title: Friction signal denoising based on deep learning
Abstract: Addressing the issue of noise present in friction signals collected by scanning probe microscopy instruments, a denoising method for friction signals based on deep learning is proposed. This article proposes a denoising model that combines convolutional autoencoder, deep residual network, and attention mechanism. By using convolutional blocks and attention mechanism, different weights can be assigned to signal features. The residual network can effectively prevent gradient explosion and network degradation caused by increasing network depth. Generate simulated friction signals through numerical calculations and add Gaussian white noise to construct a training set for training and testing the model. This method successfully increased the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of the signal by about 26dB, demonstrating excellent noise reduction performance.
Keywords: deep learning | friction | signal denoising

Title: Pleiades Neo satellites: new assets for emergency response and disasters management
Abstract: The use of Earth Observation satellites in support of emergency response is not new: operational since October 2020, the International Charter "Space and Major Disasters"was the first international initiative aimed at establishing a unified system for triggering the acquisition of space data when a major disaster strikes. In Europe, the Copernicus Emergency Management Service, whose precursor service was launched in 2009, is operational since April 2012. The very-high-resolution satellites are the most interesting assets, in particular after earthquakes, hurricanes or other disasters affecting urban areas: beyond the first estimates of damages, they allow to provide detailed delineation and grading maps supporting the first responders and other users involved in crisis management. The first part of the paper is a reminder of the performances requirements and challenges of services supporting emergency response activities, from an end-to-end perspective. Launched in 2021, the two Pléiades Neo satellites are among the most recent assets worldwide providing both very high resolution and very fast revisit. The second section explains how this operational performance became a reality with significant efforts in technology development in an end-to-end perspective: imaging instrument (providing the 30-cm native imagery), satellite platform aimed at improving revisit frequency and daily coverage, network of ground stations and the operational command, control and tasking procedures, designed to optimise the end-to-end acquisition time (from tasking decision to reception of the first image of the area of interest) and, last but not least, performance of the ground processing and image distribution chain with very innovative features. In particular, it highlights the benefits of a disruptive processing solution, based on machine-learning algorithms, aimed at delivering high definition (HD15) products from native imagery at 30-cm resolution or able to automatically extract 3D building from stereo pairs. The third part of the paper shows Pléiades Neo satellites in action with recent representative examples of operational use, e. g. during the wild fires season (summer 2023), after the Earthquake in Morocco (September 2023), the deadly floods in Mexico (October 2023) and other more recent disasters. These examples illustrate the addedvalue of Pléiades Neo and the contribution if the innovative functions. The conclusion gives an outlook of future work planned by Airbus Defence to improve further performance.
Keywords: Copernicus | disasters management | Earth Observation | emergency response | Pléiades Neo | rapid mapping | reactive imagery

Title: The Research Focuses on the Classification and Recognition of Speech Imagery EEG Signals Based on a Fusion Network Autoencoder
Abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals present significant challenges in processing and analysis due to their low signal-to-noise ratio, nonlinearity, and non-stationarity. Traditional feature extraction methods struggle to effectively capture the complex spatiotemporal patterns inherent in EEG signals. In recent years, various deep learning frameworks have demonstrated excellent performance in decoding electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. However, most frameworks tend to focus on unidimensional features, making it challenging to effectively integrate spatial and temporal characteristics. This paper proposes a model structure that integrates a fusion network based on CNN and LSTM embedded within an autoencoder. The CNN is used to extract spatial features from the EEG signals, while the LSTM is employed to capture the temporal dependencies and dynamic patterns of the signals. By embedding the CNN+LSTM fusion network within the autoencoder, the model can learn and represent the complex spatiotemporal dependency features of EEG signals. Experiments conducted on the imagined speech dataset from Track #3 of the 2020 International BCI Competition demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits significant advantages in feature extraction compared to existing models, particularly in classification tasks. The model achieves classification accuracies of 92.49% for binary one-vs-many classification and 69.01% for five-class classification.
Keywords: Autoencoder | CNN | EEG | Fusion Network | Speech Imagery

Title: Revolutionizing Leukemia Diagnosis: Fine-Tuned VGG19 CNN for Enhanced Classification Accuracy
Abstract: The complicated haematological cancer leukemia calls for precise and quick diagnosis techniques to increase patient outcomes. The VGG19 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture is explored in this work for leukemia classification from high-resolution blood pictures. With a dataset of 7,500 photos split into four categories - "Benign,""Malignant Pre-B,""Malignant-B,"and "Malignant early Pre-B"- the study seeks to improve automated leukemia detection by use of modern image processing and deep learning methods. Renowned for strong feature extraction, the VGG19 model is optimized with bespoke classification layers targeted for leukemia diagnosis. Early stopping and learning rate scheduling help to maximize performance by means of the Adam optimizer and categorical cross-entropy loss function in the training process. With accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix among other evaluation measures, the tuned VGG19 model shows an overall accuracy of 99%. With modest classification mistakes in "Benign"and "Malignant early Pre-B"instances, the model exhibits extraordinary performance in separating between leukemia subtypes. This work validates that the VGG19-based CNN method greatly improves automated leukemia classification, so offering a trustworthy instrument for raising diagnosis accuracy and helping medical practitioners in leukemia treatment.
Keywords: Automated Diagnosis | Classification Metrics | Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) | Data Augmentation | Deep Learning | Diagnostic Accuracy | Feature Extraction | Haematological Malignancy | High-Resolution Blood Images | Image Preprocessing | Leukemia Classification | Machine Learning | Medical Imaging | VGG19 Architecture

Title: Marching Forward: Redefining Human-Machine Interactions in Conversational AI Through Hybrid Intelligence, Blockchain Security, and Autonomous Agents
Abstract: Conversational AI has emerged as an essential instrument in enhancing human-computer interaction, with applications spanning customer service to personal assistants. This paper offers a comprehensive examination of recent developments in conversational AI, including novel techniques in natural language generation (NLG), dialogue systems, and dynamic response optimization. We analyze advancements including transformer-based architectures, reinforcement learning for dialogue generation, and retrieval-augmented models, emphasizing their roles in enhancing the quality and contextual accuracy of conversations. Additionally, we examine the feasibility of blockchain technology as the foundation for decentralized AI, promoting secure, transparent, and distributed frameworks for AI applications, hence improving privacy and control in data exchanges. Hybrid methodologies that combine symbolic reasoning with deep learning are analyzed, highlighting their effectiveness in addressing complex dialogues. These advancements, supported by empirical research and benchmark performance, signify the evolution towards more personalized, intelligent, and decentralized conversational systems.
Keywords: Chatbot | Conversational AI | Generative Model | Human-machine interaction

Title: Enhanced Brain Tumor Classification Using Optimized Convolutional Neural Networks: A Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: In brain tumors, both benign and malignant tumors significantly compromise health and call for accurate diagnosis and classification for the best therapy. This work uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Deep Learning's ability to improve the accuracy of brain tumor categorization. Variations in CNN design are investigated to maximize model performance on a dataset including 7,523 MRI pictures categorized as glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and non-tumor categories. The CNN model significantly improved accuracy by varying the learning rate and changing dropout and flattening layers; it reached up to 99% while lowering loss to as low as 0.0039. This work emphasizes the possibilities of DL in medical imaging, especially for automated brain tumor categorization, therefore providing a strong instrument for early and accurate diagnosis.
Keywords: and Innovation | Artificial Intelligence | Brain Tumor | CNN | Deep Learning | Glial Cells | Glioma | Healthcare | Machine Learning | Medical | Research

Title: Influencing Consumer Behaviour on E-Commerce Platforms Through Social Media Marketing Using BiLSTM-KNN Models
Abstract: E-commerce systems depend significantly on comprehending and forecasting consumer behaviour, frequently shaped by social media marketing. Current methodologies in this domain exhibit deficiencies in precision and computational efficacy. This study introduces an innovative hybrid model that integrates BiLSTM and KNN to improve customer behaviour prediction by utilizing social media sentiment and e-commerce behavioural data. The model markedly surpasses current technologies, with an accuracy of 96.5%, an F1 score of 96.0%, and a recall of 97.0%. The suggested approach adeptly incorporates sequential dependencies and neighbourhood-based categorization, rendering it a formidable instrument for forecasting consumer behaviour. The model improves performance indicators and decreases training time, rendering it extremely appropriate for practical applications in e-commerce systems.
Keywords: accuracy optimization | Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory-K-Nearest Neighbors (BiLSTM-KNN) | consumer behaviour prediction | deep learning | e-commerce | F1 score evaluation | feature extraction | hybrid models | machine learning | recall improvement | sentiment analysis | social media marketing

Title: Echo Cancellation Based on Improved Wave-U-Net
Abstract: Most current implementations of deep learning-based echo cancellation algorithms use the short-time Fourier transform domain, but this approach may be limited by frame size selection and lack of accurate phase information. To overcome these limitations, in this paper, we will use the Wave-U-Net temporal network model as the baseline model for single-channel echo cancellation. Wave-U-Net performs better than traditional methods and neural networks in speech processing tasks; however, in the echo cancellation domain, the model still underperforms in near-end microphone speech feature extraction, and its ability to low distinction between near-end and far-end speech features, which is easy to cause confusion. Based on this, this paper will optimize the structure of Wave-U-Net network, aiming to improve its efficiency and performance of echo cancellation.
Keywords: echo cancellation | feature extraction | Wave-U-Net

Title: Optimizing Synthesis Parameters of BiFeO3 Nanoparticles with Bayesian Neural Networks
Abstract: The research focuses on improving synthesis parameters for BiFeO<inf>3</inf> nanoparticles, a material with substantial promise in many applications. Conventional approaches frequently fail to precisely forecast the most favorable circumstances for synthesis due to the intricate nature of the process. This article introduces a BNN model as a solution to these restrictions. The BNN model underwent training and validation using datasets obtained from Kaggle and the Materials Project. It achieved a training accuracy of 98.5% and a validation accuracy of 97.8%. The model achieved an F1 score of 0.975 and a recall of 0.980, surpassing the performance of current technology in the sector. The findings presented here showcase the efficacy of the suggested model in delivering precise and dependable predictions, rendering it a helpful instrument for academics and practitioners in the realm of material synthesis.
Keywords: Accuracy | Bayesian Neural Network | BiFeO3 Nanoparticles | F1 Score | Hyperparameter Tuning | Machine Learning | Material Science | Model Architecture | Recall | Synthesis Optimization

Title: Optimization and Performance Evaluation of Personalized Algorithm in Music Recommendation System
Abstract: Music recommendation system (MRS) is a system that recommends music content for users based on their historical behavior and interests. Personalized algorithm is the core technology of MRS, which provides personalized music recommendation for users by analyzing their behaviors and interests. However, there are some problems in the current personalized algorithm, such as too much concentration of recommendation results and lack of diversity of recommendation results. Therefore, it is of great significance to optimize and evaluate the performance of personalized algorithms. In this paper, experimental method and comparative method are adopted to analyze content-based, user-based and hybrid recommendation algorithms, and attention mechanism and multi-task learning in deep learning are taken as improvement methods to improve the accuracy and effectiveness of personalized recommendation. Experimental results show that the hit rate of the improved algorithm is up to 0.79. The improved method presented in this paper achieves good performance on multiple data sets.
Keywords: attention mechanism | deep learning | music recommendation system | personalized algorithm

Title: Seismometer Fault Detection Based on Unsupervised Machine Learning Using Time Series Features
Abstract: Seismometers are critical instruments in earthquake monitoring networks, and their reliable performance ensures the accuracy of earthquake data. While several networks have implemented methods to monitor system health, these methods are often broad and require further analysis to pinpoint specific problems. Due to their high sensitivity, seismometers are prone to failures, and early detection of malfunctions is essential. However, seismometer fault detection remains an underexplored research area despite its importance. To address this gap, we adopt a novelty detection approach within an industrial predictive maintenance (PdM) framework, demonstrating effective fault detection. Three unsupervised machine learning (ML) models - Isolation Forest (IF), One-Class Support Vector Machine (OCSVM), and Local Outlier Factor (LOF) - are implemented. Optimal parameter is achieved to enhance each model's performance by setting the contamination parameter in IF to 0.005, nu in OCSVM to 0.05, and enabling the "true"option for LOF novelties. Suppose performance was significantly worse among the three models. LOF had an impressive accuracy of 0.98, closely followed by OCSVM. These results provide a preliminary step toward developing an effective PdM strategy. More broadly, this approach can be applied across various domains related to anomaly detection, offering a robust alternative to traditional labeling techniques for large datasets.
Keywords: machine learning | novelty detection | seismometer fault | unsupervised learning

Title: 1D CNN-Based Traditional Instrument Classification and Notation Generation in Sinhala for Gataberaya and Flute
Abstract: Applications for traditional musical instruments from Sri Lanka have not received enough attention, even with the progress in machine learning. This paper presents a novel method for categorizing and transcribing notations for the flute and gataberaya which is an indigenous drum from Sri Lanka using deep learning methods. Based on a manually recorded audio recording dataset with 168 flute recordings and 81 gataberaya recordings with varying lengths and single-noted, 1D Convolutional Neural Networks were used to construct a classification model. The system also generates musical notations from audio recordings using an algorithm and converts Western musical notation to Sinhala musical notations using a prompt with a Large Language Model API call. The methodology includes data augmentation for raw data and feature extraction with Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients, and frequency analysis using the Fast Fourier Transform. The classification model achieved 88.71% training accuracy and 91.16% validation accuracy, successfully identifying instrument types, and the notation generation for the flute shows effectiveness by correctly recognizing the notes and the relative octave of the frequency. However, challenges remain for unpitched instruments like the Gataberaya due to the limited dataset. This approach acts as a valuable tool for the preservation of Sri Lankan traditional music.
Keywords: 1D CNN | Deep Learning | Large Language Model | Music Transcription | Sinhala Musical Notation

Title: RoseGuard: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Rose Leaf Diseases for Precision Agriculture
Abstract: This study presents an advanced Convolutional Neural Networks, model that has been specifically designed for the precise categorization of rose leaf diseases. The CNN model encompasses eight different classes. To tackle the complex problem of disease diagnosis, the architecture of the model, which consists of three convolutional layers, three max-pooling layers, and two fully linked layers, has been rigorously built. Using a dataset that is both broad and carefully curated, the model displays outstanding performance by reaching high precision, recall, and F1-Score values for each illness class. The fact that the model can make accurate predictions over a wide range of illness categories is demonstrated by the fact that it has an overall accuracy of 98%. The practical ramifications of this research extend beyond the areas of technical excellence to include rose farmers. It offers a dependable instrument for the early diagnosis of diseases and the focused intervention of those diseases. The findings highlight the potential of the deep learning approach that was presented to contribute to environmentally responsible agriculture practices and to reduce revenue losses in the flower business. Through the establishment of a solid platform for future breakthroughs in automated disease of plant identification, this research contributes to the ongoing transformation of precision agriculture brought about by technological advancements. In a nutshell, the CNN model that was constructed not only demonstrates a high level of technical expertise but also shows potential for improving agriculture sustainability and resilience in the context of rose leaves disease control.
Keywords: Business | Diseases | Research | Technology

Title: Efficient Rice Grain Classification Using MobileNetV2: A Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: Rice grain categorization guarantees quality control and variety identification needed for commerce and consumption, therefore serving a critical function in agriculture. Five rice varieties: Arborio, Basmati, Ipsala, Jasmine, and Karacadag are categorized in this work using the MobileNetV2 model. High-resolution photos displaying these deviations collected from the Kaggle open source website make up the dataset. Our approach pre-processes the photos, uses transfer learning to train the MobileNetV2 model, and then assesses its performance using conventional benchmarks. Across all classes, the model produced outstanding performance showing great accuracy, recall, and F1-scores. The model especially generated a precision of 0.99, recall of 0.99, and F1-score of 0.99 for Arborio, Basmati, Jasmine, and Karacadag who scored a perfect 1.00 in all metrics Ipsala. Reflecting typically robustness and efficiency, the model had an accuracy of 0.99. These findings show that MobileNetV2 is quite capable of differentiating between several rice varieties, therefore providing a dependable and effective instrument for automated rice grain categorization. The results of this study have major consequences for enhancing quality control and automation in rice farming, therefore enabling more accurate and effective sorting techniques.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Deep Learning | MobileNetV2 Model | Model Training | Rice Grain Classification

Title: Potential of Deep Learning Technique to Enhance the Accuracy of ECG Heartbeats Arrhythmia Time Series
Abstract: The cardiac system's heart is in charge of producing both bloodstreams with and without oxygen. It does not function like a rhythm instrument, and variations in heart rate is the term used to describe the normal change in the length of the periodic intervals between a pulse. ECG signals are an essential means of keeping track on the circulatory system's health and functioning. They also help identify cardiac irreg- ularities, particularly arrhythmias. Automated ECG arrhythmia categorization that is accurate and efficient is becoming more and more important. Since the beginning of the last century, deep learning has developed quickly, reaching state-of-the-art performance in a number of disciplines. The intent of this study is to demonstrate deep learning techniques which is used to directly correlate the degree of disease with the heart's variability, which includes the actual application of these methods for the simple analysis of time series to forecast different illness kinds. Deeper comprehension of the clustering algorithm regarding the concepts of underlying discrimination, model uncertainty, and a qualitative interpret ability study supplement these evaluation and offer points of convergence for further investigation into the dataset. The results we obtain highlight the potential of deep learning-based algorithms for ECG analysis, not merely in terms of statistical accuracy but also in considerations of additional quality criteria that are practical and quantifiable, like interpretability and uncertainties estimates.
Keywords: Anomaly Detection | Arrhythmia Classification | Deep Learning | Electrocardiogram (ECG) | Time series

Title: Facial Recognition in Patient Monitoring Systems: Advanced Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Using sophisticated CNNs to improve healthcare delivery, facial recognition technology has emerged as a crucial instrument in patient monitoring systems. This technology has become more important in recent years. This solution makes use of powerful CNN architectures to reliably identify and verify patients based on facial characteristics. As a result, it enables patients to have access to their medical information and personalised treatment plans in a way that is both smooth and safe. These systems are able to monitor the health of patients, identify any abnormalities, and offer early warnings for medical actions because they integrate high-resolution imaging with real-time processing. Because the use of such sophisticated CNNs guarantees a high level of accuracy and resilience in a variety of clinical settings, face recognition has become an extremely significant asset in the domain of contemporary healthcare technology. The hybrid model, which combines ResNet and DenseNet, outperforms both architectures in deep learning tasks, especially in medical diagnostics. It improves feature learning, stable training, and gradient flow by combining ResNet's residual connections with DenseNet's dense connections. This approach addresses individual model limitations, reducing overfitting and improving generalization. The hybrid model shows higher accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity compared to ResNet and DenseNet alone. Radar charts demonstrate its performance across various medical datasets, demonstrating its potential for handling complex medical data.
Keywords: CNNs | Facial Recognition | Healthcare Technology | Patient Authentication | Patient Monitoring Systems

Title: EMVD dataset: a dataset of extreme vocal distortion techniques used in heavy metal
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Extreme Metal Vocals Dataset, which comprises a collection of recordings of extreme vocal techniques performed within the realm of heavy metal music. The dataset consists of 760 audio excerpts of 1 second to 30 seconds long, totaling about 100 min of audio material, roughly composed of 60 minutes of distorted voices and 40 minutes of clear voice recordings. These vocal recordings are from 27 different singers and are provided without accompanying musical instruments or post-processing effects. The distortion taxonomy within this dataset encompasses four distinct distortion techniques and three vocal effects, all performed in different pitch ranges. Performance of a state-of-the-art deep learning model is evaluated for two different classification tasks related to vocal techniques, demonstrating the potential of this resource for the audio processing community.
Keywords: dataset | extreme metal music | machine learning | vocal distortion

Title: Integrative Framework for Accurate Corriander Disease Classification: Unifying Deep Learning and Machine Learning Approaches with Feature-Rich Hybrid Models
Abstract: The purpose of this study is to present a revolutionary methodology for the precise categorization of plant diseases. The methodology makes use of a combination method that combines advanced machine learning and deep learning approaches. For the purpose of accomplishing robust feature extraction, the model that has been developed incorporates resulting radial distances, features based on leaf perimeters, and RGB color moments. A Random Forest classifier is developed during the training phase by making use of these features, and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is utilized as a feature extractor during this phase. The model is evaluated with the help of a dataset that contains photos of a variety of plant diseases. These diseases include powdery mildew, leaf spot, downy mildew, Cercospora leaf blight, bacterial leaf spot, Fusarium wilt, and Aster yellows. The remarkable performance of the model over a wide range of illness categories is highlighted by the thorough evaluation measures, which include precision, recall, and Fl-Score. It is noteworthy that the methodology that has been described obtains an amazing overall accuracy of 98%. The study makes use of a comprehensive confusion matrix and delivers metrics that are specific to each class. This provides a comprehensive insight of the algorithm's strengths as well as areas that could want significant improvement. Additionally, the research evaluates the proposed hybrid model in comparison to the most advanced leaf recognition techniques currently available, hence establishing the hybrid model's competitive advantage and its applicability for practical applications. The findings provide evidence that the model is reliable in the identification of plant diseases, highlighting the way in which it has the potential to be an invaluable instrument for precise farming and efficient crop management. In general, the integrated strategy that has been proposed makes a significant contribution to the field of plant disease classification by providing a solution that is dependable and accurate for the early diagnosis and intervention of diseases.
Keywords: Agriculture | Crop | Food | Forest | Precision

Title: Multi-Task Learning Approaches for Music Similarity Representation Learning Based on Individual Instrument Sounds
Abstract: Music similarity representation learning (MSRL) based on individual instrument sounds (InMSRL) is a potential technique to develop a new function in music recommendation and retrieval systems, allowing users to focus on multiple partial elements of music pieces. There have been proposed two main approaches, Cascade that sequentially performs music source separation (MSS) and music similarity feature extraction for each instrument sound and Direct that directly extracts disentangled music similarity features. Each approach has a specific problem; in Cascade, a separation error often causes adverse effects on the feature extraction; and in Direct, it is usually hard to learn accurately disentangled features. In this paper, we propose multitask learning approaches to leveraging MSS to address these issues. For Cascade, we propose end-to-end fine-tuning of the MSS model and the music similarity feature extractors using an auxiliary separation loss. For Direct, we propose multi-task learning based on the disentangled music similarity feature extraction and MSS based on reconstruction with the disentangled music similarity features. We conduct experimental evaluations and demonstrate that 1) the end-to-end fine-tuning for Cascade significantly improves InMSRL performance, 2) the multi-task learning for Direct is also helpful to improve disentanglement performance in the feature extraction, and 3) Cascade with the end-to-end fine-tuning outperforms Direct with the multi-task learning.

Title: Real-time Musical Collaboration with a Probabilistic Model
Abstract: This paper describes the development of a system to play an ancient Basque collaborative percussion instrument (the txalaparta) with a human performer. A deep probabilistic model was trained on two large datasets, and transfer learning used to train the model on high-quality data abstracted from txalaparta performances. The aim is to create a system that effectively responds to the human player in a performance environment, where the model’s response must feel instantaneous, organic, and sensible in response to the user’s input. The paper outlines the design and implementation of the system, including data collection, model training, and performance visualization. The study contributes to the field of interactive music systems and demonstrates the potential of deep learning in creating intelligent musical systems that can collaborate with human performers.
Keywords: Collaborative Instruments | Deep Learning | Human-Machine Interaction | Music Generation | Txalaparta

Title: A Deep Learning Approach to Classify Skin Cancer
Abstract: A effective treatment for skin cancer depends on early discovery, which may be a major around the world health issue. This study offers a interesting strategy for dependably classifying skin injuries as benign or malignant by utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are a promising strategy with incredible potential for skin cancer screening. CNNs are well-known for their capacity to observe complex designs from picture data and are able of accurately recognizing benign or malignant skin injuries. Analysts can make exceptionally valuable demonstrative devices by utilizing enormous datasets of skin injury photos to prepare CNN models. Methods like information augmentation, ensemble approaches, transfer learning, attention mechanisms, and generative ill-disposed systems can be utilized to make strides execution indeed encourage. Besides, making mobile and cloud-based apps and examining logical AI can progress the impact and openness of skin cancer diagnosis. CNNs are idealize for this reason because of their reputation for being able to extract complex patterns from visual information. Our approach involves employing a sizable dataset of photographs of skin injuries that have been meticulously labeled to prepare a CNN show. The demonstrate is planning to secure discriminative properties, such as asymmetry, uneven borders, color change, distance across, and creating characteristics, that distinguish benign from malignant tumors. The results of our tests appear how well our proposed CNN-based strategy works to distinguish skin cancer at high accuracy rates. The demonstrate ceaselessly beats out conventional machine learning approaches, illustrating the benefits of profound learning strategies in this field. This ponder progresses the field of dermatology's computer-aided conclusion, giving a possibly valuable instrument to assist therapeutic specialists distinguish and treat skin cancer early on.
Keywords: benignant | Convolutional Neural Network | Malignant | Skin Cancer | Transfer Learning

Title: Model and Data Management for Machine Learning (M2ML): Integrating Instruments, Edge and HPC for Accelerated Machine Learning
Abstract: The use of data produced by scientific instruments, such as the Advanced Photon Source Upgrade (APS-U), to train and fine-tune machine learning models is becoming increasingly challenging due to high data production rates, large data volumes, and the growing complexity of machine learning models. To address these challenges, researchers have developed frameworks like fairDMS to efficiently organize vast amounts of data and models for rapid querying when model degradation is detected. However, the complexity of these frameworks and the physically distributed nature of experimental facilities complicate their deployment.Here we introduce a high-performance model and data management framework for machine learning, M2ML. In contrast to previous frameworks, M2ML abstracts the tasks into three key elements that can be easily called and accessed by users. M2ML is capable of utilizing a variety of computational resources, that are distributed across scientific facilities, to accelerate machine learning tasks. For example, it can automatically transfer data from an experimental facility (such as APS-U) to a high performance computing (HPC) facility (such as the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility (ALCF)), train machine learning models at the HPC facility, and deploy the trained models on edge computing devices back at the experimental facility for inferencing.
