The high performance indicates the potential of the use of non-invasive spectral techniques in honey adulteration.
Keywords: anomaly detection | chemometrics | feature-level fusion | spectroscopic analysis

Title: Deep learning Models Used to Generate the Music in Natural Language Process
Abstract: For the goal of generating art, including music, deep learning-based language models shown encouraging outcomes. However, because to the subjective nature of music, it is difficult to put a numerical value on how well a performance sounds. As a result, most evaluations of symbolic musical generation models rely on simplistic mathematical measures, such the loss function's output. Using just creation of classical piano music, the goal of this study was to quantify and assess musical samples generated by models of deep learning from a human viewpoint. Using musical samples composed by humans and musical samples produced by artificial intelligence models, such as Performance RNN, Music Out of the 118 people who took part in the assessment, 118 were blind tested using Transformer, Muse Net, & a GRU-based proprietary model. During the experiments, it was shown that musical samples created using models based on the architecture of the Transformers neural networks were the most responsive to the test population, surpassing human compositions. In addition, the results demonstrated that participants' ability to identify the compositional source of audible samples was significantly enhanced by their degree of musical sensitivity & competence.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Deep Learning | Music Transformer | Neural Network | Transformer

Title: Exploring Cloud Computing for Real-Time Analysis and Storage of Data Generated by Medical Devices
Abstract: Real-time analysis and storage of data measured by native medical instruments, including insulin pump, pacemaker, and wearable monitor, is crucial for the advancement of modern healthcare and that has made cloud computing vital. These devices produce real-time data that has to be analyzed to make timely interventions in the projects. This work discusses the execution of these devices by using cloud- based systems such as AWS and Google Cloud for dealing with the data produced by such devices. Since cloud is inherently scalable and computational, real-time monitoring and analytical capabilities is possible, potentially beneficial in diabetes and arrhythmias. The implementation of Random Forest model together with LSTM models improved the accuracy in diseases diagnosis and patient tracking. Various strategies to tackle the scarcity issue of the real-time data include data augmentation techniques which acted as a powerful strategy used to enhance the performance of the models. The results indicated excellent fitness in outcome anticipation while the evaluation time in the cloud platforms was remarkably low. For patient monitoring, another web-based dashboard was also designed to show information about patient health to allow healthcare professionals monitor their patients from a distance. Of course, the system presented in the paper is effective when it comes to monitoring patients in real time; however, issues like network delay and syncing the devices used in healthcare facilities persist. It will be therefore deduced from this study that cloud computing is an apt answer to the real-time processing and archiving of medical related data with tangible impacts on the quality of patient care. Continuing work will involve including edge computing to enhance the system's performance in a low connectivity situation with less delay.
Keywords: Cloud Computing | Data Storage | Healthcare Data | Machine Learning | Medical Devices | Real-Time Data Analysis

Title: Dynamic Financial Time Series Modeling with Rapid Adaptation via Meta Learning
Abstract: The Meta learning framework for financial time series forecasting is proposed here, which can adapt to new financial market datasets efficiently with minimal retraining. This methodology includes two phases: the first one is cross-financial time series training on a meta-model and the second adapts this meta-model using recent data to novel market conditions. This approach of dynamic feature augmentation enhances model adaptability across a wide range of financial instruments. The performance results show that the adjusted model has higher accuracy and flexibility compared to the baseline methods. In summary, the contributions of this paper offer a robust flexible model for use in forecasting outcomes for various financial instruments and address several challenges in traditional machine learning models when applied in complex and dynamic financial markets. The proposed framework achieves a 67.33% directional accuracy (DA) in the stock market, significantly outperforming baseline models with a DA of 43.82%.
Keywords: Adaptive models | Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGboost) | Feature engineering | Financial forecasting | Meta-learning | Time series analysis

Title: Surgical Tools Detection and Localization using YOLO Models for Minimization of Retained Surgical Items
Abstract: Accurate identification and localization of surgical instruments during procedures are essential for minimizing the risk of retained surgical items. Such retained items result in serious and preventable health complications for patients. This paper investigates the application of YOLO (You Only Look Once) deep learning models for the real-time detection and localization of surgical instruments, aiming to minimize the occurrence of retained surgical items (RSIs) during surgical procedures. With the increasing complexity of surgical environments, the need for robust and efficient object detection systems has become paramount. The methodology involves a comparative analysis of YOLO versions, including YOLOv5, YOLOv8, and YOLOv10, to evaluate their performance in detecting and classifying surgical tools. The models were trained on a specialized dataset that included diverse surgical scenarios, ensuring a comprehensive assessment of their capabilities. Key performance metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 score were utilized to quantify the effectiveness of each model, with results indicating high performance across the board, particularly in distinguishing between various surgical instruments. The findings demonstrate that YOLO models, particularly the latest versions, possess significant potential for Integration into surgical environments, enhancing the tracking and monitoring of surgical tools. The study concludes that implementing these models could improve patient safety by reducing the risk of RSIs, thereby contributing to the advancement of automated systems in healthcare.
Keywords: Deep Learning Models | Healthcare | Patient Safety | Retained Surgical Items (RSIs) | Surgical Tools Detection | YOLO (You Only Look Once)

Title: Intelligent Systems for Chronic Disease Management: Integrating IOT and AI for Enhanced Delivery of Healthcare
Abstract: The latest advancements like Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and cloud computing have transformed healthcare from conventional to intelligent in order to enhance medical care. Healthcare potential arises from IoT and AI convergence. The proposed system introduces an IoT and AI-based illness diagnosis framework for modern healthcare delivery infrastructures. The article aims to induce a health problem detection algorithm for diabetes and heart disease utilizing IoT and AI integration approaches. The approach comprises data collecting, preprocessing, categorization, and modification parameter. IoT devices like sensors and wearables enable data collecting, while AI approaches diagnose diseases using the data. The method presents a Crow Search Optimization (CSO) algorithm-based Cascade Long Short-Term Memory (CLSTM) model for disease diagnosis. CSO is utilized to adjust the bias and weight parameters of the CLSTM structure to enhance medical data categorization. Additionally, the Isolation Forest (iForest) approach is utilized to eliminate outliers in this approach. CSO improves CLSTM method diagnostics significantly. CSO-LSTM model performance was validated using information related to healthcare. In experiments, the CSO-LSTM model achieved the highest accuracies of 97.02% and 97.7% in identifying diabetes and heart disease. Thus, the CSO-LSTM structure is a suitable instrument for diagnosing diseases for intelligent healthcare structures.
Keywords: Cascade Long Short Terms memory network (CLSTM) | Crow search optimization Algorithm | Internet of Things (IoT) | Isolation Forest

Title: Audio Sentiment Detection using a Hybrid Analysis Model
Abstract: Analyzing customer sentiment calls is crucial for organizations to monitor customer satisfaction, identify pain points, and improve service quality. Performing sentiment analysis on audio input, while difficult, is a vital aspect of research in the field of NLP, that can yield valuable insights into the emotional tone and attitudes expressed in spoken language.The SemEval 2016 [1], SemEval 2014 [2], and IMDB [3] datasets contain thousands of annotated reviews that serve as a resource for training and evaluation.This paper proposes a thorough approach for sentiment analysis on audio inputs, emphasizing speech-to-text conversion, text preprocessing, numerical representation using Word2Vec, Count Vectorizer, and TF-IDF techniques, and the development of multiple hybrid models. Each of the models is assessed according to metrics for accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. High accuracies of 86.58% for TF-IDF+Naive Bayes, 84.90% for Naive Bayes, 84.42% for CNN+SVM, and 67% for CNN+LSTM are shown in the results, demonstrating the usefulness of the suggested methodology for sentiment prediction tasks.By providing insightful information for applications in domains including opinion mining, social media monitoring, and customer feedback analysis, this research advances sentiment analysis techniques on audio inputs. Future developments in the fields of sentiment analysis and audio processing are outlined, along with additional improvements and expansions of the suggested methodology.
Keywords: Audio Sentiment Analysis | Hybrid model | Naiive Bayes Classifier | Text Transcription | TF-IDF

Title: Evaluating the impact of HPC on AI-driven cellular signaling simulations
Abstract: Artificial intelligence and highly performing computers are altering cellular communication. Together, these two instruments have brought about this transformation. AI runs these computer models for cell signaling, and this paper investigates how high-performance computing alters them. This paper presents a novel model. This approach combines mixed learning, dynamic network analysis, and parallel computing to help one better grasp how cellular signaling networks function and evolve throughout time. We evaluate the proposed approach in relation to others to highlight its efficiency and degree of improvement. These parallels indicate the effectiveness of the approach. These results demonstrate that a comprehensive understanding of the dynamics of live communication networks necessitates the use of large computers and artificial intelligence. Developing new medications and researching living entities depend on these extremely critical qualities.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Cellular Signaling | Computational Biology | Drug Development | High-Performance Computing | Hybrid Learning | Parallel Computing | Precision Medicine | Signaling Pathways | Systems Biology

Title: An Attention Based CNN-LSTM Hybrid Approach for Music Genre Classification
Abstract: This research designs and implementation of a music genre classification system that leverages an innovative hybrid approach combining Convolutional Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory networks, and an attention mechanism. This integrated system is adept at capturing the intricate time-frequency features and long-term dependencies inherent in music signals. The CNN component excels at extracting abstract features from audio's mel-frequency cepstral coefficients through a series of convolutional and pooling layers, while the LSTM network adeptly handles long-range dependencies within the sequential audio features. An attention layer is introduced to pinpoint and emphasize salient features, thereby enhancing the classification accuracy. The results from our experiments on the GTZAN dataset are compelling, illustrating that the model we've developed achieves outstanding performance benchmarks. Compared to the most recent research findings in academic literature, our model shows higher effectiveness and superiority in the music genre classification task.
Keywords: attention mechanism | convolutional neural network | Deep learning | long short-term memory Network | music genre classification

Title: Comparative Analysis of Gaussian Naïve Bayes with Bernoulli Naïve Bayes for Guitar Chord Classification
Abstract: Naïve Bayes Algorithm is extensively used in machine learning for classification problems. Guitar chord classification is a trivial problem in music recognition where Naïve bayes algorithm is exploited. To further investigate the performance of Naïve bayes, its types can be experimented. In this paper, we have attempted to investigate two Naïve bayes techniques viz, Gaussian Naïve Bayes and Bernoulli's Naïve bayes which are tested on guitar chord dataset with major and minor chords. Guitar chord classification problem has been explored and experimented in more than one dimension for music recognition and recommendation models. The preprocessing of guitar chords audio into numerical data is computationally extensive. In order to test the performance of variants of Naïve Bayes Algorithm we have considered the harmonics generated during the preprocessing and data transformation stage and analyzed the effect of higher order harmonics. In this paper we have evaluated and compared two versions of Naïve bayes algorithm for guitar chord classification problem for two sets of harmonics count. Gaussian Naïve bayes is compared with Bernoulli's Naïve bayes for datasets of guitar chords with harmonics count from 4th harmonic to 9th harmonic. This paper has interesting findings that at lower harmonic counts Gaussian Naïve bayes performs better and if the feature count of harmonics is higher, in that case Bernoulli's Naïve bayes exhibits better performance. All the results are elaborately discussed and visualized in the result section of the paper. Further, the classification problem and the experimental results are obtained, presented and compared with the existing work in the results and discussion section.
Keywords: Bernoulli's Naïve Bayes | Gaussian Naïve bayes | Guitar chord classification | harmonics | music-recognition

Title: Exploring Receptance Weighted Key Value Model for Single-Channel Speech Enhancement
Abstract: Speech enhancement has significantly benefited from advancements in deep learning, particularly in terms of intelligibility and perceptual quality. Traditional time-frequency (TF) domain methods rely on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) or recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to predict TF masks or speech spectra. In this study, we introduce a novel network architecture, the Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) model integrated with the Deep Complex Convolution Recurrent Network (DC-CRN), aimed at effectively training complex targets. This model combines the strengths of RNNs and Transformers, redefining the attention mechanism for speech enhancement tasks to avoid the exponential growth in computational complexity typically associated with traditional Transformer models. Through a series of experiments on the VoiceBank+Demand dataset, the RWKV-DCCRN model has demonstrated superior performance, efficiency, and scalability in handling long-range dependencies compared to traditional DCCRN models. Our implementation showcases the potential to optimize computational efficiency and performance in real-time speech enhancement applications, making it particularly suitable for environments with varying noise conditions and for devices requiring low latency processing.
Keywords: convolutional recurrent networks | deep learning | denoise | Receptance Weighted Key Value model | speech enhancement

Title: Effective features to define harmonic distance models
Abstract: Tonal Pitch Space (TPS) has been proposed as a harmonic distance model, which provides a way to compute numerical distances between two chords with keys. Although the theory itself seems sound, it still contains arbitrary presuppositions in its definition, and its adequacy has not well been investigated. In this study, we propose a framework in which we construct, train, and evaluate a variety of distance functions that share the same domain and range as TPS. We define three basic harmonic features (mode, tonic, and degree), and utilise these to define various distance functions by combining them, and then we evaluate all simple combinations exhaustively. We then train and evaluate each function through the task of key estimation. This entire process is to provide a perspective from which to examine how well various features and their combinations can represent harmony through our distance models. Experiments confirmed that some aspects of the TPS are indeed well designed, but also showed that its performance can be surpassed with a considerably smaller number of parameters.
Keywords: distance model | Harmony analysis | machine learning | tonal music

Title: Stacked-KBR: An Ensemble Method for Analyzing YouTube Bangla Song Reviews Using a Novel Dataset
Abstract: Song review analysis is very crucial in every language due to its widespread use in the cinema and music industry. The success of many movies depends on having some hit and blockbuster songs in the movie. From this one can understand the importance of developing automated methods for analyzing song reviews. This work is devoted to deploying a method for YouTube Bangla song review analysis by developing a new dataset of 43,264 comments annotated as either positive or negative, covering over 100 songs and 15 music genres which is publicly available in the repository https://github.com/cseku170202/Bangla-Song-Sentiment-Analysis. The prime goal of this investigation is to employ various machine learning algorithms to precisely recognize the sentiments expressed in Bangla song reviews and apply explainable AI to provide explanations. Our empirical study considered several algorithms including the K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM), Recurrent Convolutional Network (RCN), and a Stacking ensemble model (Stacked-KBR) which utilizes the previous three models as base classifiers. Among these models, the Stacked-KBR outperformed others with an accuracy of 83.98%. Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanation (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) from explainable AI are also considered in this work to observe the reason behind the model's performance.
Keywords: Bangla Dataset | Explainable AI | Song Review Analysis | Stacking Ensemble Model

Title: Comprehensive Lung Disease Detection Using Deep Learning Models and Hybrid Chest X-ray Data with Explainable AI
Abstract: Advanced diagnostic instruments are crucial for the accurate detection and treatment of lung diseases, which affect millions of individuals globally. This study examines the effectiveness of deep learning and transfer learning models using a hybrid dataset, created by merging four individual datasets from Bangladesh and global sources. The hybrid dataset significantly enhances model accuracy and generalizability, particularly in detecting COVID-19, pneumonia, lung opacity and normal lung conditions from chest X-ray images. A range of models, including CNN, VGG16, VGG19, InceptionV3, Xception, ResNet50V2, InceptionResNetV2, MobileNetV2 and DenseNet121 are applied to both individual and hybrid dataset. The results show superior performance on the hybrid dataset, with VGG16, Xception, ResNet50V2 and DenseNet121 each achieving an accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score of 99%. This consistent performance across the hybrid dataset highlights the robustness of these models in handling diverse data while maintaining high accuracy. To understand the models implicit behavior, explainable AI techniques are employed to illuminate their black-box nature. Specifically, LIME is used to enhance the interpretability of model predictions, especially in cases of misclassification, contributing to the development of reliable and interpretable AI-driven solutions for medical imaging.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) | COVID-19 | Explainable AI (XAI) | Hybrid Dataset | Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) | Lung Opacity | Normal | Pneumonia

Title: An Error Correction Model for Piano Teaching Based on Improved Endpoint Detection with CNN-HMM
Abstract: Piano teaching is based on teaching performance skills, which is an important practical discipline for interactive and personalized teaching. In order to realize the automation and digital teaching of piano, and to improve the level of piano performance and aesthetic effect, the research firstly uses the endpoint detection technology to realize the temporal value detection of the audio data, and then integrates the convolutional neural network and the Hidden Markov Model for the extraction and recognition of the note events, and finally completes the transcription of the piano audio and the correction of the errors. The experimental results show that the research-designed method outperforms the baseline model in terms of F1 value and receiver operating characteristic curve, with the highest convergence of F1 value at 88.47% and the maximum curve area at 0.906, which makes the model classify better. The method has the smallest average error on different datasets, the average absolute value error is lower than 0.25, the root mean square error is lower than 0.20, and the classification accuracy of note events is superior. In practical use, the research-designed method has a greater advantage in recognition accuracy and error correction accuracy compared with the manual method, which significantly improves the overall accuracy of piano error correction and is conducive to the development of piano teaching. The research-designed piano teaching aid error correction method is conducive to improving the efficiency and quality of piano teaching, and provides an effective reference for the application of artificial intelligence in the field of music education.
Keywords: Convolutional neural network | Endpoint detection method | Hidden Markov mode | Musical device | Piano

Title: Exploring Dimensionality Reduction Techniques in Word Classification using Surface EMG Signals
Abstract: Surface Electromyography (sEMG) is a revolutionary technology in the field of unvoiced speech recognition that captures and analyzes electric signals produced by facial muscles during speech. Despite the significance of providing an interface for recognizing and synthesizing spoken words, research in this area does not investigate and compare the impact of dimensionality reduction techniques to reduce complexity. This study aims to develop a frame-based word classification system incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques using surface EMG speech signals. To attain this objective, several ML models including Decision tree, KNN, Random Forest, XGB, and Bidirectional LSTM are developed as classifiers integrating the dimensionality reduction algorithms Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). The study found that the Random Forest classifier along with LDA performed remarkably in the experiment yielding an accuracy of 96.28%. Again, the XGB classifier showed an impressive classification accuracy of 93.45% with PCA. However, both KNN and DT performed poorly across both dimensionality reduction techniques, and the neural network (BLSTM) showed around 85% accuracy with both LDA and PCA. This research provides important insights into the application and effectiveness of dimensionality reduction techniques in improving the performance of different machine learning models for sEMG-based unvoiced speech recognition.
Keywords: dimensionality reduction | machine learning | sEMG | signal processing | silent speech

Title: AI Meets Agriculture: Advanced Rice Yield Forecasting Based on Historical Data using Machine Learning Approaches
Abstract: Despite the global importance of agriculture, inefficient practices persist, particularly in poorer regions. A big obstacle to increasing agricultural outputs is the inefficiency of conventional methods and the absence of accurate instruments for predicting crop yields. While various machine learning techniques have been used by several researchers to forecast yields, the difficulty lies in developing models that adequately account for regional nuances. To overcome this problem, this study proposed a novel machine learning-based approach for crop yield prediction focused on the Sylhet region, Bangladesh with a large unique dataset named "EcoRiceDynamics (1971-2021)."Four models - Linear Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosted, and K-Nearest Neighbors are evaluated to improve forecast precision. Performance was measured using the R<sup>2</sup> value and error reduction metrics. Our results show that the Gradient Boosted model achieved the highest R<sup>2</sup> value of 95% and MAE 6.71%, indicating its superior fit to the dataset. However, the Random Forest model excelled in minimizing prediction errors by 6.37% with R<sup>2</sup> value of 94.1%. Random Forest reduces prediction errors effectively, while Gradient Boosted explains variance better. Incorporating these models into agricultural systems could enhance decision-making and crop yields in regions like Sylhet. This study highlights the potential of machine learning in advancing agricultural sustainability on yield estimation.
Keywords: Climate Data | Crop Yield Prediction | Gradient boost | KNN | Precision Agriculture | Random Forest Regression | Soil Nutrients | Yield estimation

Title: Research on Speech Enhancement of Vocal Music Auxiliary Teaching System Based on Time-Frequency Fusion and Multi-Channel Attention Mechanism
Abstract: In this paper, the quality of speech signals collected in acoustic teaching scenarios is further improved. A dual-microphone speech enhancement method based on time-frequency fusion and deep learning algorithm is proposed to obtain higher quality speech information. Using dual-microphone speech enhancement algorithm based on general sidelobe canceller as the basic speech enhancement algorithm, time-frequency masking and adversarial generative networks are introduced. Then, the noise removal level of the algorithm is further improved, and the quality of the enhanced speech is further improved. Simulation results prove that compared with other types of speech enhancement algorithms, the constructed speech enhancement algorithm has better performance in different scenarios in terms of mean opinion score, signal-to-noise ratio, perceptual evaluation of speech quality, short-time objective intelligibility and log spectral distance. Therefore, the constructed dual-microphone speech enhancement method based on time-frequency fusion and deep learning algorithm has good performance, can effectively improve the quality of the enhanced speech, and can be applied to the actual vocal music teaching scene to help improve the teaching quality, witch has high feasibility.
Keywords: generative adversarial network | microphone array | speech enhancement | time-frequency masking | vocal music teaching

Title: Research on the Practice Path of Artificial Intelligence-enabled College Students' Physical Health Promotion
Abstract: Under the background of educational digital transformation, the application of artificial intelligence in school teaching has become an inevitable trend to promote the development of education and teaching<sup>[7]</sup>. To promote the artificial intelligence to promote the physical health of college students has become an inevitable choice. In this study, 30 male and female students in physical education class campus running results of tracking statistics, a total of 30 sets of campus running effective data. This paper conducts empirical analysis on the data obtained through methods such as literature review, expert consultation, field research, and interdisciplinary research. It uses physical fitness testing instruments to verify the related data of endurance run 1000 meters, 800 meters, and lung capacity of the tested students. The results show that: (1)The students' participation in campus run gradually increases, and it remains at an average of 37.8 times per semester; (2)The endurance run performance of male and female students improves significantly, especially for those who have completed the campus run of 120km or more; (3)The lung capacity of the tested students increases linearly, with the average lung capacity of male students increasing from 3,809 in the first year to 4, 620 in the second year, an increase of 21.3 percentage points, and the average lung capacity of female students increasing from 2,730 in the first year to 3,113 in the second year, an increase of 14 percentage points.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | digital education | physical health

Title: A Review of Audio Classification Techniques
Abstract: Audio classification is a rapidly advancing field, driven by the increasing demand for intelligent audio processing systems in various applications such as speech recognition, environmental sound classification and music genre detection. This survey paper provides a comprehensive overview of audio classification techniques, focusing on machine learning methods, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and hybrid models. Traditional techniques including k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Support Vector Machines (SVM) are reviewed for their foundational contributions. RNNs with their temporal sequence modeling capabilities are explored for applications where time dependencies are critical. CNNs widely used for their effectiveness in learning spatial hierarchies are highlighted for their transformative role in audio classification. Additionally, hybrid models that combine the strengths of multiple architectures such as CNN-RNN and CNN-SVM, are discussed for their ability to capture both spatial and temporal features. The survey critically examines the strengths and limitations of each approach, compares their performance on various datasets and outlines current challenges and future directions in the field.
Keywords: Audio Classification | Deep Learning | Machine Learning

Title: Leveraging CNNs for Efficient Classification of Apple Leaf Diseases
Abstract: This study investigates the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to classify apple plant diseases based on photographs of their leaves. Apple diseases require effective detection techniques because they represent serious risks to crop output and quality. The study makes use of a dataset of tagged photos of apple leaves, which includes both healthy and diseased leaves from conditions including cedar apple rot and apple scab. Data collection, preprocessing, CNN model architecture creation, and training are all part of the methodology. Several CNN architectures are taken into consideration, including VGG, ResNet, and Inception. The model is trained on a split dataset and its performance is monitored on a validation set to prevent overfitting. Evaluation measures include F1-score, recall, accuracy, and precision. Findings show that CNNs are good at correctly identifying apple leaf diseases. The study emphasizes how this strategy may be used in apple farming for early disease identification and well-informed decision-making. Suggestions for future research include integrating numerous imaging modalities, real-time field classification, and multi-class categorization for various illness types. This study advances the creation of cutting-edge instruments for managing diseases in apple cultivation, which could enhance crop yields and health.
Keywords: Agricultural Technology | Apple Plant Disease | Automated Disease Detection | Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) | Deep Learning | Leaf Image Analysis

Title: AI Framework for Keys Instruction and Music Notation
Abstract: The study of artificial intelligence focuses on the principles that guide all human intellectual endeavors. The integration of several academic disciplines, including as computer science, philosophy, politics, linguistics, systems engineering, neurophysiology, and behavioral science, has allowed it to grow. This article will describe how to build an intelligent machine, consisting of both hardware and software, that can replicate and exceed the abilities of the human brain in order to handle complicated issues that need specialized knowledge. It will specifically examine how to more effectively use artificial intelligence support systems into piano instruction. An Introduction, an oral language and music-assisted education system based on the ARM and SA algorithm, is proposed by this study in order to ascertain the implementation principle guiding the functioning of the piano automation recording system. It also delves deeply into the theory and operation of automated music recording systems, compiling and evaluating data that these systems generate via internal databases. is an effort to improve music education via the use of artificial intelligence support systems. The results of the experiment show that the training system for the automated notation algorithms for playing the piano and songs has a 56.81 and fast growing machine learning auxiliary technology utilization rate. Thus, we may infer that using an AI support system is necessary while teaching performance piano and automated notation.
Keywords: ARM algorithm | Artificial intelligence | Computational intelligence | Data mining | Machine learning | Music automatic notation algorithm | Music education | Piano performance | SA algorithm | Teaching system

Title: Deep Learning R-CNN for Throat Cancer Identification
Abstract: In the country, there are thousands and Casta de Indigenous all living in diverse pockets of islands located on a stretch of remote Arctic tundra. The few buttons at some other movements that cancer all over this planet has accelerated unfortunately opened Mainly among than what been seen with thorn beside him throughout history. It is very challenging to get the right treatment for throat cancer, especially when in advanced stages. This is a head-and-neck cancer that belongs to the category of gross and diverse diseases. In recent years, researchers have introduced a variety of diagnostic methods and instruments to diagnose throat cancer as accurately as possible for doctors. However, the quality of implementation has many issues in current tools and methods. Such problems include longer patient screening times, higher computational complexity and a poorer performance in the early detection of pharyngeal cancer. Here, the authors propose a new deep learning-based Mask-R-CNN model that leverages across multiple image datasets and real-time CT scans to detect pharyngeal cancer along with symptoms. Masu. Furthermore, the proposed technology is capable of detecting and diagnosing early laryngeal cancer in real-time patient examination with high sensitivity as explained above which may lead to time-saving for doctors allowing them screening a large number of patients per day. As the result, applying 98.99% curation-based on ImageNet dataset provides similar proposed model qualities with only less than a percent precision, score and recall improvements could produce more interesting results which might improve in usefulness. Over the last years, several researches have studied various approaches to detect tracheal cancer. There is a range of new methodologies for detecting laryngeal cancer in various image datasets that can be thoroughly investigated by prospective studies.
Keywords: clinical analysis | CT images | deep learning | early detection | image segmentation | ImageNet dataset | laryngeal cancer detection | Mask R-CNN | model performance metrics | real-time diagnosis

Title: Various Signal Transformation for Optimizing CNN Model Performance of Earthquake Detection
Abstract: Given the frequency of earthquakes in Indonesia, it is crucial to accurately identify them in order to prevent unnecessary alarms over their mitigation. In the context of earthquake detection and classification, the development of artificial intelligence is ongoing to achieve a dependable system. The objective of this work is to compare the signal transformations as a preprocessing step in order to achieve optimal performance outcomes for the deep learning model in detecting seismic signals. The signal transformations used in this study are Fourier, wavelet, Hilbert, and probability of power spectral density (PPSD) methods to obtain a visual representation of the signal spectrum. The unprocessed data obtained from the Indonesia Tsunami Early Warning System (InaTEWS) server underwent a classification process including three distinct categories: earthquake, background noise, and instrument noise. Seismic signal identification is performed by utilizing the signal spectrum obtained from preprocessing the raw data on the optimized convolutional neural network (CNN) model. The assessment revealed that PPSD represents the optimal signal transformation approach, achieving a peak accuracy of 97.2% under RMSprop optimization, whereas Adam optimization exhibits slightly superior precision and F1 scores of 97.3 % and 97.2 %, respectively. It is believed that these favorable results will improve the dependability of the earthquake detection system based on artificial intelligence, therefore minimizing the occurrence of detection errors that may result in public widespread panic and chaos.
Keywords: classification | CNN | deep learning | earthquake signal | signal transformation

Title: Research on Voice Humming to Guzheng Audio Transcription and Pitch-Lowering Processing Based on Genetic Algorithm and YIN Algorithm
Abstract: In recent years, AI-based music generation and transformation technologies have received widespread attention. This study presents an automated system for transcribing vocal humming audio into Guzheng audio, integrating the YIN algorithm and genetic algorithm, and optimizing pitch and timbre matching through pitch-lowering processing. First, the YIN algorithm is used to extract the fundamental frequency of the humming audio, and then the genetic algorithm optimizes the frequency sequence to better align with the Guzheng's pitch range. To further improve the audio generation quality, the system introduces pitch-lowering processing, adjusting the generated audio frequencies to fit within the Guzheng's pitch range. Experimental results show that pitch-lowering processing significantly enhances the accuracy of the pitch and timbre matching. Moreover, the genetic algorithm outperforms the YIN algorithm in optimizing pitch and timbre, with the generated audio exhibiting a more realistic Guzheng timbre. Ultimately, the system achieves significant improvements in pitch, timbre, and auditory effects. The proposed transcription scheme demonstrates good applicability in musical applications involving pitch range conversion and provides new research insights for automated instrument transcription.
Keywords: Genetic Algorithm | Guzheng Audio | Pitch Detection | Vocal Transcription | YIN Algorithm

Title: Classifying musical reading expertise by eye-movement analysis using machine learning
Abstract: Music reading is the key to literacy for musicians in the Western music tradition. This high-level activity requires an efficient extraction of the visual information from the score to the current needs of the execution. Differences in eye movements between expert and non-expert musicians during music reading have been shown. The present study goes further, using a machine learning approach to classify musicians according to their level of expertise in analyzing their eye movements and performance during sight-reading. We used a support vector machine (SVM) technique to (a) investigate whether the underlying expertise in musical reading could be reliably inferred from eye movements, performance, and subjective measures collected across five levels of expertise and (b) determine the best predictors for classifying expertise from 24 visual measures (e.g., the number of progressive fixations, the number of regressive fixations, pupil size, first-pass fixations, and second-pass fixations), 10 performance measures (e.g., eye–hand span, velocity, latency, play duration, tempo, and false notes), and 4 subjective measures (perceived complexity and cognitive skills). Eye movements from 68 pianists at five different levels of music expertise (according to their level in the conservatory of music—from first cycle to professional) were co-registered with their piano performance via a Musical Instrument Digital Interface, while they sight-read classical and contemporary music scores. Results revealed relevant classifications based on the SVM analysis. The model optimally classified the lower levels of expertise (1 and 2) compared to the higher levels (3, 4, and 5) and the medium level (3) compared to higher levels (4 and 5). Furthermore, across a total of 38 measures, the model identified the four best predictors of the level of expertise: the sum of fixations by note, the number of blinks, the number of fixations, and the average fixation duration. Thus, efficiently classifying musical reading expertise from musicians' eye movements and performance using SVM is possible. The results have important theoretical and practical implications for music cognition and pedagogy, enhancing the specialized eye and performance behaviors required for an expert music reading.
Keywords: classification | expertise | eye movements | machine learning | musicians | sight reading | SVM

Title: Professionals’ Perspectives of Smart Stationary Bikes in Rehabilitation: Qualitative Study
Abstract: Background: Stationary bikes are used in numerous rehabilitation settings, with most offering limited functionalities and types of training. Smart technologies, such as artificial intelligence and robotics, bring new possibilities to achieve rehabilitation goals. However, it is important that these technologies meet the needs of users in order to improve their adoption in current practice. Objective: This study aimed to collect professionals’ perspectives on the use of smart stationary bikes in rehabilitation. Methods: Twelve health professionals (age: mean 43.4, SD 10.1 years) completed an online questionnaire and participated in a semistructured interview regarding their needs and expectations before and after a 30-minute session with a smart bike prototype. Results: A content analysis was performed with inductive coding. Seven main themes emerged: (1) bike functionalities (cycling assistance, asymmetric resistance, and forward and backward cycling), (2) interface between bike and users (simple, user-friendly, personalized, with written reminders during training), (3) feedback to users (user and performance data), (4) training programs (preprogrammed and personalized, and algorithmic programs), (5) user engagement (telerehabilitation, group sessions, music, and automatic suggestion of training), (6) the bike as a physical device (dimensions, comfort, setup, screen, etc), and (7) business model (various pricing strategies, training for professionals, and after-sales service). Conclusions: This study provides an interpretive understanding of professionals’ perspectives regarding smart stationary bikes and is the first to identify the expectations of health professionals regarding the development of future bikes in rehabilitation.
Keywords: attitude | bicycle | bike | content analysis | cross-sectional | cycling | digital health | health professionals | opinion | perception | perspective | physical activity | qualitative | questionnaire | rehabilitation | stationary bike | survey | technology

Title: Development of an Automatic Musical Keys Notes Detection Technique Using Mir Toolbox
Abstract: Musical key recognition has traditionally been a difficult endeavor for humans, especially for people who lack adequate musical training. An expert musician must put up a lot of time and effort to listen to music and translate it into music sheets, which may be impossible for a novice to attempt. However, automatic musical key recognition streamlines the transcription process and is crucial for Music Information Retrieval (MIR). Although, research on an automatic system for detecting musical keys is still in its early stages, the findings thus far have shown to be extremely instructive for both machine learning and music composition.This research embraced the use of the MIR toolbox, a toolbox created specifically to extract musical features from audio samples. The musical key detection problem was transformed into a form of comparison of the audio waveforms and other musical features of the audio sample in this research, as a significant approach to solve the problem of music transcription. The MIR toolbox database which has recordings and Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) files of isolated piano and guitar sounds, was used to collect the training and testing data.The model's accuracy level was assessed using a confusion matrix as a performance indicator, and it turned out that the model has a 68% precision and 69% sensitivity, which shows a relatively high accuracy. Therefore, this study provides a potential solution to detecting musical keys.

Title: Exploiting EfficientNetB3, InceptionV3, and DenseNet121 for Enhanced Eye Disease Classification
Abstract: The various eye illnesses including glaucoma, retinopathy, and cataract are emerging as a major hurdle to health care provision especially because they are usually diagnosed late because of inadequate access to diagnostic instruments. This research proposes an early diagnosis and classification system of these eye diseases through a NN (CNN), trained on the retinal images. The proposed CNN improves three more well-architectured networks, i.e EfficientNetB3, InceptionV3, and DenseNet121 for feature extraction and diagnostic precision. The used models were trained to classify different eye diseases, and the final predictions were obtained in the form of weighted average to improve the generalization of the models. The performance of the system was measured by the confusion matrices, accuracy and F1 score, proving that the overall accuracy was high. Cross- validation was also perform to evaluate the model robustness The objective of this approach is to provide a dependable, fast, and self-serve system of eye disease diagnosis that should enhance the results for the patients and minimize the burden on the staff and doctors.
Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) | Ensemble Methods | Feature Extraction | Hybrid Machine Learning Techniques | Ophthalmic Disease Classification | Prediction Accuracy

Title: An efficient model for WSN Emerging Applications using Machine Learning
Abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are essential in the Internet of Things (IoT). These are widely used in modern industrial applications in which various security attacks are encountered to prevent and countermeasure the problems in WSN, such as data processing, analysis, and efficient utilization of network resources. To ensure secure data processing, techniques are proposed for protecting data privacy. Therefore, we propose a novel data-driven model by using a benchmark dataset BOT-IoT based on machine learning, which improves the performance of WSNs. Moreover, kernel of this proposed model evolved from regression based approach in use hyper-plane efficiently classified dataset into different classes. The proposed model's performance analysis has been analyzed using different metrics. The results obtained in the experiments depict that the proposed model effectively performs better than contemporary models in the state of the art.
Keywords: Applications | Internet of Things (IoT) | Machine Learning (ML) | Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) | WSN Security

Title: AI-Embedded Data Centres: Promoting Sustainability and Reducing Water Footprint
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications as always are growing at a rapid rate, which has raised the need for data centres and created threat to environment, especially with regard to water usage. The goal of this work is reducing the water consumption and footprint of AI-dependent data centres in order to promote sustainability. The goal of the research is to optimise water usage while preserving high performance and efficiency by investigating a variety of methods and instruments. Water recycling, hardware optimisation, water-efficient cooling techniques, and intelligent water management systems are important fields. The report offers significant perspectives on environmentally sustainable practices for data centres with AI integration, empowering operators to foster the development and progress of AI technologies while simultaneously making a positive impact on environmental preservation.
Keywords: AI-integrated data centers | sustain ability | water footprint and environmental conservation

Title: The Creativity in Music Composition “AI SUITE”
Abstract: AI Suite is a contemporary music composition for a large percussion ensemble. The piece has composed for pitched percussion instruments and unpitched percussion instruments. AI Suite for percussion ensemble inspired by mechanism of robot and machine, using modern techniques to convey meanings that are consistent with the characteristics of machines and robot. The composition contained 4 movements. They are Introduction, Robotic, Lento Appassionata and Machines. Each movement uses a variety of musical materials. Drums rudiments are an important resource for keyboard percussion’s playing technique (Marimba, Xylophone and Vibraphone) which lead to composition variety of sounds and musical colors. The common percussion instruments; auxiliary percussion and toy percussion instruments are adapted to be used new playing techniques to convey meaning of robot’s sound mechanism. AI Suite for percussion ensemble is implementing compositional techniques and variety of musical materials including rudiments, textures, pitches, articulations, dynamic and rhythmic dimensions unique to the composer identity.
Keywords: Drums Rudiments | Music Composition | Percussion Music

Title: The Comparison of Different Deep Learning Models for Chinese Musical Instrument Recognition
Abstract: Instrument recognition plays a crucial role in various domains such as music, education, artificial intelligence, and cultural preservation. While deep learning technologies have achieved significant success in the recognition of Western musical instruments, their application to Chinese musical instruments remains relatively unexplored. To bridge this gap, this study investigates the use of deep learning techniques for the recognition of traditional Chinese instruments. Four deep learning models - RNN, ResNetSE, TDNN, and ECAPA-TDNN - were chosen as experimental models for the task. A diverse dataset consisting of 37 traditional Chinese instruments, including the Erhu, Pipa, Guzheng, and Dizi, was created. The dataset incorporates different tones, timbres, and playing speeds, ensuring a comprehensive representation of Chinese musical instruments. For feature extraction, Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) and spectrograms were employed to capture significant audio features from the instrument sounds. The Chinese instrument recognition system processes the audio through three stages: preprocessing, feature extraction, and deep learning-based classification. The study further compares the performance of MFCC and spectrograms in terms of recognition accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that MFCC provides superior feature extraction results. Among the models using MFCC features, ECAPA-TDNN achieved the highest accuracy at 97.18%, followed by TDNN at 96.02%, ResNetSE at 95.01%, and RNN at 92.59%. These findings suggest that the TDNN-based neural networks are particularly effective for recognizing Chinese instruments.
Keywords: deep learning | Ecapa-TDNN | MFCC | ResNetSE | RNN | TDNN

Title: Design and Realization of Intelligent Electricity Metering Apparatus Full Life Cycle Management System Based on AI Image Recognition
Abstract: With the continuous improvement of the power grid lean management requirements, the existing smart turnover cabinet has limitations in the degree of automation, failure rate, etc., and has been unable to meet the needs of the full life cycle management of electric energy measuring instruments. For this reason, this paper designs and realizes a smart electric energy measuring apparatus full life cycle management system based on AI image recognition. First, the system adopts a model architecture combining ResNet and EfficientNet, using the deep network robustness of ResNet and the efficient deployment capability of EfficientNet to ensure the accuracy and real-time performance of the system in complex tasks; second, combining with the attention mechanism to optimize the extraction capability of key features, the system designs a customized classification layer to meet the demand of electric energy measuring instruments for multi-category recognition; finally, this paper designs and implements an intelligent electric energy measuring instruments life cycle management system based on AI image recognition. Finally, the system enhances the adaptability to low-light, reflective and other complex scenes through the image preprocessing module. The system realizes the functions of automatic storage and retrieval, real-time monitoring and early warning of measuring instruments, effectively improves the lean level of the whole life cycle management of measuring assets, and provides important support for promoting the modernization of the management of intelligent electric energy measuring instruments.
Keywords: AI image recognition | EfficientNet | full lifecycle management | power systems | ResNet | smart power metering

Title: SHAP-1DCNN Based Detection of Analogue Operational Amplifiers
Abstract: In the face of highly integrated and complex integrated circuits, traditional IC testing often relies on complex test designs and specialised test instruments, making it difficult to balance testing costs and efficiency. Deep learning algorithms can automatically learn and extract complex features from data, which can be adapted to various types of IC testing and help to realise the intelligence of the testing process. In this thesis, a SHAP-1DCNN based analogue operational amplifier testing technique (title) is proposed based on the actual test data of analogue integrated operational amplifiers (OPAs) using the SHAP-1DCNN deep learning algorithm.Firstly, the traditional CNN deep learning algorithm model is improved using SHAP analysis, and secondly, the general analogue integrated operational amplifier chip test circuit is drawn, and the precision components are patched and soldered to test the circuit board. Testing the key performance parameters of a large number of chips to obtain data sets. Train the optimised and improved SHAP-1DCNN deep learning model based on the collected data, and finally integrate this deep learning model in FPGA and accelerate its computation. The validation results show that the proposed test technique achieves a single OPA test time of 0.6s with an accuracy of 97.3%.
Keywords: Feature filtering Physical testing SHAP-CNN FPGA

Title: Explicit Content Classification in Indonesian Song Lyrics Using the LSTM-CNN Method
Abstract: Music services are currently very popular and accessible to anyone, particularly through internet platforms. However, this widespread accessibility necessitates careful consideration, as music and songs can introduce explicit content to underage children and teenagers, especially through song lyrics. Manual labeling of songs for explicit content is prone to errors and time-consuming, but this process can be improved with Natural Language Processing (NLP) technologies, such as text classification using deep learning. The LSTM-CNN model was chosen for its ability to leverage the strengths of both Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). LSTM captures long-range dependencies in sequential data, while CNN is effective at extracting localized features from text. This combination makes LSTM-CNN ideal for the complexity of Indonesian song lyrics, which often involve context-dependent content. In this research, the LSTM-CNN model demonstrated optimal performance in classifying explicit content in Indonesian song lyrics. The best results were achieved with a balanced dataset of 5,470 rows, an 80: 20 data splitting ratio, 5 epochs, a batch size of 128, and a dropout rate of 0.5. The model's performance metrics were as follows: accuracy of 74.52%, precision of 75.22%, recall of 74.37%, and an F1-score of 74.68%.
Keywords: classification | explicit content | LSTM-CNN | music lyric | NLP

Title: Road Crack Detection using Deep Learning
Abstract: The road is a path that helps to connect various locations. It is essential to our day-to-day existence. The state of the weather conditions, overloading, poor maintenance, and a few other factors all contribute to road distress. The prevalent stressors are cracks, rutting, and potholes. Accidents on the roads have increased recently as a result of poor upkeep. Safety and road upkeep are important issues for transportation infrastructure. Road cracking is the fundamental and underlying source of other damages like potholes, etc., so manually identifying this distress requires labor-intensive, human inspection. Among the many difficulties, seeing fractures in the road ahead of time is crucial to avoiding collisions and expensive repairs. In this study, we provide an automated deep learning framework technique for spotting road cracks. The suggested method is trained using road photo datasets from many sources, which include a range of road surface types, lighting situations, and fracture severity. After that, data augmentation approaches are utilized to enhance model generalization. We use a variety of deep learning frameworks and fine-tune the hyper parameters to further enhance the model's performance and Reliability and consistency in grading outcomes are provided by the proposed deep learning approach, which is also computationally less expensive. The recommended deep learning method shows amazing accuracy in identifying and categorizing potholes, making it a useful instrument for road maintenance agencies.
Keywords: DeepLearning | Inception-V3 | VGG-16 | VGG-19 | Xception

Title: The impact of artificial intelligence on musicians
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is forecasted to have more of an impact on some occupations and industries than others. We examine the impact that AI will have on musicians and singers. This analysis provides an interesting example as musicians typically engage in physical activities when playing, performing, and use creativity when writing songs. We contribute to the existing literature by linking AI to both an occupational analysis and delving into the emotional aspects AI might not be able to provide for musicians. We explore the pros and cons of using AI for the creation of AI generated music. Further, this paper explores music creation to focus on production and performance. Additional consideration is provided regarding the legal and ethical considerations of AI for musicians.
Keywords: artificial intelligence | generative artificial intelligence | musicians

Title: Comparing Rayleigh Waves for Seismograph Health Diagnostics Based on Machine Learning
Abstract: The need for high-quality seismic data requires the development of seismograph health diagnostic methods to detect instrument problems early. The rapid expansion of seismic networks, increasing data volume, and the growing complexity of analysis methods for detecting component degradation are challenged by limited resources. To overcome this problem, a more efficient method is needed to assess the health of seismographs at each station. We propose a simple seismograph health diagnostic method that uses machine learning to classify seismographs based on their condition. This method analyzes parameters derived from the similarity of teleseismic Rayleigh waves recorded by a target station and several nearby reference stations. Key metrics, including cross-correlation coefficient, amplitude ratio, and cross-spectral density coherence (CSD), are essential to label the condition of each station based on its actual status when the teleseismic event occurs, thus creating a comprehensive dataset. We rigorously evaluated this dataset using three leading classification models: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Among these, XGBoost demonstrated superior performance, achieving the highest accuracy (0.97), precision (0.99), recall (0.97), and F1 score (0.98). These results establish XGBoost as a reliable method for assessing seismograph health, classifying their status as excellent, good, fair, or poor. This approach is expected to enhance the seismograph health diagnostic and improve seismic network reliability.
Keywords: eXtreme Gradient Boosting | Random Forest | Rayleigh wave | seismograph | seismograph health diagnostics | Support Vector Machine

Title: Comparison of Emotion Recognition from Baby Cries Using CNN and SVM with Noise Reduction Techniques
Abstract: Emotion recognition from baby cries has become an important field of research, with potential applications in healthcare and caregiving. This paper presents a comparison of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM) for classifying emotions from baby cries, focusing on categories such as hunger, pain, tiredness, discomfort, and burping. Noise interference is a significant challenge in cry recognition, and noise reduction techniques are applied to enhance model accuracy. A 5-fold cross-validation approach is used to evaluate the performance of both models under noisy conditions. According to preliminary findings, the SVM outperformed the CNN, which had an accuracy of 81.7%, with an accuracy of 84% across all emotion categories. Both models demonstrated significant improvements with noise reduction, with the SVM model achieving the highest accuracy increase, rising from 81.2% to 84%. This paper highlights the effectiveness of deep learning models for real-time emotion detection and underscores the importance of noise reduction in achieving reliable results.
Keywords: 5-fold cross-validation | audio signal processing | baby cries | CNN | Emotion recognition | machine learning | noise reduction | SVM

Title: Mood Classification of Indian Melodies Automatically Through Random Forest Method
Abstract: Most frequently, we decide to play a song or piece of music that best suits our current state of mind. Despite this significant link, the majority of the music software programmes available today do not yet offer the capability of mood-aware play-list building. By associating songs with the appropriate emotion category they communicate, music listeners might avoid spending more time manually compiling a list of tracks that suit a given mood or occasion. The challenge is to automatically and intelligently recognise this element because it is time-consuming to manually add lyrics to music with the appropriate emotion. Machine learning & data mining techniques have made significant contributions to analysing and determining how music and emotion relate to one another, which has given rise to a lot of interest in the research of mood detection in the field of music in recent years. By attempting to develop a system for automatically identifying the mood underlying the audio track<sup>s</sup> by mining their spectral, temporal audio properties, we carry the same inspiration forward and make a contribution. Hindi songs that are popular in India are the main focus. In order to educate, prepare, and evaluate the model that captures the emotions of these audio songs, several data classification techniques were evaluated and created an open source platform for it. By using the grouping (ensemble) of random-forest-approach tested on a set of 2700 audio samples and determined the mood underlying Indian popular music with an adequate precision of 70% to 75%.
Keywords: Classification Techniques | Data Mining | Machine learning | Random Forest Approach | Temporal Audio properties

Title: Enhancing a Stationary Noise Suppressor with Artificial Neural Networks
Abstract: Despite artificial neural networks (ANNs) making rapid progress in the field of noise removal for audio signals, their computational complexity and unpredictable behavior on unseen noise types constitute an issue for many applications. Noise suppression systems often need to be adopted in low-resource communications systems that cannot meet the requirements of most deep learning models. These systems also require real-time low-delay processing, and are adopted in a wide variety of noise situations. To overcome these limitations, we propose an innovative hybrid noise suppressor (HNS) for speech signals which combines the robustness of a traditional stationary noise suppressor (SNS) with the generalization capabilities of an ANN. A low-complexity ANN is used to enhance the performance of the SNS by removing non-stationary noise and perceptually unpleasant artifacts. Our evaluation shows that the proposed HNS is able to perform effective real-time denoising on unseen noise types, while retaining a lower complexity than the vast majority of state of the art deep learning techniques.

Title: Optimizing Music Genre Classification: A Hybrid Approach with ACO and Ensemble Learning
Abstract: The classification of music genres accurately is an ongoing challenge due to the diverse and complex nature of music. Current methods can struggle to identify genres correctly. This study introduces a combination of ensemble learning and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) to better select features that are key to identifying music genres. Using a diversified collection of songs from Spotify, the research applies detailed data preparation before utilizing a Stacking Classifier framework, which brings together several base learners and an Extra Trees algorithm to improve prediction accuracy. This method achieved a 96.75% accuracy in classifying music genres, surpassing previous methods and advancing the field. The study also compares this new model with other innovative models, highlighting the effectiveness of using a mix of methods. These improvements have important implications for building better music recommendation systems that are both accurate and user-friendly, paving the way for future developments in automatic music analysis.
Keywords: Ant Colony Optimization | Deep Neural Networks | Ensemble Learning | Music Genre Classification | Recommendation Systems

Title: Instrumentality Classification Evaluation System for Natural Sounds
Abstract: Exploring the captivating realm of natural sounds in music creation typically presents unique challenges. Although the simplicity of producing melodies with glasses filled with varying amounts of water is enchanting, replicating such versatility with other natural sounds poses difficulties. The limitations lie in the inherent properties of most natural sounds, which lack the pitch modulation freedom akin to glass instruments, resulting in homogeneity or complexity that may not be conducive to direct musical application. This study addresses these challenges by proposing an evaluation method that leverages neural networks and deep learning techniques. Our method uses a dataset of natural sounds to train a deep neural network model, extracting feature vectors that encapsulate their sonic characteristics. Subsequently, these extracted features are applied to instrumental sound datasets, enabling the modeling of natural sound dimensions within the instrumental realm. Through a classification model, the obtained features facilitate the comparison of natural and instrumental ensembles, offering insights into the suitability of natural sounds as musical instruments. By applying this methodology, our study illustrates how natural sounds such as cowbells can be evaluated in comparison with conventional instruments such as the marimba. This approach enhances our understanding of natural sound potential in music composition and performance, offering new avenues for creative exploration and innovation in sound design.
Keywords: Machine Learning | Music Instruments | Nature Sounds | Sound representations | Sound synthesis

Title: Instrumental Timbre Transfer Based on Disentangled Representation of Timbre and Pitch
Abstract: Timbre transfer is a complex audio synthesis task that changes the distinctive perceptual attribute of one instrument to resemble another while preserving the underlying musical content. In order to investigate the possibility of effective representation for pitch and timbre, this paper explores recent advances in timbre transfer using deep learning models, and presents a framework for multiple-to-multiple instrumental timbre transfer using a beta-variational autoencoder β-VAE). Through the dual-encoder system, it effectively disentangles the timbre and pitch, enabling the transfer of timbral characteristics across different musical notes and instruments while preserving the original pitch information. The performance of our approach, evaluated through metrics including Frechet Audio Distance (FAD), pitch accuracy, and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), suggests its effectiveness for timbre conversions. This research offers potential applications in music production, audio synthesis, and sound design, paving the way for more adaptable and efficient timbre transfer solutions.

Title: Detection of Voice Disorder Using Spectral and Statistical Audio Features and SVM-RBF
Abstract: The detection of voice disorders using voice signal processing and machine learning has emerged as a promising early diagnosis and treatment approach. This paper presents a machine learning-based automatic voice disorder detection framework extracting and selecting optimum features from voice audio signals. The practical challenge of class-imbalanced scenario of disorder and healthy voices data is addressed using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Several features, i.e., Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Chroma Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), zero crossing rate, root mean square, skewness, and kurtosis; have been studied in spectral and statistical domains. Finally, the optimum features are selected using the Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (RFECV) technique to reduce the classifier model’s complexity. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier with a Radial basis function kernel is developed, prioritizing simplicity and efficiency. The SVM model is trained and tested using the well-accepted VOICED database of PhysioNet Data Bank where the audio is captured using a smartphone. The performance of the overall framework shows an accuracy of 95% and 100% precision and specificity, demonstrating its resilience for precise evaluations and smartphone-based diagnosis applications.
Keywords: audio signal processing | RBF | RFECV | SMOTE | spectral | statistical features | SVM | voice disorder

Title: Similarity Metrics for Late Reverberation
Abstract: Automatic tuning of reverberation algorithms relies on the optimization of a loss function. While general audio similarity metrics are useful, they are not optimized for the specific statistical properties of reverberation in rooms. This paper presents two novel metrics for assessing the similarity of late reverberation in room impulse responses. These metrics are differentiable and can be utilized within a machine-learning framework. We compare the performance of these metrics to two popular audio metrics using a large dataset of room impulse responses encompassing various room configurations and microphone positions. The results indicate that the proposed functions based on averaged power and frequency-band energy decay outperform the baselines with the former exhibiting the most suitable profile towards the minimum. The proposed work holds promise as an improvement to the design and evaluation of reverberation similarity metrics.
Keywords: acoustic measurements | Acoustics | machine learning | reverberation | spatial audio

Title: The Impact of AI on Accounting Technology Adoption the Mediate Role of Business Performance
Abstract: How the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on accounting technology adoption and explore whether business performance mediates this relationship. The study follows a descriptive research design conducted in Amman, Jordan that seeks to investigate the effects of AI-based accounting technologies on businesses. Sample practitioners120 business administrators were selected through a purposive sampling technique. A questionnaire was the primary data collection instrument, and face content [30] validation was conducted to assure its accuracy, relevance, and comprehensiveness. The reliability of the scale was confirmed with Cronbach Alpha, which has a value of 0.84, which indicates high enough consistency; Analysis of collected data was performed using the regression and has been assessed by level 0.05(alpha). This study discovers the positive effects on business performance by implementing AI-equipped accounting technology in terms of increasing efficiency, reliability and resources. By incorporating AI in accounting duties, it is feasible to remove workloads speedily and also minimize costs which leads further in getting reliable financial information on time. The study concludes that AI-enabled accounting technology has a positive influence on business performance, playing an essential role in promoting operational outcomes. The research advises organizations to embrace AI-driven accounting tools that can lead the way towards better financial transparency and operational proficiency. Companies must train and retrain professional accountants who develop or review financial information to maximize their utilization of AI technologies for rapidly delivering the financial data needed.
Keywords: Accounting Technology | AI | Business | Performance

Title: Machine Learning Classification of FNA-Derived Cell Nuclei Features for Breast Cancer Prediction
Abstract: In the female population worldwide, breast cancer is a prevalent and potentially lethal form of malignancy. Timely and precise identification is essential for enhancing patient results. The main objective of this work is to use logistic regression to classify breast cancer as malignant or benign using the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) dataset. Features extracted from digitized pictures of fine needle aspirate (FNA) of breast masses are included in the collection. The reliability of the logistic regression model was assessed using several performance measures, such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The model exhibited strong performance with a precision of 95.32% on the test set, underscoring its potential as a very efficient instrument for diagnosing breast cancer. Due to its straightforwardness and comprehensibility, these results indicate that logistic regression can be a valuable supplement to the diagnostic process, facilitating early identification and improving patient results.
Keywords: breast cancer | classification | machine learning

Title: ENHANCING AUDIO SIGNAL SEGMENTATION FOR MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS WITH REFINED MFCC-BASED FEATURES
Abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of modified Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) features, incorporating Delta and Delta-Delta MFCCs, for classifying musical instruments-specifically drums, guitar, and keyboard. The modified MFCC approach was compared to the standard MFCC in terms of classification accuracy and instrument detection across five cross-validation folds. The results show that the modified MFCC outperforms the standard MFCC, achieving a classification accuracy of 95% compared to 86%, highlighting the importance of temporal features in distinguishing the unique audio patterns of each instrument. Additionally, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis was employed to identify dominant frequencies, revealing that drums dominate lower frequencies, guitars occupy mid-range frequencies, and keyboards cover a broad spectrum. Clustering of these dominant frequencies further confirmed their distinct spectral characteristics, validating the modified MFCC features as reliable indicators for instrument classification. These findings have significant implications for real-time applications in audio segmentation, music transcription, and AI-based music recognition, with potential use in music production, education, and other related fields.
Keywords: AUDIO INSTRUMENT | FREQUENCY | MFCC | MODIFIED

Title: Deepfake Voice Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks: A Comprehensive Approach to Identifying Synthetic Audio
Abstract: Deepfake voice recognition has lately been one of the critical challenges in the domain of cybersecurity and digital forensics, as it has recently become increasingly used with deep learning models to create absolutely indistinguishable audio imitations. This paper proposes a CNN-based approach to detect and classify deepfake audio clips. The model is trained on an exhaustive dataset that includes both real and deepfake voice records, putting much attention into the difference between natural and manipulated speech patterns. Our approach is based on the spectrogram analysis-a method of audio signal processing by converting it into a visual format that the CNN then analyzes to extract and categorize features. We test the performance of this model, which has gone through rigorous training with an accuracy of 82.6% and a test loss of 0.386. Results indicate that the proposed CNN architecture successfully learns nuanced acoustic variations between real and synthetic voices, setting up a robust framework for the detection of deepfakes. Moreover, the generalizability of the model has been checked multiple times, keeping the training and validation metrics very close. Future works will further improve the detection accuracy by including more pre-processing techniques and increasing the dataset with more varieties of deepfake sources. The study therefore adds to the ever-increasing demand for reliable and capable tools in the identification of audio forgeries, which seriously threatens privacy, security, and integrity of information in our time.
Keywords: Audio | Classification | CNN | Deep Learning | Deepfake

Title: Automating Language Proficiency Evaluation in English Language Teaching: An NLP Framework
